author: bobbyjoecool
body:
## Changes Made

### My Reservations is in the Welcome menu too (#292)

Beta testers expected their own pages (bookings, boats and account) to be together under their name in the menu, and one went looking for his reservation there first. It wasn't there. The Welcome menu now lists My Reservations, My Fleet and User Profile, in that order. My Reservations also stays under Plan Your Stay, since other testers found it there, so either place works. On the My Reservations page, both menu names are underlined to show where you are.

Files touched:

- `src/main/webapp/includes/header.jsp` Adds My Reservations to the top of the Welcome menu and underlines that menu on the My Reservations page.

### Menus close when you tab past them (#260)

Someone using the keyboard instead of a mouse could open Plan Your Stay, tab past the last link, and the menu would stay open, covering part of the page they'd moved on to. Both header menus now close as soon as keyboard focus leaves them, the same as they already did for a click elsewhere or the Escape key.

Files touched:

- `src/main/webapp/js/header.js` Closes a header menu when keyboard focus moves outside it.

### A Forgot password? link on the sign-in box (#300)

A beta tester noticed there was no way to reset a forgotten password from the sign-in box. The reset itself already worked, but the only way to reach it was to get your password wrong three times and lock your account. There's now a "Forgot password?" link right under the Password box. It opens the reset with your email already filled in if you'd typed it.

Files touched:

- `src/main/webapp/includes/loginModal.jsp` Adds the Forgot password? link, and one shared script for it and the locked-out Reset your password button.
- `src/main/webapp/css/loginModal.css` Styles the link as a small, quiet text link with a clear keyboard focus outline.

### Book a Slip says when the start date is in the past (#301)

A beta tester typed a start date that had already passed. The Reserve button stayed grey and said "Choose a start date to continue", even though they had chosen one, so they had to work out what was wrong on their own. Now the moment a past date is entered, the page says "Start date can't be in the past. Choose today or later." under the date, and "Start date can't be in the past." under the button. The server gives the same message if a past date ever reaches it, and its date and dock messages now show under the right field instead of a general "could not be completed" message.

Files touched:

- `src/main/webapp/js/reservation.js` Shows the past-date message as soon as the date is entered and under the Reserve button, and puts the server's date and dock messages under their fields.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/ReservationServlet.java` Uses the same wording for a missing date and a past date.

### Clearer sign-up form (#304)

The boat section of the sign-up form says it's optional, but Boat Name had a red star, which was confusing. The note now says "You can add a boat now or later. If you add one, the starred fields are required." The example text in the boxes (Jack, Sparrow, Tortuga, Black Pearl) looked enough like real answers that a tester thought the form was already filled in. Name and city boxes no longer have example text, the email box shows `you@example.com`, and the rest start with "e.g.". Example text is also a lighter colour now on every form, while staying readable. The same boxes appear on Your Account, Book a Slip and My Fleet, so they get the same examples.

Files touched:

- `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/views/registration.jsp` New wording for the boat section's optional note, and `you@example.com` in the email box.
- `src/main/webapp/includes/personalInfoCard.jsp` Removes the name and city examples and rewords the rest.
- `src/main/webapp/includes/boatInfoCard.jsp` Removes the boat name example and rewords the rest.
- `src/main/webapp/css/site.css` Makes example text in every form box a lighter, still readable colour.

### New customers are signed in and taken back where they were going (#299)

A beta tester clicked Book a Slip, created an account, and ended up on the home page, not signed in, and had to sign in and find Book a Slip again. Now, creating an account signs you in straight away and takes you to the page you were heading for, with the "Account created — welcome aboard" message. That works from Book a Slip, My Reservations, the Wait List, or any page you opened the sign-in box from. If you started from the home page's Register button, you land on the home page, signed in.

Files touched:

- `src/main/java/.../util/CustomerSession.java` New file. The one place a customer is signed in, used by both signing in and registering.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/LoginServlet.java` Uses the shared sign-in instead of its own copy. Signing in works exactly as before.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/RegisterServlet.java` Signs the new customer in and sends them to the page they came from.
- `src/main/webapp/includes/loginModal.jsp` The Register here link remembers the page you were headed for.
- `src/main/webapp/js/loginModal.js` Keeps the Register here link pointing at the right page when a button like Book a Slip opens the sign-in box.
- `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/views/registration.jsp` Remembers that page through any mistakes on the form.
- `src/main/webapp/js/registration.js` The form's own "Log in" link also takes you to that page, not back to the sign-up form.

### My Fleet and User Profile ask you to sign in, then bring you back (#299)

If you weren't signed in (or your session had timed out) and went to My Fleet or User Profile, the site quietly sent you to the home page with no explanation. Now you land on the home page with the sign-in box already open and a note: "Please sign in, or register, to continue." Signing in, or creating an account from there, takes you straight to the page you wanted. The same happens if your session times out while you're editing a boat or your profile.

Files touched:

- `src/main/java/.../util/CustomerSession.java` Adds the one way a members-only page sends a signed-out visitor to sign in and remembers where they wanted to go.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/MyFleetServlet.java`, `MyFleetAddServlet.java`, `MyFleetEditServlet.java`, `MyFleetRemoveServlet.java` Send a signed-out visitor to sign in and back to My Fleet.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/EditProfileServlet.java` Sends a signed-out visitor to sign in and back to User Profile.
- `src/main/webapp/includes/loginModal.jsp` Opens the sign-in box by itself when a page asks for it, with the note explaining why.
- `src/main/webapp/js/loginModal.js` Puts the cursor in the email box, and tidies the address bar so refreshing doesn't reopen the box.

### My Fleet's behind-the-scenes code tidied up (#286)

Nothing changes for anyone using the site. The four parts of the code behind My Fleet each had their own copy of "is this customer signed in?" and seven copies of "show the page again with a message". Each now has one shared version, so a future change to how My Fleet shows a message is made once instead of seven times.

Files touched:

- `src/main/java/.../servlet/MyFleetServlet.java` Holds the one shared "show My Fleet" step.
- `src/main/java/.../servlet/MyFleetAddServlet.java`, `MyFleetEditServlet.java`, `MyFleetRemoveServlet.java` Use the shared sign-in check and the shared "show My Fleet" step.

### A blank boat name shows a message, not an error page (#255)

If a boat's name was cleared while editing it (possible with an old copy of the page open), saving showed a bare error page. It now reopens the edit box with "Enter a name for the boat." under the name, like any other mistake on the form.

Files touched:

- `src/main/java/.../servlet/MyFleetEditServlet.java` Removes the early check that showed the error page, so the normal field message appears instead.

### Robert's part of the presentation is complete

Robert's slides for the team's QA presentation ar

body:
> Issues close only when their checklist is done, so unfinished work stays open and the closer hears why.

## Background

Closes #141. A merge closed may-calendar Plan 02 with 6 of its 8 boxes unchecked. `fitness close-check` now reopens such an issue and mentions whoever closed it. `fitness pr-check` fails a PR that would close one.

A squash merge records its merge commit as the closer, so the query traces that commit back to its PR. `pr-closes-issue` now skips keywords in code, since #141 quotes may-calendar's `Closes #51`.

This replaces #143 as one commit, since two of its commits both linked #141. The org rollout moved to #144.

## Changelog

- Feat: `fitness close-check` reopens an issue closed as completed with unchecked items, unless closed as not planned or duplicate.
- Feat: it comments once, listing the items and mentioning the closer, plus the closing PR's author and merger.
- Feat: `fitness pr-check` fails a PR whose closing keyword targets an issue with unchecked items, naming each item.
- Ci: publish `close-check-reusable.yml`, and run close-check on this repo's own issues.
- Fix: `pr-closes-issue` skips closing keywords inside inline or fenced code, since they quote an example.
- Test: cover each case with a fake GitHub API, plus keywords in code.
- Docs: describe the rule and caller in the adoption guide and READMEs.

An audit that reads pnpm lockfiles found 39 production advisories in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (3 critical, 21 high, 12 moderate, 3 low), and 16 in `site/package-lock.json`. Dependabot reports none of them. This PR clears every one in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and everything in the site that a patch or minor update can fix. Both lockfiles only; no `package.json` or workflow file changes.

| browserslist | 4.28.1 | 4.29.3 | GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx, GHSA-73wf-gq98-2v4g |

About next: `apps/studio` declares `next ^15.5.14`. The root override `"next": ">=15.5.14"` is what resolved it to 16.2.1, and the app has been built and tested on 16 since. author: matthew-dean
body:
A Vue component with a boolean prop rejected a bare attribute. `<Avatar decorative>` reached `checkedProp` as `""` and threw `HR002: Must be true or false`, so the component failed to render. Vue apps normally write booleans bare, as in `<Button stretch>`. Found in Looma 0.21.x, where it breaks any bare boolean on a Looma Vue component.

Runtime props are declared `type: null` on purpose, so Vue's own Boolean casting doesn't apply. Instead, `checkedProp` now applies the HTML runtime's rule (`runtime.ts`, `invocationValue`): a present, empty boolean attribute is `true`. Other types keep their rules for an empty value, so an empty `number` or a required `string` still fails.

- `src/targets/vue-props.ts`: `""` on a `boolean` prop reads as `true`.
- `tests/vue-props.test.ts`: covers a bare boolean (optional and required), `false`, absent, and that empty `number` or required `string` still fail. The test fails without the fix.
- Declares **1.0.0-alpha.14**: all three packages, the generator version, regenerated examples, and version fixtures.

`pnpm verify:pr` passes (328 tests, package tests 4).

author: kcnyu
body:
The fallback brief card trusted a model-authored USD total that could omit the HK leg. Plan validation did not check the currency arithmetic.

Use one finite-input, positive-FX calculation for core totals, plan normalization/validation and fallback cards. Postflight binds monetary inputs to the current generation's deterministic core when available and computes both totals; invalid inputs fail publication. Fallback cards independently recompute existing plans without rewriting them, and show an unavailable reading when inputs cannot be verified. Remove the obsolete single-incident string detector and document the source-copy rule.

Historical runtime plans stay intact. CI retains 33 reviewed legacy monetary blocks only when the filename and SHA-256 of book/FX values match exactly; decision/schema errors, changed monetary values and new files remain strict. The live writer, postflight and pre-commit use no exceptions. The host check keeps structural schema failures critical and reports their retained monetary discrepancies separately as warnings.

Closes #2255.

Validation: 109 targeted book, normalization, card and ledger tests passed; the final normalization persistence check also passed. Full checks run in CI.

author: gonzalomorenoc
body:
Reescribe el guion de la demo del concurso alrededor de la tesis del producto (continuidad del conocimiento) y adapta el runbook.

## Guion (~5 min)
1. **Índice de continuidad**: `checkout-suite` 95 frente a `banca-movil` 25, con el desglose.
2. **Acta de traspaso** firmada → enlace verificable sin cuenta → enlace manipulado en rojo.
3. **Pablo pregunta** a la memoria: lección del PSP, razón de la etiqueta, contacto, runbook — con citas.
4. **De dónde sale la memoria**: runs → triaje determinista → etiqueta con razón → buscable; acta por run.

Incluye una **tabla de dónde sale cada afirmación** (código o medición en prod del 01-10). Retirado por no sostenerse: «coste de API 0 €», «100 % on-premise con Ollama», tiempos concretos y la cifra no medida de «2-6 semanas de shadowing».

## Runbook
Estado sembrado de continuidad, checklist por acto, enlaces manipulados para el acta de traspaso, plan B por acto, y corrección: la clave de firma del `.env` local ya es la real (`key_id` comprobado contra `/v2/certificates/pubkey`).

## Depende de
- #113 («contradice la etiqueta humana», detalle del Acto 4) y #114 (la razón tecleada se vuelve buscable, Acto 3).

## Pendiente (ensayo en la app)
- [ ] Respuestas del LLM a las 3 preguntas del Acto 3 (Gemini, no determinista)
- [ ] Emitir el acta de traspaso y probar los dos enlaces
- [ ] Re-ejecutar la riqueza la semana de la demo (los runs más recientes son del 13-ago)
- [ ] Retirar de la cuenta demo la org de pruebas que aparece en el selector

author: bossknight
body:
## ⚠️ Schema change
Adds a `RateLimit` model to `prisma/schema.prisma`. **Run `npm run prisma:migrate` in every environment before deploying.** No migration file is committed, matching the repo's existing convention (there is no `prisma/migrations` directory; a lone migration would conflict with the existing tables).

If the table is missing, the limiter fails open: requests are allowed and an error is logged, so a skipped migration disables limiting rather than blocking users.

## Changes

### Rate limiting (`lib/rate-limit.ts`)
Fixed-window counters in one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` upsert, so concurrent requests can't share a stale count and every app instance sees the same totals. Stale rows are swept on ~1% of calls.

| Action | Limit | Keyed by | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Register | 5 / hour | IP | 429 + `Retry-After`, checked before the bcrypt hash |
| Login | 10 / 15 min | IP | Login form shows "Too many sign-in attempts" instead of "Incorrect email or password" |
| Barcode | 30 / hour | User | 429 + `Retry-After`; protects the shared 100/day UPCitemdb quota |

Client IP is the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` entry (the one a proxy appends). Documented in the README: per-IP limits require a proxy/host that sets this header.

### Duplicate-email signup race
`/api/auth/register` now catches Prisma `P2002` from `user.create` and returns 409. Previously two concurrent signups with one email both passed the `findUnique` pre-check and the loser got a 500.

### Provider caching (`next: { revalidate }`)
| Provider | TTL | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| TMDB search | 1h | Terms allow caching up to 6 months |
| RAWG search | 1h | Caching encouraged |
| Open Library search / ISBN | 1h / 1 day | Open Library asks clients to cache |
| Google Books | none | Terms tie caching to response cache headers, which `revalidate` ignores |
| UPCitemdb | none | No terms found; left for a manual check |

Next only writes status-200 responses to the data cache (`patch-fetch.js`), so provider errors are never cached. Note: this reverses a deliberate earlier choice commented in `tmdb.ts`.

### CI and maintenance
- CI now runs `npm run build` (verified to build with no env vars set)
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: npm weekly (minor/patch grouped) and GitHub Actions weekly

### Tests (55 → 119)
- `lib/catalog-params`, `lib/catalog-query` (where/orderBy, cursor pagination boundaries, stats scoping)
- Register route (success, validation, existing email, race, rate limit), credentials `authorize`, barcode route, limiter logic and IP parsing

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (119/119), `npm run build`: all clean
- Race-fix test fails with the fix reverted
- **Against a real Postgres 16** (throwaway local instance):
  - 50 concurrent requests with limit 10 → exactly 10 allowed, stored count 50
  - Window reset, key isolation, stale-row sweep, exact `Retry-After` (fixed an off-by-one from Postgres rounding `now()` to the column's ms precision)
  - Real register route: 201 ×5 → 429 from one IP; another IP still 201; two concurrent same-email signups → 201 + 409
- Not verified: provider caching at runtime (confirmed from Next docs/source only)

## Known limits
- Two proxy hops (e.g. Cloudflare → nginx) would make the last XFF entry the inner proxy's IP, so all users share one login/register bucket.
- Login is per-IP only; per-email limits were left out because they let anyone lock a user out.

author: shanedolley
body:
`mac-build.yml` derived its release tag from `package.json`'s version and uploaded with `gh release upload --clobber`. Dispatching it on a version that had already shipped found the existing release, skipped the create, and replaced the published binary under the same tag, with no failure and no record.

This nearly happened while cutting v1.0.1: the version field still read 1.0.0, so the dispatch would have overwritten v1.0.0's DMG rather than making a release.

## The change

The step refuses when the tag already carries `girra-macos-arm64.dmg`, and uploads without `--clobber`.

It keys on the asset, not on the release, so a run that created the release and then failed to upload stays completable. Keying on the release would have turned a half-finished run into a dead end requiring a manual delete.

## The test

`config/scripts/mac-release-asset-overwrite-guard.test.mjs` extracts the step's own `run` script from the workflow and executes it under `bash` against a stub `gh`, covering three states:

| State | Expected |
|---|---|
| Tag already carries the DMG | exits non-zero, never calls `release upload` |
| Release absent | calls `release create`, then uploads |
| Release exists without the DMG | uploads, no `release create` |

Plus an assertion that `--clobber` is absent.

Checked against the previous script: two of the four cases fail, so the test constrains behaviour rather than describing it.

## Verified

`pnpm test config/scripts/mac-release-asset-overwrite-guard.test.mjs`: 4 passed. Same file against the pre-change workflow: 2 failed, 2 passed. `check:code-quality:changed` clean. The workflow still parses as YAML.

author: martinkrakowski
body:
Lane **HXF4-lane-observability** (wave `hardening-followups-w01`; plan `docs/planning/2026-09-29_wave-hardening-and-w05-follow-ups.md` §6, r2). Implemented on midnight: space-bunny, `--agent lane`. The fix round resumed the lane's own session.

## What

`yarn lane:watch` is a READ-ONLY CLI against the opencode server, reached through the ocm loopback tunnel.

- **`usage --server <url> --session <id> [--json]`:** wall time, tokens (input, output, reasoning, cache) and cost, from `GET /session/{sessionID}`. No ssh or SQLite needed. A 404 → 1; missing tokens or cost → 3 ("unknown", never 0).
- **`follow --server <url> --session <id> [--stall s]`:** `/global/event`, filtered to the session (the per-session stream is empty on this server, verified live). It prints tool, step-start and step-finish progress; consecutive identical lines are collapsed.
  - **Exits:** 0 on idle, 1 on an attributed error, 3 on a session-scoped stall (heartbeats and other sessions do not reset it), 1 on a drop after 3 reconnects 1 s apart.
  - It ends on the concluding frame itself, and aborts its socket on every exit.
- **`usage … --emit <logdir> <wave> <lane> <stage> [--event settled|failed]`:** appends the timing to the wave log through `scripts/wave-event.sh`, whose stderr and exit are relayed.
- **Safety:**
  - loopback hosts only (Node URL canonicalisation checked, including tricky forms);
  - a session-id regex;
  - ONE `get()`: GET-only, `redirect: "error"`, a pathname allowlist;
  - no dependency.
- **Docs:** "Watching a lane" in the pipeline doc.

## Verification

- **Mac:** 85/85 tests; 100% coverage on all 9 files; 3 mutations reproduced (allow any host; drop the stall timer; drop the session filter); typecheck clean.
- **Live, read-only, through the tunnel:**
  - `usage` read a real lane (3,305 s, 122k tokens in and out);
  - `follow` streamed a running lane's tool and step progress;
  - the fixed `follow` is also attached to a real fix-round session, to confirm it exits 0 on its own when that lane idles.
- **Fable:** row review (2 rounds, including a live server probe that found the per-session stream empty), brief review (2 rounds). Pre-merge review was changes-required: a concluding frame did not end the watch until the next frame arrived, and a short `--stall` misreported it as 3; null frames exited 2. Fixed in round 1, with open-stream regressions. The re-check cleared; 3 NITs deferred.

## Scope
- Make the 1 USDC entry path explicit and add a clearly fictional supplier-decision example with metadata-only and historical-proof limitations
- Expose only x402 challenge/settlement response headers; remove the invalid SDK request header without widening the request allowlist
- Distinguish completed, processing, failed and unknown delivery; prevent duplicate fresh payments with nonsecret durable state and cross-tab locking
- Preserve buyer-comprehension UI from #29 and repair mobile CSS/intro spacing
- Align existing pricing-authority assertions and make the Watch regression deterministic

## Verified
- Core full verify: pricing guards, generated types, typecheck, 64 tests, dry-run build
- Buyer full verify: manifest, typecheck, 61 tests, production build; repeated suite passes
- Independent source/release review and actual desktop + 400px phone-width cloud-browser QA passed
- Final preview: https://0d2192b6.delta-witness-app.pages.dev (f2c7fe761e66c6e3dd9bb81cd5418cb149025c6e)
- Production release run: https://github.com/15998194110/delta-witness/actions/runs/36798875560
- Release commit af9490276b8b5db5b8af532ee0d8e823343958ed has identical product-source hashes; release-only workflows remain on its dedicated branch
- Core active version 706c943b-c0e3-42c7-a662-5c3c2a6dcef0 and Pages deployment 9be54352-2d4c-42f3-8fd5-98c42598903f verified
- Live landing/docs, unsigned402 response headers, OPTIONS/CORS and canonical Base USDC amounts1/5/10 passed
- Existing bindings, routing, cron and observability settings preserved and rechecked; no migrations, secret updates, gateway or registry release

No wallet connection, signature, real payment or raw-artifact exposure was performed. Real settlement and paid fulfillment remain untested.

author: aeyakovenko
body:
Fixes #220.

## Problem
Since `94979ede`, a zero-conversion resolved source claim can only demote when `source_domain_terminal_for_haircut_demote` holds. For a Fresh or Empty bucket, that requires every *other* claimant's remaining claim in the domain to be zero, and no creditor leg to remain.

That deadlocks when the loser settles before the winners attribute their claims:
- the support gap is 0, so the loss goes to the junior residual pool and the bucket stays `Empty`;
- each winner's claim then blocks the other's close;
- an `Empty` bucket never expires, so time doesn't break it.

In the wrapper repros this locks about 1M atoms of user capital permanently.

## Fix
In `source_domain_terminal_for_haircut_demote`, treat the domain as terminal when all of these hold:
- the bucket is `Empty`;
- the market is `Resolved`;
- the domain's loss side (same asset) has `stored_pos_count`, `stale_account_count` and `pending_obligation_count` all 0.

While loss-side legs remain, the existing "others must be zero" guard still applies.

## Why it is safe
The guard in `94979ede` exists so a claim never gives up its senior share of backing that could still reach the domain. In Resolved mode, the only engine path that can fund a source domain is a loss-side leg crystallizing its K/F loss (`reserve_new_capital_backed_loss_for_source_domain_not_atomic`, which has one call site). Insurance credit reservation is compiled only under kani/fuzz.

So once those counts are zero, no backing can arrive and the senior claim is worth exactly 0. Demoting moves the face into the junior pool at the payout rate, so the claimant ends with the same amount or more. The existing burn-once/refine path is unchanged, so there is no double payment.

**Caveat:** provider top-ups (`TopUpBackingBucket`) are rejected in Resolved mode by the wrapper (`mode != 0`), not by the engine. If an engine-level top-up path in Resolved mode is ever added, this condition must be revisited. It may be worth asserting this in the engine as well.

## Tests
- New regression `v16_resolved_zero_conversion_coclaimants_on_empty_bucket_both_close` (`tests/v16_spec_tests.rs`):
  - setup: two longs against one short; the loser closes first; the bucket is asserted `Empty`;
  - fails before the fix (winner close errors), passes after;
  - pins exact payouts 1,005,000 / 1,005,000 / 1,990,000 and a final vault of 0.
- Engine:
  - `cargo test --locked`: 50 unit + 133 spec + others, 0 failed;
  - `--features fuzz`: 50 + 141 + 13/15/2/19/7, 0 failed.
- Wrapper (percolator-prog PR #452 branch, with this engine path-patched), modules inv_045/024/066/067/070/071/073: 350 tests.
  - Both inv_045 repros (`row425_matcher_handoffs…`, `fractional_positions_partition…`) now pass with their exact payout/residue assertions.
  - No new behavioral failures. The only new failures are 5 pin-guard tests, which fail by design under a path patch.

body:
The Explorer had scattered disaster context, fixture-only Kansas PLSS acquisition, and no governed Kansas knowledge or 1 km soil read path. This PR adds a disaster/BLM workspace with independent source controls and provider-verified BLM visibility scales, a bounded FEMA Kansas declaration layer, live paginated PLSS capture, a held knowledge projection with search and record pages, and a separate exact-day Crop-CASMA tile candidate. FEMA polygons are county designation locators, not disaster footprints; PLSS is a survey reference, not a parcel or title map. No source candidate is admitted or released.

The connector captured 2,360 Kansas townships, 82,466 sections, and 98,883 intersected divisions with matching provider counts before and after. An on-demand USGS GNIS capture preserved one Topeka source record as an unreleased candidate. The 2026-09-28 Crop-CASMA GeoTIFF was retained and prepared into 86 nearest-neighbor PNG tiles. Sampled Topeka and Kansas City points are source no-data, so the package declares partial coverage. The Site serves knowledge and soil only through reviewed D1 active pointers and SHA-256-checked R2 objects; no active pointer or package is installed by this PR.

The owner-private standalone Site candidate is preserved locally at `041f626585804e5c90b8075cc506aeff5333d3b1`, descended from Site source `75d749ed5711ab20e3edabeb1c6ba135417ec1c0` (deployed v131 at inspection). The repository mirror receipt verifies 283 file digests, including intentional water overlays. Connector output writes now pass through the existing local-data responsibility with immutable temporary or configured external raw destinations. The topology waiver evidence shrank only for the implemented NASS connector. Pillow was raised to 12.3.0 after CI flagged 11.3.0; the prepared candidate ID and all 86 tile digests were unchanged.

Validation at head `69bf686df1a`: standalone Site build and 248 tests passed; repository mirror build and 256 tests passed; both TypeScript checks passed; BLM/GNIS/NASS and tile tests passed; connector output gate, site mirror check, and trusted-base topology check passed locally. A local FEMA request returned 249 features with partial coverage; full Site npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities. The complete topology make target passed in an isolated Python 3.12 environment with its test dependencies. GitHub checks for this exact head completed with 113 successful and two skipped (`Trigger_APIsec_scan`, `scorecard`), with no failures; the skipped jobs do not establish test execution. The pinned Codex Security review of an earlier application diff reported no findings; an exact-head security review is still required. Browser acceptance was blocked by an unavailable admin security check.

Base: repository `fe47624f32d7f355f69309048f6624c4d64bdb98`. Hosted D1 migrations, R2 staging, source admission, rights/sensitivity decisions, independent review, activation, browser acceptance, rollback rehearsal, GLO records, additional disaster providers, and performance benchmarking remain separate gates. The currently deployed Site v131 and active storage are untouched. Code rollback is a revert of merge commit `a61f37bfc1107d1acfb6901393163df59d071836`; any future data activation must restore the previous approved pointer rather than modify immutable objects.

author: ducha-aiki
body:
Two defects in the deprecation helpers of `kornia/core/_compat.py`.

## The defects (run on `origin/main` 4df7b3040, macOS arm64, Python 3.11, torch 2.14.0 CPU)

**`@deprecated` on a class** replaced the class with a plain function (`class_wrapper`), although the docstring says "Works with classes too":

```text
type(OldCls).__name__        -> 'function'
isinstance(OldCls(), OldCls) -> TypeError: isinstance() arg 2 must be a type, a tuple of types, or a union
class Sub(OldCls)            -> TypeError: metaclass conflict: ...
OldCls.X                     -> AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'X'
OldCls.build()               -> AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'build'
```

No kornia class is decorated today (latent); `kornia.utils.ImageToTensor` works around it with a subclass.

**Doubled space.** `_emit_deprecation_warning` built `f" {extra_reason}"`, and every `extra_reason=" ..."` call site already starts with a space, so each of those warnings read `...deprecated in favor of `X`.  The ...`. Counted with an AST walk over `kornia/`: 40 `deprecated(..., extra_reason=...)` decorators (10 in `kornia/__init__.py`, 30 in `kornia/utils/__init__.py`) plus the 2 direct `_emit_deprecation_warning` calls in `kornia/utils/__init__.py` (`ImageToTensor`, `CachedDownloader`): 42 messages.

## The fix

A decorated class now stays the same class. The decorator wraps its `__init__`, so `isinstance`, subclassing, class attributes and classmethods work, and instantiation warns once, attributed to the caller (`stacklevel` unchanged). Copy and pickle do not run `__init__`, so they do not warn. The wrapped `__init__` behaves like the class did before the decoration:

- A class with its own `__init__` calls it, and `inspect.signature` of the class is unchanged (the wrapper carries `__wrapped__`, which `inspect` follows; this holds for every subclass that inherits it).
- A class without one hands on to the next `__init__` along the instance's MRO (`super(owner, self).__init__`), so a decorated mixin in `class C(Mixin, Base)` does not swallow `Base.__init__`. `owner` is the class that carries the wrapper, found by identity (a `@dataclass(slots=True)` above `@deprecated` re-creates the class), or the decorated class when something replaced the wrapper afterwards (a second decoration, a decorator above that wraps `__init__`); an object that is not an instance of the class gets the `__init__` the class had. When the next one is `object.__init__`, the class still rejects constructor arguments (`TypeError: X() takes no arguments`), and a class that customises `__new__` (a `tuple` subclass) still accepts them.
- Because another `__init__` may run under multiple inheritance, the wrapper of a class without its own `__init__` has no `__wrapped__`, and `inspect.signature` of that class is `(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None`: the undecorated class reported `()` or the inherited `__init__`'s signature, and a subclass of a builtin such as `dict`, `int`, `str` or `Exception` raised `ValueError`. A class with a `__new__` of its own keeps its `__new__` signature, which `inspect` prefers. A signature is therefore either the true one or the generic one, never a wrong concrete one.
- The wrapper takes the name, qualname, module and docstring of the `__init__` the class had; a C-level one such as `object.__init__` or `dict.__init__` gives `<Class>.__init__` in the class's module.
- A subclass whose `__init__` reaches the decorated class's warns too, naming the decorated class, at the subclass's `super().__init__()` line.

author: robzolkos
body: `basecamp connect` refused to run on a Mac: "The connector runs on Linux only, not darwin: … Linux is the only platform that seals the descriptors a process inherits". Most of us are on Macs, so most people couldn't connect an agent at all. That reason turned out not to be true. When the connector hands a worker its one-time token, it passes it on an inherited file descriptor. The CLI's first job at startup is to mark every inherited descriptor close-on-exec, so nothing it starts can pick the token up. It only did that on Linux. macOS can do the same: list `/dev/fd` and mark each one, exactly as the Linux fallback for older kernels already does with `/proc/self/fd`. I checked this on a Mac first. Without the marking, a child process could see the descriptor; with it, it couldn't. ## What changes - At startup on macOS, the CLI marks inherited descriptors close-on-exec by listing `/dev/fd`. If that can't be read, it refuses to start rather than guess which descriptors are open. - The token reader is built for macOS as well as Linux. The existing test that keeps sealing and token-reading paired on every platform we release for still holds them together. - `basecamp connect` runs on macOS. On other platforms it now says "Linux and macOS only". - The background service (hidden for now) stays Linux-only, since it writes a systemd unit. On a Mac it now says so in plain words. ## Found by running the connector's tests on a real Mac CI only runs the Go tests on Linux, so this was the first time they'd run on macOS. Three things came up, and the first two are real behaviour differences: - **macOS won't signal a process group whose only members are zombies.** That's a group of processes that have exited but haven't been cleaned up yet. Linux delivers the signal; macOS refuses with "operation not permitted". The connector took that refusal to mean the group might still be running, so it couldn't confirm a finished worker had gone. Now, when the system's own process list shows nothing in the group is running, it's treated as gone, the same as on Linux. A group that's still running but can't be signalled (another user's) still lists its members, and stays refused. - **macOS only names a socket's peer process while it's connected.** If a worker's MCP server closed before it read its token, the connector recorded an untrusted connection and gave up on that socket. Now it's "undelivered", as on Linux, and the server's next start gets the token. A different user is still refused. - **A test's fake worker crashed on macOS** before the test could run, because it blocked with an empty `select`. It sleeps now. ## Tried on a Mac - The connector's test suites, built for macOS and run on an Apple Silicon Mac: every connector package passes. One timing-sensitive token test failed once in its first ten runs, then passed in seventy runs after; I didn't catch why that first one failed. - Five general CLI tests (terminal detection, delete confirmations, bare `basecamp`, the setup wizard) fail on macOS on `main` too. They're unrelated to the connector and not touched here. - End to end, against a local Basecamp through an SSH tunnel: `auth agent connect`, `connect setup` and `connect doctor` all passed. The connector picked up a mention, boosted 👀, replied and completed the task. The worker was the e2e stand-in, because over SSH macOS keeps the Keychain locked and Claude Code reports itself logged out. --- ## Summary by cubic Lets `basecamp connect` run on macOS. Previously it refused to start on a Mac because the CLI only sealed inherited descriptors on Linux; macOS can seal its own by listing `/dev/fd`, so the token handover now works there. macOS always mounts `/dev/fd`, so if it can't be opened the CLI fails closed rather than guessing. The background service stays Linux-only since it writes a systemd unit, and now says so on a Mac. Fixes found by running the connector's tests on a real Mac: - macOS refuses to signal a process group whose only members are zombies; the connector now treats such a group as gone when the kernel's own process list shows nothing running. Linux behavior is unchanged. - A worker's MCP server that closed before its token was read is now recorded as "undelivered" instead of "refused", so its next start gets the token. - The token's recipient is now named from the trust check before the token is written, so a server that reads its token and closes at once still resolves to the right process instead of a reused pid. - A test's fake worker that blocked on an empty `select` (a runtime deadlock on macOS) now sleeps instead. Written for commit 352932e09b757212018db9abc393153a3ae0549d. Summary will update on new commits.

author: bengizmo
body:
Closes #697 (pyannote scope; whisper's torch moved to #701, synthdetect to #700).

## What changes
- **pyannote CPU image + native macOS venv: torch/torchaudio 2.5.0 to 2.8.0**, the version the CUDA image already runs. **scikit-learn 1.3.2 to 1.5.2** in the shared `requirements.txt` (all flavors). Clears Dependabot #7, #8, #9, #10 (critical) and #17.
- **`TORCH_FORCE_NO_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1`** in `Dockerfile.cpu` and the metal launcher's pyannote `service_env` (the CUDA Dockerfile already set it), and in the metal parity harness. torch >= 2.6 refuses the pyannote 3.1 checkpoints under its `weights_only` default.
- **`diarizer.load_model` names that setting** when torch refuses the checkpoints. Before, it reported "corrupt or incomplete vendored files, rebuild the image".
- **`release.yml` smoke-cpu prints pyannote's container stderr** (it was `docker logs pyannote 2>/dev/null`).
- Contracts: all three pyannote flavors on the same torch; the env var is pinned in every `services/pyannote/Dockerfile*` and in the launcher's pyannote arm; the launcher unit test and the new error-hint tests. Each was mutation-checked.

## Why the CPU image was stuck on 2.5.0
v0.36.1 reverted the CPU image to 2.5.0, citing a smoke startup timeout. That was a misdiagnosis. The exact v0.36.0 CPU image the smoke tested (digest `c64cde69...`, torch 2.8.0+cpu) exits at startup with `UnpicklingError: Weights only load failed`, and the smoke discarded the traceback. With the variable set, a torch 2.8.0 CPU build is healthy in about 10 s.

## Measured equivalence (maintainer hardware)
| Lane | Comparison | Result |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | parity corpus diarize: 0.44.0-cpu (torch 2.5.0, sklearn 1.3.2) vs torch 2.8.0 + sklearn 1.3.2 vs torch 2.8.0 + sklearn 1.5.2 | byte-identical to each other and to the committed CUDA reference |
| CUDA (RTX 5090) | rebuilt image (sklearn 1.5.2) vs committed `cuda/diarize.json` (Gate A diarize leg) | byte-identical |
| CUDA (RTX 5090) | released 0.47.0 vs rebuild, four 10-minute multi-speaker podcast excerpts (1 to 7 speakers, 9 to 81 turns) | byte-identical on all four |
| CPU | the same four excerpts, 0.44.0-cpu vs the new CPU image | running; result posted as a comment |

scikit-learn is imported when the pipeline loads, but a profiled diarization makes zero scikit-learn calls (pyannote 3.1.1 clusters with scipy).

Not measured here: **Gate M** (metal, needs Apple Silicon) and the arm64 CPU image (the release smoke runs it). uv resolves `requirements.metal.txt` for `aarch64-apple-darwin` and aarch64 Linux on Python 3.11.

## Security exposure, stated accurately
The scanners stop flagging CVE-2025-32434, CVE-2025-3730, CVE-2025-2953 and CVE-2024-5206 for the diarizer. In practice the default install changes little. pyannote never loads with `weights_only=True`, so the CVE-2025-32434 bypass never applied; its protection is that the vendored checkpoints are sha256-checked. The optional online HF path (`DIARIZER_MODEL_NAME`) has no such check, before or after this change. On 2.8.0 the metal manifest keeps #14, #15 and #16, which are fixed only in 2.9.1 or later and so unreachable while pyannote.audio 3.1.1 needs torchaudio's `set_audio_backend()`. #11, #12 and #13 have no upstream fix.

## Review
- **Code-review tier: high-risk** (inference-path dependencies, released images, a CI gate). Full panel: deepseek-v4-pro, grok-4.5, kimi-k3, qwen3.7-max (codex unavailable). No Critical findings. Applied and skipped findings, with reasons, are in commit `96a5319`.
- **Browser lane:** not triggered (no console or island change).
- Gates run locally: ruff, mypy, unit + contracts, parity (skips on Linux as designed).

body:
Radar's built-in audit (`/api/audit`) reports **443 findings** (389 warning, 54 danger) over 63 workloads in 21 namespaces. This PR clears the ones that are configurable in this repo.

## What changes

**Own manifests (`apps/*`)** — 16 files
- `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on every workload that doesn't call the API (kept on `hermes` and `omnigent`, which do)
- `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on every non-privileged container
- readiness/liveness probes where missing — endpoints checked against the running services (`/api/health` on pantrywise-server, `/health` on rustfs, `/api/healthz` on forgejo, `/api/v1/info` on netdata, `/status` on the bitwarden bridge, `pg_isready`/`redis-cli ping` elsewhere)
- CPU limits where absent; `glance` and `netalertx` pinned to the digest of the build they already run

**Helm values (`infra/argocd-apps/*`)** — 6 Applications
- cert-manager: resources on controller/webhook/cainjector
- external-secrets: resources on all three components plus the liveness/readiness the chart disables by default (enabling readiness starts the `--live-addr` health server the probes target)
- opencost: `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` + CPU limits on both containers (values live under `exporter`/`ui`)
- kube-prometheus-stack: config-reloader resources and probes via the operator's `--config-reloader-*` / `--enable-config-reloader-probes` flags, plus node-exporter resources and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`
- tailscale-operator: operator resources/securityContext, and `proxyConfig.defaultProxyClass: tailscale-proxy-hardened`
- caretta: `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on grafana and victoria-metrics

**New `apps/tailscale-ingress/proxyclass.yaml`** — a cluster-scoped ProxyClass giving all 16 operator-generated `ts-*` proxies resource limits and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` (48 findings).

**ArgoCD install (`infra/argocd`)** — kustomize patches: resources on all seven components, and the four probes upstream doesn't define (TCP on ports verified open: 7000 applicationset, 9001 notifications, 8082 application-controller).

- `kustomize build` passes for the root, every `apps/*`, and `infra/argocd`

## Deliberately not addressed

- **Intrinsic**: hostNetwork/hostPID/hostPath/privileged findings on netdata, netalertx, dnsmasq, caretta and node-exporter — those are what the workload is
- **Needs per-image work**: `runAsRoot` (76), `readOnlyRootFs`, replica counts (single-node cluster, and RWO PVCs)

author: botchkin2
body:
Upstream half of the lap-0 problem (steward #1462, after #188 fixed the surface downstream).

**Evidence (production, API traces):** a race's lap 0 is `timed`, `comparable` and `start`, but its segment is the parked car, not a lap. Sebring 574eec6c lap 0: 5,181 ticks (52 s) at LapDistPct 0 with a frozen position, then the distance ramps ~480 m per tick up to the grid slot's place on the lap (0.83 of the lap), then ~850 m of rolling to the line. `distanceM` still reads 5,747 m, so `analyze.mjs` builds that lap's 5 m grid (it passes the 90 % test): the parked car stretched over 83 % of the lap. Effect on the stored band with few comparable laps (mid-lap speed minimum of p50 / p10): Imola d04f8a41 (1 comparable) 0 / 0, Sebring 574eec6c (2) 35 / 7, Silverstone d57fd0fd (2) 39 / 8, against 74 / 65 on Daytona with 29 comparable laps. Daytona's grid is at 67 %: its lap 0 opens there with no jump. The track map (`buildTrackMap`) only takes laps within 1 % of the best lap's distance; these laps are 1.1-6.9 % short, so the map was not touched (Sebring 574eec6c is the closest at 1.1 %).

**Fix:** `tools/sessions/gridLap.mjs` `jumpsOffTheGrid(dist)`: true when the lap distance trace opens more than 100 m along the lap or rises more than 100 m in one tick (a 100 Hz tick at 100 m/s is 1 m; a 10 Hz one 10 m). `analyzeLap` sets `partial: seg.partial || jumpsOffTheGrid(dist)`, so consistency, best, band, surface and the app's reasons already exclude it with no app type change.

**Checked against production traces (rebuilt the distance as the app does):**
- All 8 comparable lap 0s: 7 flagged. The 8th (Sebring 6121da91, 413 s) sits still at the line for 93 s and then drives a normal lap with no jump; it stays a lap on purpose (test included).
- One more caught that nobody was looking for: Imola practice d184d6e1 lap 1 is a 1.4 s file-boundary sliver (144 ticks, first LapDistPct 0.982) carrying a 134.7 s game lap time, comparable, in that session's median.
- 657 other comparable laps (every lap number <= 2, after reset, start, plus a random 10 %): 0 flagged.

**Version:** #195 is on main, so the rule has its own key: `blockVersions.gridLap = GRID_LAP_VERSION` (1, in `gridLap.mjs` with what version 1 means). The sync fingerprint hashes the table, so the next sync re-analyses every session once and lap docs get `partial: true` on the grid starts. `analysisVersion` stays 17.

**Verification:** `node --test tools/sessions/*.test.mjs`: tests 141, pass 141, fail 0 (7 new in `gridLap.test.mjs`: rolling lap, standing start from the line, the Sebring ramp, Daytona's mid-lap open, the limit itself, empty traces). Not run: jest/tsc/lint (no `src/` change). Not run: the real analyzer on a `.duckdb` (traces checked through the API).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Update after review (steward #1490)

1. **Full population, not a sample.** All 3,686 production laps (2,162 comparable), distance rebuilt from each trace as the app does: **256 flagged, 8 of them comparable**: the 7 lap-0 parked starts (Daytona x2, Imola, Silverstone, Sebring x3) and the Imola 1.4 s sliver (d184d6e1 lap 1). The other 248 are already excluded (untimed or non-comparable); the rule only adds `partial` to them. No other comparable lap changes.
2. **`partialWhy`**: `'grid' | 'file' | null` on the lap doc and `Lap.partialWhy` in the app. 'grid' needs the jump AND a parked start (distance still for 10 s or more at the start); otherwise a jump is 'file', as is any other cut lap. Run on the 256: parked starts are not only race grids: 70 practice/qualify laps and post-reset laps start parked in the garage and read the same, so the app says **PARK** / "Parked start" / "Starts parked (the grid or the garage), so this is the roll to the line, not a lap." instead of GRID, and not PART. Tests in `gridLap.test.mjs` and `session/model.test.ts`.
3. Segment duration vs game lap time (steward's follow-up) is not in this PR.

author: asubbarao
body:
## What

quackapi already compressed responses with zstd and gzip. This PR fixes how it picks between them and lets operators choose a policy.

- `compression := 'auto' | 'gzip' | 'zstd' | 'off'` on `quackapi_serve`, plus `SET quackapi_compression`. The default is `auto`, so behaviour stays on by default. The old booleans still work: `true` means `auto` and `false` means `off`.
- Negotiation follows the client's q-values. The highest q wins, and zstd wins ties. Before this change, q-values were parsed but zstd won whenever it was accepted at all. q-values outside 0–1 are treated as 0.
- `Vary: Accept-Encoding` is sent on every response that could have been compressed, including when the client got identity. Previously it was sent only when compression happened, so a cache could serve one representation in place of the other.
- The `compression_min_bytes` default goes from 256 to 1024 bytes. Below about 1 KB, compression saves little and costs CPU.
- New `docs/guide/compression.md`. `coming-soon.md`, `FEATURE_STATUS.md` and the function reference were updated to say compression has shipped.

## Validation

- Release build, plus `test/sql/quackapi_compression.test`: 5/5 assertions pass (mode setting, threshold, invalid mode rejected, legacy boolean).
- `test/ultra/test_compression.sh` ran with curl against a live server for gzip, zstd, both, q-value preference, neither, below-threshold and SSE (not compressed). It round-trip decompressed the gzip and zstd bodies.
- `make format-ci-check` passes.
- Full local suite: 29/32. The 3 failures are `json_schema` not being available locally (2 tests) and one flaky HTTP pool counter. None of them touch compression. CI on this PR is the authoritative run.

## Not in this PR

- A per-route opt-out.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes to the shop/tool location-mapping feature (previously PR #227), found while testing on dev:

- **Nested marker drift**: a location nested 2+ levels deep (e.g. a tool inside a cabinet inside a room) could resolve outside its grandparent's real boundary. The 5%-of-parent visual crop padding was leaking into how stored coordinates get interpreted, and that padding compounds at every nesting level -- for a small child, it can be a large fraction of its own size. Padding now only affects the visual crop; click/drag math and coordinate resolution both operate in the true unpadded parent frame.
- **Zoomed-parent outline drawn in the wrong place/scale**: the "you are here" outline shown while zoomed into an empty location traced its points directly into the zoomed view's 0-100 frame instead of remapping them through the same padded crop the viewBox itself uses, producing a tiny misplaced rectangle instead of tracing the room on screen.
- **Zoomed container outline** (new): while zoomed into a location with nothing placed inside it yet, its own outline is now drawn so the screen isn't blank.
- **"Place on map" shortcut** (new): a button on the Tools tab jumps straight to the right shop on the Map tab, preselecting that tool in the "place a specific tool here" picker.
- **Orphaned tool markers**: picking the same tool twice in "place a specific tool here" could create two Location records with the same name, only one actually linked to the tool. Fixed two causes -- a silent failure in the tool-link call that closed the modal before confirming the link succeeded, and the picker offering tools that are already placed elsewhere.

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` on changed files (pre-existing unrelated `@capacitor` errors only)

author: finkeflo
body:
## Goal
One fetch job at a time no matter who starts it, and a history of what ran — also across restarts.

## Changes
- `FetchService` (one instance per app in `app.state.fetch`, injected into routes and the scheduler) replaces the module-level job state: `start()` checks and starts **under an `asyncio.Lock`** and raises `JobAlreadyRunning`; the task handle is kept; `request_cancel()`, `shutdown()`, SSE `event_stream()`. Before, the scheduler checked for a running job, awaited database calls and only then set the job, so a manual start in that window ran a second, invisible job.
- The scheduler starts jobs through the service and sets `last_run_at` only once its job has actually started (a schedule beaten by a manual start is retried on the next tick).
- **Run history** — migration 0005 replaces the never-written `fetch_runs` table: `id` (job id), `trigger` (`manual` | `demo` | `schedule:<id>`), `params` (JSON), `status` (`running|done|error|cancelled|interrupted`), `started_at`/`finished_at` (UTC), `files_total`, `files_done`, `rows_imported`, `warnings`, `errors`, `error`. Written at start, every 10 s while running, and at the end; the newest 1000 runs are kept. Runs still `running` at start-up, or cut off by a shutdown, become `interrupted`.
- `GET /api/fetch/runs?limit=20` (1–200) and `GET /api/fetch/runs/{id}` (404 if unknown). `/api/fetch`, `/status`, `/cancel` and `/stream` keep their contract.
- A job ends through `finish()`, which records the run before the job shows as ended (status, SSE), so a client that saw the end always finds the final run (first CI run caught this race; regression test added).
- SSE subscriber queues are bounded (1000 events; a subscriber that stops reading loses its oldest events).

## Test evidence
- New `tests/test_fetch_runs.py` (9 tests): finished run with all fields and counters; error / failed token / cancelled / demo runs with triggers and statuses; **5 concurrent `POST /api/fetch` → exactly one job** and one run; 10 concurrent `FetchService.start()` → one job, nine `JobAlreadyRunning`; progress saved while running; runs left `running` → `interrupted` on start; shutdown during a fetch → `interrupted` with `finished_at`; listing order, limit bounds, pruning, 404; bounded SSE queue.
- Full suite: 265 passed, 8 xfailed (repeated runs; timing-sensitive modules 30×). ruff, mypy clean.
- Test instance: demo import through the UI with Playwright (no console errors), `GET /api/fetch/runs` shows the demo run (1803 rows, files 1/1); fetch against a separate fake CPI server process: 3606 rows, second run 0.

author: gbresearch
body:
yadro now builds and passes its tests on Linux with GCC and Clang at `-std=c++23`, through a new `Makefile`, alongside the existing Visual Studio build.

## Makefile

```
make -j8                         # GCC, release
make -j8 TOOLCHAIN=clang         # clang++
make -j8 CXX=g++-14 CONFIG=debug
make -j8 WERROR=1                # warnings are errors, as in the VS projects
make test                        # build and run the tests (TEST_ARGS="..." passes options)
make check-headers               # Linux counterpart of tools/check_headers.ps1, at -Wall -Wextra -Werror
make help
```

- Builds `libyadro.a` and `yadro_test` from the same sources as `vs/yadro.vcxproj` and `vs/yadro_test.vcxproj`.
- Outputs go to `lib/`, `exe/` and `obj/` as with VS, under `<os>-<compiler>/<Config>` (e.g. `lib/linux-g++-14/Release`), so compilers and configurations coexist.
- Flags: `-std=c++23 -mavx2 -mfma -Wall -Wextra -pthread`, linking `-lstdc++exp` for `std::stacktrace`.
- AXE is used automatically when `../axe/include` exists (as in the VS projects); `AXE_INCLUDE=`/`AXE=0|1` override. Without it, `make test` says so and the JSON parsing tests are reported as DISABLED.
- Stops with a clear message for compilers that are too old: requires **GCC 14+**, or **Clang 20+** with libstdc++ 14+. Clang 18 can't use libstdc++'s `std::expected`; Clang 19 rejects C++23 constant expressions on references (P2280) used in `tensor.h`; libc++ has no `<stacktrace>`.
- Command-line `CXXFLAGS`/`LDFLAGS` add to the required flags (e.g. sanitizers) instead of replacing them.

## Library fixes

Mostly missing standard includes (MSVC's headers pull them in indirectly) and code MSVC accepts but GCC or Clang reject: missing `template` keywords, a shadowed template parameter, a concept used without its argument, deduction guides with non-deducible parameters, deduced return types used before definition, a coroutine defined before its return type is complete. A few were real bugs:

- `pareto_set`'s constructor never expanded its argument pack.
- `GB_TIMER` passed a runtime string to `printf` as the format, so a `%` in the output would be misread.
- `scheduler.h` used a lambda as the priority-queue comparator, which gives the member a different type in each translation unit; it now uses a named comparator.
- `epoch_manager` grew a `vector` of atomics (not movable); it now uses a `deque`.
- The only `std::from_range` use was replaced with an equivalent constructor, since libstdc++ only has it from GCC 15.

Library headers and sources are clean at `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` on both compilers. GCC's `-Winterference-size` is silenced locally where `hardware_destructive_interference_size` is used on purpose.

## Tests that can't run are reported as DISABLED

`util/gbtest.h` gains `GB_TEST_IF(condition, suite, name[, launch_policy])`: the test is registered disabled unless its constant condition holds, so the run reports it as `DISABLED` instead of passing an empty body.

- 36 JSON parsing tests (`json_test.cpp`, `container_test.cpp`) require `json_parser_axe_enabled` or `gbdb_json_axe_enabled`. `gbdb_json_reader_is_opt_in_test` stays a plain `GB_TEST`, since it checks the reader's failure without AXE.
- 35 tests of Windows-only facilities (`util_test.cpp`) require `on_windows`, and `fiber_test` requires `fibers_implemented`. Their bodies keep their `#if defined(GBWINDOWS)` so they compile everywhere.
- `make check-headers` and `tools/check_headers.ps1` compile `GB_TEST_IF` with and without a policy, as they do for `GB_TEST`.
- On Windows with AXE every condition holds, so the VS run is unchanged.

## Other test changes (worth a review)

- **`async_test_loop` deadlocked on a 4-core machine.** `then()` waits for a `std::shared_future` dependency by holding a worker in a blocking `get()`, and the test registers 40 such waits; with 4 workers all of them blocked while the tasks they waited for were still queued. The test now uses `4 * iterations + 1` threads. This would hang the same way on a 4-thread Windows machine.
- **Serialization md5.** The digest included an `unordered_map`, whose serialized bucket count and iteration order are chosen by the standard library. MSVC's 8 buckets and order 1, 2, 3 reproduce the old digest exactly; libstdc++ uses 13 buckets and 3, 2, 1. The map is now left out of the digest (the size check still covers it), and the expected digest changed (`a5d36bf4...`, the same on GCC and Clang).
- **Deterministic GA seed.** The GA draws from standard-library distributions, whose algorithms differ per library, and GCC's FMA contraction changes rounding. Seed 20 misses the target without contraction, so GCC and Clang use seed 22, which reaches it in 30–33 generations in every floating-point mode tried. MSVC keeps seed 20.
- `gbassert_eq` prints a `std::vector` only where the library formats ranges (`__cpp_lib_format_ranges`; libstdc++ from GCC 15), so the expectation depends on that macro.
- `named_resource_lock`'s test checks on other platforms that `acquire` throws. MSVC-only pragmas are guarded.

The test makefile rules silence benign "unused" warnings and two known GCC false positives (`-Wmismatched-new-delete` for the test's own `operator new`/`delete`, and `-Warray-bounds`/`-Wstringop-overflow` on a one-element vector copy) for the test sources only.

## Testing

- GCC 14.2 and Clang 20.1 (libstdc++ 14), debug and release, all with `WERROR=1`, without AXE: every build reports **252 passed, 0 failed, 74 disabled** (70 by `GB_TEST_IF`, plus the driver's 4: the three Windows pipe tests and `bounded_priority_queue_test`). That is the same 326 registered tests as before; earlier runs reported 322 passed only because 70 empty bodies counted as passes.
- `make check-headers`: 58/58 translation units with both compilers.
- Selecting a disabled test by name (e.g. `--test json.json_events_basic_test`) reports it `DISABLED`.

**Not verified:**
- **MSVC.** I couldn't build with Visual Studio. The changes are meant to be neutral there (new pragmas are GCC-guarded, `GB_TEST_IF` conditions all hold, MSVC keeps its seed and its range-format expectation), but please run the VS build and `tools\check_headers.ps1` once.
- **With AXE.** AXE wasn't available, so the 36 AXE tests weren't run on Linux.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Make the deterministic GA reproducible across standard libraries (own distributions).
- Fix the thread pool's `shared_future` starvation in the library itself.
- Implement the fiber simulator on POSIX (e.g. `ucontext`).

body:
The eight Blocktave fixes from Mr. Graham's playtest.

## What changed
1. **Pickup labels.** Every gain shows the item's icon and "+1 Maple" over the player's head. The text drifts up and fades. Gains of the same item close together count up in one label, and at most 4 labels show at once. Screen readers hear the same words through the `aria-live` region `#btLive`. INSTRUMENT mode's bonus shows in the number ("+2 Tone Shard").
2. **Item tooltips.** Every item tile (hotbar, inventory, Band Locker, Recipe Book, the Measure's slots and materials) has a tooltip. It opens on hover, keyboard focus or a touch long-press. It shows the item's name and its new one-line `desc` from recipes.js. Materials add "Found: …" and tools add "Can mine: …". The tooltip stays on screen and never covers its item, and it opens through `UI.layer`.
3. **No more dashed reach circle.** A block in reach gets the hover/aim highlight. Tapping a block out of reach outlines it faintly in red and shows "Too far: walk closer!" (throttled).
4. **THE MEASURE is now a wooden crafting station.** It has 4 big labeled slots (1st–4th) with ✕ to remove, an arrow to a RESULT box (the item, its count and the performance, e.g. "Play 1 note" or "Concert B♭ scale"), and MAKE IT, which stays disabled until a recipe matches. Materials go in by tap or drag. Slots show 2 × 2 at ≤ 760 px. In the Recipe Book, tapping a recipe fills the slots when you have the items, else shows what's missing in red. Recipe matching (`BT_RECIPES` + `match()`) is unchanged.
5. **Accidentals no longer crowd noteheads.** `spaceNotes` gives every note its own room, plus extra in front of a ♯/♭/♮. This covers every note card, Scale Veins, "Name this scale" and the Conductor's Podium. Cards widen when needed (`.bt-card.wide`).
6. **The swing.** Mining, tapping a creature or passing a block's challenge turns the avatar toward the target and arcs the tool for its tier. A wrong answer gives no swing. A broken block throws a few chips in its color.
7. **The poof.** A calmed creature shrinks into a soft cloud with notes floating up (never a flash) and plays the new sound `bt-poof` (falls back to `bt-calm`).
8. **World drops with a pickup radius.**
   - Mined blocks and calmed creatures drop real items on the ground. Each drop arcs out, lands on solid ground and bobs.
   - Drops within 1.5 tiles are picked up. Within 2.5 tiles they glide toward you first.
   - With a full bag (24 different items), the drop stays on the ground and "Bag full!" shows.
   - A drop off screen despawns after 10 minutes; one you can see never does.
   - At most 80 drops: the oldest beyond that joins the nearest drop of its kind, so nothing is lost.
   - Milestones still count at the moment a creature is calmed.

Reduced motion / the MOTION switch: no swing, chips, poof or drifting text. Drops sit still.

## Data and format
- Every new number is in `blocktave/rules.js`.
- The world save is now v2 and keeps the drops. A v1 save loads with none.
- New wood tokens `--bt-wood*` / `--bt-slot-bg` in theme.css.
- `bt-poof` is added to sounds.js and shared/sounds/README.md.
- CLAUDE.md's Blocktave section is updated.

## Tests
`tests/blocktave.spec.js` adds tests for:
- labels, including the instrument bonus
- tooltips
- reach
- the swing and poof, and reduced motion
- the Measure, including drag, the book and its layout at 4 screen sizes
- card staffs for every member × scale
- drops: magnet, full bag, save/reload, despawn, cap
- loading a v1 save

In Chromium locally:
- Blocktave + arcade-exit: 53 passed (1 perf test skipped)
- Blocktave game run + smoke: passed
- Sound Board: passed
- 43 fps at 4× CPU throttle

WebKit runs in CI.

Note: material tiles are `touch-action: none` so they can be dragged. On a phone, scrolling the materials panel has to start between tiles.

author: davidobando
body:
Fixes #4584.

## gsc correction

`KnownAttributes.IsKnownRuntimeAttribute` matched `[UnscopedRef]`, `[ScopedRef]` and `RefSafetyRules` by comparing the candidate's assembly name and public key token with the **host** type's assembly, `System.Private.CoreLib`. An SDK build binds the `System.Runtime` reference assembly instead, which has a different name and key. So gsc rejected a genuine `@UnscopedRef` and reported `GS0589` on struct members that return a reference to their own state. This was the compile failure in the self-migration of `test/Core.Tests`. The root cause is in gsc, not cs2gs.

The fix accepts a candidate when both it and the expected type come from a known BCL identity, matched by name (case-insensitive) **and** public key token:

| Assembly | Public key token |
| --- | --- |
| System.Private.CoreLib | 7cec85d7bea7798e |
| System.Runtime | b03f5f7f11d50a3a |
| mscorlib | b77a5c561934e089 |
| netstandard | cc7b13ffcd2ddd51 |

A same-named assembly with a different key is still rejected (ADR-0084 L5).

## Wider effect

The same identity check covers `@ScopedRef` and the module-level `RefSafetyRules` attribute. In SDK builds, imported modules whose `RefSafetyRules` resolves to System.Runtime are now recognized as using the C# 11 ref-safety rules, and their explicit `scoped` parameters are honored; before this change gsc treated them as legacy. That includes the BCL and any third-party library built for .NET 7 or later. Ref-safety diagnostics on calls to imported members can therefore change in SDK builds.

Self-migration check: with this change, the migrated `test/Core.Tests` compiles (no GS0589) and passes ILVerify. Test parity is 10652/10653; the one failure is #4589 (PR #4596). Validation run `2026-10-01T02-03-37Z_f73ff5`. Reaching compile also needed a local workaround for the separately tracked GS0547 regression #4556. Host-closure test runs already used the updated rules, so this brings SDK builds in line with what the tests exercise.

Unchanged: libraries targeting netstandard2.0 or pre-.NET 7 carry a compiler-synthesized `RefSafetyRules` attribute defined in their own assembly. gsc still does not recognize it, the same as before.

## Tests (ADR-0154)

`Issue4584UnscopedRefReferenceAssemblyTests` binds annotated and unannotated members against both the host closure and the targeting-pack reference closure. It also checks that a fake `UnscopedRefAttribute` in an unsigned assembly named `System.Runtime` is not recognized.

Without the fix, `AnnotatedMembers_DoNotReportGS0589(<ref pack>)` fails. I confirmed this by reverting the source change locally and, separately, by running the test file on origin/main.

author: roed-math
body:
This PR evaluates the upper-triangular contributions in Layer 11's milestone (viii), "the contribution of every conjugacy type," by proving that upper-triangular substitution on degree-`w` binary forms has Dickson trace `P_{w+2}(a+d,ad)` and by computing the exact `1`, `1/2`, `1/6`, or `0` coefficient of Popa--Zagier's explicit element.

The new contribution theorem combines those calculations for every canonical representative in `FixedDetMatrices.reps n`. A small supporting lemma exposes that monomial-basis coordinates are polynomial coefficients, so the triangular trace proof uses the existing homogeneous-monomial basis rather than introducing another model.

This is the most direct current step on the level-one trace-formula frontier recorded in `ModularForms/STATUS.md`: it evaluates the remaining upper-triangular terms needed by the algebraic trace calculation without overlapping the open period-map or modular-symbol work.

After this PR, Layer 11 still needs the remaining conjugacy-type sums and their assembly with the Hurwitz class-number term, followed by the period-polynomial transfer to the final Eichler--Selberg trace formula.

author: google-labs-stitch[bot]
body:
## Summary
This PR implements symmetrical counter-deposit bonds for task posters and task workers, fixed 20-point bond staking for community jurors, and complete slash pool redistribution upon dispute resolution.

## Key Changes
1. **Symmetrical Deposit Bonds & 48h Counter-Deposit Window**:
   - Both initiating and non-initiating parties (task poster / task worker) must deposit matching security bonds (`max(50, 20% reward)`).
   - If the counter-party fails to post matching collateral within 48 hours, the system auto-resolves the dispute in favor of the raiser via `resolve_expired_disputes`.
   - Logged new transaction type `dispute_counter_deposit` in `RewardLedger`.

2. **Community Juror Fixed-Bond Staking**:
   - Authenticated non-party users can vote on open disputes with active counter-deposits by locking a fixed 20-point stake (`juror_stake`).
   - Recorded juror votes in `DisputeVote` table (`dispute`, `voter`, `choice`, `stake`, `status`).
   - Direct task counterparties (`posted_by` / `taken_by`) are prevented from voting.
   - Enforced an 11-vote capacity cap per dispute to limit stake inflation.

3. **Total Slash Pool Redistribution**:
   - Upon dispute resolution, the winning party receives their deposit bond back plus the losing party's forfeited deposit bond, alongside task completion/cancellation point settlements.
   - Minority jurors lose 100% of their 20-point stake with ledger entry `juror_slash`.
   - Majority jurors receive their 20-point stake back plus an equal pro-rata share of all slashed minority stakes with ledger entry `juror_reward`.

4. **Testing & Audit Trail**:
   - Added unit tests in `SymmetricalFixedBondStakingTests` verifying counter-deposit submission, 48h default resolution, juror voting cap, and majority/minority pool redistribution.
   - Generated database migration `0044_dispute_counter_bond_deadline_and_more.py`.

author: lev0398
body:
## What broke

At 00:13 UTC on 2026-10-01 `Backend: Test (shard 1/4)` began failing on every pull request:

```
Failed EfCoreDashboardTrendAndDonutTests
       .GetDashboardAsync_MonthRangeStartsAtTheFirstOfTheMonthAndSpacesBucketsWeekly
Shouldly.ShouldAssertException : dto.Trend.Count
```

It is not a flake. The Fact asserted `dto.Trend.Count.ShouldBeGreaterThan(1)`, and the Month range
produces a second bucket only from the 8th. The previous author chose that deliberately, to avoid
passing hollowly when the spacing loop has nothing to iterate, and said so in the docstring.

The cost was not costed: **the backend shard fails for the first seven days of every month**, so
every open pull request is blocked from the 1st to the 7th. It was passing on PRs that ran before
UTC midnight and failing on everything after.

## The change

The bucket count is arithmetic, not luck. `BuildTrendAsync` steps seven days from the window start
while the bucket start is still before now, so on any day the count is `((now - monthStart).Days / 7) + 1`.
Asserting that pins the window on all 28-31 days instead of only on 24 of them, and the failure
message still names the day of the month.

## What this does NOT fix, measured rather than assumed

**Bucket width is still unpinned on the 1st to the 7th.** I widened the service's buckets from seven
days to six and this test stayed green, because with one bucket the loop only checks that it starts
at the origin, which holds at any width. The docstring now states that instead of implying coverage
it does not have.

So the failure mode changed and the coverage did not. That is the honest summary.

## The real fix, not attempted here

`DashboardAppService` reads `DateTime.UtcNow` in five places with no clock seam, which the test
class docstring already called out. ABP's `IClock` is injected in `BookingPolicyValidator`,
`CaseTrackerDeadLetterAppService` and `CaseTrackerMissingIntakeAppService` today, so the pattern is
established. With it substituted, this Fact could pin the 20th of a fixed month and check spacing
every day of the year. That is a change to a production service and does not belong in an unblock.

## Verification

- `EfCoreDashboardTrendAndDonutTests`: 6 passed, run at 1 October UTC, which is the exact condition
  that was failing.
- Mutation: service bucket width 7 to 6 days leaves it green today (recorded above as the gap);
  the count assertion itself fails if the derived figure is wrong.

author: sjormz
body:
## Summary
JaneT now uses one model: **Workspaces → Workspace → Project → Terminals** and **Library → Library entry → Project → Terminals**. Sessions no longer exist; every sidebar entry is a project.

- **New project** (`Ctrl+Shift+T` / `Cmd+T`, formerly "New terminal tab") opens Add project for the current Workspace or Library entry. The keybinding schema moves to 3, and customized keys are kept.
- **Add terminals to current project** is a new action with the default ``Ctrl+Shift+` `` on all platforms (VS Code's new-terminal key; xterm.js sends nothing for it). It is also in the command palette.
- **Git worktrees open as Library projects** with the **w** badge. If the repository is in the Library, the worktree becomes a project under that Library entry. Otherwise JaneT creates a new Library entry for the worktree folder. Renaming one changes only its label, and Remove project… never touches files.
- **The main process enforces the safety rules.**
  - Delete or keep by project requires `isProject === true`.
  - Library (folder) groups and any folder with a `.git` file (worktree or submodule) can never be recycled.
  - Folder renames are limited to Workspace folders and folders owned by a project. A folder that contains a Library entry, or is a worktree, is never renamed.
- **Saved sessions are migrated once**, without touching disk (`src/shared/sessionMigration.ts`).
  - A session merges into the project in the same group whose folder matches, then the deepest project folder that contains it, then the first project.
  - A worktree session becomes a Library project.
  - A group with no project turns its session into the project.
  - The 64-terminal limit is respected, keeping the project's own terminals first.
- **Wording:** user-facing text says New/Previous/Next project, Rename project, Collapse/Show workspace list and Project tools. The word "session" is removed from the UI and docs.

## Docs
- **Guides:** the workspaces guide is rewritten. Getting started, terminals, source control, shortcuts and the other guide pages are updated, plus the README.
- **Shortcut audit:** an addendum explains the Add terminals key choice.
- **Screenshots:** refreshed; there is one new image, `worktree-library-project.png`.

## Verification (Windows 11)
- `npm run typecheck`: pass
- `npm test`, Node v24.19.0: 89 files, 1233 passed, 22 skipped
  - The first full run had 1 failure in `releaseTooling` (the node-pty Windows worker path test). It passed when run on its own, and the next full run passed completely, so it looks like a timeout under load.
- `npm test`, Node v22.23.3: 1233 passed, 22 skipped (run by the agent)
- `npm run build`: pass
- `npm run docs:check`: pass
- Full Playwright run: 53 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed (run by the agent, before the final label-only commit)

**Not run natively:** macOS and Linux.

## Judgment calls for review
1. **First-project fallback.** In a Workspace that already has projects, a session merges into the first project even when its folder is a direct child that has no project of its own.
2. **Projects that own no folder.** A Workspace session that can neither be merged nor matched to a folder becomes a label-only project, not dropped.
3. **Worktree detection at startup** reads only `<cwd>/.git` (a `gitdir: …/worktrees/…` pointer). It never runs Git.
4. **Default `../` worktrees live inside the workspace folder.** Their Library entry then blocks deleting or renaming that workspace until the entry is removed.
5. **macOS uses a Control chord** for Add terminals, as VS Code does, because `Cmd+backtick` is reserved by macOS.
6. **Submodules are protected too.** The main process also refuses to delete or rename folders that are submodules.

JSON may contain escaped lone UTF-16 surrogates. Source/Search/QA response IDs previously accepted them, but Search-result and QA-citation link rendering calls encodeURIComponent, which throws. The existing shared ID schema now checks encodability without transforming the input. Its nonblank/512-code-unit limits, exact request identity, source/citation semantics and public field sets remain intact. Valid Unicode, paired emoji, combining sequences, percent signs and reserved characters are preserved, with the existing navigation encoding. Malformed responses reach the current validation-error UI before offering unsafe links/return actions. Existing QA session restoration reuses the same schema and discards malformed cached citation identities.

## Evidence and scope
Fifteen API and three actual-client/UI regressions failed before repair; six positive cases already passed. Final local suite: 355 web tests, TypeScript, 14 archive tests and 6 architecture checks pass. Independent read-only review reran all 26 focused API/cache/UI tests, confirmed actual encoded navigation and cached QA removal, and found no blocker in the exact six-file frozen diff.

Production change is only the shared response ID refinement. Other files are original synthetic regression fixtures/tests, source-delivery documentation and one explicit archive-doc allowlist entry. No textbook/private asset, backend migration, ranking change, paid API/model call, npm audit transmission, main merge or deployment.

author: copilot
body:
The Implementation Planner's step 1 optimizes for splitting without considering cohesion, resulting in over-granular task fragmentations that multiply review overhead. The issue observed 30 independently-reviewed units requiring 3–4 review cycles each, when tightly-coupled work should have remained together.

## Changes

**Modified `plugins/neo-core/agents/neo.implementation-planner.agent.md`**

Procedure step 1 now includes cohesion-bounded guidance:

- **Cohesion metric**: Units merge if they would necessarily change together when either's underlying contract, identity, or data model changes
- **One-PR principle**: Aligns with existing Technical Engineer guidance; prefer one-PR-sized units over many narrowly-scoped ones
- **Split threshold**: Clarifies that extra units cost a full implement→review cycle; only split when pieces are genuinely independently reviewable and independently valuable

### Example

Before:
```
1. Derive the smallest set of discrete units that satisfy every acceptance criterion. 
   Each unit is either a **feature/fix** or a **test** — never both.
```

After:
```
1. Derive the smallest set of discrete units that satisfy every acceptance criterion, 
   bounded by cohesion. Each unit is either a **feature/fix** or a **test** — never both. 
   **Merge units that would necessarily change together** whenever either's underlying contract, 
   identity, or data model changes — a fix to one almost certainly requires revisiting the other. 
   Prefer one-PR-sized units over many narrowly-scoped ones; each extra unit adds a full 
   implement→review cycle, so only split when pieces are genuinely independently reviewable 
   and independently valuable.
```

This guidance reduces the per-unit review gating overhead and keeps related implementation work in the same review cycle.
