author: elhoim
body:
## BLUF

- **Priority:** medium
- **Problem:** `ParseVirtualMachinesTable` looks up `"VMGuid"`, but the column is named `"VmGuid"`. As a result, `vm_identifier` is `None` on every UAL `VIRTUALMACHINES` event.
- **Fix:** Read `record_values.get("VmGuid")`. This is a one-line change.
- **Test:** `UserAccessLoggingESEDBPluginTest.testParseVirtualMachinesTable` (new)
- **Verified:** The new test fails on main (`None != '{35918bc9-...}' : event value: "vm_identifier"`) and passes with the fix. `black --check`, `pylint --rcfile=.pylintrc` and `typos` are clean on both changed files.

## Details

`ParseVirtualMachinesTable` (`plaso/parsers/esedb_plugins/user_access_logging.py:437`) called `record_values.get("VMGuid")`. In the UAL `VIRTUALMACHINES` table the column is named `VmGuid`. You can confirm this in the schema of `test_data/{C519A76A-D9B5-4F85-B667-5FAC08E0E1B4}.mdb` and in the plugin's own `_VIRTUALMACHINES_TABLE_VALUE_MAPPINGS`. `_GetRecordValues` stores each value under its real column name, and dict lookups are case-sensitive, so the lookup always returned `None`.

**Reproducing input:** any Windows Server UAL database that has a `VIRTUALMACHINES` row with `VmGuid` set. Each resulting `windows:user_access_logging:virtual_machines` event has an empty `vm_identifier`. `bios_identifier`, which is read from `BIOSGuid`, is not affected.

**Regression test:** the bundled test database has 0 rows in `VIRTUALMACHINES`, so this path had no test coverage before. The new test builds a minimal fake record and table in the test file. They implement only what `_GetRecordValues` calls on the mapped-GUID path: `number_of_values`, `get_column_name` and `get_value_data`. The fake uses the real column names `VmGuid` and `BIOSGuid`. Both columns go through `_ConvertGUIDToString`, so the fake does not need to model pyesedb column types. The VM and BIOS GUIDs are set to different values, so the test also catches the two fields being swapped.

Fixes #5230

body:
## Summary
Remove stale junction/symlink at `frontend/.next/standalone/node_modules` before building.

## Root Cause
Next's cleanDistDir follows the junction into the protected deps store, gets EPERM, and its unlinkPath retry never increments, so it loops forever.

## Changes
- Add `clean_stale_next_junction(next_dir=None, cwd=None)` helper in `workflows/portable/build_slot.py` that auto-detects `<cwd>/frontend/.next/standalone/node_modules` and `<cwd>/.next/standalone/node_modules`, plus optional `--next-dir`.
- Check `_is_link_or_junction` using `os.path.islink` and on Windows `os.stat` (`follow_symlinks=False`) with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` (0x400).
- Safely remove only the link/junction via `os.rmdir`/`os.unlink` (never `shutil.rmtree`), leaving target contents intact.
- Call the cleanup from both `acquire` and `run` entry points.
- Add `--next-dir` argument to both `acquire` and `run` subcommands.

## Verification
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `workflows/portable/test_build_slot.py` covering:
  - Junction removal while verifying target directory sentinel file is preserved.
  - Auto-detection from repo root and frontend directory, plus `--next-dir` argument.
  - Non-junction directories with files are never deleted.
  - Both `acquire` and `run` entry points trigger the cleanup.
  - CLI `--next-dir` argument parsing.
- Ran test suite: `python -B workflows/portable/test_build_slot.py` (88 tests passed in 18.4s).

body:
## Summary

Stacked on #118. Extends the Lean spec from primary headers to the p4lite parser machines (§14) and everything the DSL can reference through them.

- **Generated vocabulary**: `spec/lean/gen/vocab2lean` (Go, dev-only) dumps `dslvocab.Bundled()` — all 18 protocols, dispatch edges, declared-length rules, and parser machines — to `Kunai/VocabData.lean` (`make lean-vocab`), so the Lean vocabulary cannot drift from the `.p4` files.
- **Parser-machine interpreter** (`Kunai/Eval/Machine.lean`): extract, stacks with capacity, variable tails, write-back, counters, lookahead/field/counter select keys, first-match select, `MAX_DEPTH` loop cap, TLV option sighting by kind byte. It runs as `aux-extract` inside every layer, including the ipv4/tcp/ipv6 machines the existing vectors already exercised.
- **`where` over aux headers**: `tcp.options.MSS.value`, `gtp.opt.next_ext`, `ipv6.exts[0].next_header`, `srv6.segments[srv6.last_entry].addr`, owner-bound stacks (`tcp.options.SACK.blocks[0].left`, `ipv4.options.RR.addrs[i].addr`), bit slices, `.exists`, and `any`/`all` over the extracted entries.
- **Vectors**: 50 new golden vectors (TCP options, IPv6 extension headers, SRv6, GTP, IPv4 RR) and 1584 generated ones (`lake exe gen --generated`: truncations and byte flips of every golden packet, verdicts from `eval`). `TestSpecVectorsGenerated` runs them like the golden set.
- `dsl-types.md` §14.5 documents the constructs §14 omitted; `spec/lean/README.md` covers the generator.

Found along the way (documented, not changed here): `eth/mpls*/ipv4/tcp` accepts an ARP frame in Go, because ipv4 is dispatched against its static parent (mpls) and the parser machine does not run when no option is queried.

author: fitchmultz
body:
## Outcome
Remove history-dependent repeated work from long-running subagent sessions without weakening conversation history, ownership, completion publication, billing, questions, cancellation, or recovery.

### Root-cause repairs
- Reuse completed Agents history/configuration and unavailable boundaries; retry changed sources and transient I/O. Hydrate full cards/details only on demand, select newest continuations first, resolve ancestry linearly, and bound rendered components to the displayed page.
- Incrementally index native observations, invocation ownership, completed calls, and usage metadata. Reconcile replacements, discontinuous/off-branch appends, and hosts without metadata APIs safely. Exclude inherited IDs from current-attempt message matching and reject missing `message_end.message` with retained audit evidence.
- Match observations by native ID/ordered message identity. Filter acceptance messages only when a boundary is ready. Keep all retained nested-event identities and project once per job poll.
- Skip delivered/billed result probes and unchanged foreign decoding. Preserve canonical recovery despite corrupt/unreadable/wrong-ID disposable hints; share verified completion/accounting receipts while retaining full byte-prefix and LF authority.

## Evidence
Synthetic isolated fixtures only; no personal raw transcripts or paid inference. Node 24.21.0. Independent GPT/Claude reviews and followups completed; all supported findings resolved before the user's instruction prohibiting further agent communication.

| Same-fork operation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 completed 2,000-entry histories, five refreshes | 1,000,000 timestamp parses; 1,005 ms | 0; 1.6 ms |
| 1,000 continuations / one task | 500,500 resolutions | 1,000 |
| 10,000 delivered runs / three polls | 30,003 filesystem probes | 3 directory checks |
| 40 unchanged foreign files / three polls | 120 decodes | 40 initial decodes |
| 20,000 parent entries / ten native-owner checks | 400,020 metadata visits | 40,002, two startup scans |
| 1,500 immutable nested events / unchanged poll | 500 rereads + registry rewrite | Neither |
| Nested projection per job poll | Three registry reads | One |
| Ten 100-card windows | 1,001 cached components | 101 |

Live append tokenization drops from old-history scans to the new suffix; mutable journal byte validation deliberately remains linear. Receipt hashing remains necessary. Isolated cold factory startup has no measurable change beyond variation (old 410–605 ms, new 411–437 ms). This is not a claim that provider/native-host/other-extension latency disappears.

## Qualification
- Exact maintained fork 0.99.1 / `76dfe3d1` and latest official Pi 0.99.2, coherent selected-host peer graphs; both typechecks pass.
- Fork units: 875 pass, three Linux/procfs-only skips on macOS. Targeted integrations: 177 pass, no skips. Positive resume guard covers all six lazy historical results with zero body reads or historical lookups.
- Official portable native contracts: 119 pass, no skips. Its eager host reports the lazy-body guard as unexercised rather than claiming false coverage. Native packaged entries, bundled RPC startup/broker status, and local install/list pass.
- Native Agents rendered/inspected at 90/40/24 columns and completed/live states; drafts, history/tool text, Send/Continue and action controls preserved. Existing native interaction tests cover full details, unread/replies, paging, pinning, mouse controls, replacement, and narrow states.
- Full fork integration sweep: 1,131 pass, ten pre-existing fixture/assertion failures reproduced identically on unchanged `main`. All four affected owner files were requalified: 154 passing tests across follow-up runs; all ten repaired scenarios also pass on unchanged baseline source. No runtime safeguard was loosened. The final follow-up ran the complete 22-test single-execution owner after correcting its terminal fixture. Unchanged full-suite evidence is reused rather than repeating the 14-minute sweep after test-only repairs.
- All 24 full-sweep skips inspected: 23 legacy optional `getPendingToolCalls` cases (retired by this fork), one optional external native-editor receipt integration (not configured). Current portable/background, checkpoint and native usage/ownership contracts ran independently.
- Both packed runtime-only packages: 324 shipped files each; native compiled entries, detached runner, selected-host TypeBox, broker/RPC startup and clean shutdown pass. Both local install/list smokes pass. Actual emitted runtime SHA-256 is `fe4d22d059f3b034f8611ec50da19a2f547b00b6d327613818c95a09976d38ec`.
- Windows explicitly waived by the requester. No manually dispatched remote CI.

## Release
Git-only v0.43.1 (package remains `private: true`), including existing unreleased compatibility/storage/resume/profile fixes since v0.43.0. Performance guarantees, test owners, measured limits and remaining host costs are in `docs/performance.md`. No core upgrade or in-use checkout overwrite; local activation selects a separate tagged immutable extension path and restarts only the requesting saved parent.

author: kioku
body:
## Summary
Materialization spends time on both checkout and Git's post-checkout validation after #89 removes local transfer-protocol overhead. This change parallelizes both while retaining independent object copying, exact detached SHA, cleanliness checks, cache policy, and root-identity protection.

- Run detached checkout with command-local `checkout.workers=4`, retaining Git's default small-checkout threshold. Do not persist workspace configuration.
- For at least 1,000 indexed entries, run each cleanliness check through four read-only Git status processes. Three glob path groups cover ASCII basename ranges; the exclusion-only fourth group covers everything else, including punctuation and Unicode. Smaller checkouts use normal status.
- Preserve Git's racy-index/content validation and both verification passes. Do not modify timestamps, set assume-unchanged flags, or replace Git's content checks with custom hashing.
- Disable optional index writes in status workers to avoid index.lock contention and cross-shard refresh work. Join all workers and propagate worker failures. Clear inherited pathspec overrides so internal magic pathspecs cannot be treated as literal nonexistent paths.
- Document the policies and the index-cache trade-off in README.md.

## Measurement
Stable independent snapshot of a private monorepo: approximately 124 MiB of source objects and 7,896 tracked entries. Source repository unchanged. All comparisons use new destinations and `--object-source`, bypassing cache refresh.

The initial checkout-only commit measured **2,006 → 1,740 ms (13%)** versus merged #89 in six alternating runs per version. This result was noisier and smaller than the initial isolated checkout experiment; it does not establish another 50% reduction.

Git Trace2 on the checkout-only build found median costs of **493 ms clone**, **324 ms checkout**, **412 ms first status**, and **33 ms second status**. First status spends roughly 370–390 ms on index refresh, with approximately 7,896 additional stats. A disposable-clone timestamp diagnostic isolated Git's racy-index protection as the cause; modifying index timestamps is explicitly not proposed. Waiting before status did not eliminate the refresh cost.

Balanced read-only status groups reduced both verification passes from **603 → 282 ms** in a command-level experiment. Full CLI gains are smaller:

| Matched CLI batch, six runs/version | Checkout-only median | Checkout + parallel verification median | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Prototype | 1,258.5 ms | 1,105.3 ms | 12.2% |
| Final build, after pathspec sanitization | 1,203.8 ms | 1,129.8 ms | 6.1% |

Final serial samples: 1282.9 / 996.2 / 1246.2 / 1161.3 / 1131.0 / 1393.9 ms. Final parallel samples: 1166.9 / 1103.9 / 1120.9 / 1160.9 / 1009.1 / 1138.7 ms. Run order alternates serial/parallel/parallel/serial. Debug binaries; warm filesystem caches. Every CLI run verifies exact SHA, clean detached state, no alternates, and object link counts of one.

These are noisy local measurements, not production percentiles. Do not combine percentage gains across different batches. **An additional 50% end-to-end reduction remains unproven.** Scratch repository/workspace copies were removed; detailed benchmark evidence is retained locally.

## Trade-offs
Read-only status does not update the index's on-disk stat cache, so a subsequent normal Git status may perform the refresh. Large repositories with skewed filename distributions or constrained CPU can benefit less or incur extra overhead. Cache refresh, copying, and checkout still contribute substantially to total time. No Windows/macOS performance claim is made.

## Validation
- Pre-commit gates passed: cargo fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, full cargo test suite (**338 tests**), and ast-grep (existing unsafe-code warnings only).
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Expanded large-checkout regression to 1,200 files across object-source/cache/remote modes, checking an older SHA, contents, executable index mode, clean detached state, no alternates, and no persisted worker config.
- Added large-checkout failure regressions for every path group, same-size edits with restored mtime, hidden/numeric/Unicode/newline names, untracked files, deleted files, staged cross-group rename, symlink replacement, and worker failures. Confirm all four workers complete and failed owned destinations are cleaned.
- Regressions exercise all four inherited pathspec overrides and root replacement/final-verification protection on the concurrent status path. Existing object-independence, cleanup, ACL, and directory-identity tests remain green.

## Base
Targets `main`; #89 is now incorporated on both Foundry and GitHub. No earlier CI exception is requested for this PR.


## Review repairs
- Force untracked-file reporting in both serial and parallel verification, independent of `status.showUntrackedFiles`.
- Disable `core.ignoreStat` for detached checkout so caller preferences cannot create assume-unchanged index entries that hide tracked edits. No persistent configuration changes.
- Regression coverage exercises both sides of the status threshold under these settings, plus every untracked path group with reporting disabled in repository configuration.
- All pre-commit gates passed after repair: formatting, clippy with `-D warnings`, 338 tests, and ast-grep (existing unsafe-code warnings only). `git diff --check` passed.

## Independent review cycle 2
- Disable `core.fsmonitor` command-locally in both serial and parallel status verification. A stale or incomplete monitor response must not hide tracked edits or untracked files. A regression reproduces the false-clean result and exercises both status sizes after the repair.
- Make detached-HEAD verification fail closed: only `symbolic-ref -q` exit 1 means detached; spawn errors and other exit statuses reject materialization. An injected-error integration regression verifies rejection and owned-destination cleanup.
- Targeted materialization tests: 25 passed. All commit hooks passed: formatting, clippy with `-D warnings`, full suite (338 tests), and ast-grep (existing unsafe-code warnings only). `git diff --check` passed.
- Monitor bypass may cost additional filesystem work in repositories that otherwise benefit from fsmonitor. No new performance claim is made.

The first two independent cycles repaired four Major validation gaps. Fresh cycle 3 reviewed `3462cf685806d79f5655e99ddee97d63070317a4` without source/head changes and returned **CLEAN**, with no Critical/Major or actionable Minor findings. Targeted validation passed: 25 materialization tests, the Git-preference regression, and independent path-group coverage probes. Full hooks passed at this same head (338 tests). No merge was performed.

author: mohammadhijjawi97
body:
## Before opening this pull request

- [x] I considered whether this change belongs in `openai/codex`.
- [x] This change is specific to an Open Interpreter-owned surface, or I have
      linked the upstream Codex contribution below.

## Why this belongs in Open Interpreter

The bundled model compatibility catalog (`codex-rs/codex-api/model_compatibility_catalog.json`), its generator (`codex-rs/scripts/write_model_compatibility_catalog.py`) and the lookup in `codex-api/src/model_compatibility_catalog.rs` exist only in Open Interpreter; they are part of its provider/model support and do not exist in `openai/codex`.

## Summary

`compatible_model_catalog_entry` indexes canonical ids and suffix aliases in one case-insensitive map. The generator only checked that a suffix was unique among *suffixes*, so it could emit an alias equal to another model's own id, and when the aliased entry sorts later it overwrites that id in the index. For example `tensormesh/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` got the alias `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, so looking up `deepseek-v4-flash` returned the tensormesh entry (context window 32768, no parallel tool calls) instead of its own entry (1000000). `apply_compatibility_catalog` then overwrites the model's context window, which leads to very early auto-compaction.

In the current bundled catalog 44 canonical slugs resolved to another provider's entry, including `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-pro-latest`, `gemini-exp-1206` and `minimax/minimax-m2.5`.

This change:
- skips suffix aliases that match any canonical id (ignoring case) in `unique_suffix_aliases`;
- regenerates the `aliases` arrays of the bundled catalog from its existing ids (no other fields change, and no new litellm data is pulled in);
- adds `codex-rs/scripts/test_write_model_compatibility_catalog.py`.

After the change every canonical id resolves to its own entry (except `together_ai/BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, which collides with the canonical `together_ai/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5` id itself), and every key that resolved before still resolves.

## Related issue

Looks like the cause of #1877 (DeepSeek v4 flash context falling back to ~31.1k after the first prompt), which was closed without a linked fix.

## Test plan

- `cd codex-rs/scripts && python -m unittest test_write_model_compatibility_catalog test_write_provider_catalog`: 5 tests pass. The new tests fail on the previous generator and catalog.
- Rebuilt the Rust lookup index in a script over the old and new JSON: the 44 shadowed ids now resolve to themselves; no lookup key is lost; `gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5-codex` and `deepseek-reasoner` resolve as the existing Rust tests expect.
- `ruff format --check` on the changed scripts.
- I did not run the Rust test suites locally; CI should cover `codex-api` and `models-manager`.

author: dcccrypto
body:
## Bug
SI (`8WC8…`) is registered on pool `21bzHy…` (meteora-dlmm). That pool is what the keeper pushes on-chain and what price-ws streams. But two display paths re-resolved a different "best" pool:
- **trade chart:** `/api/chart/[mint]` took GeckoTerminal's top pool for the mint, `7Nj7m…`.
- **`/api/oracle/resolve`:** took DexScreener's most liquid pair.

So the chart and the resolved price came from a different venue than the market's mark.

## Fix
- **`lib/registered-pool.ts`** (server-only): reads a market's venue from its `markets` row: `dex_pool_address`, network, and `mainnet_ca` must match the token. `dexType` comes from the registry. Cached 60 s; DB errors are not cached.
- **`/api/chart/[mint]`:** accepts `?slab=` and uses that market's registered pool. `useTokenChart` / `TradingChart` pass the slab, and cache keys include it.
  - Without a slab (no market context), the top-pool lookup is unchanged.
  - A slab can't vouch for another token's pool.
- **`/api/oracle/resolve/[ca]`:** for a token that already has a live market, it returns that market's registered pool, its `dexType`, and that pair's price.
- **Already correct:** price-ws (DB `dex_pool_address`) and `/api/prices/[slab]` (24h stats from `dex_pool_address`).

## Evidence
- **Production data, local run of the routes:**

  | market | chart before | chart after (slab) | resolve | registered |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | SI | 7Nj7mB | **21bzHy** | **21bzHy** meteora-dlmm | 21bzHy |
  | PERC | Ebs3mX | Ebs3mX | Ebs3mX pumpswap | Ebs3mX |
- **`__tests__/api/registered-pool-venue.test.ts`:** 4/4.
  - Negative control: with the base routes, the chart and resolve tests fail (2/4). The controls (no slab, foreign token) pass on both.
- **Related suites** (27 files: chart, resolve, useTokenChart, TradingChart): 307/307. `tsc` clean.

## Separate observation (not changed here)
The keeper pushes SI at about 0.0045 from the same pool, while DexScreener quotes 21bzHy at about 0.0048. That is a pricing gap (smoothing or SOL conversion), not a pool mismatch.

author: theraccoonbear
body:
Closes #18

## What
- `run` now renders the Art Director's `scene_art` / `cover_art` prompts into `<run>/art/` (`scene-NN.jpg`, `cover.jpg`) when the story finishes. Rendering failures only warn — the story is already written.
- `art --out <run> [--force]` (`npm run art`) re-renders or retries a run's images.
- `src/artist.ts`: each image goes generate → inspect → regenerate from the inspector's revised prompt, up to `maxAttempts` (default 3). A failed generation (timeout/blocked/empty) uses an attempt instead of dropping the image. If every attempt is rejected, the last image is kept and flagged `accepted: false`.
- Continuity: the last `maxReferences` (default 3) rendered images are passed as reference images to both the generator and the inspector.
- `art/art.json` manifest records prompt, final prompt, attempts and unresolved issues; re-runs skip images whose prompt is unchanged, so extending a run only renders the new scenes and cover.
- Backends behind small `ImageBackend` / `Inspector` interfaces: Gemini (native `generateContent`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) and mock (offline placeholders, used by `story.config.json`).
- Config: top-level `artist` block (`image`, `inspector`, `maxAttempts`, `maxReferences`) rather than `roles.artist`, since roles are text-only `Provider`s. Defaults to `gemini-3.1-flash-image` (16:9) + `gemini-3.8-flash` inspector. `story.opencode-go.config.json` gains the `artist` block and an `artdirector` role.
- `postJson` / `requireKey` exported from `src/providers.ts` for reuse; `postJson` falls back to `spec.model` for its log label.

## Includes the #20 fix
This branch carries a cherry-pick of the full-scene fix from #21 so the art director sees whole scenes. Merge that PR first; this one's diff then reduces to the artist work.

## Live check
Rendered a 3-scene story + cover against real Gemini: ~10s per image plus ~5–10s inspection; characters and style stayed consistent across images. In a 1-scene live run the inspector rejected the cover twice (wrong character genders, garbled text) before accepting.

## Qué cambia
El indicador **«● Cambios sin guardar»** de la ficha de producto se quedaba encendido después de una subida de video correcta, sin que hubiera nada pendiente.

**Visto en producción** el 30/09/2026, repitiendo en `ZZ Pruebas UX` la prueba de #320: se elige un video, se pulsa «Subir y convertir», la conversión termina y la ficha enseña «✓ Video guardado en el producto» —con la tarjeta de la IA ya corregida por #320— y, abajo a la izquierda, «Cambios sin guardar». Medido: `productoTieneCambios()` daba `false` y el indicador seguía visible; desaparecía solo al tocar cualquier campo.

**Causa:** el indicador cuenta el video elegido (`firmaProducto`) y solo se repintaba con un clic o una tecla en la ficha. El estado cambia al elegir el archivo, al empezar la subida y al acabarla, y ahí no pasaba nada.

**Arreglo:** `actualizarEtiquetaGuardar()`, que ya se llama justo en esos tres momentos para cambiar el texto de «Guardar y subir video», repinta también el indicador. Una línea, con su comentario.

## Comprobación
- `npm test`: 1612 pruebas (962 en `navegador.test.js`, 2 nuevas), 0 fallos. Falla de verdad si se quita la llamada.
- Pendiente tras desplegar: repetir la subida en `ZZ Pruebas UX` y comprobar que el indicador se apaga solo al terminar.

author: ankitparekh007
body:
Timestamps and JSON now use native PostgreSQL column types (ADR 0028). The API reads and returns exactly the same values as before, so no contract changes.

## What changes

- **Timestamps:** migration 0008 converts 78 ISO-8601 text timestamp columns to `timestamptz`. Only the migration runner's `schema_migrations.applied_at` stays text. A stored time without an offset is read as UTC, whatever the server's time zone.
- **JSON:** 15 JSON columns the API only reads with `JSON.parse` become `jsonb`; their `af_json_valid` checks are dropped.
- **Left as text on purpose:** signed or digest-pinned data stays byte-for-byte as written: manifest bodies, execution grants, webhook bodies and catalog content. Chat message content isn't JSON.
- **Same values in the API:** the driver returns `timestamptz` as millisecond UTC strings (`2026-09-30T17:46:53.123Z`) and `jsonb` as text. A timestamp JavaScript can't represent (e.g. `infinity`) fails the read.
- **Migration details:** each table is altered in one statement. One column default and five identity triggers that name converted columns are dropped and recreated unchanged. The organization defaults trigger now fills times to the millisecond.
- **SQL fixes:** three statements in `execution-service.ts` that passed timestamps as text now cast them to `timestamptz`.
- `migrate()` takes an optional migration list, so upgrade tests can stop at an earlier release.

## Deployment note

The upgrade rewrites every converted table and blocks the database while it runs, so a large deployment needs a maintenance window. If any stored value isn't a valid timestamp or JSON, the whole migration rolls back and the database stays at release 7 until that value is fixed.

## Tests

`npm run check` passes: API 250 (was 246), admin console 36, employee app 5, agent runtime 25, execution runtime 20 + 1 skipped.

New upgrade tests start from a database at release 7 set to a non-UTC time zone:
- timestamps with milliseconds, whole seconds, an offset, and no offset keep the same instant and sort by time; JSON parses back to the same data;
- exactly 78 timestamp and 15 JSON columns convert, signed text stays text, and the triggers and default are restored;
- a malformed stored timestamp fails the upgrade and changes nothing;
- an `infinity` timestamp is refused on read.

Three existing tests wrote the placeholder `'x'` into timestamp columns and now use real times. One compared stored JSON text exactly and now compares parsed data.

## Known limitations

- Expiries stored as epoch milliseconds (`bigint`) are unchanged.
- SQL that passes a timestamp where text is expected must cast it; the three known cases are covered by tests, but an untested statement would fail only at runtime.

author: koopa0
body:
Closes #766

## What changed

Every snapshot build linted each note through `judge.LintFrontmatter`, which ran the whole `parseNote`: wikilink, path-reference, planned-name and callout extraction, `sequence.Parse` and the anchor surface, up to eight goldmark parses of the body. The frontmatter rules read none of it: `lintRun` reads only `frontmatter`, `noteType`, `path`, `noFrontmatter` and `badFrontmatter`. `newLintRun` also cloned the contract's definition and recompiled its `slug_pattern` for every note.

- `internal/judge/note.go`: `parseNoteWithMarks` and a new `parseFrontmatter` both call one `readNote`. It extracts the body only when it is given the marks to extract it against; `parseFrontmatter` passes `nil`. The frontmatter half (split, YAML, duplicate-key check, `buildFrontmatter`, `readTypedFields`) is the same code for both, so the two notes cannot differ in it.
- `internal/judge/schema.go`: `lintRun` now also carries the contract's knowledge scope and skipped basenames, and `checkSchema`'s loop moves onto `(*lintRun).check`, so the check command and the lint share it. New `FrontmatterLinter` / `NewFrontmatterLinter(contract)` resolve the contract once (the same `newLintRun` the check command uses); `Lint(relPath, data)` parses the frontmatter only. The zero value, which a folder no contract governs gets, says nothing. `LintFrontmatter` keeps its signature and findings and is now `NewFrontmatterLinter(contract)` plus one `Lint`.
- `internal/snapshot/snapshot.go`: `buildGeneration` builds one linter per build and hands it to `deriveNote`, which runs it inside the note parse panic guard. `recordVerdict` keeps its `(relPath, findings, err, log)` signature. A slug pattern that does not compile still logs the same warning once per note and leaves that note without a verdict, as before.

The check command still parses every note whole; its output, `LintFrontmatter`'s output and every golden are unchanged. Nothing under `internal/judge/testdata/` is touched.

Benchmark, `BenchmarkBuildSnapshot` (6-note vault, `-count=10`, this shared 4-CPU box, `benchstat` main vs this branch):

```text
sec/op     3.059m ± 51%  ->  2.054m ± 31%   -32.86% (p=0.001 n=10)
B/op       507.9Ki ± 0%  ->  332.6Ki ± 0%   -34.51% (p=0.000 n=10)
allocs/op  5.514k ± 0%   ->  3.315k ± 0%    -39.88% (p=0.000 n=10)
```

The sec/op spread is the machine's load; allocs/op is the stable number. On a scratch benchmark of one lesson note with a 6 KB body dense in links, headings, fences and callouts (not committed), one lint went from 6.9 ms and 25,161 allocs (whole parse) to 68 µs and 286 allocs (frontmatter only, contract resolved per call) to 35 µs and 192 allocs (frontmatter only, contract resolved once).

Merge with #844 (#743, open): it also edits `internal/judge/note.go` and `schema.go`. Its one line in `parseNoteWithMarks`'s `!found` branch (`n.unclosedFrontmatter = ...`) sits in code this change leaves where it is, now inside `readNote`, so the frontmatter-only parse fills the flag with no further edit. I trial-merged `refs/pull/844/head` into this branch: it merges without conflict, builds, and the new tests below and the rest of `go test ./internal/judge -run 'Lint|Frontmatter|Unclosed|CheckSchema'` pass on the merge, including over #844's new `vault-unclosed` fixture, which the equivalence test picks up from `testdata` by itself. The trial merge was not committed or pushed.

## How it was verified

Each lock was broken in the production code, run, and restored (the restored files are byte-identical to the committed ones).

```text
TestLintFrontmatterCostDoesNotGrowWithTheBody: red with Lint calling parseNote instead of parseFrontmatter — "LintFrontmatter allocates 4787 for a 1 KB body and 277848 for a 64 KB body, want the two within 10%"; green with the fix. (The test also asserts the whole parse allocates at least twice as much on the 64 KB body as on the 1 KB one, so the bodies are known to be ones a body extraction would show on.)
TestFrontmatterLinterResolvesTheContractOnce: red with Lint calling newLintRun on every call — "Lint allocates 1345 per note and LintFrontmatter 2542, want Lint under half of it"; green with the fix. (Slug pattern is a 300-way alternation, so compiling it dominates.)
TestFrontmatterOnlyParseAgreesWithTheFullParse: red with readTypedFields skipped when marks == nil — "parseFrontmatter(vault/Concepts/golang/A.md) differs from the whole parse outside its body fields ... - noteType: "concept" + noteType: """ and "LintFrontmatter(vault-status-unreachable/Concepts/stranded/Stranded.md) differs from the whole parse's findings"; green with the fix.
```

`TestFrontmatterOnlyParseAgreesWithTheFullParse` takes its notes from every directory under `testdata` named `vault*` (30 vaults, 144 notes, 457 findings today), so a fixture added later is held to it. For each note it compares `LintFrontmatter` with the findings the whole parse draws (`checkSchema` over `parseNote`, sorted), and `parseFrontmatter` with `parseNote` on every field the body extraction does not fill (the body fields are named in the test, so a field added later shows as a difference until someone decides). Putting the whole parse back leaves this test green by construction, since the whole parse is its oracle; that regression is the first lock's. The existing `TestLintFrontmatterAgreesWithTheCheckCommand` still compares the lint with the check command itself over `vault-schema`; its directory walk moved into the shared `fixtureNotes` helper.

Commands, each unpiped (output to a log where it was long), on head `f8deff2`:

```text
go build ./...                                                    -> exit 0
go vet ./internal/judge/ ./internal/snapshot/                     -> exit 0
make fmt-check                                                    -> exit 0
golangci-lint run ./internal/judge/... ./internal/snapshot/...    -> exit 0, 0 issues
make staticcheck                                                  -> exit 0
make gosec                                                        -> exit 0, 0 issues
make convention-check                                             -> exit 0
go test -race -count=1 -exec 'setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override,-dac_read_search' ./internal/judge/... ./internal/snapshot/... ./internal/note/... ./internal/report/... ./internal/shell/... ./internal/syllabus/... ./cmd/yomihon/...  -> exit 0
go test -race -count=1 -exec 'setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override,-dac_read_search' ./internal/ui/pages/...  -> exit 0
go test -run=NONE -bench=BenchmarkBuildSnapshot -benchmem -count=10 ./internal/snapshot/  (main, then this branch) -> exit 0 both
```

The `setpriv` runs drop the capabilities root uses to ignore file modes, so the permission tests ran for real. Those are scoped `go test` runs over the touched packages and their direct dependents, not a `make verify` exit code. `make check-fixtures` was not run: `git diff origin/main -- internal/judge/testdata` is empty. `make css-check` and `make frontend-check` were not run: no templ, CSS or JS changed. Full `make verify` not run locally; CI runs it.

## What was left out

- The optional third item of #766, sharing one link extraction between `newBacklinks` and `newHealth` (each calls `judge.LinkTargets` on every body). It is a separate change in `internal/snapshot` and was not asked for as part of the lint fix.
- Memoising `structure()` (#770), which lands after this.
- A contract whose slug pattern does not compile still logs one warning per note for each build. Saying it once per build would change what the log says and is its own change.
- `report.go` still uses `parseNote` for the few lines of frontmatter it validates; its body is the literal `body\n`, so there is nothing to save.
- `LintFrontmatter` no longer has a production caller (the snapshot build uses the linter); it stays as the one-shot form because the existing tests and #844's tests call it.

## Needs a ruling

None.

author: martinsphilippes
body:
## O que muda
- Na proposta que está aguardando o sinal, o cliente vê o bloco **"Pague com Pix"**. Ele traz o QR Code, o código **copia e cola** com um botão para copiar, o recebedor, a chave, o valor e a referência da solicitação.
- O código segue o padrão BR Code estático do Banco Central e é gerado no servidor. O CRC16 foi conferido com o exemplo do manual. Não há integração com banco, então a confirmação do pagamento continua manual pela Wellmix.
- **Configurações (só o admin):** novos campos para a chave Pix, o nome do recebedor e a cidade. A chave aceita CPF, CNPJ, e-mail, celular com +55 ou chave aleatória, e é validada no servidor, inclusive o dígito de CPF e CNPJ. Sem chave configurada, ou com valor fora de BRL, a tela explica a situação e não mostra Pix.
- **Comprovante:** o cliente anexa uma foto ou PDF na própria solicitação. O pagamento continua pendente e a Wellmix é avisada. A Wellmix abre o comprovante e confirma com o botão que já existia.
- **Pendências:** quando o comprovante chega, a pendência sai do cliente. A pendência da Wellmix passa a dizer que o comprovante chegou.

## Acesso
- Só o login que vê a solicitação pode enviar o comprovante, e só enquanto ela aguarda o sinal.
- Outro login da mesma empresa, o fornecedor e a Wellmix não enviam comprovante pelo cliente.
- O arquivo abre só para o cliente da solicitação e para a Wellmix.

## Validação
- lint, typecheck e 58 testes unitários passaram. Os testes novos cobrem o CRC do manual, a validação de chaves, o código montado, a falta de Pix sem chave ou fora de BRL, e o comprovante com acesso, pendências e confirmação.
- E2E e build passaram.
- Fluxo conferido no navegador:
  - o admin tenta uma chave inválida e recebe a mensagem de erro, depois salva uma chave válida;
  - o cliente copia o código, confirmado na área de transferência, e envia o comprovante;
  - a Wellmix vê o comprovante e confirma, e o pedido é criado.
- Conferido também no celular, sem rolagem horizontal.

## Dependência
- Adiciona `qrcode` (1.5.4) para gerar o QR Code em SVG no servidor.

author: thelmaoffiong
body:
Add canonical KYC_WEBHOOK_ERROR_RECOVERY table, retryable/retryHint as owned KycWebhookError properties, captureStackTrace, factory createKycWebhookError(), and classifier classifyKycWebhookError().

Previously, retryability and retry hints were computed on-the-fly by the middleware from a separate pair of Sets. This meant every call site that handled a KycWebhookError had to duplicate or import that logic, making recovery behaviour non-deterministic and untestable in isolation.

Changes:
- src/errors/KycWebhookError.js: central KYC_WEBHOOK_ERROR_RECOVERY table maps every known error code to (status, retryable, retryHint). Constructor sets these as owned properties. Unknown codes fall back to HTTP-status heuristics. createKycWebhookError() factory enforces code→status consistency. classifyKycWebhookError() converts any thrown value into a typed KycWebhookError without leaking internals.
- src/middleware/kycWebhookErrorHandler.js: remove local RETRYABLE_* Sets and resolveRetryHint(); read err.retryable / err.retryHint directly from the error instance instead.
- tests/unit/KycWebhookError.unit.test.js: 76 new tests covering constructor backward-compat, owned properties, all 15 error codes, fallback heuristics, factory, classifier, and concurrency.

Existing call sites (new KycWebhookError(msg, status, code)) remain unchanged; they now also receive retryable/retryHint on the instance.

Closes #1374

body:
Closes #274. Parent epic #255 (Phase A: SaaS layer, provider-independent). Blocked by #271 (merged) and by #268 (open — this PR ships the schema substrate it needs and leaves #268 open for the discount calc, concurrency proof, and provider handoff).

## What

The operational surface for campaign codes: create with every constraint mandatory, list with live counts, deactivate-with-history, identifier-only redemption visibility, and locked terms after first redemption.

## How

- **Migration `20261001000000` (domain, #268 substrate)**: `coupons` (code PK, percent 1–100 / amount >0 + currency, ordered window, caps with limit-in-cap, `duration` encoding first-period-vs-lifetime as a column per #268's note), `coupon_redemptions` (unique pair = double-redeem guard, coupon RESTRICT preserves history, household CASCADE honors #269), `redeem_coupon()` with distinct 23514 reasons (unknown / deactivated / not-yet-valid / expired / exhausted / household-limit / already-redeemed) checked under a row lock. RLS with no authenticated policies — households cannot enumerate codes; the code itself is the redemption capability.
- **Migration `20261001000001` (admin, #274)**: `tg_lock_redeemed_coupon()` (only active true→false may change once redeemed — value, limits, window, and reactivation rejected; unredeemed rows stay editable; there is deliberately no terms-edit RPC), `admin_create_coupon()` (all params required, currency an explicit null for percent, codes canonicalized, stillborn windows and duplicates rejected, mandatory reason, in-transaction audit), `admin_list_coupons()` (counts + remaining capacity), `admin_set_coupon_active()` (mandatory reason, before/after audit, audited idempotent no-op), `admin_get_coupon_redemptions()` (household ids + timestamps only).
- **GET/POST `/api/admin/coupons`**: zod validation (currency key required-but-nullable), neutral 404s, 400/409 mapping (duplicate create is a 409, never a second row), detail re-read through the list reader, allowlisted shapes reusing `scope.ts`.
- **Admin coupons page**: create form starting empty (no preselected type/duration/limits), per-coupon deactivate with reason, inline identifier-only redemptions, cross-links with the households list.
- **Docs**: `admin-boundary.md` function table. No boundary change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Creating a coupon requires every constraint field explicitly with no silent defaults (pgTAP 42 tests 1–10; UI starts empty)
- [x] Redemption counts are accurate and visible in the list (test 12c: 1/99)
- [x] Deactivating preserves history and immediately prevents new redemptions (tests 13–15)
- [x] An already-redeemed coupon cannot have its value or limits edited (tests 16–17; unredeemed stays editable, 18–19)
- [x] The redemption list shows identifiers, not personal data (tests 20–21 + wire-shape vitest)

## Verification

- `npm run db:test`: 47 files, 718 pgTAP tests pass (new files 41: 14 tests, 42: 25 tests)
- `npm run test`: 119 files, 876 vitest tests pass (11 new coupon-route tests)
- `tsc`, eslint, prettier clean; `BUILD_TARGET=tauri` build succeeds; `db:reset && db:types` run with regenerated types committed

## Drive-by (unrelated, flagged)

`supabase/tests/15_budgets.sql` broke for everyone on Oct 1: tests 13–15 hardcoded `period_month = '2026-10-01'`, colliding with the current-month setup row once the calendar reached October. Replaced with current-month + 3 (provably distinct from every other month in the file). Pre-existing time bomb, three lines, no behavior change.

Add coverage for skipped snapshot updates, explicit section removal, changed-state patch replay, unchanged-state deduplication, and matching live and persisted checkpoints when starting a new context window.

author: shmuelsh23a
body:
Balance rounds 34–47 (`docs/balance.md`). The AI commanders came first; the work then went back to checking the balance against real-life outcomes, using a set of reasonable attack plans rather than one scripted plan.

## Rules decisions (author)
- **67:** an attacking side gives up at 30% again (decision 66 had 40%). At 30%, a failed attack costs the attacker 16–22% killed and wounded, inside the sources' 10–25%.
- **68:** win targets for small-unit attacks on a prepared position: 3:1 **40–55%** (70–75% with surprise or strong suppression), 2:1 **20–35%** (Rowland's small-unit data). Judged on the median of reasonable plans, with losses checked as well as wins.

## Drill changes (ours)
- Bounding by platoon uses one level of alternation, not two, and starts only within 400 m of a known enemy. Before, the pace in contact was about 8 m a minute, against the sources' 15–30.
- Once released, squads step through covered ground where there is some. A platoon that reaches the last cover waits for the others, for up to 5 turns, so they close together.
- New options in the company's questions: move up to an assault position, chosen against what the scouts found, and go round a flank on the enemy's side.

## Where the balance stands
The median of the reasonable plans is **42% at 3:1 and 24% at 2:1**, inside decision 68's targets. Losses are inside the sources' ranges, and the hasty attack sits close to history (it rose to 45% with the forty-fifth round's drill changes, above history's 15–35%; open with the author). The standard measurement is 49% / 27%. Validation was rerun (`docs/validation.md`).

## AI commanders
- `jev-sim` gained `--jev`, `--claude <model>` and `--rule`, plus switches for measuring individual choices: `--order`, `--plan`, `--memory`, `--defender-plan`, `--attacker-breakpoint` and others.
- Jev, Haiku, Sonnet and Opus were all compared; on today's rules Jev wins 15% / 5% and Haiku 5% / 5%, mostly because of their own plan choices.
- The scout question now says what scouts do. Before, every model sent a single scout.

## Tried and withdrawn
- Fire on the move (`GameOptions.fireOnTheMove` is still in the code, off by default).
- An overwatch position for the company command group.
- Binoculars for command groups.
- Re-siting the assault position once the enemy is found.

## Roadmap
- Backlog 21: a doctrine engine, with drills taken from the manuals (US open doctrine for the civilian edition, the customer's for the institutional one).
- Backlog 22: an AI commander in three parts (plan once, compute the odds, execute cheaply).

`npm run check` passes (803 tests).

author: bunheang360
body:
## Summary

Builds on #36 and #38.
- **Plan credits:** a paid plan now adds its credits to the member who paid.
- **Credit packs:** any workspace member can buy credits through the same Bakong KHQR checkout.

Backend only. The frontend contract is in `docs/api.md` → *Billing (Bakong KHQR)*.

### API

```text
GET  /v1/billing/credit-packs                       (public)
POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/billing/payments   { "plan": "pro" }  or  { "creditPack": "credits-135" }
GET  /v1/payments/:paymentId                        now returns kind, creditPack, credits, creditBalance
```

- **Plans:** only owners can buy one.
- **Packs:** any member can buy one, and the credits go to that member.
- **Errors:** an unknown or off-sale pack returns `409 CREDIT_PACK_UNAVAILABLE`. A body with both fields, or neither, returns `400`.

### How credits are granted

- The payment's credits are fixed at checkout in `payments.credit_units`, so a later `.env` change doesn't alter what an open QR grants.
- When the payment becomes PAID, the same transaction writes a ledger row of `PLAN_GRANT` (plan) or `PACK_PURCHASE` (pack) that references the payment. The ledger's existing unique `(reference_id, kind)` index makes a second grant a no-op.
- The background sweep also fills in grants that are missing on already-paid payments, without calling Bakong. That's how plan payments made before this PR get their credits. The migration can't do it, because Postgres refuses to use an enum value inside the transaction that adds it.
- Credit history shows these entries as "Plan credits" and "Credits purchased". Bought credits don't expire.

### Configuration

`CREDIT_PACKS` is a list of `price:credits` pairs in USD. It defaults to the published pricing, `2.50:30,5:65,10:135,25:350,50:720,100:1450`, and an empty value sells no packs. Each pack's id is `credits-<n>`. Plan credits still come from `PLAN_<ID>_CREDITS`.

### Migration `0017_credit_purchases`

- Adds `PLAN_GRANT` and `PACK_PURCHASE` to `credit_entry_kind`.
- Adds `payment_kind` and `payments.kind`, `credit_pack` and `credit_units`, and makes `plan` nullable.
- Adds a check constraint so each payment is exactly one of a plan or a pack.
- Backfills 150/300/750 onto existing plan payments.
- Timestamped `1790900000000`, after every migration already applied to the shared dev database (which includes `1790800000000`, not on `main`), so Drizzle doesn't skip it.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`, build typecheck, `npm test`: 399 passed. New tests cover plan credits, the credit snapshot, pack purchase by a non-owner, buyer-only balance, short-payment rejection, per-buyer checkout reuse, packs not on sale, the missing-grant backfill, `CREDIT_PACKS` parsing, and route validation.
- [x] Migration applied to the dev database. The database tests (payment repository, credit repository, credit ledger), 21 in total, pass when run serially (`--no-file-parallelism`); in parallel they time out on the remote database.
- [x] Real data: the Starter payment PAID on 2026-10-01 received its `PLAN_GRANT` of 150 through the sweep, so the balance went from 50 to 200, and running it again granted nothing.
- [ ] Real credit-pack payment: `npm run payments:test -- --email <you> --pack credits-30` ($2.50). A checkout was created, but it wasn't paid yet.

## Known issue (separate fix)

The Bakong token allows 100 requests a day. The status polling and the sweep can use that up, and a payment left PENDING by a Bakong error is retried every 30 s indefinitely. Credit packs mean more checkouts, so this should be fixed before launch.

author: cinsoul
body:
v0.50.0 reached verify-version for the first time — the decoupling let the publish job run instead of being skipped behind the npm binaries — and it failed there, so npm, PyPI and the GitHub release were all skipped again.

actions/checkout with no `ref:` takes the ref that triggered the run. On the workflow_call path that is the *caller's* branch: main at the merge commit, one commit before release-on-merge's version bump. So:

    run head  be60f8c   pyproject 0.49.0
    tag       v0.50.0 -> cff7dec   pyproject 0.50.0

verify-version compared 0.49.0 against v0.50.0 and failed. Everything downstream needs it.

build-native-binaries.yml had the same bug in all four of its jobs, which is worse than it sounds: the binaries for a release were frozen from the previous version's tree, so `aria-code-bin --version` on a v0.50.0 binary would have printed 0.49.0.

It never broke before because a tag push makes github.ref_name the tag, which is what the default checkout wanted. The bug exists only on the workflow_call path — the path added to stop tags from publishing nothing.

All ten checkouts across the two workflows now pin `ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}`, which is correct on both paths. create-release keeps its fetch-depth: 0.

test_release_chain.py already had a test for this exact hazard — test_nothing_reads_the_ref_without_the_input — and it could not see this, because it greps for an explicit `github.ref_name` and the bug is the *absence* of a ref: there is nothing to grep. Added test_every_checkout_pins_the_tag, which parses the workflows and asserts each checkout names one. Verified it fails against main.

The older test also needed a fix: it matched the comment explaining the hazard, because comments naming `github.ref_name` are not uses of it.

Full suite: 2025 passed, 66 skipped, 0 failed.

body: ## Summary Tier-2 text matching no longer depends on a single Groq model id. - Default `GROQ_MODEL` is `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile` was shut down on 2026-08-16). - Default `GEMINI_MODEL` is `gemini-3.5-flash` (`gemini-2.0-flash` was shut down on 2026-06-01). Vision still uses that setting. - `TextCascade` tries Groq first. On HTTP 404, HTTP 429, or a decommissioned-model error, it asks Gemini for the same JSON verdict (text only, no images). Any other provider failure, or both providers failing, uses the existing keyword heuristic and records the error in the reason. An outage is not stored as a confidence-0 non-match unless the heuristic itself says no. - `reasoning_effort` stays unset. gpt-oss rejects `none`. ## Tests `python -m pytest` — 20 passed, including mocked Groq success, Groq 404/429 with Gemini, both providers down, and no keys. ## Summary

Adds full-text conversation search so users can find messages from prior prompts and assistant replies, not only conversation titles.

## Linked issue

Closes #37

## Changes

- Added authenticated `GET /chat/search?q=...`.
- Searches conversation titles and message content.
- Scopes results to the authenticated user.
- Uses parameterized SQLAlchemy queries with escaped LIKE patterns.
- Groups results by conversation.
- Generates snippets with matching terms highlighted.
- Updated the chat sidebar to display grouped message matches.
- Added styling for search snippets and highlights.
- Added tests for message-content search and user isolation.

## Validation

- [x] `pytest` passes
  *(Note: Targeted chat API tests pass: 15 passed. Full suite has 37 pre-existing migration failures caused by multiple Alembic heads.)*
- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `black --check .` passes
  *(Note: Existing formatting issues remain in unrelated files and routes.py.)*
- [x] Added/updated tests for the change
- [x] Docs updated if user-visible

## Notes for reviewers

Search results are grouped by conversation and message snippets are rendered through DOM APIs with `<mark>` elements, avoiding unsafe HTML injection. Search input is parameterized and strictly filtered by `Conversation.user_id`.

body:
> **Prerequisites met (2026-10-01).** The privacy page at https://o8.run/privacy covers update checks, and the update service endpoint is deployed. The README now describes the ping as current behavior.

## Mechanic

Desktop update checks previously went directly to the GitHub manifest. The update service could not observe those checks. All desktop entry points now use the same native check policy.

## What changed

- Put `https://api.o8.run/v1/update/{{target}}/{{arch}}/{{current_version}}` first, with the existing GitHub manifest as fallback.
- Limit the service attempt to two seconds, including response-body parsing. Give fallback checks a separate 15-second timeout; launch checks remain asynchronous.
- Generate a separate UUIDv4 at first launch and persist it in local update settings. Send only the install ID, macOS version, and stable/preview channel headers, with app version, target, and architecture in the path. No account or hosted-model identifier is used.
- Stop service redirects and retry GitHub locally without ping headers. Clear ping headers from download resources while retaining the updater's artifact signature verification.
- Route launch, Settings, update card, and install/restart checks through the native policy. Add IPC tests with real local HTTP fixtures and persisted settings, plus Rust CI coverage.
- Document the ping in the README and link the privacy page. Service endpoint implementation and active-install counts remain separate work.

## Verification

Before the fix, `npx vitest run tests/update-ping-entry-points.test.ts`:

```text

Test Files  1 failed (1)

```

After the fix, `npx vitest run tests/update-ping-entry-points.test.ts src/lib/app-update/client-restart.test.ts tests/linux-update-download.test.ts`:

```text

```

`node scripts/test-update-ping-native.mjs`, test file `tests/fixtures/update-ping-native/src/lib.rs` (compiles production `src-tauri/src/update_ping.rs`):

```text
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 2.15s
```

The native IPC tests cover exact fields, UUID persistence after restart, preview channel, unreachable/error/redirect/malformed/stalled service fallback, identity-settings failure, and headers withheld from fallback and downloads.

`npx tsc --noEmit`, touched-file ESLint, test classification, and rule-check passed. Independent privacy/redirect source review found no remaining production findings.

The dependency tree was corrected after the first local full run contained duplicate React and ProseMirror modules. The requested repeat of `npm test` now has only the known runtime-inventory failure tracked in #3001:

```text
Test Files  1 failed | 858 passed | 3 skipped (862)
     Tests  1 failed | 5328 passed | 4 skipped (5333)
```

The failing case is `src/lib/runtime/inventory-all-runtimes.test.ts` > `matches main policy by never discovering non-dispatchable registered adapters`. It is tracked separately in #3001 and is not changed here. All other local tests pass. The nine focused TypeScript tests, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and all six native IPC tests also pass on the corrected setup.

[Clean-install CI](https://github.com/hurttlocker/o8/actions/runs/36811479486) is green, including the full hermetic unit suite (859 files passed, 3 skipped; 5,333 tests passed, 4 skipped), type checking, lint, security audit, governance smoke, and both Rust compile/native update-ping contract gates. The additional Windows and Linux compile checks are also green.

Full local macOS `cargo check --locked` remains unavailable because the checkout lacks the bundle resource `helpers/speech-local-x86_64-apple-darwin`. The production updater module compiles and its IPC tests pass locally; Windows and Linux app compilation and native IPC tests pass in CI. An installed signed update, live update-service behavior, and privacy-page disclosure remain release verification boundaries. No release is part of this PR.

**Summary**

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->

The next step toward dropping terser, following #22377: the printer now owns every node method terser's `ast.js` writes, so what it still takes from terser is the node classes themselves, its parser, its ESTree conversion and its `Compressor` constructor.

- `tooling/generate-js-data.js` reads terser's node classes out of `ast.js` into `nodeClasses()` in `data.js`: each class's base, the fields its constructor copies, and its children in `_walk` and `_children_backwards` order.
- The walk phase builds every `_walk` and `_children_backwards` from that table, instead of parsing terser's walk sources with webpack's parser at load time.
- A new `nodes` phase ports the hand-written methods: cloning, `computed_key`, `all_symbols`, `args_as_names`, the class-part visits, `wrap_commonjs` / `wrap_enclose` and the `TreeWalker` look-ups.
- A new `defines` phase ports `global_defs` (`_find_defs`, `resolve_defines`) and `drop_console`.

Both new phases install only against the pinned `ast.js` / `global-defs.js`, like the others. Output stays byte-identical to terser on all 358 corpora. Instructions under callgrind (V8 single-threaded, a 1 GB young generation so collections don't skew it):

| jQuery, `compress: { passes: 2 }, mangle` | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| load + 3 minifies | 19.63B | 19.57B (-0.3%) |
| each further minify | 2.601B | 2.605B (+0.2%, within layout noise) |

Allocation on three.js: 153–154 MB → 149–152 MB, as walks no longer allocate a `forEach` callback per visit.

author: zoelumos
body:
On a fast flick through the lid opening (WebKit, iPhone 14), the drawn frame trailed the scroll by 5-6 frames because the decode window could not keep up.

## Changes
- **Pinned opening:** frames up to p=0.35 are decoded right after load and never evicted. Mobile budget 90 MB (88 MB used, 65 frames); desktop 200 MB (199 MB, 82 frames). WebKit keeps the `img.decode()` path.
- **Velocity-sized window:** for the rest of the story, the lead covers ~300 ms of travel at the current scroll speed, nearest-first in the direction of travel (mobile +40 MB, desktop +64 MB).
- **Never far behind:** if the exact frame isn't decoded, the closest decoded frame is drawn.
- **First-scroll dropped frame:** WebKit was building compositing layers on the first scroll. Fixed with `will-change` on the sticky stage and the starfield, and `visibility:hidden` on the closed mobile menu.

## Measured (390×664, after GPU contention ended)
- **Drawn-frame lag:** 0 in every run (steady, fling-warm, fling-cold, toolbar). Before: 6 on flings.
- **Long tasks:** 0.
- **Chromium, 4x CPU throttle:** 0 frames over 17 ms.
- **WebKit, 20 runs:** 2 single frames at 23-24 ms. Before: one 24-37 ms frame on every steady run.
- **Lighthouse (mobile):** 93. First-load JS 147 kB.

body:
# 📝 Descrição

PUT/PATCH de `/profiles/{id}` exigem a senha do caller quando o `type` cruza `MASTER`, e um caller `MASTER` passa a poder gravar `twoFactor` de alvo `WRITER`/`READER` (inclusive no mesmo pedido que promove a `MASTER`). `name`/`description`/`birthday` e o `twoFactor` de outro `MASTER` continuam só do dono (403 `{id}`). POST `/profiles` não muda.

## 🎯 Objetivos
- Impedir promoção e rebaixamento de `MASTER` só com Bearer
- Permitir que um `MASTER` ligue `twoFactor` de `WRITER`/`READER` para conseguir promover sem o 400 `{twoFactor}` / 403 `{id}` anteriores
- Reutilizar o vocabulário HTTP já usado no signout com senha e na troca autenticada (`400 {password}`, `401 {credentials}`, `429 {credentials}`)
- Manter PUT/PATCH sem alterar o hash persistido nem as sessões

## 📊 Mudanças Realizadas

### 🎲 Alterações no Modelo de Dados
- Nenhuma. O hash do perfil continua `existing.password()`.

### 🔄 Alterações Técnicas
- Campo opcional `password` em PUT/PATCH; `toCommand(id, address)` com limiter `CREDENTIALS` por endereço e e-mail do caller
- Gate de senha em `UpdateProfileUseCase` e `PatchProfileUseCase` depois de 403 `{id}`/`{type}` e 400 `{twoFactor}`, antes do `save`
- `requireOwnerWhenAttributesChange` deixa `twoFactor` de `WRITER`/`READER` para caller `MASTER`; alvo vigente `MASTER` ou caller sem `MASTER` segue 403 `{id}`
- OpenAPI de PUT/PATCH documenta 401 de senha, 429 e a exceção de `twoFactor`; `ProfileWriteErrorResponses` compartilhado com POST criar permanece intacto

### 📱 Impacto na Usabilidade
- Cliente `MASTER` que promove ou rebaixa `MASTER` precisa enviar `password` da sessão
- Cliente `MASTER` pode ligar `twoFactor` de `WRITER`/`READER` e promover no mesmo PUT/PATCH (`type` `MASTER` + `twoFactor` true + `password`)
- PATCH só `{ "type": "MASTER" }` em quem está `twoFactor` false continua 400 `{twoFactor}`
- `WRITER`↔`READER`, o mesmo `type` e PATCH que omite `type` seguem sem senha
- Senha extra fora da fronteira não valida, não confere e não encerra sessões

## 🧪 Testes Realizados
- `./mvnw verify` local **não** foi reexecutado neste push (pedido explícito). A implementação deste commit já tinha passado `./mvnw verify` na sessão anterior (1304 testes, JaCoCo «All coverage checks have been met», BUILD SUCCESS; Compose/`local.env`).
- Unitário: `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest`, `PatchProfileUseCaseTest` (fronteira de senha; MASTER liga `twoFactor` de READER; WRITER alheio 403; outro MASTER 403; promoção no mesmo comando)
- HTTP: `ProfileControllerIntegrationTest` (rebaixa/promove Bruno com senha; Alice liga `twoFactor` da Carla; promove Carla com `twoFactor`+senha; PATCH `twoFactor` false no Bruno 403 `{id}`)

| Referência (issue / épico / critério de aceite) | Evidência de teste (classe#método ou `@DisplayName`) | Notas |
|-------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| PUT/PATCH cruza MASTER com senha ok | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#replacesType`; `PatchProfileUseCaseTest#patchesOnlyType`; IT `putReplacesType`, `patchType`, `patchAliceDemotesAndPromotesBrunoWithPassword` | Promoção com senha |
| Fronteira sem senha / mal formada → 400 `{password}` | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#masterBoundaryRequiresWellFormedPassword`; IT `putDemotingMasterWithoutPasswordReturns400` / `patchDemotingMasterWithoutPasswordReturns400` | Antes do limiter |
| Senha errada → 401 `{credentials}` | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#refusesWrongCallerPasswordOnMasterBoundary`; IT `putDemotingMasterWithWrongPasswordReturns401` / `patchDemotingMasterWithWrongPasswordReturns401` | Sem `save` |
| Limite CREDENTIALS → 429 | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest` / `PatchProfileUseCaseTest` (`refusesWhenAddressLimitIsExceededOnMasterBoundary`) | Endereço e e-mail do caller |
| MASTER liga twoFactor de WRITER/READER → 200 | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#masterEnablesTwoFactorOfReader`; IT `putAliceEnablesCarlaTwoFactor`, `patchAliceEnablesCarlaTwoFactor` | Tipo do alvo permanece |
| MASTER promove READER ligando twoFactor + senha | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#masterPromotesReaderWithTwoFactor`; IT `patchAlicePromotesCarlaToMasterWithTwoFactorAndPassword`, `putAlicePromotesCarlaToMasterWithTwoFactorAndPassword` | Objetivo do segundo commit |
| MASTER não altera twoFactor de outro MASTER | `UpdateProfileUseCaseTest#masterCannotChangeOtherMasterTwoFactor`; IT `patchAliceCannotChangeBrunoTwoFactor` | 403 `{id}` |
| twoFactor + nome alheio → 403 `{id}` | `masterCannotChangeTwoFactorAndNameOfReader`; IT `putAliceCannotChangeCarlaNameAndType` | Extra de twoFactor não autoriza o resto |

author: hitezh
body:
## Why this topic
Netlify replaced V8 isolates with Firecracker microVMs for edge functions (about a billion runs a day): warm invocation went from 25-40ms to 5-6ms p50, with stronger isolation. The obvious reading ("microVMs beat isolates") is wrong. The old path left Netlify's network; the new one doesn't. That makes it a good vehicle for a decision lesson rather than a news summary.

## Central thesis
Speedups usually come from a boundary that moved, not the technology that got the credit. Freed latency can be deliberately spent on safety, and vendor limits are often architecture leaking into your roadmap.

## Title candidates
1. **Netlify got 5x faster by switching to the heavier technology** (chosen)
2. Where your latency really goes: the hop you don't own
3. Faster and safer: why Netlify dropped V8 isolates
4. Before you replatform for speed, count the network hops
5. The 5x speedup wasn't the microVM

Chosen because it carries a counterintuitive, factual claim that an exec or CTO can parse in one glance, with no clickbait.

## Business implications
- Ask "what moved?" before crediting a vendor's Nx claim; the gain may be reproducible without the product.
- Vendor limits (50ms CPU, 512MB, 20MB) came from the execution model; review the constraints your design depends on periodically.
- Owning a path has an operating cost (fleet, control plane, pager); own the boundary that matters, rent the rest.

## Technology implications
- Per-deploy hash as service ID makes the tenancy boundary equal the unit of change.
- Latency saved can buy isolation; same logic applies to sandboxing agent-run code.
- Snapshot-restore VMs share memory state, so randomness needs care when cloning.
- Caveat in the post: Netlify doesn't break down the 25-40ms, so the network-hop share is flagged as inference.

## SEO
- **SEO title:** Netlify Got 5x Faster by Switching to Heavier Tech | Hitesh Sarda
- **Meta description:** Netlify moved edge functions from lightweight isolates to full microVMs and cut latency from 25-40ms to 5-6ms. The lesson for leaders is where the speed actually came from. (172 chars)
- **Focus keywords:** edge functions architecture, Firecracker microVMs, V8 isolates vs microVMs, infrastructure latency, AI agent sandboxing
- **Slug:** faster-by-owning-the-path | **Categories:** technology | **Tags:** infrastructure, architecture, strategy, ai-agents

## Editorial scorecard
| Criterion | Score |
|---|---|
| Originality | 8 |
| Practical value | 8 |
| Executive appeal | 8 |
| Thought leadership | 8 |
| Readability | 8 |
| SEO potential | 8 |
| Social shareability | 8 |

body:
Public remission totals at two visits do not identify who remained in remission, and source-coded failures cannot be treated as measured relapse. This adds an inspectable integer constraint model and a source-audited `demeter evidence paired-remission` command, with a guide for Windows, macOS and Linux.

The DiRECT intake preserves the accepted manuscript's literal `53/129` denominator conflict with ITT 149. Frozen v1 and v2 failures remain unchanged. V3 uses the published abstract's separately stated ITT count and remission numerator under an explicit common-cohort assumption; it does not claim an endpoint denominator or author-issued correction. Marginal-only tables remain available alongside bounds conditional on the reported maintaining-remission subgroup. Assessed nonremission, unassessed outcomes and possible death remain an unknown, coupled partition.

Five attributed aggregate counts are observed benchmark-only records in the registry. Full PDFs/XML remain fetch-only and outside Git. No annual hazards, clinical transition, dietary coefficient, national transport or longevity/cost effect is activated.

Evidence and review records:

- [Guide](docs/PAIRED_REMISSION_OBSERVATIONS.md), [RFC](docs/rfcs/RFC-57-58-paired-remission-observations.md), immutable protocols and retained failure receipts.
- [Source audit and compatible tables](docs/validation/issue-57-58-paired-remission.json).
- [Before/after proof](docs/validation/issue-57-58-paired-remission-before-after.json): prior active parameters, scientific blockers and canonical numerical scenarios unchanged. Fresh acquisition from the guide reproduces all three source pins and the same audit.

author: youssgm3o8
body:
## Supported persistent runtime deployment

Deployments previously had to provide their own runtime startup and restart mechanism. This adds a packaged foreground systemd template and explicit registration helper, plus native Windows SCM support and PowerShell provisioning/registration. Console execution remains available. Installing an archive/prefix never registers, enables or starts a service.

The runtime loads protected external JSON configuration, keeps per-client HMAC credentials in a separate protected file, and preserves audit state outside the install prefix. A restart creates a new incarnation and no authority owner; clients require fresh authentication and explicit admission. The standalone router stays independently owned and has no service dependency with runtime. PR54 is untouched and excluded.

STOP closes the existing authority/final-send gate before draining IPC and the connection worker, disconnecting MAVSDK and recording shutdown evidence. Shutdown audit failure, including an outcome failure during drain, is reported as failure. Lifecycle stopping/owner/generation use one locked snapshot; service running is not aircraft readiness.

Recovery: systemd waits 5 seconds and permits 3 starts per 120 seconds, excluding permanent startup exit 78. SCM crash recovery waits 5 then 30 seconds, then stops retrying; service-reported initialization failures do not restart. Secrets are absent from argv and templates.

## Validation

- Final-head Windows full CTest: 21/21 passed (66.66 s), including service-control, explicit-barrier queued-send shutdown tests, drain-time audit failure, status coherence and runtime authentication/session regressions. Final-head lifecycle qualification also passed.
- Final-head Python: 737 passed, 45 skipped. Lint, format, complexity, changed-file commit hooks and strict documentation passed. The optional whole-tree pre-commit run reports existing missing SPDX in `scripts/hardware/servo_test.c` and formatting issues in `licenses/mavsdk-phase-a/nlohmann-json-MIT.txt` and `docs/aeac-2027.md`; unrelated hook changes were restored.
- Runtime/CLI deterministic peer smoke and persistent-history clean/crash lifecycle qualification passed, including unmatched durable intent without outcome, old-context rejection, no replay, fresh admission, duplicate startup and malformed configuration.
- Linux package and systemd render/path/syntax verification passed under WSL without registration. Hosted Linux exposed baseline ZIP extraction dropping executable bits; the verifier now restores ordinary Unix permissions, masks out special bits, and a test executes the extracted script.
- Mission Planner build/client/config migration, standalone router regressions and process smoke passed.
- Release ZIP/TGZ archive verification and staged install verification passed. Final-head authority-wire/final-send regressions and runtime/CLI peer smoke passed; the full deterministic MAVSDK transport fixture also passed during this slice.
- All final-head hosted checks passed: [Linux/Windows core, lifecycle, package and MAVSDK qualification](https://github.com/YoussGm3o8/NOMAD/actions/runs/36814483384), [lint/complexity/strict docs and advisory checks](https://github.com/YoussGm3o8/NOMAD/actions/runs/36814483339), and [ROS observation adapter](https://github.com/YoussGm3o8/NOMAD/actions/runs/36814483257). Hosted CI remains hardware-independent.

## Deployment and review scope

Windows groundstation/Mission Planner uses same-host loopback IPC and native SCM. Linux systemd supports onboard local CLI placement and deterministic peers. The checked-in standalone ground router requires Windows, so this does not claim a supported Linux groundstation profile. Optional GPU/ROS workloads remain observation/compute only.

Exactly three GPT-6 Luna MAX reviewers audited the base and re-reviewed the implementation: deployment/lifecycle architecture, runtime authority/shutdown/audit safety, and independent packaging/testing/operations. Their findings led to early signal registration, callback-only stop admission, bounded drain, shutdown audit error propagation (including failure during drain), explicit send barriers, coherent status snapshots, safe SCM event diagnostics, package checks, unmatched-intent crash qualification and a corrected OS deployment matrix. All three approve exact final head `b8b49b8d2048e35300701ba50b579d2f3b2319bc`, including the Linux ZIP verifier fix, with no remaining actionable findings. Reviews are read-only evidence; executed checks are listed separately. Concurrent status interleaving is opportunistic, while projection coherence follows from the shared snapshot lock.

Base: `18bb367e4bcf31fb01ac95b820267e3ba75e2c23`. Head: `b8b49b8d2048e35300701ba50b579d2f3b2319bc`. Branch: `runtime-lifecycle`. PR54 is neither changed nor depended on. No hardware, runtime infrastructure or installed host service was modified.

## Changed files

29 files; [complete diff](https://github.com/YoussGm3o8/NOMAD/pull/56/files).

- Runtime lifecycle/status: public runtime header, runtime implementation/status projection, process main, native SCM/console adapter and protected configuration loader.
- Deployment: four `infra/runtime` unit/config/provisioning artifacts.
- Qualification/tests: process supervisor fixture, restart qualification, C++ lifecycle cases, fake-send barrier, runtime IPC test and service artifact tests.
- Packaging/CI: CMake, package verifier, Pixi tasks and Linux/Windows test workflow.
- Documentation: operations, architecture, development, qualification, config guidance and TODO.

Qualification uses a test-only restart driver with shortened delays, static supervisor settings and an unprivileged SCM control adapter. It does not claim installed-host boot recovery, privileged service-account acceptance, deployed upgrade/rollback or physical safety. Those operational checks remain explicit. No service or aircraft hardware is installed, enabled or contacted by ordinary checks.
