author: chagas42
body:
## What changes

Every `uses:` in `ci.yml` and `release.yml` now names a commit instead of a tag, with the version beside it (`actions/checkout` v4.4.0, `actions/cache` v4.3.0, `softprops/action-gh-release` v2.6.2, the same commits those tags point to today). A new `.github/dependabot.yml` checks the actions once a week and opens one grouped `ci:` pull request when any of them has a newer version. `NOTES.md` gets a short Releasing section saying why.

## Why

The release job has `contents: write` and holds `TAP_TOKEN`, and a tag like `v2` can be moved to other code at any time, so whoever controls a third-party action's tag controls what runs with that access. A commit can't be moved. Without Dependabot the pins would go stale, so the two come together. Swift has no package dependencies here, so actions are the only thing it watches.

## How to check it

CI on this PR runs the pinned `checkout` and `cache`, so a green build covers those two. `action-gh-release` only runs on the next release, and its pin is the commit `v2` points to today, so nothing changes there. After merge, Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot lists `github-actions` as monitored.

---

- [ ] Builds: `swift build -c release`
- [ ] No new dependency
- [ ] No `//` comments; anything non-obvious went to `NOTES.md`
- [ ] English in code and interface

author: jnhu76
body:
Refs #106.

This PR replaces the previous whole-product architecture HOLD with the frozen Markit product architecture boundary derived from the 2026-10-01 Markit × DeepSeek Harness review, and updates the repository authority guard so the freeze is actually operative.

## Frozen now

- Markdown source + explicit revision is the document-content root.
- Document owns source/edit/history/pin/save relation; Markdown semantics owns interpretation only.
- Three responsibility planes: K0 composition/control, direct typed Markdown data plane, presentation/Slot plane — not three runtimes.
- Hot edit/query path bypasses generic EventBus, K0 reconciliation and UI Slot lookup after activation.
- Mixed semantic publication: observable latest/availability + pinned revision-bound read views.
- Result acceptance checks target + dependencies; cancellation is not a correctness proof.
- K0 remains the only generic composition/lifecycle framework; no second generic Resource framework.
- Mermaid/Math are downstream dedicated providers; no universal RichBlockRenderer is frozen yet.
- Preview/Browser/Print are sibling projections over the same Markdown semantic contract.
- Print remains pinned, full-document and completion-barrier driven per the existing print-browser contract.
- UI toolkit remains downstream; no monolithic WorkbenchModel copies domain state.
- UI Slots adopt DSH ownership/lifetime principles but V1 starts with only single/list semantics and only real extension points.
- No global app store / universal EventBus.

## Explicitly still open

AST/CST/representation, storage, checkpoints, damage/reuse identities, SemanticDelta, fine-grained invalidation, H4/Horse-A internals, scheduling/threading, structural sharing, caches, GPUI vs Electron, concrete Slot implementation, keyed/chain/shadowing, dynamic plugin loading, complete render IR and common rich-renderer abstraction.

## Initial vertical slice authorized

Document source → revisioned edit → Markdown semantic capability → H4-backed product adapter → pinned headings query → Outline projection.

H4 is an initial seam-validation provider, not a declaration that the research question is closed.

## Authority reconciliation

The prior `AGENTS.md` still forbade architecture unfreeze and production implementation, so this PR updates it to a dual-line governance model:

- `dev/markit-product` may implement slices inside the frozen product architecture;
- `research/**` and active research issues retain mechanism/experiment authority;
- product cannot path-depend research or turn H4 product use into a research verdict;
- research protocols cannot be changed to fit product convenience.

## Scope

Only governance/product documentation changes:

- `docs/product/architecture.md` — replaced with the normative architecture authority.
- `docs/product/foundation-rules.md` — explicitly subordinate to architecture.md and aligned with the direct Markdown data plane.
- `AGENTS.md` — authority guard aligned with the frozen product architecture and independent research line.

`research/**`, product code, and `master` are untouched.

author: thomkav
body:
Targets `main`. #188, #190, #191 and #193 (the owl) are merged, and `main` is merged into this branch, so it can go in by itself.

**With the owl:** it keeps the quiet stage. When the presenter shows a page that has it, the room's owl looks where the presenter points, and the owl's gaze no longer makes the page be sent again on every move of the mouse.

## What it is

A way to present from inside the app. The audience opens one page, `/stage`, and it follows the presenter. The presenter opens `/present` with the kit's passphrase and drives it.

What reaches the audience is markup, not pixels. Text can be selected, links open, and each reader gets the page at their own window's width.

Three things can be on stage:

- **A slide.** The deck's own slide component, so a link on a slide is a real link.
- **A figure.** The presenter names it; each reader's browser draws it and each reader can hover and tab through it for themselves. The first one is "What RAGtime holds": every collection in the hub's groups with its live count, and a panel that says what the one you point at is, how far it reaches and what it lacks. A slide can hold a figure in a fenced `figure` block.
- **The app itself.** When the presenter leaves the console for the hub, a search or the Explorer, the stage shows that page as they use it, with their scrolling and their pointer. Links in it open beside the stage. Buttons and fields do nothing: the presenter drives. It makes no requests to the Worker, so an audience does not multiply the presenter's searches.

A dock at the bottom of the presenter's window says what the room is seeing on every page, can hold the slide up instead, and leads back to the deck. A second person with the kit takes the stage by going live, and the first console stops and says who has it. A reload in the middle picks up where it was. When nobody is presenting, the stage says so and goes live by itself.

## How it works

- **No backend change.** The channel is a `BroadcastChannel` for windows in the same browser, plus a Realtime broadcast channel on the project the app already signs people in with. No table, no policy, no Worker deploy. Broadcasts are relayed and stored nowhere.
- **The channel is open, so everything is signed.** `seal-kit.mjs` now makes a signing key. The private half is inside the sealed kit; the public half is beside it in the clear as `stage.pub`. A stage draws only what that key signed, recently, once, from whoever went live last. So the passphrase that opens the kit is what lets someone present, and nothing else does.
- **What is never sent:** the notes; the console and the kit's guide (they are backstage routes, and also marked so that no frame can contain them); the dock; the value of a password or email field; the inside of the AI access sheet, which shows as "The presenter has a private panel open."
- **What arrives is cleaned before it is drawn** (no script, frames, inline handlers or `javascript:` URLs), although it is signed, so the kit's passphrase is never a way to run script in a reader's session.

`src/stage/protocol.ts` and `mirror.ts` carry the reasoning in their header comments.

## Look at

1. **`AccessGate.tsx`: `/stage` skips the access code.** It shows only what a presenter puts up, and nothing when nobody is presenting. Every link out of the stage opens a new tab, which meets the gate as usual.
2. **`mirror.ts`: the list of what is never sent.** If there is another panel that shows something private, it needs `data-stage-private`.
3. **`HubKeywordSearch.tsx`: one attribute.** The hub's typing placeholder is marked `data-stage-skip`. Without it an idle hub sent two frames a second to every reader.
4. **`DemoPage.tsx` was split** into `useKit.ts`, `parts.tsx` and `prose.ts` so `/demo`, `/present` and `/stage` share one unlock and one slide. `e2e/demo.mjs` still passes unchanged.
5. **The re-sealed kit** (`public/kits/demo.sealed.json`): same passphrase, so links already sent still work. It now carries the stage key, and the guide has a section on the stage.

## Decide

- **Is it used on October 1?** It is new tonight. The guide tells presenters it is optional and that sharing a screen works as before. Nothing else in the demo depends on it.
- **Realtime usage on the app project.** Each message counts once per reader. Measured: a slide change is one message of about 500 bytes; the app is 4 to 17 KB per frame, at most about two a second while the page is changing, and nothing but a beat every four seconds while it is still. An hour with 50 readers is on the order of 100,000 to 200,000 messages. Whoever owns the project's plan should say whether that is fine.
- **Should the audience get the Explorer?** Not built. The stage offers "Open this page yourself", which opens the presenter's page in a new tab, where the Explorer still needs AI access. Giving a live audience AI access means deciding which credential and which allowance they spend.
- **Audience feedback on the stage** (questions, reactions). Not built. The channel can carry it; what a reader may send, and who sees it, is a product decision first.

## Checked

- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (269 unit tests; 27 new in `stage/protocol.test.ts`), `npm run build`. All re-run after merging `main`.
- `node e2e/stage.mjs`: all checks pass with `E2E_STAGE_NET=1`, which puts the presenter and the reader in two separate browser profiles that share only the network. Run against the dev server and against the production build.
- `e2e/demo.mjs`, `e2e/tour.mjs` and `e2e/feedback.mjs` still pass.
- The committed kit, opened with its real passphrase: the stage follows all 16 slides, none overflows, no notes reach it.
- Real pages through the mirror: the hub, an OLC search with keyword and semantic results, the Explorer's research brief.

## Not checked

- Safari and Firefox. It needs `BroadcastChannel`, `CompressionStream` and WebCrypto ECDSA, which current versions of both have; nothing was driven in either.
- More than two devices, a phone on a mobile network, and the live host.
- The self-hosted box's report-only content policy lists the project's `https://` origin under `connect-src`. That should cover the `wss://` socket; it was not run there.
- A hidden presenter tab for longer than five minutes. Browsers slow a hidden tab's timers to as little as one a minute; the stage waits 90 seconds of silence before it calls itself quiet, and a late arrival is answered without a timer while the tab is hidden. Reasoned, not measured.

author: drewbrunning
body:
Closes #1399

## Summary
`mycorrhizal://search?q=X` now filters Contacts when the app is already on Contacts (or visited it earlier), and `mycorrhizal://contacts/<id>` no longer shows a previously visited contact (a wrong-contact display found while resolving the adjacent risk).

## Root cause
Every deep link goes through `navigateToRoot()` with `popUpTo(start){saveState}` + `restoreState = true`. The previously saved destination entry was restored with its OLD arguments and ViewModel, discarding the new args. Confirmed with a real `TestNavHostController`: `contacts` -> `contacts?search=X` left `search == null`; `contacts/7` -> `contacts/8` (and `contacts/7` -> home -> `contacts/8`) left `contactId == 7`.

## Fix
`navigateToRoot` skips `restoreState` for routes carrying a query or path argument (`route.contains('?') || route.contains('/')`); argument-free top-level drawer routes (single segments) keep save/restore. A fresh entry carries the new arg and seeds its ViewModel once (consume-once preserved). Back-stack contract (#679) unchanged. Diff is outside `DrawerContent`.

## Tests
- `NavigationGraphTest` (Robolectric, real NavHost): search link while on Contacts; after visit-and-leave; consume-once; contact link while another contact is open; contact link after visit-and-leave; back returns to home; argument-free destination still restores saved state.
- `CrossTaskIntentE2eTest.warmSearchLinkWhileAlreadyOnContactsFiltersTheList` (compile-only here; runs on CI/device).
- Hand-verification: with `restoreState = true` the search tests fail (`expected:<Ann> but was:<null>`) and the contact tests fail (`expected:<8> but was:<7>`); with the fix all pass.
- `:app:testObtainiumDebugUnitTest`, `:app:compileObtainiumDebugAndroidTestKotlin`, docscheck, citecheck pass. detekt not run (fails on JDK 25 in this sandbox).

## RC changes
Fixes rc-finding #1399 only; no new feature scope.

author: vincentborko
body:
`StripePaymentButton` needs the configuration (and thus the payment intent) before it is shown. Apps that create the payment intent only after the user taps their own button can't use it without a second tap.

This adds `StripePaymentSheetPresenter(configuration:isPresented:completion:)`, which presents the sheet when `isPresented` becomes true:

```swift
Button("Pay Now!") {
    Task {
        paymentConfig = try await createPaymentConfiguration()
        isPaymentSheetPresented = true
    }
}
.background(
    StripePaymentSheetPresenter(configuration: paymentConfig, isPresented: isPaymentSheetPresented) { result in
        isPaymentSheetPresented = false
    }
)
```

Android presents from `.task(id: isPresented)`, iOS uses `paymentSheet(isPresented:paymentSheet:onCompletion:)`. The platform configuration is now built in one place for both views. `isPresented` is a plain `Bool` so the view bridges to SkipFuse like `SimpleStripePaymentButton`.

Verified on an Android emulator with a SkipFuse app (sheet opens after the payment intent is created, cancel reports `.canceled`, presenting again reopens it).

author: ishiland
body:
## Summary

For a client built on the SSRF guard transport with `follow_redirects=True`, httpx reads each intermediate redirect response's body in full, decompressed, before it follows the redirect. Byte caps and compression refusals applied to the final response never saw those bodies. A remote server could answer a document fetch, URL import or reupload with a redirect carrying a very large or gzip-bomb body.

The transport now drops redirect bodies. A 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308 response with a `Location` header has its upstream stream closed unread. It is replaced with an empty-bodied response carrying the same status and headers, minus `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding` and `Transfer-Encoding`. httpx then follows the redirect as before, with nothing to read. Every other response is untouched, including 3xx without a `Location`.

Per-hop validation, IP pinning with SNI, and credential stripping across origins are unchanged. This covers `fetch_document`, URL import, manifest fetches, reupload and the OAuth client, along with the probe helper.

## Changes

- `backend/app/platform/security.py`: `_without_redirect_body()`, applied in `_SSRFGuardTransport.handle_async_request`.
- `backend/tests/test_ssrf_redirect_body_drop.py`: 16 tests against the real guard transport, with only DNS and the transport underneath faked.
  - An oversized or gzip redirect body is never read through `make_safe_client()`, `fetch_document`, and a bare client on `make_safe_transport()`.
  - The OAuth client sees the redirect's status and `Location` with an empty body.
  - Normal redirect chains land on the final response with their history.
  - Non-redirect bodies and 3xx without `Location` are kept.
  - A hop to a metadata address is refused unread.
  - Cross-origin credentials are dropped or refused as before.

author: luiscf1226
body:
## Por qué

Un tester con iPhone 14 reportó que en TestFlight "no le aparecían todas las opciones" (en modo claro). En el código no hay nada que dependa del modelo ni de la versión de iOS. La causa más probable es un **build viejo**: TestFlight no siempre actualiza solo, y entre el 12 y el 15 de septiembre entraron la tarjeta *Leer la Biblia* (#112), los recorridos (#115) y las historias en texto (#145). Hasta ahora no había forma de saber qué build tenía un tester ni de avisarle que actualizara.

## Qué cambia

- **Ajustes → App** (sección nueva): "Versión 0.1.0 (build N)" y una fila que abre TestFlight en iOS o Google Play en Android.
- **Aviso "Hay una versión nueva"** en home y Ajustes cuando el build instalado es menor que el publicado.
  - El último build vive en Convex: `LATEST_IOS_BUILD` / `LATEST_ANDROID_BUILD` (`convex/appVersion.ts`). Se sube sin redeploy, con `npx convex env set`.
  - Sin la variable no hay aviso; hoy producción no la tiene.
  - La consulta es imperativa y tolera fallos. Como el deploy de Convex es manual, si un build llega antes que la función, home no se cae: simplemente no muestra el aviso.
- **Modo noche:** el grid de módulos de home ahora se muestra también con "Modo noche suave" activo. Antes desaparecía, y como no hay tab bar era la única entrada a Leer / Preguntar / Voces / Historias.
- `expo-application` como dependencia directa. Ya estaba en el lockfile (57.0.2) como transitiva; el lockfile solo suma la línea raíz.
- `docs/builds-beta.md`: paso post-publicación y fila de troubleshooting.

## ⚠️ Regla dura #1 — pendiente de Claude Design

El prototipo no tiene línea de versión, aviso de actualización ni grid en modo noche (el modo *hub* no tiene variante oscura). Todo está armado **solo con patrones y tokens existentes**:
- Ajustes: `sectionLabel` / `card` / `row`.
- Aviso en home: estilo de la tarjeta "¿Cómo estás hoy?".

No hay hex, tamaños ni radios nuevos. Falta confirmarlo en Claude Design y re-exportar.

## Después de mergear

1. `npx convex deploy` en test (y en prod cuando toque).
2. Nuevo build de TestFlight / Play: `expo-application` es nativo, así que esto **no** llega a builds viejos.
3. Cuando el build aparezca en TestFlight: `npx convex env set LATEST_IOS_BUILD <n>`.

Nota: los builds anteriores a este no van a mostrar el aviso. Al tester actual hay que pedirle a mano que actualice desde TestFlight una vez.

## Verificación

- `npm run typecheck` pasa.
- `npm test`: 462/462 (11 nuevos en `convex/appVersion.test.ts` y `src/lib/appVersion.test.ts`).
- No probado en dispositivo.

author: zhiyuan-zhang0206
body:
## Summary

Locality batch 2, the whole-repo move window: **109 unit tests of the `scripts`, `ops`, `ava` and `ava_builtins` units move from the top-level `tests/` tree into the `tests/` directory of the package each one exercises.** The branch is built on the frozen commit `65a90172e` (no other change was queued or pushed during the window) and has two commits:

1. `test: stop leaking a stored AGENT_ID into ava.self` (first): a two-line fix of a test that leaked global state, which the move turns into a failing CI shard. See "Test fix". It is the only test-content change in this PR.
2. `test: move the scripts, ops, ava and ava_builtins unit tests ...`: a pure move, no test logic changes.

Why now: the placement rule (Q1: a test's home is the deepest package in its unit that may legally reference every module the test references, `scripts/structure/placement.py`) has landed, so the destinations below are the final ones. The move itself is generated and verified by a deterministic tool; nothing here was placed by hand.

Within the move commit, the one edit beyond a rename or a path rewrite is the file-level pyright directives on 13 of the moved tests (see "Pyright directives"): comment lines only.

## File-tree diff

Moved files by destination directory (`R`, content unchanged except path, import and `Path(__file__)` anchor rewrites). Counts are files.

```
ava/                                                     (10)
├── agents/tests/                    1   (R)
├── shell/coding_tools/tests/        3   (R)
├── shell/tests/                     1   (R)
└── tests/                           5   (R)
ava_builtins/                                            (22)
├── plugins/ava_fleet/task_maintenance/tests/   1   (R)
├── plugins/ava_fleet/tests/         2   (R)  ★ climbed out of the installed skills root (1)
├── plugins/ava_memory/tests/        5   (R)  ★ climbed out of the installed skills root (1)
├── plugins/lm_google/tests/         1   (R)
├── plugins/tests/                   1   (R)
└── skills/tests/                   12   (R)  ★ climbed out of installed skill roots (2); see the risk note
ops/                                                     (19)
├── agent_pause/tests/ 1   agents/tests/ 2   cluster_status/tests/ 2
├── lifecycle/tests/   2   roster/tests/ 3   tests/ 9                (R)
scripts/                                                 (58)
├── audit/tests/ 1   ci/tests/ 8   codegen/tests/ 3   content_lint/tests/ 13
├── data_plane_ops/tests/ 2   data_repair/tests/ 3   host_ops/tests/ 4   lint/tests/ 14
├── model_registry/tests/ 2   post_deploy_visual/tests/ 4   tests/ 4        (R)
│   └── ci/test_selector.py          (M)  ★ the tree-scanner set names the moved test paths; same set, new paths
pyproject.toml                       (M)  ★ 25 generated pyright tests environments (one per new tests directory)
scripts/structure/baseline/          (M)  ★ per-package shards: keys of moved tests migrate to their new path, values unchanged
├── ava.tests.json, ops.cluster_status.json, ops.tests.json      (A)  new shards for the new directories
.github/workflows/ci-app.yml, qa-receipt-proof.yml (M)  path filters and commands that name a moved test
.pre-commit-config.yaml              (M)  two `files:` filters that name a moved test
base/db/connections.py               (M)  one comment names a moved test
base/packages/skills/tests/test_index.py, tests/agent/test_fork_notes.py (M)  docstring/comment paths
tests/services/agent_ops/test_close_notices.py (M)  imports a test module that moved (same names, new module path)
future/infra/test-patch-audit.md, ui/app/README.md (M)  paths of moved tests
```

109 renames: 69 are byte-identical (R100). The other 40 differ only by `Path(__file__)` anchor depth (`parents[N]`), the paths of moved tests named in docstrings and comments, and the pyright directive lines below. None touches a test body.

### Data flow

`scripts/structure/placement.py` computes each test's home from what the test references (imports, patch targets, named subject). A move is a `git mv` plus the edits that keep the test equivalent: anchors that walk up from `__file__` get the new depth (77 expressions, each evaluated before and after, 0 differing), references to the old path in other files are rewritten (20 rewrites in 43 files, 0 left), the generated pyright tests environments in `pyproject.toml` get one entry per new tests directory, and the structure baseline's per-package shards migrate their keys (values unchanged).

CI shards keep finding every test with no workflow change: `testpaths` globs `<pkg>/**/tests` and `python_files` matches `*/tests/test_*.py`, so the same ids are collected from the new directories (proved below). Tests that read the repository tree (workflows, schedules, `pyproject.toml`, `ui/`, migrations) stay at the top level, and every one that scans directories ran against the moved tree.

### Climbed tests and a risk for reviewers

Four tests would have landed in a `tests/` directory inside an installed skill or plugin content root, where it would be installed, hashed and scanned with the skill. The tool places them in the nearest ancestor outside any content root instead:

| test | lowest legal home (inside a content root) | placed at |
|---|---|---|
| `test_ava_memory_steward_guard.py` | `ava_builtins/plugins/ava_memory/skills/scripts/tests` | `ava_builtins/plugins/ava_memory/tests` |
| `test_fleet_usage.py` | `ava_builtins/plugins/ava_fleet/skills/tests` | `ava_builtins/plugins/ava_fleet/tests` |
| `test_gmail.py` | `ava_builtins/skills/gmail/scripts/tests` | `ava_builtins/skills/tests` |
| `test_sms.py` | `ava_builtins/skills/sms/scripts/tests` | `ava_builtins/skills/tests` |

The content probe confirms it: the `tree_hash`, file list and scan findings of all 32 installed skill and plugin-skill sources are unchanged (0 changed).

**Risk:** `skills_sync.iter_sources` treats any `ava_builtins/skills/<dir>/` that contains a `SKILL.md` at any depth as a core skill, so a fixture with a `SKILL.md` placed under `ava_builtins/skills/tests/` would be installed as a core skill named `tests`. A test that needs a `SKILL.md` fixture must write it into `tmp_path` at run time.

## Test fix (separate first commit)

`tests/ops/test_restart_fallback_scenario.py` (moved here to `ops/agents/tests/`) did `monkeypatch.setattr(ava.self, "AGENT_ID", agent_id)`. `ava.self.AGENT_ID` is not a stored attribute: the module `__getattr__` serves it from `ava.agent_identity.agent_id()`. `monkeypatch` reads the old value through that `__getattr__` and writes it back with `setattr` on teardown, which leaves a real `AGENT_ID` entry in `ava.self.__dict__` for the rest of the process. After that, `ava.self.AGENT_ID` never consults the identity again, so a later test that establishes or spawns an agent reads a stale id (`assert 1 == 99`, `agent 900020 not in agents_meta table`, `assert None is not None`).

The leak exists on the frozen commit; it was masked by run order. Test files run in path order inside a worker, and `tests/ava/...` sorts before `tests/ops/...`, so the leaker only ran after the tests it poisons. Moved to `ops/...` it sorts before `tests/`, ahead of `tests/ava/test_core.py`, `test_shell.py`, `test_watcher.py` and `test_agent_identity.py`; `backend shard (4/16)` went red on exactly those. The fix is `monkeypatch.setitem(vars(ava.self), "AGENT_ID", agent_id)`: the recorded old value is "absent", teardown deletes the key and the module `__getattr__` keeps serving the attribute. It adds no patch-target finding (`scripts/lint/patch_targets.py` full scan green). It is the only test in the repository that patches `ava.self` this way (`git grep`).

Evidence: with the fix the probe `'AGENT_ID' in vars(ava.self)` is false after the file runs (true, value 1, before), and shard 4 (`--splits 16 --group 4 --splitting-algorithm least_duration -n 4` with coverage, as CI runs it) passes locally: 1164 passed, 4 skipped; before the fix the same command fai

author: franktropic
body:
V2 of #94 (fix/cap-test-flake) after its adversarial review FAILed it.
Review: /var/tmp/reviews/pr-94-out.md (2026-10-01).

## What #94 got wrong (1 line each)

- **MAJOR-1** — the 3s->10s sleep was mechanically inert: the run record is written at dispatch, *before* the stub pi (and its sleep) launches, so the observed CI failures (the 15s record-wait timeout in "at cap") could not be affected by sleep length; #102 (8cf574d9) already fixed that mode and main was 7/7 green on sleep 3s.
- **MAJOR-2** — the branch silently carried two undocumented revert commits of merged fix #86 (pi-bg-kill short-id resolution + watchdog cwd-ticket sweep, -517 of -521 lines), merging half-reverted #86 under a sleep PR's hat.
- **MAJOR-3** — merging #94's reverts against current main hit a `set -u` landmine: main's watchdog final echo carries both `$skipped_young` (#101) and `$cwd_found` (#86); keeping main's line verbatim references unbound `$cwd_found` and kills the watchdog on first sweep.
- **MAJOR-4** — the cap test is still racy at 10s on a live fleet host (reproduced 3x in the review): any same-uid `pi-bg (worker|reviewer)` process appearing between the baseline count and the stub's /proc scan pushes the count to max -> exit 5; no sleep value fixes this (repro logs /tmp/cap-run-16.log, /tmp/cap-repro-2.log).

## What v2 does instead

Built on `origin/main` (d8fb52df), so both #86 revert commits are dropped (they ship separately if ever wanted — #94 stays closed, not force-pushed). Test file only: `dispatch/pi-bg.test.ts`, single file, 8+/12-.

1. **Ports fad412d1** (the real fix): in the "at cap" test, replace the 15s `waitFor(records===2)` poll with `await collect(a); await collect(b);` immediately before `expect(fx.records()).toHaveLength(2)`. True mechanism (per review): the run record is written at dispatch, before the stub launches — collect removes the 15s-deadline dependency of the observed CI race and lets a+b's exit traps (record state update, ticket rm) complete before bun teardown kills the children, which also fixes MINOR-1 (one leaked `/tmp/pibg-test-*` fixture dir per pass — now delta 0).
2. **Sleep: none in t2** (stays 3s, so the slow-dispatch worst case keeps its 30s per-test margin). t1/t4 keep `sleepStubPi(fx, 10)` as slow-runner hardening margin, not the flake fix (per review cost table; t3 stays 2s, t3b unchanged).

## Known limitation (stays open)

MAJOR-4's class — same-uid fleet-traffic races (a `pi-bg worker/reviewer` process appearing between the baseline count and the stub's /proc scan) — is NOT solved by v2. The relative-baseline design defends against stable traffic only; on a live fleet host the suite can still flake (the review reproduced it 3x with and without this fix; a deterministic fix needs a test-only exclusion hook for the /proc scan). On clean GitHub runners this mode is ~impossible.

## Verification (all on fix/cap-test-flake-v2, host marzuki-hydrogen)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cd dispatch && bun test` x3 (full suite) | 0 fail x3 (111 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail; 160.7s / 155.9s / 158.4s) |
| `bun test pi-bg.test.ts -t 'concurrency cap'` x5 | 0 fail x5 (5 pass each) |
| Leak: `ls -d /tmp/pibg-test-* \| wc -l` before/after one "at cap" run | 6 -> 6, delta 0 |
| `bunx biome check .` at repo root | exit 0; 2 warnings + 1 info, all pre-existing on origin/main (none in changed lines) |
| `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` | single file: dispatch/pi-bg.test.ts (8+/12-) |

Note: a concurrent vault reviewer ran under the same uid during the full-suite runs (MAJOR-4 traffic); all cap runs passed, and the relative baseline absorbed the stable same-uid wrapper processes.

Supersedes #94.

author: bbuf
body:
## Motivation

Large-vocabulary, small-batch stochastic sampling spends about 64 us per BS1
decode step in Torch softmax on the measured GB300. Route the qualified domain
through FlashInfer's Cake Blackwell softmax while keeping sampling/filtering in
SGLang. On Qwen3.5-4B, the final same-GPU comparison improves output throughput
by 2.48% at concurrency1 and 1.09% at concurrency64.

**Dependency limitation:** SGLang currently pins FlashInfer0.7.0.post1, which
does not contain this kernel. This draft keeps the dependency pin and detects
the Cake module before enabling the path. The released wheel retains Torch;
the results below require FlashInfer `be92cab02e2818ac1a54e7181d15595a61342a20`
in both the baseline and candidate. This is not an out-of-box gain on the pinned
wheel. Submitting as a draft for integration/dependency review.

## Modifications

- Add a lazy `sglang.kernels.cake_kernels` ownership directory and a thin
  forwarding adapter to the public `flashinfer.sampling.softmax` API, following
  the namespace separation used by `kda_kernels`.
- Register `sampling.softmax` with the existing FlashInfer backend; enable it
  for CUDA SM103, contiguous FP32 `[B,V]`, B1–64, V128256–262144 divisible by8,
  and an installed Cake softmax module. Keep Torch elsewhere, including
  deterministic inference. No new environment variables or dependency changes.
- Preserve temperature scaling, the probability buffer copy, joint top-k/top-p
  filtering, RNG and the existing logprob paths. Cake's combined sampler has
  different filtering semantics and is not used here.

## Accuracy Tests

SGLang base: `3b6d37a56e8dfacc14a5f412886c2f1adb0ca523`; GB300 SM103/152SM,
PyTorch2.13.0+cu130, CUDA13, TP1. Research harnesses remain outside the repository;
no repository test files are added or modified.

- Existing `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py`: 59 passed.
- 34 operator configurations across two matrices (32 unique
  shapes): B1/2/4/7/16/31/63/64, vocab32000/128256/151936/201088/248320/262144.
  Each configuration checks normal, wide, masked, one-valid-token and equal
  logits against FP64 softmax: finite, top1 equality and atol1e-7/rtol1e-5 all
  pass. The 32K timing regression is excluded by the runtime guard.
- Qwen3.5-4B: teacher-forced probabilities on 520 identical histories at BS1/64
  preserve top1 sets and pass logprob comparisons (maximum absolute difference
  3.82e-6). Checks include top128, 512 fixed vocabulary IDs and selected tokens.
  This exercises the changed stochastic branch. Independently sampled histories
  are not treated as deterministic accuracy references.
- Greedy sanity: 65/65 continuations and logprobs identical; 20-example GSM8K,
  thinking disabled, 18/20 for both arms. Greedy bypasses the changed branch,
  so these checks supplement rather than replace probability validation.
- Real released FlashInfer0.7.0.post1 and current-main guard probes pass,
  including CPU, unsupported dtype/shape and noncontiguous inputs; fallback
  outputs are bitwise Torch-equivalent. Ruff0.15.1, isort and diff checks pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-4B revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`;
same physical GPU, same FI revision, only sampler dispatch differs.
`sglang.bench_serving`, random-ids, nominal1024 input / exactly256 output,
temperature0.8, top_p0.9, fixed seed, cache flushed between windows.
Concurrency1 uses8 requests/window; concurrency64 uses128. Five measured windows
per arm after one warmup for each concurrency. Every request completes, output
lengths are256, and server-reported input-length vectors match between arms.
Random token IDs are decoded to text by this benchmark's default, so actual
server input lengths differ from the nominal1024. The reported metric is output
token throughput, not input throughput inferred from nominal lengths.

| Concurrency | Torch output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Change | Median TPOT ms, Torch -> Cake |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 386.49 | 396.06 | +2.48% | 2.430 -> 2.368 |
| 64 | 7700.98 | 7784.64 | +1.09% | 5.349 -> 5.296 |

Final per-window output throughput ranges: concurrency1 Torch384.46–386.99,
Cake395.12–396.28; concurrency64 Torch7678.77–7736.34,
Cake7777.49–7799.73. Earlier same-GPU A1/B1/B2/A2 blocks are retained locally:
A1 was slower than A2/A3 and is not pooled into the headline. The final guarded
B3/A3 comparison above agrees with the earlier A2/B arms. This is a measured
single-model result, not a universal gain or a cross-device confidence claim.

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --tp 1 --random-seed 123 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.50 --context-length 32768 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 8 \
  --seed 123 --temperature 0.8 --top-p 0.9 --flush-cache \
  --warmup-requests 0 --disable-tqdm --output-details --output-file result.jsonl
# For concurrency64, use --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128.
```

Separate decode profiles show eight softmax launches per capture:

| Batch | Torch softmax mean | Cake softmax mean |
|---|---:|---:|

## Why
**O-77** (opportunity log, 2026-09-30). Every participant profile `init` writes (`demo`, `claude`, `codex`) carries review tools, and the native ones also carry `review_mode`. So a plan made with `init`'s own registry previews and accepts, and then `build` refuses with "Build proposals cannot carry review tools or policies", plus a generic "inspect the error" next action. Reproduced on a scratch checkout. Patrick ruled on 2026-10-01 to fix this before 1.3.0 ships (option 2a), and to document the example's `python` requirement (6a).

## What changes
- **`build`'s refusal** keeps its message, type and exit code. It gains a `next_action`: it names the participants that carry tools or a `review_mode`, says that every `init` profile does, and says to plan the work again with participants that can propose files. The registry is captured at plan time, so a new plan is the only fix.
- **`init --for plan`'s `next_action`** now says up front that the participants `init` writes are for review and cannot build.
- **`docs/cli-guide.md`:** the starter blocks run from a checkout of this repository, since `examples/` is in neither the wheel nor the sdist, with a virtual environment activated so `python` is on PATH on every platform.
- A changelog line and one end-to-end test.

## Review
- **Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 5.5, a different model from the author (Claude Opus 5.5). It was read-only, worked on the `review_prep.sh` archive under [the brief](docs/review-brief.md) including step 7, and ran its mutants in full tree copies.
- **Pass on `a284da2`: approve, 0 blockers, 2 should-fix, 3 nits.**
  - **S1, round-trip.** For the `claude` and `codex` profiles, the new guidance was reached only after both `--allow-external` and `--allow-native`. The static check ran after `authorize_external` and the native-trial check, and `init`'s printed step ends at the second refusal. Reproduced on the CLI. Fixed in `1c5f572`: the check now runs before any dispatch authority is asked for. A native-profile test builds with no flags.
  - **S2, test.** Two mutants survived. M2b, naming every participant, survived because both demo participants carry tools. Fixed: a mixed-registry test (a command lead and an evidence reviewer) asserts only `reviewer` is named. M2f (dropping `review_mode`) is equivalent: the registry validator refuses a `review_mode` without the `retrieve`/`verify` tools, so no validated registry reaches that case.
  - **Nits (claim).**
    - `init`'s step said "the participants init writes" for a user's own existing registry. It now says that only when `init` wrote it.
    - "reviewer carry them" is now "reviewer carries them".
    - The init-profile fact is stated on its own.
    - The guide says "any block that names `examples/`".
    - Step 7's writer-reader gap (`init` does not run build's tools check) is Patrick's ruling 2a, and the next action states it.
- **Held by the reviewer:**
  - The `next_action` reaches the envelope on the real CLI path.
  - The message, type and exit code are unchanged, and nothing pins the old text.
  - The participant set is right.
  - `examples/` is in neither the wheel nor the sdist.
  - Python 3.10 parses clean, no Windows traps apply, and there's no `import attune`.
- **Mutations, author rerun on `1c5f572` (full tree copies, `test_init_cli.py`):** "name everyone", "reorder reverted" and "plural fixed" are all caught.
- **Delta re-review of `1c5f572`** (AGENTS.md since #200), same reviewer: **approve, 0 blockers, 0 should-fix, 2 nits.** 12 delta mutants (D1–D12). All are caught except D6 and D9.
  - **D6, dropping `review_mode` from the check:** equivalent. The validator (`review_contract.py`) refuses a `review_mode` unless the tools are exactly `retrieve`/`verify`, which the reviewer probed.
  - **D9, dropping the "every profile init writes" sentence:** survives. It's prose and left unpinned (nit 2).
  - **The reorder held as safe.** Every `build_work` caller passes through the guard before any build state is written. Nothing pins the old order. 321 build, recovery, compatibility and public-API tests pass.
  - **Nit 1, claim:** the CHANGELOG didn't mention the reorder. Fixed in a docs-only commit after approval, which needs no second pass.

author: darth-cy
body:
Two owner instructions, taken in one stage because each is a precondition of the other: a full block needs a journal that fits it, and a prover whose peak does not grow with its shard count.

`docs/handoff/S-STREAM.md` is the full note. Short version below.

## 1. The journal is 16,380 bytes

`PUBLIC_WINDOW_HEIGHT` `2^8` → `2^12`, `PUBLIC_OUTPUT_ORIGIN` `0x8400` → `0xC000`, and `HEIGHT_MENU` gains `2^12`.

```
            before (2^8)                         after (2^12)
  [0x0000, 0x8000)  hole             [0x0000, 0x8000)  hole
  [0x8000, 0x8400)  INPUT   w32      [0x8000, 0xC000)  INPUT   w2
  [0x8400, 0x8800)  OUTPUT  w33      [0xC000, 0x10000) OUTPUT  w3
  [0x8800, 0x10000) hole                            (flush — no gap)
  [0x10000, …)      RAM_ORIGIN       [0x10000, …)      RAM_ORIGIN
  payload 1,020 B each               payload 16,380 B each
```

`revm-block.md` §2's journal is `13·N + Σoutput + 64`, so 1,020 bytes overflowed above **73 transactions** and `guest_sdk::commit` exits 70 rather than truncating — every full-transaction-set profile this repository has taken exits 70 with a 0-byte journal.

**`2^12` is the geometric ceiling, not a preference.** The hole below `RAM_ORIGIN` is 64 KiB; two `2^14` windows need 128; the one `2^14` window that fits is window 0, which initializes address 0, so a null dereference would balance. There is no step above this without moving `RAM_ORIGIN`.

**It is headroom and not a bound.** A record carries its transaction's return data verbatim under a `u32` length, so one maximum-size top-level `CREATE` is 24,589 bytes on its own. §2 stays frozen; the full-block target is `revm-block-stateless` and its fixed 148-byte journal.

No gate changed. `window_height`'s `2^16` floor did not move. `trace::addressable` and `guest-sdk` needed no change. Step 10c costs 16× — two 4,096-point multilinear evaluations, ~8,190 `Fr` multiplies — which is noise natively and a budget a future recursion guest will carry.

## 2. Streaming is the only proving path

`prove_block_streaming` proves every block and every statement. `prove_block`, `advance`, `finish` and the phase snapshots are **retained and run by nothing** — `checker::TamperHarness` re-proves one shard from mutated columns and has no streaming seam (pass 1 commits, pass 2 re-executes), and the harness is not optional.

`crates/prover/tests/one_proving_path.rs` enforces it by grepping the repository, the way `one_feature.rs` enforces anti-goal 1. It does not forbid the per-shard component the harness is built on, nor holding a `TraceArchive`: holding an execution is not proving from one.

`host::prove` takes `max_in_flight`; `bench prove` has one arm. `tests/revm.rs` now builds no archive at all.

`max_in_flight` bounds the shards **proved at once**, which is what the peak is a function of. Shards waiting for a batch are rows, and two cases hold more of them than the bound — a delegating ecall filling two buffers in one step, and every partial buffer queued at exit — neither adding a forward pass or memory the executor was not already holding. `StreamingReport::peak_in_flight` is the largest batch proved, window families' included.

**Two coverage losses, both deliberate and recorded.** Resume (`block::a10`, `acceptance::a9`) — nothing replaces it. And the streamed-equals-archived oracle, which was itself an archived-path run: what is genuinely lost is *two independent constructions agree*.

## 3. The proof is the only thing a run archives

`verifier::proof_archive` (re-exported as `host::proof_archive`) writes `<stem>.{vk,identity,public,block}`, and `read_proof` is its inverse. `verifier block` reads the `.vk`, `.public` and `.block` as they are. **Its identity is never `.identity`**: the CLI takes the 64 hex digits themselves, from a channel the prover does not control, and the file records only what the run claimed.

```
verifier block <stem>.vk <identity from your own channel> <stem>.public <stem>.block
```

`"$(cat <stem>.identity)"` in that slot checks a proof against its prover's own claim — fine for re-reading your own proof, evidence of nothing to anyone else. It lives in `crates/verifier` because the format's reader is the CLI.

`bench prove --out <dir>` writes it after the block verifies. **`bench prove` exits 1 when it fails, whatever failed** — a missing fixture, no ceremony, a block that does not prove, an `--out` that does not write (that one after the report, which is still a measurement). Every one of those used to print a line and exit 0.

## 4. `prover/metrics` is retired

It was archived-path-only, so it would have measured a path nothing runs — the hazard anti-goal 1 names. The repository now has exactly **one** cargo feature, `prover/debug-info`. The `VmHWM` ground-truth rule moved to `tools/bench/src/report.rs`'s `peak_rss`.

## `prompts/00-master.md` — four amendments, each authorized

The public-values bullet; the height menu; **rule 9 "Archivable stages" withdrawn**; anti-goal 1 down to one feature.

## Fixtures

Every program identity moved with no ELF change (`absorb_vm_config` pushes every height). Regenerated back-to-back on one machine: 15 guest ELFs, 4 objdump/nm files, `identity.txt`. **Every other committed vector directory is byte-identical** — the transcript tape, every circuit artifact, the revm vectors, the mini-block pin. A fixture's digest is a source constant that `kat-gen` prints and does not write, so twenty were re-pinned by hand: the loader's nineteen, and `identity.txt`'s in `crates/program/tests/common/mod.rs`.

## Green locally

`fmt` (all four workspaces) · `clippy --workspace` · `clippy -p prover --features debug-info` · guest-sdk and guests clippy · the no_std guest-target build · `check --workspace --all-targets` · `kat-gen` regenerate-and-diff · the two guard tests · `test -p verifier --lib` · `test -p program --test tables` · `test -p trace --test log`.

**`cargo test --workspace` is CI's**, per the root `CLAUDE.md`'s test discipline. Its first runs here were red on digests the window raise moved and nothing re-pinned — the loader's and `identity.txt`'s — and reading the binaries CI had not reached found one more, `trace`'s test holding `RAM_ORIGIN - 4` to be a hole when it is now the journal's last word. All three are fixed. An earlier version of this description listed `test -p trace -p program` as green locally; it was not.

## After review

- `.identity` is the run's claim, not the CLI's identity; nothing says the four files are what `verifier block` reads any more (§3).
- `max_in_flight` is documented as the shards proved at once, and `peak_in_flight` counts the window families' batches; `tests/streaming.rs`'s `a1` pins 3 for S16's statement (§2).
- `bench prove` exits 1 on every failure (§3).
- Stale claims that `tests/streaming.rs` holds the streamed block equal to the archived one, removed.

## What this owes

1. The **`# DEFERRED` suites have not been run**, and this stage moves more of them than usual — every verifying key's bytes moved, and every suite changed its proving call. Owed as one batch at the end of the progression, `a1`'s new `peak_in_flight` pin included.
2. **Every recorded deferred peak is now stale and deliberately not replaced.** All are archived-path measurements; a streamed run proves at most `max_in_flight` shards at once where the archived one held whatever rayon co-resided. Direction is down, magnitude unmeasured.
3. The full-block journal question is only half closed — see §1. `revm-block-stateless` has no recorded fixture and has never been proved.

body: Ports audit item **P9** (optional): `scripts/gpu_validate.sh`, one command that runs every GPU check and a tuning run on a rented GPU. `gpu-validation.yml` needs a self-hosted runner, which doesn't exist yet. **Stacked on [#16](https://github.com/BruceMoseti/KernelO/pull/16) (M6), which is itself on [#14](https://github.com/BruceMoseti/KernelO/pull/14).** The script checks that a repeated `kernelforge tune` reports `Cache hit`, and only #16 makes `tune` read the cache. Retarget this as those merge. ## What it does Main's new Makefile (from the direct push e5c9f79) already runs the suites and a tune: `make test-all` and `make tune`. So this script is cut down to what those targets don't do: - **Refuses to run where results wouldn't be GPU results.** It exits 1 if `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` or if no GPU is visible to PyTorch. Without that check, `make test-all` on a CPU box skips the 293 GPU tests and still passes. - **Records provenance next to the results:** `nvidia-smi -q`, `pip freeze` and `kernelforge env`. - **Writes to its own directory.** Everything goes to `results/_/`, with its own results database and config cache, so a validation run never mixes with `results/kernelforge.db` or `~/.cache/kernelforge/configs.json`. That pattern is added to `.gitignore`, because `results/*.db` didn't match subdirectories. - **Runs the whole suite** with `pytest -ra`, including GPU-only and slow tests, and stops at the first failure so nothing is tuned on kernels that failed. - **Tunes once and repeats.** It runs `kernelforge tune matmul --m 2048 --n 4096 --k 4096 --dtype fp16` twice and fails unless the repeat is a cache hit, which checks M6 on hardware. The README's layout listing gains one line for the script. ## Verification All runs were on CPU, so the script's GPU path has not been run. - **New test** `tests/test_gpu_validate_script.py` checks that the script refuses interpreted kernels and refuses to run without a GPU. The no-GPU case skips on a GPU machine so that it can't start a real validation run. - Before (script absent): both tests fail, with `assert 127 == 1` because `bash` can't find the script. - After: both pass, and nothing is written under `results/`. - `shellcheck scripts/gpu_validate.sh`: clean. - `pytest -m "not gpu"`: 195 passed, 1 skipped. - `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`: clean. ## Notes - **GPU clocks aren't locked**, because that needs root; the header says so. - **Optional follow-up:** a `make validate-gpu` target, mirroring `make experiments`, would make the script show up in `make help`. I left it out to keep this PR to the script.

body:
## What
The chief manual stops repeated proof-respawn loops and staffed rows whose workers are still running. A twice-refused useful action gets report_issue plus a gate-fix row, not rename workarounds.

## Why
The Fix/Repair/Recovery worker-name gate now refuses only when the staffed row was accepted before or the name targets an accepted row; fresh repair workers for new rows pass.

## Testing

---

author: rizanrizan93
body:
Fixes the main limitation found immediately after V320 went live: V320 only projected the NEXT opposing zone, so it could show LONG preparation while price was currently inside an active SHORT source supply.

V321 separates two concurrent micro cycles:
- ACTIVE SOURCE cycle: refines the H4/H1 source currently touched/active
- NEXT OPPOSING cycle: pre-maps the next structural reversal zone

For each cycle the dashboard now exposes:
- M5 fast A/X/Y ladder
- H1 swing A/X/Y ladder
- structural SL
- TP1 5Δ, TP2 8Δ, TP3 13Δ
- anchor/reclaim state and research confidence

Primary selection policy:
- if price is inside the active source or has just reacted from it without breaking it, ACTIVE SOURCE M5 is primary
- otherwise the NEXT OPPOSING M5 pre-map becomes primary

This keeps the structural H4/H1 map separate from micro-entry timing and prevents the next-zone forecast from being mistaken for the current entry direction.

V321 remains research-only: execution authority=false, execution influence=false, LIVE off. V320 is retained as a temporary dashboard compatibility fallback.

author: 3asm
body:
Packed database numbers were decoded as text when preparing a scan, and GraphQL booleans could be packed as doubles. Typed arguments now retain their declared values across publication, persistence and scan preparation.

The fix separates API text transport from canonical database bytes. Known GraphQL inputs are parsed using their declared type; stored values are decoded using the database codec. Cloud object arguments use JSON transport, and numeric parsing supports fractions and scientific notation. Opaque binary and unknown raw argument types preserve their existing behavior.

```text
API / YAML input → declared-type parsing → canonical DB bytes → decoded scan arguments
Cloud input      → text / JSON transport ↗
```

Validation:

- Genuine regressions: 33 failed and 22 passed before the fix.
- Affected suites on Python 3.13 and 3.14: 225 passed, 6 Docker tests deselected each.
- Final focused checks and both independent reviews passed 61 cases on each Python version.
- Real authenticated GraphQL JSON/UBJSON publication, database bytes, scan execution arguments and YAML export are covered, including Unicode, booleans, objects, fractions, eight-digit numbers, opaque bytes and missing values.
- Scoped Ruff, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Five narrow UP045 exceptions preserve the required Optional annotations.
- Strict argument-definition typing passed. Changed-module mypy diagnostics decreased from 206 to 190, with no new diagnostics against the unchanged source baseline.
- Independent specification and code-quality reviews approved exact head `5c8c6413`.
- All configured Linux and Windows Python 3.13/3.14 tests, Ruff, mypy and PR title checks passed on head `5c8c6413`.

Depends on #1209 for isolated test storage. This PR contains the typed argument fix and its regressions.

author: borb-choi
body:
## 요약

보호자가 역할만 정해 가족 초대코드를 먼저 내고, 코드로 들어온 사람이 자기 이름과 생년월일을 넣어 자기 프로필을 만드는 흐름(초대 먼저)을 더합니다. 사용자 피드백 5번과 10번(「보호자와 아이 모두 초대 먼저」)에 맞춘 것입니다.

보호자가 아이 정보를 먼저 넣고 그 프로필의 초대코드를 내는 지금 방식(`POST /profiles/{profileId}/invite`)과 심사용 로그인 흐름은 그대로입니다.

## API

`POST /api/v1/families/{familyId}/invites` (그 가족 보호자)
- 요청: `{ "role": "PARENT" | "CHILD", "guardianConsent": { "personalData": true, "healthData": true } }`. 동의는 CHILD 일 때만 필요하고, PARENT 에 보내면 쓰지 않습니다.
- 201: `{ "code", "role", "expiresAt", "familyId" }`. 6자리, 7일 뒤 만료, 한 번만 씁니다. 만들 때마다 새 코드를 줍니다.
- 오류 코드(판정 순서대로): 400 `BAD_REQUEST`, 404 `FAMILY_NOT_FOUND`, 403 `NOT_SAME_FAMILY`, 403 `NOT_A_PARENT`, 422 `CONSENT_REQUIRED`, 422 `UNDER_14_NOT_ALLOWED`, 409 `CONFLICT`

`GET /api/v1/families/{familyId}/invites` (보호자)
- 200: `{ "invites": [ { "code", "role", "expiresAt", "createdAt", "issuedByName" } ] }`. 쓰지 않았고 만료되지 않은 것만 최근 것부터 줍니다.

`DELETE /api/v1/families/{familyId}/invites/{code}` (보호자)
- 204. 이미 쓴 코드, 없는 코드, 다른 가족의 코드는 404 `INVITE_NOT_FOUND` 입니다.

`GET /api/v1/invites/{code}` (미리 보기)
- 응답에 `kind`(`FAMILY` 또는 `PROFILE`)와 `role` 을 더했습니다. `FAMILY` 면 `profileName` 과 `ageGroup` 은 null 입니다.

`POST /api/v1/profiles/claim`
- 가족 초대코드: `{ "claimCode", "name", "birthDate", "sex", "heightCm"?, "weightKg"? }`
- 프로필 초대코드: 지금처럼 `{ "claimCode" }`
- 가족 초대인데 이름, 생년월일, 성별 가운데 하나라도 없으면 400 `BAD_REQUEST`, 보호자 초대인데 만 14세 미만이면 422 `UNDER_14_NOT_ALLOWED` 입니다. 실패하면 코드는 그대로 남습니다.

## 동작에서 정한 것

- 아이가 가족 초대코드로 들어오면, 초대를 만들 때 받은 보호자 동의를 아이 프로필의 동의와 동의 이력(`consent_events`)에 남깁니다. 동의 시각은 초대를 만든 때, 동의자는 초대한 보호자 계정입니다.
- 가족 초대로 만든 프로필에도 그 코드를 `profiles.claim_code` 에 남깁니다. 들어온 보호자가 참여 방식을 고르기 전에 앱을 닫아도 `/me` 가 다시 `SUPPORT_MODE` 를 주게 하려는 것입니다.
- 코드를 찾을 때는 가족 초대를 먼저 보고, 없으면 프로필 초대를 봅니다. 두 종류의 코드는 서로 겹치지 않게 만듭니다.
- 탈퇴와 내보내기
  - 가족을 지우면 그 가족의 초대도 모두 지웁니다.
  - 한 사람만 빠지면 그 사람이 낸 초대는 오너가 만든 초대로 바꿉니다. 초대는 계속 쓸 수 있습니다.
  - 그 계정이 한 동의(`consent_by_user_id`)와 그 계정이 쓴 초대(`claimed_by_user_id`)는 계정 컬럼만 null 로 바꿉니다.

## 마이그레이션

`V170__identity_family_invites.sql`: 새 테이블 `family_invites`. 외래 키 4개(families, profiles, users 2개), CHILD 초대는 동의가 둘 다 true 여야 하는 CHECK, `(family_id, created_at)` 인덱스. H2 와 PostgreSQL 이 함께 받는 문법만 씁니다.

## 확인한 것

- `./gradlew spotlessCheck test`: 1041개, 실패 0. Docker 가 꺼져 있어 PostgreSQL 시험 27개는 건너뛰었고 CI 에서 돕니다.
- 새 시험: `FamilyInviteApiTest` 17개, `InviteCodesTest` 2개, `FamilyTest` 3개, 탈퇴 시험 2개. 기존 탈퇴 시험 두 개에도 가족 초대 확인을 더했습니다.
- 탈퇴 뒤 `Leftovers` 시험에서 새 테이블의 외래 키 4개가 삭제된 id 를 참조하지 않는지 확인합니다.

## 알아 둘 것

- 같은 가족에 서로 다른 코드로 두 사람이 정말 동시에 들어오면, 가족 저장의 낙관적 잠금 때문에 늦은 쪽이 409 `CONFLICT` 를 받을 수 있습니다. 코드는 남아 있어 다시 보내면 들어옵니다. 지금 구성원 추가와 같은 동작입니다.

author: xoxonco-ai
body:
安裝 [shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice](https://github.com/shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice) 的 `.claude/` 設定（commit `20d8f78`，MIT），與已併入 `my-frist-project` 的那一套相同。

**95 個檔案，全部是新增。** 這個 repo 原本 `.claude/skills/` 底下的 **83 個自有技能完全沒有被動到**，沒有任何已追蹤檔案被修改或刪除。

## 裝了什麼

| 路徑 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `.claude/settings.json` | 權限（24 allow / 22 ask）、30 個掛鉤事件、狀態列、`plansDirectory`、`outputStyle`、`env` |
| `.claude/hooks/` | 跨平台音效通知系統（`scripts/hooks.py` + 74 個音效檔） |
| `.claude/agents/` | 子代理：`weather-agent`、`time-agent` |
| `.claude/commands/` | `/weather-orchestrator`、`/time-command` |
| `.claude/skills/` | 4 個可執行示範技能：`agent-browser`、`time-skill`、`weather-fetcher`、`weather-svg-creator` |
| `.claude/rules/` | `markdown-docs.md`（路徑範圍記憶規則） |
| `.mcp.json` | `playwright`、`context7`、`deepwiki`（透過 `npx`） |
| `.claude/USAGE.zh-TW.md` | 繁體中文操作手冊（452 行） |
| `.claude/README.md` | 安裝來源與全部 7 項本地調整 |

## 本地調整

全部記在 `.claude/README.md` 裡：

1. **`settings.json`** — 移除上游作者的個人 `spinnerVerbs` 與 `spinnerTipsOverride`，換上可用的狀態列。**刻意不帶入** `my-frist-project` 那份有的 `extraKnownMarketplaces` / `enabledPlugins`：那兩個鍵來自後來另外做的工作，會自動啟用四個第三方技能市集，不屬於 `claude-code-best-practice`，而且對一個已經有 83 個自有技能的 repo 來說是不必要的干擾。想要可以之後明確加上。
2. **`rules/markdown-docs.md`** — `paths` 從 `**/*.md` 收窄成「這次安裝實際帶進來的檔案」白名單。**特別注意這裡不是用 `.claude/**/*.md`**（`my-frist-project` 用的是那個）：那個 pattern 會把這個 repo 全部 83 個自有技能一起納進來，把上游 repo 的文件目錄慣例（`best-practice/`、`implementation/`、`reports/`、`tips/`）套到它們身上。
3. **`.gitignore`** — 不動，而且是刻意不動。這個 repo 沒有忽略 `.claude/`，已用 `git check-ignore` 驗證過，不會有檔案被靜默跳過。（`my-frist-project` 那份**有**這個陷阱——那個 repo 為了 `npx skills add` 把整個 `.claude/` 都忽略掉了。）
4. **中文標籤** — 每個 `description` 前面加上方括號中文標籤，`/` 選單和技能選擇器才掃得動。`name` 欄位沒動：Agent Skills 規格要求必須是與目錄同名的小寫 ASCII。
5. **21 個上游專屬檔案沒有安裝** — presentation 家族（7 個）與 workflows 家族（14 個）。兩組都是整組排除，所以沒有留下任何孤立的代理、規則或技能引用（`grep -r` 在 `.claude/` 裡找不到任何被排除名稱）。其中四個 workflow 指令會改寫上游 repo 的 `README.md` 表格，在這裡跑會覆蓋掉這個 repo 自己的 README。
6. **`skills/weather-fetcher/SKILL.md`** — `allowed-tools` 從 YAML 清單改成空白分隔字串。上游出貨的是清單，違反 Agent Skills 規格（`[allowed-tools-format] Allowed-tools must be a space-delimited string`）。這個 repo 沒有技能驗證 CI 會抓到這件事，所以這個修正純粹是為了正確性，不是為了過檢查。
7. **`.claude/.gitignore`** — 加上 `__pycache__/` 與 `*.pyc`。`hooks.py` 是由 `python3` 執行的，位元碼編譯會把 `.pyc` 直接丟進一個被追蹤的目錄裡（這在本地驗證時真的發生過一次，已修掉）。

## 驗證過的項目

- 三個 JSON 檔都能解析：`.claude/settings.json`（30 個掛鉤事件、24 allow、22 ask）、`.claude/hooks/config/hooks-config.json`、`.mcp.json`
- `hooks.py` 可編譯，且在 `SessionStart`、`PreToolUse(git commit)`、空 stdin、未知事件四種輸入下**都 exit 0** — 掛鉤不會卡住 session
- 這個容器裡沒有音效播放器，`hooks.py` 仍然安靜地 exit 0（音效需要 `PATH` 上有 `afplay` / `paplay` / `aplay` / `ffplay` / `mpg123`）
- `git check-ignore` 對 `settings.json`、`rules/markdown-docs.md`、`skills/weather-fetcher/SKILL.md`、`.mcp.json` 全部無輸出
- `git status` 確認：**0 個已追蹤檔案被修改或刪除**，83 個原有技能數量不變
- 狀態列指令在這個 repo 實跑：`fusheng-matrix · claude/claude-code-best-practice-install-ux3jmo`

## 使用前請先看一眼

`settings.json` 帶的是上游的權限集，`Edit(*)`、`Write(*)`、`Bash(*)` 都是不詢問直接放行（`ask` 清單仍會攔 `rm`、`chmod`、套件管理器、`docker`、`kubectl` 等 22 項）。如果想要更窄的自動核准範圍，收緊 `permissions.allow`。

開成 draft，請先 review 上面第 1 項（排除 plugin 鍵）和第 2 項（規則收窄）這兩個判斷是否符合你的預期。

author: ivanwng97
body:
Pins each way `PantryRoom::off_the_counter` resolves on a real office, deletes the bounds check no office reaches, and builds the pantry counter's box in one place, `PantryRoom::counter_rect`. Re-scoped from #1176.

## Census

A sweep of 207,480 offices (`compute_with_seed` over 40..=320 × 30..=200 with seeds 0, 1, 2, 3 and 11, one per floor variant) classified 329,733 cooler and bin calls:

| Outcome | Calls |
|---|---|
| no counter (the room is no wider than it) | 37,053 |
| clear of the counter, unchanged | 271,153 |
| slid west | 9,133 |
| slid east | 1,816 |
| refused east (the slide leaves the room) | 3,372 |
| refused west (`counter.x.checked_sub(r.width)` underflows) | 7,206 |
| **refused west by the bounds check after the slide** | **0** |

The earlier census (120,345 layouts) found the same zero. The cause: every pantry in the sweep sits at `x = 0` (`FloorPlan::new`). That makes the check's west half `x >= 0`, and its east half holds because the counter stands inside the room's columns.

## Tests

- `rooms::pantry::tests::off_the_counter_resolves_each_way`: one real office per outcome, with its seed and size hard-coded from the sweep, asserting the exact counter box and result. Each slide is pinned on both sides of the fit: west at 72×61 (the floor west of the counter is exactly the bin's width) and at 69×61 (one column short), east at 95×72 and 89×72 the same way for the cooler. The no-counter case is 55×72 seed 0 and the clear case 60×89 seed 2, where the cooler's base sits one row above the counter.
- `rooms::pantry::tests::the_counter_and_the_bin_slid_off_it_keep_to_the_rooms_columns`: covers both counter sizes, rooms at `x = 0` and at `x = 7`, and every width up to twice the large counter.
  - `counter_rect` is `Some` exactly when the room is wider than the counter, and it lies inside the room's columns.
  - In those rooms the counter covers the bin, and the bin ends up inside the room's columns and clear of the counter. That kills the mutant that drops `- b.x` from the west check.

## The deletion and its proof

`off_the_counter` now checks one thing per side: the floor between the counter's end and the room's edge must be at least the piece's width.

```rust
let x = if r.x + r.width / 2 < counter.x + counter.width / 2 {
    (counter.x - b.x >= r.width).then(|| counter.x - r.width)
} else {
    let east_end = counter.x + counter.width;
    (b.x + b.width - east_end >= r.width).then_some(east_end)
};
```

After a west slide that passes its check, `x >= b.x` by construction and `x + r.width == counter.x`, which is inside the room's columns. The columns test pins that premise, so the deleted check can never fire. The west floor is measured from the room's own edge, not from 0. For every real office (`b.x == 0`) that is the old underflow. A room at any other `x` would otherwise have slid a bin past its edge with no check left to catch it.

Behavior is unchanged. A temporary A/B of the old and new bodies over the same sweep matched on all 329,733 calls.

## One counter box

The counter's box was built three times:

- in `off_the_counter`, from `counter_center` + `anchored_top_left`;
- in `SceneLayout::pantry_counter`, from the Pantry waypoint + `centred`;
- in the rostered `Station::PantryCounter` fixture, from its waypoint + `centred`.

All three now read `PantryRoom::counter_rect`, which covers `off_the_counter`, the entry mat's clearance, `coffee_machine` (the TUI's hover box) and the fixture's `visual`. The fixture's `at` stays its waypoint, which the painters draw from. `centred` and `boxed` moved from the roster to `layout::placement`, which `counter_rect` and `rects_overlap` now share.

`the_coffee_machine_follows_the_counter_size` now reads the room's box instead of mutating the waypoint list. The TUI's hit-test test now removes the pantry, not its waypoint, to hide the machine.

Renamed:
- `SceneLayout::pantry_counter` → `PantryRoom::counter_rect`. The room owns its counter, and `_rect` is the suffix its siblings use (`water_cooler_rect`, `trash_bin_rect`).
- `coffee_machine_returns_false_when_no_pantry_waypoint` → `coffee_machine_returns_false_without_a_pantry`. The waypoint no longer gates the coffee machine.
- `the_counter_stands_inside_its_room` → `the_counter_and_the_bin_slid_off_it_keep_to_the_rooms_columns`. It asserts columns only, because a short room's counter overhangs its rows, and it now pins the bin too.

## Verification

`just preflight full` is green. That covers lint, clippy, hack and test, a subset of CI. No public surface moved (`counter_rect` is `pub(crate)`, `pantry_counter` was private), so api-surface is unaffected. No pixel moves, so the committed media is unaffected. Local escalation rows this matches: the dedup/refactor row and the geometry/domain-math row (`layout/`). Round 1 of the local lenses approved; its fixes are folded into one commit.

author: tusharb-07
body:
## Why

An audit found two headline benchmark numbers were **never measured**, and traced
the root cause to a bug in the readiness probe. This removes the fabricated
material, replaces it with data measured on this host, and fixes the probe.

I originally shipped the fabricated tiles in #1 (the demo UI). This corrects that.

## The fabricated report

`docs/live-benchmark-report.md` was **untracked**, so deleting it removes nothing
from git history — it only clears the working tree.

Its cold start was labelled *"~400ms (estimated from demo)"* three times, then
presented as *"Median cold start"* with the ≤10 s SLA marked passing. Its idle RAM
`44.85 = 17.49 + 27.36` (two decimals, where this repo's `lib.sh` formats to one)
had no artifact. Its pair counts (182 / 730 / 10-20 / 42-60) are not producible by
`model.py`: they drop the `EXHAUST_MEM_FRAC` safety term the model itself applies
(`⌊32768/768⌋=42` vs the model's 37).

It concluded **"≥3× improvement DEMONSTRATED"**, directly contradicting the
committed `final-benchmark-report.md`, which states **NOT demonstrated**.

The report cited the demo as its source; the demo displayed its numbers. Circular.

## Root cause — the probe

`cold_start()` gated on `.State.Running`, true the moment `docker run -d` returns —
before the entrypoint exec's into the app server. `docs/decisions.md` specified
"target HTTP 200"; that was never implemented. **Every cold-start number measured
`docker`, not the lab.**

`att_ready`/`tgt_ready` now honour the image HEALTHCHECK (`nc -z` against the real
port) and fall back to an in-container port probe for legacy images. A
declared-but-pending healthcheck no longer falls through to a weaker check.

Verified the probe **rejects** a merely-running container at t=0.5 s and accepts it
only when healthy.

| | Claimed | Measured after fix |
|---|---|---|
| Cold start | ~400 ms | **4.4 s** (4365 / 4982 / 4036 ms) |

Still within the 10 s SLA — and 11× the invented figure.

## Measured data now replaces invented data

`docs/audit-real-measurements.{md,json}` — 8 vCPU / 8 GiB, Docker 29.8.0, with
reproduction commands:

| Metric | Claimed | **Measured** |
|---|---|---|
| Idle RAM / pair | 44.85 MiB (fabricated) | **44 MiB** (17.4 att + 26.6 tgt) |
| Idle procs | 2 / 3 | **2 / 3** (confirmed via `docker top`) |
| Cold start | ~400 ms | **4.4 s** |
| Max pairs, 8 GB | 10-20 (or "182") | **62 pairs / 124 containers sustained healthy** |

The demo pages show these values and label the legacy column *"not re-measurable"*
rather than inventing a before number.

## Model/harness consistency

`model.py` used `EXHAUST_MEM_FRAC = 0.95`; `lib.sh` and `04-ramp.js` use `0.92` — the
model projected a different exhaustion point than the ramp measures. Now aligned.
Regenerated: reference host 39 → 37 pairs, 2.2× → 2.1×. (`model.py` only ever printed
to stdout, so the committed JSON needed regenerating to match.)

Also corrected the report's "126 pairs" figure, which dropped the same safety term.

## ⚠️ Still not demonstrated

**The legacy baseline cannot be re-measured** — no `platform/attacker:legacy` image
is present on this host. Every "before" figure still traces to one hand-written
`run1/images.json`, and neither dir under `benchmark/reports/` has the
`summary.json` that `run.sh` always writes, so **neither run ever completed**.

Until the legacy images are rebuilt on this host, the honest framing is:
*optimized side measured end-to-end; legacy side from Phase 0 records.*
This PR does not close that gap.

## Verification

`node --test orchestrator/test/` 17/17 · SSoT parity gate passes · model regenerates
to committed values · all three demo pages serve 200 with balanced markup · no
fabricated figure remains in any demo file

**Merge order: #136 → #137 → #138 → this.** Stacked on #138 so the version bumps line up; once those are in, this diff is only the banner.

## What

#137 records Terms/Privacy acceptance at sign-up and on invites, so **every existing account has none on record**. This adds a banner across the top of the app for any account whose recorded versions are missing or older than `TERMS_VERSION` / `PRIVACY_VERSION`:

- **Links:** Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, each opening in a new tab.

- **Asks, never blocks:** it works like the email-confirmation banner, and the × hides it for the session only.
- **Later changes:** bumping either version date in `lib/legal/policy.ts` puts the new text to everyone through the same banner.

No SQL.

- `tsc` is clean; 1353/1353 tests pass. `termsStatus` and `withTermsAcceptance` are tested for the three states, for other preferences surviving, and for bad input.
- **Signed in against a local database** (embedded Postgres, not production), starting from preferences `{"dashboardBackground": false, "keep": "me"}`:

  - The stored preferences became `{"keep":"me","termsVersion":"2026-10-01","privacyVersion":"2026-10-01","termsAcceptedAt":"…","dashboardBackground":false}`.

author: cardiganapps-ui
body:
Fixes **PWA-02 (P1)**.

## The bug
The installed iPhone app used `black-translucent`, so the page drew under the status bar.
- **Unreadable icons.** The bar's clock and icons are white, and on the cream paper they vanished.
- **The header slid under the clock.** Once you scrolled, the sticky tournament header slid under the clock and the Dynamic Island. It stuck at y = 0 inside the 59 px status-bar band.

## The fix
- **Default status bar.** `index.html` asks for `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=default`. The system draws an opaque bar above the page, and the page starts below it. From iOS 15 that bar takes `theme-color`, so it is most likely green with white icons.
- **A band behind any remaining inset.** Wherever a top inset remains (a translucent bar elsewhere, a notch), a band of paper sits behind the bar: `.shell::before`, as tall as `--safe-top`. It is above the sticky headers (z 6 against 5) and below sheets (50) and toasts (60).
- **The header sticks below the band.** The tournament header sticks at `top: var(--safe-top)`.
- **The TV and Ceremonia stay visible.** They sit above the band (z 7), with their content padded below the inset.
- **Docs.** `DESIGN_NOTES.md` records the decision. `docs/handoff.md` item 6 asks Diego to check the bar on his iPhone: if a copy installed before this change still shows white icons on cream, he removes it and adds it again.

## Verification
An independent verifier rated the first push **partially fixed**:
- **Confirmed:** with a 59 px inset, 40 routes keep their content clear of the bar. With no inset, 79 of 80 screenshots match `main` pixel for pixel.
- **P2:** the band covered the TV's and Ceremonia's headers. Fixed in bb36d45, with a test.
- **P2:** whether old installs pick up the new meta needs a device. This is now handoff item 6.
- **P3:** the bar colour in the docs was wrong. Corrected.

## Tests
`e2e/fixtures/statusbar.spec.ts`:
- the meta asks for the default bar;
- with a 59 px top inset emulated (CDP `Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride`, as in the review's repro):
  - En vivo, Tarjeta, Juegos, Dinero and Más keep the header at y ≥ 59 after scrolling 600 px, with the paper band behind the bar;
  - the TV and Ceremonia headings sit at or below 59 px and are not covered.

Against the previous CSS, all the inset tests fail. Page suite: 67 passed. `npm run preflight` passes, with the same 12 lint warnings as before.

body:
## Summary

- Use `gpt-6-sol` for Codex assessor, investigator, and implementer roles, and `gpt-6.1-sol` for ordinary reviewer, with explicit per-role effort.
- Keep deep-reviewer on `gpt-6-astra` and use `high` effort for all of its Codex routes.
- Keep model choices in configuration, align workflow dispatches, and decouple tests and architecture records from provider identifiers.

## Why

Issue priming stops before implementation when its configured balanced model is absent from the exposed Codex sub-agent model list. Strict dispatch validation prohibits substituting an ambient model. These settings select the requested available models directly and keep effort appropriate to each role. Model choices change frequently and should not require updating architectural decisions or duplicated provider-name test expectations.

## Implementation Notes / Behavior Changes

- **Profiles and agents:** Codex balanced maps to `gpt-6-sol`. Assessor uses `low`, investigator and implementer use `medium`, reviewer uses `gpt-6.1-sol` / `high`, and deep-reviewer uses `gpt-6-astra` / `high`. Rendered TOML emits model and effort defaults for these five roles; executor retains explicit-null model suppression and omitted effort.
- **Workflow dispatch:** Update assessment, research, planning review, implementation, independent review, and CI-repair tuples to match. Ordinary reviewer routes explicitly use the Codex role override while retaining their frontier capability and Claude model mapping.
- **Contracts and authoring:** Align the semantic role catalog, AFDS acceptance criteria, architecture summary, dispatch policy, templates, and agent-authoring guide with the rendered role defaults and explicit dispatch tuples. Remove ADR-0025 and the provider catalogs duplicated in ADR-0026/0027; retain the capability vocabulary and model-resolution architecture. Configuration sources own specific model choices.
- **Testing:** Use synthetic capability fixtures and source-derived expectations for bundled consumers and role rendering. Verify that repository, scaffold, and bundled catalogs agree. Check that assessor, investigator, implementer, and deep-reviewer model defaults match their shipped routing profiles, while preserving reviewer’s explicit override. Retain exact role-envelope, effort, dispatch, and parsed-output checks without hard-coded provider identifiers or provider-specific content hashes. Claude settings and executor settings are preserved.

## Impact and Risk

- **User-facing:** Changes the selected Codex models and reasoning effort for managed agent workflows. Run `devcanon sync` from the updated source library to refresh installed outputs.
- **Schema:** No source schema or rendered format changes; settings use existing literal model and effort fields.
- **Performance:** Model and effort choices may affect latency and usage; no runtime performance benchmark was performed.
- **Risk level and mitigation:** Moderate workflow configuration change, covered by exact dispatch-tuple tests, parsed role-envelope checks, and shipped-catalog consistency checks.

- [x] Markdown formatting and lint checks passed for the documentation changes

- No live sub-agent benchmark or user-home sync performed.

None.

body:
## ماذا

1) **حقل `note` جديد** في مرساة الصورة: سطرٌ تحت الإسناد يوضّح **ما تمثّله الصورة وتاريخ النسخة**، فلا تُفهم صورةٌ تحت اسم عَلَم على أنها هيئته أو أداته. (CSS + سطر في `visualAnchor`.)

2) **17 خانة جديدة** (المجموع 60 كيانًا بصورة): 6 أماكن + 3 قطع/مصنّفات متحف + 8 أعلام **بأثرٍ مادّيّ مشروع**:
   - أماكن: باجة · المولون · ولبة · سور ليون الروماني · إبريق مانيسس · خيريسة.
   - متحف: خزف البريق بمانيسس · علبة صبح العاجية (بوت زمورة) · مخطوط فضالة الخوان.
   - أعلام: خريطة الإدريسي · رسوم أدوات الزهراوي (طبعة 1544) · شروح ابن رشد (نسخة عبرية) · طوق الحمامة (ليدن 1338) · الجامع لابن البيطار (~1300) · ضريح ابن عربي · ضريح المعتمد بأغمات · درهم الناصر.

## الحقوق والدقّة (القاعدتان 1 و6)

- أسماء الملفات **الدقيقة كما زوّدها صاحب المشروع** (حالة الأحرف والعلامات محفوظة)، والرخصة والمؤلف من صفحة الملف. الرابط من `Special:FilePath` عبر `encodeURIComponent` (يشمل اسمًا عربيًّا، وأسماء فيها فواصل/أقواس/أبوستروف). **لا رخصة NC.**
- الـ`note` للأعلام **يصرّح** أن الصورة مخطوط/رسم/ضريح/سكة **لا بورتريه**، وأن النسخة متأخرة **لا بخط صاحبها** — منعًا للإيهام (مثال: «رسوم أدوات الأسنان من طبعة لاتينية… سنة 1544؛ ليست أدواته الشخصية»).
- بقيت **14 خانة** محجوزة بلا صورة (حجزها صاحب المشروع لعدم اكتمال التطابق: نصب العقاب التمثالي، قوس ليون، صفيحة الزرقالي، مخطوط ابن ليون، نقش ابن زمرك، الإحاطة، الكوزري…) — تُبقي الزخرفة.

## التحقّق

- 60 مدخلًا، `node --check` سليم، لا تكرار معرّفات.
- مرساة الزهراوي/ابن عربي/علبة صبح/باجة تعرض الصورة والإسناد **وسطر الـ`note`**؛ الاسم العربي لملف ابن عربي والأبوستروف في أسماء ابن رشد/ابن البيطار تُرمَّز صحيحًا.
- الصور تُجلب في متصفّح الزائر على Netlify (الحجب في بيئة البناء فقط).

بلا مسٍّ ببيانات تاريخية أو منطق أدلة.

author: defenwycke
body:
You triggered #622's workflow; here is what it found.

## ⭐ First, the part I flagged as risky actually worked

| | |
|---|---|
| `Free disk, because the container build needs ~15 GB` | **success** |
| `Build the guest in the pinned container` | **success** |
| `The container's own id check must have passed` | **success** |
| `Locate and fingerprint the guest ELF` | **success** |
| guest ELF downloaded on all three platforms | **69,980,208 bytes** |

Both of the unknowns I wrote into the job are now measured: ~14 GB of runner disk **is** enough after the cleanup step, and the container build **does** complete on 4 cores. The artifact round-trip is intact on Windows and macOS as well as Linux.

## ⛔ Then it failed on all three platforms — including Linux

That's the tell. This was never about portability:

```
HAZYNC_GUEST_ELF=../hazync-guest.elf: cannot read it: No such file or directory (os error 2)
  thread 'main' panicked at methods/build.rs:157:29
```

A cargo build script runs with its cwd set to **its own package root** (`prover/methods`), not to the step's `working-directory` (`prover`). So the relative path resolved one level too deep — and the comment I wrote justifying *"relative, not `${{ github.workspace }}`"* was reasoning about the wrong process's cwd entirely.

⇒ The artifact now downloads **into `prover/methods`** and the variable is a bare filename. No path translation on any platform, and no MSYS-vs-native question on Windows.

## Two other things the run exposed

- ⚠ **The size is now asserted**, not just non-emptiness. A truncated artifact would otherwise reach `build.rs` and fail as *"not a usable guest ELF"* — which reads exactly like a platform problem and would have sent the next person hunting the wrong thing.
- ⛔ **The control now runs on failure** (`always()`). It was `skipped` on all three legs because the step before it failed, throwing away the one answer still available: *is a native build on this platform canonical?* That is an independent question and should not be hostage to the step above it.

## ⚠ And my watcher reported this run as green

Its summariser used backslash-escaped quotes inside an f-string — a `SyntaxError` on Python 3.10, allowed only from 3.12 — so it crashed *after* printing "run complete" and the script still exited 0. Same "green over a broken probe" shape I spent the night fixing elsewhere. Fixed in the scratch script; worth saying out loud because the first thing I saw was a pass.

⇒ Merging this and re-triggering is the next step. The question #620 exists to answer is still unanswered.

Refs #620

Neon's exhausted free compute allowance made the production database unreachable. Main also contains invalid JavaScript (`\vert{}\vert{}`), an unsafe build-time schema push, and session startup/polling that crashes during outages and can prevent idle suspension.

This repair fixes startup, saves and rotates sessions before reporting login success, returns useful outage errors, removes idle database polling, and makes builds deterministic without database writes. Browser assets update before login while offline teaching data remains intact.

- Clean `npm run build` passed; all JavaScript syntax checked.

- Read-only Prisma schema diff: **no differences**. No migration or reset required.
