The baseline branch still points to `857d1033925bcbb4eec4215e9911e2d3bdc62430` and is untouched. Production is `teacher-planner` at https://teacher-planner-qoxn.onrender.com. author: genshingarcia222-sudo
body:
**Base is `feat/knowledgebase-expansion`, deliberately — not `main`.** This PR does not merge the corpus. PR #21 stays exactly as it is and its integration gate stays closed; see "What this does not do".

**This PR was rewritten after the situation changed.** It originally carried this session's own resolution of the `main`-into-lane conflict. While it sat open, a second DEVICE-02 session resolved the same conflict in parallel and pushed `9e58995` to `feat/knowledgebase-expansion`. This PR now **adopts the lane's resolution wholesale** and keeps only what is additive: the reconciliation record. The diff against the lane is **93 added lines in `CHANGELOG.md` and nothing else.**

## What conflicted

`main` had advanced **29 commits** past the merge base `e2af2af`. `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` at `9416bf8` reported exactly two conflicted files:

| File | Classification (`docs/PHASES_BUILDING_CONTROL.md` §10) | Owner of the decision |
|---|---|---|
| `package.json` | **A — mechanical** (§10(H), non-overlapping configuration additions) | neither; both additions valid |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | **A — mechanical** (§10(G), both lanes insert at the top) | neither; §10(G) prescribes the method |

No file under `knowledge-corpus/` or `tools/knowledge-corpus/` conflicted, and no Rust, bundler, schema, entitlement or Assessment file did either. There was **no architectural conflict in the Git overlap** — the architectural conflict is real, but it is **D18**, and it does not present as a hunk.

## The two resolutions, compared

Both merges have identical parents (`6aab0c8` + `9416bf8`), so their trees are directly comparable:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | **byte-identical in both.** 23 scripts — ten base, `main`'s four `version:*` from D16, the lane's nine `kb:*` — no duplicate key, `engines` from `main`. Two independent resolutions agreeing exactly is the strongest available evidence that this conflict was mechanical |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | differed in **two** respects only: where the KB-002 entry sits inside the 2026-09-27 block (6th vs 9th — both valid newest-first), and a trailing `---` separator the lane's resolution adds to its own KB-002 entry |
| everything else | **no difference at all** |

## Which one is canonical, and why

**The lane's resolution `9e58995` is canonical, and this PR defers to it.** The Knowledge Expansion workstream owns its corpus and its own changelog entry, so its placement of KB-002 and its separator fix stand — and the separator was genuinely missing beforehand, so its version is the better of the two.

All **79** entries are taken verbatim from `9e58995`: verified **79 in, 79 out**, none missing, none duplicated, and **zero of its entries altered**. This session's own resolution of those 79 entries is **discarded in favour of theirs** rather than blended into a third variant. No third design was invented, and nothing was overwritten to make one session "win".

## A real defect both sessions found independently

`c29447e` ("Merge origin/main into feat/knowledgebase-expansion: CHANGELOG only") had relocated three **DEVICE-01** entries from 2026-09-27 — PHASES BUILDING Ledger, Route Audit, Assessment Integrity — from the top of the file down to **line 4126**, below the oldest historical sections. Nothing was deleted, so no check caught it: §10(G)'s heading-count rule detects loss, not misplacement. Both resolutions fixed it. The one remaining date inversion exists on `main` and on the merge base, so it predates both lanes and was left alone.

Both resolutions were also verified the way §10(G) prescribes: both sides first proved purely additive against the merge base (`main` +5 entries, the lane +2, **zero** entries edited or removed on either side), then **77 headings on `main`, 74 on the lane, union 79, out 79**.

## Validation on the converged tree

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `kb:manifest:check` | manifest matches: **432 records, 70 checksummed files** |
| `kb:validate` | 432 records, **0 errors / 0 warnings**, 0 duplicates |
| `kb:privacy` | **CLEAR — 0 findings** |
| `kb:test` / `kb:test:privacy` | **52/52** / **19/19** |
| preflight | **27/27**, exits 0 |
| `nexus-sync` / release tool | **81/81** / **25/25** |

Earlier, on the equivalent tree at `fa5a040`: nexus-core **804/804**, desktop **330/330**, `pnpm -r typecheck` clean, `pnpm -r build` clean, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` reporting the lockfile up to date. Every application figure reproduces baseline **B-006**. The converged tree differs from `9e58995` only in `CHANGELOG.md`, which nothing reads programmatically (both source references to it are comments), and `9e58995`'s application tree is identical to the already-green `fa5a040`.

**CI supplied the half DEVICE-02 cannot measure.** Run [36821384469](https://github.com/genshingarcia222-sudo/H.A.A.-Nexus/actions/runs/36821384469) at `640b600` passed both jobs: `windows-latest` ran `cargo test` **70/70** — including the P9-A guard `release_builds_are_windowed_not_console` — with `cargo fmt --check` clean, and the Linux job reproduced every figure on a third machine. The Rust result is therefore measured on the merged tree rather than inherited from `0c09e36`. Installers and anything needing an installed Windows artifact remain outside CI and are not claimed. Local `node` is v22.22.0 against `main`'s declared `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, so pnpm prints an engine warning — `main`'s pre-existing constraint, not a product of this work.

## What the corpus side gained or lost

Nothing. No file under `knowledge-corpus/` or `tools/knowledge-corpus/` differs from the lane tip. Records, checksums, manifests, difficulty balancing, QA, provenance, tooling and validation are untouched. No regeneration was performed and none was needed.

## What this does not do

- **D18 is untouched** and is still what blocks the merge to `main`. Two implementations of one content contract remain: D12's Zod model in `packages/nexus-core/src/knowledge-corpus/` on `main`, and `knowledge-corpus/schema/kb-record.schema.json` with its 24 policy rules on the lane. **No loader, adapter, translation layer or shim was written** — a bridge would be a third contract.
- **No open decision is resolved, narrowed or implied.** Integration gate item 2 forbids a merge that does any of those, which is why the base is the lane and not `main`.
- **No `.nexus` file was changed.** `nexus-sync` records state on `main` and this session is scoped to its own branch, so the task record is left to a session that can write it.
- **No other lane's owned file was edited.** `docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md` is DEVICE-01's; its D18 entry still says "324 KB-001 records", which KB-002 made stale at 432. Flagged, not edited.

## The coordination lesson

Two sessions in the same device's lane resolved one conflict in parallel. Nothing in `.nexus/` could have prevented it: `ACTIVE_TASK.md` is advisory and neither session held a claim on `CHANGELOG.md`. The cost here was small because the resolutions agreed — but that was luck, not process. A session about to resolve a shared-file conflict should claim it through `nexus-sync` first, and a session that cannot write state should say so **before** resolving rather than after.

## Follow-ups

1. **D18 is the only thing blocking PR #21**, and neither device may answer it.
2. `knowledge-corpus/INTEGRATION_BLOCKERS.md` says the manifest checksums **40** files; it is now **70**. Inside this lane, left for the corpus session rather than widened into this diff.
3. `docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md` D18 understates the corpus at 324 records (now 432). DEVICE-01-owned.

`feat/knowledgebase-expansion` already carries the resolution, so PR #21 should be `CLEAN` against `main` again — **mergeable, and still gated.** Git saying it can merge is not the gate.

author: nirmalkumar31
body:
**PR B of five.** Backend only — no UI change. Adds the `auto` route; `ModeSelector` reads capabilities by key so the new mode is ignored until PR C/D offers it.

## Why

A visitor had to pick an implementation strategy before asking a question. The obstacle wasn't the interface — it was that the resolver had **one bit** to report with. Every unresolvable question came back `confident=False` with a sentence, so only two policies were possible: *never ask a model* (refuses questions a model could read) or *always ask one* (spends a request on every question whose column doesn't exist).

The resolver already knew the difference. `_pick` has always said either

> the table has no column that looks like a measure

or

> the question does not name which measure to use, and the table has 3 to choose from

Different facts, different remedies, both flattened into the same non-decision.

## What this adds

`analytics/resolution.py` — 12 typed `ResolutionIssue` codes across 5 states. Exactly one earns a planning request:

| state | example | planner consulted |
|---|---|---|
| `exact` | every column named | **no** |
| `ambiguous` | "the average by chronotype" — several measures | **yes, once** |
| `unresolved` | a column the file lacks | no |
| `unsupported` | no operation this engine implements | no |
| `unsafe` | one column read as both value and grouping | no |

Ambiguity is the **weakest** claim, so a question that is *also* unresolved takes the stronger reading. A missing column refuses whatever the wording means, and spending a request to be told what the rules already knew is what makes automatic routing look expensive.

No new inference was added. Every issue is raised at a site that already refused for that reason.

## The cost argument, and why tests count constructions

`open_governed_cloud_provider` takes the **durable ledger slot at construction** — deliberately, so a run that can't be priced is refused before its first billable request. That makes construction, not the request, the moment quota is spent.

So `auto` receives a **factory**. `RunContext.open_planner` is called only once ambiguity is established:

| question | planners built |
|---|---|
| every column named | **0** |
| column doesn't exist | **0** |
| unimplemented operation | **0** |
| genuinely ambiguous | **1** |

An exact question reads no credential and consults no ledger. That preserves a property deterministic mode already had: **a deployment with a missing or broken credential still answers everything the rules resolve.** An ambiguous one is refused with a precise reason and the reformulations that would work — a weaker product, not a broken one, which is why the mode is offered wherever live analysis is.

## What does not change

The model's authority, because it was already correct. A plan still cannot alter an operation or measure the question named, add or shift a period, reverse a ranking, group by an identifier, or supply SQL — `mapping_from_plan` enforces all of it and `auto` routes **through** it, not around it. Arithmetic, verification, coverage and provenance untouched.

`deterministic`, `ai`, `compare` remain selectable and behave exactly as before. Passing no factory produces the old code path, so an audit run or a Compare Both pane cannot acquire automatic routing by accident.

`provider_kind` reports **`governed`**, not `cloud`. The record is created before the question is resolved; naming a billable path for a run that may make no request would be a false cost record. The route event says what actually happened.

## Two defects routing exposed

**A dropped restriction.** `average total_sleep_hours where mood is good` resolved as `exact` and was answered for **every participant**. An equality clause whose column didn't resolve was skipped rather than recorded — while the sibling branch, for an *ambiguous* column, refused correctly. `row_filters` states the policy it was violating: *"a false detection costs a refusal with a reason, a missed one costs a wrong answer presented as the right one."* Now refuses, classified ambiguous because a planner may bind the column. Full suite confirms no regressions.

**A test that couldn't see it.** Mutation **B7** — reporting "no candidates" as "several candidates" — survived, because the fixture always had measures and `_pick`'s empty branch was never reached. A text-only upload covers it; B7 is now caught.

## One defect deliberately left alone

`chronotype is Night Owl` binds as `'Night'` — the value grammar stops at the first space. It's **off the routing path** (the question resolves exactly either way) and the empty-population guard declines it rather than publishing a wrong number. Widening the capture would swallow a trailing `by region`, the same over-capture that once turned a filtered breakdown into a two-cut one. It needs its own change with its own corpus evidence. Recorded in **LIMITATIONS §11b** rather than half-fixed.

## One test assertion changed

`test_capabilities_describe_both_modes` pinned the mode set as closed, so adding `auto` had to change it. Renamed and **strengthened**, not merely widened: it now asserts `auto` is available **with AI disabled** (the key property), and that its description contains "only when" and never "autonomous", "the model computes" or "ai decides".

## Evidence

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| Full Python suite | exit 0, **0 failures** |
| New tests | 45 (36 unit + 9 integration) |
| Mutations | **9/9 caught** |
| `ruff` / `ruff format` / `mypy` | clean |
| `validate-recordings` | 3/3 |
| Frontend | 172 pass, typecheck clean (capabilities change absorbed) |

Mutations: confirm an exact contract anyway · ask about a missing column · treat every issue as AI-eligible · ambiguity outranking a missing column · AI-unavailable reported as executable · unbindable restriction dropped again · missing column reported as merely ambiguous · refusals carrying no issue · refused route returning a usable contract.

`assess()` is asserted to be synchronous and to reference no provider, ledger or client — read from the **AST**, not the source text, because a substring scan matched the docstring's own explanation.

## Not done

No deploy, Render change, credential use, tag, paid call, or merge.

**Owner action: merge PR B** once CI is green on this PR's exact head SHA. I'll report that SHA, then wait for CI on the merge SHA before starting PR C.

author: augusttodaniel
body:
## The bug

Accounts exported to OmniRoute worked for about an hour and then stopped. On OmniRoute the two `agy` connections showed an open **refresh circuit** (streaks of 8 and 6 failures), were inactive, and had no `projectId` or synced models, while the one `antigravity` connection that OmniRoute itself had authorized was healthy.

## Root cause (confirmed, not inferred)

Google binds a refresh token to the OAuth client that issued it and answers any other client with `unauthorized_client`.

- OmniRoute renews **every** Antigravity token, `agy` and `antigravity` alike, with its built-in client (`1071006060591-…`). Its source says so (`selectGoogleRefreshClient`, `BUILTIN_ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT`), and swapping the provider label changes nothing.
- The switcher signed accounts in with the first client found in the installed Antigravity 2.0, which carries two: `884354919052-…` came first.
- Tested against Google through the account's own OmniRoute proxy (same IP OmniRoute already uses for it; only status codes were read): the stored token renews with `884…` (HTTP 200) and is refused by `1071…` with `unauthorized_client`.

The import succeeded because the first access token was still valid; the failure appeared at the first renewal, when nobody was looking.

## The fix

**Switcher**
- Accounts remember the client that issued their token (migration 8, `oauth_client_id`) and renew with it, and only it. A recorded client is authoritative: it never falls back to another.
- An account that does not know its client (it predates this, or was imported) tries every client found on the machine and records the one that works, so existing accounts keep renewing with no action.
- A pinned client (`config set oauth_client_id …` or `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID`) now only chooses the client for **new** sign-ins. Before, pinning would have hidden the other clients from renewals and broken every account issued by one. This is why the fix is per account and not a global setting.
- `UpsertAccount` records the client the sign-in used and replaces a previous one on a re-login.

**`export-omniroute`**
- Before sending an account it asks Google, **through the account's own proxy and never from the real IP**, whether OmniRoute's client can renew the token. It refuses to export one it could not, with the reason and the fix. Without this the export reported success for tokens that could never renew.
- An account with an unknown origin and no proxy is refused rather than checked from the real IP.
- `--skip-client-check` exports anyway; `--omniroute-client-id` covers an OmniRoute whose operator set `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`.

## Testing

- `gofmt`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` (CGO disabled) pass locally.
- New tests drive a fake that behaves like Google's token endpoint (secret check, then the issuing-client binding): learning the right client, recording it, never probing a learned client again, a bound account never trying another client, a revoked token stopping at once, `ProbeRefresh` for every outcome, the probe writing nothing, re-login replacing the recorded client, and a pin not hiding other clients. The export check is tested with the fake standing in as the account's proxy: known client, unknown origin proven and recorded, mismatch refused with the fix, revoked token, no proxy never checked, and an inconclusive answer blocking unless skipped.
- Mutation-checked: removing the "try the next client" step or the "bound account uses only its client" rule makes tests fail.
- Not exercised against OmniRoute's real renewal: that needs a fresh sign-in with the `1071…` client, which is the next step after merging.

## Heads up

Accounts already exported keep failing in OmniRoute until they are signed in again with OmniRoute's client; this PR does not rewrite tokens that Google bound elsewhere.

author: xdoubleu
body:
Fixes #2098

## Summary

**Corners.** The UI's radius tokens keep corners squared, but some buttons and highlights still used `rounded-full`. Those now use the squared radius:
- `Badge` → `rounded-lg`
- `TogglePill` → inherits `Button`'s `rounded-xl`
- `DialogClose` → `rounded-xl`
- shopping list remove `×` → `Button` default
- external book provider chip → `<Badge variant="secondary">` (it was a hand-rolled copy)
- progress bars → `rounded-sm`

Real circles keep `rounded-full`: the spinner, radio buttons, and the watch party status dot.

`ui/theme-tokens` now rejects `rounded-full` and `rounded-3xl` or larger unless the same class list makes a square (`size-*` or equal `h-`/`w-`), so pills can't come back. RuleTester cases are added and the rule is documented in `convention-ui-standards`.

**Navbar.** In the installed iOS app, `--glass-edge-clear` goes from `2.5rem` to `1.5rem`. Measured from the status bar, the nav text now starts at about 42pt: 24pt clearance + 4pt `py-1` + ~14pt to the glyph top in the 44px row. That's still past the ~38–40pt Liquid Glass ramp from #1987. The dialogs share the variable and add their own 1–1.25rem of padding, so they stay clear too.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` (includes the eslint-rule tests), the full Jest suite (2388 tests), `npm run test:cov:diff`, `npm run build`, and `make lint/docs` all pass.
- Added regression tests that `Badge`, `TogglePill` and `DialogClose` are not `rounded-full`.

## Post-deploy check

The edge blur is iOS system chrome and can't be reproduced headless. On the installed iPhone PWA (re-open it), confirm the navbar text is still crisp with the smaller top gap. If the bottom of the blur reaches the text, raise the value to `2rem`.

## Manual review needed

- **Lint config** (`web/eslint-rules/theme-tokens.mjs`): check that the square heuristic (`size-*`, or the first unprefixed `h-`/`w-` being equal) doesn't flag a real circle you want to keep. Every current circle passes.

body:
## 요약
Backoffice 스웨거에 분실물 CRUD 가 생겨(`/lost-items` GET·POST, `/{id}` GET·PATCH·DELETE, `/{id}/translations/{lang}` DELETE), admin 분실물을 목 스토어에서 실제 API 캐시로 옮긴다. 공지 연결(e907b69)과 같은 틀이다. **이로써 admin 의 모든 도메인이 서버 데이터를 쓴다.**

## 변경
- `api/lostItems.ts` (새): 목록(`listAll`)·생성·수정·삭제·번역 삭제. 요청 번역에는 `id`·`lost_item_id` 를 싣지 않는다(`extra=forbid` → 422). `created_at` 은 받자마자 KST
- `mocks/lostItems.ts`: 목 데이터 → 빈 캐시 배열 (`mocks/notices.ts` 와 같음)
- `mocks/store.ts`: `loadLostItems` · `saveLostItem` · `removeLostItem`(404 는 지워진 것으로) · `removeLostItemTranslation` · `setReturned`(PATCH `is_returned`). 목 흉내(`upsertLostItem`·`restoreLostItem`·`draftId`·`nowKst`) 제거
- `app/DataGate.tsx`: 로그인 뒤 분실물도 함께 받는다
- `LostItemEditRoute`: 저장·삭제 비동기 + 기다리는 동안 버튼 잠금 + 서버 오류 표시. 생성은 `is_returned: false`(POST 필수), 수정은 빼서 반환 상태를 건드리지 않는다. 비운 번역은 전용 DELETE, 번역 삭제 실행취소는 PATCH 로 다시 올림
- `LostItemsRoute`: 반환 버튼·실행취소가 PATCH. 실패하면 행은 그대로 두고 critical 스낵바
- `imageSrc`: 분실물이 마지막 목 도메인이라 목 사진 분기와 `public/images/mock-photo-*.webp` 3장 삭제

## 바뀌는 동작
- **삭제 실행취소가 없어진다.** 서버 DELETE 가 영구라 되살릴 수 없다(공지와 같음). 확인 다이얼로그는 그대로
- 화면 규칙(사진 필수, KO 습득 장소·제목 필수, 제목·장소 짝)은 그대로. 서버는 `found_location` 이 선택이라 화면이 거는 규칙임을 주석에 정리

## 확인 필요 (이 PR 밖)
- Backoffice 필드명은 `image_url` 이지만 업로드는 S3 **key** 를 돌려준다. user 분실물 카드는 `image_url` 을 `Photo` src 로 그대로 쓰므로, 첫 실제 등록 뒤 Customer `GET /lost-items` 가 key 를 주면 user 쪽 표시 작업이 필요하다

## 검증
- `pnpm --filter admin typecheck` · `lint` · `build` 통과, prettier 통과
- 스테이징 실등록 검증(등록 → 수정·번역 삭제·실행취소 → 반환/되돌리기 → 삭제)은 로그인 발급 코드가 필요해 아직 못 했다. 진행 후 이 PR 에 결과를 남긴다

body:
**Scope split:** focused renderer-settings PR #124 is now the first contribution for #93. Review that small change first. This broad draft preserves the prior repair work and evidence; it overlaps #124 and should not be merged alongside it without reconciling the duplicated changes. Step 2 is tracked in #125, step 3 in #126, and step 4 in #127. The unchanged performance blocker is tracked in #128. Terrain compaction and shared-bake work here are partial progress, not completion of those follow-ups.

**Still draft:** 742/743 was the latest complete run on this branch. No newer commits or full-suite pass are claimed. Profiling does not prove that remaining visibility costs are unavoidable or that approximate overlay caching would pass.

Issue #93 starts with reducing oversized render targets and retained geometry. High-tier MSAA now requests 2 samples instead of 4, and a positive browser memory hint at or below 8 GB selects medium before allocating the initial buffers. Missing or invalid hints preserve normal startup behavior.

The full-suite follow-up also repairs failures in controls, NPC movement and collision, scene cleanup, and the test fixtures that exercise those contracts:

- Cupped foliage uses the same triangle-fan anchor on both windings. This removes mismatched front/back surfaces without changing vertices, colors, normals or polygon boundaries.
- Character visibility shares immutable geometry bakes across scene wrappers, keeps a bounded set of variants, and leaves oversized synchronous builds out of idle callbacks.
- Player control and gorilla movement fixes preserve explicit pointer capture, reachable work trips, stair transitions, body clearance and weapon contacts. Terrain and visibility checks retain their precision and conservative treatment of gaps.
- DSB panels update their nearby-action prompt immediately. Native HUD tests wait for the compositor's scrolled surface and verify both the actual pointer-down and click targets.
- Breakable props retain their random placement attempts, then search a bounded spiral when those attempts miss available space. Every existing placement safety check remains active.
- Rally and factory lifecycle repairs preserve bounded geometry and shared state across repeated visits. The failure ledger now handles duplicate check names from the two renderers without losing a failure or crashing.

No dependencies or content-policy changes. Checks, thresholds, sample spacing, and deadlines have not been relaxed.

### Proof and current status

**Latest complete run: 742/743 checks passed in 14.3 minutes** (`LANES=2 npm run test:full`). All gameplay, collision, unit, console, renderer-fallback and lifecycle checks passed. The only failure is the covered-cave performance check: 38.27 FPS, p95 50 ms, quality reduced to low. Its unchanged requirements include at least 55 FPS, p95 below 25 ms, and remaining at high quality. **This PR remains draft; the full suite is not yet green.**

A production-geometry comparison found 7,504 paired foliage faces with mismatched front/back triangulations before the repair and zero afterward; their vertices, normals, colors and polygon boundaries are unchanged. The complete suite found no additional failure after this repair.

The targeted gameplay and lifecycle run passed **180/180**, including real DSB clicks in both renderers, melee damage and respawning, and six factory round trips. Independent geometry comparisons preserve visibility and label anchors across 500 changing views. An idle-budget fixture verifies that large meshes never start in idle callbacks, small meshes respect the available time, and disposal cancels pending work. A placement fixture forces every random attempt to miss, verifies the fallback finds a safe location, and confirms eight blocking conditions still prevent placement.

The initial render-target measurement used native renderbuffer allocation calls in Chrome at 1440×900 CSS pixels and DPR 2. Actual sample counts fell from 4 to 2 at unchanged 2039×1274 dimensions: calculated renderbuffer storage fell from 118.91 MiB to 59.46 MiB, saving **59.46 MiB** with four-byte depth storage. This measures those buffers, not total process memory. An injected 8 GB hint started directly at medium with no high-tier allocation first; both measurement sessions had clean consoles.

Performance experiments that failed the remaining requirement are excluded from this update. The covered-view performance defect remains open and is the next required repair; this PR does not close the entire issue #93.

author: tangzzycc
body:
## Purpose

`ROCM_ATTN` stores the decoder window as `(W - 1, 0)`, where `W - 1` is the left span. The underlying [decode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py#L234) and [prefix-prefill](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/prefix_prefill.py#L435) kernels use `query_position - key_position < SLIDING_WINDOW`, so their argument must be the total window length `W`, including the current token. Passing `W - 1` excludes the oldest valid token; for `W=1`, passing zero disables the window entirely.

This PR passes `1 + self.sliding_window[0]` to `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`. This matches the existing [KV-cache docstring example](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1160): with `sliding_window=4` and seven computed tokens, the next token at position 7 must attend to tokens **4–7**. The old argument is 3 and attends to **5–7**; the corrected argument is 4 and attends to **4–7**.

`TRITON_ATTN` [stores the same `(W - 1, 0)` tuple](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py#L511) and already passes [`SLIDING_WINDOW=(1 + window_size[0])`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1133). Applying the same conversion makes the causal window boundaries consistent between the two backends. The no-window sentinel maps to zero, which the helper treats as disabled; encoder attention uses a separate path.

Open-PR searches on 2026-10-01 found no duplicate. Related #49588, #53628, and #59132 do not modify this backend argument conversion.

## Test Plan

Run the focused backend regression and the existing cached-KV boundary test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
  -k 'rocm_backend_sliding_window or cached_kv_block_table_boundary' -q
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, all four windowed regression cases fail and both no-window controls pass. After the fix: **7 passed**, including the existing boundary test. All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Gemma3 1B IT (BF16, window 512) completed inference on Radeon 890M (`gfx1150`) with inputs within and beyond the window, including chunked prefill and HIP graph decode. Compared before/after ROCM_ATTN with TRITON_ATTN and Transformers FP32. Before/after prompt logprobs were identical for input lengths up to 512; longer inputs showed changes, with errors against the reference implementations increasing or decreasing depending on input length.

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, and preparation of this PR. vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill was used to review the change.

author: proofofreach
body:
Chapter partitioning can change narration if a speech transform or sequence
normalizer rewrites, drops or reorders text. This change checks normalized text
before and after structure transformations and rejects a mismatch before cache
publication. Chapter copies prevent a failed in-place transform from corrupting
the read cache.

Adds a read-only detector for exact historical partition rewrites and an offline
benchmark for six pinned real books across English, German and French, covering
EPUB, MOBI, scanned PDF, verse and notes. Report writers reject existing files,
library/source directories and their symlink aliases. No player controls,
settings or notices are added. Automatic repair and sentence timing remain
deferred.

Validation: 3,500 existing tests; 34 partition-integrity E2E cases; 22 legacy
audit E2E cases; 20 benchmark CLI/output cases; six real-book imports with
source assertions and fresh-process artifact reads. The release also runs
browser smoke and the existing import reliability benchmark. Physical iPhone
playback verification remains pending; the checklist and unrun result template
record that limitation.

author: luckytype
body:
## What and why

cms-core reads and writes `event.locals.auth` directly in several places, assuming `App.Locals.auth` is cms-core's own `Auth` type. `@auth/sveltekit` declares `App.Locals.auth` as its own session getter, so an app using both libraries fails type-check on every one of these sites, because both claim the same key with incompatible types. `graphql/index.ts` already worked around this with an inline cast, which is a sign this clash has already been hit once internally.

Adds `aphexLocals(locals)`, a typed view used everywhere instead of touching `locals.auth` directly, and replaces the existing inline cast with the same helper. Type-only change, no runtime effect.

Closes #341

## How to verify

`pnpm --filter @aphexcms/cms-core exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm --filter @aphexcms/cms-core exec vitest run` (full suite, 217 passed, 0 failed).

No new test: this is a type-only change (the helper is an identity function at runtime), and there is no type-level test infrastructure in this repo (no `expect-type` or similar) to assert against. A reviewer can confirm the fix by adding a local `App.Locals.auth` declaration from `@auth/sveltekit` in a consuming app and checking that `tsc` now passes where it previously failed; that requires a second SvelteKit app wired to `@auth/sveltekit`, outside this monorepo.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm lint && pnpm check && pnpm build` pass for the touched package
- [x] Tests pass for what I touched (full suite; see above for why no new test was added)
- [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`), patch bump (type-only, no runtime change)
- [ ] Docs updated if behaviour or configuration changed (no runtime behaviour changed)
- [ ] Studio/template sync (not a studio-visible change)

## Alternative for a future major

Worth asking: would upstream rather rename the key for the next breaking release (for example `locals.aphexAuth`) instead of carrying this indirection indefinitely? Left that choice to the maintainer; the helper above is the non-breaking option.

body:
Implements bead mb-onzb, part of the test-suite review epic mb-06up.

Base: #250.

## What changed

Eight commits carry the change. Four more are two cancelling pairs, each for one CI run: a Makefile edit that reversed the module order, and a probe that reported leaked process state. Drop them when restacking.

1. **One autouse reset in `tests/conftest.py`** (`_reset_served_source`, `tests/conftest.py:120`).
   It resets the source session before and after every test, and puts back the served root a test changed.
   It replaces 27 of the 44 manual `reset_source_session()` calls. The 17 that remain are not teardown:
   11 are in test bodies that model a second server process, and 6 are in helpers a test calls mid-way (see "Review", P1-A).
2. **Events and counts instead of sleeps and elapsed-time asserts.**
   All 8 elapsed-time asserts are gone: 6 replaced by an event or a count, 1 replaced by a counted test, 1 removed with its test.
   18 of the 59 non-zero sleeps are gone; the 41 kept are listed below.
3. **The served-root restores the fixture now makes are deleted**: 72 of 77.
4. **Two order dependences the reversed run exposed, fixed at their cause** (see "Order independence").
5. **Review fixes** (see "Review").

## Counts

| Measure | Before (f9d88f50) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Manual `reset_source_session()` calls in tests | 44 | 17 |
| Manual served-root restores | 77 | 5 |
| `time.sleep` / `asyncio.sleep` sites | 89 | 72 |
| of which `sleep(0)` loop handoffs | 30 | 31 |
| of which non-zero | 59 | 41 |
| Asserts on elapsed time | 8 | 0 |
| Unbounded `readline()` on a child | 8 | 0 |
| `tests/test_*.py` files / lines | 276 / 79,100 | 276 / 79,037 |
| Test helper modules, files / lines | 10 / 1,967 | 11 / 2,087 |
| `def test_` functions | 2,750 | 2,749 |
| Net lines, whole diff (58 files) | | +60 |

The first version of this PR was −145 lines net. The review fixes added 205: the restored boundaries, the counted rollup test and its measurement, and the bounded child read.

DOM JS, goldens and fixtures are untouched.

Run time, from the CI `test (3.13)` job. The runs are on different runners, so read the differences as noise:

| | Before (run 36820018225, #250 head) | After (run 36832711070, this PR's head) |
|---|---|---|
| pytest | 3,534 passed, 27 skipped in 265.55 s | 3,533 passed, 27 skipped in 185.44 s |
| tryscript | 301 passed in 180.85 s | 301 passed in 99.84 s |
| `admitted-git` 2.43.7 / 2.50.1 | 444 passed, 5 skipped in 87.62 s / 119.10 s | 444 passed, 5 skipped in 119.99 s / 113.43 s |

No tryscript golden changed, so its difference is the runner, not this PR. Three earlier runs of this branch took 252 s, 252 s and 177 s for pytest.

## Order independence

The full suite ran in reversed module order in CI, by a temporary change to the Makefile's `test` target (`pytest $(ls tests/*.py | sort -r)`, which collected the same tests).

- **Run 36821796721 failed 2 tests** on Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.14t and in `stack-integration`. Neither involved the source session.
  - `tests/test_cli_acquire.py::test_no_serve_reuses_a_cache_hit_when_the_home_has_no_owner_write` saw debug log lines in a command's output.
    `tests/test_dotenv_loading.py` clears `METABROWSER_LOG_LEVEL` with `monkeypatch.delenv(raising=False)`, which records no undo for an absent name, then loads a `.env` that sets it to `DEBUG`. The value stayed in `os.environ` for the rest of the run.
    The CLI and the dotenv chain write `os.environ` by design, so this is a class of leak: `_restore_environment` (`tests/conftest.py:146`) now puts the environment back after every test.
  - `tests/test_cli_git_pin_golden.py::test_golden_multi_entry_pin_show_and_api` recorded tracebacks in a command's stderr.
    `tests/test_log_adapter_plugins.py` registers an adapter whose detector raises, in a process-global table with no unregister.
    That module now registers into a copy of the table (`tests/test_log_adapter_plugins.py:20`).
- **Run 36822751614 passed** with those two fixes: 3,532 passed, 27 skipped on each of the four Python versions and in `stack-integration`.

The full reversed run was made before the review fixes. After them, the 23 modules they touch were run locally in sorted and in reversed order: 422 passed each way.

The two orders the bead names fail on recorded session generations without `_reset_served_source` and pass with it:

```
pytest tests/test_repository_context.py tests/test_source_ref_selector_session.py
pytest tests/test_source_session.py tests/test_source_freshness_session.py
```

The full suite was not run locally, in either order: the machine was under load from another measurement.

## Deleted tests and what still covers them

- `test_rollup_budget_on_synthetic_large_index` (`tests/test_browser_rollup.py`), a 1,000 ms gate on a 40k-entry rollup with no recorded measurement.
  `test_rollup_traversal_is_bounded_cold_and_independent_of_index_size_warm` (`tests/test_browser_rollup.py:376`) replaces it with counts; see "Review", P2-A.
  The elapsed time itself is the "settled rollup, aggregated p50 (ms)" row of `devtools/bench_serving.py` (`:1293`), which does not run in CI.
- `test_parse_jsonl_cached_second_call_is_fast` (`tests/test_browser_projections.py`), 50 warm reads under 100 ms, there to catch a bypassed cache.
  It could not fail on that: 50 uncached parses of its three-line file take 3.5 ms, measured on a loaded machine.
  `test_parse_jsonl_caches_on_repeat_call` (`tests/test_browser_projections.py:58`) asserts the cache hit by call count.
- The fixture `_no_session_left` (`tests/test_mirror_companion.py`), whose only job was the reset now in conftest.

## Review

An independent review found two P1s, both tests that lost detection the base had. Each finding below was reproduced before it was fixed.

**P1-A. Tests that read one tree as a folder and then as a pin ran the pin half with the folder still served.**
Commit 1 had removed resets and root restores from helpers a test calls mid-way, taking them for teardown.
With `GitTreeSource._open_ref_path` answering from `FilesystemContentSource(paths_safe.ROOT_DIR)`, 13 tests fail at `f9d88f50`, 3 failed at `af4f29b1`, and 13 fail again now.

- Six helpers undo what they attach again: `pinned_client`, `_pinned_client`, `_with_filesystem`, `_with_pin` and both `_folder_client` helpers.
- After the folder half, its files are overwritten (`overwrite_tree`, `tests/git_pin_harness.py:77`), so a pin read that reached them cannot agree by accident. With the boundary removed again and only this kept, the mutation still fails 11.
- Audit, at `f9d88f50`, of all 110 reset and restore statements in the files this branch changed.
  Those removed from test bodies were each followed only by asserts on values already read.
  Those in fixtures were teardown.
  The six helpers above were the only ones whose callers go on to another source; besides the agreement tests, `tests/test_git_full_clone_acceptance.py` opens two pins in turn.

**P1-B. `test_work_that_must_finish_finishes_however_often_it_is_cancelled` no longer tested "however often".**
It released the work before the third cancellation was delivered. It now takes one more loop turn and asserts the job is still pending.
`_finish_despite_cancel` re-shielding once, not in a loop, fails at `f9d88f50`, passed at `af4f29b1`, and fails now.

**Every rewritten test, against a source change it guards against.** All 26 fail as they should:

| Source change | Test that fails |
|---|---|
| Pin reads answered from the served root | 13 agreement tests |
| Re-shield once, not in a loop | must-finish work |
| Tally bound without the pass's cost | bound is at least the cost (the base version passed) |
| Tally probe takes the lock blocking | probe never waits |
| Tally memo never expires | old pass not reused; bound is at least the cost |
| Lock wait ignores the abandon signal | cancelled acquisition (child reports "gave up") |
| Probe runs under another deadline | stalled https or

author: huangjeff5
body:
Stacked on the named-values PR; retarget to main after it merges.

`from genkit.telemetry import reset_instrumentation, GenkitBuiltinInstrumentation` now works. `reset_instrumentation()` gives a test a clean slate in one call: every configured telemetry provider is disposed and removed, Developer UI log export stops, and the next span starts a new trace instead of nesting under whatever was still open. `is_instrumented_by(GenkitBuiltinInstrumentation)` tells you whether traces are going to the Developer UI.

```python
# before
from genkit._core._telemetry._instrumentation import is_instrumented_by, reset_instrumentation
from genkit._core._telemetry._log_exporter import reset_log_export
from genkit._core._telemetry.http import GenkitBuiltinInstrumentation

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clean_telemetry():
    reset_instrumentation()
    reset_log_export()
    yield
    reset_instrumentation()
    reset_log_export()

# after
from genkit.telemetry import GenkitBuiltinInstrumentation, is_instrumented_by, reset_instrumentation

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clean_telemetry():
    reset_instrumentation()
    yield
    reset_instrumentation()
```

## Decisions

- **One call resets all telemetry**: Previously, a clean test needed `reset_instrumentation()` and `reset_log_export()`, both from private modules, and missing either leaked traces into the next test. `reset_instrumentation()` now disposes providers, stops Dev UI log export, and starts the next span on a fresh trace.
- **Public `is_instrumented_by` check**: Added a typed predicate for `GenkitBuiltinInstrumentation`. Tests and plugins can check if Dev UI export is active without inspecting private global state.

body:
## Summary
These fixes come from the agent benchmark (`bench/agent`, round 1, PR #278, `bench/agent/RESULTS.md`) and from zokor PR dolphlabs/zokor#27. There is one commit per fix, and each has a regression test in slang's own suite that fails on `dev` (`8b2704a`) and passes here.

| # | Commit | Fix | Evidence | Regression test (fails before / passes after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `8356e86` build | `struct StructTmpl` is now a tagged typedef (`src/codegen/internal.h`), so `generics.c:284/:384` no longer mix `struct StructTmpl *` with the anonymous typedef. Plain `make` builds with GCC 14 (14.2.0) with no extra flags. The Makefile adds `-Werror=incompatible-pointer-types`, so GCC 13 and clang reject the next one too. | GCC 14 failed to build `dev` (zokor CI had to use `CC="cc -Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types"`) | Build itself: before, `make slangc` rc=2 on GCC 14; after, rc=0 |
| 2 | `30df2a3` codegen | Integer literal operands of arithmetic are emitted at the result's width (`(long long)` for int). `60 * 1000000000` used to become `(long long)((60) * (1000000000))`, a 32-bit overflow. | zokor guide gotcha; the ratelimit task's window arithmetic | `tests/int_literal_width`: old compiler prints `-129542144`, `-1294967296`, `-294967296` |
| 3 | `64887b4` runtime | `proc.wait_idle()` and `proc.active_tasks()` no longer count the calling task when it is a spawned task, and they also ignore other spawned tasks blocked in `wait_idle`. Main-program behaviour is unchanged (main was never counted). README note. | `slangc test` runs each test in a spawned task, so zokor's drain tests hung forever (zokor#27 had to work around it) | `tests/wait_idle_spawned` (one waiter, two waiters, main with gated workers), deterministic. `tests/testcmd/idle` runs under `slangc test` with a 60 s watchdog: the old runtime hangs on it |
| 4 | `9cb506c` doc | (a) The listing prints each item's summary **above** the item (`// ...` then the signature); it used to print it below, indented. The struct view's methods get the same treatment. (b) **Search:** `slangc doc <pkg> <text>` / `slangc doc <pkg>.<text>` with no exact match lists items whose name contains `<text>`, case-insensitive. If no name matches, it falls back to signature/doc text. No match at all exits 1. | 9.8% of slang agent input went on paging whole `slangc doc zokor` output. The reported "comment on the wrong symbol" (zokor `respond`'s comment shown under `set_renderer`) **was not a mis-association**: all 298 zokor items carry the right comment (checked against zokor's `docs/gen_api.sh`). Printing the summary *below* each signature made it read as the next item's comment. The fix is the format. | `tests/doccmd/docpkg` fixture + `run_tests.sh` doc section (exact match, `pkg.name`, substring, text fallback, no-match exit 1, comment-above-item assertion): old binary fails 7 checks |
| 5 | `5a12785` diag | An error reported after a generic method instantiation names the user's file. `resolve_enum_in_body` on the fresh instance left `diag_file` pointing at the template's file. ## What this changes

A bandana given to a dog at the park was saved, but when the game opened again it was put back only on beagles. A lab or a chihuahua came back bare while the save still held the bandana (#281 in the private ledger).

- `engine/engine.js`: the line that restores bandanas at start-up asked `cr.kind==="beagle"` where it meant "any dog". It now asks `isDog(cr)`.
- Every other `kind==="beagle"` in the engine was read. They mean "a beagle" (they pick the beagle's drawing, beside the lab's and the chihuahua's), and one means "a dog this admin brush made", which only ever makes beagles. They are unchanged.
- `GAMEV` and `CACHE` go to `mq-v212`.

## How it was checked

- **A new check in `test/smoke.js`** (grep `#281`). It reads the breeds off the adoption card itself, so a breed added later is covered without editing the test. For each breed it:
  - adopts a pup the way a player does (the card, the breed button, a name);
  - gives her a bandana with the real button beside her;
  - reloads and continues;
  - requires the bandana on her again, in the record and in the drawing (pixels, with the clock and pose held still).

  The beagle is the control that proves the check can see a bandana come back. **Why every earlier check missed it:** the adoption card resets to the beagle each time it opens, so the #277 check's three dogs were all beagles.
- **Red first, on the unchanged engine:** *"after a reload, Oso the Lab has no bandana — she wore #C0392B when the game was closed, and the park record still keeps it for her"*, and the same for Kiko the Chihuahua.
- **Plants by the builder** (seven, in copies outside the repository), among them: no restore at all (the beagle control goes red too); the lab's drawer ignoring the bandana (the check refuses to pass with nothing to measure); the button not storing it; a card that offers only the beagle (*"nothing was measured, which is not a pass"*); the wrong colour restored.
- **One plant by the reviewer:** the `beagle` test put back. It goes red with the two sentences above.
- **Every public check is green** on this branch: private terms, authors, vendored, keys, the guards' self-tests, smoke, the engine suite, gauge, horno, R10 on a built site, offline, and bump. The first local smoke run timed out on an unrelated check (the #277 rename check's 6-second click) at a load average near 30; the one re-run, at about 7, was green. The same timeout hit three other lanes under that load, including one that changes only the engine suite, and passed alone each time.
- **Looked at:** before and after frames of the lab in the top camera. Before the reload: a red bandana. After a reload on main: only the collar. After a reload with the fix: the red bandana again.

author: stevenlee-oai
body:
## Problem

The module-boundary evaluator searches the package list for both endpoints of every local reference, repeating the same search when many references share a file.

## Change

Reuse the existing owner lookup through a Map local to one evaluation. Retain the original longest-prefix search, stable ties, original package objects and lazy handling of paths outside the source-file list. Cache missing owners as well.

On the current graph, **1,888 package scans become 242**, and prefix comparisons fall **4,828 -> 589 (87.8%)**. Net **+9 tooling lines**, no runtime or test changes; temporary storage is one entry per queried path, 242 in this measurement.

## Verification

- Remote CI on `0603468e`: **28 checks passed, 6 skipped**.
- `node --test tests/conformance/module-boundaries.test.mjs tests/conformance/module-policy.test.mjs`: **95 passed**.
- Complete real evaluator output, **840 graph variations**, and 12 CLI text/JSON runs are byte-identical against the baseline. Includes nested/equal-length packages, unowned paths, dependency anchors, duplicate references and changed package ownership across successive evaluations.
- Full pinned lint/formatting, syntax and workspace-boundary checks passed.
- Two substantive final-diff no-op/design reviews, including isolated GPT-6 Astra: no findings.

## Risks

The synchronous evaluator receives immutable snapshots. Its Map is discarded after each call, with no cross-run cache or invalidation. Policy decisions, edge/diagnostic order, cycles and CLI contracts stay unchanged. Counts quantify avoided work; no latency or merge-conflict-rate improvement is claimed. Independent of the workspace-sort PR.

author: gycha0109-beep
body:
## SEC-04 D1 runtime proof correction

Failed Production run: #36820524525

Root cause: the D1 proof incorrectly treated backend `pg_stat_ssl.ssl=true` as evidence for the client-to-Supabase Session Pooler TLS leg. A Session Pooler may terminate client TLS before its backend PostgreSQL connection, so `pg_stat_ssl` is not authoritative for this boundary.

This patch:
- keeps the governed strict libpq authority unchanged
- still requires `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` and the pinned governed CA
- treats successful libpq connection under that configuration as the client peer-verification proof
- verifies `transaction_read_only=on` inside an explicit READ ONLY transaction
- removes and now forbids `pg_stat_ssl` from this proof contract
- retains zero write-capable SQL and zero DB URL/password/PEM emission

Refs #1454

Watchtower-Track: security

body:
## Objet

Défauts relevés sur l'échantillon réel de production (`crm:presse:classer-medias --appliquer --limite=500`, après #270). Règles en **version 3** : toutes les fiches déjà classées seront relues au prochain passage (aucune autre écriture que `metadata.classement_media` et les étiquettes dérivées ; relation, nature, protection jamais touchées).

## Corrections

1. **Généralistes sur-étiquetés** (quotidien régional → ia-tech + économie + RH + régional + grand public, public dirigeants) :
   - les « deux mots-clés distincts » qui rendent un signal sûr ne comptent plus le **corps de page** (nom, titre/meta/h1, menu/h2 seulement) ;
   - règle **généraliste** : si `regional` ou `grand-public` est retenu ET au moins **trois** autres thèmes, on ne garde que `regional` / `grand-public` (plus un autre thème seulement s'il est dans le **nom** ou le **titre**), et le public devient `grand-public` — jamais `dirigeants`.
2. **ia-tech trop large** : il faut un mot **spécifique** hors corps (`IA_TECH_SPECIFIQUES` : IA, intelligence artificielle, IA générative, ChatGPT, tech, high-tech, cybersécurité, transformation digitale/numérique, geek, startup) ou **deux** mots tech hors corps. « Impression numérique », « informatique » seuls ne suffisent plus. « IA » dans le nom d'une fiche de presse reste un signal ; pour un « média possible », voir 4.
3. **Format TV sur un non-TV** : le format n'est calculé que si **toutes** les lignes `media` vivantes de la fiche sont `tv` / `tv_emission`.
4. **Médias possibles** : aucun thème, public ni format (même pas `inconnu`) tant que le verdict n'est pas `semble-media` — un non-média n'a pas de ligne éditoriale.

## Tests (qui rougissent sans chaque règle)

`tests/Unit/Crm/ClassementMediaReglesTest.php` (section v3) : généraliste (avec et sans thème dans le titre), public lu dans le seul corps non posé, ia-tech (impression numérique, informatique, « le numérique » → inconnu ; « IA MOTIVATEUR », intelligence artificielle, deux mots tech → retenu), format seulement si toutes les lignes sont TV, média possible sans ligne éditoriale (semble-pas-media, a-verifier) et témoin semble-media. `tests/Feature/Crm/PresseClassementMediasTest.php` : un « média possible » qui ne semble pas un média ne reçoit aucune étiquette `media-sujet:` / `media-public:` / `media-format:`.

## Relance en production

`crm-presse.yml` mode `classer-a-blanc` (limite 200) puis `classer` : la version 3 relit toutes les fiches déjà classées.

> [!NOTE] > ### Port plans backlog helpers to skills CLI as `plans` verbs > - Adds a TypeScript implementation of the plans backlog operations and registers seven verbs (`frontier`, `set-row`, `add`, `log`, `lint`, `handoff`, `chain`) in [src/areas/plans.ts](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-c852902972dfb6217d23a7c37ec397d9c99483c1eb888a691ad13da66ada57d3) > - Index updates in [src/plans/index-tsv.ts](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-03e1fedfe72e8d15a81ff875f8ef043f27e91257bbba1ced26902603f36133a2) use flock-based locking with a 10-second timeout and durable atomic writes (temp file, fsync, rename, directory sync); unchanged rows keep their raw bytes > - [src/plans/frontier.ts](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-ab15a321fad7f59926c362c9770453a3cdfc31471ddbddbdf39a9da7f334cc2b) computes ready/held/review/doing groups, stacks TODO rows on ancestor reviews, and sorts by priority, effort, and ID > - [src/plans/lint.ts](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-317710d6eeb9bde71d31a35d3d5179ccff6aa1f8557890f465748dfa9194cf95) validates plan shape, frontmatter, forward pointers, and intention phrasing, ignoring fenced blocks; non-context files over 4096 bytes error > - [skills/plans/SKILL.md](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-3cc0774c2ea8625eae7a01c1b204aebbdb7d4e3a69bfcce2bf7a717bc02650cc) and playbook references now use the CLI instead of the shell scripts; handoff is read-only and no longer writes the index > - Risk: deletes the legacy `set-row.sh` entrypoint and removes the `test-lint`, `test-frontier`, and `test-handoff` suites from [src/areas/plans.ts](https://github.com/ryuudotgg/skills/pull/74/files#diff-c852902972dfb6217d23a7c37ec397d9c99483c1eb888a691ad13da66ada57d3) > > > > Macroscope summarized 27d9094. > >

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking ID-allocation edge case to address.

Findings

1.  **Plan IDs can exceed three digits** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 src/plans/verbs.ts:195 If the highest existing plan ID is `999` and there is no matching plan file, `plans add` creates ID `1000`. The index requires three-digit IDs, and the new `blocked_by` validation accepts only three-digit IDs, so later plans cannot list that row as a blocker. Reject the allocation rather than adding a row that cannot be referenced. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

Summary

<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change
<!-- Explain what your change does and how it addresses the linked issue -->
Auditors are default members of every workspace chat. The workspace setup adds them, so removing one doesn't stick, and they come back after a refresh. [Resolve the member's own policy role when checking room member removal](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/101643) added `isRoomMemberProtectedByPolicyRole`. It protects the owner, admins and approvers, but it had no case for auditors, so the App offered "Remove from chat" for them.

This PR adds an auditor clause to `isRoomMemberProtectedByPolicyRole`. It reads the listed member's own role with `getPolicyRole(policy, login, false)`, the same way the admin check works. It doesn't use `isPolicyAuditor`, because that reads the viewer's global `policy.role` first and would say "not an auditor" whenever an admin is viewing. Both callers get the fix:
- `DynamicRoomMembersPage`: the auditor's row can't be selected.
- `DynamicRoomMemberDetailsPage`: "Remove from chat" is disabled.

The JSDoc now explains why auditors are protected. A unit test covers an auditor, including a mixed-case login.

- `npm run typecheck`: passed

author: xunssoie
body:
## PR Summary local, prod, test가 각자 다른 방식으로 만들던 DB 스키마를 Flyway 마이그레이션 하나로 통일했습니다. 테스트(H2)도 같은 SQL로 스키마를 만들고, 모든 환경에서 Hibernate는 `validate`만 합니다.
## Problem **문제 1 - 환경마다 다른 스키마 생성 방식** local은 `ddl-auto: update`, test는 `create-drop`으로 Hibernate가 엔티티를 보고 스키마를 만들었고, prod는 `validate`라 스키마를 만들 수단이 아예 없었습니다. 이대로 첫 테이블이 생기면 prod는 기동 시 검증에 실패하고, local과 test는 엔티티가 바뀔 때마다 서로 다른 스키마를 갖게 됩니다. 스키마 변경 이력도 어디에도 남지 않습니다.
**문제 2 - IDE 전용 파일의 저장소 유입** IntelliJ 실행 설정(`.run/`)이 추적되고 있었고, Kotlin 컴파일러가 빌드 중에 만드는 `.kotlin/`은 `.gitignore`에 없어 untracked로 잡혔습니다. 개인 실행 환경에 묶인 파일이 커밋에 섞일 수 있는 상태였습니다.
## Solution **해결 1 - 세 환경에 같은 마이그레이션 SQL 적용** 첫 테이블이 생기기 전이라 기존 스키마를 baseline으로 잡을 필요 없이 빈 스키마에서 Flyway를 시작했습니다. `baseline-on-migrate`는 일부러 켜지 않았습니다. 켜 두면 이미 테이블이 있는 DB를 조용히 baseline 처리해 불일치를 숨기기 때문입니다. 마이그레이션 위치는 프로젝트 규칙에 맞춰 `database/migration`과 `database/seed` 두 곳을 한 버전 순서로 읽게 했고, 세 환경 모두 `ddl-auto`를 `validate`로 맞춰 스키마는 Flyway만 만들도록 했습니다. Flyway 10부터 MySQL 지원이 별도 모듈로 빠져 `flyway-mysql`을 함께 넣었습니다. 쟁점은 테스트였습니다. 테스트 DB가 H2라 MySQL 8.4용 SQL이 그대로 돌지가 문제였는데, 규칙대로 쓴 DDL(`AUTO_INCREMENT`, `ENGINE=InnoDB`, 인라인 `INDEX`, `FOREIGN KEY`, `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `ALTER ... MODIFY`, `INSERT IGNORE`)을 H2 2.4 `MODE=MySQL`에서 직접 실행해 보니 `FULLTEXT INDEX` 하나만 실패했습니다. 그래서 테스트도 Flyway로 같은 SQL을 적용하기로 했고, 이제 `./gradlew test`가 마이그레이션 문법 오류와 엔티티-스키마 불일치를 함께 잡습니다. 이 제약은 마이그레이션 규칙 문서에 적었고, FULLTEXT는 처음 필요해지는 이슈에서 적용 방식을 정합니다. 테스트에서는 Flyway를 끄고 `create-drop`을 유지하는 안도 검토했지만 버렸습니다. 테스트 스키마가 SQL이 아니라 엔티티에서 나오면 마이그레이션이 한 번도 검증되지 않아, 이번 작업이 풀려는 문제가 그대로 남기 때문입니다. 전체 테스트를 Testcontainers MySQL로 바꾸는 안은 "기본은 H2, MySQL 전용 쿼리가 생길 때만 Testcontainers"라는 테스트 규칙과 어긋나고 모든 테스트 실행에 Docker가 필요해져서 택하지 않았습니다. H2에서 Flyway가 실행되고 `validate`로 기동되는 것은 전체 테스트(51건 통과)로 확인했습니다. 로컬 MySQL 8.4에서의 기동 확인은 아직 남아 있습니다.
**해결 2 - `.run/`, `.kotlin/` 추적 제외** 두 디렉토리를 `.gitignore`에 넣고, 이미 추적되던 `.run/ArcaApplication-local.run.xml`은 인덱스에서만 뺐습니다. 머지 후 pull 받으면 각자 작업 폴더에서 이 파일이 지워지므로, local 프로필 실행 설정은 IntelliJ에서 다시 만들어야 합니다.
## Related Issue - close #4 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## BLUF

- **Priority:** medium
- **Problem:** a task created after workers were idle for more than 5 minutes is abandoned as soon as `HasPendingTasks()` runs. If it is the last task, the foreman exits and the task is dropped as "Worker failed".
- **Fix:** `CreateTask` and `CreateRetryTask` reset `_latest_task_processing_time` when a task is queued while no task is queued or processing, so the inactivity window starts when work becomes available.
- **Test:** `testHasPendingTasksAfterIdlePeriod` and `testHasPendingTasksWithInactiveWorkers` in `tests/multi_process/task_manager.py`.
- **Verified:** both tests fail on main and pass with the fix. `tests.multi_process.task_manager` (25 tests) and `tests.multi_process.extraction_engine` pass. black, pylint (`.pylintrc`) and typos are clean on both changed files.

## Details

### What was wrong

`_latest_task_processing_time` is only updated by worker status reports that name a task (`UpdateTaskAsProcessingByIdentifier`, `UpdateTaskAsPendingMerge`). Idle workers do not report, so after any idle period longer than `_TASK_INACTIVE_TIME` the timer is stale.

`CreateTask()` followed by `HasPendingTasks()` then sees a queued task with a stale timer and runs `_AbandonQueuedTasks()` (task_manager.py:482-487). The `_HasTasksPendingRetry()` check at task_manager.py:470 has already run, so the call returns `False`. The foreman leaves its loop and the task is listed in `GetFailedTasks()`. A retry task from `CreateRetryTask()` is abandoned the same way before any worker can pick it up.

**Reproducing input:** a directory source whose preprocessing (or any other worker-idle period) takes more than 5 minutes. The last task is dropped, reported as "Worker failed to process path specification", and the timeline can be empty.

### Fix

A new helper `_UpdateLatestProcessingTimeIfIdle()` is called under the lock in `CreateTask` and `CreateRetryTask`. When nothing is queued or processing, it sets the timer to the current time. If tasks are already queued or processing, workers had work to do, so a missing report still counts as inactivity and the timer is left alone.

The order of the retry check and the queued-task abandonment is unchanged, so a task still gets at most one retry. If no worker ever reports, processing still stops after the timeout.

### Regression tests

- `testHasPendingTasksAfterIdlePeriod`: makes the timer stale, then calls `CreateTask` and `HasPendingTasks()`. The task must stay queued and not be abandoned.
- `testHasPendingTasksWithInactiveWorkers`: a processing task goes stale and is abandoned, `CreateRetryTask` creates the retry, and `HasPendingTasks()` must keep the retry queued. The timer is then made stale again; the foreman loop (`CreateRetryTask` + `HasPendingTasks`) must stop after exactly 1 iteration with 2 tasks in total and only the retry reported as failed.

### Formal model

Found while model checking the task manager with TLA+ (TLC). The `LossReal` configuration, which models the current code, violates the "no lost source" property with a counterexample after 78 states, depth 10. The `LossFixed` configuration models a re-check of `_HasTasksPendingRetry` after `_AbandonQueuedTasks` and holds exhaustively (52,886 states, depth 55). This PR does not use that approach because it can create a new retry on every loop iteration (livelock). The change here targets the stale timer instead and is covered by the tests above, not by the model. In an end-to-end replay, 5 out of 5 runs on main produced an empty timeline.

### Caveats for review

- **Behavior change:** if a task was processing when the workers died, its retry was previously abandoned at once and the run ended about 5 minutes later. The retry now gets its own 5-minute window, so the run ends after about 10 minutes. It is still exactly one retry.
- **Not changed:** if a worker pops the last queued task and dies before reporting, the task is still abandoned without a retry, as the design comment at task_manager.py:478-480 describes.
- **Simulated run:** with a simulated clock and workers that never report, the foreman stops after about 5 minutes with 1 task in total and 1 failed. No livelock.
- **Related:** #5253 (abandoned task revived by a late status update) only changes `UpdateTaskAsProcessingByIdentifier`. The two branches merge cleanly in either order. This change also removes one trigger of that bug: fresh queued tasks are no longer abandoned and then revived. See also #1867.

Fixes #5283

author: legitimate-apps
body:
Round two of Android queue follow-ups from #183's review, plus a Play that was lost before the playback service bound (spec §14.1, §28 2026-10-01).

- **Edits while a queue loads.** Move, Remove and Clear Up Next are refused (return false, change nothing) while a new queue loads, instead of editing the old queue and then being wiped. Next, Previous and Jump are not refused: they move within the old queue and abandon the one loading — and now drop its held additions at that moment.
- **Dropped additions are announced.** When additions held for a loading queue are dropped (the queue failed, was replaced, stopped, or abandoned by Next/Previous/Jump), the controller publishes how many, and the phone, TV library and TV Now Playing show it once.
- **Play before binding.** A Play pressed before the playback service binds was silently lost (`playAlbum` returned false). `PlaybackBinding` now holds the latest Play and makes it once the service binds — album, artist, track lists, playlists and phone search; TV opens Now Playing only after the Play is made, and retained TV click handlers reach the current controller. What it does not cover is stated in its doc: a held Play is lost on activity recreation or when the screen holding it leaves.
- **Defensive code.** A dead per-generation filter removed; a late failure from a replaced queue's lookup no longer wipes the newer queue's held additions (tested; failed with the check removed).

**Evidence:** host tests only — core 1139, phone 148, TV 56, 0 failures (`--rerun-tasks`, counts from XML). Soaked on the CI runner: the **full** phone and TV unit suites 5 of 5 each (runs 36820120219, 36820640503), because the before-bind tests were sensitive to earlier test classes in the same process. Not driven on an emulator or device.

**Review:** independent review blocked once (Next/Previous/Jump kept held additions, and three texts said otherwise); fixed in 60dd6fbf. Should-fixes left as follow-ups: a possible double toast when two TV activities overlap, a drop notice shown long after the fact, and a phone artist Play that can go dead when a held one is replaced.

body:
Build Checklist's length (Half day ... Longer, No limit) was read only by the older document-driven builder. Whenever a registry standard was ticked the scope-driven builder ran and ignored it, and its man-day scaling is clamped to the same floor for a multi-standard scope - so Language Services UK got 59 questions at every length.

For a surveillance, the chosen length is now a target question count. The builder scales its SAMPLED sections - process themes, Annex A controls, processes, documents and Knowledge Base clauses - and takes the largest sample that fits. The ISO/IEC 17021-1 mandatory elements, Stage 1 focus points and the surveillance core are never trimmed; if they alone exceed the target, the smallest sample is used. "No limit" covers every clause of the scope. Initial and recertification audits are unchanged (full coverage).

Language Services-style scope: Half day 25, One day 29, Two days 44, Three days 59, Longer 72, No limit 113 - every one releasable.

author: aematec
body:
Seguimiento de [#48](https://github.com/AEMATEC/AEMATEC-web/pull/48): corrige los tres hallazgos de Graphify que tenían fundamento.

## Cambios
1. **Una propuesta falsa ya no puede hacer borrar el archivo de otro material** (`assets/js/admin/moderacion.js`, `firestore.rules`).
   - El problema: quien propone un material escribe la ruta de su archivo (`storagePath`, `explanation.storagePath`). Alguien podía proponer un material que apuntara al archivo de un material bueno, y si un moderador lo eliminaba, se borraba el archivo bueno.
   - Ahora, antes de borrar un archivo, la moderación comprueba que esté en la carpeta de recursos y que **ningún otro material lo use**.
   - Además, las reglas exigen que esas rutas apunten a `recursos/<su sección>/…` con un nombre válido. Eso aplica a los materiales que se propongan desde ahora.
2. **Al eliminar un material se borra primero el registro y después los archivos.** Si algo falla a medias, queda a lo sumo un archivo sin usar, nunca un material publicado sin su archivo.
3. **`accederConRol` (`assets/js/acceso.js`) cierra la sesión** también si falla la comprobación del rol, y muestra un mensaje en vez de un error.

No se tocó el aviso sobre las redirecciones `aematec_*.html`: se borraron a propósito porque el sitio aún no es público.

## Validación
- `cd tests && npm test`: 92/92, incluidas 2 pruebas nuevas.
  - Rutas válidas o inválidas: otra sección, el Inventario, `..` y una explicación que apunta al archivo principal.
  - Que un moderador puede buscar qué materiales usan un archivo, y el público no.
- `node tests/revisar-paginas.mjs` y `node tests/revisar-enlaces.mjs`: sin errores. `admin.html` e `inventario.html` cargan sin errores de consola.

## Qué conviene revisar
- Como moderador, eliminar un material pendiente de prueba y confirmar que desaparece de la lista y que su archivo se borra en Storage.

author: manganite
body: Replaces the Dependabot PRs #8 (Werkzeug), #9 (Flask) and #10 (Jinja2). None of them could be merged: - Each bump on its own made `requirements.txt` unresolvable. Flask 3.1.3 needs `werkzeug>=3.1`, Werkzeug 3.1.6 needs `markupsafe>=2.1.1`, and Jinja2 3.1.6 needs `markupsafe>=2.0`. - Dash 1.11 calls `Flask.before_first_request` and imports `werkzeug.debug.tbtools.get_current_traceback`. Both were removed in the versions that fix the advisories, so the app would not have started. ## Changes - **Stack:** Python 3.12, Dash 4.4, dash-bootstrap-components 2.0, Flask 3.1.3, Werkzeug 3.1.9, Jinja2 3.1.6, pandas 3, numpy 2, scipy 1.18. Dependencies are declared in `requirements.in` and pinned in `requirements.txt` via `uv pip compile`. - **pandas port:** `DataFrame.append` is replaced by `pd.concat`, `fillna(method=)` by `bfill()`, and the row-wise `apply` by a vectorized `fillna`. Chained assignment is removed. - **Data range:** JHU CSSE stopped reporting recovered cases on 2021-08-05; from then on the series is 0. Active cases are derived from recovered cases, so the analysis ends on 2021-08-04 (`settings/config.py: end_date`). Labels show this date instead of "today". Seven entries with no confirmed case by that date (e.g. Korea, North, Tonga, Winter Olympics 2022) are excluded, which leaves 195 countries. - **Fixes to pre-existing behavior:** - The forecast is now a true 30 days (`HORIZON`); before, it was 29. - The panel values for the start and end of the forecast window are daily new cases and are now labeled "New cases" instead of "Active cases". - The country dropdown can no longer be cleared; clearing it sent `None` to every callback and raised `KeyError`. - **Fit robustness:** For 10 of the countries the logistic fit does not converge with the original initial guess (rate 1/day). These countries were still growing exponentially at the end of the data. In that case the fit is retried with a slow growth rate; for all other countries the result stays the same. - **Static version:** `build_static.py` precomputes all countries as JSON. `static_site/index.html` renders them with Plotly.js and stores the selected country in the URL hash (`#germany`). Country names from the CSV are escaped in the inline script and set via `textContent` in the panel. A slow earlier request cannot overwrite a newer selection, and a failed load clears the display. The builder only deletes output directories that it created itself. - **Deployment:** `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds and deploys on every push to `master`. Only the deploy job holds Pages/OIDC permissions. ## Required after merge 1. Make the repo public (Settings → General → Danger Zone), or use GitHub Pro. 2. Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**. 3. Run the workflow once (Actions → "Deploy static dashboard to GitHub Pages" → Run workflow), or push to `master`. ## Validation - Clean Python 3.12 venv installed from `requirements.txt`. - `python -W error build_static.py` builds 195 countries; only the `exp()` overflow from `curve_fit` and scipy's `OptimizeWarning` are filtered. - In headless Chromium, the static page was tested for all tabs, country switching, a delayed earlier response, a failed load (HTTP 500) and a country name crafted with ``. There were no JS errors and no injection. - In headless Chromium, the Dash app rendered all four figures and the panel and switched countries, with no server-side exceptions. - Not tested: the GitHub Actions deployment itself, which only runs after merge and Pages activation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01QxUgq3T4yeJkkoNxcwktBr

body:
## Summary

Fix the Neovim language tooling, add support for more languages and file types, and replace some plugins with current ones.

### Language tooling

- mason.nvim has no `ensure_installed` option, so a new machine did not get the linters and formatters. mason-tool-installer.nvim now installs all servers and tools.
- The tailwindcss server did not start: its `root_dir` used the old lspconfig function signature. The custom configs for vtsls, astro, superhtml, tailwindcss, unocss and autotools_ls now use the nvim-lspconfig defaults.
- All servers get the LSP keymaps (`LspAttach` autocmd).
- nvim-lint uses an explicit `linters_by_ft`, not the Mason package names.
- New: CSS, Rust, Python (ruff, basedpyright), Go, Java, Kotlin, Perl, Ruby (rubocop server), JSON and YAML with SchemaStore schemas, TOML, Dockerfile and Compose, sh and bash, Markdown, GitHub Actions.

### Install changes (dev group)

- `java` (Temurin 21, mise) for jdtls, ktlint and google-java-format. `path.zsh` sets `JAVA_HOME`: the jdtls launcher cannot start java through the mise shim.
- `gem:rubocop` and `gem:solargraph` (mise). The gem launchers that Mason makes cannot find the relocatable mise Ruby.
- `perl` and `cpanminus` (brew). `run_after_35-perl-critic.sh` installs Perl::Critic into `~/.local/share/perl5` for perlnavigator.
- The mise script hides the progress bars (`MISE_QUIET=1`). They redrew full lines during the long gem builds.

### Plugin changes

- telescope → fzf-lua (uses fzf, fd, rg).
- harpoon (v1 API) → grapple.nvim. plenary.nvim has no more users.
- mini.diff and mini.git → gitsigns.nvim.
- mbbill/undotree → the built-in undotree of Neovim 0.12.
- LuaSnip removed (blink.cmp uses `vim.snippet`). mini.ai added.
- `.chezmoiremove` removes the old plugin spec files from the target.

### Known problems

- The Mason registry entry for kotlin-lsp on Linux arm64 has a template error (`{{{`). The install can fail on that platform.
- kotlin-lsp needs `ROCKSDB_MUSL_LIBC=false` when musl is installed. The config sets it.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/check.sh` passes on each commit.
- [x] Isolated Neovim (separate config, data and mise directories): all 38 Mason tools install. A server, formatter and linter attach for each of 24 test files.
- [x] `nvim --headless +qa` writes no output, also before Mason installs the tools.
- [x] Perl::Critic installs with cpanm. perlnavigator shows its diagnostics.
- [x] Applied on a workstation. fzf-lua, grapple, gitsigns, undotree and mini.ai work.
- [ ] Lint workflow.
- [ ] Install workflow (Ubuntu amd64 and arm64, macOS arm64).

author: norvalbv
body:
## Why

sc-2785: a full suite at load avg 203 failed three `review.test.mts` ceiling tests with exit 124. Setup spent the whole `DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` before reaching the wedge, so the ceiling named `snapshot` instead of `assets`. Nothing in the output said "load, not your diff", and classifying the failures took a 15-minute solo re-run.

#677 already raised those ceilings from 30s to 90s, which is the remedy `suite-hangs-bound-at-the-spawn-site` sanctions. This PR closes the remaining gap: classifying the failure from the output alone.

## What

- `cli/__tests__/_helpers.mts`: `ceilingTimeoutMessage()`. The asset-wedge and deps-final tests now fail with `ceiling-timeout: the 90s setup ceiling fired during <phase> before reaching <phase> (… loadavg=… cpus=…)` when all three hold: exit 124, review's own setup-ceiling banner present, and the wedge's marker **absent**. The label names the likelier cause: machine load when the 1-minute loadavg exceeds the cpu count, otherwise a real hang in the named phase. Without the banner, or with the marker reached, the strict assertions still report.
- `vitest.global-setup.mjs` (root `globalSetup` only, so it runs once; also composed into `vitest.e2e.config.mjs`): every run prints `devkit test load: start|end loadavg=a/b/c cpus=N` to stderr. A globalSetup rather than a reporter, because `test-report-run` passes `--reporter`, which replaces config reporters. `summary.json` is untouched; it is a shipped, runner-agnostic contract.
- Docs: a `ceiling-timeout:` section in `docs/troubleshooting.md`, a generic paragraph in `skills/testing/SKILL.md`, and a dated note on `suite-hangs-bound-at-the-spawn-site`.

**Not done (story criterion b):** load-scaled ceilings and a serial retry. Both conflict with the raise-only / never-serialise rulings (`suite-hangs-bound-at-the-spawn-site`, `test-deadlines-are-hang-detectors`).

## Evidence

- `cli/__tests__/ceiling-timeout.test.mts`, 17 tests. Edge cases covered:
  - a reached marker with the wrong phase gives no label
  - a 124 without the ceiling banner gives no label
  - low load, and load exactly at the cpu count, both point at a real hang instead of blaming load
  - exits 0, 1, 143 and null give no label
  - colon-qualified steps stay whole
  - a fractional ceiling parses
  - Windows' all-zero loadavg prints as is
  - setup and teardown each print exactly one line
