author: tysais
body:
## The defect

CLI `--now` / MCP `force` / HTTP `force` promise "post immediately even outside the anti-bot window (8am-11pm)". The flag bypassed only the CLI/MCP queue-to-schedule layer; the engine's own gate (`UploadService._deferred`) ignored it, so a forced post still came back `Outside posting hours (8am-11pm), deferred` with nothing queued.

The **text route** is the worst case: the schedule store cannot carry a text post (no file to hold) and `manual_defer` documents a manual text post as never window-gated, yet `upload_text_to_platform` gated it anyway. Net effect on current main, observed live 2026-10-01 from the deployed CLI:

- `xpst post --text "..." -p x` at 01:40 local -> a `deferred` row, **nothing queued**, exit 0 — the intent evaporated (exactly the D2 failure G11 forbids: deferral must be scheduling, not a black hole);
- adding `--now` changed nothing (the engine gate ignores the flag).

## The fix

- `_deferred()` gains `ignore_window`; every engine manual route (`post_manual`, `post_manual_image`, `post_manual_carousel`) forwards `force_now` -> `ignore_window`, so the gate honours the surfaces' documented bypass on **every** route. (Before: a forced media post at midnight skipped the CLI's queue layer, then got deferred by the engine gate with nothing queued — a second black hole.)
- `upload_text_to_platform` **drops** the time-of-day gate: a manual text post publishes immediately, matching `manual_defer`'s documented design (a tweet at midnight is cheap; the queue cannot hold it).
- CLI `--now`, MCP `force` and HTTP body `{"force": true}` now propagate to the engine kwarg on every route instead of being accepted and dropped.
- Defaults unchanged: with no flag, the gate still defers media routes exactly as before (the existing G11 test in `test_lane_e_safety.py` passes untouched).

## Evidence

- **Live regression proof:** on this branch, a real text post fired at **03:05 local (outside the window)** published immediately: https://x.com/tysn_dev/status/2105584898765623504 — read back from X's own syndication API (`id_str 2105584898765623504`, text verbatim, `tysn_dev`, 2026-10-01T09:05:34Z). The identical command on main tip returns `deferred` + nothing queued.
- New `tests/test_force_now_window_bypass.py` (11 tests): gate respects/ignores the flag; all three engine manual routes forward `force_now` as `ignore_window` (True and False); CLI `--now` and MCP+HTTP `force` reach the engine kwarg; a night-time text post publishes (black-hole regression) on the engine and the CLI; a no-force HTTP post still passes `force_now=False`.
- Targeted suites green: new file + text posts + content-surface parity + D-wave + lane-E + preflight parity + mcp/cli parity + schedule/dashboard/upload neighbours = **285 passed, 3 skipped** across two combined runs.
- `ruff check src tests` clean, `mypy src/xpst` clean.
- Full suite was running at PR-open time on this commit; the result will be posted as a comment.

Context: found while re-verifying the live-post half of kanban card t_3419c2f9 (text posts X+Threads) — this defect sat directly on that card's acceptance path.

author: code-yeongyu
body:
## Summary

In a `bun build --compile` executable (the standalone omo binary, the desktop app's bundled engine, senpi's own binaries), Bun Shell runs a `bun` command as `process.execPath` when `PATH` has no Bun. That is the engine itself, so an eval cell's `bun test` started a **second agent** and its chat reply came back as the command's stdout with **exit code 0**. The bash tool reported `bun: command not found`. Refs code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#9362, engine side (tracking issue, P0; it closes with the omo hotfix that adopts this). omo adopts the senpi release that carries it, and the desktop picks it up through its runtime pin (code-yeongyu/omo-desktop-app#1417).

The child cannot tell it was meant to be Bun: its argv and argv0 match a normal launch (measured with a minimal compiled probe). So the fix is on the parent side:

- `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/bundled-bun.ts` (new): when `Bun.main` is under Bun's embedded root (`/$bunfs/`, `<drive>:\~BUN\`), write `bun`/`bunx` scripts (`.cmd` on Windows) that run this executable with `BUN_BE_BUN=1`. They go under `<agentDir>/bundled-bun/<execPath hash>/`, with a `tmpdir()` fallback. That directory is **appended** to `PATH`.
- `getShellEnv()` (bash tool, terminal) returns its env through `withBundledBunCommands()`.
- `senpi-codemode` `createRuntime` adds the same `PATH` to the kernels' session environment. The JS worker applies it and pins it for `Bun.$`; py/rb/jl merge it into their interpreter env.

Appending keeps a user's own Bun first. `BUN_BE_BUN` is set only inside the script, never in the engine's environment, so the engine's self-spawns (task/memory children) keep running the engine.

## Tests (user-visible behavior, compiled binary, `PATH` without Bun)

`packages/coding-agent/test/compiled-bun-shell-commands.test.ts` compiles a stand-in engine (`test/fixtures/compiled-bun-shell.mjs`) that runs one command with `getShellEnv()` through Bun Shell (an eval cell) or `/bin/sh` (the bash tool):

- happy: `bun --version` prints Bun's version; `bun install` with a local `file:` dependency, then `bun test`, shows `1 pass`; `bunx --version`; the bash-tool shell gets a working `bun`; a Bun on the user's `PATH` stays in front.
- failure: a failing suite reports `1 fail` with a non-zero exit; an unknown `bun` script fails non-zero; an agent dir that cannot hold the scripts falls back to tmp and still runs Bun.
- RED with the `getShellEnv` wiring removed: 7/8 fail (the user-Bun-first case is a guard; mutating append to prepend makes it fail).

## End-to-end on the real compiled omo binary

A mock OpenAI-compatible model drives one real agent turn (no tokens). It asks for an eval cell that runs `bun --version`, `bun install`, `bun test` (passing and failing projects), `bunx --version`, and an unknown command, with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`.

RED, released omo 5.1.7 (engine senpi 2026.9.30):

| command | exit | output |
|---|---|---|
| `bun --version` | 0 | `omo 5.1.7 (engine: senpi 2026.9.30; scheme nodef)` |
| `bun install` | 1 | `Missing install source. Usage: OmO install <source> ...` |
| `bun test` | 0 | `PHANTOM-AGENT-REPLY: I read this as a connectivity test.` |
| failing `bun test` | 0 | same phantom reply |
| `bun no-such-script` | 0 | same phantom reply |

The mock saw 3 phantom agent requests; 4 session files were created for one turn.

**GREEN on a rebuilt compiled omo binary** (omo dev + senpi 2026.9.30 with the code changes from code-yeongyu/senpi#2494; darwin-arm64), same harness as the RED run: one real agent turn driven by a mock model, `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` (no Bun).

| command | exit | output |
|---|---|---|
| `bun --version` | 0 | `1.4.2` |
| `bun install` | 0 | `1 package installed [6.00ms]` |
| `bun test (passing project)` | 0 | `bun test v1.4.2 (744846f84)` |
| `bun test (failing project)` | 1 | `bun test v1.4.2 (744846f84)` |
| `bunx --version` | 0 | `1.4.2` |
| `bun no-such-script` | 1 | `` |

Mock model: **0 phantom requests**, **1 session file** (RED: 3 and 4). `bun test` output contains `1 pass`: true; the failing project's contains `1 fail`: true.

With a real Bun 1.4.2 earlier on `PATH`, the same turn uses that Bun: 0 phantom requests, 1 session file, `bun --version` = `1.4.2`.

The PR's compiled-fixture test (`compiled-bun-shell-commands.test.ts`) runs 8 cases through both Bun Shell and `/bin/sh`: happy paths, a failing suite, an unknown command, a user Bun on `PATH`, and an agent directory that cannot hold the scripts. With the fix removed, 7 of 8 fail.

QA note: an omo dev binary takes `@code-yeongyu/senpi-codemode` from npm at the pinned senpi version. The eval-kernel half of the fix reaches users only once omo adopts a senpi release that contains it.

## Checks

- `vitest run test/compiled-bun-shell-commands.test.ts`: 8/8
- `senpi-codemode` session-env suites (`session-env`, `js-kernel-session-env`, `py-kernel-session-env`, `extension-session-env`, `bridge-protocol`): 29/29
- `bun run check`: CI Static checks pass; local `tsc --noEmit` (root and scripts) exit 0
- `test/suite/no-sync-in-session-path.test.ts`: caught the two new sync script writes on the session path. They are now in the ledger with their bound (at most twice per process, compiled executables only): 5/5

author: danielgwilson
body:
Splits `createGuestChromiumText` (src/guest/chromium-text.ts, 264 counted lines) into named steps, the way #1248 split `createGuestRuntimeDesktop`, with no behavior change. Everything stays in chromium-text.ts, so the guest packager's module set does not change.

## The cut

| Step | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Admission and protocol checks, pure | `isAdmissibleText`, `ownedFrameId`, `isExecutionContextId`, `evaluateParams`, `probeAccepted` |
| Target events | `targetHandlers`, `watchTargetEvents`, `unwatchTargetEvents` |
| Scope check | `checkScope` |
| Operation runner (5 s deadline, abort, interrupts, dispatch tracking) | `runOperation` |
| Bounded detach, one attempt per session | `sessionDetacher`; the memo stays in its closure |
| Owner check and probe | `assertOwnerReady`, `probeElement` |
| Preparation | `acquireIsolatedWorld` |
| Handle | `preparedHandle` (paste is an async method, as before), `disposePrepared` |
| Port close | `closePort` |

- `TextPortSettings` holds what never changes: context, page, assertFocusedWindow and worldName.
- `TextPortState` holds each field that changes after construction and that more than one function reads: generation, closed, unusable, dialogSeen, busy, activeDisposal, interruptions, sessions. `closing` stays a local of the factory.
- `PreparedText` holds one handle's session, contextId, used, disposed, dispatchedText and disposal.
- No await or microtask boundary is added or removed. paste keeps owner check → RECHECK probe → owner check → check → insertText with dispatch tracked. The event handlers and `checkScope` stay synchronous.
- Shared fields are read from state at each use. prepareText reads the generation before it constructs the lifetime controller, as before.
- `isAdmissibleText` and `isExecutionContextId` are the negated old refusal expressions, operand for operand.
- The factory goes from 264 to 71 counted lines; the largest function is now `runOperation` at 55. The file goes from 305 to 437 counted lines, mostly record types and parameter lists.

## Proof

- Characterization (commit 1): 33 new cases, 39 to 72, passing five consecutive runs on the unchanged closure.
  - Refusal and ordering cases stay in tests/guest/chromium-text.test.ts. Interrupt and teardown cases are in the new tests/guest/chromium-text-lifecycle.test.ts.
  - The shared fixture moved unchanged to tests/helpers/chromium-text-port.ts, so neither test file passes the 700-line lint cap.
  - 18 of the cases came from survivors of the first mutation round.
- Pure checks: tests/guest/chromium-text-checks.test.ts, 5 table tests.
- Mutation tally: 134 mutants on refusal, runner, teardown and ordering branches.
  - Round 1, on the first split: 104 of 133 killed (a 134th mutant did not apply to the formatted code).
  - Round 2, after the 18 new cases: 127 of 134.
  - Final head, after the helper rewrite and the test move: 127 of 134, the same seven survivors.
  - Two survivors change microtask timing only. They are caught by the probe below and have no unit test, because one would pin offsets:
    - dropping runOperation's initial check;
    - dropping paste's explicit `op.check()` before the insertText step.
  - Five survivors are equivalent:
    - the dispatch field on the interrupt's rejection never escapes, because runOperation's catch rebuilds the error from `dispatched`;
    - the detach memo's `.catch` guard: every caller attaches a handler synchronously;
    - the late-acquisition `state.closed` test: close interrupts every running operation, which aborts `op.signal` first;
    - disposal's code fallback: the detach memo only rejects with transport_failed;
    - disposal's `activeDisposal === self` guard: busy is released in the same `finally`, so no other handle can install itself before it runs.
- Scheduling probe:
  - It fires a caller abort, a frame navigation, a dialog or a port close 0 to 14 microtasks after each of 11 port calls: 660 cases.
  - It records the interleaved trace of calls, disruptions and outcomes, the target listener count and the caller-signal listener balance.
  - main (9bf6b6b2) and this branch give byte-identical output.
  - One extra `await` before paste's final check changes 31 of the 660 traces, so the probe resolves a single tick.
  - The probe is kept in the private handoffs folder. It is not a test, because it pins offsets.
- Codex old-versus-new review, three passes.
  - Pass 1 found three differences, all fixed:
    - the generation was read after `new AbortController()`, reachable only with an instrumented constructor;
    - paste was a plain function instead of an AsyncFunction;
    - the target handlers were arrows, so not constructible.
  - Pass 1 also noted the five new helper exports, kept for the direct tests. src/index.ts is unchanged.
  - Pass 2 confirmed the three fixes. It found two comparisons that differ only if `Buffer.byteLength` or `Number.isSafeInteger` is replaced to return NaN. Both helpers are now the negated old expressions.
  - Pass 3 confirmed both helpers resolved and found no remaining difference.
- Packager: `node scripts/guest-runtime-package.mjs`, with and without `--media`, main against e8d71470:
  - the same 56 and 58 modules and the same 982 dependency files;
  - the same payload leaf set, 1021 and 1023 files;
  - only chromium-text.ts/.js and the generated revision file change.
- Local: tsc, lint (444 warnings, one fewer than main), knip, format:check, docs:check, and vitest on tests/guest plus the two guest-runtime script tests (330 tests).

## Local VM proof

Source-built local VM proof at e8d71470: pass ([comment](https://github.com/danielgwilson/humanish/pull/1287#issuecomment-5928625922)).
- Run `cua-2026-10-01T09-26-58-744Z-8b8719e1` passed (`goal_satisfied`). Verify exited 0 with 16 ok and 0 failed.

author: huancheng65
body:
Part of #1544. Every room's session shares the session host's kernel, and one session without bounds took the others, and the services beside them, into swap.

- **Memory cap per session.** tmux puts each pane in its own scope under the user manager, outside the connector's unit, so a limit on the connector never reached a session. The launcher now re-runs itself in a `systemd-run --user --scope` with `MemoryMax` from `AGENT_SESSION_MEMORY_MAX_MB` (default 3072, 0 lifts it) and swap off, only for sessions on `AGENT_SESSION_DEVICE_ID`. It also raises the session's `oom_score_adj` to 500: under an exempt parent a capped process stalls at its cap instead of being killed. A host without user scopes runs the session uncapped and logs it.
- **TMPDIR on disk.** Sessions get `/var/tmp/cheese-<uid>/<resource>` instead of the host's tmpfs `/tmp`; room cleanup removes it with the home and work tree.
- **Admission on host memory.** The per-project `max_concurrent_turns` stays. A turn whose session starts on the session host (its backend, picked as the turn picks it, has its hands elsewhere) now also waits, with the room's queue notice, until `MemAvailable` covers one more session at the cap. Rooms whose session runs beside its workspace (pi) and rooms whose session is already running are never held; an unreadable host holds nobody.

**Preconditions on the session host.** The session host is the `nictheboy` user (uid 1000) on the dev box, home `/home/nictheboy/cheese-central-session`. Read-only checks: sessions sit in `user@1000.service/app.slice/tmux-spawn-*.scope`; `user@1000` is running with `Linger=yes`; its `cgroup.subtree_control` is `cpu memory pids`, so the memory controller is delegated; tmux 3.5a, systemd 257; current sessions have `oom_score_adj=200`; `/tmp` is a 32G tmpfs with 17G used. The one thing not verified there is whether a session's environment reaches the user bus. The tmux server creating `tmux-spawn-*` scopes says it does, but we have no access to run `systemd-run --user --scope` as that user. Locally, the launcher under real systemd 257 produced the scope with `memory.max` = 3221225472, and a 200 MB allocation in a 64M scope was OOM-killed once the score was raised.

author: mengwong
body:
Spec only, no code.

Adds `specs/todo/UNKNOWN-EVALUATION-SPEC.md`. Today an unsupplied input stops evaluation (`Stuck`) wherever it is first inspected. Because `AND`/`OR`/`IMPLIES`/`NOT` are rewritten into `IF` (`Machine.hs:1198-1205`), the answer depends on which side of the operator the unknown is on: `FALSE AND x` answers and `x AND FALSE` gets stuck. The probes also found a silent path: a `CONSIDER` with a catch-all branch quietly takes it on an unknown (§2.4).

What the spec defines (§4), as ruled:
- The connectives get their own machine frames, as regulative `RAND`/`ROR` already have (U2).
- Evaluation stays left-sequential, so every fully supplied directive's answer is unchanged. Only an undecided left operand evaluates the right one, under the strong Kleene tables, and an undecided Boolean is returned as a residual over the unknown inputs (U1).
- Every evaluation is lifted; there is no mode. The caller chooses only the report: the default ("I needed to know …", naming every input), K3, or the residual (U7b).
- Errors, refusals and give-ups under an undecided guard are kept as guarded leaves and never absorbed (U11, U11b, U13, U13b, C3).
- Residuals are decided at the boundary by truth table on every host; z3 serves only the planner and `l4 prove` (U3, DU3b, D1).

Rulings U1–U13 and D1, with their amendments and the seven Symbolic Evaluation Conflicts rulings, are recorded in §9. §8 is the build sequence in seven steps, each with its §4.12 test rows; a 15-agent audit and four adversarial reviews checked that every step is buildable from the recorded rulings. Choices made overnight on 2026-10-02 are labelled "decided by Claude overnight, pending Meng's review", and six questions for steps 4–6 are listed in §9 "Open for Meng". Nothing in §4–§8 is built.

Sibling spec: `TYPICALLY-ONE-BEHAVIOUR-SPEC.md` (#525, merged). Its T3/T4 meet U8/U9 here.

## Summary
Five reader features in one pull request. Plan §8 says one PR per work item; the owner asked on 2026-10-01 for larger, themed PRs to cut the CI wait. Each feature keeps its own commits, and each was preflighted on its own branch before being stacked here.

| Feature | Requirement | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| Read aloud across pages | FR-READ-008 | Reading goes on from the page on screen to the end of the document, skips blank pages and turns the pages as it reads. A stop or a cancel ends it. |
| Ask before opening a link | Threat T-02 | A tapped link shows its full address first. Only `http(s)`, `mailto` and `tel` can open; anything else, such as `file:`, is refused. |
| Stamps | FR-ANN-006 | Markup › Stamp: today's date, a tick, a cross, or up to 60 characters of text. A stamp is a FreeText annotation, so other PDF apps show and edit it. |
| Bookmarks | FR-READ-009 | More › Bookmark this page. Bookmarks are stored in the PDF's outline, so they survive a save and travel with the file. |
| Annotation list | FR-ANN-003 | More › Annotations lists every annotation by page, jumps to one, and shares the list as text. |

English and French strings for all five.

author: damianvtran
body:
# Summary

Defines the coalescer's output in `docs/push-cloud-ops.md`, following the ruling that **the digest is a machine-composed visible alert on its own emit type** — and that there is **exactly one composer**. Core's S5 review found that §2.1's "one digest push naming the count" collided with §3.2's silent `attention` form (the only form carrying `count`), so a coalesced catch-up produced a push no user ever saw.

Rebased onto `main` at `cc2569a` (the ADR amendment, PR #19), which left this file byte-identical.

- Kind of change: docs
- Key changes, all in `docs/push-cloud-ops.md`:
  - **§3, "The digest, exactly — and there is one composer"**: `type: "digest"`, a third emit type beside `completion` and `attention`. **The machine mints the payload** (`type`, `emit_id`, `count`, an `aps.alert` built from the house constants) once, when a catch-up exceeds its burst limit. **The cloud composes nothing** — it mints no payload, renders no banner from `type`/`kind`/`count`, and never edits, rewords or synthesises alert text.
  - **The cloud's 60/hour ceiling is a delivery guard over frames it already holds**: it re-delivers the most recent frame for that computer, **whatever its type**, collapsed as `digest:<computer>`, with that frame's `alert` verbatim, and records a drop **only when it holds no frame at all** — so the 61st event never vanishes because it happened to be a completion. Its digest record is a record of **deliveries**, not a second payload class.
  - **`alert: {title, body}` is required on `completion` and `digest` and absent on `attention`**, and is delivered verbatim; the cloud never renders a banner from `type`, `kind` or `count`.
  - Collapse: `apns-collapse-id` / `notification.tag` = `digest:<computer>`, so digests never stack. `aps.badge` still never sent; `content-available` never used for a digest.
  - **`exclude`** is permitted on a digest with the attention form's meaning and **never required** there — the required case is the ack-triggered attention emit, and a catch-up digest has no acting device.
  - **Idempotency**: one `emit_id` minted when the window closes and persisted, key `sha256("digest" ‖ emit_id ‖ computer)`, retries reuse it, a new window gets a new key.
  - Terms this file uses alone are defined where it is read alone: **P2** (no conversation name, snippet or transcript reaches the cloud) and **the house constant** (the machine's fixed sentence, never model-written text).

User impact: none — documentation only, no code.

## Related issues

- None. This is the note's half of the cross-repository digest amendment; the ADR half landed as PR #19 (`cc2569a`).

## Impact

- Breaking changes: none.
- Version bump: none.

## Testing evidence

Docs only; nothing runs. The note is **not covered by the three verification scripts** — they read ADR 0006 and `push-plan.md`, and the only place any of them touches this file is a table-integrity check (`verify-documents.py`, "tables: no wrapped row in the ops note"), which passes.

```
$ LOCAL_OPERATOR_REPO=~/local-operator python3 docs/adr/0006-verification/verify-documents.py
182/182 checks pass; ref=WORKTREE                                     (rc=0)
$ LOCAL_OPERATOR_REPO=~/local-operator python3 docs/adr/0006-verification/resolve-citations.py
mappings=30  distinct (ref,path,line) citations CHECKED=154  dual-ref pairs checked=45
OK: every cited path exists at its ref and every cited line resolves   (rc=0)
$ LOCAL_OPERATOR_REPO=~/local-operator python3 docs/adr/0006-verification/read-citations.py   (rc=0)
```

Rebase proof (byte-identical step, before the corrections above were amended in): `git range-diff dcb8fe5..e27be08 origin/main..d287334` → the single commit shows `=`, the pre/post diff hashes match (`65f41a0ea2308291`), the 21 +/- line sets are identical, and the blob is `11f2545178c54cff…` at both heads.

author: 27bslash6
body:
Golden-set fixture schema v2 and k-pass scoring for `tune.py eval`.

## What changes

**Fixture.** Each pair now records what an operator did with it (`action`, `action_survivor`) apart from what the label rule says (`label`, `sub_label`, `tags`, `source`). Operators often superseded a pair just to clear the queue, so an operator action is evidence and not ground truth. `rule_version: 2` and `label_rule` state the rule: S / P / C, plus a revocation clause and a main-point clause. The 22 adjudicated pairs are applied: coexist 35 → 51, supersession 114 → 98, unrelated 25. The other 152 pairs keep their labels (`source: operator` or `queue-read`) until they are re-read under the rule. `split.json` is re-cut for the new fixture hash. The Rust harness still parses the fixture. Its extra fields are ignored, and `label`, `survivor` and `source` keep their meaning.

**`tune.py eval`** gains `--passes k`, `--regime {default,thinking-off}` and `--max-usd`.
- With k passes, a pair's verdict is the passes' common verdict, and any dissent abstains. An abstention counts as a recall miss and a yield loss, never as a correct non-supersession.
- The headline reports the false-supersede rate (a wrong survivor counts as one), the coexist bar, recall, precision, survivor accuracy and yield. Each rate has a 95% Wilson interval, and every headline is computed twice: once with `partial` pairs counted as coexist, once as a supersession. Pairs with a `dispute` stay out of the headline.
- Per-pass scoring is unchanged and still matches the Rust harness.
- `default` is the production request. `thinking-off` adds `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`. Neither regime sets `temperature`, because `claude-sonnet-5` rejects any value other than the default 1.0, with or without thinking. The output records the exact request parameters. Unanimity is reported for the default regime only, as a variance diagnostic.
- Spend is checked between chunks of 20 calls. Verdicts already paid for are written out before any exit.

## Verification

- `uv run scripts/judge_tune/test_tune.py` passes (offline). It checks the fixture schema, asserts all 22 adjudicated pairs by hash, and covers consensus voting, abstention charging, both-ways scoring, Wilson intervals, regime parameters and the spend cap.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.15.4) pass on the changed files.
- `cargo test -p alaya-core --test golden_judge --no-run` builds. The ignored test, run without `ALAYA_URL`, panics on the env read that follows `serde_json::from_str(FIXTURE).expect("fixture parses")`, so the fixture deserialises.
- An end-to-end `eval` on 4 real pairs, 2 passes in each regime: both regimes are accepted and the output files and disagreement list are written. Judge spend was USD 0.12.

## What
Every book-level "is this translated" surface reads the stamped rung through one helper set in `src/lib/translation-completeness.ts` (`storedRung`, `isReadableInEnglish`, `translationVerdict`, `TRANSLATION_STATE_PROJECTION`). **Absent field = unstamped**: each reader keeps its pre-ladder arithmetic as the fallback, so nothing changes for a book until sync-worker stamps it.

| surface | before | now (stamped) |
|---|---|---|
| `isTranslationReadable()` (FT badge gate, `isPublicFirst`) | `translated ≥ 0.9·(ocr−blank)` | rung ∈ {readable, complete} — gains the coverage clause; "unknown coverage counts as readable" kept in the fallback |
| `furtherReadingStatus()` | own conjunction (#4653) | rung; label "Complete" at `complete` |
| book page header tick | `translated/(ocr−blank)` ≥ 100% | "✓ Translated" from `readable`, "✓ Complete" at `complete`; percentage via `translationCompleteness()` (also fixes the unstamped preview case) |
| book page `hasTranslations` | `> 50%` of pages | rung readable/complete |
| book page sibling-notice gate | `< 5%` | stamped below `translating` and not an English original |
| `TranslatedSiblingNotice` | sibling `≥ 50%` | sibling in `readable_in_english` |
| `CollectionBookCard` status | tick at 100% | Translated / Complete / "In English" (English original) by verdict, else % |
| `Reader2C` download panel, translation-request CTA (`PaneEmptyState`, `TranslationEditor`), FT progress note | various | rung |
| `translation-percent.ts` | `translated / pages_count` | **deleted**; library route + author page use `translationCompleteness()` |

Projections add `translation_state.{rung,english_original}` on `/api/books/[id]` (nav), `/api/books/library`, `/collections/[id]`, `/es/collections`, and the sibling notice.

## Public copy (Derek)
New labels: "Complete" / "Completo" (card, book header, further reading), "In English" / "En inglés" (card, English originals). Per decision 2 in the design doc.

## Tests
`tests/unit/translation-state-readers.test.ts`: one book per rung (stamps produced by the real `computeTranslationState()`), an English original, and an unstamped book, through verdict / FT gate / further reading / CTA. Negative control recorded: removing the rung check from `isTranslationReadable()` turns the De sensu rerum (23/332 preview) case red; restored. Full suite 372 files / 5181 tests green; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Out of scope
- `books-catalog.ts`, Supabase columns, collection counters (step 4). Browse/catalogue cards fed from Supabase stay on the fallback until step 4 adds `translation_rung`.
- `BibliographicInfo` / `PageMetadataPanel` "Translation: Source Library AI" credit stays on `pages_translated > 0` — a credit for any translated page, not a readability verdict.
- `/api/categories/[id]` keeps its `translated/pages_count` over counts it recomputes from `pages` (blanks in both numerator and denominator); swapping in the stored-counter formula would mix denominators. Comment updated.
- No new threshold; no dedup paths touched.

author: alexanderreaper7
body:
Closes #69

Java nullability annotations previously had no dedicated compiler enforcement, and application packages had no non-null default. Declare `@NullMarked` in all 15 production and 14 test packages and configure NullAway through Error Prone as compiler errors for production and test sources. Unsafe null arguments, returns, dereferences and generic element contracts now fail compilation. New top-level types without an explicit default and meaningless JSpecify annotation locations also fail.

Correct optional entity fields and the contracts exposed by the checker. Generated entity IDs have nullable backing fields; their non-null getters throw `IllegalStateException` before persistence, as selected by the user. Only the no-argument JPA constructor is exempt from required-field initialization checks, because Hibernate populates its fields. Ordinary constructors and all method bodies remain checked. No database migration is needed.

Add positive and negative compiler probes using the real Maven configuration with isolated sources and output, and run them in build CI. The branch starts from main and remains separate from the household and instant-login features. Framework initialization and JTE's separate generated-template compiler remain outside NullAway's analysis, documented in [decision 0027](https://github.com/AlexanderReaper7/teaterihuskvarna/blob/69-application-nullability/docs/decisions/0027-compile-time-nullability.md).

## Validation

- Full Docker `sh scripts/maven.sh verify` passed 75 unit tests and 228 integration tests, plus Checkstyle, SpotBugs and PMD. The 13 new entity checks verify nullable ID fields, failure before ID assignment and successful getter use afterwards; the integration tests exercise Hibernate persistence.
- `sh scripts/check-nullability.sh` passed. Safe code compiled; unsafe returns, arguments, dereferences, nullable collection elements used as non-null, invalid annotation locations and missing defaults produced the expected compiler errors. The probes also run in CI.
- Full `sh e2e/run.sh` built the application image and completed with 272 passed, 1 failed and 1 configured skip. Firefox failed while requesting a login link during setup of the empty-token scenario, before exercising the token. Expected `/logga-in/skickat`, received `/logga-in`, timeout 5000 ms. The trace recorded the click but no POST to `/logga-in`, matching existing E2 in [open questions](https://github.com/AlexanderReaper7/teaterihuskvarna/blob/69-application-nullability/docs/open-questions.md#found-by-the-e2e-suite). The observation is recorded there; its cause remains unknown. No passing rerun is claimed as a fix. The configured Firefox skip duplicates an API-only Chromium test; passkey tests run only under Chromium by suite configuration.
- `python3 docs/check.py --require-mermaid`, shell syntax validation and `git diff --check` passed. A mechanical package scan found no missing `@NullMarked` defaults. No manual browser verification was performed.

author: avznog
body:
The owner, from his iPhone: every date must be `DD/MM/YYYY` and every time 24h.

**Audited before anything was changed, and the remark is narrower than it sounds.** Decision 109 already did that everywhere the app formats a date itself — `lib/calendar/time.ts` and `lib/player/injury.ts` are the only two formatters, all twenty-odd call sites go through them, 24h is pinned twice over by the `fr-FR` locale and an explicit `hour12: false`, and the tests hold the literal strings. **None of that is touched here.** A reviewer should expect to see no change to any existing formatter's behaviour, and that is the point: a remark acted on literally, when the literal reading is already satisfied, produces a diff that changes nothing.

The one surface a formatter cannot reach is the **five native pickers**, which render in the *browser's* locale. On a phone set to English the owner sees `03/14/2026` and an AM/PM clock in the one place the app has no say. Decision 109 saw this and offered him a custom control; he declined then, and has come back to it now with a better answer than either option: **keep the native control — still the best thing under a thumb — and print underneath it the date the app would have printed.**

### What is in it

- **`components/ui/date-input.tsx`** (new) — one shared wrapper for all five, handling both the controlled case (the injury start date, whose value drives the return date's `min`) and the uncontrolled `defaultValue` case. `name`, `required`, `min`, `max`, `id`, `aria-describedby` and `invalid` pass straight through, so every Server Action receives exactly the fields it did before.
- **`lib/calendar/time.ts`** — `formatIsoDay` and `formatInputValueFr`, pure, with five new Vitest cases including the day-shift boundaries.
- **`lib/player/injury.ts`** — now delegates to `formatIsoDay` instead of keeping its own copy of the same arithmetic. The only reason a settled file was touched: the fix for a wrong date format must not introduce a third way to format a date.
- The five call sites, `Input` → `DateInput` and nothing else.

### Three things worth reading before reviewing

- **The echo never constructs a `Date`.** It works on the parts of the `YYYY-MM-DD` string, because parsing that as a `Date` yields UTC midnight, which in a negative-offset zone is the previous day. An off-by-one-day echo would be worse than no echo at all.
- **An empty or unreadable value renders no element at all** — not a placeholder, not `--/--/----`. A screen showing `--/--/----` is stating something; this one has nothing to state, and reserving the space would be the only reason to.
- **The echo is `aria-hidden` and deliberately not in `aria-describedby`.** The defect is that the *eye* sees the browser's locale; a screen reader already speaks the control's value correctly, and appending `14/03/2026` to the description would make the control announce the same date twice in two formats — which is the defect decisions 116 and 117 are about, arriving from the other direction.

### How to verify

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` — all pass, 1329 tests.

Then the part that matters: set the browser to **English** with a negative-offset timezone, which reproduces the owner's phone, and look at the five pickers at 390 × 844 in **both** themes. Done here with Chromium forced to `en-US` / `America/New_York`: the picker reads `10/01/2026` and the line underneath reads `01/10/2026`, i.e. the day/month swap visible side by side. « Guéri le » on a player profile is the clearest one. Check also that an empty picker shows nothing and leaves no gap.

With `javaScriptEnabled: false` the echo is in the server-rendered HTML and the inputs still post their original fields — the no-JavaScript fallback is intact.

`npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. The only contact is four `getByLabel("Coup d’envoi").fill(...)` calls (`e2e/happy-path.spec.ts:162`, `:733`, `:795`, `e2e/offline.spec.ts:83`), which resolve through an unchanged `<label for>`/`id` pair. Expected, not observed — CI is the check.

### Left alone deliberately

`formatDateFr` still returns a non-ISO value untouched and still accepts `2026-02-30`: tightening it would change a pinned test for no gain, and a native picker cannot produce such a value. The strictness lives in `formatInputValueFr` instead. And « nouvel entraînement » still opens with an empty picker rather than the next plausible slot — a product change, not this one.

The decision entry is on `## NNN`; the merging session assigns the number and deletes the italic parenthetical under its header.

body:
## Scope

Refs #6637

Rescope: repository delivery only. The five operational checks below stay on
#6637 after authorized deployment. This PR does not close the issue, merge,
enqueue, deploy, change credentials, change grant ranking, or change KG gate
freshness thresholds. The chart defaults the refresher off; the hub overlay
stages the requested 600-second setting in Git.

## Changes

Part 1:

- Refresh each configured, logged-in Codex ChatGPT grant through the broker's
  cached `GetAccessToken` path using inference-free `GET {base}/wham/usage`,
  `User-Agent: codex-cli`, bearer authorization and `ChatGPT-Account-Id`.
- Check on startup and every 60 seconds. Refresh never-observed or older-than-
  refresh-age grants, serialize each grant's requests, and measure failure
  cooldown from completion. HTTP timeout is 10 seconds; redirects are disabled.
- Keep exhausted grants untouched until future resets pass, including the
  gate's 97 percent threshold. Window-less rejections wait 15 minutes. No device
  login, inference, reset-credit consumption or response-driven credential changes.
- Share the POST quota handler's durable per-grant and per-provider persistence.
  Add `tokenbroker_codex_usage_total{grant,outcome}` without sensitive labels or logs.
- Chart default `TOKENBROKER_CODEX_USAGE_REFRESH_SECONDS=0`; hub overlay `600`;
  embervm-dev unchanged. The base URL defaults to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api`.

Part 2:

- Advance cleanup past held probe rows in ascending session-ID pages. Return at
  most five unheld guests across Claude, Codex and reviewer probe prefixes.
- Log a suppressed Codex probe's session and blocking reason: bound guest,
  running, pending turn or unknown outcome. Bound or running guests always fence.
- Age only orphaned pending/unknown evidence, including uncertain reservations.
  Evidence older than 3,600 seconds stops fencing, without deleting or settling
  its rows. Age the evidence itself, not the session. This is four times the
  900-second gate ceiling and thirty 120-second turn timeouts.
- Cover broker payload admission and probe behavior when both Codex grants are
  stale, then only codex-b or only codex-cluster becomes fresh. Document the
  broker refresher as primary and the unpinned Codex probe as backstop.

## Why #6537 did not guarantee gate recovery

Code-proven causes, confirmed from the pre-fix branch and ranker implementation:

- The probe is unpinned. It refreshes only the grant selected by the egress
  ranker, which tries fresh usable grants first, then stale grants by quota band.
  It cannot refresh an account while that account remains parked, such as codex-b.
- `_cleanup_candidates()` limited to five rows before checking holds. Five held
  rows starved later candidates and could leave a finished probe guest bound.
  `codex_claim()` treated that binding as a fence against every later Codex probe.
- The unresolved fence had no orphan age bound and returned without a signal.

Production-only questions, not established by repository inspection:

- Which path actually fired between 04:40 and 05:51 UTC on October 1, 2026.
- Whether the live monolith revision at 04:40 UTC on October 1, 2026 contained #6537.

## Operational acceptance retained on #6637

- [ ] Tokenbroker pod rolled with `TOKENBROKER_CODEX_USAGE_REFRESH_SECONDS=600`.
- [ ] `tokenbroker_codex_usage_total{outcome="refreshed"}` increasing for codex-b
  and codex-cluster about every 11 minutes.
- [ ] GET `/quota` shows codex-b `age_seconds` under 900 for an hour, including
  drain-idle time.
- [ ] No all-stale `capacity is unconfirmed` deferral over 30 drain-idle minutes.
- [ ] Record the #6537 production rows for October 1, 2026, 04:40 to 05:51 UTC,
  including the live revision and which recovery/fence path fired.

## Upstream contract checked in Part 1

Part 1 re-read these files from `raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main`:

- `codex-rs/backend-client/src/client/rate_limit_resets.rs`: GET usage route,
  separate from reset-credit consumption.
- `codex-rs/backend-client/src/client.rs`: default `codex-cli` user agent,
  authorization and account headers.
- `codex-rs/codex-backend-openapi-models/src/models/rate_limit_status_payload.rs`:
  nullable `rate_limit` envelope.
- `codex-rs/codex-backend-openapi-models/src/models/rate_limit_status_details.rs`:
  allowed, limit_reached and nullable primary/secondary windows.
- `codex-rs/codex-backend-openapi-models/src/models/rate_limit_window_snapshot.rs`:
  integer used percent, window seconds and reset timestamps.

## Validation

- Part 2 targeted Linux SQLite tests:
  `python -m pytest projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/drainer_test.py projects/monolith/factory/quota_probe_test.py projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/model_pool_test.py -q`:
  294 passed. Final probe-only rerun: 52 passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- New tests: `test_cleanup_advances_past_held_rows_and_bounds_unheld_guests`;
  `test_codex_orphan_fence_ages_evidence` (pending, unknown turn, uncertain
  reservation at 3599, 3600 and 3601 seconds);
  `test_codex_bound_or_running_fence_never_ages_out`;
  `test_broker_refresh_reopens_all_stale_kg_gate` (each grant refreshed alone);
  `test_codex_probe_stops_after_either_broker_grant_refresh` (each grant alone,
  with the 900-second cadence expired so it cannot mask the freshness guard).
- Confirmed existing Part 1 coverage:
  `TestCodexUsageSkipsOtherProvidersAndNeedsLogin` starts with no observations
  and asserts one tick refreshes logged-in codex-b. `TestCodexUsageEligibility`
  also covers the never-observed refresh path. These tests were inspected,
  not rerun locally in Part 2. Part 1 source and tests remain unchanged.
- Fourteen Part 2 mutations each failed their matching assertions and were
  restored: cleanup stops after its first five scanned rows; output cap six;

body:
## Summary
- The Pi3 Signage terminal boots from an SD card like the Pi4 kiosks, but SD health monitoring was only enabled for the `kiosk` group. Its `/etc/raspi-status-agent.conf` was written once (2026-08-05) by a retired role with `STORAGE_HEALTH_ENABLED="0"`, and the standard release does not manage that file. Only the heartbeat alert (#1584) would notice a dead card.
- The signage artifact already ships the current `storage_health.py`. The zipapp on the Pi3 contains the #1583 wear signals (checked on the device).
- `release_signage/tasks/health.yml` now imports `host-status-agent-storage.yml` after health has passed. It sets `STORAGE_HEALTH_ENABLED="1"` in the existing file with `lineinfile`. It has its own `rescue`, so it cannot send a healthy Signage release into rollback. It is placed in `health.yml` because the `main.yml` block/rescue/always shape is contract-tested.
- Result: root read-only, kernel mmc/I-O errors, disk and inode usage, under-voltage (current and since boot), and the write rate go to Slack ops through the existing `storage-health-*` alerts, and a daily wear report is logged.
- Owner decision 2026-10-01: monitoring now; adding the Pi3 to the SD backup comes after the Pi4 restore drill.
- Measured on the Pi3 on 2026-10-01, read-only: 64 GB card (06/2024), 11% used, ~0.7 GB written per day, lifetime writes 2.3x the card size, `throttled=0x0`, no kernel storage errors in 7 days. The Pi3 reboots daily at 03:00, so the write-rate window (12 h minimum) and the wear report appear from about 15:00.

## Deploy impact declaration

<!-- deploy-impact:start -->
| Item | Declaration |
| --- | --- |
| Risk | unknown |
| Target machines | pi3, pi4, pi5 |
| Changed surfaces | config, deploy, docs, unknown |
| Required files/artifacts | N/A: one Ansible task file in the release role; the agent code is already on the Pi3 |

## Description

Prepares this repo for the new release flow driven from [scalekit-sdks-wrapper#6](https://github.com/scalekit-inc/scalekit-sdks-wrapper/pull/6), including its first automated Maven Central pipeline. No change to the published artifact.

- `CHANGELOG.md`: seeded from this repo's full GitHub Releases history. From now on each release adds a section in the layout of the wrapper's `standards/release-notes.md` (Breaking changes first, migration code for every breaking entry).
- `.changes/unreleased/`: release-notes fragments wait here between releases (for changes merged with `--skip-release`).
- `pom.xml`: `autoPublish`/`waitUntil` of the Central publishing plugin become properties (`central.autoPublish`, default `false` — today's behaviour), so the release workflow can publish only after the human approval. A local `mvn deploy` still does not auto-publish.

The release tool itself stays in the wrapper (`tools/release/release.py --sdk java`); it bumps `pom.xml`, `Constants.java` and both README snippets together, so they can no longer drift.

## Usage

**No usage change.**

## Testing

- `mvn -B -ntp -DskipTests -Dgpg.skip package` succeeds with the property-based plugin config; `help:evaluate -Dexpression=central.autoPublish` returns `false`.
- `release.py --sdk java status` reads this checkout correctly (all four version locations agree).
- `release.py notes` extracts sections from the seeded CHANGELOG.
- Not run: CI on GitHub for the release workflow — see below.

## Scope

Sibling PRs: scalekit-sdks-wrapper#6 (design, skills, release tool) and the other three SDK repos on the same branch.

**Still to land on this branch:** the workflow change (new `release.yml`: started with a version, gated by the `release` environment, deploys to Maven Central with the Portal token and GPG key held only in that environment; `workflow_call:` on `build.yml`). It is saved as `specs/release-automation/workflow-patches/scalekit-sdk-java.patch` in the wrapper because pushing `.github/workflows/` needs the GitHub `workflow` scope. Apply with `git am` per the wrapper's `ADMIN-SETUP.md` §8, then this PR is complete.

Breaking changes: none.

## Summary
- add private S3-compatible login-guide video mode with server-side AWS SigV4 signing
- keep Access Key / Secret Key in read-only host secret files; never expose the S3 URL or credentials in pre-login HTML
- preserve the existing same-origin guide-video browser relay, Range/HEAD streaming, and explicit no-proxy Control→S3 socket
- default S3 region to `us-east-1` and path-style addressing to `true`
- add optional Compose overlay, pre-update credential validation, release bundling and operator docs

## Private S3 configuration
```dotenv
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_URL=
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_ENDPOINT=https://s3.example.internal
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_REGION=us-east-1
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_BUCKET=platformclaw-media
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_KEY=guides/platformclaw-guide.mp4
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_ACCESS_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/platformclaw_guide_video_s3_access_key
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/platformclaw_guide_video_s3_secret_key
PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true
```

Host credential files:
```text
<deploy-root>/secrets/guide-video-s3-access-key
<deploy-root>/secrets/guide-video-s3-secret-key
```

## Security / network behavior
- credentials are read server-side from bounded secret files
- S3 GET/HEAD requests are SigV4 signed server-side
- Control→S3 uses Node core HTTP(S) with `agent:false`; proxy env/global proxy is not used
- browser sees only the same-origin guide relay
- signed S3 mode follows no redirects
- URL-only mode and private-S3 mode are mutually exclusive
- credential files are validated before image-update teardown

## Validation
- based on latest main `050dfbd69e5`
- focused private-S3/control-plane unit tests: 46/46 passed
- PlatformClaw Docker runtime tooling suite on Windows: 39 passed / 3 Linux-only skipped
- focused oxlint: 0 warnings / 0 errors
- oxfmt check: passed
- shell syntax check: passed
- independent security review: no remaining actionable SigV4/proxy/streaming findings
- independent deployment review: no remaining safety blocker
- SigV4 GET Object construction checked against AWS's published S3 signing test vector

## Root cause
PR #256 only implemented `PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_URL`. The previously discussed `PLATFORMCLAW_GUIDE_VIDEO_S3_*` settings were not actually wired into runtime configuration, so setting those variables alone produced no login guide button. This PR makes that private-S3 configuration real.

author: mashiro01
body:
## Description

When a Store transfer times out, status polling fails, or submission partially fails, the old future can finish before TE accepts batch release. Callers can then drop borrowed descriptors or reuse payload buffers while work remains in flight.

This draft retains the batch and request vector in the existing `TransferEngineOperationState` before submission. Logical failures remain sticky while every task continues to be polled; a future becomes ready only after classic TE `freeBatchID` succeeds. Queries, release, waiting and destruction share the state mutex, and successful release invalidates the handle exactly once. A late consumer of an already completed transfer retains its successful result.

Supported TE scope is **classic, non-event-driven completion**. Event builds and TENT-selected TE paths log an error and return `nullopt` before batch allocation/submission. Local memcpy and other replica paths can still succeed. The event producer's remaining BatchDesc access after publishing task completion requires a separate TE lifecycle fix; this Store patch does not repair that producer.

Related issue: https://github.com/xray-infra/Mooncake/issues/1. Base: `cache-foundation-2026-10-01` at `719735896c86b56fabec6cf3e825fb2ea640597a`. This is an internal code-review draft, with no merge or deployment approval implied.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Breaking change (unsupported event/TENT TE paths now reject before submission)

## How Has This Been Tested?

Actual checks:

- `rtk git diff --check`: **PASS**.
- LLVM 20 `git-clang-format --diff` against the fixed base, restricted to the three changed files: **PASS**, with no files rewritten.
- Three applicable official static pre-commit hooks (`check-merge-conflict`, `check-added-large-files`, and `codespell`) on the final frozen changes: **PASS**. The complete pre-commit pipeline was not run.
- Independent source/diff review: no blocking source finding; this is not a runtime test result.
- Native CMake configure on arm64 macOS: **BLOCKED** by unavailable JsonCpp/GLOG/yaml-cpp; googletest was not fetched because downloads were explicitly disabled. The production target also has Linux/NUMA/libibverbs dependencies.
- Linux CPU production compilation and the specified native checks: **PASS** in [CI run 2](https://github.com/xray-infra/Mooncake/actions/runs/36857126975) and repeated successfully in [CI run 3](https://github.com/xray-infra/Mooncake/actions/runs/36859426215). H/J verified source `43197bae`, workflow `9d823a6` / `1cda82b`, actual production links, XML and CTest artifacts. Nine focused classic regressions passed; the classic whole target passed 19 of 21 cases, including those same nine, with the two variant-gate skips. The event rejection case executed and passed without a skip, and the existing async-fd target passed all five cases. Focused and whole counts overlap and are not additive. TENT-enabled execution and GPU/RDMA remain untested.

Added **9 classic native regressions and 2 build-variant gate tests**. The nine classic cases now have actual Linux CPU PASS evidence; the event rejection gate passed in the event build, while both gates skip in the classic build and the TENT-enabled gate has not run. They cover sticky timeout with late completion; successful completion observed by a late consumer; query error with a busy batch; one failed task alongside pending work; owned descriptors after a partial-submit history; concurrent waiters; destructor waiting; an actual zero-task submit error; and real TCP success. Gate tests destroy the engine backend before calling the rejection path, so allocation/submission must not occur. Classic histories call real TE query/Busy/free APIs with controlled BatchDesc inputs; they do not reproduce an RNIC partial-submit failure or prove DMA drain. The existing native target already registers the tests; no test-only completion abstraction was added.

The first CI run stopped during Store compilation because the validation environment lacked `msgpack.hpp`, with zero tests executed. Adding `libmsgpack-cxx-dev` to the workflow resolved that environment failure; no product code was changed. See the [canonical CI evidence](https://github.com/xray-infra/Mooncake/issues/5#issuecomment-5931521102). The stacked [TE draft #7](https://github.com/xray-infra/Mooncake/pull/7) has separate bounded event CPU RED/GREEN evidence; this Store draft still rejects event/TENT TE submission and neither draft is merged.

Required Linux command after a genuine production build:

```bash
ctest --test-dir <build> -R '^transfer_task_test$' --output-on-failure
```

Deployment gates remain open: the engine must outlive every operation; nonterminal transports can hold workers/pins indefinitely; source-lease safety, real RDMA/GPU quiescence, shutdown ordering and worker/pin capacity recovery need machine validation. Logical failure is not drain. This patch deliberately provides no bounded reclaim, generic cancellation platform, or unsafe timeout fallback. Free errors other than Busy and the full cross-rank cancellation protocol lack new native coverage.

**Test results:**

- [x] Specified Linux CPU native checks pass within the scope above
- [ ] Integration tests pass
- [ ] Hardware drain and deployment gates pass

## Checklist

- [x] Source self-review and independent review completed
- [x] Changed-line LLVM 20 formatting check passed
- [ ] All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed
- [x] Native regression tests added
- [x] Specified Linux CPU production build and native checks completed
- [ ] Human submitter reviewed every changed line

## AI Assistance Disclosure

- [x] AI tools were used

Codex assisted with pinned-source investigation, implementation, regression-test authoring and independent agent review. A human submitter remains responsible for reviewing and defending all changes before merge. The described Linux CPU tests ran; no GPU/RDMA tests ran, and bounded CPU evidence is not deployment acceptance.

author: jvust1
body:
## Practical change
Protect existing manuscripts and human scores from partial writes or accidental overwrite. ProjectStore now rejects escaping/aliased/symlink paths before file access, serializes cooperating local writers, and writes complete private files atomically. The fixed extraction JSON + summary JSONL pair uses a checked recovery intent; a fresh process can finish the original requested save after interruption, without duplicating summaries or erasing conflicts. Benchmark runs get exclusive directories even within the same second, and blank scoring generation never overwrites existing human scores.

## Actual source reuse
Reconcile Novel PR16's existing confinement/RMW rules and PR13 stable-summary ordering. Directly adapt boltons AtomicSaver/atomic_save at `4e5faa3d7e4008d89e0d8bf1ea87b6d9a061a16d` (6,932 stars observed). Preserve exact complete BSD-style three-clause LICENSE and upstream source/test snapshots, modification notice and SHA-256 pins. GitHub's license metadata is NOASSERTION; the actual text was reviewed and retained. No new runtime package, service or database. The port is used by both ProjectStore and benchmark evidence writers.

## Verification
- Source tree `013ca6c7741093bba7388eb44a7b22c9bcfcdbdc`
- Linux Python 3.11.16 and 3.12.14: **632 passed, 1 skipped each**
- 21 source-port tests; 35 independent recovery tests, including real os._exit at three publication checkpoints
- Cooperating spawned processes retain all summaries; corrupted/conflicting recovery inputs preserve targets; same-second benchmark and concurrent scoring no-clobber tests pass
- compileall and Novel-edited-file whitespace checks pass; byte-exact upstream snapshots intentionally preserve original CRLF/incidental whitespace
- Skip: optional qdrant-client absent
- Verified [CI run 36840688905](https://github.com/Jvust1/Novel/actions/runs/36840688905) for exact head `78cb607a8b4ae9cade68a62b7065a8f08e85ace0`: both Linux jobs succeeded; actual logs show **632 passed, 1 skipped** on Python 3.11 and 3.12
- Both suites also passed from the extracted source ZIP with the same counts

## Boundaries
Stacked on frozen draft #47; no main merge or deployment. This is trusted local-directory/cooperating-writer safety, not a hostile directory-swap sandbox, a Drive/general multi-file transaction, universal power-loss guarantee or native Windows acceptance. Fork-inherited lock lineage fails closed. The fixed two-file intent is bounded to 64 MiB before publication; post-publication errors require readback, not a rollback claim. Existing accepted-story evidence and original public r1 remain unchanged. Remaining provider/output-budget, vector consistency, final-report/hook, lint/dependency and human-quality gaps are explicitly retained in governance. No private manuscripts or private source reports are published.

author: squishiba
body:
Fixes run-3 finding **N1** (`in-prog-logs/user-sim-release-gate-run3.md` §3).

Run 2's BUG 2 fix covered the two *load-time* write sites. `build`, `revision`
and `release` write further down — the append-only seal file,
`.refdes/baselines/<name>.yaml`, and the rendered site under `site.out` — and
on a read-only checkout all three died with an unhandled `PermissionError`
traceback, **before any output**, exit 1. Nothing in that output distinguished
"your filesystem is read-only" from "your project is broken". This is the
failure a CI container with a frozen checkout hits.

Every command × read-only shape below was run against `main` and against this
branch. Fixture: 3 items (an active requirement covered by a passing test, one
append-only log entry), `standard: {base: hardware, version: 3}`, `chmod -R a-w`
applied to files **and** directories (a read-only directory still permits
writing through to the files inside it, so both bits matter).

## The three commands the report named

### `build` — whole tree read-only

**before** (`main`):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '.../.refdes/.log-seal-mvbchw2x.tmp'
[exit 1]
```

**after:**
```
ERROR   .refdes/log-seal.yaml — could not write this file (read-only tree?) -- the entries in it are NOT sealed, so they have no append-only protection until a build can write this file; run with --no-write to silence this
error: cannot write the site to /.../_site (Permission denied) -- nothing was rendered. Point -o/--out at a writable directory, or make this one writable.
WARNING .refdes/schema.json — could not write this file (read-only tree?); run with --no-write to silence this
3 items, 1 errors, 1 warnings
[exit 2]
```

Two writes refused, **two different shapes**, because they are different in
kind. The seal file degrades — `build` has a site to render afterwards and
nothing in the rendered pages reads the seal file, so the run goes on and says
what it could not do. The site output is `build`'s own product, the one thing
the command is for, so there is no partial `site written to …` worth printing:
refuse, name the path, exit 2.

### `build` — project read-only, `site.out` pointing at a writable directory elsewhere

This is the CI shape from the report, and the one worth reading carefully: the
site **must** still be produced.

**before** (`main`): `PermissionError` on `.refdes/.log-seal-*.tmp`, exit 1.
`.refdes/` has to be writable no matter where the site goes.

**after:**
```
ERROR   .refdes/log-seal.yaml — could not write this file (read-only tree?) -- the entries in it are NOT sealed, ...
build completed with errors (use --keep-going to exit 0)
WARNING .refdes/schema.json — could not write this file (read-only tree?); run with --no-write to silence this
3 items, 1 errors, 1 warnings
site written to /tmp/pr-site
[exit 1]
```

Site rendered, seal refused and named, exit 1. **before:** `.refdes/` read-only
only (everything else writable, site elsewhere) behaves identically — the seal
refusal is not about the rest of the tree.

### `revision` — whole tree read-only

**before** (`main`): `PermissionError` on `.refdes/baselines/rev-a.yaml`, exit 1.

**after:**
```
error: cannot write .refdes/baselines/rev-a.yaml (read-only tree?) -- revision 'rev-a' was not stamped. Make the tree writable and run it again, or run it with --no-write to see what it would stamp.
WARNING .refdes/schema.json — could not write this file (read-only tree?); run with --no-write to silence this
3 items, 0 errors, 1 warnings
[exit 2]
```

### `revision` / `release` — `.refdes/` read-only only, `items/` writable

**before** (`main`): same `PermissionError` on the baseline file, exit 1.
**after:** same refusal, exit 2 — identical output, so the half-read-only shape
is not a second code path.

### `--no-write` — whole tree read-only (**unchanged**)

```
revision 'rev-a' not stamped (--no-write): would stamp 3 items to .refdes/baselines/rev-a.yaml.
[exit 0]
```

Byte-identical to a writable tree's `--no-write` run: it never reaches the
write, so it does not care whether the tree would have taken it. Pinned by a
new test.

## Exit codes

Against `docs/cli-reference.md`'s table, which this PR also extends with a
sub-table for the case it did not cover:

| refused write | shape | code | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.refdes/` (seal file, membership manifest, `schema.json`) | error naming the file | **1** | reported through the ordinary `ERROR <file> — …` diagnostic channel, where the table says `1` is the only code a diagnostic gets |
| `site.out` directory | refusal naming the path | **2** | nothing is wrong with the project; same code as the `--no-write` refusal |
| `.refdes/baselines/<name>.yaml` | refusal naming the path | **2** | a stamp that did not happen must not read as one that did |

## Three sites the report did not name

Found by sweeping every command on a read-only tree rather than reading its
list, so this is reported rather than assumed.

### `.refdes/boards.yaml` — `build`, project with a `boards:` registry

Reached from the same `build(project, seal_write=…)` call as the seal file;
only a project that registers a board hits it, which is why the report's fixture
missed it.

**before** (`main`): `PermissionError` on `.refdes/boards.yaml`, exit 1.
**after:**
```
ERROR   .refdes/boards.yaml — could not write this file (read-only tree?) -- board and workspace membership was NOT recorded, so an accepted move will be reported again on the next build; run with --no-write to silence this
site written to /tmp/pr-site-j
[exit 1]
```

Error-level for the same reason as the seal: `build` is the command that records
membership, and an unrecorded move is a move the next build reports as new again.

### `.refdes/history/` — `history capture`, `history migrate-seals`

**before** (`main`): `PermissionError` on `.refdes/history`, exit 1.
**after:**
```
error: cannot write .refdes/history/objects/665202037cf256aba….yaml (read-only tree?) -- nothing was captured. Make the tree writable and run it again.
[exit 1]
```

These already refuse under `--no-write` (exit 2); a refused filesystem is the
same refusal arriving from the other direction, and it now rides the existing
`HistoryError` channel every caller already prints as `error: <exc>`.

### `audit` — baseline older than the current hash format

**before** (`main`): `PermissionError` on `.refdes/baselines/rel-a.yaml`,
exit 1. **after:**
```
(load could not write .refdes/baselines/rel-a.yaml -- read-only tree? run with --no-write to silence this)
3 items audited (3 local)
[exit 0]
```

A warning, not a refusal: the file already holds a correct baseline and only
its format lags, and the diff is computed in memory either way.
`former-ids propose` reaches the same site. `audit` and `former-ids propose`
print a bespoke report rather than project diagnostics, so
`cli._print_late_refusals` re-announces the refusal instead of letting it be
the one refusal in the tool nobody is told about.

## One sentence, not three

Run-3's N2 complains that the same condition is reported two ways. There is now
one function producing it — `refdes.model.read_only_refusal()` — and
`schema_json.write_schema` and `revise._refuse_unwritable` (the two existing
spellings, kept byte-for-byte identical) call it, so a third cannot appear.

## `revise`, `calc-rewrite` and `standard upgrade` — the carry-forward refusal

A seal hash or baseline entry these commands carry forward is the **only**
record that a rename was not an edit to a sealed entry or a stamped baseline.
So on a tree whose `items/` is writable and whose `.refdes/` is not, they
refuse, name the file, exit 1, and roll the whole operation back:

```
$ refdes revise mapping.yaml
refused:
  cannot write .refdes/log-seal.yaml (read-only tree?) -- the renamed entries' seals were not carried forward, and the next build would report every one of them as modified since it was sealed. Make the tree writable and run it again.

author: kpopmaker
body:
## Purpose

Prevent the two legacy Momentum stack validators from firing or false-failing on unrelated/new Momentum work.

PR #369 repaired their malformed shell/YAML content, but the pull_request routing still had two independent problems:

1. broad path filters matched future Momentum files outside the old #319/#327 stack;
2. the post319 scope guard compared live main directly to a stale PR head with a two-dot diff, so main-only changes could be misclassified as PR changes.

## Change

### Trigger ownership

Narrow both validators' pull_request path filters to the exact files they own and already allow.

### Stale-branch scope calculation

For pull requests, the post319 validator now mirrors the productionization validator and derives:

`MERGE_BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> <PR_HEAD_SHA>)`

then evaluates only:

`git diff --name-only "$MERGE_BASE...$PR_HEAD_SHA"`

This prevents unrelated commits that landed on main after the PR branched from becoming false disallowed files.

No test command, methodology, runtime, Product, scheduler, database, or activation behavior changes.

## Reproduced failure motivating the merge-base fix

Momentum PR #378 provided a current concrete example after main advanced:

- #378 head: `0caa3e92c4d2666db97d515f99c664399ac671cd`
- live main had advanced to `c42eb3fcf5404e99e790028e41f9aeced3ffbf53`
- post319 validation run `36885452330`
- failure occurred at **Scope allowlist** before any regression/test execution
- the old two-dot live-main ↔ stale-head comparison included main-only changes

The dedicated #378 recovery validator and independent current-main merge simulation both passed, confirming this was CI routing/scope behavior rather than a Momentum methodology failure.

## Current head

- `a8d610581cd24942c290151b49690e021e85643c`

author: mgrossmann
body:
Closes #575.

## Problem
The `jump` and `indirect_jump` patterns chose between `B label` and `L 14,=A(label)` / `BR 14` first, and only then called `mvs_check_page`, which may start a new page. A backward `B` at the very end of a page was therefore judged against the old page and emitted behind the new page's `DROP 12` / `USING *,12`, with its target on the old page. as370 (and IFOX00) answer that with IFO209. The 22 conditional branch patterns and BCT call `mvs_check_page` first and were never affected.

## Fix
`mvs_page_would_break (code, lit)` in `i370.c` tests the same condition `mvs_check_page` uses to start a page. `jump` and `indirect_jump` take the short form only when the `B` still fits on the current page. Otherwise the long form starts the new page, and its literal lands in that page's pool.

## Not -Os specific
The issue saw it at `-Os` in rexx370 `irx#pars.c`, but it depends only on page geometry. The new `page-jump` test in `cc370/tests/run.sh` hits it at `-O1`. It sweeps 246 variants of a small loop whose back-edge is a plain `B`, pushed across the first page end:
- before the fix, 6 variants put a `B` on page 2 with its label on page 1; as370 gives rc 8 on one of them
- after it, none do
- the same 6 take the long form as the first instruction of the new page. The test counts these "window" variants on both binaries alike, so it fails if later codegen moves the geometry out of the sweep.

## Verification
- `irx#pars.c -Os`: IFO209 before, clean after; all 33 rexx370 sources compile and assemble at `-Os`.
- `.s` output of 1,015 ecosystem sources (libc370, rexx370, ufsd, httpd, ftpd, mvsmf, lua370, lstring370, crypto370, httplua, httprexx, brexx370) at `-O1`: byte-identical before and after. 128 sources did not compile with the flags I used, on either side, and are not compared.
- At `-Os` only `irx#pars.c` changes: the jump itself, and one instruction moves to the next page because the long form takes more room on the page.
- `cc370/tests/run.sh`: 21/21.

Not changed here: the long form's `mvs_check_page (0, 2, 4)` counts 2 bytes of code for the 6 bytes of `L` + `BR`. Correcting it would move page breaks at `-O1` everywhere and needs its own MVS validation.

First step towards a usable `-Os`. The other two blockers measured on the host (unit-at-a-time dropping static tables and reordering top-level `asm`; strict aliasing) follow in their own issues.

author: surma
body:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs on a new nixenv runner in the github-runner container on Nexus:
- Pull requests from branches in this repo run `nix flake check`. Pull requests from forks never run.
- Pushes to main build nexus, archon, dark-archon, and the scout and generic-linux home configs, and pin each result as a direct GC root in /nix/var/nix/gcroots/nixenv-ci. The container shares the host store, and the host GC scans the container's gcroots directory.

Runner changes:
- A system-wide SSH config and pinned host keys for GitHub and Gitea, because the runner sets HOME to its work dir and mounts / read-only.
- The scout-repo-ssh-key secret also writes the key for the runner. Only the nixenv runner can read it (InaccessiblePaths for the others).
- The nixenv runner may write the gcroots directory (ReadWritePaths).
- MemoryMax 8G -> 16G: evaluating nexus needs about 11 GB.

Cache (machines/nexus/service-nix-cache.nix):
- Harmonia serves the Nexus store on 127.0.0.1:5000 and signs with the new nexus-cache-signing-key secret (nexus-cache-1).
- An internal-only surmhosting app exposes it as cache.nexus.* on the internal entrypoint (port 8081, LAN and tailnet). There is no public route.
- archon and dark-archon use it through profiles/nixos/nexus-cache.nix, over the Tailscale address. Priority 50 keeps cache.nixos.org first.

Verified: `nix flake check` passes (150 s, 5.2 GB peak). The nexus, archon, and dark-archon configs evaluate, and the generated runner units, SSH config, Traefik router, and Harmonia socket match the intent.

author: taew0o
body:
스펙을 최신화하니(`feature/pill-recognition/README.md`) 정본과 갈려 있던 셋이 드러났다.

## 접힘으로 시작한다

정본 ② 가 「처음엔 **접힌 상태**(읽기 전용)」다. 수정하러 들어왔다고 곧바로 고칠 칸을 펼치면 사진에서 읽은 값을 **확인할 겨를 없이** 손대게 된다. 먼저 읽고, 고칠 데를 고르는 순서다.

둘만 예외로 펼친다 — **수동 추가와 추출 실패**. 보여 줄 모델값이 없어 접어 봐야 「전체」만 늘어서고, 그 화면에서 할 일은 읽기가 아니라 채우기다.

## 구분선은 그림 칸 메뉴다

정본이 「메뉴는 **제형처럼 알약 그림 칸**」으로 적는다. 「(+)형」·「(−)형」은 말보다 그림이 빠르다 — 사용자는 손에 든 알약을 보고 고르지 이름으로 떠올리지 않는다.

마크가 글자 목록인 것과 갈리는 이유는 **종류가 296가지라 그림으로 고를 수 없어서**다. 둘은 성격이 다르다.

「없음」도 칸이다 — 선 없는 원판. 「조건 없음」과 다른 말이라 그림으로도 갈라 준다. 구분선은 모델이 내는 값이 아니라 「사진 기준」 미리보기는 비운다.

## 색은 조각 원 하나다 (MC-2)

점을 늘어놓으면 색이 늘수록 칩이 넓어져 **색·모양·제형 세 칩이 한 줄을 넘긴다.** 캡슐은 두 색이 예사고 세 색도 있다. 원 하나를 12시에서 시계 방향으로 나누면 **몇 색이든 칩 폭이 고정**된다.

- 색 순서는 그대로 둔다 — 몸통·뚜껑 순서가 뜻을 갖는 값이라 섞으면 다른 약이 된다
- 테두리 원은 조각마다가 아니라 **맨 위에 한 번** 덮는다. 조각마다 두르면 가운데에 선이 모여 바큇살처럼 보인다
- 「사진 기준」 미리보기도 같은 조각 원이다 — 되돌리면 저 모양으로 돌아간다는 뜻이라 두 자리가 다르게 생기면 안 된다

## 확인 — S24

- 수정 화면이 **접힘으로 열린다** — 슬라이더 버튼 · 꺾쇠 없는 칩 · 테두리 없는 읽기 칸
- 펼치면 구분선 메뉴가 **그림 셋**(없음 원판 · (+) · (−))으로 뜬다
- 색 칩이 조각 원 하나로 고정 폭

`spotlessCheck detekt lint test` 통과.

## 남은 것

NM-516 DoD 는 이걸로 다 찼다. 남은 건 다른 티켓이다 — 후보 영역의 **조회 중·조회 실패 모양**은 NM-529 가 DESIGN.pen 에 케이스를 추가했는데(`dce6c53`), 문구·동작은 README 정본대로 이미 구현했고 그림 대조만 아직이다.

author: damianvtran
body:
## Summary of Changes

The operator requirement this carries, **verbatim**:

> **"updates must not stop runtimes mid-session."**

Two mechanisms, plainly labelled: the **progress-gated signal drain is the guarantee**; the **fleet gate on the build-refresh rung is the net** (advisory by construction — see below).

## Wave C, briefly — the causal chain this fixes

On 2026-10-01 an install-adjacent **SIGTERM** reached the fleet (~21:04:3x). `_drain_for_signal` bounded its wait by **wall clock** (`deadline = monotonic() + SIGNAL_DRAIN_S`; expiry → `stop.set()` → dispose). An **unattached** session holding a long turn never reaches a boundary inside 120 s, so at ~21:06:3x the **bound — not a boundary — disposed the turn**: nine sessions, journaled `disposed` (the evidence-less default). **The ~120 s gap between the signal and the `disposed` rows IS the bound** — that is the proof of the mechanism.

## The fix

- `_SignalDrainBound` (`local_operator/session/runtime/process.py`): progress = movement the work reports (`_work_motion`) **or** a step executing (`_step_in_flight`); either restarts the clock. **Only no-movement AND no-step for `SIGNAL_DRAIN_S` disposes** (the old exit, byte for byte). A turn that keeps progressing is **never cut** by the bound and leaves at its own boundary — the invariant: *a runtime ends only at a turn boundary; mid-turn signals defer to it*.
- A reduced host (no readable session) keeps the **total-duration deadline** — "bounded" must not depend on a seam (the `_await_live_window` fallback rule).
- A signal drain no longer draws `_drain_for`'s abandonment arms (`_abandon_move` releases the latch and would silently revoke the signal).
- A quiet turn held open by a step is **spared and says so**: one WARNING per bound of silence in the runtime's own log.
- Killability, stated: a runtime that never settles is stopped by **SIGKILL** (the unrefusable stop). Deliberately **no second wall-clock ceiling** — it cannot tell "still working" from "never settles" (honest turns measured at 2h42m) and would cut exactly the turns this exists to save.
- **The net**: `_refresh_for` defers while another LIVE runtime's record shows an open update window (`_another_move_in_flight`; registry read in reader mode, fork-free, fail-open, cannot wedge). `BUILD_*` values unchanged; no install/prune/reload semantics touched.

## Testing Details

- Targeted unit runs (isolated `env -i` roots, `-n0`, worktree venv): the touched runtime/tui/info files — **358 passed** in the final post-fold batch; earlier batches 289/262/170 passed.
- **Falsification** ("prove the test can fail"): the five new unit cells were run against the **unpatched** `process.py` (stashed) → **5 failed, only they**; restored → green.
- New cells: `test_a_signalled_turn_that_keeps_making_progress_rides_through`, `test_a_turn_with_no_progress_and_no_step_is_reaped_at_the_bound`, `test_a_quiet_turn_held_open_by_a_step_is_spared_and_says_so`, `test_the_fleet_gate_reads_only_live_other_movers`, `test_a_fleet_mate_mid_update_defers_this_move`.
- **Design §TESTS (c)** (the prune arm): `test_a_generation_a_live_runtime_reports_is_kept` (`tests/unit/test_install_generations.py`) — the live-argv joint, closed: the string a RUNNING process reports for itself (its resolved `sys.prefix`, exactly what a runtime stamps on its record at boot) is produced by executing the generation's own interpreter, published on a record, and asserted to survive a prune of every other generation while an unreferenced sibling is still removed.
- **Wave-C regression (the exact shape)**: e2e `test_a_turn_that_outlives_the_bound_rides_through` — a real 60 s turn under a 3 s injected bound, one SIGTERM, **viewer detached** (unattached): the turn must complete and the runtime leave cleanly, with the reaping line absent. This is the old "outliving the bound is cut" cell, flipped. **Local e2e run deferred under the fleet hold** (it boots real runtimes); it collects cleanly and CI/QA carry it.
- Lint: flake8 7.3.0, black 26.1.0, isort 5.13.2 over the changed files — clean.

## Deferred under the fleet hold (stated plainly, not implied)

The **full-tree unit suite** and **whole-tree pyright** were not run locally — the host was under an operator-level ENOSPC hold during this work (light edits + targeted single-file runs only). CI's `test` and `type-check` jobs are the authoritative gates and are expected to carry both.

## Not addressed (noted, out of this PR's file scope)

- The stop-ladder receipt fallback for pre-field peers still reads "up to 2 min" — **correct for that population** (old builds still run the old deadline), deliberately left alone.
- Doc comments narrating the old total bound elsewhere (e.g. `session/runtime/reclaim.py`) were not swept.

Related: none (operator-driven; the design note lives in the update-flow lane's scratchpad).

`Release: patch — bugfix for the update-flow lane; no new feature, no API change.`

## Rig plan — design §TESTS (d), deferred under the hold

**N runtimes mid-turn + a simulated install → zero mid-turn cuts.** Not executed while the ENOSPC hold stands; this is the plan, for QA round 1. Shape: one rig, `-n0`, no browser. Four sessions boot on the old build and each parks a real 60 s turn in the real tool (`[bash:60]`, the existing broadcast cell's shape, which already covers N=3 + one SIGTERM sweep); mid-turn the build marker is flipped to a new build (what `lop-update` does last, as `test_runtime_refresh_e2e` scripts it), then one broadcast SIGTERM lands. Assert, per runtime: the turn completes (`TURN_COMPLETED` present in every transcript), `_cut_off_causes` is empty for every directory, each child exits 0 at its own boundary, and no `drain bound` line appears in any runtime log. Discriminator: the pre-fix code cuts every parked turn at the bound (its own cell asserted exactly that), so "zero cuts" fails on the old code by construction. Budget ~N x 75 s plus teardown; the sibling `test_a_broadcast_sigterm_mid_turn_lets_every_turn_finish` covers the signal half and `test_runtime_refresh_e2e` the refresh half, so the new rig is only the JOINT.
