author: ujh
body:
New Relic and pg stats from the last ~26h showed the database (1 vCPU / 2 GB on DO) is the bottleneck. Fly edge latency is p95 2.3s and p99 4.9s, with no CPU throttling or memory pressure on the Fly side. This PR fixes the largest consumers of DB time that are not already handled elsewhere.

- **`/descriptions/missing`**: crawlers hit it about 12.5k times a day, and every request sent all ~13k cached ids to Postgres as an `IN (...)` list. That was the single largest source of DB time (~5,900s/day). The sorted ids are now cached and only the ten records on the page are loaded. The fragment cache keys no longer mix the two pagination params. `robots.txt` asks crawlers to skip the missing descriptions/reviews pages.
- **Admin dashboard**: one tab left open polled about 2,100 requests an hour overnight. That drove the full scans of `agent_logs` (~94k seq scans/day), the pens micro cluster counts (~2,100s/day) and the graph aggregates (~1,300s/day).
  - A new `usePolling` hook pauses polling while the tab is hidden and refreshes as soon as it becomes visible again.
  - Stats are cached for 1 minute and graphs for 10 minutes.
  - This also fixes the `Stat`/`ConditionalStat` effects, which had no dependency array and passed `fetchData()` instead of `fetchData` to `setInterval`. Plain stats now poll too.
- **`MacroCluster.without_review`** is now a `NOT EXISTS` relation instead of `find_by_sql`. Callers that `count` or `pluck` no longer instantiate every unreviewed cluster (dev: count 496ms → 41ms cold).
- **`CheckBrandClusters`**: the hourly run now enqueues only the clusters whose effective brand name differs from their brand cluster's name (dev: ~1.2k instead of all 16k).

Investigated but not changed here:
- The `/api/v1/inks` autocomplete (12s avg) was already fixed by #3777.
- `MacroCluster.embedding_search` takes ~16s per query on prod because the macro and micro cluster searches exact-scan the TOASTed vectors. It needs a query and index redesign, which is better done together with the planned embedding_v2 re-embed.

author: stangirard
body: Closes THE-852 (https://linear.app/thevibecompany/issue/THE-852/link-the-github-app-to-the-organization-in-one-click). Follows #53 (THE-851). Parent: THE-848. ## What changes On Organization › GitHub, owners and admins get an **Install on GitHub** button. When GitHub sends them back, the installation is already linked to their Armada organization, with no separate Link step. 1. **Install on GitHub** → `GET /organization/github/install`. At the click, it signs a state of {organization, person, nonce, expiry in 30 minutes} with HMAC-SHA256, under a key derived from `ARMADA_AUTH_SECRET`. It keeps the nonce in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie scoped to `/organization/github`, then answers 303 to `https://github.com/apps//installations/new?state=…`. 2. GitHub sends the person back to the **Setup URL**, `/organization/github` (as already documented in #53). The page hands `installation_id`, `setup_action` and `state` to `GET /organization/github/setup`, so the page itself writes nothing. 3. **`/organization/github/setup`** runs `linkFromSetup`, clears the nonce cookie (the state works once), and answers 303 to the GitHub page with `?done=linked` or `?error=…`. The address ends up clean. 4. **`linkFromSetup`** refuses, with `error=state`, a state that is forged, altered, expired, already used or from another browser (no matching nonce), or made for another person or another organization than the one the viewer is in now. Then **`linkForViewer`**, the rule the Link button now shares, refuses a viewer who is no longer owner or admin, refuses an installation that GitHub's `GET /user/installations` does not list for the person (asked with their own GitHub sign-in), links it, and records `link` in the audit list, in one transaction. 5. **Keeping the link:** re-installing or changing repositories keeps it. `linkInstallation` is now one upsert that says whether the row is new (`linked`/`already`), so coming back again writes no second audit line, and a concurrent unlink cannot slip between two statements. A return without a state (repositories changed from GitHub's side, with Redirect on update) writes nothing and shows the page. 6. **`setup_action=request`** (someone who cannot install on that GitHub organization) shows a notice that the account's owner must approve the request first. 7. **The manual Link list stays** for installations made outside Armada. Members who are not owner or admin still see the plain "Install the app on a GitHub account" link. New module: `lib/github-install.ts`. `lib/github-app.ts` stays the GitHub adapter and link store. Strings are in English and French. README, runbook and `AGENTS.md` are updated. No webhook route (THE-853 owns it), and no schema change. ## Owner steps: GitHub App settings (armada.thevibecompany.co) On GitHub: the app's page › **Settings** (Developer settings › GitHub Apps › Armada › Edit) › **General**: 1. **Setup URL (optional)**: `https://armada.thevibecompany.co/organization/github` 2. Check **Redirect on update** (just under the Setup URL). 3. Leave **Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation** unchecked: when it is checked, GitHub ignores the Setup URL. 4. **Save changes**. Nothing changes on Vercel: no new variable, no redeploy needed for this setting. Then try it: sign in to Armada with GitHub as an owner or admin of an organization, open Organization › GitHub, click **Install on GitHub**, pick the account and repositories, and click Install. GitHub sends you back to Organization › GitHub with "Linked." and the installation under **Linked installations**. Organization › Keys shows a `link` line in the audit list. ## Decisions - **The state is signed at the click (install route), not at page render**, so a page left open does not expire the button. It is valid 30 minutes, which leaves time to pick repositories or approve 2FA on GitHub. - **Single-use via a cookie nonce**, cleared on return: a state copied from a URL or a Referer header cannot link anything again, and does not work from another browser. No table or migration is needed. - **The state's HMAC key is derived from `ARMADA_AUTH_SECRET`** with a domain label, so it never doubles as a session signature and needs no new variable. - **The Setup URL stays `/organization/github`** (the value #53 documented), and the page forwards to the setup route. The database write happens in a route handler, never while a Server Component renders. - **Known limit:** an installation deleted and re-created directly on GitHub gets a new id, and needs the manual Link (or the Install button). Detecting that would need the app's webhook (THE-853). ## Tests `test/github-install.test.ts` (PGlite, fake GitHub): - a genuine state links with no other click and writes one audit line; - coming back again keeps the link with no duplicate audit line; - a state that is forged (other secret), altered, truncated, garbage, expired, replayed without the cookie, from another browser's nonce, for another person or for another organization is refused; - a demoted member gets `forbidden`; - an installation GitHub does not list for the person is refused, by the button and by the Link button; - no GitHub sign-in gives `no-github`; GitHub refusing gives `failed`. `test/github-app.test.ts` covers the upsert's `already`. `bun run verify` and `bun run build` are green. Run by hand on a local dashboard (PGlite, email sign-in, a synthetic app key): - `/organization/github/install` answers 303 and logs why when GitHub refuses the app; - the Setup URL forwards to `/setup`; - a forged state gives `?error=state` and clears the cookie; - a genuine state with its cookie passes the state check (and stops at `no-github` for an email-only user); - another browser's nonce gives `?error=state`; - `setup_action=request` gives the notice; - `setup_action=update` without a state gives a clean page. The real install round-trip needs the production app's settings above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- [Open workspace in Conductor](https://app.conductor.build/workspace/f154fef6-427f-4365-b8a9-d9e5c4df975b) --- ## Summary by cubic Closes THE-852. Owners and admins can now link the GitHub App to their organization in one click: an **Install on GitHub** button opens GitHub's install page with a signed, single-use state, and when GitHub sends them back, the installation is already linked. - The state is signed at the click and valid 30 minutes; a nonce cookie makes it single-use per browser. - `linkFromSetup` validates the state, then links under the same rule as the manual Link button: the person must be an owner or admin, signed in with GitHub, and GitHub must list the installation for them. - Re-installing or changing repositories keeps the link; returning writes no duplicate audit line. - `setup_action=request` shows a notice that a GitHub account owner must approve the request first. - The manual Link list remains for installations made outside Armada; members who are not owners or admins still see the plain install link. - New module `lib/github-install.ts`; no schema change and no webhook route. Written for commit e1c8f7fc8ede2f32232e4c3e6fd3a411ac6ec35e. Summary will update on new commits.

author: entelecheia
body:
Closes #81.

- **The two silent refusals now log, as the policy refusals do:**
  - 431 "request header too large" logs `network: refused a request (...)`. Nothing of the header is logged.
  - An unreachable listed host logs `network: refused host:port (host:port is unreachable, ECONNREFUSED)`. Only the socket error code goes in, never the error text.
- **431 refuses once:** the data listener comes off before refusing. The server is `allowHalfOpen`, so in Node later chunks of the same request could refuse and log again. Under Bun 1.3.14 the server socket emits no data after `end()`, so a test cannot exercise this guard (a mutation without it still passes); it is one expression.
- **Upstream error after the tunnel opened:** this was a related bug. `refuse()` wrote an HTTP 403 into the client's TLS stream; now the client is just closed. Bun's `resetAndDestroy` produces no client-side error, so this path has no test.
- **Docs:** `docs/operations.md` says every refusal is logged (by host, with the method for plain HTTP and the code for unreachable), never a path, query or header. CHANGELOG has the entry.
- **Test:** one new test sends an oversized header in spaced chunks from a half-open client, then CONNECTs to an allowlisted closed port. It asserts exactly the two lines and no header content. It fails against the old `proxy.ts`.

Check: `scripts/check.sh` ends with `check: OK` (542 tests, 0 fail).

author: loyality7
body:
## Problem
The page traffic sync records page views and landing page performance, but not where visitors came from, and not whether visitors to a collection page go on to open a product.

## Change
- `Triple Whale Traffic Metric`: daily sessions and new visitors for sessions that began on a product or collection page, by traffic source. Sources are grouped in the query into Direct, Email & SMS, Paid ads, Organic & social, Affiliates and Other. The raw channel values are many and uneven (a misspelled facebook value, several email tools), so grouping in the query keeps the table small.
- `clicked_through` on `Triple Whale Page Metric`: for each collection page and day, the sessions that opened a product page afterwards, using the page-view order within the session. Sessions are counted distinct, because the journey table repeats each view.
- A table with no rows is filled from the full 90-day backfill, so the new data covers the whole history on its first run.
- Counts only. No visitor identifier is selected or stored.
- Tests cover the row shaping and check that every query-string pattern carries the escaped backslash. The warehouse drops a single backslash, which leaves an invalid pattern.

## Notes
- Needs a migrate for the new table and column.
- The two new queries have not been run against the warehouse yet. They are checked on a short window before the first full run.

author: nicolaspopravka
body:
## Why

A rebuilt three-delegate stack needs a check that `hdCycles.so` existing with zero
unresolved `ldd` entries does not supply. Both of those pass while the delegate is
still unusable: a wrong `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME`, or CY2023's distro-epoxy soname
sitting where the Cycles bundle would have been.

`run-demo` cannot cover it. `demo/run1`'s `render_script.sh` asks for `GL`, so it
exercises HdStorm and nothing else — the delegate a rebuild adds is never touched.

## What it does

Renders a self-contained 256x256 Teapot once per delegate token with stock
`usdrecord` under Xvfb/Mesa, and reports exit status plus image bytes per token,
failing the job if any requested delegate writes no frame. `renderers=enumerate`
(default) just lists what the image registers and which tokens resolve.

The scene is written in its own host step, so there is no heredoc inside the
container script — see the trap noted below.

## Why the push trigger is here and should be removed on merge

`workflow_dispatch` resolves against the default branch, so this cannot be
dispatched from its own branch before it lands. The branch-scoped `push` trigger
is the workaround the GH13 probe already uses. Once merged, delete that block and
the workflow is dispatch-only like its siblings.

## First result

Run `36832547979`, success on both rebuilt years:

```
--renderer {Cycles,GL,Moonray (debug),Moonray}
GL       exit=0   6223 bytes   OK
Cycles   exit=0  13708/13663   OK   (CY2023 / CY2024)
```

`Storm` is absent from that list by design — on these composites `GL` is the token
that resolves to HdStorm.

## Two traps worth knowing if you edit this

1. **A heredoc inside the container command never terminates.** The command is a
   single-quoted YAML block scalar, so the heredoc body stays indented and the
   terminator never matches column 0. The rest of the script is silently swallowed
   as file content and `set -u` kills the run with an unbound variable. **`bash -n`
   passes on it.** That is why the scene is written host-side.
2. **A workflow job env var does not cross `docker run`.** Same class as the unbound
   `$REPO` that broke the benchmark supervisor. `-e TOKENS` is required.

## MoonRay is not render-probed, on purpose

It needs a CUDA/OptiX device and the Arras client/worker split, and a GitHub runner
has neither, so a failure here would say nothing about the image. It is still
covered by the token-resolution loop. A gate that always goes red gets ignored.

Free: this runs on the GitHub runner. Cycles is CPU here, the same device the
benchmark uses, so this exercises the delegate rather than only loading the plugin.

author: vladastos
body:
Closes metel-lang/metel-core#1291 (implementation half; see below for what's left).

## Summary
- Retires postfix `T[]` in type position in favor of prefix `[T]`. `[T; N]` is unchanged.
- Grammar: merges `sized_array_type`/`array_type`/`array_atom` into one `bracket_array_type = "[" type_expr (";" INT)? "]"`, unifying onto `sized_array_type`'s always-fully-general inner slot (one parser match arm replaces two).
- Genuine semantic widening, flagged by the RFC (§2): `[&T]` and `[|i64| -> T]` dynamic arrays now parse — `array_atom`'s old base-type restriction never had a principled reason to apply only to the dynamic case.
- Corpus-wide flag-day sweep, AST-driven (never a blind regex): a one-shot migration tool modeled on RFC-0154/RFC-0136's own `pipe_migrate.rs`/`walrus_migrate.rs`, parsing under the old grammar and emitting two non-overlapping point-edits per site so nested cases compose correctly. Covered 107 fixture files (412 sites) + 4 stdlib files. 5 inline Metel source strings in Rust unit tests were outside its file-type scope and fixed by hand.
- No dedicated parse-error diagnostic for postfix `T[]` — left as a generic `P0001`, matching this repo's own precedent for the directly analogous RFC-0136 migration, and RFC-0171's own Open Question 2 framing it as non-blocking.

## Validation
- Full workspace test suite: 1045 fixture-driven integration tests + 239 + 96 + 26 + 3 unit tests, all passing.
- `cargo fmt --check --all` clean.
- `cargo clippy --release --workspace --lib -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` clean.
- Manual smoke test covering nested (`[[i64]]`), sized-of-dynamic (`[[i64]; 2]`), and the new reference/fn-type widening (`[&i64]`, `[|i64| -> i64]`).

## Deliberately out of scope here
- **metel-docs follow-up PR** (needs this commit's SHA to pin fixture citations): remove `LIMIT-PARSING-001`'s exemptions from `spec.types.arrays.legality-1` and `spec.types.fixed-size-arrays.legality-1`/`-2`, re-point their fixture citations at real `[T]`-spelled fixtures, and `rfc.py transition rfc-0171 --to implemented`.
- **Doc/RFC code-fence sweep** (~395 sites in `docs/rfcs`/`docs/reference`) — same migration tool, same follow-up PR.
- **Prose mentions of "`T[]`"** as the type's name (RFC text, Rust doc-comments describing the concept) — the sweep covers compiled Metel source only, per `PROCESS.md`'s "a syntax-changing RFC integrates its rule text, not its examples" and this repo's "no blind regex" convention.
- The one-shot migration tool is **not** kept in the tree, unlike its two precedents: its target grammar rule (`array_type`) is retired by the very migration it performs, so it cannot be re-run or even compile against the post-migration grammar. Its logic is preserved in this branch's history.

Zero-config model selection now picks the **best-available (most capable)** model for the present provider credential instead of a fixed, often-weak representative. A user with only `OPENAI_API_KEY` now defaults to `gpt-4o` rather than `gpt-4o-mini`.

The one-line selection notice already exists in the resolver and is unchanged. Existing precedence (explicit → recent → env → provider-inferred) is preserved; only the *fixed representative* step becomes a *ranked best-available* choice.

author: kshitijvikramsingh
body:
Decision 5, plus what the work turned up. Stacked on #50.

**The skinned demos adopt `Model`.** Runner, VulkanLit and Bulwark's crowd upload through `device.CreateModel`. Each skinned part draws with its own textures. Palettes are packed by `Model.PackPalettes`, with the placement baked in, and bone buffers come from `CreateBoneBuffers`. Bulwark's crowd shaders include `skinning.glsl` and take the bone count from their push constants, so its fixed `BONE_COUNT 15` is gone.

**One mesh transform.** `MeshDataExtensions.Transformed` is now the only implementation, and `Merge` and `ModelData.Flattened` both use it. Under a mirroring transform it reverses the winding and negates tangent `w`. It also moves tangents, which it previously didn't. Both private `BakeMerge` copies are deleted; they silently dropped any part with 32-bit indices.

**Engine bugs found on the way**
- Overlapping push-constant ranges, where one block is declared by two stages at different lengths. The draw path summed the ranges, which crashed Bulwark at the first wave. Now the payload is the furthest extent, pushed in stage-correct segments.
- `PropModel.Dispose` never freed the meshes it uploaded.
- There was no way to free an indirect buffer; `IGraphicsDevice.DestroyIndirectBuffer` is added.

**Every demo tears down what it made.** `BLIX_TEARDOWN_TRACE=1` now reports whatever a loop leaves for the device to free.

**Verified**
- Test.Recipes 292/292. Skinning through `Model` puts every vertex where the old hand path did (205k vertex-poses, worst 1e-6).
- `blix test --build`: 8 suites green.
- Demos gate: 16 green, with validation on; all 14 teardown reports are clean.
- `check-resize`: clean.
- Lab baseline: 116 artifacts, identical.
- Headed by the user: Runner, VulkanLit, Bulwark (a full wave) and TankArena.

author: wetsocksnsleeves
body:
### Problem

The watcher only runs while a terminal keeps `fibre watch run` open. It does not start at login or restart after a crash.

### Cause

There is no launchd integration.

### Solution

`internal/launchd` renders the watcher's launch agent plist and calls launchctl through an interface.
- The agent starts at login and restarts after an error exit.
- Its output goes to `~/Library/Logs/fibre/watch.log`.

The new subcommands use launchctl as follows.
- `fibre watch install` writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.github.wetsocksnsleeves.fibre.plist` and bootstraps it. An agent that is already loaded is reloaded.
- `uninstall` boots the agent out and removes the plist.
- `start` bootstraps a stopped agent or kickstarts a loaded one.
- `stop` boots it out until the next login or `start`.
- `status` reports whether the agent is installed, loaded and running, with its pid.

The plist runs `os.Executable()` without resolving symlinks, so a Homebrew symlink keeps working across upgrades. It records `XDG_STATE_HOME` when it is set, so the agent uses the same state as the shell that installed it.

`launchctl print` output has nested `state = ...` lines, so the parser reads only the service's own top-level `state` and `pid`. A regression test uses real output. Tests use a fake launchctl, and both golden plists pass `plutil -lint`. A manual check on real launchd is still to do.

Stacked on #9.

### Testing

`go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass on this branch.

author: adivishall
body:
Stacked on #25 (base `feat/secure-deploy`); retarget as the stack merges.

## Why

The audit chain proves only its own consistency. A storage attacker who can recompute SHA-256 can rewrite a suffix of it, and `verify` still passes. The HMAC checkpoint fixed a prefix, but:
- its key verifies and forges alike;
- it had no sequence, so an older genuine checkpoint could be substituted;
- it lived wherever the key did, usually on the store's own host.

## What

- **Signed checkpoints:** `sentinel.audit-checkpoint/1` covers the head recomputed from genesis, the length, the chain id, a checkpoint sequence and the previous checkpoint's digest. It is signed with Ed25519 by a key whose only trust-store purpose is `audit-checkpoint`; facts and policy-release keys are refused. The verifier holds only the public key.
- **Anchors:** an exclusive-create directory (one file per checkpoint, never overwritten) and an append-only JSONL file. `Anchor` is the interface a WORM store or a transparency log implements; neither is integrated.
- **Publication record:** each publication is recorded in the chain (`CHECKPOINT_PUBLISHED`), and the latest one must be present.
- **Status on every check:** `anchored`, `not_anchored` or `anchor_mismatch` is reported for the chain (`audit verify --anchor`, also with `--file`; `/v1/audit/verify`) and for each decision in replay. A mismatch makes `record_verified` false.
- **INV-AUDIT-2, tested both ways:** a consistent rewrite before an anchored checkpoint is a mismatch; one after it is reported as `not_anchored`, never as anchored. Anchoring protects from the moment of anchoring, and the reports say so.
- **CLI and configuration:** `sentinel audit checkpoint --sign-key --signer --anchor`, `audit verify --anchor [--require-anchored]`, `trust keygen --purpose audit-checkpoint`, `SENTINEL_AUDIT_ANCHOR`. The checkpoint job may run in its own process: the server adopts appended records that link to its head.

## Adversarial review

An independent review attacked the checkpoint and anchor design. Everything below was detected:
- rewrites before a checkpoint, from genesis, and with relinked hashes;
- swapped, inserted, symlinked or edited anchor entries;
- wrong-purpose and unknown keys.

It found 12 issues, all fixed in da472ff with regression tests (`tests/test_audit_anchoring.py::test_r*`):

- **High:** one corrupted record at checkpoint time disabled anchoring permanently. A statement with a null head was signed and published before the job crashed, and every later rewrite then looked like the honest state.
- **High:** the documented scheduled checkpoint job broke the running server. Its record, appended from another process, made every later decision a 500.
- `--require-anchored` was inverted.
- A revoked checkpoint key was a permanent mismatch with no recovery.
- `/v1/system` re-verified the whole chain twice per call (2.4 s at 100k events).
- Smaller issues:
  - JSON output omitted the anchoring result;
  - `--anchor` was ignored with `--file`;
  - a non-UTF-8 byte in the anchor gave a 400;
  - anchor errors leaked paths;
  - a relabelled sequence could claim coverage;
  - future-dated checkpoints were accepted.

Documented, not changed: deleting the newest checkpoint is invisible to a party who can delete from the anchor *and* rewrite the chain's unanchored tail. Only WORM storage or an external log closes that.

Tests: 893 → 919.

Closes #17

author: nndroid
body:
Long DATA query names previously reduced downstream capacity for the rest of a session. Size downstream chunks for each query and defer stored retransmissions when a query cannot carry them, allowing later short polls to deliver the preserved ciphertext.

Use the full safe upstream QNAME budget, accounting for custom markers, worst-case sequence fields, and Noise tags. Build and randomize QNAMEs in pooled byte buffers before the final string conversion. Remove obsolete longest-QNAME tracking and its extra session lock. Test port selection checks TCP and UDP together because Server.Run binds both.

Validation for head 7d2d2f845babc3be888ae70c349f95062092393a:
- Windows local full tests and vet; Linux local full race tests and vet pass.
- GitHub Actions push and PR test matrices pass on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including 64-bit race detection, Linux/Windows 386 checks, and benchmark smoke tests: https://github.com/NNdroid/dns_custom/actions/runs/36999019443
- DNS wire-boundary tests cover 190 domain lengths, custom markers, maximum sequence values, and Noise tags. Encrypted retransmission tests verify identical ciphertext and preserved queue state.
- GitHub Actions baseline-versus-head measurements against main b22d8fe: Linux Xeon 8370C, Go 1.26.1, GOMAXPROCS=2, seven 2-second samples per transport combination. Operation time decreases 23.6–32.6%, allocated bytes decrease 26.7–29.7%, and allocation counts decrease 31.1–42.1% (all benchstat p=0.001). Inverse median operation time indicates throughput gains of about 31–48%. Raw results and CPU/memory profiles: https://github.com/NNdroid/dns_custom/actions/runs/36999019433
- An independent seven-sample Linux J1900 comparison also improves all six transport combinations. Both measurements use closed-loop loopback echo traffic, not public-network throughput guarantees.

Includes the useful downstream-budget changes from PR #2 without its obsolete auto-patching workflow. Retains the current main release workflow and deterministic lifecycle test.

author: maepon
body:
Closes #21

## 変更内容

文書だけの変更です。拡張機能のコードは変えていません。

- `docs/privacy-policy.md`
  - 「ローカルで保存」「ローカルストレージ」「ローカルで管理」を、`chrome.storage.sync` に保存するという書き方に改めた
  - 「データの保存先」の節に、Chrome 同期を有効にしている場合は Google のサーバーを経由して他のデバイスに同期されることを明記した
  - 見出しを「ローカルストレージ」→「データの保存先」、「自動削除」→「アンインストール時の扱い」に変更し、tabs 権限の節からの参照も新しい見出し名に合わせた
  - 「アンインストールするとローカルデータは自動的に削除されます」という断言と「完全削除: アンインストール」をやめた。代わりに「Chrome の仕様による」と書き、確実に消したいなら拡張機能の画面でショートカットを削除するよう案内した
  - 最終更新日は 2026年9月30日（実装日。PR #20 での値と同じなので変更なし）
- `docs/chrome-store-description.md`: storage 権限の用途の「ローカルストレージに保存」を `chrome.storage.sync` に保存、に変更
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased]` の `### Changed` に 2 行追加

## なぜ

データはすべて `chrome.storage.sync` に保存しています（`storage.local` の使用は 0 件）。そのため Chrome 同期を有効にしていると、データは Google のサーバーを経由して同期されます。「ローカル」という言葉は「端末の外に出ない」と読まれやすく、PR #20 で入れた「Googleを経由した同期を除く」という開示と同じ文書の中で食い違って見えていました。どちらの文書も Chrome Web Store の審査とユーザーへの約束なので、事実として言える表現に直しました。

アンインストールしたときに sync のデータが端末や同期先から消えるかどうかは、公式ドキュメントでも実機でも確かめられていません。そのため、消える・消えないのどちらも断言しない書き方にしています。

## 受入基準ごとの対応

文書だけの変更なので単体テストは追加していません。各 AC のコマンドを実行して確認しました。

| AC | 内容 | 検証 |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1〜3 | 「ローカル」「自動的に削除されます」「完全削除」が 0 件 | `git grep` が出力なし |
| AC-4 | 見出しが「データの保存先」(37)・「アンインストール時の扱い」(112) だけで、順序も正しい | `git grep -E` で行番号を比較 |
| AC-5〜12 | 本文が指示書の文と一致する（39/40 行目と 114/115 行目は隣接） | `git grep -F` と `git diff` の突き合わせ |
| AC-13 | `最終更新日: 2026年9月30日` | 実装日の `date` 出力と照合 |
| AC-14 | 変えてはいけない 5 行が残っている | `git grep -F` で各 1 件 |
| AC-15 | storage 権限の用途の行 (102) が storage 権限 (99) と tabs 権限 (106) の間にある | `git grep` |
| AC-16/17 | CHANGELOG の `[Unreleased]` に 2 件。privacy-policy の行に `chrome.storage.sync` と `アンインストール` を含む | `git grep -E` |
| AC-18/19 | 変更は 3 ファイルだけで、未追跡ファイルなし | `git diff master...HEAD --stat` / `git status` |
| AC-20 | 整形チェック | `npm run format:check` が通過（PR 作成前に再実行） |
| AC-21 | テスト | `npm test` 33 件 pass、fail 0 |

## レビューで挙がったが未対応の点

- 行全体の一致を `git grep -x` では確認していません。`-F` の出力と `git diff` を突き合わせて確認しました（レビューの「参考」）
- AC-18 は `git diff --name-only`（作業ツリー）が前提でしたが、実装はコミット済みのため `git diff master...HEAD` で確認しました（レビューの「参考」。フローの実行順の都合です）

## 残存リスク

- **推論だけで通した AC**: 2 回目のレビューでは AC-20 を推論で通していましたが、PR 作成前に `npm run format:check` を実行して通過を確認しました。AC-5〜12 と AC-14 の行全体一致は、`-x` を使わず目視で確認しています
- **事故カタログ**: 文書のみの変更なので、コードに関わる項目はどれも該当しません
- **未確認の記述**
  - `docs/privacy-policy.md:115` の「削除は他のデバイスにも同期されます」は、`chrome.storage.sync.set` の書き換えが同期されるという理解に基づいています。実機では確認していません
  - アンインストール時の挙動は未確認のままで、断言しない文にしてあります
- **範囲外として残した表現**（指示書で対象外にしたもの）
  - `docs/privacy-policy.md:110, 116` の「Chromeの設定から拡張機能の同期データを削除」は、その操作が実際にできるか確認していません
  - `docs/chrome-store-description.md:31` の「データ消失の心配なし: Chromeのクラウドストレージに安全に保存」は言い過ぎの可能性があります
- **マージ後の作業**: Chrome Web Store の Dashboard の掲載情報と、プライバシーポリシーの公開先は人が更新する必要があります

Unblocks the `verify` gate on #96, so the D1 read ceiling can deploy.

## What was actually wrong

Not the guard, and not cross-test timing. Two test files replace `../store.js`
via `mock.module`, and bun rewrites the **shared module registry for the whole
`bun test` process**. Their stub sets `rawBatch` to `async () => [[]]`, which
outlived the file that installed it, so `src/cf/internal.test.ts` was driving
the stub instead of the executor its own `beforeEach` registered.

Consequences match the CI log exactly:

- `expect(executed).toHaveLength(1)` got `0` — the batch never reached D1.
- `expect(status).toBe(500)` got `200` — `setActiveClient`'s throwing executor
  was never called, so nothing threw.

The 3 tests that pass are the ones that assert a refusal **before** the
executor, which is why the failure set looked like a ceiling-logic bug.

`mock.restore()` does not undo a module mock, so this was not fixable from the
test side. Two files needed fixing:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/queue-owner.test.ts` | snapshot the real module by value, re-register in `afterAll` |
| `src/lib/fallback-reconcile.test.ts` | same — it stubs the same module |
| `src/cf/internal.test.ts` | assert the binding is the real `rawBatch`, so a future leak names the cause |

## Why it only ever failed in CI

Bun's test-file order is stable within a checkout but differs by filesystem, so
whether the stub or `internal.test.ts` loads first is a coin flip across
machines. Not flaky — order-dependent, and CI's order is the unlucky one.

## Verification

On a **fresh clone at `01bd731`** with the pinned bun `1.4.2` from CI:

- The leak reproduces exactly — `3 pass / 5 fail`, and the five are the same
  five the CI log lists. Confirmed by preloading the `queue-owner`-shaped stub.
- The fix clears it: `9 pass / 0 fail` under the same preload, and passing
  without it.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Full suite `787 pass / 14 skip / 1 fail`, twice. That one failure is
  `pg-runtime > lifecycle sink ignores D1 ids and handles PG ids`, which is
  **pre-existing**: it reproduces at `3d0df6f` (before this branch) and passes
  when that file runs alone. Untouched here.

## Not addressed

The VPS-side note that a 429 does not trip the caller's circuit breaker
(breaker matches `HTTP 5\d\d` only) is unchanged and not required for this fix.

author: grant-round
body:
## What

Replaces the alias-writing Phase 4 of `zebora-scoring-vec` with a **batch canonicaliser**: one command that rewrites the batch's stored entity names to the confirmed games, so reporting matches them directly.

- `scripts/canonicalise_batch.py` — dry run by default; `--apply --refresh --backup-dir …` to write. For every extracted entity in the batch's active visibility-v3 scores it matches **exact name → existing alias → unique cleaned title**, rewrites `entities[*].entity` / `.brand` (and target flags) to the confirmed game, keeps the original wording in `raw_entity` / `raw_brand`, and adds `canonicalised = {rule, entity_id, at, by}`. Unmatched variants are grouped under one spelling. Idempotent.
- `scripts/vec_titles.py` — the title cleaner (case/punctuation/accents/`&`/leading "the"/number words, "game / card game / board game" suffixes, edition/format/packaging words, word order). Colon subtitles, sequel numbers and junior/kids/family words are deliberately **not** stripped.
- `SKILL.md` Phase 4 rewritten (snapshot → dry run → apply → optional verified leftovers → stored-name audit/re-score). Aliases are now reserved for verified judgement calls (edition/family roll-ups).
- Warns against running `entity_resolution_v3` in write mode: on one batch it would have created 1,449 entities + 303 brands, and its LLM step returns shift-by-one aliases.
- Phase 1b / 7: use the per-batch `refresh_entity_metrics_v2`; the full script / `refresh_url_scores_v1` lock the live dashboard.

No schema changes, no new rows, no view changes.

## Validation (Big Potato UK, Sep 2026)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Variant aliases | 189 created during the alias-based pass | retired |
| Mentions matched to a known game | 95.87% | 95.86% |
| Unmatched rows | 732 | 727 (variants grouped) |

Re-running the dry run on the canonicalised batch rewrites only 12 items (idempotent). Pre-rewrite entities are backed up per run.

author: oleg-tkachuk
body:
The capability SourceIPCIDR check, the login rate limiter and the audit source read the first X-Forwarded-For entry. The caller writes that entry, so a capability restricted to a network could be used from anywhere by sending the header, and the login limiter could be keyed on an address of the caller's choosing.

All three now use the address the listener resolves from trusted_proxies (#84). The console also forwards the header on its own IAM calls (login, refresh), so those are not all keyed on the console pod.

This depends on trusted_proxies being set: the chart now defaults to the private ranges. A deployment with an empty list resolves every client to the ingress address.

body:
The documentation site’s skip link was keyboard-reachable, but its focus indicator relied on the browser default outline. In both light and dark themes that produced a thin, low-prominence ring compared with adjacent page chrome, making the primary bypass control harder to perceive. This change adds an explicit high-contrast focus style for the skip link in both themes.

Affected URLs audited: `/gh-aw-cao/`, `/gh-aw-cao/setup-quickstarts/`, `/gh-aw-cao/configuration/`, `/gh-aw-cao/dashboard-language-specification/`, `/gh-aw-cao/architecture-at-a-glance/`, `/gh-aw-cao/dashboard-overview/`, `/gh-aw-cao/deployment-azure/`, `/gh-aw-cao/agent-resources/`.

### WCAG finding
- Serious — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible / WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance
- Barrier: the `Skip to content` link’s focused state depended on the user agent default outline, which rendered as a 1px auto outline in rendered browser evidence and was insufficiently prominent against the surrounding header styling in both color schemes.

### Before and after browser evidence
- Before:
  - Light theme: focused `.sl-skip-link` rendered with `outline-style: auto`, `outline-width: 1px`, `outline-color: rgb(16, 16, 16)`, `border-radius: 0px`.
  - Dark theme: same default outline behavior, with no explicit repository-owned focus treatment.
- After:
  - Light theme: focused `.sl-skip-link` renders with `outline-style: solid`, `outline-width: 3px`, `outline-color: rgb(31, 111, 235)`, `outline-offset: 4px`, `border-radius: 8px`.
  - Dark theme: focused `.sl-skip-link` renders with `outline-style: solid`, `outline-width: 3px`, `outline-color: rgb(121, 192, 255)`, `outline-offset: 4px`, `border-radius: 8px`.
- Axe results on the revalidated landing page: 0 violations in both light and dark themes for WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA tags.

### Audit coverage
- Browser audit performed against Astro preview at `(127.0.0.1/redacted)
- Representative sample covered the landing page, getting-started content, reference content, image-heavy content, and dashboard documentation pages.
- Manual checks included keyboard navigation, skip-link activation, focus visibility, reduced-motion behavior, and 320px reflow checks.

### Remaining barriers or skipped checks

author: nexabyteuk
body:
## Summary

Adds `product-design/`, one reusable design skill for mobile and web app UI. It combines Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, Nielsen Norman Group research and Linear's product philosophy, with links to the originals.

- **SKILL.md** sets out 12 core principles, an order of precedence (the project's own `DESIGN.md` and `VOICE.md` win, and WCAG 2.2 AA is the accessibility floor), a table that resolves where the sources disagree, defaults for projects with no design docs, and a pre-ship checklist.
- **references/** covers heuristics, interaction patterns, voice and copy, visual design, mobile and touch (iOS 26/27, Android 16/17, Expo), web and desktop, accessibility, and checked source links.
- **references/profiles/linear.md** is an opt-in Linear-style profile. It applies only when a project's `DESIGN.md` names it, and carries over Linear's structure and restraint rather than its colours or fonts.
- **evals/evals.json** holds three test briefs (an ops dashboard, a charity event page and a mobile booking app) with their assertions.

The README lists the new skill, and `.gitignore` excludes the local eval workspace.

## Testing

Three rounds of blind A/B evaluation. Each brief was built once with the skill and once without, and a separate validator scored both without knowing which was which:

| Round | With skill (mean, out of 5) | Without | Checks passed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4.03 | 3.20 | 98% vs 74% |
| 2 | 4.13 | 2.87 | 97% vs 66% |
| 3 | 4.27 | 3.10 | 94% vs 65% |

The build that used the skill was preferred in 9 of 9 comparisons. The biggest gains were in platform behaviour (+2.7), interaction states (+2.0) and accessibility (+1.3).

author: trentnbauer
body:
The GitHub wiki is a separate git repository that pull requests (and the Claude GitHub App) can't write to, which is why it was still on the 8 August version. This PR gets the update onto the wiki in one go.

## How
- **`docs/wiki/`** holds the updated pages.
- **`.github/workflows/wiki-sync.yml`** runs when a change under `docs/wiki/**` reaches `main`, or when started manually. It makes `QueueUp.wiki.git` an exact copy of `docs/wiki/` and pushes it using the repo's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: write`).

**This is one-off.** Once the sync has run and the wiki is confirmed updated, a follow-up PR removes both the workflow and `docs/wiki/` in the same commit. They have to go together: deleting `docs/wiki/` while the workflow still exists would sync an empty folder and wipe the wiki.

## The pages
This is the full wiki update prepared earlier today:
- the v2 UI and features
- friends and profiles
- picker weights
- the new consoles and backwards compatibility
- appearance and room colours
- the Discord event switches
- the in-app backup system from #645
- `PRIVATE_INSTANCE`, how `ADMIN_EMAILS` behaves, and the `SESSION_SECRET` minimum
- upgrade steps
- the architecture and data model
- the v2 screenshots (linked from `docs/screenshots` on `main`)

## If the sync fails
Check Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions. The workflow asks for `contents: write`, but an org- or repo-level setting can still cap the token.

author: anujshrm325
body:
## What
Staff attendance ("हाज़िरी") with leave and owner-only salary. Each employee uses their own login; there is no kiosk.

**Attendance**
- **IN / OUT:** GPS is read once, only when the button is pressed. The office location is set once by the owner; the radius defaults to 100 m.
- **Outside the radius:** the employee writes a reason and it is saved as a separate **FIELD** record. No GPS means no attendance.
- **Daily limits:** one IN and one OUT per day. OUT is not allowed within 1 hour of IN.

**Rules and owner reports**
- The owner can edit the rules: 10:00–19:00, weekly off (Sunday by default), the owner's own holiday list (no automatic holidays), late after 15 min, half day after 2 h, 1 paid leave per month, optional late deduction (off by default).
- The owner gets a morning report at start + 30 min and an evening list of staff with no OUT.
- Each report is sent only within 2 hours of its time, so a restart later in the day does not send a stale report.
- Inside the 24h window the report goes as text; outside it, as the `staff_notice` template.

**WhatsApp staff mode**
- Staff numbers never reach the customer flow.
- Staff can send "हाज़िरी", "जा रहा हूँ" or "बाहर का काम: कारण", then a location (uses `location_request_message` inside the window). Leave is applied by text; "हो गया" works for tasks.
- The owner decides leave with the मंज़ूर / नामंज़ूर buttons or "मंज़ूर 5" / "नामंज़ूर 5". The staff member is told the result.

**Salary (OWNER only, checked on the server; ADMIN and EMPLOYEE get 403)**
- Monthly salary with change history.
- Per-day amount = salary ÷ working days.
- Leave quota, unpaid leave, absence and half days are counted.
- The owner adds bonus / advance / deduction with a note, then finalizes the sheet.
- Excel export. The WhatsApp slip is sent only when the owner presses "भेजो".
- Amounts are never logged.

**Web**
- New `/attendance` page in EN/HI with tabs: My attendance, Today, Leave, Month (Excel + PDF), Settings (office location via "ऑफिस यहीं है", rules, holidays) and Salary (owner only).
- New sidebar item "Attendance / हाज़िरी".

**Staff phones**
- The owner's list is written once to the Team mobile field, matched by full name.
- Names not found are sent to the owner on WhatsApp.

## Migration
`20261005120000_staff_attendance` (additive only)

## Checks
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (API 369 passed), `pnpm build` and the API bundle all pass.
- New tests cover geofence, missing GPS, IN/OUT rules, late / half day, leave approval and its notifications, salary calculation, salary owner-only (403 for ADMIN and EMPLOYEE), WhatsApp staff mode (location, too far → reason → FIELD, leave, owner buttons), staff name matching and the report window.
- E2E on a throwaway Postgres with the bundled server:
  - API: 403s, geofence, half day, leave, salary, xlsx.
  - WhatsApp webhook: staff and owner flows.
  - Logs carry only masked numbers; no coordinates and no message text.
- Playwright screenshots in EN and HI.

## Owner setup
- Meta templates `leave_request` and `staff_notice`: submit them from the Templates panel.
- `WA_OWNER_NUMBERS` (falls back to `WA_ALERT_NUMBERS`).
- Set the office location in the Settings tab (open it on a phone, standing in the office).

body:
Adds a second guide, for the Google Cloud **Professional Cloud Developer** (PCD) exam, in `pcd/`. It uses the same format and study app as the PCA guide. The app and the checkers now build either guide with `--guide pca|pcd`.

The published app: [PCD Workbook](https://claude.ai/artifact/2CHa4KR5pQHwwsxbC5CjfS) (private, `db` progress readable and writable only by the owner).

## Changes
- `pcd/content/`:
  - 46 notes pages for the 11 objectives, each 1,200 to 3,000 words, with a citation for every fact.
  - 353 questions, 550 flashcards, 300 glossary terms, 71 service profiles, and a name-changes page.
  - `SPEC.md` and `PLAN.md`.
- `pcd/labs/`: 22 labs in a dedicated `pcd-lab-` project.
  - `env.sh` refuses other project IDs. It also sets `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT`, and a lab-only `KUBECONFIG`.
  - Each lab has a teardown script and cost notes.
- `app/build.mjs`: the `--guide` option.
  - The guide's names come from the `app` block in `exam.json`.
  - The share zip keeps the dotfiles that a lab needs.
- Shared app fixes, which the PCA app also gets:
  - The "Study" links of an explanation go only to the notes pages that cite the question's sources.
  - Docs quotes show code as code.
  - On a phone, long inline code and link text wrap.
- PCA keeps its browser keys (`pca-route`, `pca-session`, `pca-workbook-v1`), so saved progress still loads.
- `tools/guides.py`: the guide paths. Each checker takes `--guide pcd`. `package.json` has `build:pcd`, `share:pcd`, and `check:pcd:*`.

- `dist/`: both apps rebuilt, including the PCA and PCD share zips.

## Verification
- **Fact checks:** each of the 12 question domains had a blind solve, and every first answer matched the key. Then a second agent checked the notes, questions, and cards against the cited docs.
- **Quotes:**
  - `npm run check:pcd:questions`: 353 questions, 0 errors.

- **Tests:** `npm test` passes 28 of 28.
- **UI:** a headless Chrome check covered 161 PCD pages and 265 PCA pages at phone and desktop width. No page overflows, and the console shows no errors.

## ⚠️ Finding for the lead: 4 lib-test failures on a local macOS run, none on Linux CI
`cargo test --locked` in this worktree on this dev Mac (8515-class Apple Silicon) fails the lib harness: **802 passed; 4 failed; 4 ignored**. CI's Linux run of the *same code* is green (782 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored). I did not write the failing local numbers into the notes; I also did not "fix" anything — reporting instead:

- 3 × `popover_snapshot_command_tests` (`the_real_command_reads_the_session...`, `...survives_a_storage_api_that_answers_500`, `lock_then_unlock_refetches_the_storage_summary`) — phase came back `finder_failed` instead of `synced`. Mechanism identified: on macOS `popover_snapshot` takes the `cfg!(target_os)` branch (lib.rs:3801) and calls `finder_location_state()` → `macos_file_provider::status()`, which reads the **real system's File Provider domain** (this dev Mac has one registered). The tests' `with_isolated_env` only isolates env vars; mirroring CI's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`TMPDIR` did not change the result. These tests pass on Linux where `is_macos` is compile-time false. Likely a test-isolation gap (never run on macOS: CI's macOS job is Rust *check* only), not a product regression.
- 1 × `engine_bridge::tests::ipc_hydrate_streams_progress_frames_before_the_final_reply` (`#[cfg(unix)]`) — expects progress frames `[(0,30),(10,30),(20,30),(30,30)]`, got `[(0,30),(10,30),(20,30)]`: the final chunk's frame is missing before the final Ok reply. Deterministic: 5/5 failures run alone. Mechanism **not** diagnosed; it is green on CI Linux at the same commit.
- Local counts vs Linux: lib announces 810 tests locally (806 non-ignored) vs 786 on Linux (782 non-ignored) — 24 extra non-ignored tests on macOS are `cfg(target_os = "macos")`-gated.

Suggested follow-up (not this PR): make the popover-snapshot tests inject/stub the Finder probe instead of hitting the real OS, and diagnose the hydrate frame race.

body: Found by the second nightly sweep. On ext4 (GitHub's Linux runners) clone is not available and placement fell back to hard links; then phpstan/extension-installer's plugin rewrote vendor/phpstan/extension-installer/src/GeneratedConfig.php through the link, changing the store copy, and the next project placed from that store got the first project's absolute paths (10 projects differed; npm-asset modes changed the same way). When no --link-mode is given and the install will run scripts or Composer steps, a failed clone now falls back to copies, and Windows copies instead of hard linking. --link-mode=hardlink keeps the old behaviour. Pure installs (nothing runs in vendor/) still hard link. Regression test: a post-install script that rewrites and chmods a vendor file leaves the store as it was.

author: notnaki
body:
Space swipes published every drag and pull update through `TabStore`, invalidating the whole browser window. The moving sidebar, background tint, and Space dots then repeatedly decoded profile files on the main thread, causing uneven updates even after the landing animation rollback.

Move gesture observation into a separate object used by those views, and share one presentation snapshot of the Space strip for the duration of the gesture. The existing landing animation stays in place. Destination switching still revalidates against disk, and ending or interrupting a gesture releases the snapshot so external edits become visible.

Validation:
- Debug build and pure checks passed.
- 105 real-WebKit browser assertions passed, including gesture cleanup, snapshot lifetime, and existing cross-profile checks.
- The new regression failed before the fix with 40 whole-browser invalidations across 20 gesture updates, and passes after the fix with zero.
- In the same isolated 100-URL Space fixture, profile Space-list reads fell from 603 to 1. The 95th-percentile interval between gesture updates fell from 25.6 ms to 9.2 ms. These are fixture update intervals, not a claim about real-world frame rate.

author: takeokunn
body:
## Summary

Implements the design-first mc-sim foundation for R-SI2/R-SI3: a per-player registry boundary and authoritative state services that mx-multiplayer can apply without making mc-compose own gameplay state. The API and responsibility boundaries are documented in [`docs/public-api.md`](docs/public-api.md), [`docs/responsibility.md`](docs/responsibility.md), and [`docs/design-notes.md`](docs/design-notes.md).

## Command ownership

mc-sim owns 18 of the 20 authoritative command tags in this slice:

| Command tag | mc-sim surface | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WorldTimeWeatherCommand` | `TimeService` / `WeatherService` | existing services |
| `ContainerCommand` | `ContainerService` | implemented |
| `FurnaceCommand` | `FurnaceService` over smelting state | implemented |
| `VillagerTradeCommand` | `VillagerService` | implemented |
| `EntityAttackCommand` | behaviour-agnostic entity damage surface | documented ownership surface |
| `EntityPickupCommand` | `EntityManager.find` / `EntityManager.despawn` | existing surface |
| `BowUseCommand` | `ProjectileChargeService` / projectile API | implemented |
| `IgniteTntCommand` | primed-TNT application surface | existing surface |
| `EndPortalUseCommand` | `PortalService` / `EndStateService` | implemented |
| `ThrowEyeOfEnderCommand` | `ProjectileChargeService` / projectile API | implemented |
| `InsertEyeIntoEndPortalFrameCommand` | `EndStateService` | implemented |
| `NetherPortalUseCommand` | `PortalService` | implemented |
| `EnderPearlCommand` | projectile / teleport surface | implemented |
| `BucketUseCommand` | `FluidService` | implemented |
| `FishingCommand` | `FishingService` | implemented |
| `VehicleCommand` | `VehicleService` | existing surface |
| `PlayerInventoryCommand` | player-owned inventory / hotbar / equipment surface behind the registry boundary | existing surface |
| `PlayerVitalsCommand` | player-owned vitals surface behind the registry boundary | existing surface |

`PlayerRegistryService` provides the typed `PlayerId` boundary and atomic `create`, `remove`, `find`, `list`, `snapshot`, `restore`, and `reset` lifecycle API. Input is decoded with Effect Schema before registry state changes. The registry integration boundary and the operation-specific state services are described in the public API documentation.

## Out of scope

- `ToggleLeverCommand`: redstone device state belongs to `mx-redstone`.
- `VehicleUseCommand`: the current wire shape does not carry a vehicle target or action; the protocol change belongs to `mx-multiplayer`.

## Verification

- Local verify passed: 45 test files and 788 tests, with typecheck, lint, and AST checks.
- Local coverage passed: Statements, Branches, Functions, and Lines are each 100%.
- Local package verification passed, including the package boundary checks and archive inspection.
- The 0.5.1 mainline change in `src/application/game-loop.ts` is included through the rebase; this PR does not modify that file.

## Scope

This PR adds state and registry APIs only. Gameplay rules remain in their owning services, and no protocol fields or cross-package ownership are invented here.

author: iflux-jr
body:
Before: there was nowhere to enter scores. Result Officers had an empty "Results" card on their dashboard.

After: **Scores** in the menu lists the arms you can enter, with how many scores are complete. Opening an arm lists its subjects, and opening a subject gives one sheet. On phones each student is a card with CA 1, CA 2, CA 3 and Exam side by side; on wider screens it's a table. Each row saves as soon as a box changes, ABS can be typed for an absent student, and the total and grade appear immediately. **Mark complete** locks the sheet once everyone has every part. After that, **Correct** needs a reason, and every changed part is kept with its old and new value. Result Officers' dashboards now point to their scores.

How:
- New `scores` and `score_corrections` tables. Parts are stored as JSON keyed by the section's score scheme (`ca1`… `exam`), along with the scheme and grade-band versions used.
- `App\Domain\Results\ScoreBook` handles:
  - access: Admins and the class's current Result Officer; a Super Admin can view only (Q-ROLE-1)
  - guards: current term only, exam-flagged classes blocked, locked terms blocked
  - who takes a subject: in classes with streams, only students who chose it this session
  - saving, completing and correcting scores
  - arm and subject progress, from grouped queries
- Score parts can't be changed on Grading once the term has scores in that section.
- Scores block deleting their subject, arm or session. Completing and correcting are audited.
- New Livewire pages `ScoreIndex`, `ScoreArm` and `ScoreSheet`. The rows use `wire:model.live.change` so each box saves when you leave it.
- ADR 0015 and traceability updated. Import, publishing and the score ETL are S9.
- Tests: `ScoreEntryTest` (8). The full suite passes on SQLite and MariaDB (191). Pages were checked in a browser at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark.

The `Resolutions - PR` workflow sets `SKIP_UPLOAD: 'True'`, but `config.py` only reads `SKIP_UPDATE`, so the flag never took effect. Every pull request ran `generate_resolutions.py` against three production assets with the real API key and uploaded the results.

Evidence: the HDR test asset 11315 "Photo studio" had its resolution files rewritten at 11:04 UTC on 16 Sep, four minutes after the PR run for `add_wider_search` started.

This sets `SKIP_UPDATE` instead. The job still downloads and generates resolutions, which is the actual test, and skips the upload and the asset patch.

Merge this before the other open `claude/` PRs in this repo: they are stacked on it so their own PR runs no longer write to production.

author: tyagiquamar
body:
### Problem
In `nested_format_specs::write`, `buffer_ctx` was constructed directly as `FormatContext(basic_appender<Char>(buf), ctx.args(), ctx.locale())`. When `FormatContext` is not parameterized with `basic_appender<Char>` (such as when custom contexts or different output iterators are passed, e.g. during compilation/custom formatters with nested formatted ranges like `std::array` or tuples), attempting to construct `FormatContext` directly with `basic_appender<Char>` leads to template instantiation and iterator mismatch errors (#4949).

### Solution
- Explicitly instantiate `basic_format_context<basic_appender<Char>, Char>` for the temporary buffer context in `nested_format_specs::write()`.

### Validation
- Validated in Linux container with GCC 14:
  - Built and passed 100% of tests in `ranges-test` (42/42 tests) and `compile-test` (19/19 tests).

author: liumingjian
body:
## Why

Every synced path got its own workspace on the mac, and every worktree is a new path, so `~/rexec-workspace` grew by gigabytes a day (22G → 33.6G in about an hour on the mac mini) with nothing ever removing it, under names like `t330-614f9a` that did not say which repository made them.

## What

- **Names** (`ws_key` in `server/rexec-lib.sh`): `<repo>--<hash6>`, `<repo>--wt-<worktree>--<hash6>`, plus `--<sub>` for a synced subdirectory. Job IDs take the repo prefix.
- **Records**: the agent keeps `~/.rexec/ws/<name>` with the source path and last use (stamped at job start and end, detached jobs included).
- **Cleanup** (`gc.sh`, written by the agent; runs at startup and hourly, logs `CLEAN` lines):
  - source gone from the server → deleted
  - unused 7 days → deleted, unless it holds files the server lacks (kept, reported once)
  - running / queued / detached → never touched; a per-workspace lock closes the race with a claim
  - server unreachable → nothing deleted that round
- **Migration**: old-style names are renamed once the new `server/rexec-ws` finds their directory on the server, and at claim time; untraceable ones go only on `rexec --gc --apply`.
- **`rexec --gc`** (dry run, also sizes Docker/npm/cache dirs) and **`rexec --gc --apply`**; requires agent cap `gc`.

## Tests (run on the mac)

- `tests/gc-test.sh`: 31 passed
- `tests/agent-test.sh`: 5 passed
- `tests/queue-test.sh`: 26 passed

## Deploy

`bash skills/misc/rexec/install.sh` on the server, then restart the agent on each mac.

author: i9experts
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the LMS build-out (see Phases 1 & 2, merged). Four pieces, all admin/teacher-side since there's still no student/parent-facing consumption app in this org's repos:

- **Completion certificates**: added a `course_completion` certificate type. `CertificatesService.autoIssueCourseCompletion` auto-issues an **audit-record-only** `IssuedCertificate` (no PDF generated or stored) the instant a student finishes every lesson in a published Syllabus. Guarded by a partial unique index (`{studentId, sourceType, sourceId}`) so re-checking an already-finished course never double-issues. Wired into `ParentPortalService.markLessonProgress`, wrapped so a certificate hiccup never blocks the student's own progress save. An admin can print the real PDF later through the existing Certificates flow — same as any other issued certificate.
- **Assignment auto-spawn**: `SyllabusLesson` gets an optional `dueDate`; `Assignment` gets `autoSpawnKey`. `SyllabusService.addLesson/updateLesson/deleteLesson` now keeps a real `Assignment` row in sync with a lesson's own due date (upserted on `autoSpawnKey`, removed when the due date is cleared), so it surfaces immediately in the already-working Parent Portal `getHomework` endpoint — no separate parent-facing UI needed for this one to pay off.
- **Student 360 Learning tab (backend)**: new `GET /students/:id/learning` — a student's published-course completion + quiz attempt history. Deliberately a **separate endpoint**, not folded into the existing `getStudent360` aggregate, so every Student 360 page load doesn't pay for three extra queries just because the tab exists.
- **Analytics**: `Syllabus.getDashboard` gets two lightweight stats (`publishedCourseCount`, `totalLessonsAuthored`) computed from the data it already fetches — no new queries.

## Test plan

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npm run build` (`nest build`) — clean.
- Real `npx nest start` boot smoke test: DI graph resolves through every new cross-module wiring (Syllabus → Assignment, ParentPortal → Certificates, Students → Syllabus/LessonProgress/QuizAttempt) and reaches the expected sandbox-only `JwtStrategy requires a secret or key` failure point — confirms no schema/DI regression.
- Manual verification will follow once deployed (no live DB/secrets in this sandbox): mark a course's last lesson complete and confirm an `IssuedCertificate` row appears once a `course_completion` template is set as default/active; set a lesson due date and confirm it appears in `getHomework`.

author: s-sanchez-gremi
body:
Step S2 of `docs/split-plan.md` (S1 shared packages is merged). One repo, one database, two apps.

**`apps/crm`** (Sam): CRM/leads, **forms** (builder, responses, public submission API `/api/forms/*`), projects, tasks, ERP registry, client portal (`/portal`). Own login + session cookie (`apex_crm_session`), menu, dashboard, `/api/health`, `/api/cron/tick`, robots (disallow all).
**`apps/web`** (Joan Marc): public site, form *rendering*, CMS admin. Lost only the CRM screens/menus/dashboard cards.

How the two apps talk (the only calls, documented in CLAUDE.md):
1. Browser still posts to the public `/api/forms/…`. Production: Caddy routes it to the CRM app (step S3). Dev/tests: the website's `proxy.ts` forwards when `CRM_INTERNAL_URL` is set.
2. After a form is saved/deleted the CRM app calls the website's `POST /api/cron/revalidate` (`WEB_INTERNAL_URL` + shared `CRON_SECRET`) so the cached form refreshes.

Also:
- Shared e2e runner `e2e/` (workspace package): builds and starts BOTH apps (ports 3100/3101) on one throwaway DB; specs live with their app (`apps/*/e2e`). The forms flow now crosses both apps (built in the CRM app, drawn by the website, submitted through the website's address).
- Unit tests split: web 122, crm 75 (separate throwaway DBs).
- `@apex/core`: CSP builder and env check moved there; migration runner finds `db/migrations` from any folder.
- `pnpm dev` starts both (3000 / 3001). `ci.sh`, the workflow and `local-setup.sh` updated (setup also falls back to npm for pnpm on Node 25+).
- Ownership: `.github/CODEOWNERS` rewritten per app; `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md` updated.

Not in this PR (step S3): second Docker image, Caddy hosts/routing, deploy scripts and drills for the CRM app, database users. The production image still builds only the website until then.

Verified locally before the final rebase: lint, types, 197 unit tests (122 + 75), both production builds with no config, and all 41 browser tests across both apps (including the cross-app form flow). GitHub CI runs the full suite on this PR.

**Review focus (Joan Marc):** files moved out of `apps/web` are only the CRM/forms ones; `proxy.ts` gains the forwarding rule; admin nav/dashboard lose CRM entries; `robots.ts` no longer mentions `/portal`.

## Why

SNC staff log in to AEGIS as `name@sixnineconstruction.com`, but those aren't real mailboxes; staff are Microsoft guests on personal Gmail addresses. Every AEGIS email to them went nowhere. That covers urgent-notification escalations, invites, CRM automation emails and compliance alerts. It's likely also why some addresses ended up on Resend's suppression list.

## What changes

One place, `core/email.py: send_email`: if the recipient is an AEGIS user who has a Teams account, the email goes to the mailbox behind that account. A guest identity like `ekowimbeah5_gmail.com#EXT#@SixNineConstruction.onmicrosoft.com` decodes to `ekowimbeah5@gmail.com`.

**Unchanged:**
- Logins and the emails stored in AEGIS.
- Clients, suppliers, and anyone without a Teams account.
- Any lookup error falls back to the original address, exactly as before.

**Not covered:** emails Supabase sends itself (its own password-reset emails) still go to the login address.

## Testing

- New tests cover decoding the real address from guest, member and malformed identities, falling back when the lookup fails, and that `send_email` resolves the recipient.
- A dry run against the live user list showed all 14 staff map to their real Gmail addresses, while `ashton@admin.com` and outside addresses stay the same.

author: schancel
body:
## Summary
- `registryAddressMetadataDigest` uses `@frank/nakamoto` `cryptoBackend.sha256`, one SHA-256 (decision #507). It matches `Sha256::digest` in `SignedPayload::parse_proto` (`backend/cashweb/cashweb-payload/src/payload.rs`) and `Sha256::digest(address_metadata.encode_to_vec())` in `backend/cashweb/cashweb-registry/tests/test_http_endpoint.rs`. It also matches bitcore `crypto.Hash.sha256` and Node `crypto.createHash('sha256')`. Not double-SHA256.
- `constructRelayUrlMetadata` uses that digest as the `signRegistryDigest` message. `updateKeyMetadata` uses the same digest for the truncated payment request, as the exact 32-byte digest rather than `Buffer.buffer`. Compact r||s stays decision #489. Broadcast message digests, address-string conversion, and script construction in this file stay on bitcore. This is not relay HMAC, salt, or envelope ECDH (#258) and not the app worker's `HDPrivateKey.fromSeed`.
- Issue #257 stays open.

## Tests
Cashweb jest: 14 suites, 111 passed. The new test checks the empty SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` against Node and bitcore, pins AddressMetadata `{timestamp:1234,ttl:10}` bytes `08d209100a` to `34095659432189c2f20da437d34a0f2a1de9016ab1ca3d4e12e4390153aac0f0`, rejects double-SHA256, and checks `constructRelayUrlMetadata` still matches bitcore's compact signature over that digest.

Not reviewed.

## قاعده‌ی جدید کد دعوت
- **دوست (دعوت‌شونده):** فقط روی **اولین خریدش** 10٪ تخفیف می‌گیره و هر نفر **فقط یک بار** از کد دعوت استفاده می‌کنه. کد برای بقیه‌ی دوست‌ها همچنان کار می‌کنه. قبلا هر کسی روی هر خریدی و هر چند بار می‌تونست 10٪ بگیره. استفاده از کد خود هم پیام خطای روشن داره.
- **صاحب کد:** به‌ازای هر دوستی که خرید اولش رو با کدش انجام بده، **یک بار 15٪** تخفیف روی خرید بعدی خودش می‌گیره.
  - در چک‌اوت خودکار اعمال می‌شه و با کد تخفیف جمع نمی‌شه: هر کدوم بیشتر بود همون اعمال می‌شه، و اونی که استفاده نشد مصرف هم نمی‌شه.
  - فقط بعد از پرداخت موفق در verify مصرف می‌شه (`inviterRewardApplied`).
- **اسم کد دلخواه:** بخش جدید «کد دعوت» در پروفایل.
  - هر کاربر اسم کدش رو خودش انتخاب می‌کنه: 4 تا 16 حرف انگلیسی یا عدد.
  - کد باید یکتا باشه، هم در برابر کد بقیه و هم در برابر کدهای تخفیف ادمین، و تغییرش محدودیت نرخ داره.
  - تعداد دوستانی که با کد خرید کردن و تعداد پاداش‌های 15٪ آماده هم همون‌جا نشون داده می‌شه.

## فایل‌ها
- `lib/referral.ts`: ثابت‌ها (10 و 15) و قاعده‌ی شکل کد.
- `lib/discountValidation.ts`: چک «اولین خرید / یک بار» و `findInviterRewards`.
- `app/api/subscription/checkout`: انتخاب بین کد تخفیف و پاداش صاحب کد.
- `app/api/subscription/verify`:
  - `referralUsageId` فقط وقتی مال همین کاربر و در وضعیت PENDING باشه REWARDED می‌شه.
  - پاداش صاحب کد فقط وقتی مال همین کاربره مصرف می‌شه.
- `app/api/account/referral` (جدید): GET برای آمار و PATCH برای تغییر اسم کد.
- پروفایل و صفحه‌ی چک‌اوت: نمایش و پیش‌نمایش قیمت.
- بدون مایگریشن؛ فقط کامنت `schema.prisma` به‌روز شد.

## مرج با PRهای دیگه
این شاخه، شاخه‌های #295 (قیمت‌گذاری ادمین)، #294 (اشتراک تصویر، که #291 رو هم داره) و #292 (لودینگ تلگرامی) رو هم داخل خودش داره، چون با هر سه روی فایل‌های مشترک تداخل داشت. تداخل‌ها این‌جا حل شده:
- **امضای چک‌اوت:** `inviterRewardId` جزو امضای HMAC چک‌اوت (#295) شد و verify اون رو هم مطابقت می‌ده.
- **پیش‌نمایش قیمت:** از قیمت پایه‌ی قابل ویرایش (#295) و درصد بزرگ‌تر بین کد و پاداش حساب می‌شه.

همه‌ی PRهای باز (#291 تا #295 و این) با هر ترتیبی بدون تداخل مرج می‌شن. پیشنهاد: اول بقیه، این آخر.

author: trois-six
body:
## Problem

The CI matrix runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on stable, beta and nightly. Clippy on the current **beta and nightly** (clippy 0.1.100) reports `clippy::map_unwrap_or` — denied through `clippy::pedantic` in `src/lib.rs` — on existing code:

```text
error: called `map(_).unwrap_or_default()` on an `Option` value
   --> src/types/place.rs:321:9
```

So `main` itself now fails the "Test Suite (beta)" and "(nightly)" jobs (it last ran green on 2026-09-07 with older toolchains), fail-fast cancels the stable job with them, and **every open PR shows red** regardless of its content.

## Fix

`Place::jurisdictions` uses `map_or_else(Vec::new, |v| …)` instead of `.map(…).unwrap_or_default()`. Same behaviour; available on every toolchain of the matrix (`Option::map_or_default` is avoided on purpose).

## Verification

Locally, mirroring `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo +stable|+beta|+nightly clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — no lint left on any of the three
- `cargo +stable|+beta|+nightly test --all-features` and `cargo test --doc`
- `cargo +stable build --release` and `cargo +stable test --release`

This is independent of the other open PRs; once it is merged, their beta/nightly jobs go green on a rebase or re-run.

author: fijisoo
body:
## What

- **A Workbook at the end of the Python chapter**: twelve exercises that mix ideas from the Basics lessons in ways the lessons don't, from the easiest to the hardest, in English and Polish. It's practice only. Like every exercise, it counts toward a reader's progress but not toward the exam or a certificate.
- **Practical tasks in the exams**, and a six-task exam for the Python chapter, so the chapter gets a certificate. Readers write code in the exam page, from the easiest task to the hardest. Questions and tasks count the same toward the score, and the pass mark stays `passScore` (80%, so five tasks of six).

Part of ML-firestarter/ML-firestarter#15. It follows the idea of step 7, coding tasks in the exam, but grades them differently (below).

## How a task is graded

The reader's code runs in their browser, in the same Pyodide as the exercises, on the cases of an instance the API drew when the attempt started. The page hands in what each case did. The API compares a keyed digest of that with the one sealed into the attempt. So the values the code should give never reach the page, and the site's servers run none of the reader's code, which would otherwise need a separate grader with no secrets and no network.

The limit, written up in the README: a reader who already knows what the right code gives on each case could hand that in without writing the code. Exams aren't proctored, as before, and questions can be asked around just the same. If it ever matters, a sandboxed server can run the code on the same cases and the API can compare it in the same way.

Each task has several instances, and each reader has their own order for them, so attempts don't repeat an instance before the others have been used.

## Where things are

- **The tasks are in the private exams repository** (`02-python/tasks/`), with their solutions, the code that makes their instances, and solutions with one plausible mistake each. Production builds download only each task's text, starter code, pool of instances and files. The pools are made by `npm run exam-tasks` and checked by `npm run check:exam-tasks`, which also checks that the solutions use only what the lessons teach and that no instance lets the starter code or a wrong solution through.
- The README has a new "Writing exam tasks" section, and the sections on secrecy, certificates and setup cover tasks.

## Deploy

- No new settings. The private repository gets the tasks right before this is merged, so the production build that follows finds them. Deploy previews are built without exams, as before, so this preview shows the Workbook but no exam.
- Exam hand-ins can be up to 400 kB instead of 200 kB, since they carry what the code did.
- The exam page's rules text is reworded to cover tasks, for every exam. Certificates of exams that only have questions read as before.

## What I ran

- `npm run check`: 0 errors.
- `npm run check:exercises`: all 42 exercises pass.
- `npm run check:exam-tasks` (needs the private clone): all 6 tasks are fine.
- `npm run build`, with the private `exams/` folder and with a tree that has neither it nor any exam settings, as a deploy preview has.
- The exam page in a browser against the real API with a fake GitHub: starting an attempt, saved drafts, Run and Stop, a failed attempt and a passing one, publishing the certificate and its page, the timeout and Python-unavailable messages, the Polish pages, and the mobile and dark layouts.

Not tested: a real Netlify and GitHub deployment.

author: adipose
body:
bzip2 came in with #4157 because LAV's ffmpeg is configured with `--enable-bzlib`, and configure fails without a `bz2.lib` to check against.  But nothing actually links it:

1. The only user of `CONFIG_BZLIB` in ffmpeg is `matroskadec.c`, and LAV builds with `--disable-demuxer=matroska`.
2. LAV Splitter reads Matroska with its own `MatroskaParser.c`, which handles zlib and header stripping only.  Any other `ContentCompAlgo`, bzlib included, makes it skip the track.
3. `bz2.lib` is not in any `FFmpegLinkDeps` list, and those come from ffmpeg's own link lines.  LAV's gcc build has no `BZ2_` code in it either.

So nothing is lost.  A bzlib compressed track in an MKV is skipped before and after this change.

This removes the submodule, the project, the include path and the flag in the regen scripts and `build_ffmpeg.sh`.  The generated configs only change `CONFIG_BZLIB` to 0 and the configuration string, which is what regen would write.  The `build_ffmpeg.sh` inside the LAVFilters submodule still has `--enable-bzlib`.  That one belongs to clsid2/LAVFilters.

Tested with clean Release rebuilds of x64 and Win32 (`build_lavfilters.bat Rebuild ... MSVC`), then playback in MPC-HC x64.  Win32 was build only.  The "before" column is LAV's existing gcc build, tested at the demuxer.

| File | Before (bzlib enabled) | After |
|---|---|---|
| plain MKV | video and audio | video and audio |
| MP4 | video and audio | video and audio |
| MKV, zlib audio track | video and audio | video and audio |
| MKV, bzlib audio track | video only, audio track skipped | video only, audio track skipped |

Stock ffmpeg 9.0.1 plays the bzlib file with audio, so it is a valid test.

author: roarge
body:
The experiment's grep and read tools left out every folder named `model`, `docs` or `experiments` at any depth. So `adapter/model`, 14 Go files of the demo holding 31 of the 169 tests the experiment links and 23 of the 69 that carry a key, could never be searched or read. EXP-SR-18 and the README meant the checkout's top-level folders, and this change makes the code do that before any run.

- EXP-SR-18 says the top-level folders are left out and gains the criterion `nestedModelIsCode`. The criterion `builtSystemOnly` and the case's documentation say the same.
- `TestEXPSR18_ANestedModelPackageIsCode` finds a word in a fixture file under `adapter/model` and nowhere else, while copies of it in code files under the fixture's top-level `model`, `docs` and `experiments` folders stay out. It fails if the top-level rule is dropped or applied at every depth.
- `tools.go` leaves out `model`, `docs` and `experiments` only as folders of the checkout's root. Hidden folders, `testdata`, `vendor`, `node_modules` and `results` stay out at any depth.

The change alters what a run can show: the code of `adapter/model` now reaches the language model through grep and read. Scoring, the corpus, the systems model the experiment reads, the budgets and the settings are unchanged.

Based on #64, which lets `make preflight` pass again.

Checked: `make experiment-test` and `make experiment-model-check` pass. The new test failed before the code change and passes after it.

author: demianmoor
body:
Card 869faenje.

**Cause:** the preview effect in `campaign-form-state.ts` read `offer_cooldown_days` / `offer_limit_times` with `form.getValues()` while building the request, but neither was in the effect's dependency keys. Editing them changed the form value without re-running the effect; the new values only went out when another input triggered a run.

**Fix:**
- A committed pair `{cooldownDays, limitTimes}` changes only on **Enter** or **blur** (never per keystroke). It is part of the preview's trigger keys, and the request sends it.
- Both inputs commit `onBlur`; a plain Enter commits (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter keeps the form shortcut).
- Same fix in the T5 draft (#271).

**Verified in the browser (dev:preview, throwaway draft, deleted after):**
- Typing in "Not within" sends nothing; **Enter** → one preview with `offer_cooldown_days: 30`, no save, the page stays.
- Typing in "Not more than" sends nothing; **click elsewhere** → one preview with `offer_limit_times: 2`.
- **Every other audience input already recalculated**, with the new value in the request: cap, both toggles, segment include/exclude, carrier filter, removing a segment.
- Enter in the cap field does not submit the form (no submit button).

tsc clean; lint: no new findings (the editor's `setState`-in-effect error is pre-existing on main).

author: pobsteta
body:
## Résumé

Lot 1 de la spec 054 : le cœur dispose d'un **flux de production biologique** mesuré par l'IFN, par sylvoécorégion et par campagne, avec une incertitude par domaine. La méthode Fay-Herriot vient d'Onwunji et al. (2026), *Annals of Forest Science* 83:46.

**Nouvelles fonctions exportées :**
- `estimer_fay_herriot()` : EBLUP et MSE (Prasad-Rao, correction REML), écrit en R de base. Il reproduit `sae::mseFH()` à 1e-14 près ; `sae` passe en `Suggests` pour ce test uniquement.
- `ifn_production_ser()` : production en surface terrière (PG, exacte) et en volume (PV, forme et hauteur constantes), par SER / GRECO / national × campagne × groupe.
- `ifn_production_reference()` : valeur à appliquer à une UGF (5 dernières campagnes, repli GRECO puis national). Le niveau et la nature de la valeur sont toujours déclarés.

**Table :** `inst/extdata/ifn_production_ser.csv` (11 754 lignes, 2 Mo), construite par `data-raw/build_ifn_production.R`.

## Résultats

| | PG | PV |
|---|---|---|
| Covariables | h_sd + alt_mean + GRECO | h_mean + h_sd + alt_mean + GRECO |
| R² synthétique (corrigé de ψ) | 0,69 | 0,83 |
| Efficacité relative globale | 2,26 | 3,38 |
| RSE médiane FH / direct | 8,7 % / 10,2 % | 8,2 % / 11,1 % |

- **Contrôle national :** PV 4,21 m³/ha/an sur 2019-2023, soit 78 % de la référence IGN (5,4). Le biais bas est documenté ; un test verrouille la fourchette 70-100 %.
- **Autocorrélation spatiale :** I de Moran par contiguïté de 0,16 à 0,34 sans effet régional. Avec la **GRECO en effet fixe** (décision du 2026-10-01), elle n'est plus significative ; seule 2020 est limite (p ≈ 0,04 sur 6 tests).

## Points d'attention

- **IR5 manquant :** depuis 2014, environ 52 % des arbres n'ont pas d'IR5. Ils sont imputés, et leur circonférence passée est recalculée depuis le taux imputé. Sans ce recalcul, l'arbre sortait de la somme sans aucun message ; un test le verrouille.
- **Ce qui reste en estimation directe :** les groupes feuillus et résineux, les niveaux GRECO et national, et les campagnes 2005-2018.
- **Jeu GEDI non comparé :** il attend un accès Earthdata (lot 1-ter).
- **Aucun indicateur ne change de comportement.** P2, `completer_volume_ifn()` et E1 brancheront ces fonctions aux lots 2 à 4.

## Tests

`devtools::test()` en local : 11 292 réussis, 0 échec, 0 erreur, 19 sautés.
