body:
The original sweep treated balance growth as collectible rewards, so purchases could be swept, and holder contributions continued after the milestone. This replaces that path with explicit reporter-authorized collections and permanently ends holder collection when the authenticated endowment coin vault directly holds 200M PENIS. Net direct donations count toward that goal; LP holdings and cumulative purchase totals do not.

## Review sequence and dependencies

| Package | Scope | Dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [PR 1](https://github.com/The-Endowment/endowment/pull/1) | Participation-count invalidation | Independently reviewable against contract `main` |
| [PR 2](https://github.com/The-Endowment/endowment/pull/2) | Direct-vault completion and V4 reporter-authorized collection | Stacked on PR 1; review its incremental diff |
| [PR 3](https://github.com/The-Endowment/website/pull/1) | Reporter service, website consent/exit and daily monitoring | Website `main`; release coordination with contract PR 2 |

This is package **2 of 3**, opened as a draft for developer review. Review the final branch diff and current documents. Some earlier commits in the stack contain superseded design drafts; the current V4 implementation and this description define the proposed behavior. After PR 1 merges, retarget PR 2 to `main`; if PR 1 is squash-merged, rebase PR 2 to remove duplicate PR 1 changes. Refresh upstream and rerun affected checks after integration. Merging these PRs does not authorize deployment or enabling collection.

## Approved behavior and trust model

- The pledge covers **all verified StonkFun rewards paid in PUMP** while enrolled and funding is active, including PUMP rewards generated by other coins. The service excludes existing balances, purchases, ordinary transfers, other reward mints, and already-paid inactive-period receipts.
- Activation is 30% committed; pause below 25%; resume at 30%. Exactly 25% does not trigger the lower-threshold pause. Counts are sampled, not continuous proof of holdings. Existing freshness, pause, retirement, market/token and capacity checks still apply.
- There is deliberately **no per-wallet daily cap**. Remaining SPL allowance and the existing treasury inventory capacity (three days of configured buy capacity) still constrain transfers. That treasury constraint is separate from a daily wallet cap.
- Only spendable PENIS in the authenticated direct vault counts toward the fixed 200M goal (`200_000_000_000_000` base units). Completion is permanent; existing treasury funds and future treasury yield can continue through the buy/liquidity path.
- **Reporter classification is trusted.** The contract verifies authorization and bounds, not receipt provenance. An incorrect or compromised reporter can collect other PUMP. Source-balance equality does not prevent spending/rebuying to the same balance between observation and execution. Daily reconciliation is diagnostic, not authorization or proof of correct individual debits.
- Collection can transfer only to the derived endowment PUMP vault. This instruction gives the reporter no destination selection or PENIS withdrawal power. Retained program upgrade authority remains a separate power to replace the rules.

## Contract changes and reviewer map

| Area | Files / checks |
| --- | --- |
| Authorized collection | `instructions/collect_reward.rs`, `reports.rs`: reporter signer, instance/source/destination identities, positive explicit amount, consent ID, next nonce, collection/reporter epochs, expected source balance and expiry of at most 120 seconds |
| Completion | `state.rs`, `instructions/buyback.rs`, `instructions/collect_reward.rs`: direct-vault completion is latched before any holder debit, including when reached through a donation |
| Consent and replay | `instructions/register_landlord.rs`, `instructions/resync_baseline.rs`, `state.rs`: owner-signed enrollment/renewal, config-wide monotonic consent IDs, monotonic report nonces; closing/recreating an enrollment cannot resurrect reports |
| Invalidation | `instructions/count.rs`, `pause.rs`, `roles.rs`: count completion, pause, parameter application and refresher invalidation advance collection generations |
| Reporter governance | `instructions/reporter.rs`: initialization, timelocked replacement, emergency disable and recovery |
| Legacy paths | `lib.rs`, `instructions/sweep.rs`: legacy sweep, registration and baseline-resync reject; historical baseline data no longer authorizes collection |

The implementation rejects an oversized report instead of silently clipping its signed amount. Failed transfers do not consume the nonce or record contributions. Accounting records actual net treasury receipt separately from the holder debit. A goal-reaching no-op may succeed without transferring funds or advancing the report nonce; the paired service must distinguish it from a contribution.

Full design, policy, accepted limitations and acceptance scenarios: [docs/reward-routing-v1.md](https://github.com/The-Endowment/endowment/blob/4b37a60b81f0e71b698961c3de4d611b052e4790/docs/reward-routing-v1.md).

## Consent, governance and compatibility

V4 preserves Config/Landlord allocation sizes and previous field offsets by consuming reserved bytes. It requires fresh V4 configuration/consent and an initialized reporter policy. **There is no migration instruction for a live V3 configuration, and old approvals are not fresh consent.** Review the deployment/migration plan separately; matching allocation size does not make a live V3 upgrade safe.

Consent is ongoing. Joining V4, leaving/rejoining or voluntarily renewing requires an owner signature. Ordinary pause/resume and reporter replacement after enrollment do not require every holder to sign again; they invalidate pending collection authorizations. The consent ID is not a permanent binding to one reporter key. Owner revoke/exit remains independent of reporter authorization.

Reporter replacement uses a 72-hour timelock, one-day admin apply grace and seven-day proposal expiry. Admin/current reporter can disable immediately; the guardian retains only its existing bounded pause. Repeated disable is a no-op after authorization and cannot veto a subsequent replacement proposal. Restart requires a new timelocked proposal. Admin renunciation permanently freezes reporter replacement/recovery, even for pending proposals; it does not remove the separate Solana program upgrade authority.

## Adversarial findings fixed in the new implementation

| Finding | Fix and recheck |
| --- | --- |
| A disabled reporter could keep cancelling its replacement | Idempotent disable preserves a later recovery proposal; independent LiteSVM reproduction verifies replacement after 72 hours and rejection of the old reporter |
| Guardian could bypass its bounded pause with indefinite reporter disable | Restrict indefinite disable to admin/current reporter; guardian rejection verified |

These findings concerned the new reporter implementation and are not attributed to the original developer. Separate agents reviewed the code, fresh agents implemented fixes, and the original reviewers rechecked them. This is scoped AI-assisted review, not independent professional audit certification.

## Validation and review targets

```sh
./scripts/test.sh
```

**34 unit + 132 integration tests = 166 passing**, both test/production SBF builds and IDL generation. Tested code commit: `834739e8283fe2568461f9bcf125902326e6dd1b`; the later `4b37a60` commit changes review-status documentation only. Environment: Rust/Cargo 1.89, Solana CLI 3.1.10 / platform-tools 1.52, Anchor 1.1.2. Known deployment-key mismatch and older-toolchain syscall warnings remain release-validation items; the source program ID was not changed.

Key regressions: `tests/regressions/completion.rs`, `reported_rewards.rs`, `reporter_recovery.rs`, plus PR 1's count regressions. Review wrong signer/account substitution, cross-instance isolation, consent closure/recreati

author: royin001
body:
## What this changes

This PR replaces the top bar's section and level switches with one switch, as the owner decided on 2026-10-01 (docs/DECISIONS.md). Before, they were two identical pill groups with Home among the sections.

- **Home:** the ORBITLAB mark and name lead home. There is no Home tab.
- **Wide screen:** a tab per section, with the current level shown as a badge on the current tab.
  - Pressing any tab opens the menu of that section's levels, one line each on what the level holds.
  - Code: `src/ui/section-nav.ts`, with the model in `src/ui/section-nav-model.ts`.
- **Phone (≤ 640 px):** one button showing the current section and level, which opens a table of sections × levels.
- **Thai level names:**
  - **รับชม:** the launch section's first level only.
  - **พื้นฐาน:** the other sections' first level.
  - **ทดลอง:** the second level everywhere. It was สำรวจ, which reads as Earth observation elsewhere in the app.
  - **วิศวกร:** unchanged.
  - Every Thai string that named a level the old way was updated, including two that #59 added.
- **English and Russian:** the Orbit and Build first level is called Basics / Основы.
- **Campaign tab:** marks the section still to come (roadmap X01, X02). Its menu lists those items; it has no route yet.
- **Unchanged:** route keys and every address (`#/launch/explore`, …), so shared links still open.

## How it was tested

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npx vitest run`: the full regular suite passed (9 550 tests in 216 files) after main was merged in up to #36. A re-run on the merge with #59 and #57 is in progress.
- `tests/section-nav-model.test.ts` (new) checks:
  - the switch's sections;
  - the level names per section;
  - every key exists in en, ru and th;
  - the Campaign items match roadmap phase 6;
  - a guard that fails if Thai text names a level by its old name.
- Also green: `tests/i18n.test.ts`, `tests/section-plan.test.ts`, `tests/app-mode.test.ts`, `tests/architecture.test.ts` and `tests/bundle-budget.test.ts`.
- `node tests/browser/run.mjs mobile-smoke` passes in Thai and Russian on all four pages. The journey now opens the phone's table and checks that every link is:
  - on screen;
  - exposed as a link;
  - named in the page's language;
  - uniquely named.
- Screenshots at 1440, 1280, 900 and 390 px: no sideways scroll, no page errors.
- `npm run budget`: ok. The CSS is 164.6 kB of main's 165 kB ceiling.

## What reviewers should look at

- **`src/ui/section-nav.ts`, how menus open and fold.** They change in place (`fold()`) instead of redrawing the switch, because a level link removed from the page during its own click would not navigate. The route change redraws the switch afterwards.
- **`src/ui/lessons/lesson-mode.ts`, which link is current.** It now reads the switch's `data-current-section` and `data-current-level`. Before, it compared every level link with `body[data-mode]`, which is `home` in the Orbit and Build sections.
- **English and Russian names.** Basics / Основы apply the owner's Thai reasoning to the other two languages. If Watch / Просмотр should stay, it is a one-line change per dictionary.
- **`#topbar` stacking.** It now has `position: relative; z-index: 46`, so the menus open over the lessons page (z-index 45).
- **The new mark (#57) inside the link home.** The link's hover background is passed to the mark (`--logo-ground`), so the gap under the orbit matches the hover background.

## Checklist

- [x] Built-in flights unchanged: no fingerprint or golden re-recorded, or re-recorded with the reason written beside the golden and a note in docs/VALIDATION.md §9
- [x] en/ru/th dictionaries complete (tests/i18n.test.ts green)
- [x] No new runtime dependency; a dev dependency only with a written reason
- [x] A physics or data change cites its published source and adds or updates its test (no physics or data change)
- [x] Docs updated where they describe the change (README, USER-GUIDE, DECISIONS)
- [x] Probe and scratch files deleted; no evidence binaries committed (no tracked file over 1 MB outside public/)
- [x] Session notes under docs/history/<date>/ when the session produced findings (none beyond the decision row in DECISIONS.md)
- [x] One line added to CHANGELOG.md
- [x] Targeted tests run and named above
- [x] For a UI change, the affected browser journey passes

author: henrycgbaker
body:
## Summary

Template settings get the three `?` hints from 0024 rule 12, and the demo's failing Student version on assignment 1 is traced. The failure is the template's content, not the engine: `solution/solution.py` on the `solution` branch of `assignment-1-f2025` (and `-f2026`) has no `### BEGIN SOLUTION` / `### END SOLUTION` fences, so derive correctly refuses to write the model answer onto main. Checking every demo template turned up one real engine bug: a blank file (the project templates' empty `src/__init__.py`) was refused because it has no fence, so those templates could never derive. Blank files are now copied as they are. The refusal text now names only the fences the file's format can carry and says what to do.

## Contract

0024 rule 12 (template settings hints; the failing derive). No contract change: `NO_SOLUTION_REGION` keeps its code; only its text grows by one sentence.

## The failing derive

- Run 36855342687 (11:26Z): `assignment.derive_starter` preview on `assignment-1-f2025` returned `failed` with `NO_SOLUTION_REGION`: `solution/solution.py` has no fenced region.
- Run 36853238612 (11:06Z) was not a derive. It was the `assignment.generate_syllabus` preview on `course-materials-f2025`, and it worked. Its public `dsl-outcome` annotation is cut by GitHub at 4096 characters (the syllabus `block` is longer), so it does not parse; `ops/outcome.py` caps at 60 000 bytes on the belief that the limit is 64 KB. The console falls back to the private outcome file. Not changed here: lowering the cap would cut the block the console shows unless the console prefers the private record. Flagged for the coordinator.
- What is wrong with assignment 1 (both semesters): the template was set up before derive existed. `main` carries a hand-written `starter.py`; `solution` carries `solution/solution.py`, an unfenced model answer. Even fenced, derive would write `solution.py` onto main next to the stale `starter.py`. Fix in the template: rename it to `solution/starter.py` and fence each answer (and the short answers at the bottom) with `### BEGIN SOLUTION` / `### END SOLUTION`.

## Every demo template (local run of the derive path over `git clone --depth 1 -b solution`)

| repo | would derive | why not |
|---|---|---|
| assignment-1-f2025 | no | `solution/solution.py` has no fences; also named `solution.py` while main holds `starter.py` |
| assignment-1-f2026 | no | same file as f2025 |
| assignment-2-f2025 | yes | |
| assignment-2-f2026 | no | `solution/solution.ipynb` has no fences and no `solution` cell tags; also named `solution.ipynb` while main holds `starter.ipynb` |
| assignment-3-f2025 | no | `solution/src/data.py` and `solution/src/pipeline.py` have no fences (`__init__.py` now passes) |
| assignment-3-project-f2026 | no | same as assignment-3-f2025 (identical tree) |
| assignment-4-f2026 | yes | |
| assignment-5-f2026 | yes | |
| assignment-6-f2026 | yes | |
| assignment-7-f2026 | yes | |
| assignment-8-f2026 | yes | (notebook and LaTeX) |

No demo repo was changed.

## Decisions

- The Student version `?` avoids "hand-out" (vocabulary forbids "handout") and does not repeat the page `?`: "Derive builds the main branch, the copy students get, from the solution branch, removing the marked answers. Run it after every change to the solution." The old sentence under the h3 is folded into it.
- The "Points per question" note under the table drops its first sentence (now in the `?`) and keeps the "marked from another file" one.
- `Questions` is also rendered by `NewAssignment.tsx`, so its `?` and the shortened note appear in the new-assignment wizard too.
- A blank solution file is copied rather than refused: it holds no answer, so rule 1 of `derive.py` does not apply to it.
- A file such as the project's `data.py` that students should get unchanged still has to carry a fence; there is no "copy as is" marker. Left as a design question.

## Tests

- `tests/test_derive.py`: blank file copied and the run is green; a `.py` refusal names only the region fence and says what to do; a notebook's names the cell tag and no chunk.
- `console/test/screens.test.tsx`: the three hints present, the student-version sentence in one place.
- vitest: `Tests  582 passed (582)`; `npm run build`: `built in 212ms`; pytest: `4888 passed, 2 skipped`.

## Doc audit

`docs/03-add-assignment-to-course.md` and `docs/reference/actions-reference.md`: the "nothing fenced is never written" rule now notes that a blank file is copied as it is.

## Feedback

> Template settings: `?` on "How it is marked", on "Points per question" and on "Student version". The demo's failing derive on assignment 1 is a bug to find.

author: hopkinsonchris-eng
body:
Wave 3, PR 4: what Chris's first live session turned up (recorded in `docs/vault-hub/wave3/06-decision-log.md`, "First live use").

## 1. World Monitor earns its money
The adapter had been written to the endpoint names without their published schemas (deviation 5 in the wave 3 decision log), so events and headlines came back empty and the panel showed one line. This PR reads `api.worldmonitor.app/openapi.json` shapes exactly: epoch-millisecond timestamps (0 is "not set"), `country_codes` and the headline bucket keyed by country, `occurredAt` and `actors[]` on ACLED events, enum names without their prefixes, and 403 reported as Pro-gated per endpoint.

- `src/intel/worldmonitor.ts`: fifteen country readers: instability index (score, trend, components, sanctions), World Monitor's intel brief with sources and evidence (Pro), coverage timeline (Pro), headlines, ACLED and UCDP events, HAPI totals, energy profile (JODI oil and gas, electricity mix), tanker traffic by port, country facts, travel advisories, sanctions pressure (Pro), resilience index (Pro), internet outages, intelligence timeline (Pro). Hourly cache per endpoint and country; 429 honoured; nothing simulated.
- `src/api/intel.routes.ts` (new): `GET /api/countries/:code/intel` serves every section as its own `{ok,data}` or `{ok:false, reason, pro}`, so a Pro-gated or failed section never hides the rest; `?sections=` narrows it. Public scope, audited with what answered.
- Hub: a Country intelligence card under the country panel with the sections above; Pro-gated ones say "Needs World Monitor Pro", failed ones say why. No browser request goes to worldmonitor.app (asserted).
- The brief's LIVE RISK block gains trend, sanctions, energy figures and World Monitor's evidence, cited as `[wm:energy:XX]` and `[wm:evidence:<id>]`; a Pro-gated brief is named in the meta.

## 2. Fields outside the project's country
A Venezuelan project had a field attached at 35.85, −119.52 (Kern County, California).
- `src/assets/geo.ts` (new): point-in-country from the same polygons the globe draws; `locationCheck` compares a record's point (or, without one, its gazetteer country) with the project's country. Coarse polygons mean a coastal miss is never evidence.
- `POST /api/projects/:id/assets` and the review-queue accept answer `409 outside_country` with the check until the caller sends `confirm_outside: true`. `GET …/assets` carries `location_check`; `GET /api/countries` carries `outside` per field.
- Hub: the Fields card and the country panel flag "outside Venezuela: this location is in United States of America"; candidates from another country say so; Attach asks ("This location is in … not …") and offers "Attach anyway".

## 3. Archive a project (hide, never delete)
AGENTS.md rule 9. A partner archives from the project file after a confirmation; the project leaves Today, the globe, the register and Cmd+K (server-side in `GET /api/countries`, client-side on the lists); every record stays; the file opens by id with a banner and a Restore button.

## Not in this PR
"The system should spend the next hour populating its Vault about the project and its fields" is per-field research (F13 miners, F14 web search), which W3-D2 did not choose. It is a new wave with its own Gate 1; I am asking Chris the gate questions separately.

## Evidence
- Vault: 401 tests (1 pre-existing skip), typecheck clean, schema fixtures current. Root: 82. Playwright: 146 passed.
- No secrets in served files (AC12); public pages unchanged vs main (AC13).
- Screenshot: `docs/vault-hub/evidence/w3-country-intel.png`; three wave 3 screenshots re-rendered because the fixtures now carry the new fields.

body:
## Summary
Refactored step management logic into a reusable custom hook to improve code organization and maintainability.

## Key Changes
- Created new `useInternshipSteps` hook in `app/hooks/steps.ts` that encapsulates step data and calculations
- Moved `Step` interface and `StepStatus` type to the new hook module
- Moved default steps data from `app/page.tsx` to the hook as `DEFAULT_STEPS`
- Hook provides computed values including current step, progress percentage, and step counts
- Updated `app/page.tsx` to remove inline step definitions
- Reset `hoursLogged` to 0 in placeholder data

## Implementation Details
The `useInternshipSteps` hook uses `useMemo` to efficiently compute:
- Current step index and step object
- Count of completed steps
- Overall progress percentage (0-100)
- Total step count

This allows components to easily access step state and progress metrics without duplicating logic.

author: bumblebiber
body:
## Why

team-up moves skills from the main agent to specialists to keep the main agent's context small. But some skills belong only to the main agent (memory, dispatch), some belong to everyone (caveman), and some belong only to specialists. Before this PR that split existed only by accident. This PR makes it explicit and enforced.

## What

### 1. Three skill layers (`team-up-scope`)
- A skill declares its layer in frontmatter (under `metadata:`). A package can also declare it with `"scope"` in `capability.json`. If the two disagree, the package is refused with `CAPABILITY_SCOPE_CONFLICT`.
- **main**: can only be enabled `--for host`. It is refused at capsule build (even if the assignment file is hand-edited), and a specialist bundle cannot ship it.
- **specialist**: can never be enabled `--for host`.
- **unscoped**: works as before.
- All supervisor skills in this repo (`dispatch`, `pipeline`, `pass-to`, `roster`, `roster-refresh`, `team-up-manage`, and the new `intake`) are now marked `main`.

### 2. `--for host`: shared skills as one copy
- `host` is a new assignment target. It is independent of `all`, because `all` means every specialist, not the host.
- Enabling a package for `host` symlinks its skill directories from the pool into `~/.claude/skills`. `TEAM_UP_HOST_SKILL_ROOTS` takes a list of directories for hosts with more than one CLI.
- The link points host → pool. Linked files are made read-only.
- Because a link makes the pool editable from the host, the launcher now recomputes each pool package's checksum before a launch and refuses `CAPABILITY_TAMPERED` if it changed. Before this, nothing checked the pool at launch.
- A host entry that team-up did not create is never replaced. The enable fails with `HOST_SKILL_COLLISION` and nothing is recorded. That only blocks the package that collides; enables and disables of other packages keep working.
- Only skills can be linked. A package that also carries plugins, MCP servers or frameworks gets `HOST_LINK_UNSUPPORTED`.
- `disable --for host` removes the link, `rollback` moves it, `capability list` shows `host_links`, and `doctor` accepts `host` as a target.

### 3. `auto_invoke`: the launcher opens the prompt with a skill
- A package can list one of its skills in `auto_invoke`. The launcher then puts that skill's invocation (`/caveman` in Claude Code) at the start of the worker prompt, before the mailbox protocol. This happens on every launch; it does not rely on the main agent remembering to ask for it.
- At most one skill per launch can do this; a second one fails with `AUTO_INVOKE_CONFLICT`.
- A harness whose adapter has no invocation syntax gets no prefix. `STATE.json` then records `auto_invoke.applied: false` and why. Codex is in this group on purpose, because its syntax is not verified.
- `style.caveman` is now **1.1.0**: scope `shared`, `auto_invoke: ["caveman"]`. The skill also gains a rule that uncertainty markers, negations and sources count as substance, not filler.

### 4. Intake: results someone actually reads
- `team-up runs uncollected [--days N | --all] [--json]` lists done or failed runs from the last 7 days (or all, with `--all`) that nobody has collected. It exits 1 when something is waiting.
- `team-up runs collect <id> [--note]` sets `state.collected`. Only finished runs can be collected.
- The new main-only skill `intake` is the procedure between the two: read the result, check it against evidence, decide, write one curated memory entry, mark it collected.
- This closes the open risk in `PLAN.md` (a result nobody picks up after the session dies).

### Other
- Version 0.4.0 in `src/cli.mjs`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `plugin.json`. The bump is needed so the host plugin sees the new `skills/intake` directory.
- Docs updated: `docs/specialists.md` (new "Three skill layers" and "Skills the launcher invokes" sections), `README.md`, `capabilities/README.md`, `PLAN.md`, `catalogue.json`.

## Testing

author: steamnoid
body:
The guard was in the wrong place and **its own reasoning said so.** The inventory refused an empty list because "a missing credential, a missing permission and a repository with issues disabled all produce an empty list."

That was true of the shape and false of the remote. **GitHub answers 401, 403 and 410 for those three,** and the reader already raises `TheIssuesCouldNotBeReadError` at or above 400. The refusal was re-deciding, one layer above the code that actually knew, a question the code below it had already answered.

### It is also what stopped the copy from ever starting

Forty-three merged pull requests and zero issues is this repository's ordinary state, and **an empty backlog is exactly what a project nobody has briefed looks like.** A rule that says a briefing must begin from a non-empty backlog cannot be run by the first repository to use it, and nobody picks that on purpose.

### What the guard protected survives

A run must not claim it checked for duplicates when it looked at nothing, and it still cannot — a read that failed is refused by the reader, the one place that saw the status code. `issues_read_from_the_remote` is the trace of that having happened, and it is false by default because a caller that builds an inventory by hand has read nothing.

**The generalisable half:** a refusal is only as good as the layer that made it. Here it sat one layer above the code that already knew the answer, and the cost of that was a repository that could never start.

author: ashwani1611
body:
Production deployments repeatedly left the web container unhealthy because Gunicorn's 30-second default killed workers while the CPU-contended host was importing the Django URL graph. This raises the production Gunicorn timeout to 120 seconds, adds a 60-second graceful timeout, and gives the container health check a 120-second startup grace period with 24 retries.

Evidence: two exact-main deployment attempts reached the new web container and failed as unhealthy; the first logged WORKER TIMEOUT/SIGKILL. The service later recovered and returned HTTP 200, showing delayed startup rather than an application exception. No staging deployment is included.

author: lemire
body:
Fixes #2897.

`key_selector<...>::describe()` was declared `static constexpr std::string` unconditionally, but `key_selector` is enabled whenever concepts are supported. With a standard library lacking constexpr `std::string` (e.g. libstdc++ 11):

- Clang 14/15 + libstdc++ 11: any use of `key_selector` fails with `constexpr function's return type 'std::string' is not a literal type`.
- GCC 11: `ondemand_object_find_field_tests.cpp` fails on the `static_assert` over `describe()`.

Changes:
- Add `SIMDJSON_CONSTEXPR_STRING` to `compiler_check.h` (`constexpr` when `__cpp_lib_constexpr_string >= 201907L`, empty otherwise; overridable).
- Use it for `describe()` and its helpers `append_uint`/`append_byte`.
- Guard the compile-time `static_assert` in the test; the runtime check of the output still runs everywhere.
- Document the requirement in the doc comment and `doc/basics.md`.

Tested: GCC 11.4 (Ubuntu 22.04) now builds and passes `ondemand_object_find_field_tests`; Apple clang still passes with the `static_assert` active.

Note: Clang 14/15 still cannot use `key_selector` for an unrelated reason (nested consteval calls through reference parameters, `key_selector.h:216`); that is out of scope here.

author: ptrio42
body:
A post can appear locally even when no relay has accepted it. If delivery fails, Wisp offers no manual retry, so the user ends up with a note that is not visible anywhere.

This PR saves public posts before sending and adds **Rebroadcast** to own-post menus in the feed, profile and thread. Retrying sends the same signed event, preserving its ID, timestamp, content, tags and signature.

- Show each relay's acceptance, rejection reason, send failure or missing confirmation.
- Remove recovery payloads after an accepted OK or an identical relay copy with a verified ID and signature. Already confirmed posts do not enter recovery storage. Keep at most 100 compact receipts without post content.
- Isolate storage and pending operations by account. Account changes and PoW cancellation stop previous work while retaining saved payloads.
- Complete composition after durable storage succeeds. Later results cannot close another screen or clear a newer draft, including during first-post onboarding.

Retry remains manual after reconnect or restart. Private replies, DMs and scheduled posts keep their existing delivery paths.

author: mfagerstrom
body:
## Summary
- `waitForReply` no longer takes Discord's "<app> is thinking..." placeholder for the reply. It
  waits, up to `TIMING.replyMs`, until the newest message is something else, for slash
  commands and components alike, and checks again after the settle in case a component's
  placeholder shows up late. Testing PR #1425, the runner pressed Check about 4 seconds after
  `/game-completion delete` while the placeholder was still up, so the conductor judged
  "No output observed".
- The runner now scrolls the message panel while it acts. Reading the newest reply
  (`newestText`, `newestWith`) scrolls to the bottom first. Finding the step message
  (`findStepMessage`, used by Check and `pendingVerdict`) scrolls up a screen at a time, at
  most 10 screens. Discord renders only a window of messages, so a tall reply can push the
  conductor's message out of the DOM.
- Adds a learning log entry and two lessons, plus a unit test for the placeholder check.

## Testing

### Step 1: Open the delete picker
```
/game-completion delete
```
Expected: An ephemeral completion list with a select menu whose placeholder reads "Select a completion to delete".
Ephemeral: yes
Changes data: no

## Judgment calls
- The Testing step is the one that failed on #1425. The bot code is the same as main, so this
  step exercises the runner: run `npm run -s conduct:playwright -- <this PR>` from this
  branch's checkout, and the step should pass without a hand-back.
- The scrolled element is found from the `Messages in` list by walking up to its first
  ancestor with `overflow-y: auto|scroll` that overflows, not by Discord's CSS class names,
  per the selector rule at the top of `discord.ts`.
- Scrolling stops at 10 screens (`SCROLL_SCREENS`). A step message further up than that is
  from a run old enough that the runner should hand it back, not go looking.
- `currentStep` and `reportUrl` never scroll. They run in the per-second polls that wait on
  the conductor and on a handed-back step, and scrolling there would move the panel under a
  tester doing the step by hand. The conductor posts the next header and the report at the
  bottom, so those reads do not need to look up.
- `findStepMessage` returns null instead of throwing, so `pendingVerdict` (called outside the
  step's try block in `runStep`) cannot crash the walk. Only Check turns a missing message
  into a hand-back that names it.
- The runner scripts sit outside `tsconfig.json`'s `src` include, so `tsc --noEmit` does not
  cover them. I type-checked `scripts/conduct-playwright` separately with a scratch config
  that extends the repo's, and it was clean.

## Self review
- Pass 1 (`code-review` high): 3 findings, 2 held.
  - Fixed: `currentStep` and `reportUrl` scrolled the panel on every poll, including during a
    15-minute hand-off, moving it under the tester. Polling reads no longer scroll.
  - Fixed: a test line was exactly 100 characters.
  - Resolved by the first fix: `currentStep` parsed headers twice after scrolling, and that
    code is gone.
- Pass 2 (`code-review` high): 1 finding, held and fixed. After `findStepMessage` scrolled
  up, the panel stayed there, so `check()`'s polls could miss the next header posted at the
  bottom and hand back a step that passed. `pendingVerdict` and Check now return the panel
  to the bottom (`scrollToBottom`) once they are done with the step message.
- Pass 3 (`code-review` high): no findings.

## Checklist
- [x] Type-check passes (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] Lint passes (`npm run lint`)
- [x] Tests pass (`npm test`)

Closes #1435

author: eliahilse
body:
## Summary

With the opt-in `experimentalWorkerOpen`, the first-page preview is laid out from a cut of the document (its first 200 body blocks). The last pages of that layout can differ from the full document's, because content past the cut is missing (keep-with-next chains, widow and orphan control, notes, floats). The preview now shows only pages that the full layout lays out the same:

- A prefix pass that stops before the cut fixes its first `provisionalPages` pages. A pass that reaches the cut fixes all but its last two pages.
- The resident worker keeps that limit for the preview session, so later `buildFrame` and `buildPages` requests and background page slices stay within it until the full document replaces the preview.
- When the cut holds the whole body, `open_preview` reports `wholeBody` and the worker-open path lays the preview out as the whole document, so short documents keep their preview pages.
- `onFirstPagePainted` fires once a built page is presented.

Page-count fields (`NUMPAGES`) in a partial or prefix layout are unchanged here: they render empty until layout completes, as on main. A follow-up renders them from the field's cached result, as Word does. The default path (without `experimentalWorkerOpen`) is unchanged.

## Evidence

Differential gate: each document is laid out twice, once through the worker preview chain (cut, prefix pass, display window) and once in full. Every page the preview builds is compared with the full layout's page, display list for display list. Lines holding a `NUMPAGES` field are compared separately and reported as page-count fields. Previews that build no page are counted on their own, not as passes.

| Set | Preview kind | Documents | Pages compared | Content mismatches | No final page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repo `.docx` corpus (98) | whole body | 70 | 110 | 0 | 0 |
| | cut | 27 | 54 | 0 | 0 |
| | refused | 1 (`wordprocessingml-comprehensive.docx`, as on main) | – | – | – |
| Synthetic stress set (113) | cut | 62 | 86 | 0 | 51 |
| Private ~880-page template | cut | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Private ~220-page document | cut | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Synthetic stress set, full open + 3-page prefix pass | – | 113 | 226 | 0 | 0 |

- The synthetic set is an ~800-page document plus 112 fixtures: 14 flavours (plain, keep-with-next, keep-with-next by style, widows, footnotes, endnotes, floats, early and final section breaks, inline fields, `NUMPAGES`, `STYLEREF`, TOC/`PAGEREF`) at font sizes 4 to 22 pt.
- The 51 previews with no final page are all cuts whose 200-block seed fit on one or two pages: every fixture at 4, 6 and 8 pt and 9 of 14 at 10 pt. These open with the full document's first frame.
- The private documents' previews keep the same two pages as on main.

### Timing

Real hardware (Apple silicon laptop, Chromium), warm open of the editor's worker-open flow, n=5 per arm, arms interleaved. Median (min–max) in ms; "first page" is the first page visible, "layout complete" the whole document laid out. Both arms showed the same two preview pages, and every run passed the open, propose, toggle and jump sequence with 0 errors.

| Document | Arm | First page | Layout complete |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Private ~880-page template | main | 918 (881–1321) | 5614 (5496–6306) |
| | this PR | 882 (875–921) | 5602 (5519–6141) |
| Private ~220-page document | main | 949 (919–1160) | 3585 (3514–3707) |
| | this PR | 944 (892–1008) | 3485 (3405–3519) |

The differences are within run-to-run noise; the preview shows the same pages on these documents, so neither clock moves.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test -p betteroffice-docx-edit preview` (new: `a_preview_reports_whether_its_cut_holds_the_whole_body`), `cargo clippy -p betteroffice-docx-edit --all-targets -D warnings` (VM)
- [x] `bun run build:docx-wasm`, `tsc` for `docx` and `docx-react` (VM)
- [x] `bun test --isolate` of `previewChain.parity.test.ts` (new), `residentEngineWorker.test.ts`, `workerOpen.test.ts`, `openPreview.test.ts`, `mediaTokens.test.ts`, `firstPagePainted.test.tsx`, `previewFailure.test.tsx`, `useYrsCoreSession.workerOpen.test.tsx`: 220 pass (VM)
- [x] Differential gate above (VM for the corpus and synthetic sets, local for the private documents)

## Review

- `residentEngineWorker.ts`: `previewFinalPages` is set to 0 right after a partial snapshot loads and to its final value at the end of `hydrate`. It is reset in `destroySession` and before each bootstrap and sync, and applied in `setFrameDisplayWindow` and to `buildPages`.
- `previewDisplayWindow.ts`: the two pure helpers that pick the final page count and clamp a display window.
- `crates/docx-edit/src/wasm.rs`: `wholeBody` is true when the parsed body has fewer blocks than the cut limit. The parser stops only once it holds the limit.

body:
## What

Testimonials and case studies are registered by this plugin again. Andrew, 2026-10-01: content types belong in each site's own plugin, not in AJR Core. AJR Core 0.15.2's `Testimonials` and `Case_Studies` are ported back with **every key unchanged**: post types, taxonomies, meta, the `ajr/testimonials` / `ajr/case-studies` / `ajr/case-study-card` blocks, markup, classes, `/case-studies/<name>/` and the `ajr_core_testimonial_text` filter. Nothing on the site migrates.

## Safe in either order

`Core\CoreModules` makes each class stand down while an older AJR Core still has its module on, so 1.15.0 can go live first and do nothing. It takes over when the module is switched off on AJR Core → Modules, or when AJR Core 0.16.0 (which removes the modules) is installed.

## Also in this PR
- Settings are `SETTINGS` constants with the folio's saved values (no archive; `/case-studies/` is a Page), behind `ajrwd_testimonials_settings` / `ajrwd_case_studies_settings`.
- **The release zip would have shipped without the blocks:** `release.yml` excluded `'blocks'`, which rsync matches at any depth, so `assets/blocks/` was dropped (dry run: 0 of 12 files; now 12 of 12). It is now `/blocks` and `/tests`.
- Rewrite rules: the activation hook registers the type before flushing. The deactivation hook unregisters it, then flushes. `heal_rewrite_rules()` (admin_init, administrators only) rebuilds the rules when the slug/archive signature changes, including the first time this plugin serves.
- Password-protected testimonials are left out of the slider (AJR Core printed them).
- Testimonials tell AJR Core's Markdown cache to drop page copies through `wpmai_flush_copies_for_post`.
- `Requirements`: the 1.9.0 "Core module off" error is gone, because off is the normal state now. The Featured Work warning has tests that can fail.
- A second PHPUnit suite (`phpunit-mocked.xml.dist`, WP_Mock) carries Core's ~40 tests for these classes. CI runs both suites, and PHPCS now covers `assets/`. PHP_CodeSniffer 3.13.6 (dev advisory).

## Proof
- **Parity on the folio DDEV site: 80/80 responses identical** between AJR Core serving the types and this plugin serving them. That covers 24 URLs (every page with the blocks, EN and DE, all 8 case studies, and home) in both optimised and un-optimised HTML, plus their `?format=markdown` copies, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, REST for both types and the tag taxonomy, `/case-studies/`, a 404 and a **freshly generated** sitemap. Only the asset folder, the handle names, `?ver=` and timestamps were normalised (each timestamp was proven to vary between two identical runs). Handover and rollback were both clean, and the local site was left as it was (Core's modules on).
- Unit tests 50 OK, WP_Mock tests 51 OK. A mutation of the stand-down guard fails exactly the two stand-down tests.
- PHPCS clean, php -l clean, FSE preflight theme+plugin: **0 FAIL**.
- Four reviewers (code-standards, build-security, build-seo, build-performance): **0 blocking**, and every advisory is fixed or recorded with a reason. The two block queries are not object-cached (identical to Core, already lean, and the site has no persistent object cache). block.json is parsed per request (needs a build step these blocks avoid).

- Live: nothing deployed (the folio deploy is on hold). Before the live handover, read live's AJR Core `case_studies.slug` / `case_studies.has_archive`. That needs Andrew's OK.
- AJR Core 0.16.0 (the removal) is a separate PR in `andrew-ajrwebdesign/ajr-core`.

author: keiran-biffo-fleet
body:
Refs #2188

Follow-up for the remaining scope the prosecutor found unaddressed while reviewing PR #2186 (verdict SURVIVES-INCOMPLETE: the PR covers part of its original claim, not all of it).

Original claim:

> core_api instance knobs: template-owned block reads instance vars (memory, warm capacity, timeout) and merges a user-owned core_api_instance_environment
> 
> Owner decision (2026-10-01, /clear-blocked; from keiranholloway/biffo-platform#217 and tabsii-com/tabsii-platform#1457): **instances customise the template-owned `module "core_api"` through knobs set in a user-owned file.**
> 
> ## Why
> `infra/environments/dev/core-api.core.tf` (#1538 option 2) made the whole `module "core_api"` block template-owned. Its adoption note says to re-home instance-specific arguments, "environment via `core_api_environment`", but `local.core_api_environment` lives in `core-api-environment.core.tf`, which is **also template-owned**. An instance has no channel for its own values. Live need, tabsii-platform's current block:
> - `memory_size = 512`;
> - `enable_warm_capacity = true` (SnapStart; tabsii-platform#1239 is tuning it);
> - `BIFFO_DB_SEARCH_PATH = "public,tabsii"`;
> - `BIFFO_SIMULATION_PERSONAS_PARAMETER_PATH = local.simulation_personas_path`.
> 
> biffo-platform's block has no extras: every argument matches the template.
> 
> ## Change
> 1. In `core-api.core.tf`, read instance knobs, each defaulting to today's template behaviour so instances without overrides are unchanged:
>    - `var.core_api_memory_size` (default: the compute module's current default);
>    - `var.core_api_enable_warm_capacity` (default `false`);
>    - `var.core_api_timeout` (default 300).
>    Declare these variables in a template-owned `core-api-variables.core.tf`.
> 2. Merge a user-owned extension last: `environment_variables = merge(local.core_api_environment, {…template keys…}, local.core_api_instance_environment)`. Define `local.core_api_instance_environment = {}` in a **user-owned** scaffold file, `infra/environments/dev/core-api.instance.tf`. `biffo core upgrade` seeds it if absent and never overwrites it, so record it as `seed` mode in core-manifest if that's how seeding is declared.
> 3. Update the adoption note: what goes in `core-api.instance.tf` and the tfvars, then delete your block.
> 4. `cli/src/lib/instance-adoption.ts` `core-api-module` pair: keep reporting unadopted instances; the message names the new file.
> 
> ## Done when (pre-merge)
> - `terraform validate` passes on the template tree.
> - An instance fixture with no overrides plans **no changes** to `module.core_api`.
> - A fixture setting memory 512, warm capacity and two env vars plans exactly those changes.
> 
> ## Verified after merge (fleet-owned)
> - The next `core-v` release ships it.
> - tabsii-platform#1457 adopts it (the instance values move into `core-api.instance.tf` and the tfvars, and the old block is deleted) with a no-op plan for `module.core_api`.

The spec says `biffo core upgrade` seeds `infra/environments/dev/core-api.instance.tf` if it is absent, never overwrites it, and records it as `seed` mode in `core-manifest.json`. None of that exists:
- `core-manifest.json` has no seed mode and no entry for the file.
- `core-upgrade.ts` only syncs template-owned paths.
- An instance that upgrades receives `core-api.core.tf`, which references `local.core_api_instance_environment`. Without the file, `terraform validate` and `plan` fail with "Reference to undeclared local value".

Needed:
- A seed mechanism in the manifest and in the upgrade: create the file if absent, never overwrite it.
- A test that an instance with no `core-api.instance.tf` is seeded by the upgrade.
- The `core-api-module` adoption pair should also flag a missing `core-api.instance.tf`, even when the instance's `main.tf` no longer declares `module "core_api"`.

author: inaridiy
body:
Observed on the production `my-agents` deployment after the 0.6.1 upgrade:

1. A harness container start did not answer; with no overall deadline on the boot, the turn waited about 15 minutes until the runtime ended the alarm, and the next attempt then started normally.
2. Meanwhile the sandbox idled out (10 minutes). The next proxied request started a new sandbox container, but nothing listened on 4500: Codex's exec-server only starts at the beginning of an execution. The turn continued without a shell ("I can't run shell commands") and wrote nothing.

The first is Cloudflare's (a start that never answers; see docs/cloudflare-containers.md), but waiting on it without a bound is ours. The second is a library bug regardless of the platform: a sandbox can be replaced at any time (idle stop, platform restart).

- `HarnessContainer.boot` fails after 3 minutes (`harness.boot`), so the lease destroys the container and the next attempt starts a new one.
- `SandboxContainer.serve` stores the command per port; a proxied request to a container that replaced the one that served it starts the command again and waits for the port (once per container).
- Container smoke: a new stage stops a completed session's sandbox and proxies to `sandbox.internal`; the new container answers.

Validation: `pnpm check`; `CF_SMOKE_HARNESSES=codex pnpm test:containers` (rootless recipe), all ten stages PASS including the new one.

body:
## Problem

The `navigate` action carries a Chatfuel `pathKey`. Only a handful of the keys the agent sends (`Deals`, `Contacts`, `Flows`, `Chats`, `Calendar`, `KnowledgeBase`) resolved in the shell. Everything else, including `FuelyAI*`, `KnowledgeBase*`, `Calendar*`, `Settings*`, `FlowID/<id>`, `ConversationID/<id>` and raw `/automation/<botId>/chats/<id>` paths, came back as "There is no … page here".

## Change

`content/shell/src/lib/shellBridge.ts`:
- Extends the alias table with the agent's page keys.
- Adds `resolvePathKey`, which handles three forms: plain names, `Name/<id>` (the name picks the module and the id becomes that module's deep-link param), and raw paths that start with `/` (the rightmost segment that names a page wins, and the segment after it is the id).
- Explicit `params` on the action still override params that come from the pathKey.
- If the target module is not installed, the key still resolves to nothing, as before.

## Mapping

| pathKey | Module | Deep-link params |
|---|---|---|
| FuelyAIAutomations, FuelyAIProfile, FuelyAITasksChats, FuelyAITasksOperations, FuelyAITasksReminders, FuelyAIComments, Keywords | automations | |
| AutomationID/<id> | automations | `automation=<id>` |
| FuelyAIBroadcasts | broadcasts | |
| KnowledgeBaseGeneral | knowledge-base | `source=profile` |
| KnowledgeBaseFAQ | knowledge-base | `source=faq` |
| KnowledgeBaseCatalog | knowledge-base | `source=products` |
| KnowledgeBaseSpecialists | knowledge-base | `source=team` |
| KnowledgeBaseGoogleCalendarSync | knowledge-base | |
| CalendarSettings, CalendarReminders, CalendarMessagesSource | bookings | |
| FlowID/<id> | flow-builder | `flow=<id>` |
| ConversationID/<id>, `/automation/<botId>/chats/<id>` | livechat | `c=<id>` |
| SettingsWhatsApp, SettingsInstagram, SettingsTikTok, SettingsFacebook, SettingsWebWidget (and `*Connect`) | channels | |

Keys without a matching wizard module stay unresolved.

## Tests

New cases in `shellBridge.test.ts` cover the keys above, id and source deep links, raw paths, the missing-module case, and explicit params overriding pathKey params. `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm validate` pass.

author: evoggy
body:
A write to the GPIO data register only reached the pins that were outputs at the time, and a write to the direction register re-initialises the pins without setting their level. Writing the level first and the direction after, which is the order that avoids a glitch, therefore leaves a new output at whatever its output latch last held, usually low. The readback of an output comes from the cached value, so it still says high.

For example, writing the data register with bit 2 set and then the direction register with bit 2 set leaves PA2 driven low, while reading both registers back gives output and high. Only a later data write, made once the pin is already an output, actually drives it high.

The data write now sets the output latch of every pin, inputs included. An input keeps the level and takes it when it is made an output, and the readback of an output matches the pin. Reads of inputs still come from the pin.

Hosts that set the direction first and the level after keep working as before, with the brief low they already have. Level-then-direction becomes glitch free.

Testing: built with `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build`. Not yet flashed to a deck controller.

#8 rewrites the same loop as `gpio_apply_data()`, so whichever is merged second needs the same change there (drop the `is_output` check).

author: wilfgrainger
body:
## Summary

Government Contracts now shows which UK nation (England / Scotland / Wales / Northern Ireland / Other-Unknown) each contract's supplier is based in, derived only from real structured data, plus a ranked-by-value supplier concentration view.

## What determines each contract's nation

Find a Tender's OCDS releases carry supplier organisations in \elease.parties[]\, each with an \ddress.postalCode\ field, cross-referenced from \ward.suppliers[].id\ (OCDS 1.1 OrganizationReference). This is a real field the upstream API returns today (confirmed against the API's own documented sample response) -- it was just not previously extracted.

\contracts/government-contracts.js\ adds \ukNationFromPostcode()\: a pure function mapping the postcode's leading AREA letters to a nation using the public Royal Mail/ONS postcode-area allocation (BT -> Northern Ireland; CF/SA/LL/etc -> Wales; EH/G/KY/etc -> Scotland; everything else well-formed -> England). Any missing, malformed, or unresolved postcode -- and anything that is not a genuine postcode -- defaults to **Other/Unknown**. Nation is never inferred from a supplier's name or any other heuristic; this is enforced by both collectors only ever reading \party.address.postalCode\.

Both collector paths (\worker/government-contracts-cloudflare.js\ and \scripts/prepare-government-contracts-ingest.mjs\) now build an id->postcode lookup from \elease.parties\ and resolve each award's \supplierNations\ from it.

## Breakdown view

\ uildSupplierConcentration()\ aggregates the existing 100 ranked awards by supplier (equal allocation across co-suppliers on the same award -- the same method already used for \summary.topSupplier\), ranked by total disclosed value. It never combines data from any other source. Nation is included as a secondary attribute/filter on the same view, and the UI states explicitly when every supplier resolves to Other/Unknown (today's live data has no postcode populated yet, since it was never collected before this change).

## Tests

- Postcode-to-nation mapping: one case per nation (Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, England) plus unrecognised and missing-postcode cases, all failing closed to Other/Unknown.
- Supplier concentration ranking is deterministic and reconciles to the award totals.
- Raw-OCDS-release normalisation resolves nations through the \parties\ cross-reference (not just the pre-shaped award object).
- Component tests for the fail-closed state, the Other/Unknown limitation notice, the ranked concentration view, and the nation filter control.

## Verification

- \
pm run lint\ -- clean on all touched files.
- \
px tsc --noEmit\ -- no new errors (two pre-existing baseline errors in this test file are unchanged, confirmed present on \main\ before this branch).
- \
px vitest run\ -- 564/564 passing (111 files), including \hosting:check\.
- \
px next build\ -- succeeds, including its own TypeScript pass.

## Limitation

Live production data has not yet collected this field (it required adding the \parties\ cross-reference, done here). The breakdown view will show Other/Unknown for every supplier until the next collection window runs with this code deployed -- the UI states this plainly rather than hiding it.

author: joakim-epp
body:
Calls to the customer service had no timeouts, so a hung customer service could block booking requests and the health endpoint indefinitely.

- `RestClientConfig` reads `customer.service.connect-timeout` (default 2s) and `customer.service.read-timeout` (default 10s). The docker profile maps them to `CUSTOMER_SERVICE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` and `CUSTOMER_SERVICE_READ_TIMEOUT`.
- `CustomerServiceHealthIndicator` adds a `latencyMs` detail to both UP and DOWN responses, so slow responses show up before they turn into timeouts.
- The health indicator tests assert the new detail.

author: r-log
body:
Part of #142 (D11) under #76. Tools only — `src/tests/tools/verbatim.py` — no core bytes, so no record run; the self-test is the proof. The named deletion of the aura-dummy handlers no 4.3.4 spell reaches (the next PR) needs the tool to rebuild a base across labels, sites and runs that the tree no longer holds; today it can only rebuild a base whose labels all still exist somewhere in the tree.

## What

- **Three spec mechanisms.** A site may list `deleted` labels: in the tree each must be neither registered nor standing; in a base its run is cut, from its label to the next label at that indent or the switch's close. A site may be `gone` whole, with the lines its switch opened and closed with: in the tree its dispatch, its typed table and any registered default must be absent; in a base the switch is cut with those lines. A file may list `cuts` of whole label runs outside any site. Cuts apply only to the rebuilt base, a base that no longer holds a cut passes, overlapping cuts fail, and the original-order spec keeps every label.
- **What a cut cannot do, after two review rounds.** A cut must start at a `case` line (never a `default:`, which is dead only with its whole switch), must not be one of a site's own labels, must be found once in the base, and must span exactly its run; a label whose run is cut must not be shared by the label above it, looking past blank and comment lines; and the code above the run must end in a terminator (`return`, `break`, `continue`, `goto`; for a braced run, the line inside its closing brace) that does not itself hang under a bare control header, so a cut can never change what the label above it runs. An if/else whose branches both return fails on the safe side. A comment line indented less than the label does not end a run. A deleted id that is not a label of its site fails with a reason, and a crash inside a self-test row fails the row.
- **Self-test: 74 → 138 rows** on generated fixtures, including every abuse shape the two reviews built: a cut of a body line, of a `return`, of a `default`; a shared body with a comment or blank between the labels; a run with no terminator above it, plain, one-line and braced, or whose terminator hangs under a bare `if` or `for`; a run holding a nested switch or a column-zero comment; a deleted label last before the close or standing twice in the base; a gone site whose dispatch, table or default still stands, whose switch does not open directly above its first label, or whose window runs past the file. Twenty-eight mutants of the new logic, each killed by named rows.
- **On the real tree** the spec and base are unchanged: `--check` IDENTICAL 65/65 bodies at 79 labels in 7 sites against the current base, the original switches and the tree's own commit. The deletion PR's tree, with its spec applied, reads IDENTICAL 56/56 at 72 labels in 5 sites with twelve cuts against the same bases, and the reviews' abuse shapes fail on it.

## What it does not do

It moves and deletes nothing. The deletion follows as its own PR, with the record.

author: ericpopivker
body:
## Problem

Some Google Meet clients deliver captions on a data channel named `captions_v2` instead of `captions`. The extension only listened to `captions`, so on those clients no transcript was captured.

## Changes

- **Listen to `captions_v2`**: added to `RTC_CHANNEL_NAMES` and routed to a new `handleCaptionsV2Message` in the interceptor.
- **Parse the v2 payload**: `parseCaptionMessageV2` reads the caption, which is nested one level deeper than in `captions`. The existing `decodeProtobuf` guesses string vs. nested message and flattens this payload into one string, so a new `decodeProtobufRaw` returns length-delimited fields as raw bytes and the parser reads each field explicitly.
- **Log unrecognized channels**: channels the extension does not handle now get a debug line per message, so the next channel rename is visible in the console.
- **Stop hiding Meet's caption overlay**: `caption-observer.ts` no longer calls `hideCaptionOverlay()`, so Meet's own captions stay visible on screen. The function itself is still defined but unused.
- **Notula merge driver**: `.gitattributes` gains the `merge=union` rule for `.notula/comments` logs (separate commit).

## Notes for review

- Most of the `caption-observer.ts` diff is formatting (single to double quotes, line wrapping). The only behaviour change in that file is the overlay no longer being hidden; viewing the diff with whitespace hidden does not help here, so look for the two removed `hideCaptionOverlay()` call sites.
- v2 captions are emitted with `langId: 0`, since the payload carries language as a string, not a numeric ID.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Verified manually in a Google Meet call that uses `captions_v2`.

author: gsusfc
body:
Related to #287 (closed). Since 2026-09-25, every Vault re-scan of a scored brand has failed at its first SV9 component. `mission` raises an `evidence_binding_failure` on tile M1, and the partial evaluation stops there, so Core never gives a single verdict on a re-scan:
- Saffron: 9fd70694fd6e, 550b63b78cb5.
- Primary: 24bc6a1d9424, 46ad24a16a04, 0e45993cd30e.

## Chain Context
- **Strategy:** stacked PRs to main. This is change **A** of the re-ordered S4a chain.
- **This PR, start → end:** from "the first failed component stops the evaluation" to "with the flag on, the remaining components are still evaluated". Off by default.
- **Depends on:** main. It is independent of #312; that PR is merged and deployed, and it touches different files.
- **Follow-ups:**
  1. B: request-scoped Core prompts, so mission itself binds; 2 PRs.
  2. S4a PR2: apply module and shared-analysis payload.
  3. S4a PR3: wiring behind the apply flag.
- **Out of scope:**
  - the binding misalignment itself (B);
  - any change to the authority outcome, score or publication;
  - turning the flag on in production.

```
main
 ├─ #312  v3 tile re-scan candidate contract (merged)
 └─ 📍 A   continue past a failed component (this PR)
     └─ B1/B2  request-scoped Core prompts
         └─ S4a PR2  apply module + shared-analysis payload
             └─ S4a PR3  wiring behind the apply flag (one brand)
```

## Summary
- **The flag.** `BRAND3_VAULT_SV9_CONTINUE_PAST_FAILED_COMPONENT_ENABLED` is off unless set to `"true"`. With it on:
  - The partial evaluation records a failed component as `{component_key, reason_code: "provider_failure"}` and keeps evaluating the remaining components. Each successful component still persists its own checkpoint.
  - `coherencia` needs every upstream judgment, so when anything failed it is skipped with `upstream_component_failed`.
  - Structural failures still stop the run.
  - The authority outcome keeps its status and reason codes, and adds `failed_components`. The scan phase mapping is unchanged.
  - Partial replay skips the recorded failed components.
- **Resume safety (with the flag on).** Before any fresh Core call, the run restores every component that already has a checkpoint. So a resumed scan never prepares a second Flow context and mixes it with the restored one. Otherwise later resumes would hit `shared checkpoint Flow context conflicts` and stay stuck.
- **Preparation failures.** The shared adapter remembers a failed Flow preparation instead of repeating its model calls on every continued component. It also no longer keeps a half-prepared candidate after a hydration failure, which could otherwise evaluate later components on empty inputs.
- **With the flag off,** the evaluation order and the outcome are byte-identical to main.

## Known limitations
- **The real shared-checkpoint restore path (`restore_shared_checkpoint_process`) is not covered by a test.** Every shared-series test fakes the flow. The ordering invariant is tested with fakes, and the restore code itself is unchanged. Enable the flag on Vault only together with a watched re-scan.
- **`failed_components` has no production reader yet.** S4a's guard will use it.
- **More Core calls.** With the flag on, a re-scan whose first component fails makes up to one evaluator call per remaining component, like a first scan.

## Test plan
- [x] `test_sv9_incremental_evaluation.py` and `test_evidence_vault_sv9_authority_evaluation.py`, plus the stabilization replay and scanner orchestration files: 239 passed
- [x] Non-database `test_sv9_*` and `test_evidence_vault_sv9_*`: 1181 passed, 11 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` on the 6 files
- [x] Mutation: disabling the restore-before-fresh-call pass fails only the ordering test
- [x] Mutation: `continue` back to `return` fails the continue test
- [x] Full suite in a clean worktree without the local `.env` (main plus these changes): 4966 passed, 75 skipped
- [ ] CI (PostgreSQL 16)

## Contributor checklist
- [ ] Linked approved issue: none; related to #287 (closed)
- [x] Added exactly one type:* label: type:feature
- [x] Shellcheck reviewed; no shell scripts changed.
- [x] No skills changed; no skill-specific test required.
- [x] Documentation impact reviewed; a flag that is off by default.
- [x] Conventional commit format.
- [x] No Co-Authored-By trailers.

author: niklas-struck-coder
body:
## Was war der Bug?

In `src/hooks/useConcierge.ts` plant `sendMessage()` einen 600ms-`window.setTimeout()`, um die simulierte Concierge-Antwort zu liefern. Dieser Timeout wurde nirgends gecleart.

## Warum ist es ein Bug?

Verlässt eine Nutzerin/ein Nutzer `/urlaubsmodus` (nutzt `useConcierge` über `Urlaubsmodus.tsx`) innerhalb der 600ms-"Denk"-Verzögerung nach dem Absenden einer Frage — z. B. durch Klick auf eine andere Sidebar-Seite — wird die Hook-Instanz unmounted, aber der Timeout feuert trotzdem und ruft die State-Setter (`setMessages`, `setAvatarState`, `setQuickReplies`, `setIsThinking`) der bereits verwaisten Instanz auf. Unnötige Arbeit/Speicherbindung durch einen hängenden Timer, exakt dasselbe Grundmuster wie der heute bereits gemergte Fix in `ChatInput.tsx` (Spracherkennung stoppte dort ebenfalls nicht beim Unmount).

## Was macht der Fix?

Spiegelt das in `ChatInput.tsx`/`KiChat.tsx` bereits etablierte Muster: Timeout-ID in einem `useRef` halten, in einem `useEffect`-Cleanup mit `window.clearTimeout()` aufräumen. Keine Verhaltensänderung für den normalen Sende-Ablauf. Neuer Regressionstest in `useConcierge.test.ts` prüft, dass `clearTimeout` beim Unmount mit ausstehendem Timeout aufgerufen wird.

## Wie sicher bin ich mir?

Sehr sicher, was die Korrektheit angeht — der Fix folgt 1:1 einem bereits im selben Code etablierten, heute erneut bestätigten Muster und ändert nichts an der sichtbaren Logik. Die Praxisauswirkung ist gering (in React 19 kein Crash/keine Konsolenwarnung bei State-Updates nach Unmount, nur ein unnötig weiterlaufender Timer), daher niedrige Priorität, aber ein eindeutiger, isolierter, risikoarmer Fix.

Testsuite konnte in dieser Umgebung nicht automatisch ausgeführt werden (`node_modules` nicht installiert, `npm install` ist für automatische Fixes nicht erlaubt) — Änderung stattdessen sorgfältig manuell gegen die Logik und das bereits bewährte `ChatInput.tsx`-Muster geprüft.

author: jonathankingston
body:
## Summary

Closes the residual recorded in decision A7: a guest shell command (same uid as the worker) could read the run's egress-proxy token from `/proc` and use it to open tunnels through the guest proxy.

- The token is no longer in any `docker create --env`. The host writes it as the first line of the container's stdin; `WORKER_ENTRYPOINT_SH` reads it and builds the proxy URL, so PID 1's `/proc/1/environ` never holds it.
- The worker is exec-ed from `/usr/local/bin/node-guarded`, a `0711` copy of node. A process whose executable its user cannot read is non-dumpable, which closes `/proc/<pid>/environ`, `/proc/<pid>/mem` and ptrace to same-uid shell children.
- No change to seccomp/AppArmor/caps; no user namespace.
- Still by design: an ACP agent's own shell children inherit the agent's token (A7 text amended to say so).

## Validation

Task brief: a shell child in the guest recovers no token, is refused `407` without one, and the worker still reaches the model.

- Before (live Docker 29.8, scripted run, probe as a normal shell child): token recoverable from `/proc/1/environ` and the worker's environ; `CONNECT` with it → `200`, `GET /v1/models` → `200`.
- After: new opt-in probe in `thread-container.integration.test.ts` (`COPSE_THREAD_CONTAINER_E2E=1`): nothing recovered, no-token CONNECT → `407`, worker egress still connects. The existing end-to-end test also passes.
- Unit: `dockerRunArgs` asserts the token is in no `--env` and not in the argv; entrypoint/Dockerfile assertions for the guarded node and the read-before-exec ordering.
- `pnpm run check` (full, security surface): 11704 tests, 0 failures, before the rebase onto `origin/main`; PR CI re-runs the full gate.
- ACP harness: `acp-container.integration.test.ts` (`COPSE_THREAD_CONTAINER_E2E=1`, Docker) passes; the agent still gets its token through its explicit env map.

No visual change.

Fixes #3364

> [!NOTE]
> **High risk**
> This changes egress-token handling and process isolation inside the thread container, touching a security boundary that protects proxy credentials from guest shell processes.
>
> **Overview**
> - Moves the run's egress token out of Docker environment arguments and sends it as the first stdin line for the container entrypoint to build the worker's proxy environment.
> - Runs the worker with a root-owned, execute-only copy of Node so same-UID guest shell processes cannot read its environment or memory through procfs or ptrace; logs whether the isolation is active.
> - Adds container integration and unit coverage for token recovery resistance, proxy authentication behavior, and guarded worker startup, and updates the container security plan.

This pull request completes Phase D of the ScholarSync security architecture project by fully removing the legacy stateless JWT authentication code now that the server-side MongoDB Session system is established and verified.

author: cevdetta
body:
Closes #451

## Rule

`script/importmap-syntax`: an import map that fails to parse, or whose top level, `imports`, `scopes` or `integrity` is not a JSON object, registers nothing, and bare imports then throw.

**harmful** · avoid · spec · document · any

- selector: none; the logic collects `script[type*="importmap" i]` and matches the type exactly after stripping whitespace
- match: `logic` (`packages/rules/logic/script/importmap-syntax.ts`, `check`)
- fix: `none`

## Definition of done

- [x] Frontmatter validates (`pnpm validate:rules`), and `ruleId` matches the file path: 196 rules valid
- [x] At least two independent sources under `## Resources`: two, the HTML Standard (normative) and MDN
- [x] `## Why avoid` states the concrete consequence: no map is registered, every bare import throws, and the module graph fails
- [x] `## Use instead` has runnable markup: a valid map
- [x] `severity` is justified: `harmful`, since the modules that rely on the map do not run
- [x] Fixtures pass in all three adapters (conformance suite): `invalid.html` gives two findings (a trailing comma, an array `imports`); `valid.html` gives none
- [x] Each tag is carried by ≥2 rules: `scripting`
- [x] No fix op: `none`, so no golden test applies

## Notes for the reviewer

**Evidence.** HTML Standard, "parse an import map string": "If parsed is not an ordered map, then throw a TypeError indicating that the top-level value needs to be a JSON object", with the same throw for `imports`, `scopes` and `integrity`. "Register an import map" reports the error and returns with no map merged. An unmapped bare specifier ends in "a TypeError indicating that specifier was a bare specifier, but was not remapped to anything by importMap". MDN lists the `TypeError`; import maps are Baseline since March 2023.

**Keys beyond the roadmap.** The roadmap named bad JSON and a non-object top level. The spec throws the same way for the three keys, and the whole map is lost, so the rule reports them. Problems inside a key (a bad address, an unknown top-level key) drop one entry with a console warning and stay out of scope.

**Fix to `script/speculationrules-syntax` (#448, unreleased).** The first run here failed the ESLint conformance test: `attr/script-src`'s fixture holds `<script type="importmap" src>`, and the new rule reported it too. `attr/script-src` already owns `src` on both types (CONTRIBUTING rule 7, one owner), so:
- both modules now leave an element with `src` to `attr/script-src`. #447 and #451 proposed a `src is not supported` detail; it is gone from both rules and their prose.
- both now pre-filter with `type*=` and compare `scriptTypeString()` exactly, as `attr/script-src` does. HTML strips ASCII whitespace from the type, so `type=" SpeculationRules "` is a rule set, which the `=` selector in #448 missed. `importmap-shim` (es-module-shims) stays quiet.

New unit cases cover a padded type, `importmap-shim`, `speculationrules-x` and `src` on both rules. #448 shipped no release, so no changelog line is lost.

**Impact.** `interop`: the failure breaks the page, it does not slow it.

**Bookmarklet: 63.1 kB of the 64 kB browser limit.** It grew 0.6 to 0.7 kB with each of the last three rules, mostly description and replacement text. The six roadmap rules still to come (19, 21, 22, 13, 20, 17) would pass 64 kB around the second of them. This needs your call before the next new rule: trim what the bookmarklet carries per rule, or shorten the strings.

author: pataforista
body:
## Resumen

Revisión de jugabilidad de Dr. Swipe y las correcciones de contenido que salieron de ella. Tres partes independientes en la misma rama; **la parte C necesita revisión clínica**.

| Parte | Qué cambia | Revisor |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Motor y jugabilidad** | `dr-swipe/src/**`, tests | Desarrollo |
| **B. Limpieza de pistas** | `tools/clean_card_leaks.py`, `tools/validate_cases.py`, `GUIA_CASOS.md` | Desarrollo y contenido |
| **C. Correcciones por guía y distractores** | `cases/**` (~600 archivos), `content_drafts/**`, `tools/*.py` | **Revisor clínico** |

Para la parte C no hace falta leer el diff de los JSON: **`REVISION_COMPLETA_CASOS.csv`** trae las 7,151 cartas del corpus contra `main`, con texto, acción y comentario originales y actuales, el tipo de cambio y su fuente (se regenera con `python3 tools/export_full_review.py cases REVISION_COMPLETA_CASOS.csv`).

## A. Motor y jugabilidad

- **Reloj:** se congelaba si se deslizaba más de una vez por segundo (el intervalo dependía de todo el snapshot de la máquina). Ahora depende solo de si el reloj corre. Verificado en navegador: 4 s de swipes rápidos pasaron de 178→178 a 98→94.
- **Tiempo por caso:** 10 / 9 / 8 s por carta según dificultad (antes 18 s/carta con tope de 180 s, y la alarma casi nunca sonaba). Tope de 45 a 180 s.
- **Error letal:** −40 de vitalidad (antes igual que uno trivial, −15). El marcador ya no tiene piso en 0; la XP se acota al cobrar.
- **Pistas:** la etiqueta "LETAL SI LO ACEPTAS/TIRAS" era 1:1 con la respuesta; fuera del modo estudio ahora es "⚠️ ALTO RIESGO". La categoría (p. ej. "Diagnóstico Diferencial" = 99% descartar) se agrupa en 5 bloques y el chip `#vitals` (sufijo del `card_id`) pasa a número de carta.
- **Deshacer:** 1 gratis por caso en guardia (5 en modo estudio); usarlo anula el bono de Guardia Perfecta.
- **Código Rojo:** pantalla completa con sirena y vibración en el estado `critical_alert`, que antes eran 1.5 s de pantalla vacía.
- **Mazo:** la pila tiene profundidad real y sube al arrastrar; sellos dentro de la carta que llegan a opacidad plena en el umbral de decisión; háptica al cruzarlo. Corrige además un atasco **previo**: tras un flick rápido el mazo se congelaba porque todas las cartas compartían un mismo valor de movimiento.
- **Vocabulario único:** Aceptar / Descartar en sellos, botones y atajos.
- **Feedback:** el mentor lleva ahora los puntos (se elimina el toast que tapaba el botón Aceptar); error letal con mentor en `shocked`.
- **HUD:** internos (vidas) visibles; el monitor dibuja un latido de ECG en lugar de una línea plana.
- **Varios:** el tinte rosa/ámbar de las cartas de riesgo funcionaba mal por el orden de CSS; `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`; botín sin asteriscos y con el bono perfecto; mazo bloqueado mientras un overlay pausa el reloj.
- **Límite de cartas:** 15 → 18 en `validate_cases.py`, `caseSchema.ts` (el esquema Zod habría **rechazado** mazos más largos al cargar) e `insert_distractors.py`.

## B. Limpieza de pistas en el contenido

Cerca del 45% de las cartas delataba la respuesta en su propio texto:
- Letras de opción de examen (`F)`, `G)`, `H)`, `I)`) en ~2,400 cartas, ~95% "aceptar".
- Etiquetas de veredicto solo presentes en cartas de descarte (`Dato anecdótico:`, `Contraindicado:`, `Información redundante:`, `Ruido en el expediente:`).
- Prefijos del mentor horneados en los datos (`🧹 DESCARTE RECOMENDADO:` y variantes con mojibake), que el juego imprimía dos veces.

`tools/clean_card_leaks.py` los elimina sin reescribir ninguna afirmación clínica (idempotente) y **el validador de CI ahora rechaza su regreso**. Los comentarios que solo tienen sentido tras un error ("¿Omites el dato clave?…") ya no se muestran tras un acierto.

## C. Correcciones por guía y distractores (revisión clínica)

**Vitales que definen la conducta estaban como "descartar" (120 cartas → "aceptar")**, contrastadas con guías:

| Caso | Fuente |
|---|---|
| Choque en lactante deshidratado → Plan C | OMS/AIEPI |
| Índice de choque >1 en HPP | FIGO 2022 |
| Inestabilidad en ectópico (cirugía, metotrexato contraindicado) | ACOG PB 193 |
| Choque séptico | Sepsis-3 (JAMA 2016) |
| Neumotórax a tensión (diagnóstico clínico) | ATLS 10 |
| Colangitis grados II y III | Tokyo 2018 |
| Fiebre materna en corioamnionitis | ACOG CO 712 / Gibbs |
| TA <185/110 para trombolizar | AHA/ASA 2019 |
| DPPNI con inestabilidad materna | AJOG 2022, Medscape |
| Neumonía pediátrica SatO₂ ≤92% | BTS |

Se eliminaron 14 cartas vacías ("TA N/A, FC N/A, Temp N/A") y se reescribió el comentario de la deshidratación moderada (sigue en descartar).

**Distractores nuevos:** 1,033 cartas de descarte en 4 lotes (`content_drafts/distractores_lote*.json`), cada una una afirmación verosímil pero falsa, con comentario que corrige el dato y **su fuente** (GINA 2024, ESC 2021/2019, CDC 2021, AAO-HNS 2020, AAP 2013, ADA, ASCCP 2019, FIGO, ACOG, OMS, AHA/ASA, Surviving Sepsis 2021, estudio DIG, CEBM, ASA 2016…). **Solo se escribieron cartas con fuente confirmada**; en RPM y DPPNI hay menos por falta de fuente verificada. `tools/insert_distractors.py` las coloca en posiciones aleatorias reproducibles.

**Balance:** descarte global 24.6% → 34.7% (acertar siempre deslizando a la derecha pasa de 75% a 65%).

## Pendiente de decisión del revisor clínico (columna `revision_pendiente` del CSV)

- Roséola (15 cartas): si un dato ya presente en el escenario de llegada cuenta como "descartar".
- Umbral de SatO₂ en neumonía pediátrica: se aplicó BTS (≤92%); falta confirmar con la GPC mexicana.
- 55 familias (417 casos) siguen por debajo de 40% de descarte: ver `PLAN_SIGUIENTES_PASOS.md` (lote 5, Shock Room, HUD, CI).

## Verificación

- `python3 tools/validate_cases.py cases`: 599 casos válidos.
- Los 599 casos pasan el esquema Zod real de la app.
- `npm test` (31), `npx tsc -b`, `npx eslint src`, `npm run build`: OK.
- `apply_guideline_review.py`, `clean_card_leaks.py` e `insert_distractors.py` con `--check`: sin cambios pendientes (idempotentes).
- Probado jugando en Chromium con viewport móvil (390×844): timer, pila, sellos, mentor, Código Rojo, sin errores de consola.

## Nota

Sin cambios en las preguntas del jefe (Shock Room) ni en la lógica de puntaje base. El audio sigue siendo procedural; se añadió la sirena de Código Rojo.
