author: tristrange
body:
**This is unblocking deploys.** `main`'s `app` job is currently failing, so nothing has shipped since the nightly pipeline ran — including PR #19.

## What happened

The cron published `2026-10-04` and the first thing it caught was itself:

```
regions 2 (#e9c46a) and 7 (#e76f51) touch but are only 0.19988 apart: expected >= 0.2
expected 5 to be 8   // a shipped region count's own colour per region
```

The `app` job failed, so `deploy` was skipped. That is the guarantee in `colours.test.ts` doing the job it exists for — but this time it was blocking rather than informative.

Worth noting: the nightly dispatch Codex asked for in #15 is what surfaced this. Those commits raise no `push` event, so before that fix the board would have shipped unverified and uncoloured.

## The floor was never the problem

I checked whether the constraint is even satisfiable before touching anything, using the app's own `colourDistance`. All nine boards are colourable at 0.2, and **2026-10-04 takes 19 nodes** in a backtracking search. So this is not a palette limit or a generator bug — `climb` is a local search that recolours one region at a time and keeps only changes that improve the score. It cannot step past a configuration where *every* single-region change makes something else worse, and 0.19988 is exactly that.

## The fix

A backtracking search, assigned most-constrained-region first and preferring an unused colour, used **only when the climb has already failed** on the floor.

That conditional is the important design decision. Handing the search a board the climb handles would repaint days people have already played, for no gain — the colours exist only to tell touching regions apart, and where that already holds there is nothing to improve. A step budget (20,000) bounds it regardless, so "rare" is not load-bearing for the page staying responsive.

`2026-10-04` now gets all 8 distinct colours with a narrowest touching border of **0.2013**.

## No test was relaxed

I expected to have to soften the "own colour per region" expectation, since `colours.ts` documents reuse as the fallback on dense boards. It is not needed: the search prefers an unused colour for each region, so the board gets all 8 and the test passes unchanged. Better outcome than the one I predicted.

## Verification

- three tests fail if the search is disabled: the shipped-puzzle floor, the distinct-colour count, and the pinned 10-04 assignment
- both 10-04's assignment and an older board's (2026-09-30) are pinned, so the day cannot go back to being uncolourable and no shipped day is quietly repainted
- the densest board the app can build — 8×8 tiled in 2×2 blocks, 16 regions, a far denser graph than any shipped day — is measured at **11ms** and asserted under 1s
- rendered 2026-10-04 in a browser: 8 distinct region colours, 64 cells, every adjacent pair visibly different, no console errors

207 tests (1 expected fail — the `×` mark contrast defect, still awaiting your call), typecheck, lint, build clean.

author: vasilyoshev
body:
## Summary

- `src/lib/escape-origin.test.tsx` carried two hypothetical paths that `tsc` rejects once expo-router's typed routes exist in `.expo/types` (written as a side effect of `expo start`): the catch-all `/tools/habits/learn/[...rest]` at the line the issue names, and — same category, found while reproducing — the nested-group string `/(app)/(tabs)/tools/journal` (no `(tabs)` group exists). Both are pure-function tests of `targetPathname`'s `[...param]` substitution and mid-path group-stripping branches, and the app has no real catch-all route and no doubly-nested group to point them at, so the routes stay hypothetical and the casts now go through `unknown`, each with a comment saying so. Verified to compile **both with and without** `.expo/types` present (generated via `npx expo customize tsconfig.json`, which runs the dev server's generator one-shot).
- **CI parity call: the verify job now generates typed routes before typechecking.** Until now CI's `tsc` checked the loose fallback `Href` while a contributor's machine (post-`expo start`) checked the strict one, so the two disagreed — the gap #2849 calls the more useful finding. Measured cost: **2s on the CI runner** (this PR's own first verify run; ~10s cold locally) against a verify job whose real baseline is ~10 minutes, and `tsc` itself is no slower (~30s locally with or without the types). The command needs no Metro, no watcher, no env files, and leaves zero modifications to tracked files. Benefit beyond this test: every href in the codebase is now validated against the real route set in CI, so a typo'd route goes red on the PR instead of on the next contributor's machine. With the cost that small and the step that inert, adding it beat documenting the divergence.

Fixes #2849 — but this merges to `dev`, not the default branch, so the issue is closed manually with a pointer.

## Review Context

- docs or roadmap updates: `docs/github-setup.md`'s CI-workflow paragraph now mentions the typed-routes generation step with its measured cost. No README change — local commands and setup are unchanged.
- important test, CI, or manual verification context: locally verified `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with `.expo/types` present **and** absent, `npx eslint` and `prettier --check` clean on the touched files, `npx jest src/lib/escape-origin.test.tsx` 22/22. The real proof of the new CI step is this PR's own verify run, which executed it in 2s and passed. One honest caveat: if a future Expo SDK's `expo customize tsconfig.json` decides tsconfig.json needs rewriting, the verify job would typecheck that rewritten config (uncommitted) — today it rewrites nothing, and a contributor's `expo start` applies the same rewrite locally, which is exactly the parity this step exists for. The second commit corrects the first commit's estimated cost figures (~10s / ~3 min) to the measured ones (2s / ~10 min job baseline, cf. the 2026-09-26 run at 10m12s).

## Product guardrails

- [x] no dark patterns or punitive mechanics introduced
- [x] no AI therapist framing added
- [x] no diagnosis, treatment, emergency-support, or therapist-replacement claims added
- [x] no new tracking, analytics, ads, paywalls, or social scope added without explicit review
- [x] reminders, streaks, quests, notifications, or progress mechanics remain optional and non-punitive
- [ ] New module or engagement-adjacent feature? → N/A — test-types and CI change only, no product surface touched
- [ ] Architectural change (service/host/provider/domain/dependency/credential)? → N/A — no service, host, domain, dependency, or credential changes; the CI step uses the already-installed expo CLI
- [ ] Copy saying what Selftend _is_ matches `docs/positioning.md`? → N/A — no user-facing or public copy touched

## Review Notes

- Privacy/safety impact: none — no runtime code changed.
- Accessibility impact: none.
- Translation/i18n impact: none — no user-visible strings.
- Dependency or license impact: none — no dependency added or changed; `expo customize` is part of the pinned expo package already in package-lock.

author: msmfa
body:
Notes are stored locally under a backend account ID. When the same verified Apple identity has different IDs across backend databases, signing in to the newer account hides notes saved under the former ID even though calendar data still loads.

Add a Find saved notes action to the empty Notes screen. It reads former IDs approved by the authenticated server and reconnects only those notes and their reviews in one SQLite transaction. Existing note IDs, encrypted bodies, dates and notification IDs are preserved; an ownership journal records the change. Network failures remain retryable, and a logout or account switch cancels recovery. A notes-loading failure now shows retry UI instead of the empty notebook.

Validation: type check, 13 targeted recovery/UI tests, and the migration queries against real SQLite, including account isolation, preserved data, repeat recovery, and rollback. Full tests run in CI. Requires the companion backend recovery-identity field and a verified account link. No note content or local inventory is uploaded.

body:
## Linked issue

Refs #925; related developer-loop evidence #1104. Broader architecture acceptance remains open.

## Outcome and scope

Libultraship transient-source selection now has one private read-only plan: original source, admitted ZIP materialization, no source argument, or cleanup after a generated archive exists. The existing adapter consumes that decision immediately through explicitly named preparation, checks cancellation before mutation, and reuses existing normalized identity checks, temporary publication and owned cleanup. This removes hidden extraction/deletion from source-choice logic without another store, framework or authority.

Preserve generated-archive and runtime-filename precedence, actual launch arguments, admitted source identity, canonical user data and existing service locks/source post-verification/executable/process boundaries. Other launch branches and service save/manifest preparation remain mutating; this does not claim the entire launch-spec API is pure.

author: anna-git
body:
## Summary of changes

MVC child actions (`@Html.Action` / `@Html.RenderAction`) no longer set the root `aspnet.request` span's resource name, `http.route` or code origin.

## Reason for change

See [APMS-20681](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/APMS-20681).

When a page that is **not** an MVC action renders a child action, the root span is named after the child action's route, which never matched the request URL. For example, `GET /page.aspx` becomes `GET /assets/{*path}` with `http.route: assets/{*path}`, or `GET /widget/index` with only the default route. The code origin points at the child's controller.

With an MVC parent nothing changes: the parent writes first, so the child's writes were already no-ops.
**How the root span gets its route today**

- `aspnet.request` is created by `TracingHttpModule` before routing runs, so it only knows the URL. The route template and endpoint method are only known inside MVC.
- Our ASP.NET MVC integration pushes them up to the root span, from hooks that run for **every** action MVC invokes, child actions included:

  | Root span write | Our integration code | Hooked MVC method |
  |---|---|---|
  | `http.route` and resource name (via `HttpContextPropagatedResourceNameKey`, applied by `TracingHttpModule` at end of request) | `AspNetMvcIntegration.CreateScope` | `AsyncControllerActionInvoker.BeginInvokeAction` |
  | Code origin | `AsyncControllerActionInvoker_BeginInvokeActionMethod_Integration` / `ControllerActionInvoker_InvokeAction_Integration` | `BeginInvokeActionMethod` / `InvokeActionMethod` |

- Each write is "only if still empty", so the first action the integration sees names the request. That's meant to be the page's endpoint.

**Why that breaks for child actions**

- A child action's `RouteData.Route` comes from **outbound** URL generation: the first route in `RouteTable.Routes` able to generate a URL for the child's controller/action ([ChildActionExtensions.cs](https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetWebStack/blob/main/src/System.Web.Mvc/Html/ChildActionExtensions.cs), `GetVirtualPathForArea` → `CreateRouteData` → `routeData.Route = vpd.Route`). It was never matched against the request.
- The child-action support added in #2139 assumed a child action always runs inside an MVC parent, which would already have filled the root slots. So the integration never checked "am I a child?" before writing to the root span. Code origin later reused the same first-action-wins pattern.
- That assumption fails whenever the page has no `aspnet-mvc.request` parent span: WebForms pages, pages served by a custom handler outside MVC routing (for example a CMS), and controllers on the synchronous invoker (`DisableAsyncSupport`), which the integration doesn't create spans for. There, the child action is the first action the integration sees, and it names the request.
- `DD_TRACE_ROUTE_TEMPLATE_RESOURCE_NAMES_ENABLED=false` is not a workaround: it only stops the resource name. `http.route` and code origin are still wrong.

**With an MVC parent, nothing changes**

The parent fills the root slots first, so the child's writes were already no-ops. Where the parent leaves a gap (a route that isn't a `Route`, an action descriptor that can't be resolved), the child's route or method would have been wrong anyway.

## Implementation details

All changes are in the ASP.NET MVC integration (`ClrProfiler/AutoInstrumentation/AspNet`):

- **Detection**: `isChildAction` now reads `ControllerContext.IsChildAction` (duck-copied into `ControllerContextStruct`). MVC sets it from the `ParentActionViewContext` token that every child action carries ([ControllerContext.cs](https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetWebStack/blob/main/src/System.Web.Mvc/ControllerContext.cs)). The previous check (`ParentActionViewContext.RouteData.Values["controller"] != null`) missed child actions whose parent route data has no `controller`. It is a strict subset of the new check. `ViewContextStruct` is no longer needed and is removed.
- **Root span writes**: child actions no longer write root `http.route` or `HttpContextPropagatedResourceNameKey` (Datadog semantics), and no longer name or set the route of the existing server span (OpenTelemetry semantics).
- **Code origin**: both code-origin hooks skip child actions (`AspNetMvcIntegration.IsChildAction`, which unwraps duck proxies).
- **Child span's own resource name**: child actions reuse the name computed by an MVC parent if there is one. Otherwise they use the URL-based name (Datadog) or just the method (OpenTelemetry, per the [HTTP span name spec](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/http/http-spans.md#name)). They never use their own route.
- **Limitation (out of scope)**: a child action has no real route, since MVC never matches it against the URL. Its span still reports `aspnet.route` with the route MVC used to build its URL (e.g. `assets/{*path}`). This PR only fixes the root span. The child span is now always named `aspnet-mvc.request.child-action`.

**Behaviour change**: pages that currently get a route template from a child action will get a URL-based resource name and no `http.route`.

## Test coverage

- New `Samples.AspNetMvc5` `SyncParentController` (synchronous invoker, so no MVC parent span) whose view renders a child action. A new `/SyncParent` case in `AspNetMvc5Tests` adds 9 snapshots: root resource `GET /syncparent`, no `http.route`, no code origin, child span `aspnet-mvc.request.child-action`.
- Existing child-action snapshots (`/DataDog/DogHouse`, MVC parent) are unchanged.
- Validated manually on IIS with an MVC 5.2.9 app covering a sync-invoker parent, a WebForms parent (with and without `controller` in its route data), a catch-all route registered before `Default`, and both values of `DD_TRACE_ROUTE_TEMPLATE_RESOURCE_NAMES_ENABLED`.

## Other details


Fixes #9181

Pages that previously got a route template "by accident" through a child action will now report `GET /<path>` with no `http.route`.

`AspNetWebApi2Integration` has the same unconditional first-writer pattern for root `http.route` and the propagated name. It isn't involved here; that's a possible follow-up.

[APMS-20681]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/APMS-20681?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: bassamsaid
body:
Two faults a phone found within a minute of each other.

## 1. The Dalia screen would not open

```
mediaUrl(esc) is not a function.
(In 'mediaUrl(esc)(a.image)', 'mediaUrl(esc)' is "/uploads/(s) => String(s ?? '')…")
```

Eight calls read `mediaUrl(esc)(x)`: the URL helper was handed **the escaper
itself** as its argument, and the string that came back was then called as a
function. Surviving wreckage of an earlier search-and-replace across
`admin.js` — every one should have been `esc(mediaUrl(x))`, which is what every
other call site in the codebase says.

The feed's photos, posts being edited and gallery tiles all go through one of
them, so the page could not draw at all.

## 2. Face ID offered on a phone that had never been set up

Tapping it asks the OS for a key that is not there. iOS answers an empty
credential list by offering to **scan a QR code with another device** — a screen
about security keys and "other accounts", shown to somebody who only wanted to
sign in.

- The button now appears only where there is something to sign in with.
- The single path to setting it up is the offer after a password sign-in.
- A second guard inside the sign-in says so in words rather than handing an
  empty request to the OS, for when the note on the device is out of date.

## Verified in a browser

With a virtual authenticator present, so only the app's own guard stands in the
way:

| | |
|---|---|
| button on an unset-up phone | absent |
| calling the sign-in anyway | explains itself, never reaches the OS |
| Dalia page with a photo post | renders |
| its image | resolves to a real `/uploads/…` path |
| script errors on that page | none |

author: dhirensoni-certistage
body:
## What was wrong

After deploying #14, Media Manager showed **"Unknown — 96 Sessions, 1840 Media, 1.9 GB"** and *Clean up now* reported nothing due.

- "Unknown" = media left behind by sessions that no longer exist in the database (deleted/old test sessions). The clean-up only looked at file age and did not recognise them.
- Every remaining file was newer than the 30-day retention, so by the rule as written there was nothing to delete, but the UI did not make that clear.

## Changes

- **Orphaned media is removed regardless of age**: files whose `{sessionId}-…` prefix matches no existing session are deleted nightly and on *Clean up now* (`findRemovableFiles` returns expired and orphaned files separately). Safety: if the session lookup fails nothing is treated as orphaned.
- **Inline "older than N days"** next to *Clean up now* (prefilled with the retention) for a one-off deeper clean-up without changing the setting. `0` = only orphans.
- **Clear status**: due now by age vs. files of deleted sessions (count + size), last run time and what it deleted (`SystemConfig.mediaLastCleanupResult`), and a toast that says exactly what was deleted or why nothing was.

## Verification

- Unit check: expired files picked, fresh file and `.gitkeep` skipped, no orphans when the DB is unreachable, session-id parsing (`xciy6t-3EB0…` → `xciy6t`, `my-session-3EB0…` → `my-session`).
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` and the server bundle all clean.

## Deploy

```bash
cd /var/www/waba && bash scripts/deploy.sh
```
(one new JSON column, `deploy.sh` runs `prisma db push`). Then Media Manager → *Clean up now*: the 1.9 GB of "Unknown" files goes immediately.

author: jeremyspofford
body:
## Why

The owner's app-opening test on 2026-09-28 found four failures:
- Nova replied "Notepad is now open" with no tool call behind it.
- She wrote tool calls out as text, sometimes inside bash fences, and nothing ran.
- She overstated a launch.
- The existing guards caught none of it.

## What changes

Two honesty corrections. Both are **append-only**: each adds one sentence, never redirects, never sends her back to act, and never invites a retry. A false positive therefore costs one sentence and never an action. Both are computed at the end of the turn from the final spans.

- **`written_call`**: a reply that writes a tool call as text gets "(I wrote `<tool>` as text; it did not run.)"
- **`device_completion`**: a reply that claims a device action that no matching call backs gets "(No `<tool>` call ran on `<device>` this turn.)"
  - It stays silent when any call of that family ran on that device, or on another agent of the same machine.
  - Failures and unanswered calls are stated as such.
  - Device names, tools and machine grouping are read from live state; nothing is a maintained list.
- **`device_launch_app`** reports what the agent said, instead of "Launched".

The web client now renders `correction` frames live. Before this change, corrections appeared only after a reload. On every path this lane touches, what streams live equals what core stores. A fixture shared by the core and web suites pins this.

Making corrections visible live also exposed older false live lines, and these are fixed here:
- **Redirect notes.** A redirect's note claims work ("Listing the files now…", "Checking the device now…", "doing it now…") only when a call reached a tool's executor. For the listing and state notes, the call must also be of the kind the note names: the originating guard is re-run on the original reply against the final spans. Tool spans now record `reached_executor`.
- **Consent correction.** It reads the same fact, so a call naming a tool that does not exist is no longer reported as "X failed".
- **Listing redirect.** When its own listing ran and only the closing round failed, it now says "I ran workspace_list_files but could not report the result", not "I did not actually list those files".
- **Speed.** `device_completion` is linear on one long clause; it was quadratic, taking 1.8 s at 200 KB. The lane's big-input timing tests now assert a growth ratio across two sizes, plus an absolute cap.

## Review

- Five adversarial fix rounds, and the rulings at the round cap.
- A final whole-lane review, one fix wave, and a scoped re-review of that wave. Verdict: ready.
- Precision on recorded real turns: `written_call` fires only on the owner's two written-call turns, and `device_completion` only on his two unbacked-claim turns. The honest launch turn stays silent.

## Tests

- Core full suite: 6,537 passed, 0 failed (on main 60841594, before the last listing fix).
- The last fix's related files plus the tripwires: 1,044 passed.
  - test_tools_registry, test_no_approvals and test_eval_corpus are unedited.
  - Only the lane's own big-input section of test_guard_regex_timing changed.
- Web: 1,339 passed, and `tsc` is clean.
- ruff is clean.

## Parked follow-ups (pre-existing on main; reviewed and ruled)

- A rewrite-class correction shown live is dropped on reload when a replace-class one also fires.
- The commitment redirect's markup regeneration shows raw markup live.
- The stack and state corrections stream in a different order than they are stored.
- `_ran_clause` reports a nonexistent tool as "failed". `reached_executor` now makes the filter possible.
- Narration corrects an honest report after a real `device_write_file`.

## Not done yet

The live walk happens after deploy, and the turns are read by turn id.

body:
Item 3 of the post-2.0.1 code review: `src/app/api/public/registrations/route.ts` (579 lines, one POST) mixed validation, eligibility, the locked transaction, notifications, logging and the HTTP response. This is a first, safe split. **Behaviour is unchanged**: same statuses, same JSON bodies, same notification payloads, ordering and dedupe keys.

## What moved

- **`src/lib/signup-notifications.ts`**: `buildSignupNotifications({ event, shifts, volunteer, registrations, tokens })`, the former inline `buildNotifications`: confirmation (active places) or request acknowledgement (#484), admin notification (via `sendAdminNotification`, so `signupAdminEmail` and the `ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL` fallback still apply), sector leaders (not for requests), waitlist confirmations. It collects into an outbox collector and returns the payloads with their `kind:firstRegistrationId:recipient` dedupe key. The route still enqueues them inside the transaction.
- **`src/lib/signup-eligibility.ts`**: the pre-transaction checks, each returning a `{ status, body }` refusal or `null`: `registrationWindowRefusal`, `requiredPhoneRefusal`, `fullShiftRefusal` (early unlocked capacity check), `selectionOverlapRefusal`, `existingOverlapRefusal` / `findOverlap`, `reservedRoleRefusal` (takes a `loadInvite` callback, so the invitation is still only queried when a reserved role is asked), `answersRefusal`, `minimumAgeRefusal`. They read nothing themselves. `fullShift` and `overlapWithExisting` are shared with the transaction's `ShiftFullError` / `OverlapError` handlers, so both paths build the same message.
- **Stays in the route**: the lock, the authoritative capacity / overlap / role-limit checks and the writes, all in the same transaction, plus logging, the invite update and the response.

`route.ts` goes from 579 to 436 lines.

## Client bundles

`signup-notifications.ts` reaches Prisma through `notification-helpers` and `sector-leaders`; `signup-eligibility.ts` imports no Prisma. Neither is imported by a client component (only the route and their tests use them).

## Tests

- New `src/__tests__/signup-notifications.test.ts` (9 cases, real helpers, Prisma/env mocked): confirmation payload with shift info and event coordinates fallback, request acknowledgement, null confirmation message, admin notification, admin notification switched off, `ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL` fallback and its absence, sector leaders skipped for requests, waitlist position, full ordering and dedupe keys.
- New `src/__tests__/signup-eligibility.test.ts` (20 cases): status and message of each rule.
- Existing route tests (`*registration*`, `signup-approval-api`, `role-*`, `event-questions-signup`, `registrations-*`, `security/*`) pass unchanged, with no mock paths changed.
- `npx vitest run`: 210 files, 1324 tests passed. `npx tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` on the changed files and `git diff --check` are clean.

No CHANGELOG entry: internal refactor.

author: edgepillar
body:
Watch previously reported caught up whenever the agreed target height was at or below its tip, even if the target conflicted with trusted local history. Require an exact retained hash, public-key, and signature match before saving or reporting caught up. A conflict now returns REFUSED with `ReasonRetainedHeaderMismatch`; an unavailable retained height returns `ReasonHeightOutOfWindow`. Continuous watch polls again, while `--once` exits 2.

Add a detached `VerifiedState.HeaderAtHeight` inspection view and fixed JSON diagnostic categories. The check deliberately refuses stale targets outside the retained window rather than claiming an unverified local binding. It does not establish independent freshness, canonicality, or finality.

Validation: reproduced eight false-success cases before the fix; two-peer continuous and single-step checks for matching, conflicting, substituted-signature, and evicted targets; immutable lookup tests; compiled CLI v2 refusal and state-preservation checks; full uncached race suite, build, vet, lint, and benchmark smoke. All network traffic in these checks uses local synthetic fixtures.

author: weegy
body: ### fix(auth): rate-limit password login - `POST /api/v1/auth/login/:providerId` ran a full argon2id verification for every attempt and counted none. Each attempt now goes through a limiter before the provider runs, with three layers: - a failure brake per client address that a trusted hop vouched for; - a backoff per (account, client) pair: five free failures, then waits that double up to two minutes; - a process-wide argon2 capacity: `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_INFLIGHT` (default 4) verifications at once and 300 admitted attempts per minute. - A refused attempt gets 429 `auth.rate_limited` or 503 `auth.busy` with `Retry-After`. It never reaches argon2 and never sets a cookie. The login page shows a localized wait message. - A successful password sign-in sets a signed device cookie. The cookie is bound to the verified account and to the password hash that sign-in checked. A browser with a current cookie keeps its own budget and a reserved share of the capacity, so other clients' failures cannot lock it out. A reset, disable or delete makes earlier cookies stale. - `POST /api/v1/auth/setup` now hashes the first admin's password inside the same capacity and answers 503 `auth.busy` when no slot is free. The setup-token check, the shared setup predicate and the atomic first-admin transaction are unchanged. The rate-limited sign-in keeps the existing session binding: the session version comes from the same row read that checked the password. - The limiter takes the client address from `AUTH_LOGIN_CLIENT_ADDRESS` and never from `req.ip`. Accepted values: `socket` (default), `xff:` (n trusted hops counted from the right) or `header:`. `fly/middleware.fly.toml` sets `header:Fly-Client-IP`. `AUTH_LOGIN_IPV6_PREFIX` keys IPv6 clients by prefix. - An admin password reset or re-enable clears the account's backoff. Those calls sit next to the existing session revocation. Limiter state lives in memory, per process. ## Docs - `docs/security-architecture.md`: - new §10m: the three layers, the device cookie, the client-address trust rules and the residual risks, including per-process state; - cross-references from §10 and §10l; - a §11 checklist item and an updated review footer. - `docs/upgrading.md`: new section "Upgrading past v0.167.10 — password sign-in is rate-limited". It covers the defaults, the Fly setting (`header:Fly-Client-IP`, not `xff:1`), and the Render and docker-compose guidance. - `docs/CHANGELOG.md`: a new `[Unreleased]` entry. - `docs/middleware-agent-handoff.md`: the sign-in flow and the setup walkthrough (§3), the configuration table (§10), and the open items (§13). - `middleware/.env.example` documents `AUTH_LOGIN_CLIENT_ADDRESS`, `AUTH_LOGIN_IPV6_PREFIX` and `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_INFLIGHT`. - `render.yaml` explains why the blueprint keeps the default client address. ## Verification - CI-equivalent gates on the final head, all passing: - middleware: build, lint, typecheck, and the test typecheck ratchet (337, at baseline); - web-ui: lint (0 errors), typecheck, `i18n:check`, vitest (160 files, 1592 tests). - middleware `npm test`: 9979 tests, 9954 pass, 24 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `test/cliBridge/cliSpawnGate.test.ts`, which reads the locally installed CLI binary and only fails locally. - middleware `npm run test:pg` against a throwaway pgvector/pg16 container: 402/402. This includes the first-admin race suites (`userStoreFirstAdmin.pg`, `setupRouteConcurrency.pg`), the session-version migration suite and the sign-in account-fold suite. - The sign-in limiter, setup and admin-users suites pass in the full run. - One web-ui run hit a timing failure in `AgentToolGrants.test.tsx`: the assertion ran while the component was still loading. That file and its component are untouched by this change, and the other two full runs passed. - No changes under `.github`, no lockfile changes, no package version bumps. - `94fc7a94` (Fly header condition in upgrading.md, reserved test hosts): the `loginAccount` suite passes 24/24. ## Follow-ups - Move to a shared limiter (Redis or Postgres) once the middleware runs more than one replica. - Test `header:Fly-Client-IP` once against a live Fly app with a made-up header value, both directly and through web-ui. - Render: find a client header the edge sets and overwrites. Until then the blueprint keeps `socket`. - Clients behind one shared key share its account pairs. A trustworthy browser address forwarded through web-ui would remove that. - Add tooling to rotate the session signing key. - Enforce the 1024-character password ceiling where passwords are set (setup wizard, admin forms). - `auth.user_disabled` is answered before the password check. - Count wrong setup tokens per client, and translate the setup page's 503 `auth.busy` message. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

Adds an API deprecation notice for three Cloudflare Radar endpoints that were already marked deprecated in the API reference but never had a published end-of-life date:

- `GET /radar/http/top/browser` and `GET /radar/http/top/browser_family`, replaced by `GET /radar/http/summary/{dimension}` with the `BROWSER` or `BROWSER_FAMILY` dimension
- `GET /radar/netflows/summary`, replaced by `GET /radar/netflows/summary/{dimension}`

End of life is April 2, 2027, six months out, matching the earlier Radar deprecations.

author: rokokol
body:
The smartd module passes `-M exec <notify script>` to smartd only when mail, wall or x11 notifications are enabled. The condition does not include `systembus-notify`. With `notifications.wall.enable = false` and `notifications.systembus-notify.enable = true`, the script contains the `dbus-send` call, but smartd never runs it. A failing disk then sends no alert, and smartd writes the problem only to the journal.

This PR adds `ns.enable` to the condition. It also adds `nixosTests.smartd`, the first NixOS test for this module. The test gives the VM an emulated NVMe disk, because QEMU's NVMe controller answers SMART queries. It enables `notifications.test` so that smartd sends one test alert at startup, and it waits for that alert as a D-Bus signal on the system bus.

Testing:

- `nix build -L --file . nixosTests.smartd` fails without the module change: smartd never runs the notify script, and the wait times out after 60 seconds
- The same command passes with the module change
- With `dbus-send --system` changed to `--session` in the notify script, the test fails again. Thus the test checks that the alert arrives on the system bus, not only that smartd runs the script

I used Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to find the cause, write the change and the test, run the test commands above, and draft this text. I reviewed the change and this text before submission.

author: pcwadarong
body:
## ⏱ 소요 시간 - 리뷰 예상 시간: 25분
## 📌 작업 요약 모바일 웹뷰에서 **로그인 화면 배경이 비는 버그**를 잡다가, 원인이 "화면 여백과 배경을 누가 책임지는가"가 화면마다 달랐던 것이라 그 경계를 레이아웃으로 모았어요. 거기서 드러난 간격 어긋남과 QA 중 나온 UX 문제를 함께 정리하고, 파트·장르 선택 바텀시트 디자인을 반영했습니다. | | 전 | 후 | | --- | --- | --- | | 배경 | `body`가 소유 → 툴바·safe area 뒤가 밝은 띠 | `html`이 소유 → 배경과 무관하게 전부 덮음 | | 하단 safe area | 네비 있는 화면만 보정 | 네비 없는 화면도 레이아웃이 보정 | | 헤더 아래 콘텐츠 시작 | 32 / 31 / 24 / 0px 제각각 | **전부 32px** | | 헤더 높이 | 상수 120px 하드코딩 | 실측값 동기화 (제목 줄바꿈 추적) | | 대표 파트·장르 | 1·2·3 번호 (없는 순위를 표시) | 📌 핀 + 2부터 번호 | 적용 범위: 프론트엔드 전역 레이아웃 + 프로필·알림·투표·합주 공간 화면. **백엔드 변경 없음.**
## 📝 작업 내용 ### 1. 배경 — `body`가 아니라 `html`이 소유하게 `body` 배경은 canvas로 전파되는데 `attachment: fixed`라 위치 영역이 뷰포트뿐이에요. `viewport-fit=cover`를 쓰고 있어 canvas는 브라우저 툴바·safe area 뒤까지 뻗는데 거기엔 닿지 않고, `background-repeat` 기본값 탓에 그 자리에서 그라데이션이 **밝은 쪽부터 다시 시작**해 밝은 띠로 보였습니다. ```css html { background-color: var(--gradient-top); background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, …); background-repeat: no-repeat; /* 띠의 직접 원인 */ background-size: 100% 100lvh; /* 툴바가 접혔을 때의 최대 뷰포트까지 */ } ``` 높이를 `dvh`가 아니라 `100lvh`로 둔 건, 툴바가 접히면 그 뒤가 배경색(밝은 쪽)으로 남기 때문이에요. ### 2. safe area — 네비 없는 화면의 하단을 아무도 잡아주지 않았다 `main`이 하단 inset을 `showBottomNav`일 때만 보정하고 있어서, 로그인·가입·온보딩은 마지막 줄이 홈 인디케이터·툴바에 물렸어요. 레이아웃이 `pb`로 잡고, 높이를 `100dvh`에 맞추는 페이지는 **위아래 inset을 모두** 빼게 했습니다(`min-h-page` 유틸). > 한쪽만 빼면 합이 `100dvh`를 넘어 딱 그만큼 유령 스크롤이 생겨요. 실측으로 비밀번호 찾기가 노치 기기에서 81px 스크롤됐습니다. ### 3. `fullBleed` → `bleed: 'x' | 'all'` 가로(`px-5`)와 세로(`py-8`)를 **한꺼번에** 끄는 플래그였어요. 정작 쓰는 화면들이 원한 건 가로 흘림뿐이라 세로 여백을 각자 다시 썼고(`pt-8`·`py-6`·없음), 그래서 헤더 아래 시작 위치가 갈렸습니다. | 값 | 의미 | 쓰는 곳 | | --- | --- | --- | | 없음 | `px-5 py-8` 둘 다 | 대부분 | | `'x'` | 가로만 흘림, **세로는 레이아웃이 계속 소유** | 밴드 메인·스페이스·투표 3종 | | `'all'` | 둘 다 끔 | 로그인·검색·프로필 | `'x'`가 핵심이에요 — 세로 여백의 소유권을 레이아웃이 쥐고 있으면 새 화면이 추가돼도 간격이 어긋날 수가 없어요. 프로필이 쓰던 `-mx-5 -my-8` 음수 마진도 `'all'`로 대체했습니다. ### 4. 헤더 높이 — 상수에서 실측으로 헤더 높이가 `min-h`라 탭 유무·제목 줄바꿈에 따라 달라지는데 `main`은 `120px`를 박아 쓰고 있었어요. 실제가 더 커지면 본문 첫 줄이 헤더 뒤로 **조용히** 들어갑니다. `RouteHeader`가 `ResizeObserver`로 자기 높이를 재서 `--route-header-height`로 넘기고 `main`이 그 값을 씁니다(`--bottom-nav-clearance`와 같은 패턴). 첫 페인트 전에는 기존 상수를 `var()` 폴백으로 써서 깜빡임이 없어요. ### 5. 대표 표시 — 없는 순위를 보여주던 1·2·3 선택 칩에 1·2·3을 달아 순위처럼 읽혔지만, 실제로 저장되는 건 플레이 파트의 **첫 번째(`isPrimary`)뿐**이고 장르는 대표 개념 자체가 없어요. 1번 자리를 📌 핀으로 바꿔 "대표는 하나"를 모양으로 말하고, 번호는 2부터 시작해 나열 순서만 나타냅니다. 바텀시트 높이는 400px 고정, 칩이 늘어나면 그 영역만 스크롤해요. 프로필 칩에도 같은 핀을 달아 두 화면이 같은 말을 하게 했습니다. ### 6. 함께 고친 QA 항목 - **알림 편집 모드에서 리스트가 41px 튀던 것** — "모두 읽음"이 숨겨지며 버튼(33) + `mb-2`(8)가 함께 사라졌어요. 숨기는 대신 비활성화해 자리를 지킵니다 - **알림 편집 헤더에 글자가 몰리던 것** — `0개 선택됨 / 0개 삭제 / 취소`로 개수를 두 번 말했어요. 개수는 제목 자리가 한 번만 말하고 삭제는 아이콘으로 - **파트·장르 토스트가 쌓이던 것** — 삭제마다 토스트가 생겨 화면을 가렸어요. 같은 `id`로 하나만 뜨게 하고 닫기 X를 추가(sonner의 per-toast `closeButton`이 `classNames`에 `hidden`으로 박혀 켜도 안 보이던 상태였습니다) - **밝은 모달에서 휠의 위아래 값이 묻히던 것** — 모달과 휠 카드가 둘 다 `white/24`라 흰 베일이 두 겹(약 42%) 쌓였어요. 표면을 중간 톤 토큰으로 고정 - **투표 목록만 글자가 한 단계 작던 것** — 같은 스페이스 탭인데 혼자 18/14였어요(나머지 24/16)
## 🚨 주요 고민 및 해결 과정 ### 문제 같은 증상이 **반대 방향의 요구**를 냈어요. 휠 카드는 어두운 화면에선 배경보다 밝아야 하고 밝은 모달에선 어두워야 하는데, 흰색 반투명은 뒤를 그대로 따라가 어느 한쪽에선 반드시 대비가 깨집니다. 고정 글자색으로는 해결이 안 되는 구조였어요. ### 해결 과정 표면을 **중간 톤(`surface-3`)으로 고정**했습니다. 중간 톤은 어두운 화면에선 밝게, 밝은 모달에선 어둡게 떨어져 배경과 무관하게 같은 대비를 냅니다. 페이드 마스크도 30/70 → 18/82로 완화했어요 — 보이는 3칸 중 위아래 2칸이 기존 페이드 구간에 통째로 걸려 마스크만으로도 절반쯤 지워지고 있었습니다. > **조용히 깨지는 자리 둘** > - `bg-primary-main`은 이 레포에 없는 유틸이에요(`@theme`가 `--color-primary = --primary-main`으로 매핑). 없는 유틸은 에러 없이 사라져서 화면을 보기 전까지 드러나지 않습니다 — `bg-primary`가 맞아요 > - Figma에서 받은 `pin.svg`는 `fill`·`stroke`가 `#1B1B32`로 박혀 있었어요. 같은 아이콘이 라임 칩(어두운 글자)과 프로필 칩(흰 글자) 양쪽에 올라가므로 `currentColor`로 바꿨습니다(레포의 다른 아이콘도 모두 그렇습니다) ### 의도적으로 하지 않은 것 - **알림 목록만 헤더 아래 16px** — `-mt-8 pt-4`로 레이아웃 여백을 되돌리고 있어요. 드리프트가 아니라 일부러 쓴 음수 마진이라 디자인 의도일 수 있어 그대로 뒀습니다 - **투표 마감 기한은 팝오버 유지** — 한 번 휠 카드로 바꿨다가 되돌렸어요. 굴려서 맞추는 값(합주 기간·일정 시간)과 딱 지정하는 값(마감 기한)은 성격이 달라 같은 UI로 묶는 게 맞지 않습니다 - **온보딩의 "선택한 순서대로 적용됩니다"** — 파트는 첫 번째만 대표고 장르는 순서가 의미 없어 사실과 다른 문구지만, 칩 배지가 큰 시각 요소라 디자인 판단이 필요해 남겨뒀어요 - **밴드 설정 3탭** — 범위 밖
## 📑 참고 문서/ ADR - 디자인: [Figma — 바텀시트 (3157:2232)](https://www.figma.com/design/aaWoovc3smAZNnGCt3SowV/bandco-personal-?node-id=3157-2232&m=dev) - 배경 전파 규칙: [CSS Backgrounds — The Canvas Background](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-backgrounds-3/#special-backgrounds)
## 💬 리뷰 요구사항 1. **`bleed: 'x' | 'all'` 네이밍과 경계** — `'x'`를 기본값으로 삼을 만한 화면이 더 있는지, `'all'`이 정말 로그인·검색·프로필 셋뿐인지 봐주세요 2. **헤더 높이 `ResizeObserver`** — 라우트 전환 시 1프레임 이전 값이 보일 수 있는 구조입니다. 실기기에서 탭 헤더 ↔ 일반 헤더를 오갈 때 튐이 보이는지 확인 부탁드려요 3. **휠 카드 표면을 `surface-3`로 고정** — 합주 공간 모달 가독성 때문인데 일정 추가 화면 톤도 같이 바뀝니다. 과하면 모달에서만 처리하는 쪽으로 좁힐 수 있어요 4. **장르의 "대표"** — 서버에 대표 플래그가 없어 "첫 번째 = 대표"를 프론트가 배열 순서로만 지킵니다. 이대로 둘지, 백엔드에 플래그를 둘지 의견 주세요 ### ✅ Test plan - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend exec tsc -b` — 통과 - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend run lint` — 0 errors (기존 경고 1건, 이번 변경과 무관한 `BandMemberSettings.tsx`) - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend exec prettier --check` — 통과 - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend test` — 447 passed · 1 skipped - [x] `TZ=UTC pnpm --dir frontend test` — 447 passed · 1 skipped (날짜·휠 변경이 있어 타임존을 바꿔 재실행) - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend run build` — 통과 - [x] 390×844 실측: 헤더 있는 화면 전부 간격 32px, 유령 스크롤 0 - [x] safe area 47/34px 시뮬레이션: 로그인·비밀번호 찾기 스크롤 0 (이전 81px) - [x] 헤더 제목을 줄바꿈시켰을 때 본문 상단이 121 → 133px로 추적 - [x] 바텀시트: 칩 35개로 늘렸을 때 시트 400px 유지, 내부만 277 → 470px 스크롤 - [ ] **실기기 미실행** — safe area·사파리 툴바 뒤 canvas는 데스크톱에서 재현이 안 돼 1·2번 항목은 기기 확인이 필요합니다 - [ ] **일정 추가 모달 화면 미확인** — `ScheduleCreateModal`이 아직 어느 라우트에도 연결돼 있지 않아 테스트로만 커버됩니다 ### 🔜 후속 - **일정 추가에서 날짜 변경** — 백엔드는 이미 가능해요(`startAt`/`endAt`이 ISO8601 전체, 검증은 `startAt < endAt`뿐). 자정 넘김도 `resolveEndAt`이 이미 처리합니다. 날짜 휠을 어떤 레이아웃으로 넣을지가 **디자인 결정 대기** 중이라 이번 범위에서 뺐어요 - **디자인 토큰 통일** — 같은 색이 세 가지 표기로 흩어져 있어요(`bg-surface-3` / `bg-[rgba(101,99,122,0.48)]` / `bg-[#65637a]/48`). 하드코딩 색상이 15개 파일에 있습니다. 토큰으로 모으면 글래스 강화 같은 변경을 토큰 값만 바꿔 처리할 수 있어 **디자이너와 방향 합의 후** 진행할 예정 - **밴드 설정 3탭 슬라이드** — 설정 화면 디자인 정리와 함께 별도 PR - **`TagSelectContent.handleToggle`** — setState 업데이터 안에서 부모 콜백을 호출해 React 경고가 납니다(기존 코드). 지금은 경고뿐이지만 업데이터는 순수해야 해서 정리 대상 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **개선 사항** * 화면별 여백과 안전 영역 처리가 조정되어 페이지 콘텐츠가 화면 크기와 헤더 높이에 더 잘 맞습니다. * 장르와 플레이 파트 선택 시 첫 항목이 핀 아이콘으로 대표 항목임을 표시하고, 선택 순서를 확인할 수 있습니다. * 일정 시간과 합주 기간 입력에 안내 문구를 추가했습니다. * 알림 편집 시 선택한 항목 수가 제목에 표시되며, 선택한 알림을 아이콘 버튼으로 삭제할 수 있습니다. * 날짜·시간 선택기와 투표 목록의 표시 방식 및 레이아웃을 개선했습니다.

author: diopmo399
body:
## Pourquoi

Quand le code ne dit pas comment l'application écrit (client OpenAPI généré, service générique, bundle illisible, code qu'on ne peut pas partager), l'intelligence fonctionnelle restait vide : 0 workflow, 0 transition. **Le réseau, lui, le dit** — à chaque run.

## Ce que ça fait

- **`RuntimeLearner`** (`src/functional/runtime-learning.ts`) :
  - une écriture acceptée (2xx) que rien ne décrit → **workflow appris** `VERBE:ENTITÉ` (verbe : libellé du bouton, segment d'action `/approve`, ou méthode HTTP ; route avec identifiants remplacés par `{param}`) ;
  - un code d'état lu dans une réponse (`{ "status": "PENDING" }`) → **état métier** ;
  - l'état de la ressource avant / après une écriture → **transition** (la réponse fait foi : une écriture acceptée qui ne change rien n'apprend rien).
- Appris = `RUNTIME_OBSERVED` (`RUNTIME_CONFIRMED` si l'écran montre aussi le nouvel état), et produit aussitôt des **objectifs de test**.
- **Gardé d'un run à l'autre** (`knowledge/functional/`, section `learned`) et repris au run suivant comme connaissance **HISTORICAL** : objectifs et signal du moteur de décision dès la première page — jamais une preuve tant que le run ne l'a pas revu.
- **Confidentialité** : seuls des codes d'état (valeur en capitales d'une clé `status` / `state` / `…Status`) ; jamais d'identifiant de ressource ni de saisie.
- **Rapport** : origine « appris du réseau » / « appris lors d'un run précédent » ; une énumération « …Status » sans transition (un code de résultat) listée à part au lieu d'une machine vide ; les erreurs seulement déclarées par l'OpenAPI résumées par opération.
- Config : `functionalIntelligence.runtimeLearning.enabled` (défaut : activé).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/runtime-learning.test.ts` : gabarits de route et intention ; workflow + états + transition appris ; écriture acceptée sans changement → aucune transition ; même route, autre état → deux workflows ; confirmation à l'écran, objectifs, persistance et reprise comme historique ; désactivation ; lecture des codes d'état seulement.
- E2E Chromium : **deux runs sans code ni contrat** — le premier apprend `APPROVE:REGISTRATION` et confirme PENDING → APPROVED ; le second part de l'historique et choisit « Approve » pour l'objectif.
- typecheck, lint, prettier ; unit + integration : 943 passés, 2 ignorés.

author: betha2516
body:
## Resumen

- **Balanceo binario (sección 8):** se elimina la clase MUERTOS (0.3 % de los registros) y `GRAVEDAD` pasa a ser binaria (SOLO DAÑOS vs HERIDOS). Se submuestrea SOLO DAÑOS al 50 % con `RandomUnderSampler` y se sobremuestrea HERIDOS con **SMOTENC** hasta 50/50. Las filas se mezclan para que los registros sintéticos no queden concentrados en los últimos folds.
- **Modelos con `GridSearchCV` (sección 11):** el split 70/30 se reemplaza por validación cruzada de 10 folds con `f1_macro`. Se comparan seis modelos: árbol de decisión, Random Forest, XGBoost, KNN, SVM y red neuronal. Para cada uno se reporta el f1 de Train CV y Test CV para revisar overfitting y underfitting.
- **Verificación con datos reales (11.8):** el mejor modelo se reevalúa con los datos reales sin balancear (`X_real`, `Y_real`) usando un `Pipeline` de imblearn que balancea solo dentro del fold de entrenamiento. Así se evita la fuga de información de SMOTENC.
- **Conclusiones (11.9):** tabla comparativa y análisis de los resultados.
- `docs/` deja de versionarse (se agrega a `.gitignore`).

## Resultados (f1 macro, CV de 10 folds)

| Modelo | Train CV | Test CV | Brecha |
|---|---|---|---|
| KNN | 0.967 | **0.814** | 0.153 |
| Random Forest | 0.895 | 0.805 | 0.089 |
| XGBoost | 0.916 | 0.798 | 0.118 |
| Árbol | 0.911 | 0.767 | 0.144 |
| SVM | 0.822 | 0.765 | 0.057 |
| Red neuronal | 0.779 | 0.750 | 0.029 |

Con datos reales (proporción ~80/20, balanceo solo dentro del fold), el f1 de KNN baja a **0.671 ± 0.007**. Esa es la estimación realista del desempeño.

## Cómo probar

- [ ] Ejecutar el notebook completo en Colab (la SVM puede tardar entre 20 y 40 minutos).
- [ ] Revisar que la sección 8 deje dos clases al 50 %.
- [ ] Revisar la tabla comparativa de la sección 11.7 y la verificación de la sección 11.8.

author: amielnoy
body:
A function called over HTTP logs to `prod`. **A function called by an agent logs to `preview`.**

So the entire agent-driven half of this system — every interview, every `submitLead` the model triggers, every calendar write behind a completed conversation — is recorded only in the draft. The nightly job was archiving production alone.

## It cost two investigations in one day

A visitor reported a failed interview on Android. Production logs showed nothing, and I concluded the function had never been called and the fault lay between the agent and the tool.

**The run was in `preview` the whole time.** By the time I looked there it had aged out — Base44 keeps roughly a day of draft logs — so the cause is now unknowable, and the conclusion I reported was never supported by the evidence I had.

## The change

A second step: same credentials, same window, `LOG_ENV: preview` into `logs/preview`, riding the same upload.

`continue-on-error` like its sibling, because an unarchived day is a gap in a record and not a broken build — a nightly job that reddens the badge is one everyone learns to ignore.

Two contract cases pin both halves:

- the draft is archived into **its own directory**, not over production's
- it **cannot fail the run**

`A-53` records it, including the part worth keeping: *when logs show nothing, confirm you are reading the environment the work ran in before concluding the work did not happen.*

`lint` · `typecheck` · **987 vitest** (8 opt-in skipped) — all green. Contract 431 → 433.

body:
## Issue

Related to [ODE-620](https://linear.app/hugo-marin/issue/ODE-620/ai-03-un-error-al-sugerir-titulo-no-corrompe-el-documento-no-deja) and its copy follow-up [ODE-653](https://linear.app/hugo-marin/issue/ODE-653/ai-03-follow-up-normalize-title-suggestion-error-copy).

## What changed

- Added a request-generation guard to `RenameWritingModal`. A late success or error from a prior document/opening is discarded, and its `finally` cannot clear the current document's loading state.
- Extended AI-01's existing URL-routed fetch proof with a real web `EditorShell`, real `webAIService`, and real title-suggestions route. It covers provider timeout, 503, network rejection, visible error/loading reset, preserved local title/body, and retry.
- Added a Desk-shaped retained-modal A→B proof with a positive suggestion control, then stale success and error responses while B is loading.
- Updated AI-03's capability row and harness catalog. The status is `PARTIAL_INTEGRATION`: the desktop `desktopAIService` absolute `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` plus Bearer path is not exercised.

The UI error copy remains unchanged; ODE-653 owns its normalization.

## Reuse Check

Extended the canonical lifecycle owner, `RenameWritingModal`, and reused AI-01's existing URL router plus `tests/support/editor-shell-harness.tsx`. The test calls the real web service and route; it does not use `aiServiceDouble.suggestTitle` or add another router/service.

## How to test

```bash
npm test -- tests/integration/ai/suggest-title-lifecycle.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run ops:status:drift:strict
npm run ops:delivery:gate
```

## Gate outputs

- `npm run typecheck` — PASS (exit 0).
- `npm run lint` — PASS (exit 0; no warnings in the changed files).
- `npm test -- tests/integration/ai/suggest-title-lifecycle.test.ts` — PASS (12 tests).
- `npm test` — PASS (333 files; 2,395 passed, 10 expected failures, 3 skipped; 178.94s).
- `npm run ops:status:drift:strict` — PASS (499 built-ledger issues aligned with `origin/main`).
- `npm run ops:delivery:gate` — PASS (traceability passed; performance gate skipped because this change has no performance contract).

The live pre-fix mutation made both A→B cases fail: `la respuesta de A no debe limpiar el loading de B: expected undefined to be truthy`.

Din auditul pre-vânzare (P1 copy + decizia „Trial 7 zile”). Conține și #140, #145, #146 (dependențe) până la merge.

## Texte (8 limbi)
- AI: „AI inclus pentru planuri pas cu pas (sau cheia ta)” — niciodată „full”/„nelimitat” (test de politică actualizat).
- **Mișcare Pro** apare pe /pricing, în cardul din Setări și în tabelul de comparație; FAQ-ul de pe landing menționează biblioteca de exerciții gratuită.
- Anual: în loc de linia de suport repetată → „O singură plată pe an — fără taxe lunare”.
- Setări → Plan: rândul AI = „Planificator pe dispozitiv” vs „AI inclus + bonus de rang, sau cheia ta”.

## Trial (opțional)
`VITE_PRO_TRIAL_DAYS` (1–30) → „Primele N zile gratis · Dacă anulezi în perioada de probă, nu plătești nimic.” + buton „Începe N zile gratuit” — doar pentru conturi care n-au avut abonament. Nesetat = niciun trial afișat.

**De făcut de tine:** activezi trial-ul de 7 zile pe **ambele** variante Lemon (lunar + anual), apoi setezi `VITE_PRO_TRIAL_DAYS=7` în variabilele build-ului (GitHub → Settings → Variables, unde sunt și celelalte `VITE_*`).

## Verificat
Vizual pe /pricing cu trial=7. Teste: `trialDays`, rândul Mișcare (12 rânduri), politica AI, pagina în RO. lint, tsc, vitest 1771 ✓, build, secret-scan.

body:
## Summary
Five new Home widgets, inspired by the KosherKotlin demo's luach (in the gallery, not in the default layout):
- **לימוד יומי**: parsha of the week, daf yomi Bavli and Yerushalmi; a click opens the text in a new tab (Chumash at the parsha via its Parasha alt TOC, Gemara at `דף X.`).
- **הזמן הבא**: the next zman with a countdown and the two after it; a click points the Earth/sky/solar system at it.
- **מועדים קרובים**: coming Shabbatot, festivals, fasts and Rashei Chodashim with candle lighting / havdala / fast times; a click moves every widget to that day.
- **תפילת היום**: mashiv haruach / morid hatal, vesein tal umatar, tachanun, hallel, yaaleh veyavo, al hanissim, omer.
- **מולד וקידוש לבנה**: the coming molad and the Kiddush Levana window per the community's opinion.

Shabbat candle lighting and havdala move out of the zmanim widget (`candleLightingTime` / `havdalahTime`) so festivals use the same times; the calendar's frame becomes the shared `PanelCard`.

KosherKotlin 3.0.0's `TefilaRules.isMashivHaruachRecited` throws (kdroidFilter/KosherKotlin#28); the widget computes the season itself until a release ships the fix.

Draft: visual pass on every widget still in progress.

## Test plan
- [x] `LuachDataTest` (parsha/daf places, tefila lines, events times, next zmanim, Kiddush Levana window)

## Summary

I3.1b of v0.6.0 I3 publishes the draft 0.6 public contract for `get_service_dependencies_by_locality`, as frozen in the I3 decision record (#386). It contains contract only: no service method, Cypher, projection, REST route or MCP registration (those are I3.2/I3.3).

**`app/architecture_intelligence/locality_contracts.py`** holds closed Pydantic models:
- **Request:** `LocalityQueryRequest` and `LocalityEvidenceRequest`, combined as the `mode`-discriminated `ServiceDependenciesByLocalityRequest` (D3, D11).
- **Envelope:** `LocalityAnswer` (D2, D9). It reuses `Producer`, `SnapshotRef`, `Outcome` and `EvidenceRecord`, and never the 0.5 tool, claim or limitation enums.
- **Payloads:**
  - `ServiceDependenciesByLocalityData` (D10): inventory, candidates and pairs, localities, provider groups, unresolved owners, selection and comparison;
  - `ScopedLocalityEvidenceData` (D11).
- **Cursor:** D5 encode/decode, including a canonical-form check.
- **Page size:** the D4 `candidate_page_size` rule, `min(500, ⌊2000/S⌋)`.

**Schemas.** `schemas/architecture_intelligence/v0.6/service-dependencies-by-locality-{request,answer}.schema.json` are generated by the extended `schema_export.py`. The v0.5 schema files are byte-identical and their frozen tests are untouched.

**Decision record D16** adds nine I3.1b clarifications:
- **D16.4 (owner decision):** a provider filter narrows `localities`.
- **D16.1 (needs review):** evidence mode uses `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` for both `PARTIAL` and `NOT_ANSWERED`, so the outcome rule differs by mode.
- The others cover request shape, assessment field placement, ordering, inventory fields, ref kinds, cursor form, and which rules are schema-expressible versus model-only.

**Small refactor:** `contracts._ENVIRONMENT_PATTERN` is now public (`ENVIRONMENT_PATTERN`) so the new module can reuse it. The generated v0.5 schemas are unchanged.

## Tests

- **`test_locality_contracts_schema_frozen.py`:** the committed schemas must equal the generated output byte for byte, and generation must be deterministic.
- **`test_locality_contracts.py`** (107 tests). The valid answers are hand-written in the shape of the rehearsal's C1 run, not produced by code.

Replaces the onboarding app with the Pricing Strategy Intelligence Engine.

## What's in it
- **Engine** (`src/lib/pricingEngine.js`): a client-side rules engine, with no backend and no LLM. It reads a CSV of internal pricing and competitor data (one row per SKU × region × channel × period) and compares the latest two periods.

  - **Analyst:** a chat-style console that answers the supported questions from the loaded data.
  - **Data:** drag-and-drop CSV, column coverage, data gaps, and a row preview.
- Every statement is tagged FACT / SIGNAL / HYPOTHESIS / RECOMMENDATION. A missing column is reported as a data gap rather than guessed.
- Severity colors pass contrast and colorblind-separation checks, and each one is paired with an icon and a text label.
- Ships with a synthetic sample dataset (made-up SKUs and "Competitor A/B/C") and a CSV template download.

## Summary
- preserve current server installation state when a factory reset is merely queued
- perform destructive cleanup only after the ESP32 reports factory_reset success through the existing result service

body:
Vorher: Wer im heruntergeladenen Programm (v0.1.0) sein Passwort vergaß, kam nicht mehr hinein. `theta reset-password` gab es nur im Quellcode, und jedes Argument startete einfach eine zweite Website. Die Anleitung empfahl auf dem Mac „Rechtsklick → Öffnen“, was ab macOS 15 nicht mehr hilft, und unter Linux einen Doppelklick, der dort meist nichts Sichtbares tut.

Nachher: `./theta reset-password deine@adresse.de` (Windows: `.\theta.exe reset-password …`) setzt ein neues Passwort, auch während Theta läuft. `backup`, `restore`, `export` und `hilfe` funktionieren genauso. Jede ZIP bekommt eine `LIESMICH.txt` für ihr eigenes System: macOS mit „Trotzdem öffnen“ und der `xattr`-Abkürzung, Linux mit Start im Terminal, Windows mit SmartScreen und CRLF-Zeilenenden. README, Download-Seite und FAQ der Website sowie die Release-Notes für 0.1.1 passen dazu.

## How

- Die Befehle liegen jetzt in `src/commands.ts`. `src/cli.ts` (`bun run theta …`) und das Programm (`src/desktop.ts`) nutzen sie gemeinsam. Das Programm behandelt nur bekannte Befehlswörter als Befehl, alles andere startet wie bisher die Website.
- `openDatabase` wartet bis zu 5 Sekunden auf eine Sperre (`busy_timeout`), damit ein Befehl schreiben kann, während der Server läuft.
- Fehlversuche beim Anmelden zählen pro Passwort. Ein Reset hebt deshalb die Sperre nach 10 Fehlversuchen auf, sonst wäre das neue Passwort bis zu 15 Minuten abgewiesen worden.
- Der Release-Smoke-Test ruft im gebauten Programm auch `hilfe` und `backup` auf, auf allen vier Systemen.
- Version 0.1.1, Release-Text in `docs/releases/v0.1.1.md`.

## Geprüft

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun test`: 234 Tests grün. Darunter neue Tests für Reset, Sperre nach Reset, Sicherung, Einspielen und Hilfe. Der Sperr-Test schlägt ohne die Änderung in `src/auth.ts` fehl.
- Das gebaute Linux-Programm habe ich mit allen Befehlen aus einem anderen Ordner getestet, mit und ohne laufenden Server. Eine zweite Prüfung lief unabhängig davon. Der Windows-Build hat CRLF in der `LIESMICH.txt` und `.\theta.exe` als Befehl.
- `docker exec <Container> bun src/cli.ts reset-password …` funktioniert in einem Image aus diesem Stand.

Nicht an der Quelle geprüft (aus Wissen geschrieben, kein Mac oder Windows hier):
- die genauen deutschen Menünamen „Systemeinstellungen → Datenschutz & Sicherheit → Trotzdem öffnen“
- ob macOS die mitgelieferten Bibliotheken in `node_modules` noch einmal einzeln sperrt (die Anleitung nennt den Fall vorsichtshalber)
- „cmd“ in der Explorer-Adresszeile
- `.\theta.exe` folgt dem dokumentierten Verhalten von PowerShell, wurde aber nicht ausgeführt.

body:
## Summary

Adds an `inspect-runtime` skill. It lets agents reach a running app's live `Application` through the Engine 2.23 devtools hook (`globalThis[Symbol.for('playcanvas.inspector')]`), without adding `window.app` or debug code to the app.

**Merge decision:** in 2.23.0 only the debug build announces apps. Release, profiler, and minified builds build the hook's `{ version, revision }` from an import that sits inside an `#if _DEBUG` block, so the call throws a `ReferenceError` that the Engine swallows. The fix, engine#9646, is merged on `main` and backported to `release-2.23` (`f059dc005`), but it isn't released yet. The skill states this as a 2.23.0 gotcha. Drop that line once the next 2.23 patch ships, or hold this PR until then.

- **`skills/inspect-runtime`**
  - `SKILL.md`: how to attach, what to read, how to pause and step a frame, and the optional `@playcanvas/inspector` panel (dev builds only, and destroy it before pixel captures).
  - `scripts/devtools-hook.js`: a plain init script that records apps in `globalThis.__playcanvasApps`. It chains a hook defined before it and installs only once.
- **Cross-references:** `apply-conventions`, `assemble-scene`, `configure-animation`, and `verify-pixels` now point their "measure in the running app" steps at `inspect-runtime`. `build-app` notes that `devtools` defaults to `true`.
- **Inventory:** README row and context-cost figures, plus the Claude plugin `skills` list.

## Package contracts

- `playcanvas` 2.23.0: I probed six builds. Only `playcanvas/debug` and `build/playcanvas.dbg.mjs` call the hook.
- `@playcanvas/react` 0.11.7: creates its app with `new Application(canvas, …)` and doesn't pass `devtools`, so it gets the default `true`. Checked by reading the source, not run.
- `@playcanvas/web-components` 0.26.0: creates `AppBase` with `AppOptions`, which defaults `devtools` to `true`. Checked by reading the source, not run.
- `@playcanvas/inspector` 0.2.0: public API only (`Inspector`, `EntityInspector`, `visible`, `paused`, `step()`, `destroy()`).

## Manual smoke test

1. Serve a page that imports `playcanvas/build/playcanvas.dbg.mjs` and creates an app with one entity, then open it in a browser with `skills/inspect-runtime/scripts/devtools-hook.js` added as an init script. Expected: `globalThis.__playcanvasApps.size` is `1`, and its value is `{ version: '2.23.0', revision: 'cfef43d', protocol: 1 }`.
2. In the page, read the entity's world position after the next `frameend`. Expected: it matches the position the app set.
3. Reload the page. Expected: the map again holds exactly one app.
4. Switch the import to `playcanvas/build/playcanvas.mjs` and reload. Expected on 2.23.0: the map stays empty (the engine#9646 bug).

## Checks

- [ ] Repository tests pass on Node 24. (28/28 plus the `tsc` smoke compile pass locally on Node 22.22.0; Node 24 wasn't run. The new `test/devtools-hook.test.mjs` covers registration, `devtools: false`, chaining, and installing only once.)
- [x] Every changed skill passes the Agent Skills validator.
- [x] Direct Engine, React, and Web Components references remain aligned where applicable. (No reference files changed; the skill doesn't depend on the surface.)
- [x] Runtime or screenshot evidence is attached for visual or interactive changes. (Headless Chromium with SwiftShader, debug build: registration, a position read after `frameend`, and re-registration after reload all passed. No screenshots, since nothing visual changed.)

body:
## Change

The atlas globe now looks like a hand-wound ball of yarn, and the countries and oceans are still readable on it.

- **Countries** are wool patches in six earthy colors. Colors are chosen with a greedy coloring over the TopoJSON neighbor graph so bordering countries differ. They are assigned on the 1:110m map and carried by name into the 1:50m and 1:10m tiers, so a country keeps its color as you zoom.
- **Ocean** is a denim-blue ground.
- **Strands**: 15 bands of parallel strands are wound along great circles in many directions. They are fixed to the globe, turn with it, and later bands lie over earlier ones. Each strand is a small circle around its band's axis. Only the arc facing the viewer is sampled, and strands get finer with zoom so their on-screen thickness stays roughly constant.
- **Shading**: strands are neutral grays blended with `mix-blend-mode: hard-light` inside an isolated group. They shade whatever wool or ocean color lies beneath, and the opaque gray still lets upper bands hide lower ones.
- **Details**: borders are cream running stitches, coastlines a darker cord, the rim fuzzy (turbulence displacement), and a loose yarn end trails off the ball at default zoom. The flat map uses the same wool and strands.
- **Performance**:
  - The ball is drawn in its own background SVG (`aria-hidden`, separate compositing layer). The interactive `.globe-svg` with routes, markers and labels sits on top, so animated routes no longer re-rasterize every strand.
  - Strands are projected with direct orthographic math instead of d3 path resampling.
  - The idle sway repaints at about 30 fps.
- The decorative "ONE PLANET" caption now shows only when the whole ball is in view. At zoom it overlapped the help text, which was already happening before this change but became more visible on the darker globe.

No new dependencies. The 1:110m globe still works from `dist/offline.html`.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 17 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- `npm run test:browser`: exit 0, including "Standalone HTML opens offline", the globe zoom/keyboard checks, axe accessibility checks and "No browser JavaScript errors".
- Headless Chromium (software raster) frame timing:
  - Spin paused: 16.7 ms median frame, about 8% CPU.
  - Idle sway: about 33 ms (the intended 30 fps throttle).
  - The first unoptimized version of the yarn ran at 50 ms per frame on the same setup.
- Screenshots: `docs/screenshots/atlas-desktop.png` and `atlas-mobile.png` are regenerated by the browser suite. I also checked the default globe, 1:50m zoom, the flat map, a journey-page mini map and a 390 px mobile view.

No content changes. Routes, data and sources are untouched.

author: schmichael
body:
Upstream version: https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/pull/28620 (tests actually run here)

## Description

This commit proposes a significant new scheduling feature for Nomad that I've been referring to as duration-aware drains.

**The Problem**

Draining nodes is a regular cluster maintenance operation. Workloads with long shutdowns are a common pain point with draining because a single running workload may block a drain indefinitely. Even when using all of the timeouts and tools available in Nomad - max_run_duration, kill_timeout, drain deadline, etc - in order to meet user expectations, some workloads may need 24+ hours of time to complete and allow the drain to finish. In most clusters these workloads represent the long tail of all workloads which means each draining node may be likely to have a small number of them and delay nearly all drains.

Operationally long drains are a minor annoyance, but leaving a long draining node lightly loaded is incredibly inefficient and expensive.

**The Solution: Duration-aware Drains**

For clusters with heterogeneous batch workloads there may be many candidate workloads that are *guaranteed* to finish before the drain deadline. Duration-aware drains allow placing these workloads onto draining nodes. This feature is *opt-in* with a new drain parameter.

The scheduler makes the following comparison to determine if a time-bounded batch workload is eligible for placement on a draining node:

```
now.Add(max_run_duration).Add(max_shutdown) < drain_deadline
```

2 complexities should be immediately obvious:

1. `now`?! In _my_ scheduler?!
2. `max_shutdown` is not an actual parameter anywhere in Nomad

`now` is unavoidable in this feature since `max_run_duration` is based off the _allocation's_ `CreateTime`. The new allocation hasn't been created yet! Only when updating existing batch jobs do we know the base time of their `max_run_duration` in advance because we use the original allocation's `CreateTime`. A `BackfillBuffer` parameter was introduced as a scheduling-time and clock-skew tolerance between scheduler and plan applier. Schedulers use the following as the drain deadline in the above comparison:

```
drain_deadline - backfill_buffer
```

So if the drain deadline is 15:00:00 and the backfill buffer is 30s, the scheduler will only schedule jobs that will complete by 14:59:30.

The _plan applier_ meanwhile, which serializes all placements, _ignores_ the backfill buffer. This means that if by the time the plan applier sees the workload above the max run time would be 14:59:45, well into the buffer, the plan applier still accepts it.

Without an appropriate buffer the slightest latency or clock skew between schedulers and plan appliers could lead to the pathological case where schedulers keep resubmitting plans they think are valid and the plan applier keeps rejecting them.

`max_shutdown` is unfortunately not a single obvious workload parameter in Nomad. The logic to calculate it can be found in nomad/structs/drain.go:MaxShutdown and is approximately:

```
alloc.shutdown_delay + leader.shutdown_delay + leader.kill_timeout +
max(task.shutdown_delay + kill_timeout)
```

The complexity is because all non-leader tasks are shutdown concurrently, so only the slowest-to-shutdown task's parameters should be considered.

**Correctness**

Nomad's scheduler has never been completely consistent:

https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/commit/d36d420a71fe193a8bb9bd335dcffc39c1e034fd

Node updates concurrent with plan application may make placements invalid. Fixing this inconsistency would require a second plan-applier-esque placement validation pass in the FSM.

This has never been fixed because the window is small, and there are significant performance gains from optimistically placing allocations without the second validation pass. To my knowledge there has never been an observed case of this inconsistency having a detrimental effect, but I acknowledge it would be difficult to detect and report.

Duration-aware drains are not only susceptible to this but in some ways widen the window because they depend on more aspects of nodes (drains as opposed to just eligibility) that could be concurrently updated with plan application.

**Q & A**

Q Why use the drain's deadline instead of the existing allocations
  deadlines?

A Long running workloads may not have an explicit max_run_duration set.
  Using the drain deadline gives the operator a single value to consider
  and makes the behavior much easier to predict.

Q Why explicitly only allow batch and sysbatch when max_run_duration
  already enforces that implicitly?

A I wanted to make the restriction implicit and not dependent on
  max_run_duration's behavior. Not a hard requirement though.

Q Why the high (+10) boost for backfilling? Overriding a -100 weight
  affinity against a node seems bad?

A I wanted to ensure backfilling was always preferred over bin packing,
  and the way nomad averages all scores makes it impossible to have 1
  score only interact with 1 other. I think this behavior is preferable as
  if the job absolutely must not be placed on a node, it should use a
  constraint instead of an affinity.

## Description

Adds `steam.overlay.onGameOverlayActivated(handler)`, exposing Steam's `GameOverlayActivated_t` callback so a game can pause while the overlay is open.

```typescript
const unsubscribe = steam.overlay.onGameOverlayActivated(({ active, userInitiated, appId }) => {
  active ? game.pause() : game.resume();
});
```

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Test improvement

## Related Issues

Fixes #89

## Motivation and Context

The library can open the overlay but can't tell when it opens or closes. `GameOverlayActivated_t` is the only signal the SDK provides for this, so it can't be polled.

## Changes Made

- `onGameOverlayActivated(handler)` returns an unsubscribe function. The event is `{ active, userInitiated, appId }`.
- New internal `SteamPushCallback` helper that registers the callback with Steam:
  - Subscribing before `init()` works; registration happens once `init()` succeeds.
  - A handler that throws or rejects is logged and doesn't stop the others.
  - Cleanup is safe to call more than once, and the callback stays valid after `koffi.reset()`.
- `shutdown()` unregisters the callback before `SteamAPI_Shutdown()`.

author: paulsavignano
body:
Fixes #43.

An output scan can see a temporary dangling symlink while an owned command removes its target before the alias. Previously, that observation immediately terminated the command and discarded the failing path, errno and captured failure output. The verifier now reports the first path/cause and permits complete running-command scans to retry within one fixed second. Baseline and final scans remain strict; persistent invalid links, escaping aliases, output limits, cancellation and identity-checked cleanup remain enforced.

Failed commands retain their actual exit/signal, cleanup errors and captured stdout/stderr in the existing private content-addressed evidence store. Bytes still buffered inside a killed child remain unavailable. The synthetic reproduction establishes this verifier defect; it does not identify the original report's first triggering path or event order.

Validation: deterministic real filesystem teardown, command-error, cancellation, persistent-link and positive-byte-limit cases; a separate injected-deadline regression proving late complete scans are rejected; required contributor checks, build and complete package inventory/confidentiality review. Independent consequential review covered the exact source and archive. Package metadata advances to 0.3.9 for the supported correction.

Previously kind_lower was computed only for the privileged-scope authorization comparison, but the original (possibly mixed-case) self.kind value was what got persisted to Postgres. author: adc77
body:
## What this fixes

The guard had fourteen holes, each one a way a run could report `passed` while depending on the host. The worst was the reason this branch exists:

A handler reading the clock through libc reported `status: passed` while the run digest **changed on every replay**.

That is the one guarantee this library exists to provide, and it was silently false. There was no test for it.

## Closed, each verified to fail with the right code and no side effect

| leak | fault |
|---|---|
| `ctypes` dlopen/dlsym, including libc `clock_gettime` | `real_io` / `ctypes` |
| `time.perf_counter`, `time.process_time` | `real_clock` |
| `random.Random` instance methods | `unseeded_random` |
| `open`, `os.open`, `os.stat`, `os.listdir`, `os.scandir` | `file_read` |
| `os.mkdir`, `os.rename`, `os.remove`, `shutil.copy` | `file_write` |

Only `random.Random.random` had been patched before, so a fresh instance walked straight past it.

Two facts established by probing the interpreter rather than by reading the docs: `ctypes.dlopen` and `ctypes.dlsym` **do** raise audit events, which is what makes libc reachable to the hook at all; `os.stat` raises **none**, so it is patched directly. `os.scandir` raises its event when the iterator is consumed, not when it is created.

## The filesystem is now a policy

Reads and writes are refused unless the path is allowlisted. The builtin `open` reports a mode string and `os.open` reports integer flags, so write intent is read differently for each. Paths are exact, never prefixes.

Interpreter directories are allowlisted for reads, so a lazy `import` inside a handler still works. Without that, `import subprocess` faulted on the module file before the real leak was reached.

Reads a handler did make are recorded in the artifact under `fs_reads`, deliberately **outside** the digest. A read is provenance about the host, not an input to the run, and a run that read nothing leaves the key out so existing artifacts stay byte-comparable.

`allow_read` and `allow_write` are the documented way for a product to declare a fixture path, and a registration made before `install_guards` now survives the policy reset.

## Four bugs found while implementing this

All fixed, all recorded in `BUILD_LOG.md` rather than quietly patched:

- `os.path.realpath` calls `os.stat`, which is the patched hook, so path resolution recursed until the stack blew.
- `allow_read` before `install_guards` was discarded by the policy reset, so a product could register a path and still be refused.
- Interpreter paths resolved at `Policy` construction ran before `_norm` and `_REAL_STAT` were defined.
- Interpreter paths were only populated on reset, so `is_interpreter` was wrong whenever consulted before install.

Two existing tests asserted the old permissive behaviour. Both now express the policy; the test's own I/O runs inside `seam.guard.trusted()`, which is what that context manager is for.

## The README now says what the guard is not

Exit codes, the fault table, and plainly: **this is not a sandbox.** It refuses the listed standard-library paths; it does not contain a process. A name bound before `install_guards()` still points at the original object, and a C extension can reach libc without going through `ctypes`.

## CI

The 38-test claim had only ever been checked on one Mac. The workflow runs the suite on ubuntu and macos against 3.13 and 3.14, re-runs the checkout proof and asserts its pinned digest, and confirms the wheel builds, installs, and ships the proof cases.

A second job asserts that **the audit events the guard depends on actually fire on the runner**. Without it, a platform missing an event would silently weaken the guard while the suite stayed green.

## Verification

- Suite: **38 tests, green**, Python 3.13.9 on macOS.
- All fourteen escapes re-probed after the final refactor: closed, each with the expected code and `op`, and none leaving a file on disk.
- The libc case run twice: faults, exits 2, same digest both times.
- Every CI command was executed locally before being committed. The `os.scandir` check failed on the first attempt and was corrected.

**Not done:** generator ports, fault schedules, multi-process, and the LLM grader remain v2, as before. No 32 MiB artifact fixture.

author: wingedguardian
body: ## What `tests/test_observability/test_eval_staleness.py` builds fixture timestamps as exactly N days ago. The query under test (`src/genesis/observability/snapshots/eval_staleness.py`) floors `julianday('now') - jd` to whole days. After SQLite's millisecond rounding and the float subtraction, an exact N-day age lands at N or just under it, so it can floor to N - 1 and fail an assert like `days_ago == 1`. Measured directly in SQLite with no delay between insert and query: an exact 1-day age floored to 0 in 9,685 of 20,000 trials. The same happens at 20 and 45 days. At real test speed it is rare, but it failed a CI run on an unrelated PR. ## Fix `_ago()` subtracts one extra minute, so every whole-day fixture age sits inside its day. That one change covers all call sites, including asserts at 20 and 45 days. The production query is unchanged: flooring to full elapsed days is the intended convention, and only exact-N-day fixtures hit the edge. ## Verification - The test file passes 31 of 31, in 6 repeated runs. - `ruff` is clean. - With the offset applied, the direct SQLite measurement gave 0 wrong out of 20,000. E2E: none (test-only change, no runtime surface) Ledger: 02bf5631ec4b49238c5080891c57687a ---

body:
## Context

Operators have no durable view of how much index storage each provider uses. go-indexer-core adds a background metering scan to the pebble value store (ipni/go-indexer-core#262). This exposes it through the admin API.

## Proposed Changes

- Admin endpoints: `GET /metering` (whole-store totals), `GET /metering/providers`, `GET /metering/providers/{providerID}`, `GET /metering/scan`, `GET /metering/scan/{providerID}`, and `POST /metering/scan` to start a scan. Returns 204 when no scan has completed, 202 on trigger, 409 when a scan is already running, and 501 when the value store cannot meter. A failed scan reports its error in the scan status.
- Admin client methods for each endpoint.
- New `Indexer.Metering` config: `Enabled`, `ScanInterval`, `ScanBatchSize` (default 1000000), `TimeFill` (default 0.1), `ExportProviderMetrics`. Not reloadable, off by default. Passed to pebble only. With `ValueStoreType` `relayx`, metering is configured on relayx and the admin API forwards to it.
- `doc/config.md` documents the new section.

Depends on ipni/go-indexer-core#262 and the relayx metering PR. Both pins are pseudo-versions for now. Replace them with released tags before merging.

## Tests

`TestMeteringNotSupported` and `TestMeteringAPI` in `server/admin`, plus config default and populate tests. `go test ./...` passes (end-to-end tests skipped as in CI), and `go vet`, staticcheck and `go mod tidy` are clean.

## Revert Strategy

Change is safe to revert. Metering is off unless enabled, and its records live under their own key prefix in the pebble store.
