author: trosper3
body:
This PR makes the default solvers for DFA, NFA and Prime Factorization return answers their own verifiers accept, and adds a way for solvers to explain their result separately from the answer. It builds on #626 and will retarget to CSharpAPI once #624 and #626 merge.

Features:
- DFA and NFA solvers now return the plain list of states (e.g. `1,2`) instead of a sentence, so solving and then verifying the answer gives True. When the input is rejected, `/solve` returns `{}` like other solvers.
- The NFA solver now returns one accepting run, the same one the table visualization shows first, and stops searching once it finds it. Its description and complexity notes were updated to match; the worst-case complexity is unchanged.
- Prime Factorization now uses the classical trial division solver by default, so solving works without the external quantum service. This matches the other quantum problems. Shor's algorithm is still available as a solver.
- Solvers can now report a result with three parts: a status (Solved, NoSolution, NotFound, Timeout), the answer (or nothing), and a readable reason. This is so an MCP tool or the frontends never have to guess what `{}` means, and it is the groundwork for the structured solve endpoint in #618. Solvers that haven't been updated report "Unclassified" with their usual output, so nothing else changes.
- DFA and NFA use this to keep the explanations they used to put in their answer, e.g. "The DFA has no transition from state 1 on 'b', so it rejects the input."
- The whitespace test from #626 no longer skips these three problems.

Notes for reviewers:
- The detailed result isn't exposed by any endpoint yet; `/solve` output is unchanged apart from the DFA/NFA/Prime Factorization fixes above. Exposing it is #618.
- NoSolution means the solver proved no answer exists, so only exact solvers should report it. Approximation and heuristic solvers should report NotFound. This is my proposed answer to #605.

Issue Handling:
Closes ReduxISU/Redux#625

Mobile and tablet pass over every route in `main.tsx` and the dialogs, at 360×740, iPhone 14, Pixel 7, iPad mini, iPad Air, iPad Pro 12.9 and an Android tablet (800×1280), each upright and on its side, plus iPad split view (590×820).

Draft: the session hit its weekly usage stop (45%), so I'm handing this over with the list below.

## Fixed
- **Touch targets everywhere.** The coarse-pointer rules now sit outside Tailwind's layers, so they win over mouse-sized utilities (`sm:min-h-9`, `h-[26px]`, `min-w-[26px]`). A phone on its side or a tablet is wider than `sm` but is still used with a finger. Labels of tick boxes and radios, colour, range and file inputs are now 44 px too. Text fields keep 16 px text, so iOS doesn't zoom in.
- **Home:** each row shows only its main action (Open or Start layout). Everything else goes in a ⋯ menu (`ui/MoreMenu.tsx`): Share…, Export .zip, Template for new layouts, Move or copy…, Rename…, Delete. The menu works by tap, mouse and keyboard. The All · Mine · club filter wraps onto more lines instead of hiding clubs off the side.
- **Editor (tablet, Edit):** below 1024 px the task tabs get their own header row; before, they overlapped "Share picture" on an iPad mini. Below 1280 px, Share picture shows only its icon. The edit toolbar wraps instead of scrolling, and "To front" no longer overprints "Snap". The sheet visibility box has a 44 px target. The Mouse readout is hidden on touch screens. Module library row actions were hover-only; they now always show on touch. The Modules "Rotate ▸" submenu opens on tap.
- **Room designer:** on a phone held upright, the tools sit in a row along the top, then the map, then the inspector. On its side, the panels are narrower. The header and the Show row wrap, so Undo, Redo and Save were cut off before and aren't now. Safe-area padding was added.

- Install the app: iPads that report themselves as Macs with touch are already handled by `isAppleMobile` (unit-tested in `pwa/test/install.test.ts`).

- `e2e/test/mobileRoutes.spec.ts`: for each route, plus every admin and club-admin tab, on all 15 device sizes. It fails on sideways scrolling, on content cut off at the right edge, and on any control under 44×44 px. Links in running text are exempt. `MOBILE_SURVEY=<file>` reports findings instead of failing. `MOBILE_DEVICES=<regex>` limits the devices; `SHOTS_DIR` saves screenshots.
- `e2e/test/mobileDialogs.spec.ts`: home row menus, Share, Move or copy, New layout/module/room. In the editor: Share, Share picture, the Help menu and the layout menu (phone, View), and 11 Map-menu dialogs (tablet, Edit). Each dialog must fit the screen, scroll when tall, keep its content on screen and have 44 px targets.
- Unit tests: `pwa/test/keyboard.test.ts` and `ui/test/cardTables.test.ts`. The owners and venues tests were updated for the ⋯ menu.
- Results: all 495 route checks were clean (survey), and 132 assert-mode runs on 4 devices passed. All 68 dialog checks passed. Vitest: 853 passed.
- Mutation checks, each restored in place:
  - coarse rules back inside `@layer base`: admin range buttons 36 px, test fails;

  - tick-box label min-height removed: the Find dialog fails;
  - room designer header back to one row: Undo is cut off, test fails;

- `src/ui/ModulesPanel.cpp:131`: change `tr("Save to Module Library")` to `tr("Save to Module library")`.

author: endeavoryen
body:
Fixes #458

## Summary

I checked the issue against the code and it is right. I found two more ways a daemon could lose its socket:
- Both clients unlinked the path before spawning: `getOrStartTabDaemon` after a failed connect, and `open`. If another client's daemon bound the path in between, the client removed a live socket. A connect that timed out on a slow but live daemon had the same result.
- libuv unlinks a bound pipe's path when its server closes. So the orphan's `server.close()` in `createDaemonShutdown` removed the survivor's socket, even apart from the explicit unlink.
- The losing daemon also truncated the tab's session log, because `initializeSessionLog` ran before the listen.

Changes:
- **`lib/daemon-transport.mjs`** gets four new helpers:
  - `probeDaemonEndpoint` returns `answers`, `absent` or `unknown`. It uses the same absent codes as `stop`; a timeout or `EACCES` never counts as proof that nothing is listening.
  - `daemonSocketIdentity` reads the socket's dev/ino.
  - `claimDaemonEndpoint` listens without unlinking first. On `EADDRINUSE` it lstats the path, probes it, and unlinks only when two things hold: the probe returned `absent`, and the file still has the dev/ino it had before the probe. That check runs immediately before the unlink. If the file changed, the claim listens again, and the next probe finds the daemon that replaced it. If the holder answers, or the probe returns `unknown`, the claim reports that holder and never unlinks.
  - `watchDaemonSocket` checks the path every 5 s on an unref'd timer.

  Windows named pipes keep the plain `listen`.
- **`createDaemonEndpointLifecycle`** (new, in `cdp.mjs`) holds the daemon's endpoint ownership. `runDaemon` and the tests both use it.
  - It builds `shutdown`. `serve()` runs the claim and then handles each outcome.
  - **Winner:** records the socket identity, writes `.daemon.json`, runs `onServing` (the session log start and `runtimePrune.arm()` from #462), and starts the watch.
  - **Loser:** shuts down, exiting 0 when a daemon answers and 1 when the holder could not be probed. It leaves the socket, the record and the session log alone.
  - `daemonAlreadyServes` is the POSIX pre-check `runDaemon` runs before connecting to CDP.
- **`createDaemonShutdown`** closes the server only while the path still holds this daemon's socket (same dev/ino). libuv then removes the path. The explicit `unlinkSocket` is gone because it was redundant; Linux CI confirms that `close()` removes the path. A daemon that never bound the path, or whose path now holds another socket, does not close the server; exiting releases its listener.
- **`removeOwnDaemonRecord`**: the existing pid-guarded record removal, pulled out into a function.
- **Clients:** `getOrStartTabDaemon` and `open` no longer unlink the path before spawning.
- **`docs/contracts/v2.18.0/runtime-dispatch.v1.json`** was regenerated. The diff is only line shifts and source digests.

There are no public surface changes.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs tests/issue-458-daemon-socket-takeover.test.mjs`: 18 passed. 2 tests use real Unix sockets and skip on win32; they run on Linux CI. The new race tests drive `createDaemonEndpointLifecycle`, the same code `runDaemon` uses. The fake server's `close()` unlinks the path the way libuv does. They cover:
  - Two daemons racing, from an empty path and from a stale file.
  - A newcomer next to a live daemon.
  - A socket that replaced the stale file while the probe ran: no unlink, and the late daemon exits 0.
  - A probe result of `unknown`: exit 1 and no unlink.
  - A listen failure: exit 1 and no close.
  - On Windows the server is still closed on exit.
  - The watch's `onLost` exits the older daemon and leaves the newer socket and record in place.
  - Shutdown ownership.
  - The pre-check.
  - On real sockets: a stale file is left after `process.exit`; the owner's `close()` removes the path; a non-owner's shutdown leaves the newer socket.
- Mutation checks:
  - Commenting out `identity = claim.identity` fails 2 race tests.
  - Turning the dev/ino recheck into `probed || …` fails the replaced-during-probe test.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on `daemon-request-server`, `runtime-supervisor-characterization`, `stop-dead-daemon`, `runtime-v3-table-policy-authority-owners`, `runtime-v3-table-policy-authority`, `daemon-transport`, `issue-444-445-socket-path-and-quoting`, `issue-462-daemon-hygiene`, `current-open-issues` and `release-package`: all passed.
- Existing tests I updated:
  - Shutdown order: there is no `socket:unlink` step any more.
  - The client no longer unlinks.
  - The owners mutation anchor follows the new shutdown text.
  - The #462 wiring regex checks that `runtimePrune.arm()` runs inside `onServing`.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The one warning is existing.
- `npm run check:docs`: OK.
- `node scripts/runtime-dispatch-inventory.mjs --check`: OK after `--write`.
- `npm run check:contracts`: OK.

## Not covered / honest notes

- **Remaining race:** a takeover now needs another daemon to replace the stale file between the lstat recheck and the unlink, two syscalls back to back. If that still happens, the replaced daemon's watch makes it exit within 5 s. It does not close the newer daemon's socket, and it removes the record only if the record names itself. Identity capture has a similar window of microseconds between bind and the `listening` stat. Closing either window fully would need a lock file with its own stale-lock recovery.
- **Probe depth:** the probe is a plain connect, not a `meta` round trip. The socket path is per target inside the private runtime dir, so any listener there is a daemon for that target.
- **macOS:** `ECONNREFUSED` on a full listen backlog would read as stale. `stop` already treats it the same way. There is no macOS CI.
- I did not run `npm run smoke:live`. The attach, perceive and act paths are unchanged.

author: dlynch42
body:
## Description

A 403 from the platform was reported as `Not signed in. Run 'cirron auth login'`. `classifyHttpError` mapped 401 and 403 alike to `NotAuthenticatedError`, and `request()` then refreshed the token, rewrote `~/.cirron/config.json`, retried, and got the same 403. Now that the platform enforces RBAC on the CLI routes, a 403 means signed in but missing a permission. The server names the permission (`{ "error": "Forbidden", "permission": "storage:files:upload" }`), and the CLI was discarding it.

- New `PermissionDeniedError` in `src/utils/api-errors.ts`. It extends `PlatformBadRequestError` (status 403, **exit 1**) and carries `permission`.
- `classifyHttpError` takes a `details` object (`retryAfterSeconds`, `permission`). `requestRaw` passes the body's `permission` through.
- A 403 is no longer a `NotAuthenticatedError`, so no refresh happens. As a 4xx, it isn't retried either.
- 401 is unchanged: `NotAuthenticatedError`, exit 2, refresh once.
- `spool flush` had its own 401/403 branch, which is split the same way.

## Related Issues

Fixes #140

## Change impact

Fix. A 403 now exits 1 instead of 2.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated and `npm test` passes locally.
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass locally.
- [x] `README.md` updated if the command surface or user-facing behavior changed (no README change needed).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Change impact noted above.

## CLI output sample (if applicable)

Before: `Error: Not signed in. Run 'cirron auth login' to authenticate.`
After: `Error: Permission denied: your role does not have the "storage:files:upload" permission in the active organization.`

## Additional Notes

Tests cover 401 vs 403 in `classifyHttpError`, 403 with and without `permission`, "403 does not refresh or retry" (one fetch, stored tokens untouched), and the spool 403 message. This hasn't been checked live against an RBAC-enabled platform yet; it's covered by unit tests only.

Docs: the "Permission denied" troubleshooting entry for `apps/docs/cli/commands/auth.mdx` is staged separately in the platform repo.

author: snowson
body:
## 摘要

B73 系 macOS flake 两处夹具容错修复（#103/#105 两例复发，不同测试、同族根因：GitHub macOS runner 上 git 瞬态失败未被夹具容错）。tests-only 改动，不改断言语义与产品代码。

## 复发实例（均 docs-only PR、代码零改动时挂）

- #103：`test_events_equivalence` 匿名 origin 的 `git clone --bare` 报 `fatal: hardlink different from source`（APFS 硬链接偶发）。
- #105 两连挂：`test_dispatch_robustness` 的 `test_stale_slot_reclaimed_with_salvage` 与 `test_stages_scoped_to_attempt`——夹具执行方脚本的 `git add/commit` 单次 `check=True`，瞬断即执行方轮失败，重试预算耗尽后派发器退出 1。本机 macOS 全量一直绿（runner 慢放大时序）。

## 修复（两个提交，格式化与语义分离便于评审）

1. `style`：两文件先单独 ruff format——main 上它们本就不符合 ruff format（CI lint 只跑 `ruff check` 的历史遗留），不先格式化则语义 diff 会被 515 行重排淹没。
2. `tests`：
   - `executor_script` 的 git add/commit 改 3 次退避重试（0.1/0.3/0.9s，与 test_events_agents 的 T126 模式同款；T126 未覆盖本文件）；
   - bare clone 加 `--no-hardlinks`（夹具不需要硬链接提速，直接消除该错误模式）。

## 验证

两组测试本地 10/10 通过；提交时守卫 verify 通过；推送后 ls-remote 与本地一致（d276029）。

## 后续

- B73 观察期两例复发据此闭环，backlog 行随后续 docs PR 更新（T126 重试只覆盖 executor_script 位点的教训：容错应按「夹具 git 调用」全覆盖）。
- 建议（不在本 PR）：CI lint 增加 `ruff format --check`，防再积累 format 不一致的文件。

author: costafitness
body:
When a hop observes a different layer from the starting one, the existing flow can treat that as success and leave the helper's group even when it is not the requested destination. Delayed helper offers and invite buttons can also act after the helper's eligibility has changed.

This change requires the requested zone/UID and two distinct recent NPC readings before automatic departure. It rechecks helper eligibility before offers and invitations, handles destination observations arriving before the roster event, waits for late offers after an early decline, and prevents cancelled or stale callbacks from leaving an unrelated group.

It also adds `/oly hop list`, `any`, `<zone UID>`, `status`, and `cancel`, plus progress/cancel controls and report ages in the Realm layer section. Plain `/oly hop` retains the King's-layer behavior. Report counts remain samples, not population or available-helper counts. The existing wire protocol, opt-in defaults and request rate limits are preserved.

## Validation

- Original v1.1.2 baseline: 968 offline tests pass.
- Patched `bash scripts/check.sh`: 985 tests pass, including 17 added regression/feature tests; Lua syntax, TOC references, generated answer bank and local/global lint pass.
- New tests against original code: 18 expected failures (the 17 added tests plus the intentionally updated early-decline/backoff expectation). The backoff assertion now waits for the original collection deadline so slower helpers can still answer.
- `bash tests/check-scripts.sh`: 8 applicable checks pass.
- Native Python separately verified syntax for 4 scripts, border textures, and 14 cryptographic fixture vectors. Bash could not find `python3`, so its Python checks and signing round trip were skipped; the signing round trip remains unverified locally. The unchanged web suite was not run locally.
- The distributable and source ZIP contents match the tested files; the patch applies to a clean v1.1.2 snapshot.

## In-game verification pending

This has not been tested in a running WoW client. Before a stable release, test with two players in the same faction/realm/zone on different observed layers: request a specific UID, join, observe two different nearby NPCs, and verify the requested layer persists after departure. Also test wrong/intermediate UIDs, server delay, stale helper location/opt-in, full parties, combat, cancellation, roster replacement, a stock 1.1.2 helper, and controller mode. The full checklist is in `LOCAL-LAYERFIX.md`.

The fork's [experimental download](https://github.com/Costafitness/olympus-addon/releases/tag/v1.1.2-layerfix.1) is labeled `layerfix.1` through `X-Local-Build` and `/oly hop status`; the upstream protocol version is unchanged. This PR does not request an official release before multiplayer validation.

author: jonathanhefner
body:
## Summary

Remove the Catalog Projection statement that points projected `urn:air` entries to generic trust-domain alignment requirements in the Trust Manifest Identity section.

## Rationale

[PR #105](https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog/pull/105) added this cross-reference while the specification still defined a generic relationship between an entry identifier and `TrustManifest.identity`. [PR #110](https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog/pull/110) subsequently replaced that model with a concrete signature profile: a signed `urn:air` subject authorizes the exact corresponding root `did:web` issuer.

Therefore, the remaining statement in the Catalog Projection section refers to requirements that no longer exist under that name, and appears to apply them to any Trust Manifest (including unsigned Trust Manifests).

If a projected entry preserves a publisher-authorized `urn:air` identifier and corresponding signed Trust Manifest, the `did:web` publisher profile already governs verification. Otherwise, the profile does not apply. Thus the Catalog Projection section doesn't need a separate trust-domain alignment rule.

author: patclay7325
marshaco
body:
> **Stacked on #20** (backend foundation). The first step of filing intelligence: getting filings and their text into the database. Summaries and embeddings (Claude, OpenAI) come in the next PR. **Problem** - Filing intelligence is monolyth's headline feature, and nothing existed for it. `services/ingestion` was only a README, and there was no table for filings. **What was fixed** - SEC EDGAR filings for any list of tickers can be pulled into Postgres with their readable text, by hand (`uv run monolyth-ingest AAPL MSFT`) or from code (`ingest_filings()`), ready for summarisation. **Changes** - **`packages/db`:** new `Filing` model and migration (`filings` table). - Columns: `accession_number` (unique), `ticker`, `cik`, `company_name`, `form`, `filed_on`, `report_date`, `document_url`, `description`, `text`, `parsed_at`, plus timestamps. - Indexed on `ticker` and `filed_on`. - Keyed by ticker rather than linked to holdings: one filing matters to every user who holds the company. - **New `services/ingestion` (`monolyth_ingestion`)**, added as a uv workspace member: - `edgar.py`: `EdgarClient`. - `company(ticker)`: ticker-to-CIK lookup via `company_tickers.json`, fetched once per client. Maps `BRK.B` to EDGAR's `BRK-B`. - `recent_filings(company, forms, since)`: reads the submissions API, filters by form and date, builds each document URL, newest first. - `document(url)`. - Throttled to SEC's limit of **10 requests/second**. - `parse.py`: `filing_text(html)`. Drops the hidden inline-XBRL header, `display:none` blocks, scripts and styles. One paragraph per line, tables as tab-separated rows, whitespace and ` ` collapsed. - `ingest.py`: `ingest_filings(session, client, tickers, forms = {10-K, 10-Q, 8-K}, since = 90 days ago)`. - Inserts unseen filings, then fetches and parses any stored filing that has no text yet. - **Idempotent:** a re-run inserts and fetches nothing new. A failed document fetch is retried next run. - Returns new, parsed, unknown tickers (e.g. LSE listings) and errors, without stopping on one bad ticker. - `cli.py`: the `monolyth-ingest` command (`--since`, `--forms`). Exits 2 with a clear message if `SEC_USER_AGENT` is missing, and 1 if anything errored. - `config.py`: **`SEC_USER_AGENT` is required.** The SEC rejects requests without a contact email, so there's deliberately no default. - Docs: `services/ingestion/README.md`, and the `monolyth-ingest` command in CLAUDE.md. **Tests** - `uv run pytest`: **19 passed**, 11 of them new. EDGAR is mocked with `httpx2.MockTransport` serving fixtures in EDGAR's documented JSON formats: - User-Agent: required, must contain an email, and is sent on every request. - Ticker lookup: `aapl`, `BRK.B` → `BRK-B`, unknown `VOD.L`. The ticker map is fetched once. - `recent_filings`: a Form 4, an SC 13G and a 2025 10-K are filtered out. Dates, report dates and the exact archive URL are checked. - Throttling: 4 requests take at least 0.3s. - Parser: exact line-by-line output for an iXBRL 10-Q sample (paragraphs, `
`, a table, ` `). Hidden XBRL, scripts, styles and the title are absent. - Ingest (against the `monolyth_test` database): new filings are stored with text and metadata, a second run is a no-op with no document re-fetched, unknown tickers are reported, and failed fetches (503) leave `text` null and succeed on the next run. - Migration round trip now includes `filings`. - `monolyth-ingest AAPL` without `SEC_USER_AGENT` prints the config message and exits 2. - **Not tested against the live SEC API.** That needs a real contact email in `SEC_USER_AGENT`, and I didn't want to send yours without asking. To check it: `SEC_USER_AGENT="monolyth you@domain" uv run monolyth-ingest AAPL MSFT`. ## Decisions for review - **The contact email for SEC requests:** your choice of address. - **Forms:** 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K by default, per CLAUDE.md. Proxy statements (DEF 14A) and insider forms (Form 4) are easy to add. - **Full text is stored in the `filings` row.** Chunking and embeddings go in a separate table in the intelligence PR. 10-Ks are large (a few MB of text), which is fine for Postgres `TEXT`. - **Only the primary document is parsed**, not exhibits. For 8-Ks the substance is often in Exhibit 99.1 (the press release), so a later improvement is fetching the filing index and including EX-99. - **No scheduling yet.** The Celery task that runs this for every held ticker belongs in `services/sync`, which is next on this track. - `httpx2` (the Pydantic-maintained httpx successor, already used for tests) is now a runtime dependency, alongside `beautifulsoup4` and `lxml`.

author: justinnewbold
body:
## What changes on screen
- **Add a looper, one tap**, in the chain editor on the phone and in the browser. It goes after your last effect, right before the Output, on the row your guitar comes in on, and is joined in on both sides so it's on the signal path.
  - If there's no space before the Output, the Output moves one space along and the looper takes its spot.
  - If the looper is stuck on a spare row that isn't joined to the chain (as in the screenshot), the button offers to move it, and asks first because moving it resets its settings.
  - Once the looper is in the chain, the button disappears.
- **Empty spaces are one line each, not one button per cell.** A run of free cells now reads as "row 1, columns 2–12", so an empty row no longer fills the screen with twelve "Put Looper here" buttons. Putting a block into a run puts it in the run's first column.

## Details
- `shared/split-chain.mjs`: `planLooper(map, catalog)`. It makes the place step, any clear or move of the Output (or of a stray looper), and a cable into each next cell from the last effect to the Output.
- `shared/grid-plan.mjs`: `laneItems` merges runs of gaps into one item (`col`..`last`), plus a `gapCols` helper. Drag-to-move is unaffected because it counts only blocks.
- New `LooperAtEnd` components (`mobile/src/components/LooperAtEnd.js`, `src/components/LooperAtEnd.jsx`), wired into `Edit.js` and `GridEditor.jsx`.
- Tests: the planner (normal spot, already there, stray looper, Output shuffle, full row) and run collapsing. 948 pass.
- Tried in the demo in a browser: the looper landed at column 9 between Reverb and Output, and Output moved to 10.
- Both platforms bundle. Fingerprint: **Unchanged** (OTA update, no build).

body:
## 📌 Description

## 🏛️ Architectural Changes (Clean Architecture)

### 1. Domain Layer (`src/domain`)
- Added the `DatosActualizarReserva` DTO in [IReservaCampingRepository.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/domain/repositories/IReservaCampingRepository.ts) to decouple mutable fields (`personas`, `fecha_entrada`, `fecha_salida`) from the persistence model.
- Ensured contract methods in the repository interface: `actualizar(id, datos)`, `eliminar(id)`, and `obtenerPorId(id)`.

### 2. Application Layer (`src/application`)
- **[ActualizarReservaCampingUseCase.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/application/use-cases/ActualizarReservaCampingUseCase.ts)**:
  - Verifies that the reservation exists and is not already soft-deleted (returns `404 Not Found`).
  - Validates date coherence (`fecha_salida > fecha_entrada`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` format).
  - Enforces tent capacity bounds (1 to 4 persons per tent).
  - Validates camping zone capacity constraints (`409 Conflict` if the update exceeds available spots).
- **[EliminarReservaCampingUseCase.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/application/use-cases/EliminarReservaCampingUseCase.ts)**:
  - Checks reservation existence and active status before deletion to prevent inconsistent state (returns `404 Not Found` if not found or already deleted).
  - Executes logical deletion by setting `eliminado_en` (timestamp) without physical data removal.
- **[ApplicationErrors.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/application/errors/ApplicationErrors.ts)**:
  - Strongly-typed custom application errors (`ValidationError`, `NotFoundError`, `ConflictError`).

### 3. Infrastructure Layer (`src/infrastructure`)
- Implemented update and soft-delete persistence operations in [PrismaReservaCampingRepository.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/infrastructure/database/PrismaReservaCampingRepository.ts) using Prisma Client.

### 4. Interface Layer (`src/interface`)
- **[ReservaCampingController.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/interface/http/controllers/ReservaCampingController.ts)**:
  - Implemented `actualizar` and `eliminar` handler methods.
  - Strict validation of the `:id` route parameter (requires a positive integer; responds with `400 Bad Request` otherwise).
  - Standardized response formatting adhering to conventions: `{ "data": ... }` for successful requests and `{ "error": "message" }` for errors.
- **[reservaCampingRoutes.ts](file:///home/sanma613/Desktop/festival-campingg/src/interface/http/routes/reservaCampingRoutes.ts)**:
  - Registered `PATCH /api/reservas-camping/:id` and `DELETE /api/reservas-camping/:id` route handlers.

---

## 🔌 Exposed Endpoints

author: louisbaudry
body:
Closes #7

## What
- **`web/src/drafts.ts`** (pure, node-tested): the open editor's target is kept in `localStorage` 500 ms after typing pauses and at once on leaving, until the server answers for that write.
- **Recovery on next load** (`recoverDrafts`): a draft still over the stored version is resent through the save queue as the ordinary leave-write (audited, status/origin derived server-side); one that already landed is dropped; one whose segment was saved elsewhere since is **marked `!` on its row with its words, never applied** (the 409 rule).
- Drafts are scoped by account + project (the grid now also reads `/api/me`), carry the source hash (a merge/split/recreated project never receives a stale draft), are pruned after 30 days; blocked storage = the editor as before.

## Why this design
audit-spec §2.2 says the audited write is per segment boundary, never per keystroke. A server-side draft table would be unaudited content changes or an event storm; the browser survives everything autosave guards against short of losing the machine, and recovery turns a draft into the one write #29 already makes. **§2.2 needed no amendment.** Recorded in `v1-spec.md` §7.2 *Keystroke drafts*; backlog #31 rewritten as record.

## Verified
- `pnpm format:check`, `lint`, `build`, `typecheck`, `test` — all green (12 new tests; the recovery tests fail when the version check is inverted).
- Chromium smoke run against the real server + Vite: crash via CDP `Page.crash` (no `pagehide`, no write) → reopen restores and saves as `translated`; a conflicting draft is flagged and the other write kept; Esc clears the draft once saved.
- Not run: `test:gate` / `test:golden` — nothing under their paths changed.

Security: no new outbound data, dependencies or permissions. Unsaved target text persists in the browser's `localStorage` (per account) until saved or 30 days old.

body:
Node adhoc (routed by neat-boar-16 through quiet-gull-780): `//gunbc/instruments:compile-clean-diagnostic-census` refuses because the advisory class `AlgebraApplicationEvidenceUnavailable` has no ceiling row. Admitted under `gunbc.v1_maintenance_standing v1_seed_standing`: the class hides a silent element mistyping on the self-host path.

## Bisect (by execution)
There is no recent cause. On main 7af52ea7e2 the class fires at exactly two sites in the census's own corpus (`dag` + `src/v2`). Both sites already fire at 1f1feb26d2 (#12240, 2026-09-25), the commit that wrote the `type_binder` line. The class's disposition hasn't changed since #10625, and no ceiling row has ever existed. The census reaches its ceiling check only after its earlier refusals pass. Today it stops first at the 65-vs-67 schema-specimen count, which belongs to eager-ibex-722 and is left alone here.

| Site | Shape |
|---|---|
| `src/v2/std/type_binder.dag` `type_param_names` | `fold` over an accumulator seeded with `Empty` |
| `dag/gunbc/spark/host_commitment.dag` `spark_commitment_causes_text` | `Cons { head, tail }` literal with no expected type |

## True or false?
**False at both sites.** An annotated twin of each shape is clean, so the type argument is present in authored facts and inference drops it. The drop is also **not harmless**. The algebra placeholder reads a dropped argument back as the *container*, so the element is mistyped. In the probe, `t.v` on the fold result refuses `no field 'v' on type 'FreeMonoid'`. At `type_binder` the same mistyping is silent because nothing reads a field.

## Chain (DESIGN §6b)
- **Fold:** the fold call already refines its accumulator from the step's return (`refined_call_fold_acc_type`). It does so only when `is_fully_resolved` says the accumulator is under-resolved. An unapplied generic expansion (a `Disj` with declared params) reads as fully resolved, so the refinement never fired. That condition is the earliest unjustified link.
  - **Fix:** one structural predicate, `fold_accumulator_is_unapplied_generic`. There is no binding or unification change and no new spelling-keyed identity decision (cf. `generic_identity_decided_by_spelling`). It never overwrites an *applied* accumulator.
- **Variant literal:** `infer_record_lit_structural` types `Cons { .. }` as the parent's unapplied declaration. Instantiating it mints an applied type node by parameter name. That's the construction derived-node identity step 2 exists to retire, so per quiet-gull-780 it is **not** fixed here. It's a residue on a derived ceiling row, and it has been added to clever-lynx-801's step-2 inventory.

## Evidence
| | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| `unannotated_empty_accumulator_is_refined_from_the_step_return` | FAIL | PASS |
| `annotated_accumulator_twin_stays_clean` (control) | PASS | PASS |
| `algebra_expansion_evidence_witness_test` (variant shape still raises; nominal does not) | PASS | PASS |

**Census, both directions.** Whole-corpus `gunbc compile --source-root dag --source-root src/v2 --target dag --repository gunbc --measured-root-demands tools/whole_corpus_compile_measured_root_demands.json`, sequential, local, same base. Blocking errors are unchanged.
- **Departs:** `advisory type_binder.dag:246` `AlgebraApplicationEvidenceUnavailable`.
- **Arrives:** `advisory src/v2/std/grammar.dag:2989` `DeclaredTypeInhabitanceUndecided` (generic formal). Another `Empty`-seeded fold, whose step is `list_append(left: acc, ..)`, now refines to `FreeMonoid<α>`, and `outcome_accepted(value: classes)` reports undecidable. My reading, *not* separately measured: main's silence there compared the bare `FreeMonoid` with itself, so it was vacuous. The new state is the honest one, and it falls under that class's existing ceiling row.

Regen: `first_generation_equal=true`; `fixed_point_equal=true`.

## Rows
- New `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode.unapplied_generic_accumulator_types_element_as_container`.
  - The class's rung is still **outside the ladder**, because the variant-literal path is unchanged. The repaired fold path is not cited as the class's rung.
  - Trigger: the stall row's grounding, via derived-node identity step 2.
  - It also records a gap the review control exposed and this change does *not* repair. A fold seeded with an applied `List<A>` whose step pushes a `B` is admitted on main and on head alike.
- New `AlgebraApplicationEvidenceUnavailable` row in `advisory_class_ceilings` (`WallAfterGrounding`). It cites `gunbc.guarantee_stall.algebra_expansion_positional_argument_stall` rather than restating it.
- Corrected the emission-site note in `v1.compiler.infer_types` `algebra_child_or_placeholder`. Its "the evidence does not exist" holds at that seam, not upstream.

author: wesm
body:
A push into a local bare repository runs `receive-pack`. Git starts it without the pusher's `-c` options (`unset GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`), and `receive-pack` then starts a detached `git maintenance run --auto` in the bare repository. The `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` flags in test helpers such as `commitTestRun` therefore never reached it. The background process could still be writing when Go removed the test's temporary directory, so cleanup failed with `directory not empty`. This happened to `internal/gitclone` `TestListCommits` in a CI run of #1258.

- `gitsafe.SharedConfig`, the global config every real-Git test shares, now sets `maintenance.auto = false` and `gc.auto = 0`. `receive-pack` keeps `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, so the setting applies on the receiving side of every test push. `MutableRunner` starts from the same config.
- `gitfixture` `TestPushToFixtureOriginStartsNoBackgroundMaintenance` pushes a commit to the shared fixture's bare origin (`gitfixture.NewRepository` with an upstream) and asserts that no maintenance run starts. It fails without the shared setting. `gitfixture` gains the isolated `TestMain` that every real-Git test package uses.
- `gitfixture.NewRepository` refuses temporary directories inside an existing repository or worktree before running `git init`, so no test using the shared fixture can act on an enclosing checkout when `TMPDIR` points into one.
- The assertions that the shared config is empty now check that it holds exactly `SharedConfig`. `context/testing.md` describes where auto-maintenance is disabled and why per-command flags are not enough.

body:
## Description

`cirron env` printed `Error: Error: Error: <msg>` plus a stack trace containing the build machine's absolute source path. The cause was `logger.error("Error:", error)`: the logger already prefixes `Error:`, the literal adds a second, and `util.inspect` renders the Error with a third plus its stack. The same call, or a label followed by the raw error object, appeared in ~40 sites across 17 commands and `src/index.ts`.

- New `errorMessage()` and `reportCommandError(error, context?)` in `src/utils/errors.ts`. `reportCommandError` hands a `PlatformError` to `handlePlatformError`, as before. Anything else prints `context: message`, with the stack only under `--verbose`.
- Every such site now goes through them. That includes the lazy-command wrappers in `index.ts`, whose "Failed to load X command" label was wrong anyway, since they catch the command's own errors, and the `unhandledRejection` handler. Caught errors interpolated with `${error}` now use `errorMessage()`.

Related fixes in the same rendering path:
- `env list/set/delete` and `run list` now **exit 1** on failure. They used to exit 0.
- `CLIError.format()` no longer starts with `Error <code>:`, which doubled the logger prefix in compile and plan. It now ends with `(code <n>)`.
- `compile --strict` with no project config now exits `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND` (31). It used to exit `INTERNAL_ERROR` (81).

Fixes #97

body:
Six items. Migrations form one head, `20261001_0206`.

## What is in it
- **D-FIN-24 (fix):** an income or expense account's ledger statement in its second or later financial year closed on the cumulative figure while the running balance ended at the adjusted one. The closing now takes off the profit brought forward, as the opening already did. This covers both the single-period and month-range statements.
- **§64.4 Rate includes GST** on the counter bill (migration `0200`, decision **A27**):
  - A switch on the bill, defaulting from Settings > Selling > Sales Stages.
  - Only rates typed on this bill are treated as inclusive.
  - The line stores the derived pre-tax `unit_price` and keeps what was typed in `entered_rate`.
  - Sales orders and quotations are still open.
- **§63.3 Output tax per GST head** (migration `0201`, decision **A28**):
  - Sales and sales returns post one output-tax leg per head: IGST, CGST and SGST (2210-2230). UTGST goes with SGST. Cess and documents without components go to 2200.
  - A credit note splits its tax the way its invoice was taxed.
  - `0201` maps the new accounts for every existing firm without overwriting a mapping. History stays in 2200 as posted.
- **§68.8 Reverse charge on purchase bills** (migration `0202`, decision **A29**):
  - Reverse-charge tax is kept on the line, outside what the supplier is paid.
  - Approval issues a self-invoice from its own series (SI). It debits input tax and credits RCM_PAYABLE per head. Cancelling mirrors all of it.
  - GSTR-3B reports 3.1(d) and 4(A)(3).
  - The GST payment pays reverse charge in cash only and clears output tax head by head.
- **§68.4 Purchase order approval limits** (migration `0205`, decision **A30**):
  - Each role may carry a largest order it approves, judged on the order's grand total including tax.
  - Above the limit, approval is refused and the refusal names the amount needed.
  - Bulk approval judges each row on its own.
  - Endpoints: `GET/PUT /api/v1/purchases/approval-limits`, with a desktop page under Settings > Buying > Approval Limits.
- **§68.10 The supplier's credit note on the debit note** (migration `0206`, decision **A31**):
  - The supplier's credit note number and date are recorded on the debit note, both or neither.
  - Each supplier's number may appear on only one live note.
  - New reason: DISCOUNT.
  - The supplier statement names the note, and the list searches and filters on it.

Decisions A27-A31 in `docs/OWNER_DECISIONS.md` are marked "OK?" for the owner.

author: bee-san
body:
## Summary

Adds examples (tests) for every regex in `regex.json` that had none — all the API keys listed in #150 plus a few more (Heroku, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Stripe, Square, PayPal/Braintree, MWS, Picatic, Google OAuth/FCM/GCP, NuGet, SendGrid, Zoho, New Relic, Microsoft Teams, Cloudinary, Shopify, Dynatrace, AMEX). It also enables `test_if_all_tests_exist` and requires the `Examples` key in `test_check_keys`, so a new regex has to come with examples.

## Root cause

Most of these regexes had never been run against a real-format value. Once they had examples, several turned out to be unable to match one:

- **Microsoft Teams Webhook** expected three 64-character path segments. Real URLs use GUIDs and a 32-hex ID, and since 2021 they live on `<tenant>.webhook.office.com/webhookb2` (optionally ending in a V2 token).
- **Picatic API Key** used the character class `[live|test]` instead of a group, so `sk_live_` keys never matched. It now also refuses to match inside a longer Stripe key in boundaryless mode.
- **Square Access Token** had the letter `O` instead of a zero in `sq0atp-`.
- **Square OAuth Token** allowed spaces inside the secret.
- **Google Cloud Platform API Key** matched an 8-4-12 hex string. GCP API keys are `AIza` followed by 35 characters.
- **Google OAuth Access Key** required exactly 64 characters, but access tokens are longer.
- **Stripe** keys can have up to 99 characters after the prefix, **Twitter** API secrets have 50, and newer **Heroku** tokens start with `HRKU-` (added as a second regex in the list format from #244).

## Fake API keys, GitHub push protection and SonarCloud

GitHub push protection blocks any push that adds fake keys in the Stripe, Shopify, Square, SendGrid, Dynatrace, Heroku, New Relic or Google OAuth formats. I found the 21 flagged examples by pushing candidates to a throwaway ref that the server always rejected, so nothing reached the remote. Push protection was not bypassed. SonarCloud's secret rules then flagged 11 more examples on this PR (Google/GCP API key, Facebook, Heroku, Square, MWS, NuGet, SendGrid, New Relic and FCM).

Those examples are now written in `regex.json` as a list of parts, e.g. the provider prefix and the rest:

```json
"Valid": [
   [
      "shpat_",
      "d07fa97cc5213b189110525a4048ea84"
   ]
]
```

`load_regexes()` joins them (`helper.join_examples`), the same way #244 handles lists in `"Regex"`. So:
- the examples stay in `regex.json`, and are still run by `test_regex_valid_match` / `test_regex_invalid_match`;
- the API and `--json` output still contain plain strings;
- `scripts/format_regex.py` keeps the format.

The fake keys in `tests/test_identifier.py` are split the same way with implicit string concatenation. This is documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which the README now links to.

## Tests

- New examples run through the existing parametrised `test_regex_valid_match` / `test_regex_invalid_match`. Every entry has valid examples, and the entries touched here have invalid ones too (wrong prefix, wrong length, wrong characters, near misses).
- `test_examples_format`, `test_join_examples`, `test_examples_are_joined_on_load` cover the split examples.
- `test_boundaryless_api_keys` covers Heroku, Google OAuth, Teams and Stripe keys inside text. `test_boundaryless_picatic_api_key_not_inside_longer_key` covers the Picatic fix.
- Full suite with the CI linters (`pytest` with black, isort, flake8, mypy): 1734 passed, 7 skipped (the skips also happen on `main`).

Fixes #150

author: roschaefer
body:
Visits to roschaefer.de stopped showing up in GoatCounter. The /gc/count Netlify rewrite made every hit arrive from Netlify's AWS egress IPs, and GoatCounter takes the connecting proxy as the client IP and flags AWS ranges as bots (isbot BotRangeAWS). Those hits were stored as bots and never counted, while the endpoint still answered 200 with a GIF.

The edge function records the hit through /api/v0/count instead, passing the visitor's own IP and user agent so bot detection and unique-visitor sessions work again. It keeps the first-party /gc/count path, so ad blockers still don't block the beacon; loading GoatCounter directly was the simpler alternative but loses that.

Requires a GoatCounter API token with the "Record pageviews" permission in the GOATCOUNTER_API_TOKEN Netlify environment variable.

Verified with pnpm check:quick; not yet exercised on a Netlify deploy.

## 为什么改

米哈游游戏必须通过 HoYoShade 外部加载，所以它们一直在单独的“米哈游”页里设置。普通游戏页的安装设置里却还留着一块“米哈游兼容”（加载模式：常规加载 / HoYoShade、正式客户端、绑定启动器、选择启动器程序）。

这块只在游戏是米哈游客户端时才会出现。可是管理器本来就不会把米哈游客户端放进“我的游戏”列表（它们只出现在“米哈游”页），而“米哈游”页走的是自己的安装设置，不会用到这块。所以玩家实际上看不到这块，但代码和测试一直在维护它，还让人误以为普通游戏也要选“米哈游”加载方式。按维护者的决定，米哈游相关设置只放在“米哈游”页。

## 改了什么

- `desktop/src/renderer/game-page-ui.js`：删除普通游戏页的“米哈游兼容”区块，以及只为它服务的草稿处理和“选择启动器程序”按钮。“米哈游”页用到的米哈游 Core 范围、启动设置和应用流程都没动。
- `desktop/main.js`、`desktop/preload.js`：删除只给这个按钮用的 `pick-hoyo-launcher` 接口。“米哈游”页绑定启动器走的是自己的接口，不受影响。
- `desktop/test/helpers/game-page-beta3-fixture.cjs`：测试数据和正式程序保持一致，米哈游客户端不再出现在普通游戏列表里。原来在普通游戏页测“米哈游兼容”的部分，改成检查普通列表里没有米哈游客户端。

## 验证

- **本地（Linux）**：
  - 全量单元测试和改动前逐项对比：1818 项，失败 188 项，失败的测试名逐条相同（都是本机缺 ReShade 等环境原因）；
  - Electron 界面测试：全部 21 个场景和改动前逐项对比，结果一致（含“米哈游”页场景 `GAME_UI_HOYO=1`，通过）；两边都因本机环境失败的有 6 个，停在同样的位置；

- **托管 CI**：以本 PR 的检查为准。
- **实机安装、游戏内验证**：未做。米哈游游戏的实机加载仍需在“米哈游”页按原流程验证。

author: mashkovd
body:
Refs mctlhq/mctl-telegram#679

Wires the `/start` bridge: mctl-agent owns `@MCTL_AI_bot`'s webhook, so when it sees `/start` it forwards a minimal observation (no raw message text) to mctl-telegram's internal endpoint. A shared bearer token authenticates the call. mctl-telegram's own Telegram receiver stays off.

## Merge preconditions

Do not merge until all three hold:

1. ✅ (met 2026-10-01) **The Vault value exists.** It goes at `secret/platform/shared/bot-start-bridge`, key `token`: a dedicated random value, 64 hex chars, distinct from every service, admin and surface token. It is written by hand and never appears in this repo. If it exists but is shorter than 32 chars, mctl-telegram refuses to start.
2. ✅ (met: 0.77.0 on main) **mctl-telegram with #725 is released**, and its `image.tag` here points at that release.
3. **This merges before, or together with, the mctl-agent forwarder release.** The forwarder needs `BOT_START_FORWARD_URL`, the token and the NetworkPolicy below in place when it ships.

The secret refs are `optional: true`, so a merge before step 1 breaks no pod: both Secrets are simply absent and the feature stays off. The only visible effect is that the two new ExternalSecrets report `SecretSyncedError` until the value exists. The preconditions are still the intended order.

## Changes

### `platform-gitops/services/labs/mctl-telegram/values.yaml`
- New `extraExternalSecrets.labs-mctl-telegram-bot-start-bridge`:
  - store and path: `vault-backend` ClusterSecretStore, `secret/data/platform/shared/bot-start-bridge`, property `token`;
  - writes `BOT_START_BRIDGE_TOKEN` into Secret `labs-mctl-telegram-bot-start-bridge`.
  - It is a separate ExternalSecret, so a missing value cannot fail the sync of the other secrets.
- `envFrom` reference to that Secret with `optional: true`. Without it, mctl-telegram does not mount `/internal/bot-start-observations`.
- `env.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_BOT_USERNAME: "MCTL_AI_bot"`, the public bot username for the `t.me/<bot>?start=` deep link. Not a secret.
- A comment saying `BOT_RECEIVER_ENABLED` must never be enabled on this webhook-owned token. Long polling would get 409, and `deleteWebhook` would cut mctl-agent off. `BOT_RECEIVER_ENABLED` itself is not added or changed.

### `platform-gitops/bootstrap/templates/mctl-platform/mctl-agent.yaml`
- `env.BOT_START_FORWARD_URL: http://labs-mctl-telegram-base-service.labs.svc:8080/internal/bot-start-observations`, cluster-internal only.
- New `extraExternalSecrets.mctl-agent-bot-start-bridge` with the same Vault path and key, written into the Secret as `BOT_START_FORWARD_TOKEN`.
  - It is deliberately kept out of `mctl-agent-secrets`. A missing remote key fails the whole ExternalSecret, and that one carries the 15-minute GitHub App token rotation.
- `envFrom` reference to `mctl-agent-bot-start-bridge` with `optional: true`. If either the URL or the token is unset, the forwarder is a no-op.

### `platform-gitops/bootstrap/templates/mctl-platform/mctl-telegram-bot-start-netpol.yaml` (new)
- NetworkPolicy `allow-mctl-agent-to-mctl-telegram-bot-start` in `labs`. It allows ingress only:
  - to pods labelled `app.kubernetes.io/instance=labs-mctl-telegram` and `app.kubernetes.io/name=base-service`;
  - on TCP 8080;
  - from pods labelled `app.kubernetes.io/instance=admins-mctl-agent` and `app.kubernetes.io/name=base-service` in namespace `admins`. The namespace and pod selectors sit in one `from` element, so both must match.
- Why it is needed: labs runs the tenant chart's `default-deny-all`, which admits only intra-namespace, Traefik and monitoring traffic.
- The policy is additive, so it does not widen access for the preview instance or for other admins pods.
- Egress needs no change: `admins` has `allowClusterEgress`, which covers the pod and Service CIDRs.
- It is platform-owned, so it lives in the bootstrap chart next to `allow-monitoring-to-mctl-agent`. base-service `extraObjects` refuses NetworkPolicy.
- Labels were checked against live pods.

### `platform-gitops/bootstrap/templates/system/admission-policies.yaml` (fix round, bd165e2)
- `allow-mctl-agent-to-mctl-telegram-bot-start` is added to the `mctl-tenant-networkpolicy-allowlist` CEL list. Without it, the API server rejects the labs policy at sync.

### `scripts/validate-tenant-networkpolicy-allowlist.py` and `.github/workflows/validate-manifests.yml` (new check)
- The new script reads the rendered bootstrap chart and fails when a NetworkPolicy in a tenant namespace is missing from that allowlist. Validate Manifests runs it with `--selftest`.
- Mutation-checked: it fails with the allowlist entry removed.

## Validation
- `helm lint platform-gitops/bootstrap`: ok.
- `helm template` of the bootstrap chart, of base-service with the mctl-telegram values, and of base-service with the rendered mctl-agent Application values: ok. The rendered output was checked for:
  - both optional envFrom refs;
  - both ExternalSecrets with the right `secretKey`;
  - the URL env var;
  - the NetworkPolicy spec.
- `kubeconform -ignore-missing-schemas` on all three renders: 0 invalid.
- `yamllint` with the CI's relaxed config: clean.
- All `scripts/validate-*.py`: pass.
- The Vault read policy for `vault-backend` covers `secret/data/platform/*`, which includes the new path.

author: akshita317
body:
GetAuthServerMeta rejected an authorization server that advertises no
PKCE method, but accepted one whose code_challenge_methods_supported
lists only "plain". The SDK's clients always send an S256 challenge
(oauth2.S256ChallengeOption in auth and auth/extauth), so with such a
server the flow failed late, when the authorization endpoint rejected
the request in the user's browser, rather than during discovery with a
clear error.

Require "S256" in the advertised methods. The MCP authorization spec
requires clients to use S256 (OAuth 2.1 section 7.5.2), and the
TypeScript SDK refuses such a server during discovery in the same way.
Servers that offer both methods, such as Google's (see
testdata/google-auth-meta.json), are unaffected.

The new server_with_only_plain_pkce case of
TestGetAuthServerMetaPKCESupport fails without the change;
server_with_plain_and_s256_pkce checks that a mixed list is accepted.

Fixes #1326

author: mrityunjaybhardwaj
body:
## What this does

#177 asked whether a re-judge's replies could come from "a different version of the same model name". I checked what OpenRouter actually returns: **no version** (`model` is just the slug, `system_fingerprint` is null), but it does name the **provider** of each call. Two live calls today were served by **DigitalOcean** and then by **Baidu**. One model name is several deployments.

- `OpenRouterModel` records `"<model> via <provider>"` per call ("an unreported provider" if the field is missing).
- An artifact stores the distinct pairs: `served_by` for the run, and `same_served_by` for a judge added later by `rejudge` (only the calls that rejudge made).
- `None` = not recorded (older artifacts, or a model that doesn't report); `()` = no call was made. `occam replay` prints which, every time.
- It's for audit only: nothing is derived from it, and replay ignores it.

The limit is that it records **which providers served the run, not which provider served each reply**. That's enough to see a mix, or a re-judge served elsewhere. Pinning a reply to its provider would mean threading the provider through every stage's stored replies, which is a bigger change than this gap justifies.

## Checked

| | result |
|---|---|
| suite | 1250 passed / 4 skipped, pytest exit 0 (1245 + 5 new) |
| stored artifacts via `occam replay` | 37 of 37 match (run 2, run 2 judged, run 3, run 3 controls, run 4 controls), each printing "served by: not recorded" |
| one live call through `OpenRouterModel` | `served == ['z-ai/glm-5.2 via Baidu']` |

Breaking each part turns a test red: a rejudge counting earlier calls, unreported read as "no calls", a missing provider printing `None`, and the later judge line dropped.

Refs #186 (and #177). The base is `webapp`, so auto-close won't fire; #186 gets closed by hand after the merge.

author: mgoldey
body:
The RHF internal stability descent added in #244 was available only from the library. The CLI config already passed the flag through to `solve_rhf`, but the CLI gate refused `[scf] stability_descent` for anything except the UHF/UKS route.

The gate now accepts `kind = "rhf"`, `"uhf"` and `"ksdft"` (any multiplicity) with `task = "energy"`. `rohf` and every other kind are still refused, and the error says why. A KS functional with no stability verdict (range-separated or meta-GGA) skips the descent and prints the reason, as the library does.

**Test** (`cli_wired_keys.rs::stability_descent_reaches_the_library_rhf_minimum`): runs N2 at 1.60 Å / def2-SVP through the CLI, with and without the key.
- With the key, the energy equals the library's `check_stability + scf_stability_descent` result to 1e-8. That result is the stable minimum, −108.5016165203.
- Without the key, the run stays on the saddle, more than 1e-2 Ha higher.

The unit test for the gate covers all three accepted kinds plus the refusals. A mutation in which the CLI ignores the key for `rhf` fails the test.

Docs: the `input.md` row and the field's doc comment now describe the RHF and KS scope.

author: baltazaradamealvarez-creator
body:
## What's new

### WhatsApp alerts through a linked phone
**Admin → Settings → WhatsApp alerts:**
1. Click **Connect WhatsApp**. A QR code appears and refreshes by itself.
2. On the alerts phone, go to WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device, and scan the code.
3. Once it shows **Connected**, pick the **dispatch group** and send a test. Every new lead is then posted to the group automatically, in the same format as **Copy for WhatsApp**, plus a link to the lead.

Status chip, **Disconnect**, and an on/off for posting new leads are on the same card.

> ⚠️ This is the unofficial WhatsApp Web style link (Baileys). WhatsApp may disconnect or block the linked number, so the card says to **use a separate number just for alerts**. The app's own and phone notifications always go out regardless.

### WhatsApp alerts per person
- In **Account → Profile → WhatsApp alerts**, anyone can add a WhatsApp number and switch on **Send my alerts to WhatsApp**. They then get every in-app alert there too: new leads, assignments, orders, @mentions and call-back reminders.
- **Send me a test** is available.
- Numbers are normalised; US numbers get +1.
- If the admin hasn't connected WhatsApp yet, the number is saved and alerts start once they do.

### Instant new-lead alerts for dispatch
- Every active dispatcher is alerted **the moment a new lead comes in**: in the app, as a phone notification, and on WhatsApp if they turned it on. The alert reads "🆕 New lead: … Tap to take it."
- This closes the gap where unassigned leads waited for the 15-minute speed-to-lead alert.
- Admins can switch it off under Admin → Settings.

### Reliability
- **Paced send queue:**
  - messages go out 1.5 s apart, with a cap of 200 an hour;
  - each message gets up to 3 tries;
  - messages wait while the link is down, capped at 300 in the queue;
  - numbers without WhatsApp are skipped.
- **Automatic reconnect:**
  - retries with backoff, and a 60 s start watchdog;
  - "restart required" after scanning is handled.
- **"Logged out from the phone":** the link resets and admins are told to scan again.
- **Linked somewhere else:** it stops and doesn't fight over the session.
- **If it can't reconnect for a while,** admins get one in-app alert.
- The session is stored on the persistent disk next to the database (`whatsapp-auth/`), so it survives deploys.

### Under the hood
- `@whiskeysockets/baileys@6.7.24` (the official WhiskeySockets package, current stable) and `qrcode@1.5.4`, both pinned exact. The library doesn't need a browser, so it's light enough for the current Render plan.
- Baileys depends on `libsignal`, installed from a GitHub git URL. npm wrote that URL as `git+ssh://` in the lockfile, which would make `npm ci` on Render fail without SSH keys. It's rewritten to `git+https://`, I verified a clean `npm ci` with it, and a test now fails if an SSH URL ever comes back.
- The WhatsApp code sits behind a small transport interface (`src/whatsapp-baileys.js`), so tests run against a fake.
- New shared `public/waformat.js` is used by both the copy button and the group posts. The service-worker cache was bumped.
- Migration v12 adds `users.whatsapp` and `users.whatsapp_alerts`.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 46 pass. New `test/whatsapp.test.js` (fake phone link) covers:
  - QR → connected → group list → group test → a new lead posted in the dispatch format
  - posting switched off
  - profile number and opt-in validation
  - every dispatcher getting the instant in-app alert, and WhatsApp only for those opted in
  - an Ordered alert reaching the rep on WhatsApp
  - numbers without WhatsApp being skipped
  - test-me
  - the instant-alert switch
  - messages queued while disconnected and sent on reconnect
  - logged-out → admins told to rescan
  - disconnect
  - the lockfile guard
- Playwright, against a stand-in for the phone link:
  - the admin card QR, then Connected, group pick, and test
  - a dispatcher saving their number on a phone-sized screen
  - a rep entering a lead, which posts it to the group and sends the dispatcher a WhatsApp alert
- The real Baileys connection loads and opens a socket here, but can't reach WhatsApp from this sandbox. The actual QR scan needs to be done on the live site.

body:
Fixes #426, fixes #427

Outside the FDS slices pyFDS-Evac keeps reading ambient air and clear sight, as FDS+Evac does (default unchanged). This PR fixes two defects at the domain edge and makes the assumption visible.

## Fixes
- **#427** `FdsFedField.sample_inputs`: a point that some loaded gas slices cover and others do not (CO/CO2/O2, and loaded optional species) raises `ValueError` naming point, time and missing quantity, as heat already did. Fully outside: ambient, as before.
- **#426** `VisibilityModel`: an observer off the FDS vismap grid (beyond half a cell past the edge coordinates) gets clear-air sight when the sign is within its reading distance (sign `max_distance` or `--max-sign-distance`), measured from the observer; `visibility_to_node` returns `None` there. View angle and obstructions are not applied outside the grid. Clear-air models are unaffected.

## Diagnostics
- Setup check (`pyfds_evac/core/fds_coverage.py`) in `run_scenario`: walkable area, exits, checkpoints, spawn areas, signs and route edges vs. the intersection over sampled quantities of their subslice-rectangle unions; one log summary; `metrics["fds_coverage"]` and manifest `fds_coverage`.
- Signs off the vismap grid warn (fdsvismap 0.2.1 snaps their ray origin to the grid edge; no upstream issue yet; removal condition in `VisibilityModel.signs_outside_grid`).
- `in_fds_domain` in smoke and FED history rows/CSVs (appended last, only with FDS output) and in `agent_scalars`; end-of-run count `metrics["fds_outside"]` (rows, agents, agent-seconds) plus one log line.

## Evidence
- `tests/test_fds_domain_defects.py` (existing API only): 8 tests fail on 4f859bf5 by assertion, pass here. `tests/test_fds_domain.py`: new features incl. a coupled run on `assets/iso_table21_coupled` with the walkable area extended to x = 60 m.

- vismap crash on slice holes (needs a real non-rectangular FDS case).

body:
Fixes #253

`GuavaMultimapDeserializer.findTransformer()` returned the `create(Multimap)` copy factory for `ArrayListMultimap`, `HashMultimap` and `LinkedHashMultimap`. Each deserialization therefore built the multimap via `createMultimap()`, which already returns the requested type, and then copied every entry into a second instance via `Method.invoke`.

This change skips the transformer for those raw types, as was already done for `LinkedListMultimap`, `ListMultimap` and `Multimap`. Types that do need conversion are unaffected: `ImmutableListMultimap`, `ImmutableSetMultimap`, `TreeMultimap`, `Forwarding*`, and abstract `SetMultimap`/`ListMultimap` targets. The comparison is by exact raw class, so these still go through their factory.

Existing `MultimapsTest` coverage (`testHashMultimap`, `testLinkedHashMultimap`, `testArrayListMultimap`) checks both content and concrete type. All guava module tests pass locally.

The same code is in 2.x and could be backported if wanted.

author: yjiod
body:
When a publisher switches the latest software catalog, another Collector process can still hold the previous catalog and admit new tasks for that obsolete target. Persist the current publication fingerprint and generation in SQLite, and validate them within the same transaction that admits each new task. Stale processes now return a fixed 503 for publication reads and new task creation; exact retries and claims for already admitted tasks retain their immutable references and original deadlines.

Catalog transitions require administrator-supplied startup compare-and-swap. Identical restarts are idempotent, including restarting after the transition committed but listener startup failed. Fingerprints bind all selected metadata, and generations prevent an old process from becoming valid again after an A→B→A publication sequence. Business writes roll back together on conflicts, corruption, generation exhaustion, or failed head writes. The release view exposes the generation for controlled deployment tooling.

Validation: 51 software-task tests, 11 OpenAPI tests, and 8 latest-target compiler tests passed without skips. Five mutation probes detected missing startup/admission fences without unexpected errors. Independent product/architecture and quality reviews passed. Reproducible release generation, release verification, dependency lock, npm audit, lint, TypeScript, build, and asset/API boundary checks passed. Built-in source SAST found no added findings; the Collector's inherited medium empty-exception-handler finding remains. Final-source CI is required before merge and deployment.

This change is a prerequisite for latest-only publication, not completion of arbitrary-version upgrades. Production target planning/signing, trusted component and maintainer measurements, old maintainer/protocol migration, four-architecture runtime validation, and safe retirement of obsolete stored artifacts remain open. No client package qualification or deployment is claimed. Updated processes sharing one SQLite database are fenced; deployments must stop all prior implementations that do not implement this check.

author: jpkintu
body:
Customers order online without signing in: from a shared link, or a QR code on a printed flier or table card.

## Customer side (`/order`)
- **Menu.** Live menu with categories and the branch picker. Required and optional sides follow the dish's rules.
- **Basket and checkout.** Pick-up or delivery, with a typed address and/or "Use my location". Name, phone, notes.
- **Payment.**
  - Cash on pick-up or on delivery.
  - Mobile money: a request to the customer's phone with automatic collection, or the merchant code plus the transaction ID, which a cashier checks.
- **Tracking page** (private token, updates by itself):
  - steps: received → being prepared → ready / on the way → done;
  - payment state;
  - the customer can cancel until the kitchen starts.

## Staff side
- **Board.** Online orders are counter orders on the `online` channel. They land in Incoming tagged **Online**, with the customer's number as a tap-to-call link. Deliveries get a rider like call-in orders (the rider earns the delivery fee only). Pick-ups paid in cash are open bills.
- **Pause.** Cashiers pause or resume online orders from the kitchen board (`setOnlineOpen`).
- **Admin → Online orders.**
  - Switch it on.
  - Choose pick-up and/or delivery, cash and/or mobile money, and a line for customers.
  - Copy, share or open the link; download the QR code as PNG.
  - Print **A4 / A5 fliers or table cards (4 per A4)** with a custom headline and a live preview.

## Server (`cloud/online.js`)
- **Functions:**
  - public: `getOnlineMenu`, `placeOnlineOrder`, `getOnlineOrder`, `cancelOnlineOrder`;
  - staff: `setOnlineOpen`;
  - owner (behind the PIN): `adminGetOnlineOrdering`, `adminSaveOnlineOrdering`.
- **Totals.** Prices, sides and the delivery fee are computed on the server (`priceLines`). The menu builder is shared with staff ordering (`operationalMenu`).
- **Protection.** A repeated send is placed once (`requestId`). Throttled per address (8) and per phone (4) every 15 minutes. Anonymous users still cannot query orders.
- **Settings.** New Configuration fields `online*` (defaults, schema) and `Order.onlineToken`. `config.online` added to the profile.

## Tests
- e2e 193/193 in CI mode. The new suite covers:
  - switching it on and the rules for what must be offered;
  - the menu;
  - a pick-up paid in cash: an open bill held by nobody, deduplicated, tracked, cancelled;
  - a delivery with a rider assigned;
  - mobile money by merchant code;
  - pausing;
  - switching it off.
- Permission matrix updated.
- Unit tests for the flier HTML.
- Checked in the sandbox on a phone-sized screen: menu, sides sheet, checkout, tracking, the owner's page with QR and flier preview, and the online ticket on the board.

author: mister-guiiug
body:
Une fonction qui lève `40001` (`serialization_failure`) derrière PostgREST le fait rejouer la transaction **sans fin** : la requête ne répond jamais, et le backend tourne à plein jusqu'à ce qu'on le tue. Supabase le documente pour PostgREST 14, corrigé en 16 : [fiche Supabase](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/high-cpu-and-infinite-transaction-retries-when-using-custom-error-codes-in-rpc-functions-77326b). Les tests pgTAP ne peuvent pas le voir : ils appellent le SQL sans passer par PostgREST.

C'est arrivé le 01/10 en production sur mister-molkky (mister-guiiug/mister-molkky#127). miss-uwh levait le même code pour ses conflits de version (mister-guiiug/miss-uwh#178).

## Ce que fait cette PR

Elle ajoute un **troisième invariant de structure** dans `supabase/tests/structure-securite.test.sql` : aucune fonction de `public` ne mentionne `40001` ni `serialization_failure`. Le corps entier est lu par `pg_get_functiondef`, et les membres d'extension sont écartés. Aucune fonction de ce dépôt ne lève ce code aujourd'hui : la règle l'empêche pour la suite. Un conflit métier se signale par `PT409`, que PostgREST rend en HTTP 409 sans le rejouer.

Le même ajout part dans les sept apps Supabase du parc qui ont des tests pgTAP et ne l'avaient pas encore. mister-molkky et miss-uwh l'ont déjà.

**Test seul** : aucune migration, rien ne change en production.

author: rtb-12
body:
## Summary

Any group admin can name any application id in governance, and the lazy-upgrade download path bound whatever it fetched under that id.
A signed release in the `ApplicationMeta` row could be replaced by an older signed release of the same app, or by raw wasm, and a context with no activation marker would then run those bytes.

Installs now carry an `InstallOrigin`, and the row follows one rule on every remote-triggered path: the downloader (`bind_application`), the blob-share and resync install (`install_expected_bundle_blob`), the join bootstrap and a relay resolving a member's target (`install_by_coords` with `Remote`).

- A signed bundle must derive the id it is written under.
  It replaces the row only when its version equals, or is semver-newer than, the signed release the row names.
- Any other signed release (older, or not orderable because either version is not semver) is kept as a local blob for the contexts bound to it.
  The row is left alone and none of its service blobs are stored; the install still succeeds.
- Raw wasm only fills a missing row or a governance stub that holds no bytes yet.
- The blob-share install now checks the bundle id before it writes anything.

Operator installs through the admin API (`install_application`, `install_dev_application`) keep their previous behaviour and may set the row to any release, including an older one, so the documented recovery of reinstalling a missing intermediate version still works.
The check and the write happen under one per-node lock (`row_writes`).
The release order used by the upgrade ladder, `get_latest_version` and `list_application_versions` is now one shared `compare_versions`; the remote rule uses semver precedence, so build metadata does not count as newer.

A separate commit gates `LwwKind::from_legacy` on the `borsh` feature: its only caller is the borsh decoder, and per-crate clippy failed on it as dead code.

## Behaviour changes

- A remote install of an older or unorderable signed release no longer moves the row; the bytes stay as a blob.
- Raw wasm can no longer replace a row that holds bytes (signed or raw); that bind now fails and the fetched blob is released.
- A relay resolving an older target returns the stored bundle's blob id instead of reading it from the row.
- `install_by_coords` takes an `InstallOrigin` and returns the stored bundle blob id with the application id.
- `install_application_from_bundle_blob` is test-only (`testing` feature); production paths name the id they expect.
- The unused `update_compiled_app` is removed, and `calimero-context` drops its now unused `semver` dependency.
- Docs: `protocol/applications.mdx`, `protocol/upgrades.mdx` and the node and app-downloader `AGENTS.md` describe the rule.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p calimero-node-primitives --test registry_install`: new tests drive the real entry points (`ApplicationDownloader` over `NodeClient`, `install_by_coords`, `install_expected_bundle_blob`, `install_application_from_path`):
  `a_downloaded_older_release_never_replaces_the_installed_row`, `a_held_older_release_never_replaces_the_installed_row`, `downloaded_raw_wasm_never_replaces_a_signed_row_and_is_released`, `downloaded_raw_wasm_never_replaces_a_raw_row_and_is_released`, `a_remote_coords_install_keeps_the_newer_row`, `a_remote_coords_install_keeps_the_row_for_an_unordered_release`, `a_remote_semver_release_never_replaces_an_unordered_row`, `an_expected_blob_install_keeps_the_newer_row`, plus controls `a_downloaded_newer_release_replaces_the_installed_row`, `an_expected_blob_install_accepts_the_same_version`, `a_remote_install_of_the_same_unordered_version_replaces_the_row`, `an_operator_install_may_roll_the_row_back`, `downloaded_raw_wasm_fills_a_placeholder_row`.
- On master the first three failed (row replaced by the older release or by raw wasm, and a direct older install succeeded); with the guard disabled, every keep and refusal test above fails.
- `compare_versions` unit tests in `crates/node/primitives/src/client/application/tests.rs`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `calimero-primitives`, `calimero-node-primitives`, `calimero-app-downloader`, `calimero-context-client`, `calimero-context`, `calimero-server`, `calimero-node`, and `cargo machete`: all pass.
- CI: the new tests run in the `Rust tests` job (`cargo nextest run --workspace`) in `ci-checks.yml`.

body:
## Summary

Folds the four launch UI tests (each relaunching the app) into one test, `testLaunchedAppAddsOpensHidesAndDeletesAnItem`, that launches once. The steps run in an order where none undoes what a later one needs: add → open detail and back → complete and hide completed (all-done state) → show completed again → Edit-mode delete. Each step is a named `XCTContext` activity with its own assertion messages, so a failure still names the broken behavior.

**Grouping trade-off (speed over isolation):** the scenarios now share one app state, and `continueAfterFailure = false` means a failure stops the walk, so steps after the failing one go unreported until it is fixed.

Measurement, same simulator (iPhone 17e), warm, local machine under load: before ≈ 68.5 s across 4 tests (77.6 s testing phase); after 36.7–47.0 s for 1 test (45.5–62.2 s testing phase). author: briangraves
body:
1.0 P1 (`docs/spec/1.0-plan.md`): the last port. Integrations get a runner-neutral contract method, so a site on `payloadJobs()` can run them. **Additive.**

## Why this one needed a contract change rather than a port

The webhook builds its functions through `Integration.createFunctions(ctx)`. forumone-2026's HubSpot and Greenhouse integrations implement that same contract, and use `ctx.inngest` directly. The integrations context is also built at `onInit`, while a jobs adapter needs its jobs before that. So:

- **`Integration.createJobs(getContext)` is optional.** It takes a function, not a context, and the handler calls `getContext(job)` when it runs. An integration without it runs on Inngest only, as today. HubSpot and Greenhouse compile unchanged.
- **`IntegrationContext.emit`** sends on whichever runner the site uses.
- **`IntegrationContext.inngest` stays required in the type**, so existing integrations keep compiling. On a site with no Inngest client it's a guard that throws, naming `ctx.emit` and `createJobs`, rather than being `undefined`. Making it optional is a breaking change, so it waits for P3.

## What changed

- **The webhook implements `createJobs`,** and `createFunctions` is derived from it: `inngestJobs(ctx.inngest).functions(createWebhookJobs(() => ctx))`.
- **`integrationsJobs(options)`** returns every registered integration's jobs, the webhook included, as the plugin includes it. Each job reads the context from Payload when it runs, and says which piece is missing when one is.
- **`integrationsPlugin` accepts `emit`** (for example `payloadJobs().emit`) in place of `inngest`, and needs one of the two. The manual-sync endpoint, `trigger_sync` and `requestManualSync` send through it. Their `inngest` options become optional, which loosens them without breaking callers.

## Proof the Inngest side didn't move

`webhook/registration-parity.test.ts` snapshots the webhook's two registrations: `webhook-deliver` with `retries: 5` and five events, and `webhook-manual-trigger`. It was written before the port and passes unchanged. All existing integrations tests pass against the ported code.

## Roadmap

This completes "Port every workflow and plugin job to `defineJob`": workflows (#214), email (#215), integrations (this PR), with forms won't-do since it isn't in 1.0.

## Verification

| Package | Tests | Typecheck | `eslint src` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| integrations | 112 passed, including the new `integrationsJobs` and no-Inngest tests, and the snapshot | `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -b` clean | clean |
| create-throughline | 128 passed | — | — |

Prettier was applied only to files that were already Prettier-clean on `main`.

`integrations` now depends on `@forumone/throughline-workflows`. There's no cycle: workflows depends on core and publishing.
