author: rtb-12
body:
## Summary

`persist_root_state` is a JS app's own write, but it was the one JS host write left outside the storage key and value caps and the per-execution write count and byte budget that `storage_write` and the JS collection host functions are held to.
It now goes through the same write meter (`metered` / `WriteMeter::settle` in `write_meter.rs`), so an oversize root, or a root write past the budget, traps like `storage_write`.

`apply_storage_delta` stays unmetered: it replays a delta during JS sync, and that must not be refused by this execution's write limits.

## Behaviour changes

- A JS method whose root document exceeds `max_storage_value_size` (10 MiB by default, measured on the stored row) now traps instead of persisting.
  Every mutating method on such a context traps until the app shrinks its root.
- Root writes now draw on `max_storage_writes` and `max_storage_write_bytes`; at the defaults (100,000 writes, 128 MiB) a normal root write uses a handful of each.
- Known gap, unchanged here: `apply_storage_delta` is importable by any guest, so a guest can still write unmetered by handing it a delta of its own. The docs now say so. Closing it would need the node to mark sync executions (or to meter replayed deltas too), which is a separate decision.
- Docs: `HOST_FUNCTIONS.md`, `build/host-functions.mdx`, `crates/runtime/AGENTS.md` and the `VMLimits` comments describe which writes are charged.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p calimero-runtime --lib -- root_state apply_storage_delta`, new tests in `crates/runtime/src/logic/host_functions/system.rs` that call the real host functions:
  - `test_persist_root_state_refuses_an_oversize_root_like_storage_write`: the same oversize value is refused by `storage_write` and by `persist_root_state` with `ValueLengthOverflow`.
  - `test_persist_root_state_draws_on_the_storage_write_budget` (`StorageWriteCountExceeded`) and `test_persist_root_state_draws_on_the_storage_write_byte_budget` (`StorageWriteBytesExceeded`).
  - `test_persist_root_state_charges_the_budget_it_draws_on`: a successful root write is charged, so interleaved writes run out of budget.
  - `test_persist_root_state_accepts_a_root_within_the_limits`: a normal-size root persists and reads back.
  - `test_apply_storage_delta_ignores_the_write_limits`: a delta carrying an 8 KiB root is applied under a 4 KiB value cap and a zero write budget.
- On master the refusal and charge tests fail (the root write succeeds); metering `apply_storage_delta` makes the apply test fail.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p calimero-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p calimero-runtime`: all pass.
- CI: the tests run in the `Rust tests` job (`cargo nextest run --workspace`) in `ci-checks.yml`. No core CI job runs a JS app end to end, so calimero-sdk-js should run its e2e suite against this change.

author: graemegrant
body:
## Why

The `build-check` dependency audit has been failing on `main` since new advisories were published (the weekly Security Audit on main failed on 28 Sept). Because the audit runs before lint, typecheck and build, every PR currently fails CI without those checks running, including #30.

## What changed

**brace-expansion: patched, not allowlisted.** This is a high-severity DoS advisory, reached only through ESLint tooling. Patched releases exist within the same major versions, so the lockfile moves to 1.1.21, 2.1.7 and 5.0.12. Those version bumps are the only lockfile changes. (`npm update` also tried to prune an optional peer, `@swc/helpers` under next-intl; that was put back so nothing else moves.)

**adm-zip ×4, decompress ×1: allowlisted.** These come through the same `@sanity/cli` deploy-tooling path that `.audit-ci.jsonc` already allowlists: the template deploys via Vercel, never runs `sanity deploy`, and none of this code is in the site's runtime bundle. The real fix is still the sanity@6.x major upgrade, which is left as its own sign-off decision.

| Advisory | Package | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| GHSA-7q85-xj36-vmfc | adm-zip | high |
| GHSA-8238-w5pm-2374 | adm-zip | high |
| GHSA-j5f4-cc29-5x44 | adm-zip | high |
| GHSA-rcw4-f5rp-g42v | adm-zip | high |
| GHSA-hrh2-vp3x-79xf | decompress | critical |

## Checks (local, on a clean `npm ci`)

- `audit-ci --config .audit-ci.jsonc`: passes
- `npm ls`: no invalid or missing packages
- `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`: pass

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a way to convert hex counts into real-world land area by introducing configurable physical hex dimensions and land-share percentages for `Coastal Land` and `Island` hexes. 
- Expose controls so users can set and edit the hex physical size and land-share parameters at map creation and later in the inspector. 
- Ensure imported maps and autosaved maps normalise the new `hexDimensions` field so older saves remain compatible.

### Description

- Added a `HexDimensions` type and `DEFAULT_HEX_DIMENSIONS` to `shared/types.ts` and threaded a `hexDimensions` field through `MapState` with `createMapState` defaulting to the default dimensions via `createMapState` in `shared/layers.ts`.
- Implemented `normaliseHexDimensions` and `politySurfaceAreas` in `shared/surfaceArea.ts` to compute per-polity land area using the pointy-top hex area formula (¾ × width × height) and accounting for `coastalLandPercent` and `islandLandPercent`.
- Plumbed the feature through the UI: Setup screen now collects hex width/height/unit and land-share options, the Inspector gains an `AreaSettings` panel to edit dimensions post-creation, and the Legend shows polity areas formatted with units; `App.tsx` and `Inspector.tsx` call `normaliseHexDimensions` when loading maps.
- Updated app state handling: added `setHexDimensions` action in `src/state/store.ts` and applied changes to map state with `updatedAt` bump; `src/state/import.ts` now normalises `hexDimensions` during import.
- Minor wiring: `politySurfaceAreas` is used in `src/components/Legend.tsx` to annotate polity swatches with computed areas, and the new UI fields are validated and passed into `onCreate` from `src/components/SetupScreen.tsx`.

### Testing

- Added unit tests in `test/surfaceArea.test.ts` covering `politySurfaceAreas` behavior for coast/island weights and multiple owners, and the `setHexDimensions` reducer case. The tests were run and passed. 
- The new tests exercise the area math and the reducer update, and they completed successfully with no regressions reported.

author: will383842
body:
## Identité

Auteur: A07
Relecteur: A09 exactitude · A09 securite
Couvre: REQ-JUR-009, REQ-JUR-060
Lot:

## Ce que fait cette PR

JUR-T09 (revendication #355). Elle écrit **un seul texte** d'information de l'article 14 du RGPD pour la personne qu'un apporteur déclare.
- `src/content/micro-copy/courriels/information-article-14.ts` est porté par l'e-mail de confirmation W20 : une entrée par rubrique de l'art. 14, son ordre de rendu, une version, et le libellé du lien d'opposition.
- `src/content/micro-copy/console/script-de-qualification.ts` en est la mention orale lue à l'appel. Elle y renvoie sans recopier aucune rubrique, et prévoit deux cas : l'e-mail est parvenu, ou l'information part au plus tard lors de l'appel.

Les textes ne portent aucune valeur. Responsable, apporteur (prénom et nom seulement), durées et mention de transfert sont des paramètres. Ils ne donnent ni la date du contact (REQ-JUR-040), ni aucun lien autre que ceux de REQ-JUR-060.

`docs/runbooks/mise-en-service.md` gagne une case bloquante : aucun e-mail de confirmation réel ne part tant que la base légale de TRT-TIERS, les durées de conservation (HYP-RGPD-RETENTION) et la localisation de l'hébergement du serveur et des sauvegardes ne sont pas tranchées au registre. Ce sont trois décisions de Williams, soumises à sa séance du 2026-10-02. L'hôte d'envoi est documenté comme `smtp.zeptomail.eu` dans des commentaires du code d'axion-ia (AFF-48). La valeur effective de `SMTP_HOST` sur `axion-ia-worker` est constatée dans Coolify et datée avant que la case soit cochée.

**Choix de rédaction à juger par les lentilles :**
1. La base légale est un PARAMÈTRE, `{baseLegale}`, lu au registre. La proposition A07 (l'intérêt légitime, 6.1.f) est écrite en en-tête comme À TRANCHER par Williams : une autre décision change le texte et sa version (v4).
2. L'opposition vaut pour **toutes** les présentations qui concernent la personne (HYP-W20-OPPOSITION), et pas pour la seule présentation en cours.
3. Le ton répond à une question de Williams (« ça ne fait pas très pro non ? »), à faire valider en séance : une suite commerciale d'abord, la vérification ensuite. Les deux usages restent écrits dans la finalité, donc la notice reste fidèle au traitement réel.

**Garde `ux:exhaustivite` :** deux entrées sont ajoutées à `MICRO_COPIE_HORS_PORTEE` (`scripts/gates/ux-exhaustivite.ts`), chacune avec sa raison. `console/script-de-qualification.ts` : « script de la console, lu par le qualifieur, jamais par l'apporteur ». `courriels/information-article-14.ts` : « courriel au prospect, hors de l'espace : couvert par le témoin information-article-14 ».

**Reste, hors de cette PR :** aucun motif de `scripts/gates/lexique-apporteurs.ts` ne couvre `src/content/micro-copy/courriels/**`. Ce texte, comme celui d'UX-P1-41, n'est donc jugé par aucune garde lexicale, et `ux:exhaustivite` le déclare hors de portée : seul le témoin de la tâche le protège. Le motif `courriels/**`, versé dans UX-P1-41, fermera ce trou.

## ROUGE avant VERT (REQ-GOV-012, RM-02)

<!-- rouge-vert:debut -->

ROUGE : sur main c478d8e7, `npx vitest run tests/unit/juridique/information-article-14.spec.ts` → « FAIL tests/unit/juridique/information-article-14.spec.ts — Error: Failed to load url ../../../src/content/micro-copy/courriels/information-article-14 (resolved id: ../../../src/content/micro-copy/courriels/information-article-14) in …/tests/unit/juridique/information-article-14.spec.ts. Does the file exist? » — Tests no tests. Sur la tête, avec un texte muté (source : « … et indique avoir échangé avec vous le 12 mars. ») : « AssertionError: expected [ 'source : une date du contact' ] to deeply equal [] » — Tests 1 failed | 5 passed (6). Base légale (v4) : `npx vitest run tests/unit/juridique/information-article-14.spec.ts`, témoin « base légale en clair » ajouté AVANT de retirer l'exception : `× REQ-JUR-060 — TÉMOINS : chaque règle rougit sur un texte cassé d’un geste` ; `AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'baseLegale : un nombre en clair' ]` ; `Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)`. L'ancienne exception laissait passer « l’article 6, paragraphe 1, point f ».
VERT : `EXCEPTION_BASE_LEGALE` retirée (0 occurrence), tout chiffre dans toute VALEUR du gabarit est une faute : ` ✓ tests/unit/juridique/information-article-14.spec.ts (6 tests) 15ms`, `Tests  6 passed (6)`. Le commentaire du spec dit que la règle porte sur les valeurs, pas sur le texte rendu (`{baseLegale}` y sera rempli avec « 6, paragraphe 1, point f »). `pnpm mutation:pr` : « aucun fichier mutable (src/domain/, src/server/, src/lib/) dans les 4 fichier(s) de la PR contre origin/main : rien à muter » (les textes vivent sous src/content/).
Correctif ux:exhaustivite (960108ec) :
ROUGE : gate-a de #368 sur 9446fa1d, `ux:exhaustivite` → `micro_copie_non_lue`, 2 fautes (`console/script-de-qualification.ts`, `courriels/information-article-14.ts`), constat de la CI.
VERT : `npx tsx scripts/gates/ux-exhaustivite.ts` → `✅ ux:exhaustivite — 12 issue(s) confrontée(s) à REQ-UX-002, dont 6 refus confrontés à REQ-SEC-022 ; 23 écran(s) confronté(s) (17 de l'espace, 6 de la console) avec leur état vide ; 9 composant(s) .tsx confronté(s), aucun libellé en dur ; 7 fichier(s) de micro-copie.` ; `information-article-14.spec.ts` → `Tests  6 passed (6)`.
Rouge constaté par: A06

<!-- rouge-vert:fin -->

> A07 n'a pas d'outil d'exécution : A06 a écrit le témoin, produit le rouge et signé la ligne.

## Attaque (REQ-GOV-011)

<!-- attaque:debut -->

Scénario joué : une valeur réelle glissée dans un texte remis au contact (une date du contact, une URL, une coordonnée de l'apporteur, un nombre en clair à la place d'une durée paramétrée, une rubrique recopiée dans le script) apprendrait au contact plus que ce que REQ-JUR-040 et REQ-JUR-060 permettent, ou ferait diverger les deux textes.
Résultat : onze témoins cassés, chacun rouge sur sa règle, dont la base légale en clair, sans contre-témoin ; sur la tête, le spec est vert 6/6, donc les textes livrés n'en portent aucun. Aucune autre attaque n'a été jouée.
Joué par : A06

author: jeedo
body:
Implements plan task 25: `dr-ansible draft PATH MODULE`.

## Usage
```
dr-ansible draft PATH MODULE [--merge | --full] [-o/--output FILE] [--config FILE]
```
- **`--merge`** (the default) uses `render_merge` from task 20. It keeps the existing `RETURN` byte for byte and adds only the missing keys (AC-9). With no valid `RETURN` to merge into, it gives the full draft with a note. For a sidecar `.yml`, it gives the entries to paste in.
- **`--full`** uses `render_draft` from task 19.
- `--merge` and `--full` are one click flag pair, so the last one given wins.
- MODULE is chosen as in `returns`: a name, alias or FQCN, or a glob that matches exactly one module.
- `--run` comes in task 27.

## Decisions to review
- **`--output` and NFR-5.** The command refuses any `--output` path inside the project's module directory or action-plugin directory, and exits 2. That covers the module file itself, its sidecar, and any new file among them. The architecture says "no code path writes to the analysed tree". I chose the narrower rule so you can still write drafts elsewhere in a repo, for example `drafts/`. Tell me if you'd rather refuse anything under the project root.
- **Writing a file.** When `--output` is given, stdout stays empty and `wrote draft for <fqcn> to <file>` goes to stderr. An existing file at that path is overwritten. A failed write, such as a missing directory, exits 2.
- **Exit codes:**
  - `0` when a draft was printed or written. A draft is the requested output, not a finding, so `draft` doesn't use `audit`'s exit code 1.
  - `2` for a module that can't be parsed (`cannot draft <fqcn>: <reason>`), and for a PowerShell module. In both cases there's nothing to draft, and the spec maps parse errors to 2.
  - `2` for the usual usage and project errors.
- **Exempt modules** can still be drafted.

## Tests (`tests/test_draft_command.py`)
- The CLI output matches `render_merge` / `render_draft` exactly, with merge as the default.
- A missing `RETURN` falls back to the full draft.

author: mattjj
body:
**Not needed for correctness if #41160 lands:** #41160 fixes every example this PR fixes, and more (table at the end). But this PR also makes grad tracing faster with custom_jvp3 (next section), so it's worth landing on its own.

Under reverse mode, custom_jvp3 linearized each application into an opaque CustomJVPTraced.linearized node whose only rule is its transpose. But backward_pass3 runs an eqn forward when it can't tell it's linear, which happens when a linear computation has no linear inputs, like a jit whose tangent comes from a fresh Ref (see #41160):

```python
@jax.jit
def g(x):
  ref = jax.new_ref(0.)
  return jax.nn.relu(ref[...])

jax.grad(g)(1.)
# with JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1: TypeError: can't apply forward-mode autodiff (jvp)
# to a custom_vjp function.
```

With jax_custom_jvp3=0, the jvp rule's linear part is traced into ordinary ops (here a select_n), so running it forward just wastes work computing a zero. Now custom_jvp3 does the same under vjp as it already does under linearize: it stages its `linearized` map as ordinary ops instead of the opaque node, so the linear jaxpr matches the classic one. This also fixes jaxpr_effects_test's test_scan_const_input_effect_indexing under JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1.

Batched applications, from grad of vmap, keep the opaque node, since a rule can produce more-batched tangents than its primal output, which only the reverse rule handles (see CustomJVP3Test.test_hard_stuff2). That case, and custom_vjp functions, which have no forward rule, are covered by #41160.

**Tracing time.** Without this PR, each custom_jvp3 application's backward rule traces its linear map again and transposes it with `jax.linear_transpose`. With it, the linear map is staged once into the outer linear jaxpr and transposed there. That was about 20% of grad-tracing time in a profile of the benchmark below. Times per relu to trace `jax.jit(f)` and `jax.jit(jax.grad(f))` for `f` = a chain of n `jax.nn.relu(x) * 1.01 - 0.001` steps, at n from 100 to 3000. Every configuration scales linearly in n, so the per-relu cost is the same at every size:

| | forward trace | grad trace |
|---|---|---|
| classic (all flags off) | ~130 µs | ~520 µs |
| all three flags | ~158 µs | ~800 µs |
| all three flags + this PR | ~158 µs | ~650 µs |

**Which examples each PR fixes** (✗ is the TypeError):

```python
@jax.custom_vjp
def h(x):
  return x
h.defvjp(lambda x: (x, None), lambda _, ct: (ct,))

@jax.jit
def f(x):  # custom_vjp
  ref = jax.new_ref(0.)
  return h(ref[...])

@jax.jit
def g(x):  # custom_jvp; x only enters through stop_gradient, so the tangent stays disconnected
  ref = jax.new_ref(0.)
  return jax.nn.relu(ref[...] + jax.lax.stop_gradient(x))

xs = jnp.arange(1., 4.)
```

| example | flags | main | #41199 | #41160 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jax.grad(f)(1.)` | default | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| `jax.grad(lambda x: f(x) + jnp.sin(x))(1.)` | default | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| `jax.jit(jax.grad(f))(1.)` | `JAX_CUSTOM_VJP3=1` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| `jax.grad(g)(1.)` | `JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1` | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `jax.grad(lambda x: g(x) + jnp.sin(x))(1.)` | `JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1` | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `jax.vmap(jax.grad(g))(xs)` | `JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1` | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `jax.grad(lambda xs: jax.vmap(g)(xs).sum())(xs)` | `JAX_CUSTOM_JVP3=1` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| `jax.grad(jax.remat(lambda x: f(x) + jnp.sin(x)))(1.)` | default | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `jax.grad(jax.remat(lambda x: f(x) + jnp.sin(x)))(1.)` | `JAX_REMAT3=1` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

The custom_vjp rows come out the same with `JAX_CUSTOM_VJP3=1`, except that `jax.jit(jax.grad(f))` already works on main with default flags, because DCE removes the eqn before lowering. Landing both PRs gives exactly the #41160 column, so **if #41160 lands, #41199 isn't needed for correctness**, though it still speeds up tracing.

author: ashley-hunter
body:
Closes #271

## Cause

- `keyboardType` only wrote `inputmode`, and `secureTextEntry` wrote `type` as `password` or `text`, so a one-line `<input>` was never `type="tel"` or `type="url"`.
- The multiline swap (`BrowserEngine.fieldFor`) focused the new element but did not carry the selection, so the caret jumped to the end.

## Fix

- `props.ts`: one `setInputType` writes a one-line field's `type` from both props: `password` while `secureTextEntry` is on, else `tel` for `phone-pad`, and `text` for the rest. Both handlers call it, so either can change without undoing the other.
- `url`, `email-address` and the number keyboards stay `inputmode` only. In Chromium, `type="url"` and `type="email"` trim a value the app sets (and the value of a field whose type changes to them), so the field would disagree with the model. `type="email"` also throws `InvalidStateError` from `setSelectionRange` (which `setSelection()`, `[selection]` and the `setTextAndSelection` command use), and `type="number"` has the same selection gap and changes the value to a number. `tel` keeps the selection API and the value as set (checked in Chromium).
- `browser-engine.ts`: a focused field swapped by `multiline` gets its `selectionStart`, `selectionEnd` and `selectionDirection` back after it is focused. `keyboardType` is written again after the swap, with `secureTextEntry` and `numberOfLines`.

## Verification

- New jsdom tests in `element-props.test.ts`: the type for each keyboard, password winning over the keyboard and handing back to it, a value with spaces around it kept through every keyboard and a password-to-url change, the type surviving a swap back from a textarea, and focus plus a backward selection carried both ways.
- New Chromium test in `browser/events.test.ts`: types into a phone field, selects 2 to 5, swaps to a textarea and back, and a typed key replaces that selection.
- Bite: with `props.ts` and `browser-engine.ts` reverted, the four jsdom tests fail (`text` where `tel` was expected, selection `[11, 11, 'none']` for `[2, 7, 'backward']`), and the Chromium test fails with the caret at the end of the field. The spaces test guards the url change from review and passes on main, which never sets a type.
- `@ng-native/web` lint, typecheck, test and test:browser through Nx, and `pnpm format:check`.

## Left out

- `type="url"` and `type="email"`: would need the value kept in step with what the browser trims, and for email, `setSelection` and `[selection]` to skip a field with no selection API.
- `web-search` and `numbers-and-punctuation` keyboards still map to nothing on the web.

body:
## Zusammenfassung

Archivist lässt sich jetzt jederzeit beenden, auch während eines großen Scans oder einer OCR. Danach ist ein Neustart sofort möglich.

**Job-Queue (`packages/core/src/services/jobs.ts`)**
- Neu: `interrupt(timeoutMs = 5000): Promise<{ interrupted: number; unfinished: number }>`. Es startet keine weiteren Jobs. Laufende Jobs werden über ihr `signal` mit einem `JobInterruptedError` abgebrochen und auf „wartend“ zurückgesetzt. Die Unterbrechung verbraucht keinen Versuch, und die Meldung lautet „Beim Beenden unterbrochen – wird beim nächsten Start fortgesetzt“.
- Die Methode wartet höchstens `timeoutMs`. Jobs, die das Signal ignorieren, werden danach aufgegeben: Ihre Zeile steht bereits wieder auf „wartend“, und was der Handler danach noch tut, wird nicht mehr gespeichert, auch nicht `report`.
- `JobInterruptedError` erweitert `JobCancelledError`, deshalb behandeln Handler die Unterbrechung wie einen Abbruch (`isJobCancelled` liefert `true`). Mit `isJobInterrupted(err)` lassen sich die beiden Fälle unterscheiden.
- Eine Unterbrechung ist kein Abbruch: Die Hooks `onCancelled` und `onFailed` laufen nicht. Fehler, die ein Handler nach der Unterbrechung wirft (abgebrochene LLM-Anfrage, beendeter Worker-Pool …), gelten nicht als Fehlschlag. Ein Job, den der Benutzer vorher abgebrochen hat, bleibt abgebrochen.
- `throwIfCancelled()` wirft den Grund aus dem Signal, also bei einer Unterbrechung den `JobInterruptedError`.
- `stop()` ist unverändert (Pause, wartet auf laufende Jobs).

**Dienste**
- `shutdown(opts?: { jobTimeoutMs?: number })` verwendet `jobs.interrupt` statt `jobs.stop`.
- Wird eine Dokumentanalyse unterbrochen, bleibt das Dokument „in Analyse“ und wird nicht als abgebrochen markiert. Nach dem Neustart setzt der wiederaufgenommene Job die Analyse fort; `recoverInterruptedAnalyses` erkennt, dass ein Job es abdeckt.
- Der Scanner erkennt eine Unterbrechung über `isJobCancelled` und meldet sie nicht als Scanfehler.

**Desktop (`apps/desktop/src`)**
- Neu ist `lifecycle.ts` mit `QuitController`, ohne Abhängigkeit von Electron und daher testbar. `before-quit` fährt die Dienste mit einem Zeitlimit von 5 s für Jobs herunter. Der Prozess endet spätestens nach 10 s, auch wenn das Herunterfahren hängt oder fehlschlägt.
- `second-instance` öffnet ein neues Fenster, wenn keins existiert; sonst holt es das vorhandene Fenster nach vorn. Wird die Anwendung gestartet, während sie sich noch beendet, startet sie danach neu (`app.relaunch()`).

## Tests
- `tests/integration/quit-interrupt.test.ts`: kooperative Unterbrechung, Zeitlimit bei Jobs, die das Signal ignorieren, Fehler nach der Unterbrechung, vorher abgebrochene Jobs, Beenden während einer Analyse mit anschließendem Neustart (in beiden Fällen: der Handler reagiert auf das Signal bzw. wird nach dem Zeitlimit aufgegeben).
- `tests/unit/desktop-lifecycle.test.ts`: Ablauf beim Beenden (genau ein Exit, Frist, Fehler, Neustart während des Beendens).
- Lokal erfolgreich: typecheck, format:check, lint, depcruise, knip, `npm test` (620 Tests), build, Playwright-E2E unter xvfb (32 Tests).

Closes #75

author: oliviertrudeau
body:
## Problem

AWS connectors are org-shared, but ExternalIds are stored per-workspace. Every AssumeRole path resolved the ExternalId from the **caller's** workspace:

```python
ws = get_or_create_workspace(user_id, "default")
external_id = ws.get("aws_external_id")
```

Meanwhile `get_all_user_aws_connections` matches on `user_id = %s OR org_id = %s`. So for any org member who didn't personally run AWS onboarding:

1. They see every org-shared account in the UI ✅
2. `get_or_create_workspace` finds no workspace for them → **mints a brand-new random ExternalId**
3. STS sends that ExternalId; the trust policy requires the original → `AccessDenied`
4. **All** accounts fail identically, because it's one shared secret — not one policy per account

`get_or_create_workspace` is what made this silent. On a read path it created a workspace as a side effect, so there was never a "missing workspace" error to notice — just a wrong secret. The correct value was already sitting in `user_connections.workspace_id`, which the connection SELECTs didn't return.

Azure is unaffected (no ExternalId, no workspace coupling), which is a useful tell when triaging.

## Why it was mistaken for a region bug

AWS returns a byte-identical error for a rejected *principal* and a rejected *ExternalId condition*:

```
User: arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/... is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: ...
```

It never says which. With the fan-out collapsing everything to `"Failed to assume role"`, the only visible symptom was "all AWS queries fail" — which reads as a region or permissions problem. Real time was lost auditing IAM permissions that were correct all along.

## Fix

- New read-only helper `resolve_connection_external_id()` — resolves from the workspace that **owns the connection**, and fails closed. Never calls `get_or_create_workspace`.
- `workspace_id` added to the connection SELECTs so callers can reach it.
- Applied at all three AssumeRole sites: single-account agent path, multi-account fan-out, and `get_credentials_from_db`.
- `AccessDenied` now names both possible causes and logs a **fingerprint** of the ExternalId sent (never the value — it's the trust-policy shared secret).

## Verification

Reproduced and confirmed on staging. One org, three users; only the onboarding user could use AWS. The failing user's workspace was created **99 seconds before** its first failed AssumeRole — `get_or_create_workspace` minting it mid-query — and carried a different ExternalId than the role's trust policy requires.

Ruled out IAM permissions: the caller role has `sts:AssumeRole` on `*`.

- 5 new unit tests (`server/tests/utils/test_connection_external_id.py`), including that the read path never mints an ExternalId
- Verified the tests fail against the old logic
- Full server suite: 2007 passed (pre-existing Redis collection errors unrelated)

## Not in scope

An earlier revision of this PR added a region field to onboarding. Dropped — the stored region is only a CLI *default*, not an access boundary: the trust policy's sole condition is `sts:ExternalId`, the session policy has no `aws:RequestedRegion`, and an explicit `--region` from the agent passes through untouched. Credentials already reach every region.

There is a separate, real issue there — a wrong default returns an empty result rather than an error, and `provider_rules.py` never tells the agent which region it's in, so it can't tell "no resources" from "wrong region." That wants agent-prompt work and multi-region support, not a text input. Filing separately.

## Follow-ups

- `_verify_external_id_required` fires a second AssumeRole per account per command — 36 STS calls for an 18-account org — and fails closed on any non-`ClientError`, e.g. a transient timeout.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes CVE-2026-65905 (GHSA-9xv2-5v5q-p794, CWE-294): a replay bug in the Tomcat DIGEST authenticator. `tomcat-embed-core` comes in transitively at **8.5.23**, the version managed by `spring-boot-starter-parent:2.0.0.M7`. The 8.5.x line is EOL and won't get a fix, so this PR overrides the BOM-managed version through the parent's `tomcat.version` property: ```xml 1.8 + 9.0.121 ``` That property controls every `org.apache.tomcat.embed:*` artifact (`tomcat-embed-core`, `-el`, `-websocket`). 9.0.121 is the earliest version that fixes the CVE. Java stays at 1.8 (Tomcat 9 needs Java 8 or later). **This is a major bump (8.5 → 9.0).** We stay on Spring Boot 2.0.0.M7, a milestone release that targeted Tomcat 8.5. Tomcat 9 is the line Boot 2.1+ ships with, and its embedded API (`Tomcat`, `Connector`, `Http11NioProtocol`) is mostly the same as 8.5. Even so, nobody has checked this exact pairing; see the gaps below. The proper long-term fix is to move off the 2.0.0 milestone parent onto a supported Boot release, which is out of scope here. Exposure note: the app authenticates with Spring Security form login, and nothing in `src/` configures Tomcat DIGEST auth. The vulnerable path is probably not reachable at runtime, but the vulnerable artifact still ships. ## Verification — NOT completed - **Build/tests not run.** This session's network policy only reaches the git proxy. Network access to Maven Central, repo.spring.io and Snyk was requested but not approved. The `2.0.0.M7` parent POM isn't in the local Maven cache, so `mvn` can't resolve the project even on unmodified `master`. The repo also has no `src/test`, so there are no existing tests to run. - **Snyk before/after issue count not available**, for the same reason. Expected result: the CVE-2026-65905 issue on `tomcat-embed-core@8.5.23` goes away. Please confirm with `mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=org.apache.tomcat.embed` (should show 9.0.121) and `snyk test` before merging. body:
Hygiene fixes to the seat bridge from today's four seat rounds (Varka identities, Varka expansion, Furina pool, Kokomi pool). Python only; the bridge DLL is unchanged, so no deploy is needed.

1. **Lane torn down on a slow state read** (Varka lane 2, act 3, floor 45). The lane's `godot.log` shows the window regaining focus after 47 minutes in the background and the bridge writing both state answers just after the 20 s client timeout. `lanewatch` no longer counts state timeouts as a death; `blindplay` retries the read after 5, 15 and 30 s while health answers, then refuses with `NO ANSWER: the game is up but slow` (no teardown). The log-flood and memory signals still end a storming lane.
2. **`play` targeting.** An aimed card with no living enemy (Test Subject dead, revive pending) is refused as such, not "more than one enemy, so say which". An `end turn` typed right after a refused command on an unchanged board is held once, so a batched turn is not lost.
3. **Ransack gave no potion.** The game offered it (run history: `POTION.HEART_OF_IRON`, `was_picked: false`); the seat walked past the reward screen. `proceed` past gold, a potion or a relic is now held once (also closes the BACKLOG gold-drop line).
4. **Crystal Sphere `leave`** on its reward screen is now that screen's `proceed`, with the same unclaimed check.
5. **? room merchant with no shelves.** The fake merchant's shelves sit under `fake_merchant.shop.items`; the page read only `shop.items`. Fixed; `buy` resolves.
6. **`--brief`** drops the italic `*Word* — meaning` glosses and the standing reference notes (FRONT, aura, multi-intent, intent figure, repeated names); a gloss that carries a protected line is kept in place.

The Archive folder and the archive action shared one translation key, `mail.archive`. Most languages translate it as the folder name, so archive buttons, menu items, tooltips and the confirmation dialog showed a noun: "Arquivo" in Portuguese, "Archivo" in Spanish, "Archiv" in German.

- **New key:** `mail.archive_action` is added to the types and to every locale.
  - Each value matches the wording the locale already uses for the archive filter action (`settings.fam_org_filter_action_archive`).
  - Hindi uses "आर्काइव करें", the polite form of its other mail actions.
  - English stays "Archive".
- **Action sites now use the new key:**
  - the context menu and the reading pane and detail toolbars;
  - the list row hover button and the popup, detail and thread menus;
  - the archive confirmation dialogs, the select-all confirmation and the bulk toolbar;
  - the sender and newsletter archive buttons, the search result quick action and the keyboard shortcut list;
  - on mobile: the long-press menu, the detail toolbar and sheet, the bulk bar, the swipe actions and the toolbar settings.
- **Folder names stay on `mail.archive`:** the sidebar and mobile drawer, view and page titles, folder pickers, search scopes and filters, mail rules, and alias delivery.

- New `inbox_dialogs.archive_label.test.tsx` renders the single and bulk archive confirmations with the real pt and pt-BR translations.

author: xxxcess
body:
## Problem

Recon run for *"what can you tell me about donald trump and his social media activity?"*:

1. Tools suggested under "Additional context" (`sociavault_profile`, `keybase_identity`, `stackexchange_users`, …) never ran.
2. Search-result publishers were extracted as entities: `apnews`, `kark`, and `Donald Trump` typed as an organization with domain rollcall.com.
3. After the first version of this PR, the user's test showed SociaVault, Keybase and Wikipedia users all skipped with "no input can be derived from the subject". Only Stack Exchange ran, `truthsocial (organization) truthsocial.com` appeared as an entity, and the run died on an OpenRouter 429.

## Discovery and selective enrichment: new flow for people and organizations

The flow applies only when the targeted subject is a **person or an organization**. That is decided by `investigation::target_kind` / `accounts_flow` from the question: explicit identifiers, event/topic/place/product words, org words, pronouns, and name shape. Topics, events, places, products, domains/IPs and unclassified subjects keep the existing investigative-question search and get no handle step.

1. **Firecrawl query 1:** general identity and context for the subject (unchanged).
2. **Firecrawl query 2: associated online accounts.** The query is `<subject> official social media accounts profiles handles`, with role `accounts`. The model may rewrite it, but the rewrite must still be an accounts query. The Discovery note reads "…one for identity and one for the subject's associated online accounts" only in this flow.
3. **Account extraction** (`orchestrate::extract_accounts`). The Recon model reads both result sets and returns `accounts` (platform + handle) and up to four `tools` to call.
   - Each model handle must appear as a whole token in a result, use a known platform, and belong to the subject. Either the handle carries the subject's name, or its own profile page is titled with the subject.
   - The **deterministic fallback** (`investigation::fallback_accounts`) reads profile URLs in result links and text: x.com, twitter.com, truthsocial.com/@, instagram.com, facebook.com, github.com, keybase.io, youtube.com/@, tiktok, threads, linkedin, twitch.
   - Model and fallback results are merged and deduplicated (`merge_accounts`). Only accounts that belong to the subject are kept, and they are attached to the subject entity as handles (`attach_accounts`).
4. **The handles feed the tools.** Tool isolation runs the model's tool picks first, then the catalog relevance ranking (up to 4 distinct tools in this flow).
   - `sociavault_profile` runs **once per supported account** (platform + handle) up to the turn's SociaVault allowance. Accounts over the allowance are listed as skipped.
   - `keybase_identity` / `wikipedia_users` use that platform's own handle, else the subject's best-evidenced handle.
   - `stackexchange_users` / `wikidata_entities` use the subject's name.
5. The decision block shows **Accounts found:** (e.g. `twitter @realDonaldTrump (model, pattern)`) with a note on how they were extracted, plus **Tool isolation:** listing what ran and what was skipped, with reasons.

**Account platforms are never entities.** truthsocial.com, x.com, instagram.com, github.com, keybase.io and similar hosts never become organization entities or subject identifiers. They become handles on the subject when the account belongs to it, and stay as citations otherwise.

## Provider errors / 429
- New per-turn `ModelGate`. The first Recon model call that fails with a provider 429 or rate limit trips the gate. Account extraction falls back to the URL extractor, and every later Recon model step in the turn (subset, assessment, …) uses its existing rule fallback **without calling the provider again**. No retries were added.
- If the answer (synthesis) step fails, the run is marked failed with an explicit message: `Answer step failed: provider 429 …. The provider rate limit was reached. The N tool result(s) from this run are saved; resume run <id> when the provider is available.` Tool calls are already persisted, and resume skips completed calls.

## Kept from the first version of this PR
- `question_subject` subject parsing: drops lead-ins such as "can you tell me about" and trailing clauses such as "and his …".
- News and source filtering: publisher sites, article pages and call-sign stations are citations, not entities. The subject is typed person or organization and never inherits a source domain.
- Suggested tools execute through `execute_budgeted`: credits, call budget, opening Hunter/SociaVault caps, missing-key skip reasons, plus one bounded follow-up wave for the assessment's suggestions.

## Tests (Rust 1.94)
`cargo test --workspace`: core **56 passed** (43 on main), bin 15 passed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean.

New or updated tests:
- `person_and_organization_discovery_searches_for_accounts_second`: query 2 is the accounts query for Trump, Bezos, Amazon, and "Acme Holdings Inc".
- `other_subjects_keep_the_investigative_question_and_skip_accounts`: ukraine war, "How did Amazon start?", inflation, example.org and an election keep the investigative query, and `accounts_flow` is false. Hypothesis and adaptive strategies are also unaffected.
- `fallback_extractor_keeps_only_the_subject_accounts`: `realDonaldTrump` is found from x.com and truthsocial.com/@ URLs, plus instagram and keybase. A reporter's X account and an unrelated GitHub user are dropped.
- `model_accounts_are_grounded_owned_and_merged_with_the_fallback`: invented, unowned, unsupported-platform and substring-only handles are rejected. Firecrawl and unknown tool picks are dropped. Model and pattern results merge as `(model, pattern)`.
- `account_platforms_attach_to_the_subject_and_are_never_entities`: no truthsocial/x/instagram/github/keybase/apnews entity. Donald Trump is a person with twitter, truthsocial, instagram and keybase handles and no domain.
- `extracted_handles_feed_sociavault_keybase_and_wikipedia`: SociaVault steps run for twitter then instagram (platform + handle). Keybase and Wikipedia get usernames and Stack Exchange gets the name. With an allowance of 1, the instagram lookup is skipped with the allowance reason.
- `rate_limited_account_extraction_falls_back_and_the_loop_continues` (async): a local mock provider returns HTTP 429. Extraction returns pattern accounts and a note containing 429, the gate trips, and later model calls make no further provider requests. Cancellation still fails the step.

author: sisyphuszheng
body: ## Summary Root-cause fix for the A2 JSX whitespace incident (owner ruling 2026-10-02): the element compiler now cleans JSX text with the **React-contract algorithm** — a faithful port of Babel's `cleanJSXElementLiteralChild` / the TypeScript JSX transformer's line-based cleaning, replacing the blunt `\s+`→space collapse at `lower-program.ts:481/:983`. Three rules, per the facebook/jsx spec as React implements it: - **R1 (node boundaries)**: leading/trailing whitespace runs touching a newline are stripped; - **R2 (node interior)**: whitespace runs containing a newline fold to one space; pure space/tab runs are preserved verbatim; - **R3 (between elements)**: sibling-delimiting runs with a newline are removed; newline-free runs survive (the one-space form inline siblings render today). Effect: any React-family formatter (oxfmt included) is now structurally safe on OE JSX — the multiline layout they produce serializes identically to the inline layout (`40⏎4` renders `404`, not `40 4`). This also harvests the documented transition state from #1497 (page-home arrow's temporary extra spaces converge). ## Implementation notes - Input is the parser's canonical `JsxText.text`, not `getText(sourceFile)` — the latter drops whitespace abutting tags and would narrow the runs before the rules apply (documented in-code). - 297-line matrix test (`compiler-jsx-text-whitespace.test.ts`) covers the three rules' boundary combinations including CRLF and the 404 wrap shape. ## Verification - `deno task --cwd packages/element test` green (full suite + new matrix). - `deno task check` green. - `deno task site:build` green (real SSG build — the gate whose absence let the item-context regression through last round). - Independent review confirmed spec fidelity and no oracle weakening; no oracle baselines required movement (none pin multiline-text output shapes). ## Provenance Inserted between A2 (#1497) and A3 by owner ruling after the "40 4" incident chain: root cause was OE's deviation from the JSX whitespace contract that React-ecosystem formatters rely on. Not a filed issue — rides the alpha7 milestone.

author: danielgwilson
body:
With `E2B_DEBUG=true`, the E2B SDK (e2b 2.49.0, `dist/index.mjs:4731`) returns `true` from `Sandbox.kill` without sending a request. `killById` read that `true` as `terminated`. So `humanish reclaim` in debug mode:
- reported every recorded sandbox `killed`;
- wrote that into `reclaim-receipt.json`;
- with `--preflight`, discarded the journals of sandboxes that may still be running.

## Change

- **Reclaim refuses.** `reclaimRunSandboxes` and `reclaimPreflightSandboxes` return `HUMANISH_RECLAIM_E2B_DEBUG` before doing anything else. The message names `E2B_DEBUG`. They load no SDK and write no receipt, and they read and discard no journal. The CLI exits 2.
- **A debug-mode `true` reads unconfirmed.** `killById` returns `{ status: "unconfirmed", reason: "release_unavailable", detail }`, where the detail names `E2B_DEBUG=true`.
  - The routes already treat `release_unavailable` as "no kill reached E2B": no teardown time is recorded and `killed` is false.
  - `DesktopReleaseResult`'s unconfirmed variant gains an optional `detail`. `readE2BRelease`, the terminal route and reclaim's `kill-failed` detail use it. For a missing kill method, `detail` is absent and the existing text is unchanged.
- **The desktop startup cleanup reads it too** (second commit, from Codex's review in `handoffs/2026-10-01-second-review/codex-review-of-1329.md`). `reclaimFailedDesktopCreate` calls the instance `kill()` directly, so it bypassed `killById`. A debug-mode `true` there became cleanup `"killed"`, and the terminal route recorded `terminal-lab.cleanup.killed` with `killed: true`.
  - It now reports cleanup `"unconfirmed"`. `E2BDesktopStartupError.cleanupDetail` carries the `E2B_DEBUG` detail, and the terminal route's cleanup reason includes it.
  - An unconfirmed startup cleanup is not retried, as before.
  - The detail text now lives in `sdk.ts`, so the guard and `killById` share one string.
- **`e2bDebugMode`** in `src/substrates/e2b/sdk.ts` reads the variable the way the SDK does (`index.mjs:1308`): lowercased, equal to `"true"`. `killById` reads it when the call starts, the same point the SDK reads it.
- The `trust-boundaries.mdx` reclaim paragraph gains one sentence on the refusal. CHANGELOG.md gains a line under a new Unreleased → Fixes, after 0.106.0.

## Checked

New tests:
- `tests/substrates/e2b/sandbox.test.ts` "E2B debug mode": the reading table (`true`, `TRUE`, `True`, `false`, `1`, empty, unset), allocation close, `destroyE2BSandbox` and `readE2BRelease`.
- `tests/run/reclaim.test.ts` "reclaim with E2B_DEBUG=true":
  - The refusal loads no SDK, kills nothing, writes no `reclaim-receipt.json` and keeps the receipts.
  - `humanish reclaim --json` exits 2 with the code.
- `tests/lab/preflight-receipts.test.ts`: `--preflight` refuses and keeps a journal whose lease has elapsed.
- `tests/substrates/e2b/desktop-sdk-compat.test.ts`: the installed SDK's own static `kill` in debug mode, behind the startup guard, gives cleanup `unconfirmed` with the detail, and the error is not retried.
- `tests/routes/terminal/lab.test.ts`: a terminal lab whose desktop startup fails with `E2B_DEBUG=true` ends `HUMANISH_TERMINAL_LAB_CLEANUP_UNPROVEN`. Its ledger has `killed: false` and `terminal-lab.cleanup.unconfirmed`, with no `cleanup.killed` event.

The two startup-cleanup tests fail at the first commit (be87af2f, 0f0ea403 before the rebase). Six of the others fail with main's src. I checked by restoring main's `sandbox.ts`, `reclaim.ts`, `desktop-session.ts` and the terminal route and running the tests. The reading-table tests need the new helper, so they don't run on main.

Local gates: typecheck, lint, knip, format:check, docs:check, vocabulary:check, prose:check, `node scripts/public-surface-scan.mjs` and the site typecheck pass. vitest on tests/substrates, tests/run, tests/lab, tests/routes and tests/cli, rebased on the 0.106.0 release (f50939ae): 2400 passed, 8 skipped. Lint is at 444, the cap after the release ratchet.

## Not checked

- A live E2B run or reclaim with `E2B_DEBUG` set.
- A debug flag passed as a create option (`debug: true`) rather than through the environment. No `src/` caller passes it; the SDK compatibility tests use it to skip HTTP and override `kill` themselves.

author: hiansoares
body:
## O que muda

A investigação automática de offense passa a usar os metadados de campos reais, a continuar jobs pelo mesmo search ID dentro de um orçamento explícito, a investigar processos e PowerShell quando os registros associados os mostram, e a concluir proporcionalmente às evidências. As 15 tools e seus schemas de entrada continuam iguais; os retornos ganharam chaves novas sem remover as existentes.

### Metadados de campos (`aql_fields.py`)
- Os resources `events`/`flows` são lidos como dados não confiáveis. Propriedades Windows/Sysmon opcionais só entram no SELECT quando estão listadas; nomes inseguros são ignorados, nunca escapados.
- Cada consulta registra campos obrigatórios, opcionais selecionados, ausentes e rejeitados. Se o QRadar rejeitar os opcionais, a consulta é validada de novo sem eles, preservando INOFFENSE. INOFFENSE nunca é trocado por busca de IP.

### Continuidade, paginação e diagnóstico (`ariel_collection.py`, `aql_errors.py`)
- Orçamento explícito: tempo, jobs, polls e páginas (padrão 60 s, 12 jobs, 60 polls, 40 páginas de 500).
- Jobs pendentes são consultados pelo mesmo search ID; nada é recriado para retomar resultados.
- Cada consulta tem `outcome`: `pending`, `error`, `unavailable`, `empty`, `complete_in_window`, `limited`, `partial` ou `not_started`.
- Ao fim do orçamento, `continuation_plan` traz search ID, cursor, AQL, escopo, motivo e tools. LIMIT atingido gera `new_partitioned_query`, separado da paginação do mesmo job.
- `record_count` de agregação não é confundido com COUNT(*)/UNIQUECOUNT; agregação sem linha não recebe número inventado.
- Erros tipados: política local (não transitória), validação do QRadar, formato, conexão, timeout e permissão. Mensagens não repetem texto upstream, URLs ou tokens.

### Processos, PowerShell e integridade (`windows_events.py`, `process_chain.py`, `integrity_evidence.py`, `focused_queries.py`)
- **Campos extraídos com proveniência:** EventID, Computer, UtcTime, ProcessGuid, ParentProcessGuid, ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Image, ParentImage, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine, User, LogonId, LogonGuid, TerminalSessionId, Hashes e RecordNumber.
  - As fontes são propriedades listadas e payloads XML/JSON/texto.
  - EventID não depende só de QIDNAME.
  - Rótulo repetido no texto torna o valor ambíguo e impede seu uso em vínculos.
- **Vínculo pai/filho:** só por GUID normalizado + host.
  - PID, IP ou tempo isolados não ligam processos; a reutilização de PID é reportada.
  - Ciclos são limitados.
  - Pai ausente na janela é lacuna.
- **Classes de evidência separadas:** criação de processo observada, arquivo citado como argumento, conteúdo de sessão PowerShell (4104/4103) e hipótese legítima.
- **IEX:**
  - O critério é documentado e distingue o token de `iexplore.exe`.
  - CommandLine sem argumentos não exclui conteúdo posterior.
  - Base64/UTF-16LE é decodificado só como dado.
- **Integridade:** 5038/6281 são descritos sem concluir corrupção ou comprometimento.
  - Arquivo diferente da cadeia fica como achado separado.
  - Hash repetido ou caminho de fornecedor não provam integridade.
  - Hashes abreviados não comprovam igualdade.
- **Consultas focadas:** busca de pai, script blocks, integridade e flows do host. Só rodam com gatilho registrado e literais validados.

### Avaliação proporcional (`offense_assessment.py`)
- `gap_details` traz identificador, escopo, estado, relevância por conclusão (`blocks`/`secondary_for`), evidência e próxima ação.
- O assessment separa `collection_completeness`, `confirmed_facts`, `hypotheses` e `final_verdict_possible`. Um censo de flows pendente não bloqueia relatar uma cadeia de processos observada.
- `final_benign_verdict_permitted` continua `false`, com o significado explicado: não proíbe relatar fatos comprovados e não é forçado para `true` para encerrar o caso.

### Instruções do Kiro e documentação
- O steering `offense-verification` e o `qradar-aql-conventions`, os agents `case-investigator`, `threat-hunter`, `report-writer` e `response-advisor` e a skill `offense-investigation` incorporam as dez regras de condução pedidas: continuar buscas read-only autorizadas sem perguntar, "não localizado" ≠ "não coletado", `truncated_fields`, sessão Windows ≠ PSM, natureza de conta, logging retroativo, QRadar-only vs `investigate_*`, `get_rule`, LAST/epoch vs START/STOP, e contenção/tuning condicionados.
- Atualizados `docs/offense-verification.md`, `docs/bridge-known-limitations.md`, `README.md` (em inglês) e `README-kiro-pack.md`.
- `configure_kiro.py` e `start-kiro-soc-bridge.ps1` não foram alterados.

## Validação

- Base antes da mudança: 94 testes aprovados.
- `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests` com `PYTHONPATH=src`: **125 testes aprovados**, incluindo o teste de transporte MCP HTTP local.
- 31 testes novos, só com dados sintéticos (IPs RFC 5737, domínio `example.test`, GUIDs e hashes artificiais). Cobrem:
  - processo só na última página;
  - job pendente retomado sem duplicação;
  - orçamento esgotado com cursor preservado;
  - LIMIT atingido com `has_more=false`;
  - `record_count` agregado diferente de COUNT;
  - campos opcionais ausentes ou rejeitados;
  - vínculo por GUID com reutilização de PID;
  - PowerShell sem argumentos com 4104 posterior;
  - ausência de 4104 sem inferência sobre forwarding;
  - IEX versus `iexplore.exe`;
  - 5038 de arquivo diferente da cadeia;
  - hash repetido sem prova de integridade;
  - truncamento preservado no parsing;
  - rótulo injetado no payload;
  - isolamento entre offenses e argumentos inválidos;
  - classificação e redação de erros;
  - schemas e permissões read-only das 15 tools.
- Três testes antigos que faziam patch de `run_query` em `offense_evidence` foram reescritos com um QRadar sintético de páginas, mantendo a mesma intenção.
- `git diff --check` sem problemas. Varredura dos arquivos alterados sem IDs reais, IPs fora das faixas de documentação/privadas ou segredos.

## Limites desta revisão

- Nenhuma consulta foi feita em produção. Os formatos de resource de campos e de payload do QRadar real podem diferir dos sintéticos; o parser trata isso como lacuna, não como ausência.
- **Critério de IEX:** não detecta ofuscação.
- **Associação 4104→processo:** por host+PID+tempo, é sempre candidata.
- **Security 4688:** sem GUID, não gera vínculo pai/filho.
- **Busca de pai:** fica na janela de ±15 min dos eventos INOFFENSE e se limita a quatro consultas.
- **Orçamento padrão:** pode encerrar antes das consultas focadas; o `continuation_plan` indica o que retomar.

author: smaug123
body:
The interpreter answered "which member does this MemberRef name?" with its own search. It looked only at the parent type's own members, matched by comparing *concretised* signatures, and crashed when nothing matched. TypeSystem already answers the same question as CoreCLR does, with `MethodReferenceResolution` (`MemberLoader::FindMethod` over method tables, base classes included). The Loader does the same for fields with `FieldReferenceResolution` (`FindField`, comparing signature blobs exactly). The escape analysis uses both. This PR switches the interpreter's `resolveMemberWithGenerics` to them, so there is one MemberRef resolver rather than two.

## How the declaring type is instantiated

- **Member on the parent itself:** instantiated from the parent as the frame instantiates it, exactly as before.
- **Method on an ancestor:** instantiated through the extends clauses, using the declaring-type arguments that #1653 added to `MethodReferenceTarget.Defined`.
- **Returned type arguments:** these are now the declaring type's. Every caller passes them on as the declaring type's generics. Prose that called them the parent TypeSpec's has been updated.
- **`TypeReference` parent:** it still spells no arguments. Naming a generic definition that way names its typical instantiation, which the `ldtoken`/`ldftn` callers recognise by the empty arguments and refuse (`TestLdtokenMemberTokens` holds this).

## What it refuses

Each refusal is a `failwith` naming the reference and the case:

- `Missing` / `ParentTypeMissing`. CoreCLR throws `MissingMethodException`/`MissingFieldException`/`TypeLoadException` while compiling the method that uses the reference, which is not modelled.
- `DependsOnInstantiation`: the parent is a type variable of the referencing context.
- `ArrayMethod`: callers handle array accessors before they resolve.
- A generic definition named without an instantiation, when an ancestor of it declares the method.

The ThreadId parameter is unused, as it was before; I've kept it so the public signature is unchanged.

## Evidence

author: sinelaw
body:
Importing the LMMS song from sinelaw/rosaclef#18 (`a_mentsch.mmpz`) and opening the Score view froze the page ("Script terminated by timeout" in `pieces` ← `put` ← `eventsOf` ← `buildScore`).

## Cause
`buildScore` sizes the bars from the notes' **unquantized** ends. A short note just before the song's end rounds onto the final bar line: an arpeggio note at 15.99 beats in a 16-beat clip becomes ticks 17088–17100 when the score ends at 17088. When `eventsOf`/`put` laid it out:
- `measureAt` returned the last bar;
- `mEnd` came out *before* `t`;
- `t = mEnd` stepped back, so `put` looped forever.

The LMMS importer's written-out arpeggios make this easy to hit, but any song with a very short final note could.

## Fix (`web/src/notation.js`)
- Size the bars to hold every note as `chordsOf` quantizes it (a note rounded to nothing lasts a step). A last sixteenth that ends on the bar line still adds no bar.
- `put()` stops if a stretch ever falls outside the bars, so the view can't spin even on input that isn't expected.

## Testing
- New `score.test.js` cases:
  - a note quantized onto the last bar line gets a bar of its own;
  - a last sixteenth ending on the bar line adds no bar.

  The first one hangs on the old code: `timeout` exits 124.
- The imported song (~10k notes): `buildScore` takes about 130–170 ms and `engrave` about 320 ms in Node, where it used to hang.
- In the browser-only build (Playwright/Chromium): import the `.mmpz` → open it → Score. The score appears in about 1.9 s and the page stays responsive.
- `npm test` and Prettier pass. I couldn't run inty locally, so the CI type-check covers it.

author: killjoy00
body:
## Summary

This branch merges PR #783 ("Add public identity safety and moderation") into current `main` with a clean merge (no conflicts). It then changes how players accept the Public Identity rules:

- **Guests never appear on leaderboards.** Ranking stays a signed-in-only feature.
- **No checkbox is needed to rank.** Rules acceptance no longer affects whether a player appears on leaderboards.

The #783 branch itself is untouched: no rebase or force-push, and its commits are included here through a merge commit. If this PR lands, #783 can be closed as superseded.

## Behaviour

| Situation | #783 as written | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Guest (not signed in) | not ranked | not ranked |
| Signed-in player with a free, allowed nickname | not ranked until they tick the checkbox and save | claimed at sign-in, ranked |
| Existing ranked players (before 0046) | dropped from boards until they accept | unchanged, no prompt |
| Daily finished before acceptance | never reaches the board (`persistResult` gate) | ranked as on `main` |
| Prohibited guest nickname at sign-in | not claimed | not claimed (server name filter) |
| Moderator-hidden identity | excluded | excluded |
| Restored identity, later sign-in | not re-owned | not re-owned (claim skips any identity with moderation history) |
| Saving a name or public profile | requires `acceptPublicIdentityTerms` (409 without it) | records current rules version/time; flag optional |

## Changes

- `worker/public-identity-safety.mjs`: eligibility no longer returns `terms_required`. Players must be signed in, own their name, and not be hidden.
- `worker/draft-run-function.mjs`, `worker/draft-run-season.mjs`: removed the terms predicates from the score insert, standings, shared-run names and leaderboard rows. The block-filter parameter is renumbered.
- `worker/growth-function.js`:
  - `reserveUsername` claims a nickname at sign-in without a terms check. It still refuses hidden or placeholder names, names the filter rejects, and identities with moderation history.
  - Public profile, profile lookup and block-target queries drop the terms predicates.
  - The profile save records acceptance; `PUBLIC_IDENTITY_TERMS_REQUIRED` is removed.
  - The `username_ownership_conflict` analytics event is back to main's condition.
- `migrations/0046_public_identity_safety.sql`: comments only. The merge still leaves an adopted nickname unowned, and the app-side claim applies the filter.
- Web (`growth.mjs`, `profile-product.mjs`) and native (`mobile/app/account.tsx`):
  - The checkbox is removed.
  - A "By continuing / By saving … you agree" notice with a rules link is added on the sign-in screens and next to profile save.
- Docs: `docs/PUBLIC-IDENTITY-SAFETY.md`, the store-review notes in `docs/mobile-store-submission.md`, and the `terms/index.html` wording.

## Testing

Run locally on this branch:

- `npm run test:syntax`: passes.
- `node scripts/run-js-tests.mjs`: 781/781 pass.
- Python unittest: 395 OK.
- Mobile: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint . --max-warnings=0` are clean. All mobile `node --test` suites pass (160 tests).
- Browser tests (Chromium):
  - `profile-e2e` passes, including the new assertions that the notice is shown and there is no checkbox.
  - `account-e2e`, `auth-context-e2e` and `patreon-activation-e2e` pass.
  - `email-verification-e2e` passed its Chromium half. Its WebKit half was not run because WebKit isn't installed in the container.

Not run locally (they need an isolated Neon dev branch, so they run in the backend gate):

- `username-uniqueness-backend-smoke`: restores main's link/claim expectations and adds a prohibited-nickname case.
- `public-identity-backend-smoke`: saves without the flag and adds a restore-then-sign-in case.
- `fixed-daily-backend-smoke`, `season-backend-smoke`, `account-session-backend-smoke`, `draft-run-backend-smoke`, `mobile-auth-backend-smoke`: reverted to their `main` versions.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- **Name filter shows the wrong reason.** A guest nickname that fails the name filter shows the existing "choose a unique username" prompt (`username_taken`), not a filter-specific message. Saving it again returns the explicit `USERNAME_NOT_ALLOWED` error.
- **Google Play wording is unverified.** Google Play's UGC policy says users must accept terms before creating UGC. A sign-in-adjacent "By continuing, you agree" notice is a common way to do this, but I have not confirmed how Play reviewers treat it.
- **Load tests from the #783 audit are still open.** NAT never passed on #783, and the distributed-capacity runs are still unresolved. Per the owner's decision, 100-player certification does not block this change.

author: otolock
body:
Since iOS 27, when FreshRSS is added to the home screen and opened as a standalone web app, iOS applies its "Liquid Glass" scroll-edge blur to the top of the screen. The status bar sits on a frosted band that bleeds into the FreshRSS header and washes it out. There is no CSS or meta switch to turn this effect off, but WebKit skips it when something is painted at the very top edge of the screen. Changes proposed in this pull request: - Add an empty, `aria-hidden` `
` at the start of `` in `app/layout/layout.phtml` (not emitted for Ajax responses) - In `p/themes/base-theme/frss.css`, only under `@media (display-mode: standalone)`, make it a fixed 11px strip at the top of the viewport. `background-clip: text` with no text keeps it invisible, and `pointer-events: none` keeps it from intercepting taps - Regular browser tabs and desktop are unaffected, since the rule only applies in standalone mode Workaround credit: https://tips.ojapp.app/en/ios-27-pwa-top-blur-workaround-2/ How to test the feature manually: 1. On an iPhone or iPad running iOS/iPadOS 27 or later, open FreshRSS in Safari and use Share → Add to Home Screen 2. Launch FreshRSS from the home screen icon 3. Before: the top of the screen has a frosted blur band over the header. After: the status bar sits on a clean edge with no blur 4. Check that regular Safari tabs and desktop browsers look unchanged Before (iPad): After (iPad): Before (iPhone): After (iPhone): Pull request checklist: - [x] clear commit messages - [x] code manually tested (iPadOS 27, standalone web app) - [x] code manually tested on iPhone - [ ] unit tests written (optional if too hard) — N/A, CSS/layout only - [ ] documentation updated — N/A _Disclaimer_: Troubleshooting and fix implemented with the help of AI. author: mcc197
body:
## Summary

### Scheduled checks (`.github/workflows/watch.yml`)
- **Nightly watch** runs `airegs watch`. When a watched source changes it opens a `source-change` issue, or comments on the open one. Hashes are kept in the Actions cache.
- **Weekly stale report** (Mondays) runs `airegs stale --official` for instruments and requirements. It keeps one `stale` issue up to date and closes it when nothing is due.
- Both can also be run by hand from the Actions tab (`workflow_dispatch`).

### Watcher fix
EUR-Lex gives scripts an empty bot-challenge page. The watcher was hashing that empty page, so the AI Act, Omnibus, DSA and DSA audit rules could never show a change. Now:
- a page with no visible text is reported as an error, not hashed;
- EUR-Lex ELI links are checked through the Publications Office CELLAR SPARQL endpoint. A change lists each new or removed amending act, corrigendum, consolidated version, repeal, supplementing or implementing act, or Commission proposal, by CELEX number with a link.

Also:
- `airegs stale --exit-code` exits 3 when anything is due.
- ISO/IEC 42001 is now watched via the IEC webstore, because iso.org returns 403.
- The coe.int treaty page is no longer watched (always 403). The stale report covers the Convention.

### Data
- **AI Act follow-up from the first watch run.**
  - Added the consolidated text of 27 Jul 2026 as an official source.
  - The corrigenda have no English version, so they don't affect the English text.
  - Implementing Regulation 2026/1755 is procedural only.
  - New instrument `eu-md-ivd-simplification`: proposal COM(2025) 1023, which would move the MDR and IVDR to Annex I Section B and take AI-enabled medical devices out of the high-risk regime.
- **`eu-gdpr`.** Verified against the Official Journal text. Four requirements: Art. 22, Arts. 13–15 (information about automated decisions), Art. 25 and Arts. 35–36. They are crosswalked to the AI Act, ISO/IEC 42005, ISO/IEC 42001 and the California ADMT rules.
- **`eu-digital-omnibus`.** Proposal COM(2025) 837. Its GDPR changes for AI are a new Art. 88c (legitimate interest), Art. 9(2)(k), a recast Art. 22 and EU-level DPIA lists.
- Both proposals are recorded with status `proposed`, linked with `amends` / `amended_by`, and have no requirements until they are adopted.

## Notes for the reviewer
- GDPR controllers are mapped to the existing `provider` / `deployer` roles, following the CCPA precedent. The role vocabulary is unchanged.
- `test_obligations_cli` now expects two EU deployer impact assessments: AI Act Art. 27 and GDPR Arts. 35–36.
- The scheduled jobs need Issues enabled on the repo. GitHub pauses schedules after 60 days without repository activity.

## Testing
- `python -m airegs validate`: OK, 24 instruments.
- `python -m pytest -q`: 46 passed.
- `actionlint`: clean.
- Both workflow jobs dry-run locally with a stand-in `gh`, including a simulated new amending act.

## Summary

This PR transforms the historical vulnerability-detection prototype into COVE-Code: Controlled Evaluation of Parameter-Efficient Vulnerability Detection in Source Code.

### Methodology changes
- Canonical task is binary function-level vulnerability detection.
- Replaces the incompatible 10-class/7-field task definitions.
- Adds leakage-aware, project-grouped train/validation/test preparation.
- Adds frozen-encoder linear-probe, full fine-tuning, and LoRA conditions.
- Adds LoRA rank and dataset-scaling configurations.
- Adds F1, recall, PR-AUC, calibration, threshold, error, language/CWE, and efficiency infrastructure.

A CI workflow is included for syntax compilation and unit tests. Full empirical validation still requires a verified dataset release and actual model training/evaluation.

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

Nothing you can see changes, except speed. Supply pages that show stock across the network now load in the same time however many field workers a program has: the program map, the portfolio, an item's page, an order's "where is this equipment now" panel, the checks page, the overview, and the hourly stock alert. Every figure on them stays exactly the same.

Worker stock reports can now only be read in for test (labs-only) programs, the same rule that already applies to reading stock from visits.

## Technical Summary

The two follow-ups from #2103 (plan Deviation 19) that block switching stock-from-visits on for a real program.

**1. Every `network_stock` reader in grouped SQL.** Under the visit model every worker is a supply point, so a `resupply.plan` per point grew with the roster.
- `network.network_stock` takes every rate from grouped SQL: `belief.beliefs_for` (one pass per item held), and a new `_rates_across_items` for a point with no one item. That is `resupply.plan(item=None)`'s rate, grouped, for points holding several items or stock recorded against the product only. The `network_stock` operation is used by the map (`map_data.py` `_cover` and `program_map`), the portfolio, and the item and order pages (`views.py`), and it needs no change at its call sites. The chain summary (`summary.py`) and checks get the same treatment.
- Figures are unchanged. A point holding several items keeps its summed rate everywhere except the Stock page, which keeps the "choose one" behaviour it got in #2103 (`several_items="refuse"`, replacing `grouped=True`). A window shorter than 30 days still gives the plan's "too short" reason (`resupply.window_too_short`, now shared).
- `network_stock(per_point=True)` is kept as the reference the parity tests compare against. No caller uses it.
- Checks: the count-day variance is `soh.counted_against_ledger`, which is `stock_on_hand`'s figure grouped per item, using the row's sole item as `stock_on_hand` resolves it. The never-reported check's "holds stock" fact is one query instead of an `exists()` per worker.

Query counts, going from 3 to 15 workers on the same world (before → after):

| Caller | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `network_stock` operation, all items | 43 → 115 | 24 → 24 |
| `network_stock` operation, one item | 43 → 115 | 14 → 14 |
| map cover (`_cover`) | 44 → 116 | 15 → 15 |
| `checks_list` | 81 → 213 | 47 → 47 |
| `chain_summary` | 71 → 143 | 42 → 42 |

**2. Labs-only gate on stock reports.** `supply_ingest_stock_reports` now refuses a program or opportunity that is not labs-only, using `scopes.require_synthetic` and `require_programme_opportunity` as `visit_consumption_ingest` does. It checks at entry, before a token is read, and again right before `fetch_visits`. The `stock_report_ingest` operation refuses before any write. The visit reader's own report path calls the service directly and is already gated by `visit_consumption_ingest`.

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story

- Read paths only, plus a refusal. No migration and no data change.
- Every figure is pinned to the per-point code it replaces. On a world with single-item, several-item and product-only points, plus counted and uncounted workers and a count followed by later deliveries:
  - every `network_stock` row equals the `per_point=True` row, field by field, for all items and for each item;
  - every variance equals `soh.stock_on_hand`'s;
  - the whole stock-checks output equals what the old per-point reads produce.
- The gate only narrows what can run. The dev seed and the synthetic seeder register their programs as labs-only first, so they are unaffected.

### Automated test coverage

- New `tests/test_belief_callers.py` covers parity (rows, the summed rate, the Stock page's refusal, the short window, variances, the stock checks) and query counts that stay constant as workers grow for each caller.
- `test_worker_reports.py`: the command refuses a real program, a real opportunity under a labs-only program, and a saved export of a real program. It also refuses at the fetch itself. The operation refuses and writes nothing, and records a labs-only program's reports.
- `test_stock_operations.py`'s stock-report tests now register their program as labs-only.
- Locally, `make test ARGS="connect_labs/supply_chain -q -n auto"`: 2406 passed, 9 skipped.

### QA Plan

After the next deploy, open `/supply/network/`, `/supply/stock/`, the checks page and the program map on the seeded synthetic program. Figures should match the previous deploy.

### Labels & Review

- [x] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: bobdolefever
body:
## What this does

**Six more native functions** (`src/native`): `Magic_PushEventContext`, `Magic_PopEventContext`, `Card_IsInPlay`, `Card_ColorMaskToColorIndex`, `Card_RemapColorIndexF9`, `Card_RemapColorIndexFF`. These are the helpers the first six natives used to *replay* from recorded calls; the natives now call them directly, so a recorded vector of a caller holds their reads and writes as its own. Only four functions are still reached through the replay hook: `Magic_ScanCards`, the two sprite-marking calls and the free-slot finder.

The push and pop's depth compares were read off the real instructions (`jl`, `jle`: signed) rather than trusting the decompiler's `< 0x20`.

**Vectors:** re-recorded from two games (mono-green mirror, and against the red AI deck) with the existing recorder, extended to the new functions. 83 recorded vectors curated across all 11 recorded functions, plus 6 synthetic remap vectors (no recorded game ever had a non-zero remap byte, and the FF lookup was never called). All pass; about 970 recorded calls were checked in total with zero failures.

## A finding the recordings forced

`Card_IsTapped` is misnamed. Recorded calls show it returns **1 for flags `0x30882` (untapped) and for `0x30892` (the same plus the tap bit)**, and 0 only for cards not in play: it ignores tapping entirely. Renamed `Card_IsInPlay`. Its formula also requires bit `0x20` clear; that bit never appeared together with bit `0x2` in any recorded game, so that half is static only, and the docs say so. The two colour-remap lookups were also mislabelled (`Card_UntapCard`/`Card_SetTapState`, `Duel_GetCardModifiedPower`/`Duel_GetCardColorOverride`); they are renamed by what the body does, with the semantic claim marked static.

Same drift pattern as before: most of these had names in the C sources while the three DUEL index files still said `FUN_<address>`, so renames were applied by address as well as by name.

## Checks
- `make check` clean, `make test` 85/85, `tools/difftest` + `tools/registry` + `tools/twins` tests 50/50, registry checker 112 rows with 0 mismatches.
- Native build clean under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wconversion`, and under ASan/UBSan.

## Note for anyone building on this Mac
The default macOS SDK here (27.0) no longer links with the installed Command Line Tools linker, even for an empty `main`; I built with `SDKROOT=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX26.5.sdk` (set per command, no system settings changed). Updating the Command Line Tools should fix it properly.

author: nitjsefnie
body:
## Summary
Adds an opt-in per-account cap on concurrent claims, keyed by the claimant's repository role: a caller sets `max-claims` to comma-separated `ROLE=CAP` pairs (roles `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain`, `admin`; `-1` unlimited, `0` forbids the role), and the action counts the commenter's open assigned issues in the repository with the search API before assigning, refusing above the role's cap with a reply that names the role and the cap. The default `-1` keeps behavior exactly as today.

## Related Issues and Pull Requests
Fixes #29
Relates to #61 (idle expiry, deliberately out of scope here)

## Changes
- `action.yml`: new optional input `max-claims` (default `-1`), wired to the step env as `MAX_CLAIMS`.
- `claim.py`: strict grammar validation of the value (`-1` alone, or `ROLE=CAP` pairs with CAP `-1`/`0`/positive; any other negative, non-integer, unknown role, duplicate role or empty entry fails the run before any API call); a role lookup against `repos/{repo}/collaborators/{actor}/permission` using `role_name` (custom roles fold to their base via the `permission` field); a cap of `0` refuses with a "claiming is disabled for your role" reply, a finite cap counts the actor's open assigned issues via `search/issues` (`total_count`, first page) and refuses at the cap; unnamed roles and `-1` are unlimited and skip the search call; refusals exit 0 and never touch assignments; manual assignments are never counted or blocked.
- `tests/run.sh`: 15 new cases pinning every detection branch of the grammar, the exact argv of both new endpoints, the refusal texts, boundary caps, role folding and both failure shapes; `action_contract` updated for the seventh input.
- `.github/workflows/claim.yml`: this repository's own workflow sets `max-claims: 'read=2, triage=4, write=6, maintain=10, admin=-1'` per the maintainer's ruling.
- `README.md`: the input documented — grammar, boundaries, outsider-counts-as-`read`, custom-role folding, the cap's confinement to the action's own `/claim` path, and the search index's eventual consistency.

## Testing
- [x] Bash suite (`tests/run.sh`) — 120 cases, 0 failures on the pushed head (main's suite plus the 19 cap cases; re-run on the branch tip after the rebase onto merged main).
- [x] ShellCheck (every shell file under `tests/`) and Python compilation (`claim.py`) — both clean.
- [ ] Workflow and action lint (actionlint and zizmor) — not installed locally; read from CI on this PR instead.
- [x] Mutation proof: `>=`→`>` failed `cap_refuses_at_limit` and `cap_custom_role_folds_to_base`; dropping the duplicate-key rejection failed `cap_malformed_value_duplicate_key`; both restored and green.

## Follow-ups / Known Limitations
- `.github/workflows/claim.yml` names `max-claims` while its pinned action SHA predates the input, so the caps activate only when a follow-up bump moves that pin to this PR's merged SHA; until then GitHub logs an unexpected-input warning and behavior is unchanged.

## Footer
Generated by GLM-5.3-Flash (brief, implementation, review, verification)

author: o-mario88
body:
> **Stacked on #196 (→ #195 → #193).** Draft until those merge. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## Why

Step 4 of 4 of the Country Director dashboard fix (owner, 2026-10-01). Two things the audit found that the earlier steps did not yet close:

1. **Two pages, two answers.** The Planning Monitor counted every visit type, left out Core Graduate schools, and counted work handed to a Partner as "scheduled by partners" before the Partner had dated it — so it disagreed with Country Planning Oversight for the same plan.
2. **Stale figures.** The dashboard's figures were kept for five minutes; a visit scheduled now could be missing from the Country Director's page until the cache let go.

## What changes

**The Planning Monitor counts by the rulebook** (`apps/planning/country_oversight/rules.py`):

- The people are the rulebook's: a Lead or a CCEO by the role they hold, so a Lead switched to another role keeps their team. This applies to the Execution & Completion Monitor's roster too.
- Visits planned are Follow up, In-school Training and SSA Support, planned and dated. Donor, story, social and invitation visits no longer count.
- Partner activities are those the Partner has dated; everything else in a Partner's hands is "awaiting". Partner work is credited in the same order as on the dashboard (its monitor, then who assigned it, then who holds the school).
- Core Graduate schools are followed like Client schools; "clustered" means in an active cluster.
- The "About these figures" text says so.

**The dashboard follows the plan as it changes** (`freshness.py`): saving or deleting an activity, a Partner hand-over, a cluster roster row or a school is noted; a reader served a snapshot older than the last change gets it rebuilt, at most once every 20 seconds, one reader at a time. With no change, nothing is rebuilt; with no cache configured, nothing changes.

## How the numbers were verified

- `OneRulebookWithCountryOversight`: the monitor's country totals equal the dashboard's — target, visits planned, Partner scheduled, awaiting, schools with a Partner, schools with no visit.
- On a private copy of the dev database the two pages agree for FY2026 and FY2027, and 50 of 50 dashboard and table figures match hand-written SQL.
- `FreshnessTest`: a new plan, a hand-over and a roster change each reach the page on the next read; nothing is rebuilt while nothing changes; a burst of saves does not rebuild on every one.

## Testing

- `apps/planning/test_planning_monitor.py`: three assertions updated for the counting rule (a donor visit is not a counted visit), four agreement tests added.
- `apps/planning/test_oversight_freshness.py` (new).
- Inventories and the traceability matrix regenerated.
