author: a-matson
body:
## Why
Plan item O5 (OBS-5): a run crosses the API, the orchestrator, Redis and a worker, and nothing tied those hops together. One trigger now produces one OpenTelemetry trace. Tracing is off unless `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set.

## What changed
- `backend/internal/tracing`:
  - `Setup` installs an OTLP/gRPC provider configured by the standard `OTEL_*` variables, and stays a no-op without an endpoint. It returns a flush function that `main` runs on shutdown with a detached 5 s context.
  - `TraceParent` and `Start` carry a span across the queues as a W3C `traceparent` string.
  - `newResource` names the service `fluxor-backend`, and `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` still overrides it.
- Spans:
  - the HTTP server span comes from `otelhttp`, skipping `/ws`, `/api/health` and `/api/ready`;
  - `start workflow` (`StartWorkflow`) is the run's root, a child of the request when there is one;
  - `dispatch task` (`dispatchTask`) writes its traceparent to `TaskMessage.TraceParent`;
  - `run task` (worker `executeTask`) continues the message's trace, writes `TaskResult.TraceParent`, and on failure sets the error status with the redacted error text;
  - `process result` (`ProcessResult`) continues the result's trace, so the next dispatch is its child.
- `ExecutionContext.traceParent` keeps the root for dispatches that have no span of their own. This is a marked shortcut: it lives in memory, so a run loaded after a restart continues in new traces. A column on `workflow_executions` is the upgrade path.
- `docker-compose.yml`:
  - adds `jaeger` (`jaegertracing/jaeger:2.21.0`, digest-pinned, UI on `127.0.0.1:16686`, OTLP only inside the network) under the `observability` and `tracing` profiles;
  - passes the backend `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` and `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY`.
- `make e2e` enables `COMPOSE_PROFILES=tracing` and points the backend at Jaeger, so CI checks the trace end to end.
- README (Observability) and `.env.example`; regenerated `frontend/src/types/generated.ts` for the two new fields.

## Evidence
- `make e2e` → `--- PASS: TestE2E_TriggerIsOneTrace (2.07s)` and `ok  github.com/a-matson/workflow-orchestrator/backend/e2e 10.087s`. The test triggers a run and finds, in Jaeger's v3 API, one trace containing a server span and the `start workflow`, `dispatch task`, `run task` and `process result` spans.
- Probing Jaeger 2.21 with a real span showed two things:
  - it serves only `/api/v3/…` (`/api/traces` returns 404), and it ignores `query.attributes`, so the test matches the run's trace client-side;
  - the first resource setup reported `service.name=unknown_service:zzprobe`, because `resource.Merge` let `resource.Default()` override the name. Fixed with `resource.New`; `TestNewResource_ServiceName` covers it.
- govulncheck flagged the first dependency versions: GO-2026-6505 in otel/sdk and otlptrace v1.43.0, and GO-2026-6348 and GO-2026-6061 in grpc v1.80.0. On otel v1.46.0, otelhttp v0.71.0 and grpc v1.84.0, `govulncheck ./...` exits 0.
- Full local gate on `322a1d0` (base `9583f4e`): gofmt clean; `go vet` (default, integration, e2e) ok; golangci-lint (default, integration, e2e) `0 issues.`; gosec v2.29.0 exit 0; `go test -race ./...` and the integration suite: no FAIL; frontend lint, type-check, knip, test:unit and build: rc 0; tygo drift: none; `scripts/check-compose.sh` exit 0.

## Tests
- unit: `TestSetup_OffWithoutEndpoint`; `TestStart_ContinuesTraceParent` (a traceparent continues the trace as a child, a span in ctx takes precedence, separate roots get separate traces); `TestNewResource_ServiceName`.
- integration: `TestTracing_OneTracePerRun` (a two-task run started under a request span: every dispatch, run and process span is in the request's trace, with counts 1/2/2/2).
- integration: `TestExecuteTask_ContinuesTrace` (the worker's span is a child of the message's dispatch span, and the result carries the worker span's traceparent).
- e2e: `TestE2E_TriggerIsOneTrace` (real stack plus Jaeger).

## Assumptions
- Assumption: losing trace continuity for runs resumed after a restart is acceptable for now (see the shortcut above).
- Assumption: outbound HTTP made by tasks does not propagate `traceparent`, so trace IDs do not leak to third-party endpoints.
- Assumption: CI pulling the Jaeger image for e2e is worth it for an automated check of the acceptance criterion.

## Risk & rollback
- With `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` unset (the default), spans are no-ops and nothing is exported.
- With it set, export is asynchronous (batch processor). An unreachable collector costs dropped spans, not failed requests.
- Rollback: revert the commit. There is no schema change.

## Dependencies added
- `go.opentelemetry.io/otel`, `otel/sdk`, `otel/trace`, `otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc` and `contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp`. The standard library has no tracing or OTLP support, and these are the reference implementation the plan selected (§ dependencies, O5). They raise `google.golang.org/grpc` to v1.84.0.

author: xam1dullo
body:
Fixes the five HIGH regressions from the 2 Oct 2026 production audit of automaktab.uz, plus four cheap MEDIUM items. No copy changes, no redesign. The fixes use the existing road-signal tokens and fonts (Nunito, Manrope, JetBrains Mono). Every issue was reproduced on a local `next build && next start` of `origin/main` (5cc37db). Each one got a regression test that failed on `main` before its fix and passes on this branch. ## Screenshots (before = origin/main build, after = this branch) | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | /pricing 1440 | | | | /pricing 390 | | | | /changelog light | | | | /changelog OS dark | | | | /ru/changelog light | | | | /ru/changelog OS dark | | | (The PNGs live only on the `pr-assets/release-regressions` branch, not in this diff. The test Mac has no Barlow installed, so the "before" changelog shows the Times fallback that most visitors get.) ## H1: inner pages almost unstyled (pricing, features, privacy, terms, blog; uz/ru/en) **Root cause (confirmed):** 6685218 "adopt road-signal landing visual system" (PR #23, merge 11c05a5) rewrote `globals.css` (−2159 lines). It deleted the shared component rules: `.section-shell`, `.eyebrow`, `.signal-point`, `.glass*`, `.button*`, `.article-tags`, `.article-cta`, `.blog-empty`, `.article-back`, `.article-meta`. But the SEO, blog, changelog and not-found templates and `GlassPanel` still render those classes. `git log -S` on each class points to that commit. #21 (dc014ac) had added the `.glass*` rules and was not at fault. #26 later re-added only `.blog-page`, `.article-page`, `.article-header` and part of `.article-prose`. The related links were also invalid markup: `
  • ` directly inside `
    `. Hypotheses, ranked: 1. The rules were deleted from source while the markup kept using them. **Confirmed.** 2. Tailwind v4 purged "unused" custom CSS. **Falsified:** the shipped sheet still has `.article-prose`. 3. Inner routes don't load `globals.css` after the #26 layout split. **Falsified:** /pricing loads the same single stylesheet with the other global rules. 4. A stale CDN asset. **Falsified:** the local build reproduces it. **Fix:** - Restored the vocabulary in `@layer components`, restyled in road-signal tokens. `.glass` is now a paper card with a sand border. `.button-primary` and `.button-secondary` copy the header and report CTAs. The layer lets Tailwind utilities on `GlassPanel` still refine these rules. - `.section-shell` reuses the `.landing-container` rule. - Added the `.article-prose` heading and paragraph spacing that preflight was zeroing. - Wrapped the related links in a `
      `. **Tests (browser):** - `release-regressions.spec.ts`: "ships CSS for every class it renders" on /pricing, /ru/pricing, /en/pricing, /features/payments-and-debt, /privacy and /blog. It walks every CSSOM rule and fails on any class in `
      ` that no rule matches. - "/pricing renders the eyebrow, related links and CTA as components". **Prevention:** - Keep the class-coverage check in CI. - Before deleting a visual system, list the class vocabulary still used in markup (e.g. `rg -o 'className="[^"]+"'`). - Better still, move shared templates onto shared components or utilities. ## H2: /changelog unreadable in OS dark mode **Root cause (confirmed):** `ChangelogView` (added in 6685218, #23) uses `dark:` utilities. In Tailwind v4 those default to `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. The site is light-only (`colorScheme: "light"` in `home-metadata.ts`, body stays `rgb(245,247,242)`). Measured locally: in dark mode the h1 turns `rgb(255,255,255)` on that light background, a 1.08:1 contrast. The CSS has exactly one `prefers-color-scheme` block, and it is these utilities. Hypotheses: 1. The media-based `dark:` variant fights a light-only shell. **Confirmed.** 2. Browser auto-dark or forced colours. **Falsified:** the colours come from author CSS. 3. A dark page background was meant to flip as well but got lost. **Falsified:** no dark shell rule exists anywhere. **Fix:** a single `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));` in `globals.css`. Nothing ever sets `.dark`, so `dark:` stays inactive until the whole site supports a dark theme. **Test (browser):** "keeps AA text contrast when the OS prefers dark mode" on /changelog and /ru/changelog. Under `colorScheme: 'dark'` it composites each text node's background and requires at least 4.5:1. **Prevention:** the site-wide variant stops any future `dark:` from following the OS. If dark mode is adopted later, build it class-based and end to end. ## H3 and H4: changelog falls back to Times; /ru/changelog mixes serif Cyrillic with Latin Barlow **Root cause (confirmed):** - `ChangelogView` hard-codes `font-['Barlow']` and `font-['Barlow_Condensed']`, arbitrary family names with no fallback, instead of the font tokens. This worked only while `next/font` happened to register a family named "Barlow". - 02a2b1e (PR #34, 2 Oct) replaced the `next/font` Barlow fonts with Nunito and Manrope in `LocaleDocument` and in the `--f-*` tokens. The changelog was not updated, so `document.fonts` now holds only Nunito, Manrope and JetBrains Mono. The computed `"Barlow Condensed"` matches nothing and falls back to the browser default serif. - H4 is older. Barlow has no Cyrillic glyphs (and was loaded latin-only since #23), so Cyrillic always fell back per glyph. Hypotheses: 1. Barlow is no longer loaded and the stack has no generic family. **Confirmed.** 2. CSP `font-src` blocks Barlow. **Falsified:** Barlow is never requested at all. 3. Barlow has no Cyrillic. **Confirmed** for H4. **Fix:** - `font-['Barlow_Condensed']` → `font-display` (Nunito) - `font-['Barlow']` → `font-body` (Manrope) - `font-['JetBrains_Mono']` → `font-mono` All three are loaded through `next/font` with latin and Cyrillic subsets (mono is latin-only) and real fallback stacks. **Test (browser):** "renders every glyph with the site's web fonts" on /changelog and /ru/changelog. It asserts no Barlow in computed stacks, then uses CDP `CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode` to require zero glyphs rendered in system (non-web) fonts for h1, h2 and li. **Prevention:** - Ban arbitrary `font-['…']` families (lint rule or a grep test) and use only the `font-display`, `font-body` and `font-mono` tokens. - W

Synchronous generation occupies R's foreground thread. D-037 adds `llm_generate(async = TRUE, on_progress = ...)`, returning a standard promise while a native worker reuses the loaded model/context, plus `llm_cancel(m)` for cooperative cancellation. One active job, no queue, bounded inputs/outputs and deferred close/GC preserve ownership.

This is a development milestone following 0.3.0. Only the approved optional later/promises dependencies and scoped transitive exception are added; no Rust dependency or vendor patch. Namespace shutdown keeps the DLL mapped for surviving finalizers; forced DLL unmapping is unsupported.

body:
## Summary
- Extract a grant-aware write-attempt coordinator while retaining exact-call binding and downstream approval policies in the Tools adapter.
- Reuse the managed API transport for writes and PR reads, including sanitized synchronous executable-resolution failures.
- Replace warning-text parsing with structured, bounded completeness evidence. Bind pagination protocols to tool contracts and preserve unknown state for missing or malformed metadata.
- Consolidate field/grant card observation, polling, retries, cancellation, session/call isolation, and revocation fencing behind a domain-aware hook.

author: nickstassen
body:
## Summary

NickLink v1.2 shrinks the board from **34 × 33 mm to 33.19 × 25.5 mm (−25% area)**. It keeps both 2×10 headers and all four M2 holes. Every header pin is now **labelled beside it on the front silkscreen**, and the v1.1 review findings are fixed.

![v1.1 vs v1.2 at the same scale](https://github.com/NickStassen/nicklink/blob/v1.2/docs/images/compare.png?raw=true)

| | v1.1 | v1.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Outline | 34 × 33 mm | **33.19 × 25.5 mm** |
| Pin labels | numbered table on back | **name beside every pin, front** |
| 5 V on headers | — | **J1.1** (VBUS via Schottky; ≤5.5 V input) |
| Reset / boot | NRST pin / BOOT0 slide switch | **RESET + BOOT buttons** |
| SWD | split across J1/J3 | **all on J3** (3V3, GND, SWDIO, SWCLK, SWO, NRST) |
| Crystal | 16 MHz | **8 MHz** (Blue Pill / STM32duino / CubeMX default) |
| LDO | AMS1117 SOT-223 + tantalum | **TLV75533** WSON + ceramics |
| USB ESD | — | **USBLC6-2P6** |
| I2C pull-ups | fixed 1.5 kΩ on PB6/PB7 | removed |
| LEDs | power | power + **user LED on PC13** |

**The pinout changed.** v1.2 is not pin-compatible with v1.1. The new table is in the README and `docs/pinout.csv`.

## How it's built

The design is now generated from two files:
- `tools/spec.py`: parts, nets, header pinout and LCSC numbers.
- `tools/placement.py`: board size and part positions.

`tools/build_all.sh` runs the whole flow: it generates the schematic, runs ERC and checks the netlist against the spec, places the parts, autoroutes with Freerouting, adds GND stitching vias, and runs DRC with schematic parity. `tools/fab.sh` then produces the Gerbers, drills, JLC BOM/CPL, PDFs, renders and check reports. Everything runs in Docker (`kicad/kicad:10.0`). See `tools/README.md`.

## Verification
- ERC: 0 errors, 0 warnings (`checks/final-erc.rpt`)
- DRC: 0 violations, 0 unconnected, 0 schematic-parity issues, no exclusions (`checks/final-drc.json`)
- Crystal traces: top layer only, no vias. USB D+/D−: 10.9 / 15.6 mm.
- Edge.Cuts outline in the Gerbers: 33.19 × 25.50 mm

## Before ordering / bring-up
- [ ] Check the CPL rotations in JLC's placement preview. These are KiCad's raw values, not corrected for JLC; check U1, U2, U3, Y1, D1–D3, SW1/SW2.
- [ ] Several parts are JLC Extended (loading fee each); see `tools/parts_research.md`.
- [ ] Hand-solder the through-hole parts (USB-C, headers).
- [ ] Bring-up checklist is in `docs/REVIEW.md`. Key items: measure 5V/3V3, HSE startup (try 18 pF if it runs fast), USB both orientations, BOOT+RESET into the USART1 bootloader, LDO temperature at load (the 250 mA budget is an estimate).

author: zachooper
body:
This replaces the Python models framework from step 6 with a dbt project, `transform/`. The scope is what we agreed: the stg/int models now, and the new `dim_*` / `fact_*` tables from step 16 on. The old marts in `fmstats/mart.py` stay in Python, since the plan retires most of them.

## What changes
- **`transform/`** builds the 13 stg/int models in schemas `stg` and `int`, with the same relation names as before. A file `<layer>_<name>.sql` becomes `<layer>.<name>`.
  - **SQL that depends on the store** is Jinja over `adapter.get_columns_in_relation` / `run_query`. That covers the column-driven `int.players`, the attribute decode built from the coefficient rows, and the stored-name fallback.
  - **The values that SQL is built from** (attribute order, column names, codes) are dbt `vars`. `tests/test_boundary.py` checks them against `fmstats/contract.py`.
  - **References leave out the database name.** By default dbt writes the store's file name into every view, which breaks the cached R2 copy, `open_readonly`'s temp copy and `ATTACH … AS m`.
- **Tests run inside the build.**
  - **Loader:** it runs `dbt build` in its own process (`load_duckdb.build_models`), so every load and every `--refresh-only` tests what it just built, and a failing test fails the load.
  - **Data tests:** each model's grain and keys. The ratings are checked on a sample, 50 players recomputed a different way plus one rank slice, at ~0.6 s each against ~45 s for a whole-table test.
  - **Unit tests:** the rules that were Python tests building their own store (squad membership, latest entry, loans, the one-year freshness rule, names) are now dbt unit tests in `models/int/_int_unit_tests.yml`: fixed rows in, the rows each model must produce out.
- **The models are built once per load,** at the end.
  - **One exception:** `history.player_snapshots` copies the player views' column layout when it's created. On a store's first load, or a store with no models yet, the models are therefore built once early with `dbt run`, since there's no data to test yet.
  - **Before,** that early build ran on every load.
  - **Compat views:** `raw.players`, `raw.persons`, `v_player_ratings`, … stay in Python, now in `fmstats/compat.py`, and are created after dbt.
- **Dependencies:** dbt is a default dependency group, so a plain `uv run` keeps it. It takes the environment from 8 packages to 64 and from 192 MB to 456 MB. `fmq` doesn't use dbt; a query-only machine can drop it with `uv sync --no-group transform`.
- **Removed:** `fmstats/models/`, `tests/validate_models.py`, the framework's unit tests, and the two Python model tests now ported to dbt.
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md, the plan and the docs that pointed at the old framework are updated.

## Checks
- **Fresh build, seven Frem gate saves, vs step 8,** testing on every load: identical on all 13 models, the compat views, `player_snapshots`, `squad_current`, `squad_finances` and `world_fixtures`. It takes 3.7 min.
- **`--refresh-only` on a step-8 store:** identical, in 13.6 s including the tests.
- **Reloading a snapshot:** one build.
- **Snapshot archive:** superseding a snapshot archives all 25,714 players, with names and attributes. The gate saves never trigger this step, so it was run on purpose.
- **Tests fail when they should:**
  - Changing the freshness rule fails two unit tests.
  - Breaking the ratings fails the sample tests (4,500 flagged; the rank test fails when the order is reversed).
  - An empty sample fails rather than passing.
  - A failing test makes the loader exit 1.
- **Site export:** unchanged apart from its timestamp.
- **`test_attribute_model`** on the gate store: all 41,958 modelled values match an independent evaluation of the stored coefficients and reproduce `fmparser/model.py` exactly.
- **`test_boundary`:** the dbt vars match `contract.py`, and the check fails when a var is changed.
- **`run_tests`:** 33 pass, 1 skipped. The skipped one is `test_attribute_model`, which needs a full store; it was run separately above.

body:
Before: fast window vaults only needed a 2.5 m sprint at up to 40°. Barricades were yellow boards the Hunter broke. A window's 3-vault count never started over. The map was 112 m square with corner zones.

After:
- **Fast window vaults:** you need 0.75 s of full-speed sprinting at the window, no more than 45° off straight. Going back over the same window needs 1.125 s.
- **Trash cans replace barricades:**
  - Each can stands beside its gap. Knocked over, it leans at 45° against the structure across the gap, with trash spilled out.
  - The Runner slides over it: fast with Shift held while pressing Space, slow without.
  - The Hunter kicks it away for good, with a visible wind-up (leg drawn back) before the kick. The can then flies off.
- **Visible stun:** a stunned Hunter now staggers and sways, so the Runner can see it.
- **Window blocking:** a window's 3-vault count starts over after 30 s between vaults.
- **Bloodlust:** the Hunter's bloodlust resets the moment a hit lands.
- **Map:** it follows DBD's Rotten Fields: 24 m cells inside a stepped wall, 144 x 192 m.
  - Tiles sit in the clock-position cells: wall pairs at 12 and 3, T walls, a bent wall at 4, and the only long wall at 6.
  - Train-car loops sit at 1, 7 and 10.
  - A shack sits in the middle.
  - The depot spawn is in the top-left corner, with sparse container filler elsewhere.

How:
- `player.gd` keeps about 2 s of movement history for the vault check. It also has new `Pose.SLIDE`, `Pose.KICK` and a swaying `Pose.STUNNED`, replicated with `FLAG_SLIDE` and `FLAG_KICK`.
- `barricade.gd` draws the can and hides the collider. `kick_away()` animates the kick-off.
- `arena.gd` builds the outer wall from an outline polygon and places tiles by cell.

Tested headless:
- **Bot vs bot:** five chases ran with no errors, and the bot Hunter kicked two cans away in each.
- **Vault test:** sprinting at 0° and 40° gave fast vaults; 60° and a 0.5 s sprint gave medium.
- **Bloodlust:** it dropped from II to 0 on a hit.
- **Visuals:** screenshots show a knocked-over can and the Hunter's kick wind-up.

author: is-9108
body:
## 概要

### 1. 利用上限でのモデルの切り替え（`fallback`）
pi は一時的なエラー（429・overloaded・5xx など）を自分で最大 3 回再試行しますが、**利用枠の上限は再試行せずに止まります**（pi-ai の `NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN`: OpenCode Go の月間上限、ChatGPT サブスクリプションの上限、`insufficient_quota` など）。これまでは piHarness のプロセスがそこで止まり、ユーザーが手でモデルを変えて再開する必要がありました。

- 新しい `quota.ts`（純粋関数）: エラーの種類の判定（`quota` / `transient`）、解除の時刻の読み取り（`Try again in 2 hours`・`retry after 90 seconds`・ISO 時刻）、上限の記録
- `agent_settled` で、最後のアシスタントメッセージが利用上限のエラーで終わっていれば:
  1. そのプロバイダーを `.pi/harness/provider-status.json` に上限として記録（解除の時刻が読めなければ `quotaCooldownMinutes` 既定 60 分 / `transientCooldownMinutes` 既定 10 分）
  2. そのプロセスの `models` の候補から、上限中でない次のモデルに `pi.setModel` で切り替え、**同じセッションで**再開の指示を送る（会話は引き継がれる）
  3. 以降のプロセスも、解除されるまでは上限中のプロバイダーの候補を飛ばす（`applyProcessModel`）
  4. 候補がすべて上限なら、解除の目安を表示して止まる（勝手に再開しない）
- 認証エラー（401 など）は切り替えの対象にしない
- `/harness models` に上限中のプロバイダーと解除の時刻を表示
- `install.mjs` は `.gitignore` に `provider-status.json` を追加。`commitArtifacts: true` でもコミットしない

**仮想モデル（`pi.registerVirtualModel`）を使わなかった理由:** 仮想モデルの `route()` が失敗したモデルを受け取って切り替えられるのは、pi が自動で再試行するとき（`reason: "retry"`）だけです。再試行されない利用上限のエラーはその経路を通らないため、この用途には使えません。1.0 の時点でも実験的な機能です。

### 2. 開発用の依存を pi 1.0 に更新
- `devDependencies` の `pi-coding-agent` / `pi-ai` / `pi-agent-core` を `^1.0.0` に更新（`^0.99.1` では 1.x に上がらないため）。`peerDependencies` は `*` のまま
- README に pi 1.0 のフルスクリーン表示の案内（スクロールバックで見返したいときは `tuiMode: "regular"`）を追加。推奨する pi のバージョンを 1.0 以降に

## テスト
- `npm run check`（型チェック + ユニット 151 件 + E2E 4 本）が pi 1.0.0 ですべて通過
- 新しい E2E `test/e2e/fallback.ts`: 偽のプロバイダーを 2 つ（primary / backup）用意し、
  - primary が利用上限のエラーを返す → backup に切り替えて同じセッションで再開し、作業を続けられる
  - エラーの本文（`Try again in 2 hours`）から解除の時刻を読む
  - 次のプロセス（新しいセッション）でも primary を避けて backup を使う
  - backup も上限 → 再開の指示を送らずに止まる
  - `fallback.enabled: false` にするとこのテストが失敗することも確認済み
- ユニット: `quota.test.ts`（エラーの判定・解除の時刻・記録と解除）、設定の検証、`.gitignore` の追加

## ドキュメント
README（`fallback` の設定と「利用上限での切り替え」の節、`/harness models`、pi 1.0 のフルスクリーン）、`docs/architecture.md`（「利用上限でのモデルの切り替え」の節）、`AGENTS.md`（Pi の落とし穴）を更新。

author: basnijholt
body:
## Summary

The opt-in heap probe (#2468) logs a type histogram of GC-tracked objects plus RSS. In a long-running primary, RSS can grow steadily while the tracked object count and the top types stay flat. The probe cannot yet tell the two remaining explanations apart:

- **Fragmentation:** freed memory that glibc keeps in its per-thread arenas.
- **Live allocations:** strings, bytes or native-library buffers that the GC does not track.

Each probe record now also carries:

- `malloc`: glibc `mallinfo2()` totals across all arenas, as `arena_bytes`, `arena_in_use_bytes`, `arena_free_bytes` and `mmap_bytes`. Live malloc bytes are `arena_in_use_bytes + mmap_bytes`. It is `null` on C libraries without `mallinfo2` (glibc before 2.33, musl, macOS).
- `python_allocated_blocks`: `sys.getallocatedblocks()`.

How to read it:
- RSS grows while live malloc bytes stay flat: this suggests freed memory that malloc retains.
- Live malloc bytes grow while the type histogram stays flat: this suggests untracked objects or native allocations.

## Notes

- `mallinfo2` is resolved once through `ctypes` and cached.
- The call walks the arenas under their locks. That costs far less than the existing `gc.get_objects()` walk, and it only runs when the probe is enabled.
- There are no new settings. The probe stays off unless `MINDROOM_HEAP_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` is set.

## Tests

- New tests check that the record has the new fields with sane values on glibc, and that `malloc` is `None` when `mallinfo2` is unavailable. Both fail before the change.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_heap_probe.py tests/test_orchestrator_runtime.py`: 139 passed, 4 skipped.
- The pre-commit hooks pass: ruff, ty, vulture, tach and module privacy.

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve the opt-in heap probe so memory growth can be diagnosed as live allocations or allocator-retained memory.

New Features:
- Extend heap probe events with glibc allocator totals and Python allocated-block counts to help distinguish live allocations from retained fragmented memory.

Enhancements:
- Document how to interpret allocator and RSS measurements across supported C libraries.

Documentation:
- Update heap probe configuration documentation and generated reference content with the new diagnostics and interpretation guidance.

Tests:
- Add coverage for allocator metrics on glibc and graceful absence of mallinfo2 on other C libraries.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Heap-probe events now include allocator memory totals and Python’s allocated-block count when available. These metrics provide additional visibility into memory use alongside resident memory and type-histogram data.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for interpreting these metrics: rising resident memory while allocation measures stay flat may indicate memory retained by the allocator; rising allocation measures may indicate live objects not shown in the type histogram.

author: amirmohamadazimi
body:
Before: only experiment 1 ($1,000, frozen code) ran on GitHub Actions. The v2 code with the $100 engine was merged but nothing ran it.

After: merging this starts experiment 2. A second scheduled workflow runs one paper-trading cycle every 3 hours from `main`, with its own database on the `paper-data-100` branch and its own REPORT.md there. Its runs are offset from experiment 1's. The report names the experiment and shows the commit it started on and the commit running now.

Experiment 2 runs from `main`, so improvements merged during the 30 days reach it. Every result stays tied to the code that produced it:
- Each run records its commit.
- Each change of code version is logged in `system_events`.
- Predictions already carry their model, calibrator and feature-set versions.

**How**
- `.github/workflows/paper-trading-100.yml` is a copy of experiment 1's workflow with these differences:
  - It uses the checked-out `main` code.
  - It saves state to `paper-data-100`.

body:
A monthly 31 January was placed on the last day of each short month. February became the 28th, and that clamped day consumed COUNT. A yearly 29 February did the same in a non-leap year.

A month with no such day is now skipped and does not consume COUNT. 31 January monthly is 31 January, 31 March, and 31 May. A 28th still lands in February. A yearly 29 February keeps leap years only. Completing a to-do still uses its own date arithmetic.

meson test covers the 31st, a 30th, a 28th, a yearly 29 February, and the 31st beside a one-off on 2 February in one calendar.

body:
Refs #263; follows #328 and #331.

## Summary

The real-process disabled-recovery test used a 60-second deadline. A killed reconcile pass can retain its source cursor claim for 60 seconds, after which settlement needs another tick. This caused an intermittent SQLite failure in post-merge CI.

Use the existing DBOS process harness budget (120 seconds by default) for this recovery role. Keep the assertions requiring a policy-cancelled Job, failed orphan rows and exactly one producer attempt. The wait for orphan bookkeeping also yields and checks the deadline on every poll. The existing enabled predecessor-recovery test also used a 60-second override and hit the same boundary in PR CI after the disabled-recovery tests passed. Remove that override so it uses the shared 120-second budget too. Its one-hour executor stale window still verifies prompt recovery without waiting for executor expiry. Production code is unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] Backend full gate not repeated locally: production code is unchanged and the prior Deep CI full tests passed on Python 3.11 and 3.13.
- [x] Frontend checks not needed: no frontend changes.
- [x] Manual testing not needed: real process harness correction.
- SQLite/PostgreSQL policy process suite: all 5 tests pass in 284.46 seconds, including restart, disabled crash recovery and already-running split workers. After the final polling adjustment, both SQLite/PostgreSQL crash-recovery cases pass again (195.32 seconds).
- Enabled predecessor recovery passes on SQLite and PostgreSQL: 2 tests in 126.14 seconds after removing the 60-second override.
- Ruff passes. The existing suite passed Pyright before this test-only edit.
- The original 60-second SQLite case passed alone in 53.69 seconds; that does not erase the post-merge CI failure.

## Coverage matrix

| # | Behaviour | Category | Precondition / input | Observable outcome | Tier | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | prevents disabled producer recovery | Edge | Kill a real DBOS producer after admission; disable in the database; restart; abandoned cursor claim may await expiry | Policy-cancelled Job, failed orphan rows and unchanged attempt count of one within the shared bounded recovery budget | E2E SQLite/PostgreSQL | ✅ `tests/e2e/test_derivative_policy_processes.py::TestDurablePolicy::test_disabled_crash_recovery_never_reexecutes_the_producer` |

| 2 | recovers enabled predecessor work before executor expiry | Edge | Killed API, enabled mesh policy, one-hour executor stale window | Metadata and thumbnail ready within the shared bounded recovery budget | E2E SQLite/PostgreSQL | ✅ `tests/e2e/test_job_engine.py::TestCrashRecovery::test_a_restarted_api_reruns_its_predecessors_work_at_once` |

### Tier check

- [x] E2E with the real application and engine on both supported databases.
- Other tiers and the feature headline behavior are unchanged.

### Self-check

- [x] Existing assertions remain intact; no skips or xfails.
- [x] Real fixtures and infrastructure, with no patched business seams.
- [x] Shared deadline matches the other DBOS process roles.

## Notes

No runtime, API, schema, dependency, version or release changes. The disabled-recovery failure is https://github.com/xiao-villamor/PrintStash/actions/runs/36928017179; the enabled predecessor-recovery failure is https://github.com/xiao-villamor/PrintStash/actions/runs/36931464226. After merging, validate CI and Deep CI on the resulting main SHA.

body:
The autofocus directive focused its input 150ms after starting the scroll, without checking again. Focusing another input in that window (e.g. typing the password right after the email) moved the focus back, which also made e2e logins flaky.

author: robertgorsuch
body:
Phase 2 of the backlog drawn from the NGRA 8.2.0 → 10.1.0 upgrade guide: one commit per item, each passing `scripts/mvn.sh verify` on its own.

> **Stacked on #13.** This PR targets `feat/phase-1-upgrade-routes`. Merge #13 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## How the findings surface
- `customizations scan --vendor <running version> --target <target> [--to <version>] [--merge-dir <dir>]` reports what becomes of each changed or added file, in text and in `--json` under `findings`.
- The upgrade plan applies the same rules to the registered customizations. It reads the webapp that will actually be deployed, including the patched WAR given with `--war`.

## Commits

### Groundwork (ADR-0003)
- `PackageIndex` reads a webapp, as a directory or a WAR, in one streaming pass, nested jars included. It records files, jar coordinates (from `pom.properties`, else the file name, never guessed) and which jar holds each class. Nothing is unpacked or loaded.
- `compat/matrix.yaml` moves to version 3, with `jarRules`, `relocations` and `constructs` as data. Each rule applies between a `from` and a `to` version range and cites its source.
- jrs-hotfix's line merge (`Diff`, `Diff3`, `Text`) is ported into `ops.merge`. No new dependency.

### #4: JAR retirement
Each site jar gets a verdict: `DROP`, `KEEP`, `REPLACE` (a named rule, such as the Progress `TI*.jar` drivers), `REVIEW` (the target ships an older version) or `UNRESOLVED` (no coordinates).

### #5: vendor classes and Jakarta
- Class files are read as data; no class is loaded.
- Every `com.jaspersoft.*` or `net.sf.jasperreports.*` type they use is reported as `PRESENT` (naming the jar), `MOVED` (same simple name in another package, naming it) or `MISSING` (naming the package it was last seen in).
- For a 10.0+ target, jars that refer to `javax.servlet`, `javax.ws.rs`, `javax.persistence` or `javax.annotation` are flagged for a Jakarta recompile.

### #6: relocations and three-way merges
- Relocation hints, such as `ehcache.xml` → `appCacheType` and `*-ehcache.xml`, appear in the scan, the plan and the reconcile step's `CONFLICT` lines.
- `--merge-dir` writes `.base`, `.mine`, `.theirs`, `.merged` and `.patch` for each changed file the target also ships.

### #8: semantic checks
- Spring XML, `web.xml` and CSRFGuard properties are parsed, not only hashed. XML is read with SAX, with no DTD or external entity fetched.
- Constructs the matrix's rules name are reported with their file and line: `annotatedClasses` on the vendor `sessionFactory`, `javax` servlet classes, a versioned Spring Security schema, custom `filter-chain` and `intercept-url` entries, CSRFGuard `UnprotectedMethods` and `TokenPerPage=false`.

### #10: Ad Hoc templates
- After a newdb hop from before 9.0, `check-adhoc-templates` names the vendor templates the old export overwrote and lists the site's own as left alone.
- `--restore-vendor-templates` runs `js-ant import-minimal-pro` once, with the server down. Only the flag triggers it, never `--yes`.

## Before relying on it
- The bundled rules cite NGRA guide sections as the issues quote them. Vendor guide page numbers, which #6's acceptance asks for, are still to be added.
- The ESAPI and CSRFGuard file paths in the rules, and the 10.0 cut-off on the CSRFGuard, Spring Security and filter-chain rules, need checking against real packages.
- `import-minimal-pro` imports the vendor's whole minimal catalog, not only the templates. The plan says so.

## Tests
- New: `PackageIndexTest`, `UpgradeRulesTest`, `Diff3Test` (ported), `JarRetirementTest`, `VendorClassCheckTest`, `CustomizationAssessTest`, `ConstructCheckTest`, `CustomizationFindingsPlanTest`, `AdhocTemplatesTest`.
- A `--json` scenario for `scan --target`.
- Idempotency tests for `restore-vendor-templates`.
- Full verify: 1615 tests, 0 failures, Spotless clean, coverage floor met.

author: iandballard
body:
Fix Roadmap batch 20: RecipeParser writes that can lose a link, a picture or an embedding.

Fixes F-128, F-131, F-132, F-174, F-175.

## Changes
- **F-128, category links.** A `recipe_categories` batch insert that got no answer (a dropped connection) gave up every link in it. It now falls through to the existing row-by-row retry. The insert also names its conflict target, `on_conflict=recipe_id,category_id`, as the recategorise worker does. Without it PostgREST arbitrates on the primary key, and each row carries a fresh id, so a link that had already landed was refused with a 409 and counted as lost.
- **F-132, embeddings.** `get_embeddings` backs off on a rate limit or a transient server error, like every other Gemini call. One loop, `_with_backoff`, now serves both; `_call_with_retry` keeps its signature and behaviour. `POST /embed` takes one retry, not the whole ladder, because a person is waiting on that search.
- **F-131, the detected measuring system.** A source host is evidence only of the system the prompt gives it: `.co.uk` is UK, `.com.au` is AU, `.co.nz` is UK. Before, `taste.com.au` offered as evidence for US was accepted. A host the prompt does not map, such as a `.com`, is evidence of nothing. A quote from the recipe text is unaffected. A port or a trailing dot on the host is read past.
- **F-174, shared pictures.** If a copy attempt stored the picture and crashed before the copy call, and the redo found the original gone or already received, the stored picture stayed in the bucket for ever. The worker now removes the picture under the copy's id whenever the answer is `duplicate` or `unavailable`. `copy_shared_item` answers a redo whose copy landed with `accepted`, so those two answers mean no recipe has that id.
- **F-175, share endpoints.**
  - `recipe_ids` and `skip_item_ids` are bounded at parse time, at 400. That is twice the limit, because the endpoint removes duplicates before it counts. The 200 limit and its sentence are unchanged.
  - A `22023` from `create_recipe_share` is now a 422 with a sentence, not a 503.

## Testing
- Each fix was written test-first. The full suite passes offline, with credentials blanked: 1,480 tests.
- An independent review returned "ship". It found the missing conflict target and the host port case; both are fixed in the last commit. It traced every path that returns `duplicate` or `unavailable` and confirmed the F-174 discard cannot remove a picture a live recipe points at.
- Not tested against a live PostgREST: the conflict-target behaviour rests on its documented default and on the recategorise worker's existing use of the same target.

## Not changed
The embed stage passes no rate limiter, so an embedding retry takes no limiter slot, as embedding calls never have.

- AI agent accounts: the `agent` upsert, both the UPDATE and the INSERT
- Google/Apple sign-in: `identity-create` and its random unusable password (`stack/src/sign_in.rs`)
- Not changed: server accounts (`sex 'S'`, `s1`). The char and map servers log in with plain text, and the fork leaves those accounts unhashed too.

**Format.** This matches the fork's `src/login/password.cpp` at the pinned commit 74026199:
- `$pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash>`, with 200000 iterations
- a 16-byte salt from the OS (`private_fs::random_bytes`: /dev/urandom or BCryptGenRandom)
- one 32-byte PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 block
- base64 in the standard `+/` alphabet, with no padding

`pass_flags` uses the same rule as `password::flags`:
- **1, weak:** not 8–23 printable ASCII bytes, all spaces, or the userid ignoring ASCII case
- **2:** exactly `ragnarok`

**Implementation.** No new crates. HMAC and PBKDF2 live in the new `stack/src/password.rs`, built on `archive.rs`'s SHA-256, which gains `digest()`. The hash stays hex-encoded in the SQL, the same way the plain text was.

**Tests** (`cargo test`, 239 passed):
- Known answers:
  - SHA-256 from the FIPS 180-4 examples
  - HMAC from RFC 4231 cases 1 and 6
  - PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from RFC 7914 §11 (c=1 and c=80000) and the published RFC 6070-style vectors (c=4096)
- A hash made by the fork's own `password.cpp`, through a harness that includes it, with a fixed salt. The supervisor must produce it byte for byte.
- A random-salt hash from the fork's `password::hash`, which must verify against a verifier written from the fork's spec.
- The other direction, checked by hand: a hash the supervisor wrote verified with the fork's real `password::verify`, and the fork's flags for that password agreed with ours.
- Every `user_pass`-writing statement is checked to contain neither the password nor its hex, and to contain the hash and the right `pass_flags`.

`node --check electron/main.js` passes, and `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` gives 454 passed, 0 failed.

**Docs.** `docs/DATABASE.md`'s `login` row now covers the hash, `pass_flags`, and what happens to a plain-text password set by hand. No doc line said "within a minute", so nothing else needed changing.

### TESTING ONLY: pairs with Flux159/rathena#19
That PR removes the login server's per-minute sweep. It keeps the one-time conversion at start-up, for worlds from 1.3.x, and the hash-on-save after a login. **This PR is safe without it.** The login server checks any stored `$pbkdf2-sha256$` value with `password::verify`, whatever the timer does, and the timer finds nothing to convert because the app no longer writes plain text. So the two can land in either order.

Not tested end to end: no game world was started.

author: hartra344
body:
Scrolling or laying out the Device section in Settings previously called `DeviceIdentity.loadOrCreate()`, causing synchronous Keychain access and potentially key generation on the main thread. Settings now reads an observable ID cached by AppModel when it loads the shared identity for saved Gateways or creates the first app-managed Gateway. An empty app shows a placeholder without creating a key.

The pairing identity and Gateway lifecycle are preserved. Tests use a package-scoped isolated memory Keychain and a bounded identity-read counter so they neither delete shared test state nor access real credentials. The security guide documents the cached display and placeholder.

Closes #611.

Validation:
- Committed baseline repro `1a47231` before the fix. Hosting the real macOS Device section failed because layout created an identity; the Gateway lifecycle control passed.
- Five targeted tests passed: actual macOS Settings hosting, first/later/replacement/restored Gateway identity cache, and existing Keychain isolation. The hosted test passed in 0.098s and the lifecycle test in 0.147s.
- Native iOS Simulator hosted test passed: one actual Swift Testing test, 0.344s. It lays out the same real Settings form before and after the first Gateway is added, asserts no identity read/creation during initial rendering, and no additional reads on refresh.
- All new offline checks passed. Offline run: 1,703 passes and the established 80 protected-file failures on this locked host.
- Demo Extras: 542 passed, zero failed, including the cached-identity lifecycle checks.
- iOS test build and macOS extraction build emitted localization data; `scripts/sync-strings.sh --skip-build` succeeded with both outputs. The placeholder is punctuation; no new catalog key was needed, and unrelated catalog churn was excluded.
- Independent product review found no blockers. Merged current main before opening the PR; CI must pass before merge.

Interaction cost: the Settings row reads one cached optional 64-character ID and displays a bounded 16-character prefix. Rendering performs no Keychain access, disk I/O or cryptographic work. Existing identity loading at app/Gateway initialization is unchanged.

Follow-ups: #59 for physical-device Settings scrolling and the visible placeholder/ID transition. This is a separately confirmed Settings hotspot; it is not claimed as the reproduced cause of the user's original physical-device freeze.



Integration: resolved the actual Registry conflict with #610 by retaining both the device identity and rejected-preference demo checks. The integrated branch passes 11 affected unit/UI tests and Demo Extras (552 checks, zero failures).

💡 **Vulnerability**: Unsanitized backend error messages (`err.message`) were being passed directly to the client in `server.js` and `backend/index.js` (specifically `manageShiftMarketplace`). Exposing detailed backend errors can reveal system architecture, stack traces, and database failure specifics, which aids attackers in reconnaissance and crafting exploits.
🎯 **Impact**: An attacker could intentionally trigger errors on these endpoints to glean information about the internal workings of the backend system or the database.
🔧 **Fix**: 
- Replaced `res.status(500).json({ error: err.message })` in `server.js` with a generic `"An unexpected error occurred"` message, securely logging the actual error to `console.error`.
- Replaced `error.message` passed as the third parameter in `throw new HttpsError('internal', ...)` within `backend/index.js` with a generic `"An unexpected error occurred"` message.
✅ **Verification**: Run `pnpm test` and `cd backend && npx jest`. Verify that errors thrown by these endpoints now log internally without exposing internal specifics to the caller.

author: pujitha24
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Download graph as PNG** button to the application graph's controls, under zoom in, zoom out and fit view. It exports the whole graph, not just the part in view, as a PNG at its natural size on a white background. The file is named `<application>-graph.png`.

## Reason for change

#33 asks for buttons next to the app graph that export the current diagram as an image or PDF, so it can be shared outside the dashboard. In the issue thread, willtsai pointed to React Flow's [download image example](https://reactflow.dev/examples/misc/download-image), and this PR follows it: `html-to-image`'s `toPng` on `.react-flow__viewport`, with a transform built from the node bounds. The bounds come from `getNodesBounds`, the current name of `getRectOfNodes` in reactflow 11.11.

Fixes #33

### Details

- **Where the button lives.** It is a `ControlButton` inside the existing React Flow `<Controls>` in `@radapp.io/rad-components`. That keeps the package free of Backstage and MUI, as described in the code organization docs.
- **Format.** It exports PNG only. PDF would need a second dependency, and an image covers the issue's "PDF or image".
- **New dependency.** `@radapp.io/rad-components` now depends on `html-to-image`, pinned to exactly `1.11.11` (MIT, no dependencies, released February 2023, no known advisories). I tested the latest versions in the browser: 1.11.12 and 1.11.13 leave React Flow's SVG edges out of the image, so the export shows only the nodes. 1.11.11 keeps them, and it is also the version React Flow's own example pins. `.github/dependabot.yml` is synced from `radius-project/.github`, so I didn't add an ignore rule there. Instead, a unit test checks the installed version and explains why, so a Dependabot bump to 1.11.12 or later fails CI with that reason. The only `yarn.lock` change is the new entry, and `yarn install --immutable` passes.
- **File name.** The real `getGraph` response (`ApplicationGraphResponse`) has only `resources` and no name. `ApplicationTab` now fills in the graph name from the application ID, so the file is named after the application.
- **Button states.** The button is disabled while an export is running and when the graph has no resources. If the export fails, the graph shows a `role="alert"` message, which clears on the next attempt.

## How to test

1. Run `kubectl proxy` and `yarn dev`, then open an application and go to its **App Graph** tab.
2. Click the download button, the fourth button in the controls at the bottom left. Its accessible name and tooltip are "Download graph as PNG".
3. A file named `<application>-graph.png` downloads. It shows every node and edge, even if you zoomed or panned first.

### Screenshots

Taken in headless Chromium at a 1440x1000 viewport against `yarn start`. The Radius API responses were route-mocked in the same way as `packages/app/e2e-tests/radiusGraph.test.ts`, using the repo's `multi-tier.json` graph fixture without a `name`, matching the real API.

| Before (`main`) | After: download control added to the graph controls |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/pujitha24/dashboard/blob/pr-assets/issue-33/before-graph.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/pujitha24/dashboard/blob/pr-assets/issue-33/after-graph.png?raw=true) |

Close-up of the control: ![control](https://github.com/pujitha24/dashboard/blob/pr-assets/issue-33/after-export-control.png?raw=true)

**The downloaded file:** [`todo-app-graph.png`](https://github.com/pujitha24/dashboard/blob/pr-assets/issue-33/exported-todo-app-graph.png?raw=true), 439x770. It has all four nodes and three edges.

![exported file](https://github.com/pujitha24/dashboard/blob/pr-assets/issue-33/exported-todo-app-graph.png?raw=true)

### Tests run

- `yarn install --immutable`: passes.
- `yarn tsc`: passes.
- `yarn lint:all`: passes.
- `yarn format:check`: passes.
- `yarn test:all`: 55 suites and 484 tests pass. The skipped suite and tests were already skipped on `main`. Coverage thresholds are met, including the `rad-components` ones.
- New `AppGraph` tests mock `html-to-image`. They cover the labelled control, the download and its file name, the failure alert and retry, the disabled state while exporting and for an empty graph, the image size and transform from the node bounds, the file name rules, and the version pin.
- I ran the new tests against the code without this change, and they fail there. That includes the `ApplicationTab` test that names the graph after the application.
- Browser check (Playwright): the download control works, the downloaded PNG contains every node and edge, and it is the same full-graph image after zooming in four times.

### Not verified

- I did not test against a live Radius cluster, and I only checked Chromium.
- I didn't add a Storybook or component e2e test for the export. The real rasterising was checked with Playwright against the dashboard, as described above.
- `docs/design/2026-09-radius-backstage-plugin.md`, which is a draft, proposes moving the graph renderer into a shared `graph-react` package later. This control is self-contained in `AppGraph.tsx`, so it should move along with the renderer.

## File change summary

| File | Summary of change |
| ---- | ----------------- |
| `packages/rad-components/src/components/appgraph/AppGraph.tsx` | Adds `exportGraphToPng` (whole-graph bounds plus padding, white background) and `graphImageFileName`. Adds the "Download graph as PNG" `ControlButton` with its in-progress and empty-graph guards, and a `role="alert"` panel shown when the export fails |
| `packages/rad-components/src/components/appgraph/__test__/AppGraph.test.tsx` | Tests for the control, download, failure and retry, guards, sizing, file name, and the version pin |
| `packages/rad-components/package.json`, `yarn.lock` | Adds `html-to-image` `1.11.11` |
| `plugins/plugin-radius/src/components/resources/ApplicationTab.tsx` | Names the graph after the application, since the `getGraph` response has no name |
| `plugins/plugin-radius/src/components/resources/ApplicationTab.test.tsx` | Tests the name fallback |

The first part of the Black Ring path (`docs/plan-phase7-lore.md`).

**The oath**
- Go into the Stone Kingdom's dark temple wearing the Black Ring and press Place on the altar's Nightstone heart. The King grants you **1,000 warriors**.
- If you try without the ring on, the altar tells you why it won't work.
- Once you've sworn, the King has new lines for you as his ally.

**The army** (`world/Army.js`)
- The army is tracked as a count, as decided earlier: at most **30 warriors are on the ground** at once.
- When one falls, the count drops by one and a fresh warrior marches in from behind, as long as any are left.
- Orders, from the new **⚔ banner** in the HUD (it shows the count and the current order; tap it for the four orders):
  - **Follow:** in ranks behind you.
  - **Hold here:** they stay where you gave the order.
  - **Attack:** they go after anything hostile near you.
  - **Form a line:** a wide line ahead of you.
- Whatever the order, they fight anything hostile that comes close. Raiders fight them back, the same way they now fight your barracks soldiers.
- **Rations:** each game day the army needs one food per hundred warriors (10 a day for the full thousand). It's taken from your bag first, then your storehouses. Each day without enough food, 3% desert. Days you missed are all counted.
- The army is saved with the world: whether you've sworn, how many are left, and the current order.

**The camp**
- **War Tent:** press Place on it to make camp. You'll wake there after dying, and the army holds position around it.
- **Campfire:** a ring of stones with burning logs and its own light.
- Both are made at the workbench.

author: samintisar
body:
## Summary

The first production iOS build failed before uploading:

```
Failed to patch capabilities: [ { capabilityType: 'APPLE_ID_AUTH', option: 'OFF' } ]
The bundle '37ZQ59G3Q3' cannot be deleted. Delete all the Apps related to this bundle to proceed.
```

EAS syncs the App ID's capabilities to the app's entitlements before every build. Sign in with Apple is now enabled on `com.solomindlm.app`, which is the primary App ID for the `com.solomindlm.web` Services ID and the sign-in key (#274/#276). The app didn't declare the entitlement, so EAS tried to switch the capability off, and Apple refused.

Declaring `com.apple.developer.applesignin: ["Default"]` in `ios.entitlements` keeps the capability on. I didn't use `ios.usesAppleSignIn`: without the `expo-apple-authentication` package installed it only emits a warning and adds no entitlement. That package is also a native module the app doesn't need, since sign-in runs through the browser OAuth flow.

## Test plan
- [x] The introspected production config now includes `com.apple.developer.applesignin: ["Default"]` next to the existing associated-domains and push entitlements
- [x] Biome passes on `app.json`
- [ ] `eas build --platform ios --profile production` gets past capability sync

author: mrmidi
body:
## Audio Analyzer (preview)

A new **Audio Analyzer** screen in the app that reads the driver's own output ring, with no copies, and runs its DSP on the GPU. It's a preview: it works, but isn't optimised yet.

### What it shows
- **Monitor:** L/R/M/S levels with peak markers, true peak, correlation, balance, stereo width and side energy.
- **Stereo:** goniometer, plus 60-second correlation and side-energy history.
- **Spectrum:** FFT 512–4096 with a choice of window, L/R power or M/S, fast or slow averaging, and peak hold.
- **Loudness:** EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770 at 48 kHz: momentary, short-term, integrated, LRA, max true peak, PLR, crest factor, history, and a Pause/Reset session.
- **Diagnostics:** waveform, ring-buffer state and per-pass GPU timings.

### How it works
- **Data:** the driver maps the shared output ring into the app (`IOConnectMapMemory64` type 2). The app wraps it as a Metal buffer with `bytesNoCopy`, so the GPU reads the samples the driver writes.
- **No locking against the driver:** each pass reads a small control state (write position, oldest valid frame, epochs), encodes a frame range, and reads the state again when the GPU finishes. If the writer overtook the range or an epoch changed, the result is discarded. The driver never blocks for the observer.
- **DSP on the GPU:** stateful K-weighting (only committed once its range proves valid), true peak, and a radix-2 FFT. Analysis runs every 40 ms in batches of up to 12 × 10 ms loudness chunks.
- **Drawing:** every plot and every number goes through the panels' shared Metal canvases, one command buffer per visual frame. Numeric readouts are drawn from a Core Text glyph atlas at 10 Hz (2 Hz for diagnostics). SwiftUI only lays out a hidden template, so a changing value never re-lays out a panel.

### Driver-side change
Two new user-client methods, so the app can choose a device and read the observer state:
- `kMethodSelectAudioObserver = 66`;
- `kMethodGetAudioObserverState = 67`.

**They moved from 65/66 during the rebase:** #165 had already taken 65 for the FCP exchange log behind the AV/C Report. The app uses the new numbers.

### Known limits (preview)
- About 20% of one CPU core while the screen is open, measured on a clean Release build before the final round of changes. The 40 ms acquisition and the Metal readouts have not been measured without Xcode's Metal capture layer yet.
- It may keep running while its window is hidden. Close the screen when you're not using it.
- Loudness is 48 kHz only. Other rates show "Unsupported".

### Tests
- Host C++ suite: 2704/2704.
- Swift: 448 passed, covering:
  - the GPU kernels;
  - publication isolation and render-submission batching;
  - the display smoother;
  - the glyph atlas: coverage of every character readouts use, tabular digits, alignment, refresh cadence.
- DriverKit and app build succeed.
- Hardware: run on an Apogee Duet at 48 kHz during development. Screens checked by the maintainer; nothing automated covers the visuals.

### Tools
- `tools/profile_analyzer.py`: headless Time Profiler capture and summary.
- `tools/perf-swiftui/swiftui_updates.py`: summarises SwiftUI-instrument update exports.
- Measurements so far are in `documentation/ANALYZER_PERFORMANCE.md`.

<!--

Fixes premature AI-ready completion and post-restart destination timeouts when successful native connection, recovery and model verification take longer than the previous combined deadlines.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.

Users get separate bounded completion phases and localized timeout guidance while exact model, route, device, session and listener ownership remain mandatory. An unused destination handle still expires after five minutes. First exclusive acquisition grants one non-renewable execution window shared by explicit retries and process restarts.

**Installed-package blocker remains:** MSIX 2026.9.700.0 at packaging commit `133deeb1a5efac2bcbc6564c90c038a999e6e842` returns exit 1 for `Starting` after 90 seconds and omits structured Gateway state from that response. Pending status does not attest launch identity. This PR still rejects that ambiguous failure. Conditional polling fixtures do not establish support for that installed contract. Draft pending upstream packaging and current-head native/UI proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The chooser separates a 30-second page drain from six-minute verification. Authorization can start/roll back its owned runtime; provider writes and finalization are excluded from that deadline. Successful finalization remains one-shot.

`SetupNativeCompletionTiming` centralizes two 210-second authenticated connection/authorization phases, a 210-second join of already-admitted Local AI recovery, 150 seconds for exact-model verification including its existing 120-second RPC, and 30 seconds for navigation. Total execution ceiling: 810 seconds. Underlying owner failures or shorter caller deadlines still win.

`SetupDashboardHandoffStore` retains five-minute unused admission and atomically persists execution start and absolute expiry under its exclusive file lock. Retries cannot refresh either value. Malformed, expired, interrupted in-flight and legacy retry records without execution provenance fail closed. The launcher consumes only after fresh authority checks and successful presentation. Gateway credential lifetimes are unchanged.

`IsolatedGatewayRuntime` polls only after a successfully acknowledged own start. The 180-second start/readiness budget permits a bounded ten-second confirmation allowance after late acknowledgement, at most 190 seconds for start/status and always subordinate to the caller deadline. A pending-status/listener transition gets one fresh status recheck, not another Start. Only fresh Running plus unchanged complete port/process attribution can succeed. Terminal states, unattributed listeners and identity drift fail closed.

Native credential reauthorization now has 210 seconds; non-native five-second behavior is unchanged. Typed phase diagnostics preserve safe startup messages, localize specific completion timeouts and log only exception type/finite phase. The coordinator's aggregate deadline uses neutral readiness guidance rather than incorrectly blaming inference.

Docs pin the needed upstream pending-start/launch-identity/guarded-stop contract. Gateway 9.4 success versus 9.7 failure is correlation, not a controlled regression measurement. Local AI ownership recovery remains separate.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Receipt tests cover concurrent first acquisition, unchanged deadlines across restart/retries, malformed/legacy records, expiry, backward clocks and late callbacks. Runtime tests cover 68 successive two-second polls, cancellation during awaited start/status, late acknowledgement, a safe listener-transition recheck and rejected attribution drift.

Actual runtime/authorizer composition succeeds with 197 seconds of preflight/start/confirmation/inspection, while slower preflight correctly hits the outer 210-second deadline and rolls back. Native reconnect tests allow 187 seconds and reject deadline expiry, cancellation and record drift. Real local fixture Gateway/manager tests exercise verifier phase cancellation and subsequent successful exact-model verification. Six-locale presentation contracts reject arbitrary exception-message rendering. None of these fixtures starts the installed Gateway.

It runs on GitHub Pages with no server: `index.json` and each run's `view.json` are pre-generated by the plugin's own `serve.py`, and the viewer's one absolute URL is made relative.

## Size

`maproom/` is 771 MB and the published site is 773 MB of the 1 GB Pages limit. The largest file is a 32 MB video.

## Verification

- `python test/run.py`: 689 passed, 0 failed.
- Every `view.json` matches the plugin's `serve.py` output byte for byte. `index.json` differs only in the trimmed file lists, the null trace field, and two run folders that have no `run.db`.
- All 3,489 data references in `index.json`, the `view.json` files and each `run.db` resolve to a file with the exact same case, which matters on the Linux Pages host.

author: thomasgorisse
body:
## Problem

`build-apks.yml` attaches two debug APKs to every GitHub Release: `sceneview-android-demo.apk` (`io.github.sceneview.demo`, built with `-PdemoPlainDebug=true`) and `sceneview-android-tv-demo.apk` (`io.github.sceneview.sample.tv`). Until now the runner signed them with its own throwaway debug key, a new one on every run. That causes two problems:

- A release APK cannot install over the previous one (`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`), because each release has a different signer.
- Android developer verification, enforced since 2026-09-30 in some countries and everywhere in 2027, blocks sideloading a package unless its signing key is registered in the Play Console. A different key on every run can never be registered.

## Fix

One dedicated key (RSA 4096, alias `github-apk`, `CN=SceneView, O=SceneView`) now signs both GitHub APKs. It is registered in the Play Console Android developer verification for both package names: `io.github.sceneview.demo` and `io.github.sceneview.sample.tv` are both **Registered** (2026-10-02).

- **`build-apks.yml`**: a new step decodes `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEYSTORE_BASE64` into `$RUNNER_TEMP` and exports `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEYSTORE_FILE`. The build step passes `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEY_ALIAS` and `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEY_PASSWORD`. A tag ref with no secret fails the job, the same rule as #1909. A plain manual dispatch only warns and falls back to the debug key.
- **`samples/android-demo/build.gradle`, `samples/android-tv-demo/build.gradle`**: a `githubApk` signing config, written in the same env-var style as the existing `signingConfigs.release`. The debug build type uses it **only** when `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEYSTORE_FILE` is set. `ci.yml`, PR and local builds are unchanged and keep the debug key.
- **`docs/docs/try.md`**: the download card said "Debug-signed". It now says the APK is signed with the SceneView key, and to uninstall the Play Store version first (different signer).
- **`tools/try-demo.sh`**: `--download` asked for `sceneview-demo.apk`, but the release asset is `sceneview-android-demo.apk`, so it 404'd before installing. Fixed. When `adb install` fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`, it now prints the exact `adb uninstall io.github.sceneview.demo` command (with `-s` when `ANDROID_SERIAL` is set) and exits non-zero. It never uninstalls by itself, since that deletes the app data.
- **Changelog fragment** `changelog.d/4255-github-apk-stable-key.md`. It tells sideload users to uninstall an APK from an earlier release once, since the signer changes one last time, and says the GitHub APKs are debug builds for trying the samples. The build type is unchanged.

Signer certificate SHA-256: `2B:03:B7:0A:33:94:24:27:7C:5E:B5:9C:E4:BB:4A:51:FC:E5:7B:A6:7A:A4:59:A8:24:B9:19:C4:2B:B7:2C:49`

## Testing done

- `./gradlew --configure-on-demand :samples:android-demo:assembleDebug :samples:android-tv-demo:assembleDebug -PdemoPlainDebug=true` with the four variables set: BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- `apksigner verify --print-certs` on both APKs: `Verifies`, v2 scheme. Signer `CN=SceneView, O=SceneView` with the SHA-256 above. Package names are `io.github.sceneview.demo` and `io.github.sceneview.sample.tv` (checked with `aapt2 dump badging`).
- Same build of the TV demo without `SCENEVIEW_GITHUB_KEYSTORE_FILE`: signed by `C=US, O=Android, CN=Android Debug`, so the default path is unchanged.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/build-apks.yml`: clean. `check-changelog-fragments.sh`: well-formed.
- After the build, the keystore password does not appear in plain text anywhere under `build/` or `.gradle/`.
- **Real signing path on CI**: `build-apks.yml` dispatched on this branch, [run 36934162943](https://github.com/sceneview/sceneview/actions/runs/36934162943): success. The decode step used the repository secrets, and "Attach to GitHub Release" was skipped (branch ref, not `refs/tags/v*`), so no release changed. `apksigner verify --print-certs` on the `sample-apks` artifact: both APKs `Verifies` (v2), signer `CN=SceneView, O=SceneView`, SHA-256 `2B:03:…:2C:49` as above. Packages `io.github.sceneview.demo` and `io.github.sceneview.sample.tv`.
- `tools/try-demo.sh --download` with stubbed `adb`/`curl`: an `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` install prints the uninstall command and exits 1, with and without the `android-cli.sh` helper; a successful install still launches and exits 0. `shellcheck` clean.

author: fastner
body: ## Summary Concurrent `archive.extract` applies to one destination could remove each other's `in-progress` containment entry (race 1 in the containment design notes). If the apply whose entry was removed was then killed, links its merge had published were never verified, and `check` could report convergence. Applies to one destination are now serialized by a per-destination lock. The design follows the planning comment on #224. ## Changes - **Per-destination lock.** `archive-extract-lock-` in `/var/lib/paratix/flags`, keyed by the same destination normalization as the containment entries. It is held from just before the containment entry is created through the final clear. Upload and preflight stay outside the lock, and `check` takes no lock (its exec count is unchanged). - **Contention.** A second apply waits up to 300 s, then fails. The message names the lock path, the holder's owner lines (controller host, PID, start time, entry name), the marker age, when the lock becomes reclaimable, and when removing it by hand is safe. - **Heartbeat and guards.** The holder refreshes its marker about every 60 s through a token- and age-checked refresh guard. Guards inside the merge exec and the clear script refuse once the lock is lost; the reserved exit code 75 is mapped to "merge not started". In that case no merge runs, no entry is removed, and the apply fails visibly with its failure recorded. - **Thresholds.** A lock is reclaimed once its marker is older than 540 s. The holder's guard refuses once the marker is older than 300 s. Both come from the same `find -mmin` primitive. A test enforces that the guard bound plus the 110 s host-side merge limit stays below the reclaim age, so an orphaned merge has finished before anyone can reclaim. - **Shared mutex wait fix.** `withMutexLock` previously waited in a single exec of up to 300 s under the 120 s exec timeout and threw. It now polls in rounds of at most 60 s under one deadline, tries a stale reclaim right away and after every round, retries a lost re-acquire within the same deadline, and returns a structured failure. This also affects the cron, hosts, fstab, sshd and release-upgrade mutexes and `applyWithFlagLock`. Their defaults (300 s wait, 4 h stale bound) and messages are unchanged. - **Holder marker.** Line 1 stays the compared token. Only the archive lock supplies a random token and adds owner lines; every other lock keeps `$$@host epoch`. - **Docs.** `packages/paratix/llm-guide.md` and `docs/module.md` describe serialization, the wait, stale recovery, manual release, and the remaining limits instead of "not supported". The race list in `archiveContainmentFlag.ts` and the recovery hint are updated. The lock primitives moved into `flagLockScripts.ts`, `flagLockRefresh.ts`, `flagLockWait.ts`, `mutexLock.ts` and `archiveExtractLock.ts` to stay within the lint file-size limit. `withMutexLock` is still exported from `moduleHelpers.ts`. ## Remaining limits - Nested destinations (e.g. `/srv/a` and `/srv/a/b`) use different locks. - Old and new paratix versions running concurrently on one destination do not coordinate. - A target clock jump, or a merge stuck in uninterruptible I/O beyond its timeout, can make a live holder look stale. ## Validation - `pnpm agent:check`: passed (lint, format, typecheck, build, unit, dist, scripts). - `pnpm --filter paratix test:integration` against Docker 29.5.2: 27/27 passed, including three new cases: - a held fresh lock produces the contention message - a backdated lock is reclaimed, the whole destination is verified, and `check` converges - a lock released mid-wait lets the apply proceed - `moduleHelpers.test.ts`, `archive.test.ts` and `flagLock.shell.smoke.test.ts`: run 3× back to back, stable. - The smoke case "merges as before when the merge guard passes" needs GNU `cp` and is skipped on macOS. It runs on Linux CI, and the guarded merge is exercised in the Docker suite. Closes #224 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: parrydeanward-creator
body:
## The problem
ONE Brain hasn't been getting your ONE GO and ONE MOVE numbers. Every request to MASTER for them was refused today, 10 out of 10.

I checked inside MASTER:
- **The data side is fine:** run without the secret check, it returns your real numbers.
- **The refusal is the secret check:** the secret this site holds doesn't produce the fingerprint MASTER has on file. That fingerprint came from you on 30 Sep, and the secret in Vercel hasn't changed since.
- **The likely cause:** a hidden space or line break, either in the pasted secret or in how the fingerprint was made.
- **The other three products** received the same fingerprint today, so they would refuse it too.

## The fix
- **A fingerprint page for you only:** `/api/fingerprint`.
  - When you're signed in, it shows the SHA-256 fingerprint of the secret this site actually holds.
  - Anyone else gets "Not available".
  - It never shows the secret. A fingerprint isn't a secret.
- **The secret is trimmed before use**, so a stray space or line break can't cause this again.

127 tests pass, including one that checks the page is yours only and never returns the secret.

## What you do after merging (two minutes)
1. Wait about two minutes for the deploy.
2. While signed in, open https://vip50one-site.vercel.app/api/fingerprint.
3. Copy the long `fingerprint` value and paste it to me.

I then write it into all four databases (MASTER, Marquee, ONE Open and Showly) and check your dashboard shows real numbers again.

body:
Мелкие правки в правилах сборки программы в `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (`ai_trainer.py`). Каждый пункт — отдельный коммит. Текст только дописан, ничего не переставлено: префикс кэша выше места правки не меняется. Ветка остаётся открытой под следующие пункты.

## Что изменилось

1. **Ограничение из профиля — вслух** (пункт 7). В живом прогоне «правое колено» из памяти молча попадало в программы, о которых человек просил без всякой связи с коленом. Англоязычному атлету пришло «easier on cranky knees», хотя про колени он не писал. Теперь тренер одной строкой говорит, что учёл, что это из прежних слов человека, и предлагает стереть: «Учёл колено, про которое ты говорил раньше, — скажи, если уже не беспокоит, сотру.» Эта строка пишется на языке ответа.
2. **Ответ на программу короче** (пункт 8). Раньше ответ занимал 400–700 слов. Теперь у него рамка из четырёх частей: логика сплита, прогрессия, стартовые веса, одно предложение про еду (только если цель — масса или сушка). В конце — один вопрос. Ориентир по длине — 150–200 слов, без таблиц и заголовков. Объём и состав дней тренер не пересказывает, формулировка: «состав и подходы видны в превью программы». Она верна и без параллельного PR с превью.
3. **Подтягивания у новичка** (пункт 9). Если подтягиваний в истории нет или лучший подход меньше 5 повторов, тренер ставит «Тяга верхнего блока» (она есть в `seed_data.EXERCISE_TEMPLATES`) или гравитрон, если он есть в каталоге. Подтягивания он называет целью на будущее. Дома без блока — негативные или австралийские подтягивания, если они есть в каталоге, иначе подтягивания с меньшим числом повторов. Сейчас гравитрона, негативных и австралийских подтягиваний в каталоге нет, поэтому правило условное.

## Контракт API

Не меняется: правятся только инструкции модели, без новых маршрутов, полей и таблиц.

## Проверки

- В `tests/test_ai_trainer.py` добавлены три теста на наличие правил в промпте. Тест на пункт 9 также проверяет, что «Тяга верхнего блока» есть в каталоге.
- `python -m pytest -q`: 4595 passed, 1 skipped.
- `ruff check .`: чисто.

Строки с объёмом (~497, ~661) и `_clean_progression` не тронуты, их правят параллельно.
