body:
Third of four PRs for the app rebuild. Stacked on #40.

## What changed

**Mobile**
- `app/(auth)/welcome.tsx`: three first-launch pages (Figma Onboarding 1–3). Shown once per device; every page has a way out, and the last offers today's devotional with no account.
- `app/(auth)/sign-up/[step].tsx`: eight questions, one per screen, driven by one step table: name, gender, contact, date of birth, region, province, zone, parish. Answers live in `SignUpProvider` above the stack, so Back keeps them.
- `app/(auth)/verify.tsx`: six code cells over a single hidden input (so the OS can autofill), wrong-code state, resend after 45 seconds. Used by sign-up and by log in.
- `app/(auth)/all-set.tsx`: the finish screen with the church that was joined.
- `app/(auth)/log-in.tsx`: email or phone, with a password or a code.
- Kit additions in `src/ui/`: `TextField`, `OtpCells`, `SearchField`, `Crumbs`, `QuestionScreen`.
- `app/register.tsx` and `app/sign-in.tsx` are deleted; every link to them now points at the new routes.

**Backend** (one small commit)
- Password login accepts an email or phone as well as a username.
- Code login finds a phone stored as `0803…` when the app sends `+234803…`.

## Where this differs from Figma, and why

| Figma | Built | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Step 3 asks for a phone number and sends the code there | Step 3 asks for email and phone; the code is sent when step 8 is submitted | The code goes to both, as decided. Sending at step 3 would let it expire (10 minutes) during the church steps. **The Figma frame needs an email field added.** |
| "Remember me" checkbox | Left out | A phone session always persists, so the box would offer a choice that does not exist. |
| "Forgot password?" | "No password? Get a code" | Accounts made in the app have no password to forget. |
| Google button | Drawn; says "coming soon" | No Google sign-in on the backend yet. |
| Region rows show a state ("Lagos") | Name only | The hierarchy has no such field. |
| Province and zone titles | "Which province?", "Which zone?" | I did not pull those two frames; the copy and badge colours are my guess and should be checked against Figma. |
| Welcome pages swipe | Buttons only | Kept simple; swipe can be added. |

## Checked

Driven in headless Chrome at 360×800 against a throwaway backend (SQLite, in-memory email, a seeded hierarchy), not your Neon database:

- Welcome → all eight steps → code screen: screens compared with the Figma frames.
- A wrong code is rejected, the cells clear, the message shows.
- The right code creates the account and lands on the finish screen with the parish and its zone, province and region.
- In a fresh browser, log in with a code sent to the phone typed as `0803 555 0142` signs in as the new account.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.

## Not checked

- **Nothing on a phone or emulator.** Keyboard avoidance, OTP autofill and the safe-area insets only exist there.
- Dark mode on these screens.
- Password log in (only code log in was exercised end to end).
- The new backend tests were not run:

```
cd backend && venv/Scripts/python.exe manage.py test users.test_signup users.test_otp hierarchy.tests.test_public
```

## To try it on a phone

The church steps need hierarchy nodes in whatever database the backend uses, and production needs `OTP_PROVIDER=users.otp_providers.EmailAndSmsOTPProvider` (see #40). In DEBUG the code is logged by the console provider at debug level.

author: steinybot
body: Fixes #11739 ## Problem On macOS, a `TextField`, `SecureField` or `Text` that fills a stack overhangs it by 2pt on each side, so its layer border and background draw outside the column. AppKit gives a label-shaped text field 2pt alignment rect insets, and Auto Layout pins the alignment rect, not the frame. `Text` always has the insets; the fields get them once `textfieldSetBackgroundColor` turns off the cell background. ## Solution Make the three widget classes report zero alignment rect insets, so each one fills the width it is pinned to, and keep `Text`'s text where a stock label draws it. ## Screenshot Each case sits in a 300pt column above a green box that fills the column. Before the fix, the widget's border sticks out 2pt past the box on each side. **`TextField`, borderless, with `textfieldSetBackgroundColor`** **`SecureField`, borderless, with `textfieldSetBackgroundColor`** **`Text` with a background and a border** ## Changes 1. **Zero alignment insets on `PerryTextField`** — [`alignment_rect_insets`](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-5463f02e937171460bfc530787fd52c5f78a4d18f36dfe4d341c53d6d6aa2babR212-R218). A bezeled field already has none, so only a borderless field with a background changes. https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/blob/7b6d4d233a40c58bbbeb790b6f01eb29091c2453/crates/perry-ui-macos/src/widgets/textfield.rs#L212-L218 [View in diff →](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-5463f02e937171460bfc530787fd52c5f78a4d18f36dfe4d341c53d6d6aa2babR212-R218) 2. **The same override on `PerrySecureTextField`** — [`alignment_rect_insets`](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-fdde4446e7fa6d18a6e691b47e1c21f1048334b4fc21f2cd128e905f026a3db2R96-R102). https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/blob/7b6d4d233a40c58bbbeb790b6f01eb29091c2453/crates/perry-ui-macos/src/widgets/securefield.rs#L96-L102 [View in diff →](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-fdde4446e7fa6d18a6e691b47e1c21f1048334b4fc21f2cd128e905f026a3db2R96-R102) 3. **Zero alignment insets on `PerryLabel`** — [`alignment_rect_insets`](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-4831eb3c55dbfee958f5366e43483ad37f8750cd302f6da58fa578dfe40fc6a9R137-R142). This is the `Text` and `AttributedText` class. https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/blob/7b6d4d233a40c58bbbeb790b6f01eb29091c2453/crates/perry-ui-macos/src/widgets/text.rs#L137-L142 [View in diff →](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-4831eb3c55dbfee958f5366e43483ad37f8750cd302f6da58fa578dfe40fc6a9R137-R142) 4. **The label cell draws over AppKit's 2pt text padding** — [`cancel_line_padding`](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-e27b2e64be316b3c611ed36b19feca69da49c6efb31b6425cf0e9f1d8a77df31R114-R122). A stock label's insets exist to hide this padding, so zero insets alone would move every `Text`'s text 2pt right and widen it by 4pt. The cell takes the padding off its insets, which covers drawing, editing, selection and `cellSizeForBounds:`. https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/blob/7b6d4d233a40c58bbbeb790b6f01eb29091c2453/crates/perry-ui-macos/src/widgets/padding.rs#L31-L38 [View in diff →](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-e27b2e64be316b3c611ed36b19feca69da49c6efb31b6425cf0e9f1d8a77df31R31-R38) - `text::label` turns it on for every `PerryLabel` ([diff](https://github.com/PerryTS/perry/pull/11740/files#diff-4831eb3c55dbfee958f5366e43483ad37f8750cd302f6da58fa578dfe40fc6a9R156-R158)). - A `Text`'s text now sits at its frame's left edge, as a web `` does. ## Verification - Local macOS, `perry-dev` build of this branch, Geisterhand `/widgets?tree=true`: the repro from #11739 reports both fields at x 0, width 300 (was x -2, width 304 for the field with a background). - Same setup, a `Text` with a background and border in a 300pt column: frame x 0, width 300 (was x -2, width 304). In a screenshot, a plain `Text`'s "H" ink starts 1.5pt from the column edge before and after the change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01R98ryabw6WeZReF6BMQEzV

author: talic
body:
## What changed

While a print runs, PrintGlance now estimates whether an AMS spool will run out before the print ends, and where.

- **Card:** an orange notch on the progress bar at the expected runout, the track past it shaded, and a line such as *PLA Matte in A2 runs out around 15:45.* If another AMS slot holds the same filament and color, it adds *AMS may switch to A3.* While paused it gives a percent instead of a time.
- **Notification:** *Filament may run out*, once per print and slot, under the existing **Low Filament** setting.
- **Version:** 1.3.0 (build 21).

## How the estimate works

`RunoutTracker` (in `FilamentAlert.swift`) fits a straight line through each spool's AMS percent against print progress (`mc_percent`), one reading per whole percent. Progress, not the clock, so pauses and speed changes don't skew it, and the marker lands in the bar's own units. The clock time comes from the printer's time left.

It guesses only when:
- the slope is clearly downward (two standard errors below flat), and
- the guess reaches no more than 3 times the progress the readings cover.

Readings below 5% stay out of the fit. The last guess made above that stands, and it goes once the print passes it still running. A rise of 10 points or a new filament name or color starts that spool over. The sums persist per job in `UserDefaults`, so a relaunch or Mac sleep keeps the history.

## Tested on a real print

A first version counted 1% drops. During a live X2D print with a spool at 3–5%, the AMS reading swung 3–5 for 15% of progress, then read 0–2 for the last 20% of the print. **The print finished without running out.** That version took two dips as a rate 20 times too fast and said *about to run out* at 80%.

That log is now `testNearlyEmptyNoisySpoolGuessesNothing`. On clean data the fit lands within half a percent of the truth; with ±2 points of noise, within about 2.5%.

## Limits

- Needs a Bambu RFID spool with **Update Remaining Capacity** on.
- A spool that starts the print nearly empty gets only the existing 20% warning.
- It treats 0% as empty, though the X2D printed on at 0 (marked `ponytail:`).
- It can't warn before the print starts.

## Needs the user

- Weigh the A2 spool (pink PLA Pure) that read 0–1% at the end, to learn how much filament "0%" really is. That could set an offset per AMS model.

## Checks

- `make test`: 140 tests, 0 failures (10 new in `RunoutTrackerTests`).
- Renders of the card (printing, printing with backup, paused) viewed in light and dark.
- Installed and ran against the live X2D.

author: trueadm
body: ## Summary - Fix a load-sensitive race in `packages/octane/tests/hydration/independent-parent.test.ts` ("preserves an independently owned input through parent hydration and updates (%j)"). - After the island activates, the test now waits for the runtime's passive queue to drain (`hasPendingWork()` false) before it asserts the exact replay count. ## Why - `activated` flips as soon as the island activator returns. The click captured before activation replays later, from the island's `notify` passive effect (`createIndependentHydrateActivator` in `runtime.ts`), which drains through `schedulePostPaint` (requestAnimationFrame plus a post-paint task). - `expect.poll` checks every 50 ms. If activation lands less than a frame before a poll tick, or a loaded event loop delivers the frame late, the synchronous `expect(record).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` runs before the replay. Observed under load averages of 60–90 as `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` at line 128. - The runtime's post-paint scheduling is correct. Only the test's wait was wrong. ## Changes - Import `hasPendingWork` and add `await expect.poll(() => hasPendingWork()).toBe(false)` between the activation poll and the count assertion. - The assertion is unchanged: the click must replay exactly once, or zero times when the button is replaced (stale). Before this change the stale case could pass before the replay ever had a chance to run. Now it shows that no replay arrives after the flush. - Test-only change, so no changeset. ## Validation - [x] **Reproduced the race first.** A temporary copy of the old test that delays `requestAnimationFrame` by 120 ms failed all 24 non-stale cases across `octane` and `octane-prod`, with the same error at the same assertion. author: dumijdev
body:
The quality gate of BuildCLI/BuildCLI#685 fails on **Reliability D** (needs A) and **Security C** (needs A). The 411 maintainability findings (cognitive complexity, duplicated literals...) do not fail the gate and are not touched here. Findings were read from SonarCloud's public API (33 bugs/vulnerabilities, 0 hotspots).

## Reliability (D came from the CRITICAL one)
- `RunCommand` S2119: one `SecureRandom` instead of a new one per call.
- S2142 (x7): waiting for an answer / the writer and inbox loops swallowed the interrupt. `Approvals` now catches `InterruptedException` apart and re-interrupts; the loops re-interrupt before returning. New `InterruptedApprovalTest`.
- S3078 (x6): `Task.attempts`/`tokens` were `volatile int` with `++`/`+=`; now `AtomicInteger` behind `attempts()`, `nextAttempt()`, `tokens()`, `addTokens()`. Call sites updated.
- S1751: `Approvals.first()` looped just to return the first element.
- S5850 (x3) / S5855: regex alternations grouped; redundant `|passwd` removed from the secret-name regex (`passw(?:or)?d` already matches it).
- S2184 (x7): `256 * 1024` etc. as `long`.
- S6218: `Previews.Image` compares its pixels.
- S6906: process pipe drained on a platform thread.
- `javabugs:S2259` in `ConnectView.chooseModel`: guard against a null provider.

## Security (C)
- `StateSchema` S2077 (x2): H2 version row uses a `PreparedStatement`; the SQLite `PRAGMA user_version` (cannot take parameters) uses a fixed statement per known version, picked by index.
- `TerminalText` S6389: bidirectional characters written as `\uXXXX` escapes instead of the characters themselves.
- `DoctorCommand` S4036 (MINOR): `git --version` is meant to run the `git` first on PATH. **Marked with `// NOSONAR` and a comment, not fixed** - decide whether you accept that; the alternative is to mark it "Accepted" in SonarCloud.

## Verified
`mvn verify` green. **Not verified:** SonarCloud itself (I cannot run its analysis): the gate result is known only after #685 is re-analysed. Behaviour changes worth a look in review: interrupted approvals now keep the interrupt flag; the drain thread is a daemon platform thread.

author: internetcalifornia
body:
## Summary

Workbooks the model creates (`chat_write_file` / `sandbox_render_document` → `.xlsx`) can now contain real Excel formulas, including references to other sheets.

- **Syntax:** any cell starting with `=` becomes a formula in CSV, JSON or Markdown-table input: `=B2*C2`, `=SUM(B2:B9)`, `=IF(C2>100,"High","Low")`, `=Detail!D4`, `='Q3 Sales'!B4`. JSON also accepts `{"formula": "..."}`. A leading `'=` keeps the cell as literal text, as in Excel.
- **Recalculation:** the workbook sets `fullCalcOnLoad`, so Excel, Excel Online and LibreOffice compute results when the file is opened.
- **Safety:** formulas that reach outside the workbook stay as plain text. That covers DDE (`|`), links to other workbooks (`[...]`), and `WEBSERVICE`, `CALL`, `REGISTER` and similar functions. Cell content may be copied from untrusted sources such as emails, so a formula must not be able to run anything when the file opens. A side effect is that structured table references like `Table1[Col]` also stay as text.
- **Markdown:** table cells holding a formula are read as written, so the `*` in `=A2*B2*C2` isn't treated as emphasis (raw cell text was added to the table block).
- **Read side:** results don't exist until a spreadsheet app opens the file. Until then, the sheet preview in chat and the `document-text` extractor show the formula itself (`=SUM(B2:B3)`) instead of an empty cell.
- **Tool descriptions:** both file-writing tools share one description of the syntax (`XLSX_FORMULA_GUIDE`), and the chat system prompt mentions formulas.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** new tests for formula parsing and escaping, the unsafe-formula filter, Markdown `*` handling, writing and reading back a workbook, the extractor, and the sheet preview. All suites pass: document-render 54, document-text 46, web 79. Typecheck, eslint and prettier are clean.
- **Calculation check:** generated workbooks were run through an independent formula engine (the Python `formulas` package). Every result was correct: line totals, `SUM`, `IF`, a cross-sheet reference, a quoted sheet name with a space, the Markdown `=A2*B2*C2` (24), and the `'=` escape staying text.
- **Playwright:** `e2e/artifact-inline.spec.ts` was extended with a formula cell in the workbook preview and run locally on `desktop-light` (it includes a phone-width pass). It passes.

author: viniciusks
body:
## O que foi feito

Pilha 1 da auditoria de integração (2/5). Empilhado sobre #516 (`issue-514`).

Nos formulários do web, o botão de envio só ficava desabilitado por `form.invalid`, e `POST /api/wallets/:walletId/positions` grava um documento com id novo, sem idempotência. Dois cliques criavam posição duplicada e dobravam a quantidade na carteira.

**Web**

- Novo `Submission` (`shared/utils/submission.util.ts`): reserva o envio, recusa o segundo e libera ao fim, com sucesso ou falha (o formulário preenchido não se perde).
- Aplicado em todos os pontos de escrita que o web tem: posição, mover para a geladeira, item da geladeira, descongelar e ativos do admin.
- Os quatro subformulários ganharam o input `submitting`, que deixa o botão indisponível e faz o `submit()` não emitir.
- O guard vem **antes** de montar a requisição: a chamada ao serviço é o envio.

**API** (decisão do dono do projeto: a API também recusa)

- Novo `addUnlessRecentDuplicate` (`shared/recent-duplicate.ts`): em **transação**, recusa com **409** a criação idêntica (mesmo `ticker` e mesmos valores) a uma gravada há menos de 10 s. Transação e não consulta + `add`, porque o toque repetido chega em milissegundos e dois pedidos lendo antes de qualquer gravação criariam os dois documentos. A consulta é só por igualdade em `ticker`, sem índice composto.
- Usado em `createPosition` e `createItem`. Quem cadastra de propósito a mesma compra duas vezes, com mais de 10 s entre elas, continua aceito.
- `openapi/dindin.yaml` descreve o 409 nas duas rotas; os contratos gerados não mudaram.
- A regra fica no AGENTS.md (seção de operações de escrita).

**Fora deste PR**

- `createWallet`, `createFridge` e `createDividend` não passam pelo helper (o web não tem formulário para eles e o app já se protege). O helper serve para elas num próximo passo.
- A garantia de exclusão mútua das transações é a do Firestore em produção; o teste de concorrência roda contra o emulador.

### Commits (TDD)

1. `test(#497)`: reprova o envio repetido de formulários do web
2. `feat(#497)`: bloqueia o envio repetido nos formulários do web
3. `test(#497)`: reprova a criação idêntica em sequência na API
4. `test(#497)`: reprova posição e item duplicados na rota de criação
5. `feat(#497)`: API recusa criação idêntica de posição e item em sequência

## Testes

- **Web: 16 novos testes** (helper, 4 formulários, 3 componentes pai). 769/769 passando.
- **API: 12 novos testes** (8 do helper contra o emulador, incluindo dois envios simultâneos; 4 de rota). 1405/1405 passando, repetida 5 vezes sem falha.
- Lint, `format:check`, build do web e `contracts:check` limpos.
- O teste do helper usa projeto próprio no emulador: o de regras limpa o `dindin-test` inteiro e apagava os dados daqui no meio da suíte (as falhas intermitentes que isso causou foram corrigidas).

## Checklist

- [x] Testes passam (`npm run test --workspace=apps/api`)
- [x] Código formatado (`npm run format`)
- [x] Issue vinculada no GitHub Projects
- [x] Branch segue o padrão `issue-<N>`

Closes #497

author: webmagic123
body:
feat:
Two graph reads fail outright once their results pass 2,000 rows: the supporter/opposer counts on claims, and a debate's vote tally.
Both now page by cursor instead of offset, so they drain every page without an offset ceiling

Implemented:
  Converted both reads from offset paging to cursor paging, so they walk after -> next cursor until there are no more pages - which has no offset ceiling. 

  - Claim summaries — swapped the offset userVotes query for a userVotesConnection (cursor) query, drained with collectCursorPages; removed the old offset query + its test.
  - Debate votes — swapped backlinksList(offset) for the backlinks(after) connection and reused the same helper
  - Page size 1000 -> 500
  - Both decoders now error on a missing connection instead of returning an empty tally, so a failed read can't look like "nobody voted."

### What

Unblocks Dreaming Sarah PPSA02929 boot to gameplay:

- Implement \sceKernelGetModuleInfoForUnwind\ (VirtualQuery on Windows, /proc/self/maps on Linux), mirroring \sceSysmoduleGetModuleInfoForUnwind\. The bundled libc unwinds at startup and previously terminated with \sceKernelGetModuleInfoForUnwind not implemented\.
- Make \sceKernelDebugRaiseException\ / \OnReleaseMode\ log-and-continue (debugger notification, same as KytyPS5). The game raises it on a handled parse path; throwing there kills a bootable title.

### Tested

Windows 11, RTX 4080, MinGW GCC 15.2.0. Relinked unwrapped eboot (\--windows\, SELF unwrapped beforehand: upstream relinker rejects SELF containers) with fresh \libs\ build:
- Before: \FAIL: unresolved ELF import kbw4UHHSYy0\ (stale patched libs), then \sceKernelGetModuleInfoForUnwind not implemented\, then \sceKernelDebugRaiseException not implemented\.
- After: C2 BOOT completes, 108 resources background-loaded, Vulkan swapchain up, window runs, orderly exit 0 on close.
- Note: game also needs \/app0/~INDEX\ present in the layout (opened first at boot).
- \ctest -E agc_driver_graphics|guest_rendering_wait\: 93/93 passed.
